articles.title: Prediction of Iron-Deficiency Anemia Among Pregnant Patients With First-Trimester Iron Deficiency Without Anemia: A Preliminary Predictive Model.
articles.authors: Sigman II, Mickas KH, Konecke N et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Iron repletion is the standard of care for iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in pregnancy to reduce adverse perinatal outcomes. Treatment is not recommended for iron deficiency without anemia (IDWA), but IDWA in the first trimester may progress to IDA later in pregnancy. This study aims to determine predictors associated with development of IDA among a cohort of pregnant patients with first-trimester IDWA and create a prediction model.
METHODS: This prospective cohort included singleton pregnancies with a complete blood count and ferritin before 14 weeks gestation. Exclusion criteria included anemia, previable delivery, fetal anatomic malformation, or aneuploidy. Candidate predictors were clinical variables associated with increased risk of IDA during pregnancy. Logistic regression used purposeful selection. Model fit, discrimination, and validation were assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, concordance index (AUC), and bootstrapping, respectively.
RESULTS: Among 511 eligible pregnant people, 129 (25%) had first-trimester IDWA, of whom 87 (67%) developed IDA before delivery. The prediction model includes prepregnancy BMI, ethnicity, and multiparity. Only ethnicity was significantly associated with IDA progression; Hispanic participants had higher odds than non-Hispanic participants (OR 4.69, CI: 1.65-17.0). The apparent AUC was 0.67, with corrected AUC of 0.64 and calibrated slope of 0.84. The Brier score was 0.199 with a scaled Brier score of 0.86.
CONCLUSIONS: Hispanic individuals with IDWA may have higher odds of progression to IDA compared with non-Hispanic individuals with IDWA. Results are limited by small sample size and few predictor variables, and should be carefully interpreted.

articles.title: Association of Type of Anti-Hypertensive With Unplanned Healthcare Utilization After Delivery Among Individuals in a Postpartum Remote Hypertension Monitoring Program.
articles.authors: Echeng N, Talbot S, Konecke N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Nifedipine and labetalol are commonly prescribed first-line antihypertensive medications for patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), although outcomes related to their use may differ. Prior studies suggest that nifedipine may reduce rates of postpartum readmission compared with labetalol; however, whether this association persists in the setting of remote blood pressure monitoring is unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether unplanned healthcare utilization differed among participants in a postpartum remote monitoring program who were prescribed nifedipine versus labetalol.
STUDY DESIGN: Postpartum patients with HDP at our tertiary care hospital are offered enrollment in a remote self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) program. This prospective observational cohort analysis included patients with HDP who were prescribed nifedipine alone or labetalol alone during the delivery hospitalization or after discharge. Patients receiving combination therapy or other antihypertensive agents were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of postpartum readmission or emergency department (ED) presentation for hypertension-related reasons within 30 days of delivery hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included hypertension-related severe maternal morbidity (SMM) after discharge, adherence measures, and sustained engagement with the SMBP program. Adjusted relative risks were estimated using generalized linear models controlling for maternal age and HDP diagnosis.
RESULTS: Among 2,644 patients enrolled in the SMBP program, 571 were prescribed either labetalol alone (n=143; 25%) or nifedipine alone (n=428; 75%). In multivariable analysis, the risk of the composite outcome of hypertension-related postpartum readmission or ED presentation was similar between those prescribed labetalol versus nifedipine (18% vs 17%; adjusted relative risk 1.07, 95% CI 0.65-1.77). Secondary outcomes were also similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: In our remote SMBP program for postpartum patients with HDP, there was no difference in the risk of hypertension-related unplanned healthcare utilization between those prescribed labetalol alone and those prescribed nifedipine alone. These findings suggest that within a structured postpartum SMBP program, antihypertensive choice alone may matter less than the monitoring framework itself.

articles.title: Reach of State-Mandated Insurance Coverage for Fertility Preservation in Patients With Cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.authors: Chacón KM, Zhang A, Nguyen K et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fertility preservation (FP) before cancer treatment effectively reduces iatrogenic infertility. Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia have passed insurance mandates for medically indicated FP coverage, but empiric data on population reach are lacking. We assessed the reach of California's mandate among young patients with cancer and sought to identify if social determinants of health (SDOH) are associated with mandate eligibility.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of all female patients age 0-42 years and male patients age 0-49 years newly diagnosed with cancer at a National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center between 2021 and 2024. SDOH included sex, age, race, ethnicity, primary language, and Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). The primary outcome was eligibility for FP coverage under California's mandate. Secondary outcomes included insurer confirmation of FP benefits and time required for benefit verification.
RESULTS: Of 903 patients, 18% were eligible for state-mandated FP benefits. Ineligibility was due to insurance by Medicaid (49%), ineligible commercial plans (37%), military-based plans (9%), federal-employee plans (2%), or being uninsured (3%). Non-English-speaking patients were 64% less likely to be eligible versus English-speaking patients (adjusted relative risk, 0.36 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.75]) in adjusted analysis. Subgroup analyses showed that eligible patients differed significantly from ineligible Medicaid-insured patients by race, primary language, and SVI, but did not differ from ineligible commercially insured patients. Among patients with plans subject to the mandate, insurers inaccurately reported that they had no FP coverage 28% of the time. Benefit verification required a median of 45 minutes per patient (range, 9-350 minutes, interquartile range, 25-80). These secondary outcomes differed significantly by insurer (P < .001).
CONCLUSION: California's mandate excludes most at-risk patients with cancer and perpetuates disparities in access. Future work in oncofertility health policy must consider mandate design and downstream implementation to eliminate barriers to care.

articles.title: Elevated blood lead levels among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen: Socio-demographic correlates and associations with a history of spontaneous abortion.
articles.authors: Qasem L, Al-Shami A, Yahya TAA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lead exposure in pregnant women is a critical public health concern, particularly in resource-limited settings where environmental regulations are less stringent. Prenatal lead exposure (Pb) is associated with various adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Therefore, this study aimed to assess blood lead levels (BLLs) among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen, and to identify health risks associated with environmental, behavioral, and socio-demographic factors.
METHODS: A cross-sectional multi-center study was conducted between August and November 2024, involving a sample of 150 pregnant women (aged 20-41 years) recruited across public and private healthcare facilities in Amran. Data were collected via structured questionnaires, and venous blood samples collected in K2 EDTA were analyzed using atomic absorption spectrophotometry (UNICAM 929AA). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 24, with a significance threshold of P < 0.05.
RESULTS: The results revealed a critically high prevalence of heavy metal exposure, with 82.7% of the sampled cohort exhibiting BLLs above 10 µg/dL. The median BLL of the sample was 40.8 µg/dL (IQR: 19.0-62.0), ranging from 1.0 to 143.0 µg/dL. Multivariable logistic regression identified a history of spontaneous abortion as a significant independent factor strongly associated with elevated BLLs (AOR = 5.88, 95% CI: 1.66-20.89, p = 0.006). Notably, the wide confidence interval indicates statistical imprecision due to limited reference cell counts. Elevated blood lead levels were positively, but non-significantly, associated with residential proximity to petrol stations and battery recycling sites, para-occupational exposure, and current smoking. Conversely, maternal age, formal education level, and housing type showed no significant independent association with lead levels.
CONCLUSION: This study identifies a severe public health crisis in Amran, highlighting the need for immediate investigations to identify sources of lead exposure, strengthened environmental regulation, and the integration of routine blood lead level screening into antenatal care. Such measures could help identify women with critically elevated BLLs who require close monitoring and follow-up.

articles.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic, 2018-2019.
articles.authors: Khounvisith V, Samountry B, van Beek J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women.
METHODS: Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18-76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection.
RESULTS: Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer. AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively). Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1-2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1-3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan. Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5-3.7, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. Periodic screening of women too old to benefit from the recently introduced vaccine should be considered.

articles.title: Effects of telerehabilitation pelvic floor muscle training on urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Yan H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telerehabilitation-based pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) may improve urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), but its effectiveness remains uncertain.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with telerehabilitation PFMT as the intervention. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for eligible English-language studies published up to November 15, 2024. The revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials was used to assess the risk of bias, and data were analyzed using Stata 16.1.
RESULTS: Three RCTs involving 100 participants were included in the meta-analysis, showing that telerehabilitation PFMT significantly improved urinary incontinence symptoms (weighted mean difference [WMD] = -2.53, P < .001) and bladder overactivity (WMD = -7.13, P < .001). However, no significant improvement was found in quality of life (WMD = -0.88, P = .002). Sensitivity analysis confirmed the stability of the results with no significant publication bias.
CONCLUSION: Telerehabilitation PFMT demonstrated positive effects on urinary incontinence and bladder overactivity in MS patients, although its impact on quality of life remains unclear. Further large-scale, high-quality RCTs are needed to confirm long-term efficacy and guide the development of clinical guidelines for telerehabilitation in MS rehabilitation.

articles.title: Association between distinct subgroups of perinatal depressive symptoms and exclusive breastfeeding behaviors: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Liu L, Xiao G et al.
articles.abstract: Previous studies have reported inconsistent findings regarding the association between perinatal depressive symptoms (PDS) and exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) behaviors. This inconsistency may be partly explained by the fact that previous studies often assessed depressive symptoms at a single time point and failed to capture variations in the timing and persistence of depressive symptoms throughout the perinatal period. Longitudinal assessments at multiple time points may help clarify whether depressive symptoms occurring at different stages of the perinatal period are differentially associated with EBF behaviors. This study investigates the longitudinal associations between distinct subgroups of PDS (i.e., antenatal, postpartum, persistent, and no depressive symptoms groups) and EBF behaviors in a prospective cohort study. We conducted a prospective cohort study in a tertiary hospital in Hunan, China, enrolling 304 women over the period from October 2022 to December 2023. The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale was administered at 7 points: the first, second, and third trimesters of pregnancy and again at 1 week, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months after delivery. EBF behaviors were assessed according to World Health Organization guidelines. Participants were divided into antenatal, postpartum, persistent, and no depressive symptoms groups. Generalized linear mixed models were used to examine the longitudinal associations between PDS subgroups and EBF behaviors. A total of 304 women were included in the study. After adjusting for confounders, women in the persistent depressive symptoms group were less likely to practice EBF compared with those in the no depressive symptoms group (P < .05). No significant associations were observed for the antenatal or postpartum depressive symptoms groups. Distinct subgroups of PDS showed different associations with EBF behaviors. Persistent depressive symptoms were linked to lower rates of EBF. Continuous screening and monitoring of depressive symptoms throughout the perinatal period may facilitate the early identification of women at risk for poor breastfeeding outcomes.

articles.title: Global research landscape of fertility preservation in cervical cancer: A bibliometric analysis (2001-2025).
articles.authors: Liu XQ, Ge L, Chen LQ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) persists in young adults despite vaccination, and the unique oncological and reproductive characteristics of these patients make fertility preservation (FP) research essential to avoid unnecessary fertility loss. In gynecological oncology, FP has evolved from an experimental concept into a standard component of comprehensive cancer care for young women. This study employed bibliometric analysis to identify research hotspots and forecast future trends in FP studies on patients with early-stage CC.
METHODS: Studies focusing on FP-related CC were searched for using the Web of Science Core Collection database. We used bibliometric software (VOSviewer and CiteSpace) for bibliometric analysis.
RESULTS: Overall, 782 articles published between 2001 and 2025 were included. The annual publication volumes fluctuated considerably, with no steady or uniform growth patterns observed. Cooperation network analysis indicated that the United States occupied the leading position in FP-related CC research, with the largest number of publications and citations, conferring the greatest influence. The Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center exhibited the highest publication output, and Gynecologic Oncology was the most productive journal in this field. Pedro T Ramirez, made the greatest contribution in terms of article quantity, and Denis Querleu was the most co-cited author. Four clusters (FP, CC, conservative treatment, and recurrence) were identified through a cluster analysis of the author-supplied keywords. Moreover, relatively recent terms, such as FS surgery, conservative treatment, and outcomes, have been gaining increasing attention among researchers.
CONCLUSIONS: This bibliometric study presents an objective, data-backed account of FP-related CC research, offering readers a useful resource to inform and support future research. Potential biases stemming from the exclusive use of a single database and English‑language‑only literature should be noted when interpreting our findings. Global FP research in patients with CC has shown a directional shift from technical‑oriented exploration toward personalized‑care‑related publications. Ovarian tissue cryopreservation and individualized protocols are emerging topics of growing research interest in this domain. Gaps in research capabilities continue to exist across regions, warranting strengthened global cooperation.

articles.title: Prenatal clinical features and clinical outcomes of fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome: A single-center case series of 22 patients.
articles.authors: Zhang R, Wang Z, An Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: This study analyzes 22 fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome in Eastern China to investigate the prenatal clinical features and postnatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study of 22 fetuses diagnosed with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion (312-855 kilobase) via chromosomal microarray analysis among 2607 prenatal cases from January 2022 to September 2024. Parental origin, ultrasound findings, and postnatal outcomes were evaluated. The 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion prevalence was 0.84% (22/2607). Prenatal ultrasound anomalies were observed in 54.5% (12/22), primarily mild cardiac findings (tricuspid regurgitation), choroid plexus cysts, and thickened nuchal translucency. Parental testing (13 cases) revealed 6 paternal, 6 maternal, and 1 de novo case. Postnatal follow-up of 18 live births (mean 14.7 months) showed normal development in most cases (17/18), with 1 child exhibiting delayed language development. Four pregnancies (18.2%) were terminated despite genetic counseling. Our study underscores that the 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion exhibits incomplete penetrance and variable prenatal phenotypes, complicating outcome prediction. Long-term pediatric follow-up is essential, and early reassurance should be avoided even in cases with normal prenatal findings or favorable short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Prognostic comparison of albumin-related inflammatory ratios in sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
articles.authors: Hu N, Wang S, Ma M et al.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) is associated with markedly elevated organ dysfunction and mortality. Integrated albumin-related inflammatory ratios may improve prognostic assessment, yet no systematic comparison of multiple ratios exists in SIC patients. This retrospective cohort study included 2214 SIC patients from the MIMIC-IV database. Five albumin-related inflammatory ratios-neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR), lymphocyte-to-albumin ratio (LAR), monocyte-to-albumin ratio (MAR), platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR), and red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) - were calculated from the first 24-hour laboratory values. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Discrimination was evaluated using ROC curves and time-dependent AUC; prognostic associations and dose-response relationships were examined using Kaplan-Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and restricted cubic splines. Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI) and Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI) quantified incremental value added to existing severity scores. Among 2214 patients, 673 (30.4%) died within 30 days. RAR and NAR showed relatively better discrimination than the other ratios, with AUC values of approximately 0.60, indicating modest prognostic discrimination. In fully adjusted Cox models, high-level RAR (T3 vs. T1) was associated with 52% increased mortality risk (HR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.21-1.89), and high-level NAR with 30% increased risk (HR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.04-1.63). NAR showed a significant nonlinear dose-response relationship with mortality (P for nonlinearity = .011). Incorporating RAR into SOFA, SIC-score, OASIS, and APS III significantly improved model discrimination and reclassification (all IDI and NRI P < .05). RAR and NAR are independent prognostic factors for 30-day mortality in SIC patients, and RAR provided statistically significant incremental value when incorporated into existing critical illness scoring systems. These readily obtainable ratios offer cost-effective tools for early risk stratification and individualized management.

articles.title: Associations of personalized prenatal care with delivery and perinatal outcomes in women with high-risk pregnancies.
articles.authors: Kong Y, Yang M, Shen C et al.
articles.abstract: This study examines whether the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with delivery and perinatal outcomes among women with high-risk pregnancies in a retrospective observational cohort. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 100 women with high-risk pregnancies who delivered between January 2020 and December 2023. Participants were classified according to documented receipt of personalized prenatal care or routine prenatal care. Propensity scores were estimated using maternal age, gravidity, parity, pre pregnancy or early-pregnancy body mass index, gestational age at registration, gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, thyroid dysfunction, uterine scar, and history of adverse pregnancy outcomes. One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed using a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score. All 100 women were retained after matching. Outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted independent-group comparisons (50 women per group). Vaginal delivery was more frequent in the personalized-care group than in the routine-care group (62.0% vs 40.0%), corresponding to an absolute difference of +22.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], +2.4- + 39.3) and an odds ratio (OR) of 2.45 (95% CI, 1.10-5.47; P = .028). Cesarean delivery occurred in 28.0% and 48.0% of women, respectively, corresponding to an absolute difference of -20.0 percentage points (95% CI, -37.1-- 1.0) and an OR of 0.42 (95% CI, 0.18-0.97). Preterm birth occurred in 10.0% versus 26.0% of women (absolute difference, -16.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -30.7- - 0.8; OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.10-0.97; P = .037). One and 5-minute Apgar scores were higher in the personalized-care group (P = .026 and P = .006, respectively). The composite adverse perinatal outcome, defined as the occurrence of at least one of preterm birth, low birth weight, neonatal asphyxia, or neonatal intensive care unit admission, occurred in 16.0% versus 36.0% of women (absolute difference, -20.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -35.8- - 2.8; OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.13-0.88; P = .023). In this study, the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with differences in delivery patterns, selected neonatal outcomes, nursing-compliance measures, and end-of-care psychological scores. The findings represent associations rather than causal effects and should be interpreted in light of the small sample size, residual confounding,…

articles.title: The trends and hotspots of research on polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents over the past three decades: A bibliometric analysis from 1995 to 2024.
articles.authors: Wan D, Cai J, Luo M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women, with increasing research attention directed toward adolescent populations. However, no comprehensive bibliometric analysis has systematically mapped the research landscape in this subspecialty. This study aimed to evaluate global research trends and hotspots in adolescent PCOS over the past 3 decades using bibliometric methods.
METHODS: Publications on adolescent PCOS from 1995 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer and Citespace were employed for data analysis and visualization, while key bibliometric indicators were computed and presented in tabular form.
RESULTS: A total of 1070 publications were included. Research output steadily increased over time, with the United States (n = 384, 35.89%), Turkey (n = 105, 9.81%), and India (n = 82, 7.66%) being the most productive countries. The most prominent institutions included the University of Pittsburgh, the University of Barcelona, and Monash University. Ibanez, Lourdes (n = 34) was the most prolific author, while the Journal of Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology (n = 84) and the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (highest citations, n = 6921) were the leading publication platforms. Core research areas encompassed mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, metabolism, and clinical outcomes. Keyword burst detection identified "diagnosis" (strength = 14.12) and "luteinizing hormone" (strength = 13.6) as the most intense hotspots. Notably, "quality of life" (2020-2024) and "depression" (2015-2024) emerged as the most recent and ongoing research frontiers.
CONCLUSION: This first bibliometric analysis of adolescent PCOS reveals growing global interest and active international collaborations in this field. Future research is expected to focus on refining diagnostic approaches and improving long-term quality of life for adolescent PCOS.

articles.title: Mendelian randomization study reveals the effects of air pollution on the risk of male and female infertility.
articles.authors: Huang Y, Zhang R, Li X et al.
articles.abstract: Recent observational studies have reported the links between particulate air pollutants and infertility, but the causal links still remain uncertain. This study was designed to determine the link between 5 types of air pollutants (NOx, PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10, and NO2) and risk of infertility via Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. Genetically predicted air pollutants (NOx, PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10, and NO2) and outcomes (male and female infertility) were obtained from UKbiobank and Finngen, respectively. Instrumental variables were strictly selected based on the 3 assumptions. Four mainstream MR analysis methods and sensitivity analyses were performed to provide a satisfactory level of causal evidence between 5 types of air pollutants (NOx, PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10, and NO2) and female and male infertility. Genetically predicted PM2.5 was correlated with the increased risk of male infertility (P = .04), but this correlation became indicative after Bonferroni test. No support was found for the causal associations between exposure to NOx, PM2.5-10, PM10, NO2, and male infertility. However, no evidence of causal associations was observed between 5 types of air pollutants (NOx, PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10, and NO2) and female infertility. Moreover, neither heterogeneity nor pleiotropy was found in any causal relationship. The present MR study suggests that PM2.5 might have a detrimental effect on male infertility, which indicates that PM2.5 contributes to the occurrence of male infertility. This study highlights the importance of improving air quality to reduce male infertility.

articles.title: Comparison of claims-defined postpartum depression after cesarean delivery under spinal versus epidural anesthesia: A nationwide propensity score-matched cohort study in Korea.
articles.authors: Min WK, Tae BS, Kang G et al.
articles.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common and serious mental health disorder that adversely affects maternal well-being and early parenting. Although spinal and epidural anesthesia are widely used during cesarean section, their differential associations with PPD remain unclear. This nationwide retrospective cohort study used data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service between 2013 and 2022. Women who underwent cesarean section with either spinal or epidural anesthesia were included. Propensity score matching (1:1 nearest-neighbor without replacement) was applied to control for baseline differences. The primary outcome was claims-defined PPD within 1 year postpartum, identified by diagnostic codes or antidepressant prescriptions. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between the anesthesia type and PPD. The absolute difference in PPD proportions between the spinal and epidural anesthesia groups was approximately 0.69 percentage points (3.03% vs 2.33%, respectively). Epidural anesthesia was associated with significantly lower odds of PPD than spinal anesthesia (adjusted odds ratio, 0.833; 95% confidence interval, 0.740-0.938; P = .003), even after adjusting for clinical and sociodemographic confounders. Among women undergoing cesarean delivery, epidural anesthesia was associated with lower odds of PPD than spinal anesthesia. Further studies are needed to confirm this association and determine its clinical relevance.

articles.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
articles.authors: Zhou Y, Tang S, Huang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.
METHODS: The data are derived from the Web of Science Core Collection and the PubMed database, covering relevant literature on asthma during pregnancy. The time range is from 2008 to 2024. The search strategy combined asthma-related terms ("asthma" OR "bronchial asthma") with pregnancy-related terms ("pregnancy" OR "gestation" OR "gestational"). After screening, 4088 eligible publications were included in the bibliometric analysis. A separate search of PubMed identified 28 clinical trials for the supplementary analysis of clinical research progress. Bibliometric analyses and visualization were performed using the bibliometrix R package (developed by Massimo Aria and Corrado Cuccurullo, Department of Economics and Statistics, University of Naples Federico II [with an academic spin-off, K-Synth Srl, associated with its dissemination]), CiteSpace (developed by Chaomei Chen, College of Computing and Informatics, Drexel University), and VOSviewer (developed by Nees Jan van Eck and Ludo Waltman, Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Leiden University).
RESULTS: This study comprised 4088 publications focusing on asthma during pregnancy. Annual publication counts demonstrated a gradual increase with intermittent fluctuations. The United States dominated both in publication output and international collaboration. Litonjua AA, Bisgaard H, and Weiss ST demonstrated high centrality and citation influence among authors. The core contributing journals included Pediatric Allergy and Immunology and Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. Major research focuses encompassed mechanistic exploration, influencing factors, and fetal and child health. Research hotspots were primarily concentrated on "air pollution," "birth cohort," "pregnancy complications," and "maternal diet." In recent years, emerging research frontiers have included "inflammation," "impact," "gut microbiota," "climate change," and "survivors." Clinical trial analysis highlighted nutritional interventions (particularly vitamin D) and precision management using biomarkers like fractional exhaled nitric oxide as current…

articles.title: Effects of Chinese herbal medicine with hCG on luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Wang Y, Ji J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluated the clinical efficacy and ovarian hemodynamic effects of adjunctive Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) combined with human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) versus hCG alone in infertile women with luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome (LUFS).
METHODS: Seven electronic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data) were searched from inception through October 6, 2024. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 (Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool for Randomized Trials) tool and modified Jadad scale. The primary outcome was ultrasound-confirmed ovulation rate; secondary outcomes included clinical pregnancy rate, ovarian artery pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI). Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using the Mantel-Haenszel method, whereas continuous outcomes were pooled as weighted mean differences (WMDs) using the inverse-variance method, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran Q-test, and publication bias using Begg and Egger tests. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025637729).
RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs were included in the review. After exclusion of Zhang LX 2015, the ovulation analysis included 16 RCTs and showed a higher ovulation rate with CHM plus hCG than with hCG alone (RR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.37-1.59; P < .001; I2 = 2%). The combined intervention was also associated with a higher clinical pregnancy rate (RR 2.01, 95% CI: 1.62-2.49; P < .001; I2 = 61%; 15 RCTs). Ovarian artery PI (WMD - 0.49, 95% CI: -0.81 to -0.17; P = .002; I2 = 52%) and RI (WMD - 0.18, 95% CI: -0.31 to -0.06; P = .005; I2 = 78%) were lower with combined treatment, although each analysis included only 2 RCTs. Tests for funnel plot asymmetry were not statistically significant for ovulation rate (Begg P = .260; Egger P = .080). Interpretation was limited by methodological weaknesses, variation in CHM regimens, and sparse evidence for hemodynamic outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive CHM may enhance ovulation and clinical pregnancy rates and improve ovarian arterial hemodynamics in infertile women with LUFS. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given methodological limitations, heterogeneous herbal regimens, and sparse hemodynamic data. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs using standardized CHM…

articles.title: A Simple Clinical Score for Predicting Curve Progression to the Bracing Threshold in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
articles.authors: Ogata Y, Asada T, Kotani T et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective longitudinal cohort study.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a simple, clinically applicable scoring system to predict progression to the bracing threshold before skeletal maturity in patients with mild adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS).
SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: AIS frequently presents with mild curves below the bracing threshold. Although most patients are initially managed through observation, a subset of patients progresses to require brace treatment during growth to skeletal maturity. However, a prediction model to guide early risk stratification and follow-up strategies is lacking.
METHODS: We included East Asian female patients aged ≥10 years with AIS who presented with major Cobb angles of ≥10° and <25° at baseline. Patients were followed until progression to ≥25° or attainment of skeletal maturity (Risser sign of 4-5 with <1 cm growth within 6 months and ≥2 years post-menarche). A prediction score for progression to ≥25° before skeletal maturity was developed using multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination based on the Bayesian Information Criterion. Model performance was evaluated, and internal validation was performed with 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results were validated using a separate cohort from the same source population.
RESULTS: In the final model, initial Cobb angle ≥20°, Risser sign 0-2, and time from menarche were retained. The resulting score ranged from 0 to 6 points. The model demonstrated discriminative ability, with optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.833 (development cohort) and 0.867 (validation cohort). Calibration was satisfactory, and decision curve analysis demonstrated clinical utility across a wide range of threshold probabilities. The score stratified patients into low-, moderate-, and high-risk groups with progressively increasing rates of curve progression.
CONCLUSIONS: Our simple scoring system uses readily available clinical variables to predict progression to the bracing threshold in female patients with mild AIS. This tool enables early risk stratification and may guide individualized follow-up strategies and timely clinical decision-making before brace initiation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Post-Menarcheal Height Gain After Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Treatment in Girls with Central Precocious Puberty.
articles.authors: Helvacioglu D, Öge S, Kelestemur E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Post-menarcheal growth varies by genetic height potential and menarcheal age, but data on residual growth after discontinuing gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (GnRHa) treatment in girls with central precocious puberty (CPP) are limited. This study aimed to evaluate menarcheal timing and post-menarcheal height gain after GnRHa treatment discontinuation.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 66 girls with CPP treated with GnRHa who had documented menarcheal timing and final adult height (FAH). Auxological and treatment data were collected at treatment initiation, discontinuation, menarche, and FAH.
RESULTS: Mean age at treatment initiation, discontinuation, and treatment duration were 7.91±1.22, 10.91±0.34, and 3.02±1.25 years, respectively. Mean bone age (BA) and BA/chronological age (CA) ratio were 9.62 ± 1.62 years and 1.23 ± 0.17 at treatment initiation, and 12.13 ± 0.74 years and 1.08 ± 0.07 at treatment discontinuation, respectively. Menarche occurred at 12.33±0.71 years, 16.36±7.74 months after treatment discontinuation. Mean height at menarche and FAH were 156.92±6.50 cm and 162.52±6.25 cm, respectively. Mean post-menarcheal height gain was 5.55±3.32 cm. Post-menarcheal height gain correlated negatively with the interval from treatment discontinuation to menarche (r= -0.54, p< 0.001), age at menarche (r= -0.34, p= 0.006), and height at menarche (r= -0.33, p= 0.007). Girls with a BA >11 years at GnRHa treatment initiation had a higher first-year growth velocity SDS but a shorter treatment duration, less height gain after treatment discontinuation, lower final adult height and final adult height SDS, and lower final adult height SDS relative to target height (p<0.05 for all). In contrast, none of these parameters differed significantly between the CA groups (<8 vs. ≥8 years), except for treatment duration.
CONCLUSION: A longer interval from treatment discontinuation to menarche and greater skeletal maturation at treatment initiation were associated with lower post-menarcheal height gain. These findings may help clinicians counsel families regarding expected menarcheal timing and residual growth after cessation of GnRHa treatment.

articles.title: Motile ciliopathies: a focus on primary ciliary dyskinesia.
articles.authors: Jones MG, Roy S
articles.abstract: Cilia are microtubule-based organelles found on almost all eukaryotic cells. In humans, cilia can be described as either motile or primary (immotile). Motile cilia are typically present on multiciliated cells (MCCs), which can potentially contain hundreds of these organelles that beat to generate directional fluid flow over epithelia. MCCs have a variety of roles in human physiology, such as mucus clearance from the lungs and gamete transport in the reproductive organs. Variants in over 50 genes have now been shown to disrupt cilia motility, causing a disease known as primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD). PCD patients typically suffer from mucus build up in the airways, laterality defects, hydrocephalus, scoliosis and infertility. Currently, treatment options for PCD are limited, with prevalent therapies mainly aimed at limiting lung damage. In this review, we will introduce motile cilia disorders under the umbrella of PCD and discuss key genetic factors involved in their aetiology, also highlighting what we currently know about PCD in the context of the Indian population. We will also explore how motile cilia have been linked to other diseases, such as COVID-19. Lastly, we will discuss how PCD is being researched and how these investigations could provide better treatment options, and possibly, a cure for the disease in the years ahead.

articles.title: Bisphenol A in follicular fluid and its association with oocyte maturation and embryo arrest in women undergoing in vitro fertilization.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Marconetto A, Iraci GS, Ñañez M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the presence and concentrations of bisphenol A (BPA) in follicular fluid (FF) from women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF) and to evaluate its associations with the proportion of metaphase II (MII) oocytes and the embryo arrest rate.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 36 women with infertility undergoing IVF at a public university hospital in Córdoba, Argentina. BPA concentrations in FF were determined by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Associations between BPA concentrations and MII and embryo arrest rates were assessed using Spearman correlation. Outcomes were also compared between groups defined according to the 50th (P50) and 75th (P75) percentiles of BPA concentration using the Mann-Whitney U test.
RESULTS: BPA concentrations were negatively correlated with the MII rate (ρ = -0.395; p = 0.017; n = 36) and positively correlated with the embryo arrest rate (ρ = 0.626; p < 0.001; n = 32). The embryo arrest rate was significantly higher in the BPA = P50 (p < 0.001) and = P75 (p = 0.001) groups, whereas the MII rate was significantly lower in the BPA = P75 group (p = 0.030).
CONCLUSION: Higher BPA concentrations in FF were associated with a lower MII rate and a higher embryo arrest rate among women undergoing IVF. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Current perspective in the pharmacological management of platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Bogani G, Polignano M, Di Donato V et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) remains a major therapeutic challenge. The traditional definition based on recurrence within 6 months after platinum is useful for trial design but does not capture the biological and clinical heterogeneity of recurrent disease.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines contemporary systemic treatment for PROC, including conventional chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab, biomarker-selected ADCs such as mirvetuximab soravtansine, novel anti-VEGF strategies, glucocorticoid receptor modulation, and immunotherapy-based combinations. Emerging ADCs and selected investigational targeted approaches are also discussed, with emphasis on their current level of clinical evidence. A targeted narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted, including literature available up to 27 July 2026.
EXPERT OPINION: Treatment should move beyond a fixed platinum-free interval toward an individualized assessment of platinum appropriateness. The new regimens are not interchangeable and should not be ranked by indirect comparisons. Biomarker availability, previous therapy, residual toxicity, disease kinetics, and patient priorities should guide selection. Over the next five years, the main challenge will be treatment sequencing and the development of dynamic models that estimate the probability of benefit from platinum and non-platinum options at each recurrence.

articles.title: "Bikini Medicine" No More-Major Medical Societies Propose New Framework for Female Heart Health.
articles.authors: Anderer S

articles.title: Prospective Validation of a Doppler-Enhanced Multimodal Ultrasound-Clinical Model for Predicting Clinical Pregnancy After IVF/ICSI Single Embryo Transfer.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.authors: Zhou H, Zhu H, Gao C et al.
articles.abstract: We developed and temporally validated a Doppler-enhanced multimodal ultrasound-clinical model for predicting clinical pregnancy after single morphologically high-quality embryo transfer. This single-center study included 795 participants undergoing autologous in vitro fertilization or intracytoplasmic sperm injection. The retrospective development cohort included 534 participants (427 for training and 107 for internal testing), and 261 participants with prospectively collected data formed the temporal validation cohort. B-mode and Doppler videos acquired 1 day before transfer underwent automated endometrial segmentation and feature extraction. A four-branch gated-attention network combined feature- and branch-level gating with self-attention to integrate imaging features, short-sequence descriptors, clinical variables, and embryo developmental stage. The locked model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.829 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.728-0.918) in internal testing. In temporal validation, the AUC was 0.771 (95% CI, 0.661-0.874), with an accuracy of 0.747, sensitivity of 0.780, and specificity of 0.703. The Brier score was 0.187 and the calibration slope was 0.947. Modality and architectural ablation analyses showed numerically higher AUCs and accuracies for the complete model in both cohorts, with statistically significant AUC differences in selected comparisons. Decision curve analysis suggested potential net benefit over part of the evaluated threshold range. These findings suggest the potential of the Doppler-enhanced multimodal model for individualized prediction of clinical pregnancy after embryo transfer.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology and genetic association analyses prioritize FASN as a potential molecular link between cigarette smoke exposure and male infertility.
articles.authors: Dai Z, Wang L, Wang S et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility (MIF) is a complex reproductive disorder influenced by genetic, lifestyle, and environmental factors. Cigarette smoke (CS) contains numerous reproductive toxicants and has been associated with impaired semen quality and fertility. However, the molecular mechanisms linking CS exposure to MIF remain unclear. Representative toxic constituents of CS were selected based on previous studies, and multiple databases were integrated to identify CS associated targets, which were intersected with MIF associated genes to obtain CS-MIF common targets. Three MIF transcriptomic datasets (GSE6872, GSE34514, and GSE22331) were integrated for differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Candidate genes were identified by integrating CS-MIF targets, differentially expressed genes, and WGCNA-derived key module genes, followed by LASSO and SVM-RFE machine learning analyses. Associations between genetically predicted candidate gene expression and MIF risk were investigated using cis-eQTL-based two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) analysis using testis-derived eQTL data was subsequently performed to provide complementary tissue-specific genetic evidence for FASN. Molecular docking suggested potential structural compatibility between FASN and several representative CS-associated compounds, while MD simulation supported the structural stability of the FASN-benzanthrone complex. Finally, TM4 Sertoli cells were exposed to cigarette smoke condensate (CSC), and FASN mRNA expression was evaluated by RT-qPCR. Four hub genes, including ABCC1, FASN, GAPDH, and SGK1, were identified from 14 candidate genes. MR analysis demonstrated that genetically predicted higher FASN expression was significantly associated with increased MIF risk (IVW: OR = 1.256, 95% CI = 1.109-1.423, P < 0.001; FDR-adjusted P = 0.004). SMR analysis using testis eQTL data further supported the association between FASN expression and MIF (P_SMR = 0.040, P_HEIDI = 0.307). Molecular docking identified benzanthrone as the compound with the most favorable predicted binding affinity for FASN among the 20 selected compounds (- 7.129 kcal/mol). Subsequent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation suggested structural stability of the FASN-benzanthrone complex under the investigated conditions. Furthermore, exposure of TM4 Sertoli cells to 100 μg/mL CSC for 24 h significantly increased FASN mRNA expression. This study…

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Ultrasound Mapping and Step-by-Step Excision of a Periurethral Leiomyoma: A Video Article.
articles.authors: Gutierrez-Contreras P, Gómez M, Blumel B et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Periurethral leiomyoma is an extremely rare benign mesenchymal tumor whose variable presentation can mimic other genitourinary tract conditions. We advocate for pelvic floor ultrasound (PFUS) as an accessible, noninvasive tool for diagnosis and surgical mapping. We also present a detailed surgical technique with key tips and tricks.
METHODS: A 39-year-old woman presented with a palpable vaginal mass and stress urinary incontinence. Evaluation included transperineal PFUS with 2D grayscale, color Doppler, 3D reconstruction, and tomographic ultrasound imaging (TUI), followed by vaginal surgical excision.
RESULTS: PFUS identified a well-defined, homogeneous, isoechoic solid mass (26 × 20 × 23 mm) at the junction of the proximal and middle urethral thirds (30% of the urethral length from the bladder neck), 1.6 mm from the urethral longitudinal muscle, with peripheral and intralesional vascularization (color score 3). After counseling, the patient elected to undergo surgical excision. A richly vascularized pseudocapsule was found, consistent with Doppler. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed a leiomyoma. At 1-month follow-up, the anatomical and functional outcome was optimal, without urinary incontinence.
CONCLUSIONS: PFUS may be a useful, accessible first-line or complementary imaging modality for periurethral lesions. In this case, it provided detailed anatomical mapping that correlated well with intraoperative and histopathological findings.

articles.title: Reliability of Offline Measurements of Stored Transperineal Ultrasound Images: An Exploratory Analysis by Observer Experience.
articles.authors: Xiao T, Cao Y, Du S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Previous studies have evaluated the reproducibility of transperineal ultrasound (TPUS) parameters for stress urinary incontinence (SUI); however, their relative reliability remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to evaluate inter- and intra-observer reliability of four TPUS parameters measured offline on stored images and explore differences by observer experience.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 398 women who underwent TPUS 6-8 weeks postpartum. Four observers, all radiologists (two senior and two junior), independently assessed four parameters: bladder position (BP), bladder neck descent (BND), urethral rotation angle (URA), and retrovesical angle (RVA) on stored dynamic midsagittal cine loops. Measurements were repeated after 2 weeks using the same image dataset. Reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), standard error of measurement (SEM), minimal detectable change (MDC95), and Bland-Altman analysis; analyses stratified by observer experience were exploratory.
RESULTS: Interobserver ICCs were highest for BP 0.981 (95% CI 0.965-0.988) and BND 0.977 (0.971-0.982), lower for URA 0.850 (0.827-0.871), and lowest for RVA 0.694 (0.653-0.733). SEM/MDC95 were 1.33/3.68 mm for BP, 1.43/3.96 mm for BND, 9.69/26.87° for URA, and 13.69/37.94° for RVA. Stratified by observer experience, ICC estimates for URA and RVA were lower among junior observers, whereas BP and BND remained high in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Interobserver reliability of offline measurements of stored TPUS images was highest for BP and BND and lowest for RVA. In exploratory analyses, reliability estimates for URA and RVA were lower among junior observers, whereas BP and BND remained highly reliable.

articles.title: Developing quality of care indicators for community-based pharmacist prescribing of ambulatory conditions and contraception in British Columbia, Canada.
articles.journal: Canadian pharmacists journal : CPJ = Revue des pharmaciens du Canada : RPC
articles.authors: Piszczek J, Humphrys E, Price M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-based pharmacists can prescribe for ambulatory conditions and contraception in many jurisdictions. Evidence that describes the measures of a high-quality prescribing service delivered by pharmacists is lacking.
METHODS: We sought to develop measures that could inform potential quality indicators to evaluate pharmacists' prescribing in the community setting in British Columbia. This study used a qualitative methodology comprising 1:1 semi-structured interviews with patients, pharmacists, physicians/nurse practitioners, and leaders from stakeholder organizations to identify measures of a high-quality prescribing service delivered by pharmacists. Data analysis was completed using reflexive thematic analysis. A constructive workshop with a sample of participants was conducted to validate and prioritize the quality measures and determine implementation feasibility.
RESULTS: Sixty-four interviews were analyzed (16 patients, 12 pharmacists, 23 physicians/nurse practitioners, and 13 stakeholder organization leaders). Thirty-three measures were proposed, aligning with 5 major themes: patient experience, efficacy, safety, access, and cost-effectiveness. Patients emphasized the importance of privacy and the use of appropriate pronouns within the theme of patient experience, while physicians/nurse practitioners focused on clinical efficacy, suggesting that adhering to documentation standards and interdisciplinary communication are the top measures of quality. All interviewee groups agreed that access-based quality indicators, such as wait times and geographical distribution, are important to develop. Cost-effectiveness, a unique theme not typically linked to quality, emerged as a key measure.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: This study identified 33 possible measures that can be used to develop quality indicators for pharmacists prescribing in community-based practice settings to evaluate such programs.

articles.title: Epidemiologic profile of self-reported drug allergy in a sample of adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
articles.authors: Vázquez-Nava F, Vázquez-Rodríguez CF, Vázquez-Rodríguez EM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-reported drug allergy (SRDA) continues to be a major global public health problem, particularly among adult females.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine the epidemiologic profile of SRDA in adolescent females aged 13-19 years with dysmenorrhea.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: In this cross-sectional study, data of 821 participants were analyzed. The data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire. The diagnosis of allergic disease was established with self-reported information provided by participants, without performing laboratory tests or physical examination.
RESULTS: The mean age of adolescent females was 17.8 ± 0.7 years. The mean age at the onset of menarche was approximately 11.8 ± 1.4 years; moreover, 59.3% of the participants experienced regular menstruations, but 72.0% suffered from dysmenorrhea. A total of 83 (10.1%) adolescent females reported having SRDA; of these, 23 participants (27.7%) reported being allergic to more than two medications; moreover, the age at the onset of SRDA was 10.7 ± 6.6 years. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that allergic rhinitis, consumption of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and recommended use of NSAIDs by mothers were associated with SRDA. Allergic rhinitis and consumption of NSAIDs without prescription were associated with SRDA in adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
CONCLUSION: It is important that parents understand the adverse effects that these medications generate if used without professional supervision. Healthcare professionals should be better trained to identify adolescent females with greater susceptibility to reporting SRDA.

articles.title: Why don't they tell women about these issues? A qualitative investigation into barriers for women seeking help for pelvic floor symptoms.
articles.authors: Campbell KG, Moffatt F, Shaw R et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate barriers to help-seeking for women with pelvic floor dysfunction.DesignQualitative semi-structured interview and focus group study, reflexive thematic analysis to develop overarching themes.SettingInterviews and focus groups were conducted online, via TEAMs.ParticipantsThirty adult women were recruited by email from an existing database of women who previously self-reported pelvic floor symptoms. Poster adverts and word of mouth were also used to purposefully increase representation. Twelve interviewees took part in three focus groups (n = 3, n = 4, n = 5). Most, 24 (80%), were white, and six (20%) were Pakistani Muslims. The majority (23, 76.7%) were educated to degree level or above. Other demographics such as age, reported symptoms, and employment status varied.ResultsThree main themes were developed: (1) 'An inevitable part of womanhood: the daily and ongoing challenges of pelvic floor symptoms', the embarrassment of coping with symptoms in public and the inevitability of this as part of women's lives; (2) 'The challenges: stumbling blocks to healthcare', with the key barrier identified as being lack of knowledge regarding symptoms, how and where to seek help; (3) 'The solution: navigating the route to pelvic health', including the need for clear public health messaging and education throughout the lifespan.ConclusionWomen believed that public health messaging regarding women's health issues should include clear, reliable information about pelvic health, delivered at all stages of women's lives. Simple education could empower women to make informed, appropriate choices regarding their pelvic health, thereby improving their quality of life.

articles.title: A Multimodal Hyaluronic Acid Approach to Compensate Menopause-Related Skin Changes: Hyaluronic Acid Serum Subanalysis With HA Filler Injection.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Bravo BSF, Braz AV, Coimbra D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estrogen depletion during menopause reduces collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans (GAG) synthesis, particularly hyaluronic acid (HA), and is associated with skin thinness, wrinkles, reduced elasticity, and decreased hydration.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of an integrated facial antiaging approach using a multiglycan HA serum with HA filler injection in menopausal women.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A serum formulation (containing HA, dipotassium glycyrrhizate, purple rice extract, Lactobacillus/soybean ferment extract, pro-Xylane) was applied twice daily on the face from Day -14 to Day 56 and integrated with nasolabial fold HA dermal filler injection on Day 0. In a post hoc subanalysis of 12 menopausal women, facial aging signs were assessed using instrumental measurements of skin elasticity and firmness, and standardized photography.
RESULTS: At baseline, net skin elasticity in the temple area and in the nasolabial fold area were lower in the menopausal subgroup compared with the overall cohort. In menopausal women, nasolabial and temple skin elasticity showed improvement between baseline and Day 56.
CONCLUSION: A multimodal HA serum integrated with HA dermal injection may offer a promising facial rejuvenation strategy in menopausal women with skin aging signs.

articles.title: Data quality assessment of maternal and newborn indicators from District Health Information Software 2 in five African countries for the period 2014-2023.
articles.authors: Akuze J, Otieno GP, Shabani J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracking progress of sustainable development goal (SDG) targets requires robust monitoring systems, yet data quality remains challenging across sub-Saharan Africa. Most countries rely on aggregated data from District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) or surveys to track maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) indicators. We evaluated MNCH data quality in DHIS2 across Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe (2014-2023).
METHODS: We analysed 16 ENAP-aligned indicators and their 29 corresponding data elements captured in DHIS2 across health facility levels. We applied the WHO Data Quality Review framework to assess availability, reporting completeness, internal consistency (ratio-based validation metrics and temporal trends), and external consistency (comparison with UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME), Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG), and World Health Organization Global Health Observatory data).
RESULTS: Of 29 data elements, Uganda had highest availability (72-76% during 2020-2023), followed by Kenya (62-66%), Tanzania (52%), and Ghana and Zimbabwe (41% each). Reporting completeness varied substantially: Tanzania achieved >95% facility reporting across all levels, while other countries showed disparities between hospitals and lower-level facilities. Internal consistency revealed problematic patterns for mortality-related ratios in Ghana (stillbirth-to-neonatal mortality ratios reaching 5.0-12.5) and Kenya (KMC-to-low birthweight ratios >2.0). After adjusting DHIS2 estimates for facility birth coverage, stillbirth rates generally exceeded or matched UN IGME estimates, whereas maternal mortality ratios showed substantial underreporting relative to MMEIG estimates. Ghana showed the closest MMR alignment and Kenya the largest discrepancy. Neonatal mortality was underreported in Ghana and Uganda but appeared higher than UN IGME estimates in Tanzania, a finding sensitive to aggregation method.
CONCLUSIONS: DHIS2 data quality varies substantially across countries, with country-specific challenges in availability, completeness and consistency. Strengthening facility-level data capture and developing an MNCH data quality module are crucial for improving data reliability.

articles.title: EPIGEN-Prostate: Identifying multi-omic markers of prostate cancer in Aotearoa New Zealand men.
articles.authors: Smith J, Yee A, Dutta A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: DNA methylation biomarkers have demonstrated promise as potential clinical biomarkers for improved detection and risk stratification of prostate cancer (PCa). Despite this, only sparse genome-scale, sequencing-based DNA methylation data are available in the early PCa setting. The EPIGEN-Prostate study aims to identify novel cell-free DNA methylation biomarkers from blood and multi-omic biomarkers from prostate tissue for detecting clinically significant PCa (csPCa).
STUDY DESIGN: EPIGEN-Prostate is a multi-centre, prospective, longitudinal cohort study of patients undergoing investigation for potential PCa, with a biomarker discovery-focused design. The primary objective of this study is to characterise novel cell-free DNA-based molecular biomarkers for non-invasive PCa detection and risk stratification. Secondary objectives include the development of multi-omic risk classifiers to predict disease progression and treatment response.
ENDPOINTS: The primary endpoint is the presence or absence of csPCa, defined here as International Society of Urological Pathology grade group ≥2. Secondary endpoints will include disease stage at presentation, disease recurrence following curative treatment, metastasis-free survival, and overall survival.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Individuals aged ≥18 years, scheduled to undergo prostate biopsy, and able to provide informed consent are eligible to participate. Blood samples will be prospectively collected before prostate biopsy, and prostate biopsy tissue will be retrieved for analysis after regular processing. Participants proceeding to radical prostatectomy may contribute surgical tissue and serial postoperative blood samples. Pre-biopsy plasma and matched prostate tissue samples will undergo genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using reduced representation bisulfite sequencing approaches. Tissue samples will also undergo RNA sequencing and genetic profiling. Clinical outcomes will be collected for up to 15 years. Biomarker discovery and validation will integrate molecular and clinical data using nested case-control analyses for each objective.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. Human ethical approval was obtained via the New Zealand Health and Disability Ethics Committee - Southern (HDEC 21/STH/184).

articles.title: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer: pharmacology, efficacy, safety and future perspectives.
articles.journal: Expert opinion on drug metabolism & toxicology
articles.authors: Ferrero S, Alessandri F, Centurioni MG et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is an established post-platinum option for advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, particularly mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) disease, in which single-agent programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade has limited activity.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review critically evaluates the pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, metabolism, drug-interaction potential, efficacy and safety of pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib. Evidence from KEYNOTE-146, KEYNOTE-775, its 5-year analysis, ENGOT-en9/LEAP-001 and contemporary real-world cohorts was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from database inception to 14 August 2026, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, regulatory documents and major congress proceedings.
EXPERT OPINION: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib improves survival after platinum therapy in immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive advanced endometrial cancer, but substantial toxicity requires proactive monitoring and frequent lenvatinib dose modification. Its therapeutic position is being redefined by first-line chemoimmunotherapy and the negative ENGOT-en9/LEAP-001 trial, while post-immunotherapy efficacy, predictive biomarkers and prospectively validated dosing strategies remain key research priorities.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery versus chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Athanasiou A, Bowden SJ, Ellis LB et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the primary treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). However, CRT is associated with high toxicity, and access to radiotherapy infrastructure remains limited or unavailable in some settings globally. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) followed by radical surgery has therefore been proposed as an alternative to CRT, but the evidence regarding its efficacy and toxicity compared to CRT remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To compare NACT followed by radical surgery versus CRT for LACC.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to 20 May 2026, with no date or language restrictions. We also searched the reference lists of included studies and contacted experts in the field.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) in women with LACC (FIGO 2018 stage IB3/IIA2/IIB/IIIA-C/IVA) comparing NACT followed by radical surgery to CRT. We excluded non-randomised studies.
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were overall survival, disease-free survival, and progression-free survival. Important outcomes included recurrence, acute and late toxicity, and quality of life.
RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias in the included studies using Cochrane's RoB 1 tool.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We performed a random-effects meta-analysis using the inverse-variance method. We assessed the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach.
INCLUDED STUDIES: Three RCTs (from four reports), with a total of 1326 women, reported on the outcomes of interest and were included in the meta-analysis.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: NACT + radical surgery may result in little to no difference in five-year overall survival compared to CRT (hazard ratio (HR) 1.11, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.90 to 1.36; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1259 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain for five-year disease-free survival (HR 1.28, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.69; 1 study, 635 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and five-year progression-free survival (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.07 to 1.75; 1 study, 626 participants; very low-certainty evidence). NACT + radical surgery probably increases grade ≥ 3 acute toxicity (risk ratio (RR) 1.82, 95% CI 1.45 to 2.29; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1224 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain for grade ≥ 3 late toxicity (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.01; 1 study, 591 participants; very low-certainty evidence). NACT + radical surgery may result in little to no…

articles.title: Association of postpartum glycemic control with serum MMP-9, ET-1, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in women with gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Lu H, Song R, Dong J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between 12-month postpartum glycemic control and serum matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)/endothelin-1 (ET-1) levels, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to explore statistical indirect effects involving these biomarkers.
METHODS: A total of 300 women with prior GDM followed up at 12 months postpartum were included. HbA1c, MMP-9, ET-1, blood pressure, and lipid profiles were assessed at the same follow-up visit. Participants were stratified into good (n = 141) and poor (n = 159) glycemic control groups based on a glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) cutoff of 5.7%. General characteristics, vascular biomarker levels, and the prevalence of hypertension and dyslipidemia were compared between the groups. Correlation and logistic regression analyzes were performed, followed by exploratory regression-based indirect-effect analyzes involving MMP-9 and ET-1.
RESULTS: The poor control group had significantly higher levels of MMP-9 and ET-1. HbA1c was positively correlated with both biomarkers. The prevalences of hypertension and dyslipidemia in the poor control group were 28.9% and 37.1%, respectively, and were significantly higher than those in the good control group. Exploratory analyzes showed significant indirect-effect estimates involving MMP-9 and ET-1, with model-derived proportions of approximately 22% to 26%; however, these contemporaneous associations do not establish causal mediation.
CONCLUSION: Poor glycemic control at 12 months postpartum was associated with higher MMP-9 and ET-1 levels and a greater prevalence of hypertension and dyslipidemia. The observed indirect effects should be interpreted as exploratory statistical associations rather than evidence of temporal or causal mediation.

articles.title: Underrecognised legacies of preeclampsia: a biosocial DOHaD perspective for research in sub-Saharan Africa.
articles.authors: Penkler M, Conrad ML, Fahlbusch FB et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is often approached as an acute obstetric complication, yet its longer-term implications for maternal and offspring health remain insufficiently understood, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Preeclampsia is a significant contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in SSA. Although its clinical management has improved, particularly in high-income countries, important questions remain regarding its causes, long-term consequences, and the extent to which existing evidence applies to SSA populations. In this viewpoint, we propose that conceptualising preeclampsia in SSA through a biosocial Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) lens provides a useful framework for investigating how biological, social, and environmental processes jointly shape maternal and offspring health across the life course. We review evidence and identify four priority domains for investigation: understanding context-specific causes and mechanisms; improving detection, care-seeking, and health system pathways; examining long-term maternal and offspring outcomes; and strengthening research infrastructures. We argue that advancing research on preeclampsia in SSA requires interdisciplinary approaches that integrate biological, clinical, epidemiological, and qualitative research. Such a research agenda has the potential to improve understanding of preeclampsia beyond its acute manifestations and to inform more equitable strategies for maternal and child health across the life course.

articles.title: Sexual Violence/Abuse and Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review of the Relationship.
articles.authors: Hooper L, Crentsil C, Meyrick J
articles.abstract: Sexual violence/abuse may influence cervical carcinogenesis through increased human papillomavirus exposure, trauma-related immune dysregulation and reduced engagement with prevention and care. However, the evidence on the co-occurrence of cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse has not been systematically synthesised. MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL Plus, PsycArticles, EMBASE and Scopus were searched for English-language studies published between January 2000 and January 2025. Studies were eligible if they reported the prevalence of cervical cancer among survivors of sexual violence/abuse or vice versa. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Seven studies from community, primary care and gynaecological oncology settings met inclusion criteria, covering a population of 8,840 participants. Among survivors of sexual violence/abuse, cervical cancer prevalence ranged from 5.4% to 32.3% and was consistently 1.5 to 2.7 times higher than among non-exposed comparators within the same settings. Among cervical cancer populations, sexual violence/abuse prevalence ranged from 18.4% to 57.5%, with stronger associations observed for severe or penetrative exposures. Adjusted odds ratios and relative risks ranged from approximately 3.3 to 11.15 at the highest exposure levels, consistent with a dose-response pattern. Findings point to a need for prevention strategies that consider how gender intersects with exposure to sexual violence/abuse. The review also suggests elevated co-occurrence between cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse relative to global population estimates (~10% intimate-partner violence and ~6% non-partner violence). Limitations include small samples and measurement heterogeneity. Findings support co-produced, survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches to cervical cancer prevention and oncology care that address barriers to healthcare engagement. Larger studies using validated measures and confounder-aware designs are needed.

articles.title: Ferric derisomaltose for the treatment of iron deficiency with or without anemia in women's health: an expert review.
articles.authors: Murji A, Abdul-Kadir R, Benson A et al.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency (ID) with or without anemia is highly prevalent in women, and is commonly caused by abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB; including heavy menstrual bleeding), increased iron requirements during pregnancy, or postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). ID or iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in women of reproductive age has been associated with a substantial burden on quality of life, impaired physical and cognitive functioning, decreased productivity, and increased healthcare costs. The presence of ID/IDA during pregnancy has also been linked to poorer maternal outcomes and fetal developmental impairments, including an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in neonates. Despite the high prevalence of ID/IDA and negative impact on women's health, these conditions are frequently overlooked and undertreated, in part due to the nonspecific nature of symptoms, such as fatigue. There is an increasing body of evidence for the use of intravenous (IV) iron to treat ID/IDA in women. Although efficacy is largely comparable among IV iron formulations when equivalent doses are used, there are factors that distinguish certain IV iron formulations from others. This review aims to discuss available evidence for the treatment of ID/IDA in women with ferric derisomaltose (FDI; a high-dose IV iron formulation), focusing on AUB, pregnancy, and PPH. Based on existing data, FDI represents a clinically-effective option for iron repletion in these contexts, and a low risk of hypersensitivity reactions and hypophosphatemia. There is scope for further research within the field of ID/IDA in women's health to address unmet needs and evidence gaps across the patient care pathway.

articles.title: Quality benchmarks in CRS-HIPEC surgery: An 11-year single-center analysis of outcomes, safety, and perioperative performance (2014-2024).
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.authors: Kazanowski M, Lesiak P, Wierzbicki J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality indicators (QIs) are central to safe delivery of cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC), yet program-level benchmarking across tumor types is scarce.
