OBJECTIVES: To describe the structure, process, and outcome QIs of a single-center CRS-HIPEC program (2014-2024) and to assess temporal trends in cytoreduction completeness, early mortality, length of stay (LOS), renal safety, and multidisciplinary team (MDT) integration against contemporary international benchmarks.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of consecutive CRS-HIPEC procedures (2014-2024) was conducted at a Polish tertiary center. Prespecified QIs included complete or near-complete cytoreduction (CC-0/1), 30- and 90-day mortality, LOS, LOS > 10 days, unplanned reoperation, 30-day readmission, MDT uptake, and acute kidney injury (AKI; defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) serum creatinine criteria). Time trends were displayed with Shewhart charts and funnel plots; Wilson's 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were used for proportions.
RESULTS: Among 319 procedures (colorectal cancer (CRC) 111; ovarian cancer 87; mesothelioma/other 57; low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm/pseudomyxoma peritonei (LAMN/PMP) 52; gastric cancer 12), the CC-0/1 rate was 93.4% overall (CRC 96.4%; LAMN/PMP 100%; ovarian cancer 90.8%; gastric cancer 91.7%; mesothelioma/other 86.0%). Thirtyand 90-day mortality were 0.6% and 1.6%, respectively; tumor-specific 30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 1.9%. Median LOS fell from 8.6 to 7.4 days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024), and LOS > 10 days declined from 25.0% to 13.2%. Peritoneal cancer index (PCI) correlated weakly with LOS (Spearman's ρ = 0.13, p = 0.019), while AKI occurred in 70/308 (22.7%, 95% CI: 18.4-27.7), predominantly stage 1; AKI did not differ by cisplatin exposure (26.0% vs 21.2%, p = 0.389). The proportion of procedures with documented MDT discussion increased to approx. 20-33% after 2018.
CONCLUSIONS: Over 11 years, a single-center CRS-HIPEC program achieved high-quality cytoreduction with low early mortality and a reduction in LOS, meeting or exceeding contemporary QI standards. Incorporating AKI and MDT uptake into routine audit supports comprehensive, program-level benchmarking.

articles.title: PM54 induces transcriptional collapse across cell-derived and patient-derived cancer models.
articles.authors: Diez MM, Fernández-Miranda I, Nuñez GS et al.
articles.abstract: Oncogenic transcriptional programs sustain malignant cell states and create therapeutic vulnerabilities in cancer. Here, we evaluated the antitumor activity and mechanism of PM54, a next-generation synthetic ecteinascidin analog, across diverse preclinical models. PM54 was tested in a 59-cell-line panel, mechanistic flow cytometry assays, short-term RNA sequencing in 32 cancer cell lines, six cell-derived xenografts (CDX), and three patient-derived orthotopic xenografts (PDOX). PM54 formed stable DNA adducts and showed broad low-nanomolar antiproliferative activity, with a mean half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 4.19 nM. Mechanistically, PM54 reduced nascent RNA synthesis, decreased RNA polymerase II levels, activated DNA-damage signaling, promoted S-phase accumulation, and triggered apoptosis. Short-term RNA sequencing revealed conserved repression of cell cycle, DNA repair, MYC-, mTOR-, and RNA polymerase II-associated programs. Pathway-level analyses identified two transcriptional response patterns, termed primed and adaptive patterns, differing in the extent of PM54-induced suppression of proliferative and oncogenic pathways. In vivo, PM54 reduced tumor growth and extended survival across six CDX models, with complete regressions in selected small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), melanoma, and prostate cancer models. In three PDOX models, PM54 reduced tumor burden by 81% in an experimentally generated cisplatin-resistant high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, 69% in ovarian clear cell carcinoma, and 84% in gastric adenocarcinoma. These findings support evaluation of PM54 as a transcription-targeting therapeutic.

articles.title: CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers are selectively sensitive to HSP70 inhibition.
articles.authors: Kumari S, Gupta S, Jamil A et al.
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, emphasizing the need for new targeted therapies. We recently identified CARM1-expressing HGSOCs as a distinct molecular subset associated with poor prognosis. To uncover therapeutic vulnerabilities in this subgroup, we performed a small-molecule inhibitor screen and identified the molecular chaperone heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) as a selective target in CARM1-high epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) cells. Pharmacological inhibition of HSP70 suppressed the growth of CARM1-expressing cells but not CARM1-knockout or normal epithelial cells, confirming on-target selectivity. Mechanistically, coactivator-associated arginine methyltransferase 1 (CARM1) regulates expression of multiple HSP70 co-chaperone genes from the DNAJ family without affecting total HSP70 expression. A newly developed HSP70 inhibitor, AP-4-139B, significantly reduced tumor growth in CARM1-high xenografts. Importantly, AP-4-139B was well tolerated with no detectable toxicity. Together, these results identify CARM1 as a key regulator of the HSP70 co-chaperone network and reveal HSP70 inhibition as a selective and well-tolerated therapeutic strategy for CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers.

articles.title: Racial Disparities in Postpartum Morbidity and Mortality: A Systematic Review of Structural and Healthcare Systems Factors With AI/ML Applications.
articles.journal: International journal of MCH and AIDS
articles.authors: Baba D, Mmamelu P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Racial disparities in maternal and postpartum health remain substantial in the United States. In 2024, the maternal mortality rate among non-Hispanic Black women was 44.8 deaths per 100,000 live births, compared with 14.2 among non-Hispanic White women. This systematic review synthesized contemporary evidence on racial disparities in postpartum morbidity and mortality, contributing structural and healthcare factors, emerging artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions intended to improve postpartum outcomes and equity.
METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. The evidence synthesis focused on U.S.-based primary empirical studies and authoritative government surveillance and analytic sources addressing maternal and postpartum outcomes, racial and ethnic disparities, structural and social determinants of health, healthcare access, artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions relevant to postpartum health. We used systematic and scoping reviews for citation identification and contextual interpretation but did not count them as independent primary evidence. Because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, exposures, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: The evidence demonstrated persistent racial and ethnic disparities across maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity and postpartum hemorrhage, peripartum cardiomyopathy and hypertensive disorders, postpartum mental health, and access to postpartum care. In 2024, non-Hispanic Black women experienced a maternal mortality rate approximately 3.2 times that of non-Hispanic White women. Pregnancy-related mortality surveillance further showed that a substantial proportion of deaths occurred beyond 42 days after pregnancy, underscoring the importance of care throughout the first postpartum year. Machine-learning studies demonstrated promising discrimination for selected maternal morbidity outcomes, but evidence regarding external validation, equitable performance across demographic subgroups, and prospective clinical implementation remained limited. Evidence on interventions was strongest for standardized obstetric quality-improvement initiatives, while postpartum Medicaid extensions, doula care, and paid family leave showed benefits in selected access,…

articles.title: Emerging antimicrobial resistance among uropathogens causing urinary tract infections in pregnant women: a retrospective study from Saudi Arabia.
articles.authors: Akhtar MS, Muyidi AA, Alqhtani R et al.
articles.abstract: It is evident that urinary tract infections (UTIs) can lead to poor maternal and perinatal outcomes. We designed this study to assess the susceptibility patterns of urinary pathogens to antimicrobials, along with their applicability for the mother and fetus, to ensure effective UTI treatment during pregnancy. This retrospective study was conducted to assess bacterial UTIs in the inpatient department of a tertiary care teaching hospital in Saudi Arabia. A total of 154 pregnant women with a confirmed case of UTI were included. Urine samples were collected by the midstream urine sampling method as per the standard procedure. We observed that around 52% of participants were in the 26-35 age group. The most common isolate was Escherichia coli (58.44%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (22.73%) and Streptococcus group B (3.90%). Considering the best choices in pregnancy for Escherichia coli isolates, nitrofurantoin (100%) showed the highest efficacy among participants, followed by fosfomycin (88.8%), amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (84.28%), and cefotaxime intravenously (90%). In prenatal care, it is of the utmost importance to regularly evaluate the susceptibility and resistance pattern of antimicrobials to UTI-related pathogens during the course of pregnancy in order to provide optimal therapy for both mothers and infants.

articles.title: Limited predictive value of second-to-third trimester complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices for preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics & gynecology and reproductive biology: X
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X
articles.authors: Suntipap M, Kassayanan P, Nontaprom K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the discriminatory performance of seven complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices for preeclampsia (PE) and their incremental value beyond a primary maternal clinical comparator.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies with routine CBC testing between 26.0 and 36.9 weeks of gestation at a tertiary hospital in Thailand. Pregnancies with PE or eclampsia were compared with normotensive pregnancies. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and logistic regression. Incremental value beyond a model comprising maternal age, body mass index, gestational age at CBC measurement, primigravidity, and pregestational diabetes was evaluated, with false discovery rate correction for multiple testing.
RESULTS: Among 8982 pregnancies, 276 (3.1%) were complicated by PE or eclampsia. CBC testing occurred at a median gestational age of 32.1 weeks. Individual indices showed limited discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.438 to 0.513 in the primary direction. NLR, MLR, and SIRI were lower among pregnancies with PE. After adjustment, SIRI reached nominal statistical significance, while NLR and MLR showed similar inverse estimates; none remained significant after false discovery rate correction. The primary maternal clinical comparator had an AUC of 0.723. Adding any individual index increased the AUC by no more than 0.0037 and provided minimal incremental net benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: CBC-derived inflammatory indices showed limited standalone discrimination for PE and negligible incremental value beyond the primary maternal clinical comparator. These findings do not support their use as standalone or incremental markers of PE risk at this gestational window.

articles.title: 4P-model: A machine learning-driven approach to expand non-invasive prenatal testing for early risk stratification of placenta accreta spectrum via genome-wide cfDNA promoter profiling.
articles.authors: Hao R, Wang B, Zhang B et al.
articles.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is a leading cause of life-threatening obstetric hemorrhage, yet early diagnosis remains challenging. Traditional non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is limited to fetal aneuploidy screening, while its potential for maternal placental disorders is underexplored. We conducted a multicenter nested case-control study to investigate whether machine learning-driven genome-wide cell-free DNA (cfDNA) promoter profiling, derived from routine NIPT data, could extend the utility of NIPT to enable early prediction and subtype risk stratification of PAS. NIPT data were analyzed from 1060 individuals with a history of uterine surgery (126 increta/percreta, 139 accreta, and 795 controls after propensity score matching). A training set of 280 participants was used for feature selection with recursive feature elimination across five machine learning algorithms, and the best-performing model was validated in an internal cohort, a PLUS cohort with deeper sequencing, and two external cohorts generated on independent platforms. Pairwise differential analyses identified 211 candidate genes with altered promoter coverage. After feature selection, we developed the 4P-model, a 15-gene multiclass risk stratification model, to differentiate increta/percreta, accreta, and controls with a macro-average AUC of 0.973. Robust performance was reproduced across three NIPT platforms and the PLUS cohort, with AUCs of 0.882-0.946. These findings support that machine learning facilitates the translation of genome-wide cfDNA promoter signals embedded in NIPT data into early prediction and risk stratification of PAS. This noninvasive and scalable approach extends the diagnostic window, offering a clinically feasible tool for timely referral, improving perinatal outcomes.

articles.title: Periconceptional Uptake of Folic Acid and Associated Factors Among Pregnant Women at Soroti Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda.
articles.authors: Atwijukire A, Namujju J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periconceptional folic acid supplementation reduces the risk of neural tube defects, but timely uptake remains low in many low- and middle-income settings.
PURPOSE: To determine the prevalence of preconceptional and first-trimester folic acid uptake and to identify factors associated with uptake among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Soroti Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 179 pregnant women attending antenatal care between 14 March and 23 April 2024. Folic acid uptake was self-reported. Data were collected using a researcher-administered structured questionnaire and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used as an association model, and adjusted odds ratios (aORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and p values are reported.
RESULTS: Preconceptional folic acid uptake was 10.1% (18/179; 95% CI 6.5%-15.3%), while 54.7% (98/179; 95% CI 47.4%-61.9%) reported first-trimester uptake. Knowledge of folic acid benefits was associated with higher odds of preconceptional uptake, but the estimate was imprecise because only 18 women reported this outcome (aOR 19.51, 95% CI 2.40-158.51; p=0.005). For first-trimester uptake, first antenatal care attendance at 4-6 months rather than 1-3 months was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.075, 95% CI 0.033-0.170; p<0.001), while knowledge of folic acid benefits was associated with higher odds (aOR 3.50, 95% CI 1.40-8.75; p=0.007).
CONCLUSION: In this single-center, cross-sectional study based on self-reported information, preconceptional folic acid uptake was very low, and almost half of the participants did not report first-trimester uptake. Knowledge of folic acid benefits and earlier first antenatal care attendance were associated with timely uptake; these associations are not causal, and estimates for preconceptional uptake are imprecise and should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Public financing, external assistance and household health payments: a causal machine learning analysis of 173 countries, 2000-2023.
articles.authors: Alraeesi R, Alsawalqa RO, Khan Y
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-pocket (OOP) payments remain the dominant health financing mechanism in many countries while development assistance for health is contracting. Existing cross-country evidence on financing composition and household payments is weakened by an accounting identity linking regressors to the outcome and by the allocation of financing to high-burden settings.
METHODS: We analyzed 4,141 country-year observations from 173 countries (2000-2023) using the WHO Global Health Expenditure Database and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicators. Government and external shares of current health expenditure (CHE) were entered jointly, so each effect represents a reallocation from domestic private financing. The primary outcome was per capita real out-of-pocket spending. Double machine learning was applied across three specifications, culminating in a within-country design with three-year lags, pre-treatment covariates, and a baseline adjustment. Inference was country-cluster-robust.
RESULTS: Within countries, reallocating 10 percentage points from private to government financing was associated with 11.4% lower out-of-pocket spending per capita (95% confidence interval [CI: 7.9-14.8]), and reallocating to external financing was associated with 14.7% lower spending (11.2-18.0); the difference was not significant (p = 0.075). Conventional specifications overstated these effects by 2.6-2.9-fold. Share-based estimates matched the value implied by the accounting identity. Results were robust across all sensitivity analyses. No effects on tuberculosis, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), or maternal mortality were detected, and regional estimates did not support a policy typology.
CONCLUSION: Shifting financing toward pooled government or external sources is associated with lower household payments, but by far less than cross-country estimates suggest. Financing targets and assessments of aid withdrawal should rely on evidence from within the country.

articles.title: Fetal structural and chromosomal anomalies and cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal status: A population-based study in Central New York.
articles.authors: Rojas-Mendez P, Sampson R, Wojtowycz M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies suggest higher cesarean delivery (CD) rates among pregnancies complicated by congenital anomalies; however, the contribution of specific indications, particularly CD coded as non-reassuring fetal status (NRFS), remains understudied.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between fetal anomalies and the likelihood of CD coded as NRFS, and to characterize this association across joint categories of small-for-gestational-age (SGA) and preterm birth.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study used data from the New York Statewide Perinatal Data System, including 220,368 deliveries ≥20 weeks' gestation from 2011 to 2023. The primary outcome was CD coded as NRFS as the sole indication. The primary exposure was the presence of ≥1 structural or chromosomal fetal anomaly, analyzed as a composite and by anomaly subgroup. Logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and absolute risk differences were calculated to aid clinical interpretation. Joint-category analyses were performed to evaluate the association across combinations of SGA and preterm birth. Bivariate analyses compared baseline characteristics by anomaly status.
RESULTS: Among 220,368 deliveries, 904 (0.4%) were classified as having a composite anomaly. The rate of CD coded as NRFS was higher among pregnancies with a composite anomaly (9.8% vs. 3.7%; relative risk, 2.69), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 6.2 percentage points. After adjustment, composite anomaly status was associated with higher odds of CD coded as NRFS (aOR, 2.72). The magnitude of association varied by anomaly type, with higher odds observed in omphalocele (aOR, 4.66), chromosomal disorders other than trisomy 21 (T21) (aOR, 4.09), and congenital heart disease (aOR, 2.97). In joint-category analyses, the magnitude of association varied across combinations of composite anomaly status, SGA, and preterm birth.
CONCLUSION: Selected fetal structural and chromosomal anomalies were associated with higher odds of CD coded as NRFS, after adjustment for intrapartum factors. This association varied by anomaly subtype and across joint categories defined by SGA and preterm birth. These associations may reflect both underlying fetal vulnerability and variation in clinical decision-making rather than physiologic intolerance to labor alone.

articles.title: Testosterone Therapy and Sexual Health in Men and Women: Is There a Role for Long-Acting Subcutaneous Pellets?
articles.authors: Rojas-Zambrano JG, Molina-Varas EA, Rojas-Zambrano A
articles.abstract: Testosterone influences sexual desire and sexual response in men and women, but the clinical reasons for prescribing it differ between the sexes. In men, treatment is reserved for symptomatic hypogonadism confirmed by repeated morning measurements, and placebo-controlled trials show improvements in libido and sexual activity, with smaller and less consistent effects on erectile function. In women, the indication with the strongest support is hypoactive sexual desire disorder after menopause, where randomized trials of transdermal testosterone show moderate gains in desire, arousal, orgasm, and satisfaction, along with less sexual distress. Subcutaneous testosterone pellets release the hormone for several months after a single office procedure and appeal to patients who prefer infrequent dosing. Most of the evidence for testosterone therapy, however, comes from transdermal and injectable preparations. Pellet studies in men describe steady release, a predictable duration of action, extrusion as the most frequent complication, and erythrocytosis that cannot be corrected by lowering the dose once the pellets are in place. The few randomized comparisons of pellets with other formulations were small, did not include transdermal testosterone, and were not designed around validated sexual-function outcomes. In women, pellets are used off-label, are often compounded, and can produce serum concentrations well above the female physiological range; current professional guidance advises against their use for hypoactive sexual desire disorder. This narrative review describes the physiology of testosterone in both sexes, the diagnostic criteria and validated instruments used to assess sexual function, the trial evidence for testosterone therapy, and the pharmacology, effectiveness, and safety of pellets. Pellets are a reasonable option for selected hypogonadal men who do not seek fertility, accept a formulation that cannot be quickly reversed, and agree to hematocrit monitoring. In women, current guidance does not support their use, and any exception requires informed consent, close monitoring, and acknowledgment that it departs from that guidance.

articles.title: Peripartum infective endocarditis in complex congenital heart disease: Melody valve infection after caesarean delivery.
articles.authors: Hopkins TM, Wander G, Tari S et al.
articles.abstract: We describe the pregnancy and postpartum course of a 26-year-old nulliparous woman with repaired double outlet right ventricle, ventricular septal defect, and severe pulmonary stenosis who was managed by a multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team. She underwent emergency caesarean delivery at 38 weeks. Her postpartum course was complicated by suspected pulmonary embolism and infective endocarditis of a Melody valve, requiring right ventricle-pulmonary artery conduit replacement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of postpartum cardiopulmonary symptoms in women with complex congenital heart disease and raises important questions regarding infective endocarditis prophylaxis in women with prosthetic cardiac material.

articles.title: Effect of radiofrequency therapy in the treatment of de novo dyspareunia at 4 to 12 months postpartum: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.authors: Box C, Carralero-Martínez A, Manresa M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstetric pelvic floor trauma, including vaginal, perineal, and anal sphincter injuries, commonly causes postpartum perineal pain, which may persist for up to 12 months. As a result, sexual dysfunction is frequent, with dyspareunia being one of the most common symptoms.
OBJECTIVE: The main goal of this study is to assess radiofrequency (RF) therapy efficacy in women with de novo dyspareunia persisting 4 to 12 months postpartum, in terms of pain, sexual health, quality of life (QoL), and the effects that persist 6 months after treatment.
STUDY DESIGN: A total of 88 women presenting de novo dyspareunia due to obstetric lesions that persisted at 4 to 12 months postpartum were included in this double-blinded randomized clinical trial. The goal was to assess the effect of intravaginal and abdominal capacitive-resistive monopolar RF therapy in combination with self-performed daily perineal massage. The participants were divided into two groups, on-RF and off-RF, and received 5 sessions. In both groups, pain, QoL, sexual function, and pelvic floor dysfunction symptoms were assessed at baseline, after completing the study, and at 6 months. To assess the efficacy of RF therapy, the difference between baseline and postintervention numeric rating scale scores (the primary variable) and the secondary variables, sexual function and QoL, was compared between the intervention and control groups.
RESULTS: A total of 76 participants finished the intervention, 39 in the on-RF group and 37 in the off-RF group, and a total of 37 completed the 6-month follow-up. Patients in the on-RF group showed a greater reduction and ended with lower mean pain scores (standard deviation) [2.1 (1.9) vs 5.6 (2.1); P<.001] and greater improvement in sexual function and QoL.
CONCLUSION: Active RF therapy combined with patient-performed daily perineal massage significantly reduces pain levels in women with de novo postpartum dyspareunia to a greater extent than sham-RF therapy and daily perineal massage, and this effect seems to persist for at least 6 months after treatment as seen in the participants with available follow-up data.

articles.title: Unilateral Anesthesia Mumps After Robotic Gynecologic Surgery: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Vlahos F, Panagodimou EK, Sgouta E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthesia mumps is a rare, benign postoperative complication following anesthesia.
CASE: A 63-year-old woman developed unilateral, nontender parotid swelling following robotic-assisted hysterectomy in the Trendelenburg position with shoulder restraints. She had no systemic symptoms, an unremarkable intraoral examination, and a patent airway. No imaging, serology, or amylase testing was performed. Supportive management with hydration, head elevation, and analgesics led to resolution within 24 h.
CONCLUSIONS: Unilateral anesthesia mumps likely resulted from dehydration and salivary duct obstruction associated with Trendelenburg positioning. Prompt recognition enabled conservative management, avoiding unnecessary investigations or treatment. As robotic surgery becomes increasingly common, requiring Trendelenburg positioning, anesthesiologists should recognize this complication.

articles.title: Cell type-specific transcriptomic responses to progesterone and bazedoxifene prevent estradiol-driven proliferation in the human endometrium.
articles.authors: Dias Da Silva I, Wuidar V, Blacher S et al.
articles.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) combining estrogen with a progestogen protects the endometrium in non-hysterectomized women but increases breast cancer risk, prompting the search for progestogen-free alternatives. Selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), such as bazedoxifene (BZA), offer a potential solution, yet their use for menopausal indications remains debated. MHT evaluations rely largely on mouse models or clinical measurements of endometrial thickness, providing limited mechanistic insight in human tissue. Here, we performed cell-type-specific transcriptomic profiling of patient-derived endometrial xenografts to compare how progesterone and BZA prevent estradiol-induced proliferation. Both treatments act through specific mechanisms: progesterone preserves half of the estradiol-dependent transcriptional response while inducing new programs, whereas BZA broadly abrogates estradiol-driven signaling in epithelial and stromal cells. We further identified cell-specific transcription factors and differential regulation of paracrine/autocrine networks. Overall, this study provides mechanistic and transcriptomic resources from human endometrium, with important implications for the development of improved MHT strategies.

articles.title: Prediction of severe neonatal morbidity using maternal, fetal, social, and delivery factors.
articles.authors: Blitz MJ, Jackson FI, Lee JY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate prediction models for severe neonatal morbidity (SNM) at admission for delivery and at delivery while evaluating the incremental contribution of maternal, fetal, social, intrapartum, and immediate post-delivery factors.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of singleton deliveries ≥32 weeks' gestation at two tertiary hospitals (2019-2023). SNM was defined using a composite of severe neonatal diagnoses and procedures. The cohort was randomly divided into training (70 %) and testing (30 %) cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression models were developed iteratively to predict SNM at admission for delivery and at delivery. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), compared using the DeLong test, and overall accuracy using Brier scores.
RESULTS: Among 53,872 singleton deliveries, 3,775 newborns (7.0 %) experienced SNM. Maternal factors alone demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC 0.721, 95 % CI 0.704-0.738); adding fetal and social factors produced a modest increase (AUC 0.738, 95 % CI 0.721-0.755; difference 0.017, 95 % CI 0.005-0.029; p=0.0051). Gestational age was the strongest predictor; others included major structural anomalies, polyhydramnios, abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers, hypertensive disorders, and substance use disorder. Adding intrapartum factors and newborn sex increased the AUC to 0.776 (95 % CI 0.761-0.791); birthweight relative to gestational age added minimal improvement (AUC 0.780, 95 % CI 0.765-0.795).
CONCLUSIONS: SNM can be predicted with moderate accuracy using routinely available clinical information. Fetal and social factors modestly improved discrimination, and intrapartum information further improved it, supporting staged neonatal risk assessment during the delivery hospitalization.

articles.title: DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
articles.authors: Hlady RA, Wang L, Marek GW et al.
articles.abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to the clinical and histopathologic features of AATD may provide insight into disease heterogeneity, progression, and therapeutic response. We analyzed a longitudinal cohort of ZZ-genotype AATD patients with paired liver biopsies, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and clinical data collected at baseline and 3-y follow-up. Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of liver tissue identified 15 CpG clusters associated with liver disease severity, immune pathways, and clinical measures including METAVIR fibrosis score and γ-glutamyltransferase. Parallel methylation profiling of matched plasma-derived cfDNA identified eight analogous CpG clusters enriched for similar biological pathways and associated with clinical parameters. Integration of tissue and cfDNA datasets revealed fifty-one shared CpGs representing disease-associated methylation signatures, including loci such as ZFP57 that tracks with portal inflammation. We also identified a DNA methylation signature associated with fibrosis progression based on changes in METAVIR score. These findings demonstrate that liver- and cfDNA-derived DNA methylation signatures robustly stratify AATD patients by relevant measures of liver injury and fibrosis, supporting their potential as non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring responses to emerging therapies.

articles.title: EPB41L4A‑AS1 promotes endothelial dysfunction in preeclampsia through the miR‑26a‑2‑3p/15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK axis.
articles.authors: He J, Ran H, Xia R et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy characterized by systemic endothelial dysfunction. Long non‑coding RNA EPB41L4A‑AS1 has been implicated in pregnancy‑related disorders, but its role in PE remains unclear. Our previous work demonstrated that downregulation of miR‑26a‑2‑3p promotes endothelial injury via activation of the 15‑lipoxygenase‑1 (15‑LOX‑1)/p38 mitogen‑activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK) pathway. In the present study, whether EPB41L4A‑AS1 contributes to PE pathogenesis by regulating this axis was investigated. EPB41L4A‑AS1 expression was significantly upregulated in placental tissues from patients with PE and negatively correlated with miR‑26a‑2‑3p levels. Functional experiments revealed that EPB41L4A‑AS1 overexpression suppressed miR‑26a‑2‑3p, activated the 15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK pathway and promoted endothelial dysfunction, effects that were partially reversed by miR‑26a‑2‑3p mimics. In an L‑NAME‑induced PE mouse model, EPB41L4A‑AS1 overexpression exacerbated hypertension, proteinuria, placental apoptosis and oxidative stress, whereas miR‑26a‑2‑3p agomir administration attenuated these effects. Mechanistically, luciferase reporter assays revealed no direct binding between EPB41L4A‑AS1 and miR‑26a‑2‑3p, suggesting an indirect regulatory mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify EPB41L4A‑AS1 as a critical upstream regulator of the miR‑26a‑2‑3p/15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK axis in PE and suggest that targeting this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Bidirectional regulatory roles of COMMD1 in tumorigenesis and progression: Translational prospects as a diagnostic and therapeutic target (Review).
articles.authors: Lin W, Yu L, Shi R et al.
articles.abstract: Copper metabolism MURR1 domain‑containing protein 1 (COMMD1) is one of the best‑characterised members of the COMMD protein family. Initially identified as a key regulator of copper ion homeostasis, accumulating evidence has shown that COMMD1 does not function as a canonical tumour suppressor or oncogene in malignant tumours. Instead, it serves as a context‑dependent molecular hub whose activity is dynamically influenced by cellular background, signalling pathway status and post‑translational modifications. On the one hand, COMMD1 exerts antitumour effects by inhibiting NF‑κB and hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1 signalling, regulating DNA damage repair, modulating cell cycle progression and enhancing apoptotic sensitivity. Conversely, in certain tumour types, COMMD1 may promote drug resistance and adaptive tumour evolution by preserving DNA repair capacity, supporting cell survival or modulating ubiquitination networks. This review systematically summarises the differential expression patterns and functional mechanisms of COMMD1 in lung cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, multiple myeloma, neuroblastoma and breast cancer, with particular emphasis on its pivotal roles in the inflammatory immune microenvironment, hypoxic adaptation, genomic stability and drug sensitivity. Furthermore, translational strategies targeting COMMD1 are discussed, including COMMD1‑dependent peptide therapeutics, small‑molecule stabilisers, copper chelation‑based combination therapies and gene regulatory interventions. Collectively, the evidence supports COMMD1 as a potential integrated diagnostic and therapeutic target in precision oncology. However, its tissue‑specific and bidirectional functions highlight the need for further mechanistic investigation and patient stratification to enable precise clinical translation.

articles.title: Cervical cancer risk reduction in the era of human papillomavirus vaccination.
articles.authors: Phillips SA, Bandi P, Star J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination status is important to consider when evaluating the population-level impact of cervical screening uptake on cervical cancer risk, yet screening rates are rarely presented by vaccination status, limiting assessments of population-level protection against cervical cancer.
METHODS: Using females 21-39 years old from the 2019 National Health Interview Survey (N = 4000), the authors report the proportion up-to-date with cervical screening stratified by age and self-reported HPV vaccination status. Using assumptions of 85% and 70% reduction in cervical cancer risk from HPV vaccination and up-to-date screening status, respectively, the authors explore the population-level reduction in cervical cancer risk from varying screening coverage by HPV vaccination status.
RESULTS: A total of 78.4% of females were up-to-date with screening, 38.0% reported ever receiving an HPV vaccine, and 15.3% were both unvaccinated and not up-to-date with screening. Across age groups, the proportion of females up-to-date with screening was 6.3%-19.1% higher for vaccinated versus unvaccinated females. The relative reduction in cervical cancer risk from vaccination and screening ranged from 62.1% for females 36-39 years old to 73.1% for females 26-30 years old, compared to the absence of vaccination and screening. Despite females 21-25 years old having the lowest screening uptake, their reduction in cervical cancer risk was not the lowest due to higher vaccination levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Cervical screening rates are higher among females who were vaccinated against HPV, resulting in a higher population-level risk of cervical cancer than expected from considering vaccination and screening rates independently. Including vaccination status in national surveillance data sets would help identify and target interventions within communities at higher risk.

articles.title: Compartment-specific remodeling of placental and fetal hepatic amino acid metabolism in a rat model of protein restriction-induced fetal growth restriction.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.authors: Simmerl M, Menendez-Castro C, Schuessler S et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal protein restriction is a widely used experimental model of fetal growth restriction (FGR), yet fetal metabolic adaptations across placental and hepatic compartments remain incompletely characterized. We investigated placental and fetal hepatic amino acid and related metabolite profiles in a rat model of protein restriction-induced FGR. Pregnant Wistar rats received either a low-protein diet (8.1% protein; LP) or an isocaloric normal-protein diet (17.3% protein; NP). At embryonic day 18.5, placental and fetal liver samples from standardized uterine positions were analyzed using targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Metabolomic data were evaluated using nonparametric Wilcoxon rank-sum testing with false discovery rate reporting, unsupervised hierarchical clustering, partial least-squares discriminant analysis for visualization, and quantitative enrichment analysis. Maternal protein restriction revealed compartment-specific remodeling of fetal amino acid metabolism. LP placentas showed higher concentrations of non-essential and glucogenic amino acids, driven mainly by glutamate and aspartate, together with higher kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratios and lower tryptophan concentrations. In fetal liver, most altered amino acids were lower in LP fetuses, whereas kynurenine, 2-aminoadipic acid, and kynurenine-to-tryptophan and putrescine-to-ornithine ratios were higher. Enrichment analyses supported involvement of tryptophan metabolism, glutamate-aspartate-linked nitrogen handling, malate-aspartate shuttle activity, arginine/proline metabolism, and lysine degradation. Maternal protein restriction during gestation induced compartment-specific remodeling of placental and fetal hepatic amino acid metabolism, characterized by fundamentally different adaptive amino acid signatures despite both tissues originating from the same fetuses. These findings are consistent with altered hepato-placental amino acid cycling and nitrogen handling and provide a descriptive basis for future mechanistic studies of nutritional FGR.

articles.title: Maternal-fetal considerations of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.authors: Wang Z, Prewer G, Karunagaran K et al.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in cystic fibrosis (CF) treatment, particularly the development of CFTR modulators (CFTRm), have transformed disease management and substantially improved survival, health status, and reproductive outcomes in people with CF. In addition to lung symptoms, CF is characterised by pancreatic insufficiency, meconium ileus, and reduced fertility, leading to a shorter life expectancy. CFTRm, e.g. elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor partially restore CFTR function. Together, these treatments have markedly improved survival and quality of life for individuals with CF. As increasing numbers of women with CF conceive while taking CFTRm, understanding maternal-fetal drug exposure has become a clinical priority. Emerging evidence demonstrates that CFTRm cross the placenta and can be detected in cord blood, neonatal plasma, and infant tissues. However, the extent of fetal exposure, tissue accumulation and potential developmental implications remain incompletely understood. Herein, we emphasise the mechanistic and pharmacological evidence underlying fetal exposure to CFTRm . This review synthesises current evidence regarding the transplacental transfer, fetal exposure and developmental implications of CFTRm during pregnancy. We discuss emerging pharmacokinetic data, reported maternal and infant outcomes and key knowledge gaps that remain regarding the safety of in utero CFTRm exposure.

articles.title: Hormonal Milieu-Dependent Cervicovaginal and Mammary Gland Effects of a Long-Acting Relaxin Agonist in Female Rats: A Nonclinical Evaluation Across Investigative Studies.
articles.authors: Bhaskaran M, Vidal JD, Abernathy MM et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical and vaginal epithelial hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis were observed in a 6-month repeat-dose toxicology study in rats administered the long-acting relaxin agonist (LY), with mammary fibroadenomas noted following a 6-month off-dose period. Two investigative studies characterized these findings: a 6-month study in intact and ovariectomized (OVX) rats with interim sacrifices at 1, 3, and 6 months, and a 12-month study in intact rats. In the 6-month study, no test article-related effects occurred in OVX rats, demonstrating dependence on an intact ovarian hormonal milieu. In intact rats, cervicovaginal hyperplasia/hyperkeratosis and stromal edema with or without cervical/vaginal prolapse progressed in incidence and severity as animals entered reproductive senescence, then plateaued with no progression to neoplasia. No effect on estrous cyclicity was observed. In the 12-month study, LY increased the incidence of mammary fibroadenomas and diffuse pituitary hyperplasia. These findings were attributed to an interaction between sustained relaxin pharmacology and age-related changes in endogenous hormones during progression through reproductive senescence. Rodent reproductive senescence differs fundamentally from human menopause, and this spectrum of hormonally dependent findings is likely rodent-specific but warrants consideration in clinical risk assessment in the context of human hormonal milieu and age.

articles.title: Maternal obesity and risk of congenital heart disease in offspring: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.authors: Choi S, Kim TE, Kim YJ et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is a well-established risk factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its association with congenital heart disease (CHD) in offspring remains uncertain, particularly across different body mass index (BMI) categories and CHD subtypes. Evidence from Asian populations is limited, despite distinct BMI distributions and classification criteria. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Information Database, including 779,091 live births from 2014 to 2021. Maternal pre-pregnancy BMI was classified according to Asia-Pacific criteria. Offspring CHD was identified using ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Subtype analyses were performed for ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect (ASD), pulmonary valve stenosis, and other major CHD subtypes. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance covariates across BMI categories, and robust Poisson regression was used to estimate RRs and 95% CIs. Compared with the normal BMI group (18.5-22.9 kg/m2), adjusted RRs for CHD were 1.08 (95% CI 1.06-1.10) for overweight at risk (23.0-24.9 kg/m2), 1.13 (95% CI 1.11-1.15) for obese class I (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), and 1.37 (95% CI 1.35-1.40) for obese class II (≥30.0 kg/m2). Maternal underweight (<18.5 kg/m2) was not significantly associated with CHD risk (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-1.00). Maternal obesity was associated with a dose-dependent increase in overall CHD risk, while subtype associations were not significant after adjustment. These findings support public health strategies emphasizing weight management before conception to reduce the burden of congenital heart anomalies.

articles.title: Association of the cerebroplacental ratio with small fetal size and adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Jia X, Wang T
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is frequently complicated by fetal growth compromise. The cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) shows promise for identifying fetuses at risk, but its diagnostic performance specifically in preeclamptic pregnancies remains unclear.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 236 women with singleton preeclamptic pregnancies (January 2020-December 2023). Inclusion criteria: ISSHP-defined preeclampsia, gestational age 28-40 weeks at Doppler examination, and complete UA-PI and MCA-PI data within two weeks before delivery. The primary outcome was antenatal identification of small fetal size (estimated fetal weight <10th percentile). Multivariable logistic regression with prespecified covariates was used to assess independent associations. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis determined optimal cutoffs; bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) corrected for optimism. DeLong test compared AUCs.
RESULTS: CPR demonstrated moderate-to-good diagnostic accuracy for small fetal size (AUC 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.92; optimism-corrected AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91), higher than UA-PI (AUC 0.76, p = 0.018) and MCA-PI alone (AUC 0.75, p = 0.015). The exploratory optimal cutoff was 1.08 (sensitivity 66.0% [95% CI 55.8-75.2%], specificity 80.3%[95% CI 73.0-86.3%]). Abnormal CPR was independently associated with composite adverse outcomes (aOR 3.5, 95% CI 1.8-7.0, adjusting for baseline confounders; aOR 2.4, 95% CI 1.2-4.8, after additional adjustment for birth weight percentile and gestational age at delivery), including emergency cesarean for fetal distress (42.2% vs. 18.5%), 5-minute Apgar <7 (18.9% vs. 5.5%), and NICU admission (48.9% vs. 21.2%). CPR showed higher discrimination in early-onset versus late-onset preeclampsia (AUC 0.87 vs. 0.76), although this difference was attenuated after gestational-age adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In preeclamptic pregnancies, reduced CPR is independently associated with small fetal size and adverse perinatal outcomes, with numerically higher discrimination in early-onset disease, attenuated after gestational-age adjustment. These findings support CPR as a potential adjunctive tool for contemporaneous risk stratification in preeclampsia, particularly early-onset disease, pending prospective validation with serial measurements.

articles.title: Beyond semen analysis: a systematic review of sperm CatSper dysfunction in male infertility and a proposed framework for functional assessments.
articles.authors: Huang WR, Huang YX, Wang SY et al.
articles.abstract: A subset of infertile men presents with normal or mildly abnormal semen parameters but experiences fertilization failure, indicating defects not detected by routine semen analysis. Sperm-specific calcium channel (CatSper), a sperm-specific calcium channel essential for hyperactivation and fertilization-associated sperm function, has emerged as a relevant contributor to this form of male infertility. Therefore, we performed a systematic review to clarify the relationship between CatSper dysfunction and reproductive phenotypes. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Cochrane Library for studies published from January 01, 2001 to February 07, 2026. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria and involved pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in cation channel sperm associated 1 (CATSPER1), cation channel sperm-associated 2 (CATSPER2), cation channel sperm-associated 3 (CATSPER3), and cation channel sperm-associated auxiliary subunit epsilon (CATSPERE). The study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. The available evidence showed heterogeneous semen phenotypes, ranging from oligozoospermia and asthenozoospermia to semen parameters within reference limits, particularly in more recent CATSPER2-related cases. Where functional data were available, the affected sperm showed absent or markedly attenuated CatSper-mediated calcium ion (Ca2+) responses. In reported cases of assisted reproductive technology, conventional in vitro fertilization was frequently associated with fertilization failure, whereas intracytoplasmic sperm injection often achieved favorable fertilization outcomes and pregnancies. Based on this evidence, we propose a multilevel assessment framework integrating phenotypic screening, physiological functional assays, and genetic testing. This framework should be regarded as a translational approach, rather than a validated diagnostic pathway. Larger prospective studies are required to establish standardized protocols, reference thresholds, and clinical utility.

articles.title: Anti-HLA Alloantibody Responses in Living Donor Uterus Transplantation: A Single-center Case Series.
articles.authors: Regnath F, Löffler MW, Hammer S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Until 1 decade ago, absolute uterine infertility invariably prevented women from bearing their own biological child. A major causative factor is Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. However, uterus transplantation (UTx) has recently emerged as a successful treatment strategy, with >70 children being born to UTx recipients. This clinical situation represents a unique immunological scenario-namely the combined sensitization risk from solid organ transplantation and exposure to paternal alloantigens of the fetus.
METHODS: Given the rarity of such cases, we assessed HLA sensitization in this context using a microbead-based assay (Luminex) with HLA screening as well as single-antigen beads in 7 UTx patients.
RESULTS: We observed broad, strong IgG alloimmune responses in 3 UTx recipients, directed against both donor and paternal alloantigens. These responses primarily emerged and amplified after graft hysterectomy and withdrawal of immunosuppression, while intermittently also being evidenced before hysterectomy in 1 case. This contrasts with 4 women with transplants remaining in situ and on immunosuppressive treatment, who lack sensitization signs so far.
CONCLUSIONS: These scarce preliminary data already suggest a relevant risk of broad sensitization in this unusual setting. UTx may therefore (1) represent a unique model for studying HLA sensitization under combined physiological and nonphysiological conditions, (2) warrant informing recipients about the risk of HLA alloimmunization, and (3) require further investigation to understand the implications and long-term consequences, demanding the generation of larger datasets.

articles.title: Changes in Perinatal Management in Pregnancies With Abnormal Findings Detected on Ultrasound in the Late Second and Third Trimester.
articles.authors: Heinrich H, Demir D, Rijvers B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the indications, findings, and impact on perinatal management of referrals for advanced fetal ultrasound in the late second and third trimesters in a setting without routine third-trimester screening.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study (July 2020-November 2022), we included women referred for advanced fetal sonography after a prior normal second-trimester anomaly scan, prompted by suspected congenital anomaly, abnormal biometry, poly-/oligohydramnios, or fetal arrhythmia. The primary outcome was change in perinatal management; the secondary outcome was transfer from midwifery-led to hospital-led or tertiary care.
RESULTS: Among 1116 referrals, advanced ultrasound confirmed an abnormal finding in 65.0% (725/1116): congenital anomalies (n = 266), abnormal biometry (n = 246), poly-/oligohydramnios (n = 104), and arrhythmia (n = 109). Invasive testing was performed in 2.5% (18/725), with abnormal results in six. Follow-up data were available for 96.6% (700/725), with a live birth rate of 95.0% (689/725). In total 43.9% (318/725) received perinatal follow-up, of which 20.0% (145/725) was induced for the anomaly. Hospital-led care rose from 38.9% to 69.4% after confirmation of abnormal findings.
CONCLUSION: Despite the absence of routine third-trimester ultrasound, abnormal late-pregnancy findings frequently alter perinatal management. These findings support offering all women a third-trimester scan that includes a standardized assessment of key anatomical structures to improve diagnostic consistency and equity of care.

articles.title: Cell-free DNA-guided detection, surveillance, and therapeutic adaptation for breast cancer.
articles.authors: Li C, Chow TW, Tey SK et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) analysis provides a minimally invasive approach to breast cancer assessment across early detection, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and treatment adaptation in advanced disease. This review evaluates these applications by distinguishing analytical validity, clinical detection performance, prognostic validity, and clinical utility. In early detection, assays integrating genomic, epigenomic, fragmentomic, and protein-based features have shown encouraging performance in evaluated cohorts; however, sensitivity remains limited in low-burden disease, particularly stage I breast cancer. Their potential clinical role depends on the incremental information they provide beyond established imaging and diagnostic pathways. In the curative-intent setting, circulating tumor DNA detection after treatment is associated with recurrence risk and can precede clinical or radiographic relapse, supporting prognostic stratification and the design of MRD-guided intervention trials. Whether such interventions improve clinical outcomes remains a central unresolved question. In advanced breast cancer, plasma genotyping supports treatment selection in defined molecular contexts. Randomized trials of ESR1 mutation-guided endocrine switching have demonstrated progression-free survival benefits with specific treatment strategies, providing evidence beyond biomarker-outcome associations, although overall survival benefit remains to be established. Across applications, interpretation depends on assay characteristics, molecular input, disease setting, sampling schedule, and the clinical decision being evaluated. Future studies should connect assay performance to patient benefit through comparison with existing care, clinically meaningful endpoints, and assessment of treatment burden and downstream investigations. This approach will help define where cfDNA testing can contribute meaningfully to breast cancer management.

articles.title: Experiences of parents during their intrauterine or perinatal child loss - a qualitative narrative interview study.
articles.authors: Bauernfeind L, Nuber-Fischer D, Sterr F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the psychological consequences of intrauterine or perinatal child loss have been extensively studied, little is known about how parents experience the immediate period from the first suspicion of pathological alterations through pregnancy to birth. A deeper understanding of these experiences is essential for developing evidence-based recommendations for healthcare professionals.
AIM: To explore and organize parents' experience of child loss during pregnancy or at birth.
METHODS: This qualitative study represents the second phase of an exploratory, sequential, participatory mixed-methods project aimed at developing recommendations for healthcare professionals caring for families following intrauterine or perinatal loss. Twelve parents (nine mothers and three fathers) participated in nine narrative interviews in 2025. Data were analyzed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis according to Braun and Clarke within a phenomenological framework.
FINDINGS: Parents´ experiences were organized into two interwoven dimensions. The first dimension describes a chronological trajectory comprising five themes: living in suspended uncertainty, the collapse of normality, carrying the burden of decision-making, being held or dropped by the system, and becoming parents under impossible circumstances. The second dimension consists of four overarching themes accompanying the entire experience: contextual factors of child loss, preparing and adjusting, need time to process and grieve, and experiencing an inner conflict. Together, these dimensions demonstrate that parents´ experiences extend far beyond the moment of diagnosis or birth and evolve through continuously changing emotional, relational, and organizational demands.
CONCLUSION: Parents experience intrauterine or perinatal child loss as a dynamic process rather than a single event. Their experiences are shaped by both phase-specific challenges and overarching processes that persist throughout the trajectory loss. Healthcare professionals should therefore provide continuous, individualized, and coordinated support across all stages of care. The conceptual model developed in this study offers a foundation for developing evidence-based recommendations to improve compassionate and family-centered care following intrauterine or perinatal child loss.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered in the National Library of Medicine on January 13th, 2025 with the unique ClinicalTrials.gov…

articles.title: Determinants of breast and cervical cancer screening uptake among women in Zambia: analysis of the 2024 Zambia demographic and health survey.
articles.authors: Shumba S, Hachisaala M, Nkumbwa D et al.
articles.abstract: Breast and cervical cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women globally, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The World Health Organization (WHO) has prioritised both cancers through the Global Breast Cancer Initiative and the global cervical cancer elimination strategy, which targets 70% screening coverage using high-performance tests among women aged 35 and 45 years. Despite Zambia's expansion of cervical cancer prevention services, little is known about the population-level uptake of breast and cervical cancer screening and the sociodemographic factors that drive it. This study assessed the determinants of breast and cervical cancer screening uptake among women aged 15-49 years using data from the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS).We categorised the women into four mutually exclusive groups: no screening, breast-only screening, cervical-only screening, and breast and cervical screening. Survey weights were applied to account for the complex sampling design of the survey. Associations were examined using survey-adjusted multinomial logistic regression. All analyses were conducted using Stata 14.2.Among the 13,876 women included in the analysis, 68.84% reported no cancer screening, 4.67% reported breast-only screening, 17.87% reported cervical-only screening, and 8.63% reported both breast and cervical screening. Screening uptake increased with age but remained below recommended targets even among priority age groups: 43.8% of women aged 35-39 years and 51.3% of women aged 45-49 years reported any cervical cancer screening (cervical-only or combined). In multivariable adjusted analyses, these patterns were largely confirmed. Women aged 45-49 years were significantly more likely to undergo cervical-only screening (RRR 9.64; 95% CI 6.66-13.96) and combined screening (RRR 12.01; 95% CI 7.35-19.63) compared with adolescents aged 15-19 years. For breast-only screening, older age (35-44 years) and higher parity were the principal significant determinants, with women of parity 6 or more nearly twice as likely to report breast-only screening compared with nulliparous women (RRR 2.22; 95% CI 1.25-3.93). Higher education was associated with increased cervical-only (RRR 1.36; 95% CI 1.03-1.79) and combined screening (RRR 1.43; 95% CI 1.03-2.00). In contrast, rural residence was associated with lower cervical-only screening uptake (RRR 0.76; 95% CI 0.63-0.93), and high community poverty was…

articles.title: Dynamic machine learning for time-updated prediction of death within the next 24 hours in critically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction.
articles.authors: Nong J, Ban Y, Tang Z et al.
articles.abstract: Critically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) may deteriorate rapidly, yet most existing prognostic tools rely on static admission information and do not update risk as clinical status evolves. We developed and externally validated a dynamic landmark-based machine-learning model to predict in-hospital death within the next 24 hours during ICU stay. Adult ICU stays with AMI were identified in eICU-CRD for model development and internal validation and in MIMIC-IV for external validation. Repeated 6-hour landmarks were generated, and a dynamic LightGBM model was compared with dynamic penalized logistic regression, static first-window LightGBM, dynamic SOFA, an AMI nomogram, APS III/APACHE III, and OASIS. Internal validation included 109,675 eligible landmarks from 10,613 ICU stays; external validation included 52,946 landmarks from 4,505 ICU stays. Dynamic LightGBM achieved the best internal performance (AUROC 0.892, AUPRC 0.231, Brier score 0.0142) and remained the strongest model externally (AUROC 0.868, AUPRC 0.215, Brier score 0.0182). External recalibration improved calibration while preserving discrimination. Decision-curve analysis showed the highest net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds, and the model provided earlier warning with the lowest alert burden (28.4 alerts per 100 patient-days). Performance remained stable across prespecified high-acuity subgroups and sensitivity analyses. These findings support dynamic landmark-based machine learning as a practical framework for short-term mortality monitoring in critically ill patients with AMI.

articles.title: Real-World Risk of Venous Thromboembolism with Bevacizumab Biosimilar versus Reference Biologic in Japanese Patients with Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Ooba N, Sakai R, Sekine K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Large-scale safety data for newly introduced bevacizumab biosimilars in routine oncology practice remain limited. As part of post-marketing safety evaluations under the Risk Management Plan in Japan, we evaluated the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) associated with a bevacizumab biosimilar (CTNK) and compared the findings with those for a reference biologic (Avastin®) in Japanese patients with cancer.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study using a large-scale hospital-based claims database (Medical Data Vision) in Japan, we identified new users of bevacizumab diagnosed with colorectal, breast, or ovarian cancer or glioblastoma between November 2020 and February 2025. Patients were classified into the biosimilar group or the reference biologic group. The primary outcome was the incidence of VTE, evaluated using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Exploratory safety outcomes, including bleeding/hemorrhage and infections, were also assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 8599 eligible patients (1967 in the biosimilar group and 6632 in the reference biologic group; male versus female patients, 45.60% and 41.74% versus 54.40% and 58.26%, respectively; median age, 69.0 years in both groups) were included in the primary analysis. The overall incidence of VTE was 2.36%. The adjusted hazard ratio for VTE in the biosimilar group compared with that in the reference biologic group was 0.82 (95% confidence interval, 0.57-1.19; P = 0.30), indicating no significant difference. This finding was consistent across subgroups stratified by target cancer type or by VTE history. Furthermore, the incidence of exploratory safety events was comparable between the two treatment groups.
CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective cohort study showed no evidence of increased VTE risk with the bevacizumab biosimilar or major safety differences between the bevacizumab biosimilar and the reference biologic in Japanese patients with cancer, providing reassuring real-world evidence supporting the safe use of the bevacizumab biosimilar in routine clinical practice. Graphical abstract available for this article.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials identifier, jRCT2031250738, retrospectively registered on February 13, 2026.

articles.title: Long-Term Postpartum Dyspareunia and Sexual Dysfunction After Childbirth.
articles.authors: Zulfikaroglu E, Zulfikaroglu B
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postpartum sexual dysfunction is common, but long-term outcomes beyond the early puerperium remain insufficiently integrated into routine postpartum and gynecologic care.
OBJECTIVE: The objective was to systematically review dyspareunia and sexual dysfunction beyond 6 months postpartum, including associated factors and rehabilitation interventions.
STUDY DESIGN: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL from inception to January 31, 2026. Eligible primary studies included postpartum women with at least 1 relevant sexual outcome assessed at or beyond 6 months after childbirth. Prevalence and associated-factor findings were synthesized descriptively. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to randomized rehabilitation trials reporting validated sexual-function outcomes at eligible postpartum time points with extractable numerical data.
RESULTS: Twenty-two eligible reports representing 21 unique studies or cohorts were included; 2 randomized rehabilitation studies contributed to quantitative synthesis. Dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remained clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum, with incomplete recovery persisting in a substantial subset of women. Persistent morbidity was most consistently associated with severe perineal trauma, including obstetric anal sphincter injury; associations with operative delivery were less consistent. Breastfeeding-related symptoms, depressive symptoms, pelvic floor morbidity, and genital or body image concerns were also reported. The pooled rehabilitation estimate favored intervention but was imprecise and highly heterogeneous (standardized mean difference: 1.19; 95% CI, -0.18 to 2.57; I²=91.7%), with very-low-certainty evidence.
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remain clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum and warrant proactive assessment within routine postpartum and gynecologic follow-up, with multidisciplinary management and referral for pelvic floor rehabilitation or urogynecologic evaluation when indicated.

articles.title: Optimizing IUI: evidence-based guidance for use of add-ons and variations in IUI treatment, a British Fertility Society policy and practice guideline.
articles.authors: Chronopoulou E, Shaikh S, Raperport C et al.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine insemination (IUI) is a widely used fertility treatment with numerous add-ons and protocol variations, many of which are offered empirically. This guideline systematically reviews the available evidence to provide evidence-based recommendations for their clinical use, aiming to optimise treatment outcomes, standardise practice and facilitate future research. A total of 25 interventions were evaluated, including follicular monitoring, LH surge detection, catheter type, bladder filling, insemination technique, operator experience, cervical mucus aspiration, endometrial scratching, hydrotubation, ovarian stimulation, ovulation triggering and timing, intrauterine infusions, medications affecting endometrial receptivity or uterine contractility, double insemination, ultrasound guidance, bed rest and luteal phase support. A systematic literature search identified 154 randomised controlled trials involving 34,825 participants. Meta-analyses were conducted where feasible. However, the limited availability of adequately powered trials and the predominantly low-quality evidence restrict the certainty of most recommendations. These limitations should be clearly communicated during patient counselling. Future research should prioritise high-quality trials evaluating the effectiveness of IUI add-ons in specific patient populations, considering underlying infertility diagnoses.

articles.title: Food Environments, Structural Disadvantage, and Risk of Gestational Diabetes and Preeclampsia.
articles.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
articles.authors: Amoah AA, Wychgram C, Curriero FC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preeclampsia, conditions that elevate maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Lifestyle interventions are standard preconception recommendations for risk reduction, yet their feasibility is shaped by neighborhood and structural contexts. To explore these relationships, we evaluated associations of GDM and preeclampsia with neighborhood food environments, access to vendors authorized to accept benefits from the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), and racialized economic segregation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from individuals with live births (N = 12,635) at three Maryland hospitals (2016-2021). Neighborhood exposures included the following: 1) food swamps-areas with a high density of unhealthy food retailers relative to healthy ones-measured using the modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI); 2) racialized economic segregation, measured using the Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE); and 3) WIC vendor density per 1,000 residents. All exposures were modeled in tertiles, with the lowest tertile (Q1) indicating the most disadvantaged or lowest access and the highest (Q3) as reference. We used multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations to assess associations with GDM and preeclampsia.
RESULTS: Lower WIC access (lowest vs. highest tertile: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.02, 1.41]) and greater neighborhood disadvantage (ICE Q1 vs. Q3: aOR, 1.21; 95% CI [1.01, 1.44]) were associated with higher odds of GDM. No neighborhood measures were consistently associated with preeclampsia.
CONCLUSION: Structural disadvantage and lower WIC vendor density were associated with higher odds of GDM but not preeclampsia. Expanding nutrition assistance infrastructure and addressing neighborhood disadvantage may improve maternal cardiometabolic health.

articles.title: First trimester cervical length and cervical change in the prediction of prematurity related outcomes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Souka AP, Rouvali A, Antsaklis P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvaginal cervical length (CL) measurement in the second trimester is an established screening tool for identifying pregnant individuals at risk of spontaneous preterm birth, but the clinical value of the first trimester cervical length (CL) remains controversial. As the majority of the studies focus on a single time-point measurement, less is known about the prognostic value of the change in CL between the first and the second trimester in predicting prematurity.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate first trimester CL as well as the change in CL between the first and the second trimester as predictors of late miscarriage, cervical shortening at anytime before 32 weeks, cerclage insertion and spontaneous preterm delivery (SPD).
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective study included 6,116 singleton pregnancies with transvaginal cervical evaluation at 11-14 weeks and/or at 18-24 weeks and documented pregnancy outcomes. Outcomes assessed were late miscarriage at 16-24 weeks, cervical shortening (≤15 mm and ≤25 mm) before 32 weeks, placement of cervical cerclage, spontaneous preterm delivery before 28 weeks (SPD 28), before 32 weeks (SPD 32) and before 37 weeks (SPD 37), and a combined adverse outcome (CAO) including all the above. Prognostic accuracy was assessed using multivariate logistic regression and ROC curve analysis, adjusting for maternal characteristics and obstetric history.
RESULTS: First-trimester CL was significantly associated with late miscarriage (p=0.049), SPD 37 (p<0.014), cervical shortening (p<0.01), cerclage placement (p<0.01), and CAO (p<0.01). The risk increased nonlinearly, with a marked rise below 30 mm. For each 1 mm of decrease in first-trimester CL, the risk of CAO increased by 26%. Overall, mean CL change between first and second trimesters was minimal (-1.7%); however, pregnant individuals with CAO exhibited a significantly steeper decline compared to the ones without CAO (-9.4% vs -0.03%, p<0.001). The combination of second-trimester CL and CL change outperformed single-timepoint measurements in predicting late miscarriage (p=0.015) and cervical shortening (p<0,001).
CONCLUSIONS: Shorter first-trimester CL and pronounced cervical shortening between the first and second trimester are significantly associated with a spectrum of the adverse pregnancy outcomes related to prematurity.

articles.title: Endometrial fertility. Management of adenomyosis in gynecology and infertility.
articles.authors: Somigliana E, Fornelli G, Benaglia L et al.
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis has long been underrecognized, with limited evidence guiding its clinical management. In the last decade, the introduction of the Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria and the growing recognition of its strong association with endometriosis have substantially changed the understanding of the disease. In women seeking pregnancy, treatment options remain challenging. Surgery is invasive, technically demanding, and associated with recurrence and potential obstetric risks, while hormonal therapies are incompatible with conception and have not demonstrated a benefit for infertility. IVF may overcome some adverse effects of adenomyosis on fertility, but its impact on embryo implantation remains problematic. Accordingly, available evidence suggests a possible reduction in live birth rates following IVF. However, current studies are limited by potential confounders. Studies investigating the use of medical pretreatment before IVF, including GnRH agonists, dienogest, or levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine systems, remain insufficient and inconsistent. Further prospective studies and randomized controlled trials using standardized inclusion criteria are needed.

articles.title: Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 4/6 Inhibitors in Non-Breast Malignancies.
articles.authors: Ghidini A, Garassino, Bukovec R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitors established a major role in breast cancer, but activity across other malignancies varies substantially. This structured narrative review asks whether apparently similar cell-cycle alterations confer clinically meaningful dependence and contrasts controlled with signal-finding evidence.
METHODS: In this structured narrative review we synthesized prospective non-breast CDK4/6-inhibitor studies represented in the authors' existing literature collection and expanded extraction table, prioritizing randomized comparisons, histology, biomarker strategy, clinical benefit, survival maturity, and toxicity. Published 2026 trial reports and meeting results were selectively verified.
RESULTS: The most compelling randomized signal is in dedifferentiated liposarcoma: SARC041 (108 randomized patients) improved median progression-free survival (PFS; 9.67 vs 1.52 months; HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.25-0.59), whereas overall survival (OS) remains inconclusive (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.28-1.07), with crossover complicating interpretation. Endocrine combinations show encouraging phase II results in low-grade serous ovarian and estrogen receptor-positive endometrial cancers. Negative randomized and alteration-selected basket studies caution against extrapolating from isolated pathway lesions. Emerging clinical activity with other inhibitors, including dalpiciclib, requires controlled confirmation.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical development beyond breast cancer should be organized by lineage-specific dependence, demonstrable RB-axis function, rational combination partners, and endpoints suited to cytostatic treatment. Evidence strength, competing options, and toxicity must determine whether a promising signal warrants practice change.
