Recent advances have focused on the use of novel drug delivery systems (NDDS) for mechanism-based targeted therapeutics, including nanoparticles, liposomes, hydrogels, vaginal delivery and stimuli-responsive delivery vectors designed to exploit specific biochemical pathways and morphological features of uterine fibroids. NDDS are being investigated for the targeted administration of hormone modulators, TGF-β inhibitors, ECM-targeting agents, anti-angiogenic agents and genetic therapy (siRNA/miRNA) to fibroid tissue, with the aim of reducing systemic toxicity and improving treatment success. However, the evidence is largely preclinical (cell and animal models), and this review critically appraises the strengths, limitations and stage of development of each strategy. The translation of these advanced medicines into clinical practice is challenged by fibroid heterogeneity, possible immunogenicity and toxicity of nanomaterials, manufacturing difficulty, and regulatory constraints. However, future strategies are based on individualized nanomedicine, AI-driven drug discovery and multi-target combo therapy to increase effectiveness, limit recurrence, and maintain fertility. In summary, mechanism-based targeted drug delivery is a promising but still largely preclinical strategy for uterine fibroids. By linking molecular pathology with delivery technology, it may enable more precise and patient-centred therapies, but this potential must be confirmed in clinically relevant models and clinical trials.

articles.title: Bruceine D induces ferroptosis in ectocervical Ect1/E6E7 cells by modulating GSTP1 and MAPK14 signaling and downregulating GPX4.
articles.authors: Han M, Lian S, Zhu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical cancer. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated malignancies. Bruceine D (BD), a bioactive quassinoid isolated from Brucea javanica, exhibits antitumor and antiviral activities. However, its effects on HPV-associated cervical epithelial cells remain unclear.
METHODS: The effects of BD on HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized ectocervical epithelial cells (Ect1/E6E7) were evaluated using cell viability, colony formation, EdU incorporation, and cell-cycle assays. Ferroptosis-associated changes were assessed by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, and the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. Pharmacological rescue experiments using ferroptosis inhibitors and pathway inhibitors were performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation were used to identify candidate regulatory targets.
RESULTS: BD significantly inhibited Ect1/E6E7 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest in a concentration-dependent manner. BD treatment increased lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, depleted intracellular GSH, disrupted mitochondrial function, and downregulated GPX4. Ferroptosis inhibitors partially reversed BD-induced cell death, supporting the involvement of ferroptosis. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation implicated GSTP1 and MAPK14 in the cellular response to BD. Pharmacological inhibition of MAPK14 attenuated BD-induced ferroptotic responses, suggesting a role for GSTP1/MAPK14-associated signaling. BD also exhibited synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with the ferroptosis inducer erastin.
CONCLUSION: BD reduces the survival of HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized cervical epithelial cells by inducing ferroptosis associated with GPX4 downregulation and GSTP1/MAPK14 signaling. These findings support further preclinical investigation of BD and ferroptosis-based approaches in HPV-associated cervical disease.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy and child internalising and externalising problems over time.
articles.authors: Keestra SM, Molenaar ACM, de Rooij SR et al.
articles.abstract: Adequate gestational thyroid function is important for offspring neurodevelopment, yet behavioural implications of variation within the normal range are unclear. We examined associations with externalising and internalising problems across repeated assessments in childhood and adolescence. 2,606 mother-child dyads from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) cohort with maternal free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) measurements in the first half of pregnancy and at least one child SDQ assessment. Primary analysis excluded women with overt thyroid disease or thyroid medication use and children born < 32 weeks or < 1500 g. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) scores at 5-6, 11-12 and 15-16 years, via mother-, teacher-, and self-report. Secondary analyses included logistic regression for borderline SDQ cut-offs, sex interactions, and effect modification by TSH. FT4 showed a U-shaped association with teacher-reported externalising problems (quadratic β = 9.49, FDR-adjusted p = 0.03), with higher scores at both low and high FT4. Higher FT4 was associated with lower child-reported internalising problems (β = -0.17, FDR-adjusted p = 0.04). For both primary associations, there was no evidence of FT4-by-age interaction, suggesting differences in problem levels rather than thyroid-related differences in symptom change over time. At age 5-6, FT4 showed a non-linear association with teacher-reported hyperactivity/inattention above the threshold, with a negative linear term (OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.97) and a positive quadratic term (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.20). At age 11-12, higher FT4 was associated with fewer self-reported peer problems (OR = 0.84, 95% CI:0.71-0.99). In exploratory analyses, curvature of the FT4-externalising association varied by maternal TSH; no sex modification was detected. Within a cohort free of overt thyroid disease, maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy was associated with domain- and rater-specific differences in child internalising and externalising problems. We found no evidence that these associations changed across the available repeated assessments, suggesting differences in average problem scores rather than differences in how symptoms changed with age.

articles.title: Persistent bowel dysfunction and health-related quality of life after surgery for Hirschsprung disease: generic versus disease-specific outcomes and measurement heterogeneity in children and adolescents.
articles.authors: Fatima R
articles.abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a condition that can implant intestinal continuity surgically although technical success does not necessarily correlate with its age-specific bowel functionality. This critical narrative review addresses the association of persistent postoperative bowel dysfunction and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) with specific emphasis on discordance between generic and disease-specific measures, and on heterogeneity in the outcome measures. The literature review was updated: June 20 to July 15, 2026(PubMed), Web of science, Google Scholar, and NCBI Bookshelf. Twenty-five records were filtered and 19 sources published since 1998 constituted the main evidence base of outcomes; all sources were categorized according to evidence level and population and mixed HD/anorectal-malformation (ARM) evidence was classified as indirect. Reported constipation and fecal incontinence/soiling do not represent consistent reliable prevalence studies and vary greatly among the studies because of age, follow-up, operative method, definitions, questionnaire, type of respondent and bowel-management practice. The chronic obstructive symptoms need an assessment of mechanical or histopathologic errors that can be corrected prior to the intensification of bowel management. No statistically significant difference in generic HRQoL at the group level was shown between healthy comparison and available evidence, though results indicated a great degree of heterogeneity, precluding a general interpretation; disease-specific instruments and symptom-stratified analyses showed evidence of statistically important impairment in a sub-group with chronic dysfunction. Parent- proxy and child self-reports are not interchangeable but rather give complementary views. A standardized follow-up ought to thus combine effective bowel-function evaluation, generic and disease-specific HRQoL questionnaires, in addition to child plus parent reports.

articles.title: Cardiac Function Profiling of Preeclamptic Patients by Impedance Cardiography.
articles.authors: Belk SS, Novotny S, Amin G et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is associated with cardiac dysfunction during pregnancy and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Although thoracic fluid content (TFC) is increased in preeclampsia, its relationship to cardiac performance remains unclear. This study used impedance cardiography to characterize maternal hemodynamics and to evaluate the associations among TFC, cardiac performance, and disease severity. A retrospective analysis included 645 pregnant women, comprising 128 normotensive controls, 170 women with moderate preeclampsia, and 347 with severe preeclampsia. Thoracic fluid content increased progressively across preeclampsia severity groups. Stroke volume index and cardiac index were lower, while systemic vascular resistance index was higher, primarily in women with severe preeclampsia. Correlation analysis demonstrated an inverse association between stroke volume index and systemic vascular resistance index, whereas associations between thoracic fluid content and other hemodynamic measures were comparatively weak. These findings suggest that increased thoracic fluid content in preeclampsia is not strongly explained by variations in systemic vascular resistance or indexed cardiac output and stroke volume alone.

articles.title: Association Between Pelvic Floor Electrophysiological Integrity and Sacral Neuromodulation Outcomes in Patients With Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury.
articles.authors: Chang R, Guo W, Liao L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To examine the association between preoperative pelvic floor neurophysiological findings and Stage II sacral neuromodulation (SNM) conversion in patients with incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI) and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 74 patients with incomplete SCI who underwent an SNM test phase between 2020 and 2024. A positive test response was defined as a ≥ 50% improvement in the predominant LUTS measure recorded in a 72-h voiding diary. Preoperative testing included somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP), sacral reflex (SR), and pudendal nerve (PN) function. Because absent evoked responses were common, each pathway was classified as intact or non-intact according to institutional laboratory reference ranges. Associations with Stage II conversion were assessed using logistic regression and Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, injury level, AIS grade, and LUTS duration.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight of 74 patients (51.4%) underwent Stage II implantation. In the overall cohort, intact SR and PN function were associated with a higher likelihood of conversion and remained significant after multivariable adjustment (SR: adjusted OR: 4.47, 95% CI: 1.46-16.46; p = 0.008; PN: adjusted OR: 3.52, 95% CI: 1.25-10.62; p = 0.017). In subgroup analyses, SR was associated with conversion in patients with overactive bladder and PN in those with detrusor underactivity on univariable analysis, but neither association remained statistically significant after adjustment. SEP was not associated with Stage II conversion. SR integrity was also more strongly associated with the overactive bladder phenotype than with detrusor underactivity (adjusted OR: for DU: 0.21, 95% CI: 0.06-0.66; p = 0.007).
CONCLUSION: Preserved SR and PN function were associated with Stage II SNM conversion in the overall cohort. The subgroup findings for overactive bladder and detrusor underactivity were less robust after adjustment and should be interpreted cautiously. Pelvic floor neurophysiological testing may provide additional information for preoperative assessment, although prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Prefrontal hemodynamic fluctuations and functional connectivity during propofol and sevoflurane anesthesia: A functional near-infrared spectroscopy study.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Chen M, Liang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measures cortical hemodynamics, yet its ability to characterize anesthesia-related functional changes remains unclear.
METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis used prospectively collected data from 120 female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under propofol or sevoflurane anesthesia (60 per group). Twenty-channel prefrontal fNIRS recordings covered wakefulness, induction, and maintenance. Deoxygenated hemoglobin-derived amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), functional connectivity (FC), network topology, and within- and cross-state FC similarity were assessed. Support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest classifiers assessed discrimination between states.
RESULTS: During induction, ALFF increased by 89.8% to 202.2% with propofol and 75.2% to 242.0% with sevoflurane across five prefrontal regions (all P < 0.001). During maintenance, mean ALFF was below awake levels, with significant reductions of 20.0% to 40.1% in three regions under sevoflurane (all P ≤ 0.019). Induction-related FC changes were limited and regionally heterogeneous. Regional FC, modularity, and global efficiency showed no significant maintenance-versus-awake differences in either group. Within-state between-subject FC similarity was significantly higher during maintenance than during wakefulness only with sevoflurane (mean difference [MD], 0.110; 95% CI, 0.054 to 0.169; P < 0.001). Cross-state between-subject FC similarity was higher for awake-maintenance than awake-induction comparisons with propofol (MD, 0.072; 95% CI, 0.055 to 0.090) and sevoflurane (MD, 0.144; 95% CI, 0.126 to 0.161; both P < 0.001). Support vector machine classification of induction versus wakefulness yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.75 to 0.90) for propofol and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91) for sevoflurane; maintenance-versus-awake AUCs were 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58 to 0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.68 to 0.85).
CONCLUSIONS: Prefrontal fNIRS detected widespread induction-related hemodynamic changes, but the present connectivity measures provided limited discrimination between maintenance of anesthesia and wakefulness.

articles.title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
articles.authors: Gong C, Tao X, Tian D
articles.abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development. After birth, rapid microbial colonization occurs in the intestine and lungs. Through signaling molecules including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, and bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs), coupled with vagal nerve and mucosal immune pathways, the microbiota maintains intestinal and pulmonary immune homeostasis, preserves blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and modulates microglial activation, thereby regulating neurogenesis, synaptic pruning, and brain functional programming. Early-life dysbiosis is commonly associated with preterm birth, cesarean delivery, infection, and antibiotic exposure. In human observational studies, it accompanies disrupted organ homeostasis and neuroinflammatory signatures, and is linked to an increased long-term risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability; in neonatal animal models, it aggravates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and encephalopathy of prematurity. Because dysbiosis frequently co-occurs with prematurity, infection, and other confounders, these associations do not by themselves establish causality. This review summarizes early-life colonization patterns of intestinal and pulmonary microbiota and their underlying neuroimmune mechanisms, analyzes the impacts of dysbiosis on neuroimmunity and related diseases, and proposes intervention strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for neonatal health protection and neurodevelopmental disorder prevention.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Association of Estrone-Estradiol Balance With B-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Older Adults With Heart Failure.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.authors: Nakamura S, Numata G, Tokiwa H et al.
articles.abstract: Estrone (E1), the predominant circulating estrogen after menopause, may exert biological effects distinct from, and potentially opposite to, those of estradiol (E2), raising the possibility that the relative E1/E2 balance has physiological significance. However, the clinical significance of the E1/E2 balance in heart failure (HF) remains unknown. We investigated the associations of circulating E1, E2, and their balance with B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) by sex. We analyzed a multicenter cross-sectional cohort of 260 adults aged 60-89 years (102 men and 68 women with HF; 49 men and 41 women without HF). Associations with ln(BNP) were evaluated using multivariable models with sex interactions. E1 and E2 were analyzed separately and jointly, and the joint model was reparameterized into the E1/E2 balance [ln(E1/E2)] and overall estrogen level [ln√(E1×E2)]. Neither E1 nor E2 was significantly associated with ln(BNP) in separate models. However, in joint models, E1 and E2 showed opposite associations after mutual adjustment, which were reversed between sexes. The E1/E2 balance was positively associated with ln(BNP) in men (β=0.828; P=0.003) but negatively associated in women (β=-0.961; P=0.010) (sex interaction P<0.001). In contrast, overall estrogen level was not associated with ln(BNP) in either sex. Among participants without HF, no sex-dependent pattern was observed, and the balance-by-sex association differed according to HF status (three-way interaction P=0.010). These findings suggest that the E1/E2 balance, rather than overall estrogen level, is a sex-specific hormonal correlate of BNP in older adults with HF.

articles.title: All About the Meds: Contraception, Infertility, and Immunosuppression in Reproductive-aged Female Transplant Recipients.
articles.authors: Katz-Greenberg G, Rossi AP, Afshar Y et al.
articles.abstract: The number of reproductive-aged solid organ transplant recipients continues to rise, underscoring the need for comprehensive reproductive health counseling that spans throughout the transplant continuum. Fertility is often impaired in end-stage organ disease but often resumes within months after transplantation, which may cause unintended pregnancy during a period of heightened maternal, fetal, and allograft vulnerability. This review synthesizes the evidence and expert consensus from the American Society of Transplantation Women's Health Community of Practice Controversies Conference on contraception, infertility, and immunosuppression in reproductive-aged female transplant recipients. Recommendations are largely US-based, although reference to international variability is noted, where relevant. We outline contraceptive options with attention to efficacy and safety in transplant recipients. Data on infertility and assisted reproductive technologies in solid organ transplant recipients remain limited, although emerging evidence supports the feasibility and safety of ovulation induction, in vitro fertilization, and single-embryo transfer with careful monitoring for complications such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Immunosuppressive regimens require individualized adjustment before, during, and after pregnancy: calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids, and azathioprine are generally considered safe, whereas mycophenolate is strictly contraindicated due to teratogenicity; the safety of mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors and belatacept remains incompletely defined. Lactation is supported with most immunosuppressants, although caution is warranted with mycophenolate and mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors. Ultimately, preconception counseling, shared decision-making, and coordination amongst transplant, maternal-fetal medicine, and reproductive endocrinology specialists are essential to optimize outcomes for recipients, grafts, and infants. Closing persistent knowledge gaps and enhancing access to reproductive care should remain a research and policy priority in transplant medicine.

articles.title: Early Detection of Ovarian Cancer: Current Strategies and Future Directions.
articles.authors: Zhang N, Zhuang D, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, mainly because most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Although early detection is essential for improving clinical outcomes, accurate and accessible screening remains a major challenge, owing to the non-specific nature of early symptoms, the pronounced histological and molecular heterogeneity of the disease, and the poor performance of conventional screening approaches based on cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) and imaging modalities. This review outlines the major biological and technical challenges in the early diagnosis of OC, briefly summarizes the value and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches and focuses on current progress in emerging biomarkers, including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)/cell-free DNA (cfDNA) alterations, exosomal biomarkers and mesothelin multi-marker combined detection strategies, and novel technologies, such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, single-cell sequencing and biosensors for early detection. We also discuss the advantages, current limitations, practical considerations and translational barriers of these approaches. Future advances in OC screening will require the integration of sensitive biomarkers, multimodal detection strategies and more accessible, cost-effective technologies to improve early diagnosis and patient survival.

articles.title: Role of Transvaginal Three-dimensional Power Doppler Ultrasound and Hysteroscopy in Postmenopausal Bleeding.
articles.authors: Sharma V, Meena J, Singhal S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) is a warning symptom and is associated with endometrial malignancy in 10%-15% of cases. Endometrial thickness (ET) measurement using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) guides the course of action, with ET >4 mm being ominous. Three-dimensional power Doppler (3DPD) ultrasound raises diagnostic utility with endometrial volume (EV) and vascularity indices-vascularization index (VI), flow Index (FI) and vascularization FI (VFI), while hysteroscopy provides a direct view of uterine lesions. Previous studies have worked on role of 3DPD or hysteroscopy in PMB patients, but none have compared these two. Hence, this study was conducted.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary center, including 75 women with PMB. They underwent 3DPD ultrasound followed by hysteroscopy and endometrial biopsy. The diagnostic accuracy of Doppler parameters was analyzed using receiver operating characteristic curves. Hysteroscopic results were compared with histopathology, followed by comparison of 3DPD and hysteroscopy.
RESULTS: Out of 75 patients, 65 (86.6%) had benign pathologies and 10 (13.4%) had malignancies. 3DPD parameters VI, VFI, and EV were significantly higher in the malignant group. EV had the highest diagnostic performance, with an area under curve (AUC) of 0.88 (cutoff ≥7.34 cm3), yielding 80% sensitivity and 80% specificity. VI, FI, and VFI achieved sensitivity/specificity of 80%/78.5%, 70%/70.8%, and 80%/73.8%, with AUCs of 0.83, 0.69, and 0.82, respectively. Hysteroscopy demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for detecting endometrial malignancy and endometrial polyps. Cohen's kappa analysis of hysteroscopy and 3DPD showed agreement of 78.67%, 70.67%, 78.67%, and 80% between hysteroscopy and VI, FI, VFI and EV, respectively.
CONCLUSION: 3DPD, particularly EV, is a valuable noninvasive tool in PMB. Hysteroscopy remains a highly sensitive and specific modality for detecting malignancy, showing good correlation with 3DPD.

articles.title: ORIHIME® Mesh Size Adjustment Can Improve Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Prevent Complications Such as Prolapse Recurrence in Patients Undergoing Transvaginal Mesh Surgery.
articles.authors: Kuroda K, Hamamoto K, Kawamura K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP), a multifactorial condition defined as the descent of the pelvic organs through the vaginal wall, often correlates with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). Transvaginal mesh (TVM) surgery has a significant impact on LUTS; however, its therapeutic effects may vary depending on the type and shape of the mesh used. This study investigated the effects of mesh type used on LUTS and other surgical outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 169 patients with POP who underwent TVM at our hospital. Preoperative and postoperative parameters were evaluated for the following patient groups: the Polyform™ group; those in the ORIHIME® group treated without adjustment of mesh size (AMS) beneath the bladder, with or without wide arms, designated as AMS (-), and those in the ORIHIME® group treated with AMS beneath the bladder with wide arms, designated as AMS (+).
RESULTS: Post-void residual urine volume, International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), Quality of Life (QOL) scores, the Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS), and International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire Short-Form score significantly decreased after surgery compared with the preoperative condition in all groups. However, the 60-min pad weight test showed a significant change after surgery only in the AMS (+) group. Upon comparing the preoperative and 1-year postoperative outcomes, the AMS (+) group showed significantly better outcomes in the IPSS plus QOL scores, OABSS, and the rate of prolapse recurrence than the AMS (-) and/or Polyform™ groups.
CONCLUSION: AMS beneath the bladder can improve LUTS and prevent complications such as recurrence.

articles.title: Transvaginal Mesh Surgery using the Adjusted Size of ORIHIME® Mesh with Wide-arm Widths: Favorable Postoperative Outcomes Compared to Conventional Polypropylene Mesh.
articles.authors: Kuroda K, Hamamoto K, Kawamura K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is defined as the downward displacement of pelvic structures. Transvaginal mesh surgery (TVM) is a surgical approach that serves as a viable intervention for POP repair; nonetheless, its effectiveness may differ depending on the mesh type and design employed. This study aimed to examine the influence of mesh type on postoperative quality of life (QOL) related to POP and other postoperative outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Preoperative and postoperative parameters, including the prolapse QOL (P-QOL) questionnaire score, were evaluated between two patient groups: patients treated with a wide-arm ORIHIME® mesh of adjusted mesh size (AMS) were assigned to the ORIHIME® AMS (+) group, and patients treated with a Prolift-type TVM using Gynemesh® PS or an Elevate-type TVM using a Polyform™ mesh comprised the nonORIHIME® group.
RESULTS: Almost all postoperative P-QOL component scores significantly decreased from preoperative scores in both groups. However, no significant decreases were found in the personal relationship subscale scores at 3 and 12 months postsurgery in the ORIHIME® AMS (+) group and at 3 months postsurgery in the non-ORIHIME® group compared with their preoperative values. The role limitations' subscale was significantly lower in the ORIHIME® AMS (+) group than in the non-ORIHIME® group. The ORIHIME® AMS (+) group demonstrated significantly better outcomes in urinary incontinence (UI) and mesh exposure rates compared with the non-ORIHIME® group.
CONCLUSION: Adjustment of the wide-arm ORIHIME® mesh size improved postoperative QOL and reduced complications such as UI compared with TVM using conventional mesh products.

articles.title: Development, Comparison With Genetic Counselors' Assessments, and Usability Evaluation of Japanese Version of Cancer Risk Assessment System in Primary Care (JCRAS-PC) for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer and Lynch Syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
articles.authors: Narumoto K, Kojima R, Shibata A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer risk associated with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and Lynch syndrome (LS) can be mitigated by risk assessment based on personal and family health information, followed by evidence-based preventive strategies. However, no validated risk assessment digital tool exists for primary care in Japan. We aimed to develop a guideline-based digital tool, called the Japanese version of the cancer risk assessment system in primary care (JCRAS-PC), compare its assessments with those of genetic counselors, and evaluate its usability.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary team developed JCRAS-PC, where primary care physicians (PCPs) enter personal and family cancer history within a pedigree and receive an assessment of whether referral for genetic counseling or testing for HBOC/LS is warranted. Referral criteria were consolidated from Japanese and international guidelines. We compared JCRAS-PC assessments with those of two genetic counselors across 35 de-identified real-world cases and calculated kappa statistics. Usability was evaluated through semi-structured individual interviews with seven PCPs using inductive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: In the evaluation, JCRAS-PC was revised for implementation errors. The revised JCRAS-PC assessments showed complete agreement with those of genetic counselors in all 35 cases (prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa = 1.00). Thematic analysis confirmed enhanced usability, and PCP participants' feedback led to revisions to improve functionality. In interviews, JCRAS-PC appeared to positively influence PCPs' knowledge and attitudes toward clinical cancer genetics.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed JCRAS-PC, evaluated its agreement with genetic counselors' assessments, and confirmed its usability for Japanese PCPs. Its clinical validity and utility in primary care populations warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Racial and ethnic disparities in cervical length screening for spontaneous preterm birth prediction.
articles.authors: Wang-Koehler E, Cenac LA, Wheeler SM et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) remains the leading cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality in the United States, with persistent racial and ethnic disparities, particularly at earlier gestational ages. Cervical length (CL) screening is one of the few clinically actionable strategies for identifying individuals at elevated risk for spontaneous PTB (sPTB), providing a focused lens to examine these disparities. This review examines (1) CL screening disparities among patients with and without a history of sPTB, (2) differences in CL across racial and social groups, (3) how race and social context relate to CL-based prediction of sPTB, (4) sPTB disparities after accounting for CL, and (5) whether CL screening reduces disparities in sPTB outcomes. Overall, evidence on disparities in screening uptake is mixed. Opt-out programs with high overall uptake (>90%) showed minimal racial differences, whereas programs with lower uptake found Black, Hispanic, and/or Asian patients less likely to receive CL screening; most studies cannot distinguish screening never offered from screening declined. Black individuals are consistently more likely to have a short cervix before 24 weeks-with rates of CL ≤25 mm approximately two to four times higher than White individuals across studies-as well as higher rates of funneling, intra-amniotic debris, and cervical dilation, though the factors underlying these differences are not well characterized. Findings for Hispanic and Asian patients were less consistent. Prediction models that combine CL with race and social factors perform better than CL alone, but differences in the test performance of CL itself across groups have not been established. Evidence on the remaining questions are limited, and whether CL screening reduces disparities in sPTB remains uncertain. Further research is needed to answer the questions that remain and to identify the structural factors that may contribute to these disparities.

articles.title: Oral microbiota, serum metabolites, and gestational diabetes mellitus: a multistage Mendelian randomization study.
articles.authors: Pan C, Li X, Xiong X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral microbial dysbiosis may connect oral health with systemic metabolic disease, including gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). We assessed associations of oral microbial features with GDM, and explored potential mediation by serum metabolites.
METHODS: We integrated Chinese oral microbiota, serum metabolites, and GDM genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets using multistage Mendelian randomization (MR), with external replication in European-ancestry and multi-ancestry datasets. Generalized Summary-data-based MR was the primary approach, supported by complementary MR approaches, bidirectional analyses, heterogeneity and pleiotropy assessments, and multiple-testing correction.
RESULTS: Ten of the 3,117 oral microbial features were significantly associated with GDM after false discovery rate (FDR) correction within the same genus. The strongest positive and inverse associations involved s_Treponema B USGB 1373 (OR: 1.83, 95% CI: 1.29-2.61, P adj  = 0.003) and s_Bacteroidaceae USGB 979 (OR: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.64-0.90, P adj  = 0.001). Screening 2,759 serum metabolites yielded three candidate chains with nominal indirect effects involving s_Streptobacillus USGB 672 with 4-(3-hydroxybutyl) phenol, and s_Saccharimonadaceae USGB 1287 with Azelaoyl PAF or 5-chloro-2-hydroxy-p-benzoquinone (estimated indirect-effect proportions 15.2%, 20.8%, and 31.8%, respectively). Neither the microbiota-metabolite nor metabolite-GDM associations survived FDR correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest potential associations between oral microbiota and GDM risk. Larger GWAS datasets on oral microbiota, serum metabolites, and GDM are needed to validate these associations and assess mediation.

articles.title: Impact of co-occurring maternal nicotine use, depression, and anxiety on perinatal outcomes.
articles.authors: Mize EJ, Garg B, Crosland BA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nicotine is the most commonly used substance in pregnancy, and the prevalence of mental health disorders in pregnancy is rising. In this study, we analyzed the association of nicotine use and depression and/or anxiety disorders, separately and together, on perinatal outcomes, an understudied area.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using California linked vital statistics and hospital discharge data (2008-2020). Patients were categorized into eight categories: (1) no nicotine use or depression or anxiety (reference), (2) nicotine use only, (3) depression only, (4) anxiety only, (5) depression and anxiety, (6) nicotine use and depression, (7) nicotine use and anxiety, and (8) nicotine use with depression and anxiety. The maternal outcomes measured were hypertensive disease of pregnancy, preterm delivery <37 and <32 weeks, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), and non-transfusion SMM; while the neonatal outcomes were neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, small for gestational age (SGA), respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), infant deaths, and hypoglycemia. We included 4,897,855 singleton, non-anomalous gestations delivered between 23 and 42 weeks and excluded individuals using other substances or diagnosed with bipolar disorder. Results were analyzed by chi-square tests and multivariable Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: Of the pregnant individuals included in this study, nicotine use was present in 1.4%, depression alone in 1.1%, anxiety alone in 1.2%, and combined depression and anxiety in 1.2%. Among maternal outcomes, SMM demonstrated a statistically significant association with combined nicotine use, depression, and anxiety (adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 2.20 [1.29-3.75]). Hypertensive disease was higher in groups with anxiety: only anxiety (15.3%), depression and anxiety (15.4%), and nicotine and anxiety (15.4%) compared to the reference group (7.7%). Among neonatal outcomes, infant death (aRR, 3.96 [1.66-9.46]), RDS (aRR, 2.03 [1.20-3.43]), and hypoglycemia (aRR, 1.67 [1.82-3.92]) were each significantly associated with combined nicotine use, depression, and anxiety. No other statistically significant increase in groups with nicotine use, depression, and anxiety were found in the other outcomes measured across the statistical analyses used.
CONCLUSION: Nicotine and depression/anxiety combined was associated with a higher risk of SMM, RDS, hypoglycemia, and infant death than each alone. These data can inform mechanistic research into…

articles.title: Anti-HBc seropositivity among women of childbearing age in Indonesia: a nationally representative cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Pracoyo NE, Musadad DA, Besral et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate the national prevalence of hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) seropositivity, indicating prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure, among Indonesian women aged 15-49 years. Additionally, the study sought to identify associated sociodemographic factors.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the 2018 Indonesian Basic Health Survey (Riskesdas), a nationally representative survey with a complex sampling design and appropriate sampling weights. Anti-HBc seropositivity was measured at the Sulianti Saroso Laboratory. Of the 19,418 participants, 12,617 women were included in the final analysis. Survey-weighted logistic regression was applied to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORₐⱼ) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Anti-HBc seropositivity was significantly more common among women aged >35 years (ORₐⱼ = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.58-1.87), those with lower educational attainment (ORₐⱼ = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.05-1.28), employed women (ORₐⱼ = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.09-1.29), rural residents (ORₐⱼ = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.18-1.40), and women reporting contraceptive use (ORₐⱼ = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.11-1.35).
CONCLUSION: Anti-HBc seropositivity remains a significant public health concern among Indonesian women of childbearing age, particularly those who are older, less educated, employed, living in rural areas, and reporting contraceptive use. Policy recommendations should prioritize maternal screening, timely and universal birth dose vaccination, administration of hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) when indicated, and improved vaccination coverage among unvaccinated adults.

articles.title: Surgical Resection of Extra-Abdominal Metastases of Low-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer: A Case Series.
articles.authors: Gaillard T, Mariolo A, Hotton J et al.
articles.abstract: Surgical removal of extra-abdominal spread of low-grade serous ovarian cancer has not been largely described in the literature. We report three cases of the association of abdominal and thoracic surgery in patients with metastatic low-grade serous ovarian cancer. It seems to have no deleterious impact on global management. Real impact on survival remains unclear.

articles.title: A novel postpartum hemorrhage prediction model for women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in secondary hospitals of middle-income settings.
articles.authors: Yang M, Wang M, Li N
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to develop and validate a risk-stratification tool to aid clinical referral decision-making for postpartum hemorrhage among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. The tool targets secondary hospitals with basic laboratory capacity in middle-income settings.
METHODS: This was a retrospective study. 2,761 women diagnosed with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy formed the development set (training and internal validation sets), and 592 women from the same hospital constituted a temporal validation set to evaluate model performance. LASSO regression was applied for optimal feature selection, and the prediction model was constructed using multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curves.
RESULTS: Key predictors, including placental abruption, placenta previa, placenta accreta, macrosomia, hemoglobin level, international normalized ratio, D-dimer concentration, and parity, were incorporated into a nomogram. The model achieved areas under the curve of 0.733 (training set), 0.756 (internal validation set), and 0.877 (temporal validation set). The apparent and bias-corrected calibration curves deviated from the ideal line at low predicted probabilities and gradually approached it as predicted PPH risk increased. Decision curve analysis indicated that the model yielded a higher net benefit compared with treat-all and treat-none strategies, whereas the clinical impact curve characterized the counts of predicted high-risk women and observed PPH events across risk thresholds.
CONCLUSION: The model demonstrated moderate discrimination and may be suitable for stratifying postpartum hemorrhage risk among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

articles.title: Androgen-Secreting Thecoma Fibroma Mimicking PCOS-A Diagnostic Challenge.
articles.authors: Aljenaee K, Alsubaiei M, Hajji S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian fibrothecomas are uncommon benign sex cord-stromal tumors, accounting for ~3.3% of ovarian tumors. They are usually hormonally inactive or estrogen-producing; androgen secretion is uncommon. Because hyperandrogenism is frequently attributed to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor may be overlooked when symptoms are progressive but virilization is absent.
CASE REPORT: A 42-year-old woman developed new-onset hirsutism, acne, menstrual irregularity, and later scalp hair loss. She was initially diagnosed with PCOS after being reported with biochemical hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound (US); the original testosterone value was unavailable. Following transient symptomatic improvement with a combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP), her symptoms recurred and progressed. Repeat evaluation showed a total testosterone level of 5.83 nmol/L and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) of 14 µmol/L. CT demonstrated a 5.1 × 4.2 × 4.0 cm mass adjacent to the right ovary with normal adrenal glands. Right oophorectomy was performed, and histopathology confirmed a fibrothecoma with focal luteinization. Three months after surgery, acne and hirsutism improved, and total testosterone decreased to 0.50 nmol/L.
CONCLUSIONS: Progressive or newly developed hyperandrogenism should not be attributed to PCOS solely on the basis of polycystic ovarian morphology. The tempo of symptoms, biochemical findings, and clinical context should guide evaluation for alternative ovarian or adrenal causes. This case illustrates an uncommon PCOS mimic and the importance of reassessing the diagnosis when the clinical course is atypical.

articles.title: Perioperative factors associated with delayed passage of flatus after laparoscopic uterine myomectomy: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Liu Q, Gu J, Luo R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delayed passage of flatus (DPF) after laparoscopic uterine myomectomy may indicate slower gastrointestinal recovery, but procedure-specific evidence is limited.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 342 consecutive adult patients who underwent laparoscopic uterine myomectomy between March 2021 and March 2025. The endpoint was no documented passage of flatus within the first 3 postoperative days. Because oral-intake intolerance, nausea or vomiting, abdominal distension, and nasogastric-tube use were not systematically captured, the endpoint was treated as DPF rather than consensus-defined postoperative ileus. A three-variable logistic regression model was restricted to preoperative and intraoperative variables and interpreted as an exploratory association model.
RESULTS: DPF occurred in 35 patients (10.2%). Plain radiographs in all 35 patients meeting this threshold showed multiple air-fluid levels and diffuse small- and large-bowel gas. No focal mechanical obstruction was documented after record review that included bedside abdominal findings and radiography. In the primary complete-case model (341 patients; 35 events), pre-existing constipation (odds ratio [OR] 12.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.65-45.21), intraoperative intestinal adhesion (OR 39.91, 95% CI 13.89-114.71), and operative time (OR 1.014 per minute, 95% CI 1.006-1.023) remained associated with DPF after adjustment. The wide CIs, particularly for intestinal adhesion, indicated substantial uncertainty in the magnitude of association. The model had an apparent area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.939 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.894-0.978) and a Brier score of 0.040. At the data-derived Youden-index threshold, apparent sensitivity was 0.857 and apparent specificity was 0.908. A single 5-fold cross-validation yielded an area under the curve of 0.923.
DISCUSSION: These center-specific findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective external validation using a multidimensional gastrointestinal-recovery endpoint.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of vascular endothelial growth factor levels in placental, fetal-membrane, and umbilical-cord tissues: associations with maternal obstetric complications.
articles.authors: Altal O, Hulliel AF, Al Sharie AH et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is a central regulator of placental angiogenesis, but the extent to which tissue-level VEGF expression differs across obstetric complications and among gestational compartments remains unclear. This study evaluated VEGF protein concentrations in placental villous tissue, fetal membranes, and umbilical cord across diverse pregnancy phenotypes.
METHODS: A prospective observational cohort study with subsequent group classification was conducted at King Abdullah University Hospital, Irbid, Jordan. Eighty-six pregnancies were classified into five groups: uncomplicated controls, small-for-gestational-age (SGA), pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and thrombophilia. VEGF concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in placental, membrane, and umbilical cord tissues obtained at delivery. Between-group differences were assessed using non-parametric analyses, while multinomial logistic regression, Spearman correlation, principal component analysis, clustering, and cross-validated receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed.
RESULTS: VEGF concentrations showed substantial overlap among clinical groups. No significant differences were observed in placental VEGF (P = 0.802), membrane VEGF (P = 0.139), or umbilical cord VEGF (P = 0.525), with negligible effect sizes (ε 2 ≤ 0.04). Multivariable modelling demonstrated no significant association between any VEGF compartment and pathological pregnancy groups. Correlations between compartments were weak, with modest associations between membrane and umbilical cord VEGF (ρ = 0.29, P = 0.006) and placental and membrane VEGF (ρ = 0.22, P = 0.046). Multivariate analyses failed to identify distinct VEGF expression patterns, and a three-marker classifier showed poor discrimination after cross-validation (AUC = 0.52).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, total tissue VEGF measured at delivery did not clearly distinguish pregnancies complicated by SGA, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, GDM, or thrombophilia from uncomplicated pregnancies. The limited sample size, however, means that smaller effects cannot be excluded. The weak inter-compartment correlations may be more consistent with locally regulated angiogenic processes than with a unified tissue signature, although sampling and methodological factors may also contribute. These findings highlight the limitations of total VEGF tissue measurement as a biomarker of…

articles.title: Releasing Immunosuppression in the Tumor: A Phase 1/2 Study of Arginase Inhibitor INCB001158 in Combination with Chemotherapy in Advanced Malignancies.
articles.journal: Journal of immunotherapy and precision oncology
articles.authors: Naing A, Javle M, Cho M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Arginase is overexpressed in many advanced cancers, which can deplete arginine in tumors to promote immunosuppression. Arginase inhibition may enhance the efficacy of standard chemotherapy regimens by increasing arginine levels and modulating arginine-mediated immune function. INCB001158 is a potent and selective arginase inhibitor that was assessed in combination with chemotherapy.
METHODS: This was an open-label, nonrandomized, phase 1/2 dose-escalation/expansion study in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. INCB001158 was administered orally twice daily (bid) in combination with chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6, gemcitabine/cisplatin, or paclitaxel). Phase 2 tumor-type cohorts were colorectal cancer, biliary tract cancer (BTC), ovarian cancer (OC), gastroesophageal cancer, and endometrial cancer. Primary end points included safety, tolerability, and overall response rate (ORR).
RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were enrolled in phase 1 and 95 in phase 2. No dose-dependent adverse event trends were observed. Recommended phase 2 dose of INCB001158 was 100 mg bid. Two phase 2 expansion cohorts met criteria for Simon 2-stage expansion: patients with BTC treated with INCB001158 100 mg bid plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, and patients with platinum-resistant OC treated with INCB001158 100 mg bid plus paclitaxel. The overall response rate was 24.2% (8/33 patients, all partial responses) in the BTC cohort and 16.7% (1/24 complete response and 3/24 partial responses) in the OC cohort. Pharmacodynamic increase in arginine levels was observed systemically in blood plasma and locally detected by mass-spectrometry images of tumor tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: INCB001158 was generally well tolerated and associated with increases in arginine levels and responses in the BTC cohort, suggesting that combination regimens with chemotherapy may provide clinical benefit for some patients. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT03314935; EudraCT 2017-002904-29.

articles.title: Revisiting common female infertility factors traditionally associated with impaired oocyte quality: insights from IVF outcomes and AI-derived oocyte score performance.
articles.authors: Del Collado M, Braga DPAF, Setti AS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While advanced maternal age is consistently associated with impaired oocyte competence and poorer reproductive outcomes, the effects of other female infertility factors, including polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), endometriosis, and body mass index (BMI), remain debated. Moreover, whether AI-derived oocyte quality metrics retain their predictive value across different female infertility conditions remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether common female infertility factors are associated with oocyte and embryo competence and cumulative reproductive outcomes in intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles, and assessed the performance of an AI-derived composite oocyte score across these populations. The study included 14,420 injected oocytes from 1,856 autologous ICSI cycles performed between 2020 and 2025. Outcomes were compared between controls and women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), endometriosis, overweight, or obesity; controls were additionally stratified by maternal age (<38 versus ≥38 years). Age-based propensity-score weighting was applied for pairwise female-factor comparisons, followed by adjusted mixed-effects regression models accounting for patient- and retrieval-cycle-level clustering.
RESULTS: Endometriosis and obesity were not associated with consistent reductions in laboratory or clinical outcomes, whereas overweight was associated with lower top-quality blastocyst and cumulative reproductive outcomes. Advanced maternal age showed the most consistent detrimental pattern, including lower MAGENTA and KIDScore values, reduced blastocyst development and euploidy rates, and lower cumulative pregnancy rates. PMOS cycles showed largely preserved laboratory outcomes, higher MII yield, and higher observed cumulative pregnancy rates. The composite MAGENTA score was associated with higher odds of fertilization (OR 1.53), blastocyst formation (OR 1.67), and top-quality blastocyst formation (OR 1.26), and with higher KIDScore (β = 0.21). These associations were generally observed across the evaluated female-factor groups, and MAGENTA provided modest incremental discrimination beyond clinical variables.
DISCUSSION: Overall, female infertility factors appear to affect reproductive competence through distinct patterns rather than a uniform impairment in oocyte quality, with maternal age showing the most consistent adverse association and AI-derived oocyte assessment…

articles.title: Association between preoperative MRI-measured membranous urethral length and early urinary continence recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Mao P, Ye F, Zhu X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is a key surgical approach for localized prostate cancer, yet early postoperative urinary incontinence remains a major functional concern. Membranous urethral length (MUL), measurable by preoperative MRI, may predict continence recovery, but its relationship with early outcomes warrants further clarification.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between preoperative MRI-measured MUL and early complete urinary continence recovery after RARP, and to evaluate its dose-response relationship and discriminative ability.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 152 patients who underwent RARP (October 2024-March 2026). MUL was measured on preoperative T2-weighted MRI by two independent observers. Urinary continence (0 pads/day) was assessed at 1 and 3 months after catheter removal. Multivariable Logistic regression (1 month) and Firth penalized Logistic regression (3 months) were used. Restricted cubic spline, ROC curves, and propensity score matching were performed.
RESULTS: Median MUL was 13.49 mm. Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC = 0.946). Complete continence recovery rates at 1 and 3 months were 51.32% and 79.61%, respectively. Each 1-mm MUL increase was independently associated with higher odds of continence recovery at 1 month (OR = 1.758, 95% CI: 1.450-2.132, P<0.001) and 3 months (OR = 1.502, 95% CI: 1.247-1.809, P<0.001). Older age and higher BMI were associated with lower odds of 3-month recovery (both P<0.05). RCS analysis showed a linear dose-response relationship (P overall<0.001; P nonlinearity=0.540). MUL demonstrated moderate discriminative ability for 1-month (AUC = 0.822) and 3-month (AUC = 0.773) continence recovery.
CONCLUSION: Longer preoperative MUL was independently associated with higher likelihood of complete urinary continence recovery at 1 and 3 months after catheter removal, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. MUL has good measurement reproducibility and moderate predictive value, supporting its potential as an imaging biomarker for preoperative continence risk stratification in RARP patients.

articles.title: Association of uterine-entry technique with chorioamniotic membrane separation after fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome: two-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Burnett BA, Parobek CM, Imamoglu M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chorioamniotic membrane separation (CAS) is a recognized iatrogenic complication of fetoscopic laser photocoagulation (FLP), the standard treatment for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS). We compared the incidence of CAS between two different means of uterine entry for FLP: the sharp-trocar and Seldinger techniques.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies complicated by TTTS undergoing FLP between 16 + 0 and 26 + 0 weeks' gestation at two tertiary fetal centers in the USA from January 2012 to August 2025. The uterine-entry technique was center-specific: one center used the Seldinger technique exclusively, while the other used sharp-trocar entry exclusively. All patients at both centers underwent routine short-interval postoperative fetal ultrasound examination, with particular attention paid to membrane integrity at the entry sites. The primary outcome was CAS diagnosed intraoperatively or during postoperative ultrasound performed within 48 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included gestational age at delivery, latency from FLP to delivery, preterm birth < 32 and < 34 weeks, and survival 48 h after FLP, at birth and at 30 days postnatally. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis evaluated associations between clinically relevant anatomical and procedural variables and the occurrence of CAS.
RESULTS: In total, 889 pregnancies that underwent a FLP procedure for TTTS were included (591 using Seldinger entry, 298 using sharp-trocar entry). Sharp-trocar entry was associated with a lower rate of CAS (8.1% vs 14.4%; P = 0.01) and lower rates of delivery before 32 weeks (42% vs 59%; P < 0.001) and delivery before 34 weeks (61% vs 77%; P < 0.001). Among cases with complete data, after adjusting for clinically relevant anatomical and procedural variables, sharp-trocar entry was independently associated with lower odds of CAS (adjusted odds ratio, 0.46 (95% CI, 0.24-0.82); P = 0.01). Delivery was later in the sharp-trocar entry group (median gestational age, 32 + 4 (interquartile range (IQR), 29 + 1 to 34 + 4) weeks vs 31 + 0 (IQR, 28 + 1 to 33 + 5) weeks; P < 0.001), and the median interval from procedure to delivery was longer (82 (IQR, 58-105) days vs 74 (IQR, 48-96) days; P = 0.002). Survival of donor and recipient twins 48 h after FLP, at birth and at 30 days postnatally, was similar between the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Sharp-trocar entry during FLP for TTTS was associated…

articles.title: Impact of the pink October campaign on breast cancer screening in the Alpes-Maritimes region (France): A regional perspective.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Barranger E, Najib B
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to describe monthly variations in breast cancer screening activity during the Pink October campaign and assess whether the observed increase extended beyond the campaign period in the Alpes-Maritimes region of France.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of aggregated monthly mammogram counts from January 2022 to December 2024. Data on organized screening (DO) were available for all 3 years, whereas data for individual screening (DP) were available only for 2024. Monthly screening activity during October and November was compared with activity during the remaining months using the statistical methods described below.
RESULTS: Organized screening activity peaked in October in each study year, with reported increases of 31% in 2022, 27% in 2023, and 48% in 2024 relative to the respective annual monthly means. The October-November comparison yielded P-values of 0.001 in 2022, 0.049 in 2023, and 0.054 in 2024. The 2024 result did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance. Individual screening showed a smaller October increase in 2024 (+10% relative to its annual monthly mean), and the October-November comparison was not statistically significant (P = 0.178). These findings describe temporal variations in screening activity and do not establish a causal effect of the campaign.
CONCLUSION: Mammography activity, particularly organized screening, increased during the Pink October period in the Alpes-Maritimes region. However, the aggregated data cannot establish whether this increase represented additional screening or a redistribution of examinations across the calendar year. Further multicenter studies using longer time series and individual-level data are needed to assess the campaign's effect on screening participation.

articles.title: Early Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Lower the Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Women With Pre-Pregnancy Obesity: Protocol for the Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial (GLOW).
articles.authors: Lu Y, Tian Z, Niu J et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pre-pregnancy obesity substantially increases the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet preventive strategies before routine GDM screening remain limited. The Glucose monitoring to Lower risk of GDM in Obese pregnant Women (GLOW) trial aims to determine whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) initiated in early pregnancy reduces the incidence of GDM in women with pre-pregnancy obesity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: GLOW is a national, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group randomised controlled trial enrolling 1034 women with pre-pregnancy body mass index ≥ 28 kg/m2, a singleton pregnancy and gestational age ≤ 14+6 weeks at eight hospitals in China. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to routine antenatal care alone or routine antenatal care plus CGM. In the CGM group, five consecutive 14-day sensors will be used from 14+0-14+6 to 24+0-24+6 weeks of gestation (70 days in total), with access to glucose values and standardised CGM education. The primary endpoint is the incidence of GDM diagnosed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24+0-24+6 weeks. Secondary outcomes include gestational weight gain, maternal metabolic and anthropometric measures, lifestyle behaviours and maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: GLOW will determine whether early CGM introduced before routine GDM screening can reduce GDM incidence and favourably influence maternal metabolic and pregnancy outcomes in women with pre-pregnancy obesity. The findings may inform the role of early CGM as a preventive strategy in this high-risk population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2600130043.

articles.title: A body shape index and body roundness index in women with and without the polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Pérez-López FR, Fernández-Alonso AM, Hernández-Bustamante EA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association of a body shape index (ABSI) and body roundness index (BRI) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), also known as polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS).
METHODS: This study was registered at PROSPERO [CRD420251177545] and followed the PRISMA Guidelines. We searched evidence in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases. Two case-control and seven cross-sectional studies reported ABSI and BRI results in PMOS patients and women without the syndrome.
RESULTS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of ABSI (eight studies, 3193 participants) association with PMOS (SMD = 0.45, 95%CI = 0.07, 0.83; I 2 = 90.5%, τ2 = 0.18) and body mass index (BMI) (MD = 3.76, 95%CI = 1.61, 5.91 kg/m2; I 2 = 93.8%, τ2 = 5.84). In five studies (840 participants), BRI levels were higher in PMOS patients than in the control group (SMD = 1.09, 95%CI = 0.53-1.66) 95%CI = 0.53-1.66; I 2 = 85.9%; τ2 = 0.17), and BMI MD = 4.31 kg/m2, 95%CI = 1.98, 6.65; I 2 = 83.9%, τ2 = 2.87). Subgroup analyzes by geographic region showed no significant differences in ABSI and BRI estimates between European and Asian. The BRI finding remained statistically significant in all leave-one-out analyzes, whereas the statistical significance of the ABSI finding was sensitive to individual study exclusion.
CONCLUSION: PMOS patients have enhanced ABSI and BRI levels compared to women without the syndrome. Further high-quality studies from other world regions are needed to evaluate heterogeneity at different PMOS clinical stages.

articles.title: Patient barriers to colposcopy attendance following an abnormal Cervical Screening Test: A qualitative study of patient and healthcare professional perspectives.
articles.authors: Temminghoff L, Bastable A, Steele A et al.
articles.abstract: Approximately 53 percent of people referred for colposcopy after an abnormal Cervical Screening Test in Australia face barriers to accessing appointments within the recommended 90 days, increasing the risk of delayed diagnosis and poorer health outcomes. This study aimed to explore barriers to colposcopy attendance from the perspectives of Australian patients and health‑care professionals. A qualitative thematic analysis design was used. Semi‑structured interviews were conducted with four patients referred for colposcopy and 11 health‑care professionals who refer to or perform the procedure. Interviews were transcribed and thematically analyzed. Three main themes describing barriers to colposcopy attendance were identified. 1. Stress and anxiety were common, driven by limited understanding of the procedure and misconceptions about cancer risk. 2. Information barriers affected both groups, including difficulty interpreting screening results and a lack of resources to support patient education. 3. Structural and health system barriers, including logistical barriers, inflexible appointments and poor clinic communication, further hindered attendance. In addition to screening and vaccination, patients need to be supported through the clinical pathway to equitably eliminate cervical cancer. Focusing on patient education and communication poses a cost-effective solution for improving colposcopy attendance and patient experience.

articles.title: Exercise self-efficacy, physical activity, and menopausal symptoms in Malaysian midlife women: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Nga CZJ, Che Muhamed AM, Farah NM
articles.abstract: Physical activity (PA) is associated with fewer menopausal symptoms, yet many midlife women remain insufficiently active. Exercise self-efficacy is a key correlate of exercise behavior, but evidence among linking all these factors in Malaysian women is limited. We examined the associations between menopausal symptoms, PA and exercise self-efficacy in 159 women aged 40-60 years (93 perimenopausal, 66 postmenopausal). Participants completed a symptom questionnaire, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form and the Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale (ESES). The most reported symptoms were dry skin (44.7 percent), brain fog (42.1 percent) and hair thinning or loss (39.0 percent). Mean moderate-to-vigorous PA was 139 minutes/week; 39.6 percent of women had low PA and 32.7 percent met the WHO recommendation. Each one-point higher ESES score was associated with 13 percent higher PA after adjustment for age, BMI and menopausal phase (p < .001), and the proportion meeting the WHO recommendation rose from 17 percent in the lowest to 56 percent in the highest ESES quartile. Higher PA was associated with modestly fewer symptoms (IRR = 0.96 per 600 MET-min/week, p = .027), although this was not robust in sensitivity analyses. Strengthening exercise self-efficacy is a promising target for increasing PA in midlife women, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish whether PA reduces menopausal symptoms.

articles.title: Women's Understanding of Risk of Postpartum Hemorrhage: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Carr BL, Pollock W
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) has significant short- and long-term effects for women. Research typically focuses on women who experience severe bleeding. Little is known about women's understanding of their risk or decision-making regarding PPH.
METHODS: The aim of this study was to explore women's understanding of risk for PPH, preferences for discussing this risk, and views on a prediction tool for postpartum hemorrhage. Women who had recently birthed were invited to participate. Eight women were interviewed to discuss their experiences and also comment on a graphical model representing variables associated with risk and conditions related to change of risk for PPH. This Bayesian Network model was developed using perinatal data and expert knowledge from maternity clinicians. The Framework Method was used to identify, manage, and analyze themes across six phases.
RESULTS: Three main themes were identified: Personal Risk, Controlling the Risk, and Knowing. Personal Risk had two subthemes: Transparency and Continuity of Care. Both women who experienced PPH and those who did not wanted to be informed about the possibility of PPH and what the impact of this would be. The prediction tool was considered a useful, visual tool to help aide this discussion.
CONCLUSION: Women want to understand their individual risk and be informed about how their risk of PPH relates to their personal circumstances. Being informed about their risk afforded some degree of control, assisted decision-making, and enabled women to choose what to do with that information. Participants reported the prediction tool was easy to understand and potentially useful.

articles.title: Quality of life with first-line ribociclib plus endocrine therapy vs combination chemotherapy in clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC: RIGHT Choice.
articles.authors: El Saghir NS, Abdel-Razeq H, Im SA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The RIGHT Choice phase 2 randomized clinical trial of pre/perimenopausal women with clinically aggressive hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) reported a statistically significant progression-free survival benefit with ribociclib plus endocrine therapy (ET) over combination chemotherapy (21.8 vs 12.8 months; HR, 0.61; 95% CI: 0.43-0.87; P = .003), with lower rates of symptomatic adverse events. This prespecified analysis compared QOL outcomes between treatment arms in RIGHT Choice to support treatment decision-making in these patients.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Pre/perimenopausal women with clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC were randomized 1:1 to first-line ribociclib plus letrozole/anastrozole/goserelin or investigator's choice of combination chemotherapy. Median time to definitive deterioration (mTTDD) from randomization in Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast (FACT-B) scores (≥10%) or a composite mTTDD endpoint (including treatment discontinuation) was determined by Kaplan-Meier methods.
RESULTS: mTTDD in FACT-B overall health status, trial outcome index (TOI), and nausea scores was prolonged in patients receiving ribociclib plus ET versus combination chemotherapy (HR, 0.72, 0.63, and 0.59, respectively), while the pain score was similar between treatment arms (HR, 1.05). The composite mTTDD in overall health status, TOI, pain, and nausea scores was longer in patients in the ribociclib arm (HR, 0.68, 0.65, 0.76, and 0.62, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with first-line ribociclib plus ET translates into improved QOL versus combination chemotherapy in patients with clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC. These data reinforce efficacy and safety findings supporting cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors plus ET as the preferred option in this population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03839823.

articles.title: Feasibility and factors associated with successful back transfer after maternal transfer for postpartum hemorrhage: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Imatake H, Haraoka Y, Ueda Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) requires multidisciplinary management at tertiary care centers. Back transfer after clinical stabilization is an important component of regional perinatal care, but the clinical characteristics associated with back transfer decisions remain poorly understood. This study examined the rate of back transfer and the factors associated with actual back transfer decisions among women transferred for PPH.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted among postpartum women transferred to the Kyoto University Hospital for established or impending PPH between April 2013 and September 2025. The primary outcome was the rate of back transfer, and associated clinical factors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 163 eligible women, 92 (56.4%) underwent successful back transfer. A higher shock index at admission was negatively associated with successful back transfer (odds ratio, OR = 0.12; 95% confidence interval, 95% CI = 0.02-0.46; P = 0.005). Compared with tone, trauma (OR = 0.10, 95% CI = 0.03-0.28, P < 0.001) and tissue (OR = 0.26, 95% CI = 0.09-0.74, P = 0.013) were negatively associated with successful back transfer. A higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration was positively associated with successful back transfer (OR = 1.32, 95% CI = 1.02-1.74, P = 0.041).
CONCLUSION: More than half of the women in this selected cohort underwent back transfer after maternal transfer for PPH. Lower shock index at admission, hemorrhage caused by uterine atony, and higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration were associated with back transfer. These exploratory findings may inform future efforts to develop standardized back transfer criteria.

articles.title: Circulating biomarkers in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma for risk stratification, diagnosis and prognosis.
articles.authors: Monti E, Bella M, Vianello C et al.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. We focus on key liquid biopsy components, including circulating cell-free DNA, particularly circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, non-coding RNAs, extracellular vesicles, proteins and metabolites, such as bile acids and lipids, highlighting their diagnostic and prognostic potential and their possible integration into personalized management strategies for patients with early-stage HCC.

articles.title: Fertility care for transgender and gender diverse individuals in Germany: an interview study with healthcare providers on the importance of care, care provision, barriers, and improvement strategies.
articles.authors: Werner M, Barton C, Becker-Hebly I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As gender-affirming care can impact fertility in transgender and gender diverse individuals (TGDI), fertility preservation (FP) may help TGDI to have biological children in the future. The reported discrepancy between the proportion of TGDI who express a desire to have biological children (up to 50%) and low FP utilization rates (3-10%) highlights the need for high-quality fertility care, including fertility related counseling and the provision of FP. However, there is limited knowledge of the extent to which fertility care is being offered in Germany. Therefore, this study aims to examine the current state of fertility care for TGDI in Germany from the perspective of healthcare providers.
METHODS: We conducted 30 semi-structured interviews with healthcare providers from various somatic and mental healthcare disciplines caring for TGDI in Germany. The interview guide addressed four topics of interest: the importance of care, care provision, barriers to care, and improvement strategies. The interviews were transcribed and analyzed using structuring qualitative content analysis by Kuckartz. Deductive and inductive coding were applied to identify main and subcategories from the interviews.
RESULTS: Almost all interviewees considered fertility care for TGDI to be highly important and believed that fertility counseling should be an integral part of care, while they highlighted that the importance of FP depended on the individual family planning desires and life circumstances of TGDI. Most interviewees routinely provided fertility counseling prior to gender-affirming care. We identified several barriers to fertility care for TGDI in Germany: TGDI-related (knowledge gaps, low priority of FP, dysphoria), healthcare provider-related (lack of knowledge, experience, gender sensitivity), procedural (invasiveness of FP, dysphoria triggers), structural (inadequate healthcare infrastructure, research, costs), legal (historic requirement of infertility, prohibition of surrogacy and egg donation), and societal (discrimination, cis- and heteronormative image of family life).
