To address these barriers, the interviewees suggested promoting healthcare providers' competence, further research and guidelines, standardizing fertility counseling, enhancing interdisciplinary cooperation, ensuring transparency of services, routine cost coverage of FP, and promoting societal acceptance.
CONCLUSIONS: According to the interviewees, optimized fertility care for TGDI requires…

articles.title: Treated and untreated maternal asthma and early pregnancy outcomes: a retrospective cohort study of 324,238 infants.
articles.authors: Shakhshir LA, Pell JP, Hastie CE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continued use of asthma medication during pregnancy is recommended, because asthma exacerbations often increase during pregnancy, and poor control may adversely affect maternal and foetal health. However, evidence on whether adverse outcomes arise from the treatment itself or just the underlying disease remains inconsistent. This study examined the relationship between maternal asthma, and its medication, and early pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective birth cohort was constructed using population-wide linked Welsh health records of 324,238 infants born between 2009 and 2022. Logistic regression was used to investigate associations between maternal asthma (treated, untreated, and medication exposure) and pregnancy outcomes: stillbirth, iatrogenic and spontaneous preterm delivery, small/very small for gestational age (SGA/VSGA), and low Apgar score.
RESULTS: Of the 324,238 infants, 39,040 (12.0%) had mothers with asthma: 20,840 (6.4%) had treated asthma, 8,230 (2.5%) had untreated asthma, and 9,970 (3.1%) were prescribed asthma medications without recorded asthma diagnoses. Compared to offspring of mothers with no maternal asthma (reference group), those whose mothers had treated asthma had higher odds of SGA (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.07-1.19), VSGA (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.26), Apgar score < 7 (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.01-1.29), and iatrogenic preterm delivery (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26). Associations were observed across multiple classes of asthma medication with stronger associations among the offspring of mothers prescribed more than one medication class and those with add-on therapies including long-acting muscarinic antagonists, short-acting muscarinic antagonists, leukotrienes antagonist and theophylline, consistent with more severe, or poorly controlled, asthma rather than medication effects. Untreated asthma was associated with higher risk of iatrogenic preterm delivery, and treated asthma was associated with lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery (aOR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.89). No associations were observed with stillbirth.
CONCLUSIONS: The non-specific associations observed across different classes of asthma medication and dose-relationships with polytherapy suggested confounding by indication and severity. The findings for iatrogenic preterm delivery further supported an effect of the underlying disease rather than its treatment. These findings, together with the lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery among treated mothers,…

articles.title: Biopsychosocial factors associated with menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, health literacy, and physical activity across age-based cohorts: a cross-sectional comparative study.
articles.authors: Yiğit Kocamer M, Sert B
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menstrual pain is influenced by biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors. This study compared menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, health literacy, and physical activity across age-based cohorts of women and examined the associations between menstrual attitudes and menstrual pain.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 1,220 women with primary dysmenorrhea were classified into three age-based cohorts corresponding to Generations Z (n = 380), Y (n = 440), and X (n = 400). Menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, health literacy, and daily step counts were assessed using validated instruments. Group differences were examined using χ² and Kruskal-Wallis tests followed by Dwass-Steel-Critchlow-Fligner post-hoc comparisons where appropriate. Spearman correlation and adjusted multiple linear regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Significant differences were observed across the age-based cohorts in menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, and health literacy (all p < 0.05), whereas physical activity did not differ significantly. Women in the youngest age-based cohort reported the highest pain levels and more positive menstrual attitudes, whereas women in the oldest age-based cohort had the lowest health literacy scores. Significant differences were identified across all MAQ subscales, with the largest effect observed for the Anticipation and Prediction of Menstruation subscale (ε²=0.084). Correlation analyses showed that the associations between menstrual attitude dimensions and pain varied across cohorts, although a weak negative association between pain and the Denial of the Effects of Menstruation subscale was consistently observed. In the adjusted regression model, perceiving menstruation as a bothersome event (β = 0.159, p < 0.001) and as a natural event (β = 0.062, p = 0.026) were positively associated with pain, whereas denial of the effects of menstruation was negatively associated with pain (β=-0.243, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Menstrual pain and menstrual attitudes differed across age-based cohorts, and specific dimensions of menstrual attitudes were independently associated with pain severity. These findings support a biopsychosocial perspective on menstrual pain and highlight the importance of age- and life-stage-sensitive approaches to menstrual health. Because of the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be made.

articles.title: Performance of a DNA methylation marker panel in cervical samples from women with abnormal cytology findings.
articles.authors: Zeiser I, Schubert K, Hippe J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable triage methods are essential in cervical cancer screening to avoid overtreatment. DNA methylation markers offer an objective molecular readout with potential to keep false-positive rates low. We evaluated the GynTect® DNA methylation assay as a triage marker in cervical samples from women with abnormal cytology, in comparison with the p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain test CINtec Plus®.
METHODS: Surplus liquid-based cytology samples from 1,000 women with cytology ≥ PAP III (Low-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion = LSIL, or worse) were tested with GynTect® (markers: ASTN1, DLX1, ITGA4, RXFP3, SOX17, ZNF671). cobas® HPV and p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain (CINtec Plus®) results were available for all samples; histopathology was available for a subset of 601 samples. Positivity rates with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using the Wilson score method.
RESULTS: Overall GynTect positivity was 27.7% versus 88.3% for p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain. Methylation positivity correlated with cytological severity: 17.0% in LSIL, 30.2% in moderate High-​Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion HSIL, and 65.0% in the PAP IV group (high-grade SIL/AIS and HSIL suspicious for invasion). Among HPV16/18-positive samples, 38.4% were GynTect-positive versus 94.8% p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain-positive. By histopathology, GynTect positivity was 15.0% (CIN I), 27.0% (CIN II), and 56.5% (CIN III); all four cancer cases were GynTect- and p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain​-positive. Of 191 GynTect-positive cases with histopathology, 73% had CIN II or CIN III.
CONCLUSIONS: GynTect positivity (27.7%) was significantly lower than p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain positivity (88.3%), with a statistically significant monotonic trend across increasing cytological severity (Cochran-Armitage trend test, p < 0.001) and histopathological categories (p < 0.001). All four histologically confirmed carcinomas were GynTect-positive. These findings are consistent with a potential role for GynTect in selective triage after abnormal cytology, with lower positivity rates suggesting higher selectivity for high-grade disease compared with p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain. Prospective validation in primary HPV-screening triage populations is required to determine whether this translates into clinical benefit.

articles.title: Clinical efficacy of hysteroscopic Mirena ring broken-arm slipknot suture fixation for adenomyosis.
articles.authors: Feng G, Chen G, Nie Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of hysteroscopic Mirena ring broken-arm slipknot suture fixation (BA) compared with non-broken-arm slipknot suture fixation (NBA) and Giman ring anchor fixation (Giman) for the treatment of adenomyosis (AM).
METHODS: A total of 102 patients with AM treated from October 2023 to July 2025 were retrospectively enrolled and divided into three groups: BA group (n = 40), NBA group (n = 45), and Giman group (n = 17). Clinical efficacy, pain scores (VAS), menstrual blood loss (PBAC), sex hormone levels (E2, FSH, LH), endometrial thickness, and uterine cavity depth were compared using generalized estimating equations (GEE), repeated measures ANOVA, and difference-in-differences (DID) models. Causal forest analysis was applied to estimate individualized treatment effects. Adverse events were assessed by Log-binomial regression.
RESULTS: The overall effective rate was 92.50% in the BA group, 84.44% in the NBA group, and 64.71% in the Giman group (P < 0.05). GEE analysis showed that both the BA and NBA groups had significantly lower PBAC and VAS scores compared with the Giman group across all follow-up time points (P < 0.05). Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significant interaction effects between treatment method and time on sex hormone levels (P < 0.001). DID analysis demonstrated that the BA group had the greatest reduction in endometrial thickness and uterine cavity depth. The total adverse event rate was significantly lower in the BA group than in the other two groups (RR < 1, P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, hysteroscopic Mirena ring broken-arm slipknot suture fixation was associated with better 12-month clinical outcomes and fewer adverse events compared with the NBA and Giman approaches for treating AM.

articles.title: Effect of low-dose esketamine on quality of recovery after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: He W, Chen C, Wu X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although low-dose esketamine has shown analgesic benefits, its effect on the quality of recovery after gynecologic laparoscopy remains unclear.
METHODS: In this double-blind randomized controlled trial, 140 adults with ASA I-II and a BMI of 18.5-30 kg/m² undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopy (hysterectomy, myomectomy, or ovarian cystectomy) were randomly assigned to Group E (esketamine group) or Group C (control group). Patients in Group E received 0.25 mg/kg esketamine bolus after anesthesia induction followed by a continuous infusion of 0.1 mg/kg/h until 15 min before the end of surgery, whereas those in Group C received an equal volume of normal saline. The primary outcome was the total score on the Quality of Recovery-40 questionnaire (QoR-40) at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) scores at rest and during activity at 0, 6, 12, and 24 h postoperatively, tracheal extubation time, rescue analgesic consumption, and the incidences of nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and nightmares.
RESULTS: Group E had significantly higher global QoR-40 scores than Group C at 24 h postoperatively (adjusted mean difference 2.30, 95% CI 0.21 to 4.39; P = 0.034). Pain scores at rest and during activity were lower in Group E at 6 h (rest: mean (SD), 2.28 (1.69) vs. 3.01 (2.09), P = 0.025; activity: 3.03 (1.80) vs. 3.81 (2.08), P = 0.020) and 24 h (rest: 1.88 (1.30) vs. 2.29 (1.32), P = 0.045; activity: 2.56 (1.43) vs. 3.16 (1.60), P = 0.022), but were comparable between groups at 0 h and 12 h. The incidence of dizziness was significantly higher in Group E than in Group C during the PACU period (23.5% vs. 8.7%; risk difference (RD) 14.8%, 95% CI 2.8% to 26.9%; P = 0.033). However, this difference resolved by 24 h postoperatively (25.0% vs. 23.2%; P = 0.962), and no significant differences were observed in other secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose esketamine was associated with a statistically higher QoR-40 score, but the magnitude was below the Minimum Clinically Important Difference (MCID) and therefore may not represent a clinically meaningful improvement in gynecologic laparoscopy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trials Registry ( www.chictr.org.cn , registration number: ChiCTR2300072538, date of registration: 16/06/2023).

articles.title: Beyond Fertility: Pioneering AI-Enhanced Health Solutions with AMH and Inhibin B.
articles.authors: Xu H, Bishop F, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract: The review article underscores the pivotal roles of Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) and Inhibin B in the realm of reproductive health. AMH, with its stable secretion patterns irrespective of the menstrual cycle, serves as a robust indicator of the quantity of remaining oocytes, offering a reliable measure for ovarian reserve, predicting ovarian longevity and fertility potential. This makes AMH an indispensable tool in both fertility assessments for women contemplating delayed childbearing and in evaluating the risk of conditions like premature ovarian insufficiency. On the other hand, Inhibin B provides critical insights into ovarian function. Its levels peak during the early follicular phase and are closely tied to the growth of the dominant follicle, regulated by and in turn regulating Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH). This interplay offers a dynamic view of the real-time ovarian response, thus contributing to the chances of successful outcomes. The integration of these biomarkers and other common clinical indicators into AI-driven diagnostic tools marks a significant advancement in personalized medicine. Such tools leverage complex algorithms to analyze biomarker levels and predict individual reproductive outcomes with greater accuracy. The future of these biomarkers in clinical practice looks promising, with ongoing research aimed at refining their predictive power and expanding their application. Innovations in biomarker technology and data analytics are expected to further enhance the precision of reproductive health diagnostics, enabling earlier and more accurate interventions that can lead to better health outcomes for women worldwide. By deepening the understanding of these hormonal interactions and their implications, the field moves closer to a more comprehensive and nuanced approach to managing reproductive health, illustrating the profound impact of integrating endocrine science with cutting-edge technology.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of TUNEL and SCSA Methods for Assessing Sperm DNA Fragmentation on the Sperm-Cyto Platform.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.authors: Yakimova AS, Hegaj AD, Seliverstova AA et al.
articles.abstract: A comparative evaluation of two methods for assessing sperm DNA fragmentation was carried out: the visual TUNEL assay and the automated SCSA method utilizing the Sperm-Cyto flow cytometer. Semen samples (n = 30) from patients of reproductive age were examined. The results demonstrated a high degree of concordance between the two techniques: the mean DNA fragmentation index was 15.47 ± 5.56% for TUNEL and 15.20 ± 6.35% for SCSA. Statistical analysis revealed no significant differences between the methods (p = 0.9) and showed a strong positive correlation (r = 0.8; p < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis confirmed a minimal systematic bias (0.27 percentage points), indicating a slight tendency for TUNEL to overestimate values compared to SCSA, with limits of agreement ranging from -7.7 to 8.2 percentage points. Regression analysis further confirmed the absence of significant systematic bias. These findings confirm the interchangeability of the TUNEL and SCSA methods in the clinical diagnosis of male factor infertility. Furthermore, the SCSA method may be considered preferable for routine use in embryology laboratories.

articles.title: Exploring family support and conflict in intergenerational co-parenting families: scale development study.
articles.authors: Guan Z, Zhao R, Li H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing family support scales often fail to capture the culturally specific structure and role expectations within Chinese families. This study aimed to develop and validate a culturally grounded, role-differentiated measure of family support and conflict among Chinese postpartum women in intergenerational co-parenting families.
METHODS: Drawing on literature review, interviews, and principal component analysis, the Postpartum Family Interaction Scale (PFIS), comprising 12 factors across both support and conflict dimensions and distinguishing between partner and parental sources as perceived by postpartum women, was developed. A total of 528 postpartum women completed the scale. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), measurement invariance tests, internal consistency, construct validity, and predictive validity for postpartum depressive symptoms were examined.
RESULTS: The PFIS presented a 12-factor structure with high reliability and validity. The 12 factors are intergenerational emotional/instrumental/ informational support, intergenerational emotional/instrumental/ informational conflict, partner emotional/instrumental/ informational support, and partner emotional/instrumental/ informational conflict. Specifically, partner emotional and informational support significantly predicted lower postpartum depressive symptoms, while partner emotional conflict and Intergenerational instrumental and informational conflict were positively associated with increased depression.
CONCLUSIONS: The PFIS shows strong psychometric properties and provides a culturally and relationally nuanced tool for assessing postpartum family dynamics in Chinese families. It enables targeted assessment and supports the development of more precise, role-specific family interventions in maternal mental health support.

articles.title: The impact of anxiety on menopausal symptom severity: findings from a second-order confirmatory factor analysis.
articles.authors: Hoseinzadeh F, Esmaily H, Saki A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety disorders are prevalent and contribute substantially to the global burden of disease. During the menopausal transition, women may experience anxiety and depressive mood alongside menopausal symptoms. This study evaluated a hypothesized model of the associations between anxiety, depressive mood, and menopausal symptom severity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study, conducted in Mashhad, Iran, assessed menopausal symptom severity using the validated Iranian version of the MSSI-38 questionnaire in 664 premenopausal, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal women. The analysis examined direct and indirect associations, with depressive mood specified as a potential mediator.
RESULTS: Among all participants, 246 (37.0%) experienced relatively severe anxiety symptoms, while 172 (25.9%) experienced relatively severe depressive mood symptoms. In the first-order confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) model, the goodness-of-fit indices were CFI = 0.895, TLI = 0.879, and RMSEA = 0.055. Model 3, the adjusted second-order CFA model, showed CFI = 0.958, TLI = 0.953, and RMSEA = 0.034. These findings support associations between anxiety, depressive mood, and menopausal symptom severity. Life events, underlying disease, adequate income, marital status, and physical activity were among the factors associated with menopausal symptom severity.
CONCLUSION: This study identified associations between anxiety, depressive mood, and menopausal symptom severity. Considering anxiety and depressive mood may be relevant to the assessment and management of menopausal symptoms; however, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal or causal relationships.

articles.title: NOTCH3 deficiency contributes to mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Wu D, Tang X, Yin F et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE), a major cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity, is characterized by impaired trophoblast invasion and defective spiral artery remodeling. Although these pathological features are well-established, their underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. In this study, we identified a significant downregulation of NOTCH3 in PE placentas. Our findings demonstrated that NOTCH3 deficiency led to increased apoptosis of trophoblast cells and impaired their proliferation, migration, and invasion, which is associated with altered gene expression related to mitochondrial function, loss of mitochondrial mass, and disruption of mitochondrial biogenesis. Our mechanistic studies uncovered transcription factor A, mitochondrial (TFAM) and fructose-bisphosphatase 2 (FBP2) as target genes of NOTCH3 that are responsible for mitochondrial regulation. We demonstrated that NOTCH3 positively regulates TFAM and negatively regulates FBP2 through upregulating the expression of HEY1, a known NOTCH target gene. Therefore, NOTCH3 deficiency decreases TFAM expression and increases FBP2 expression, impairing mitochondrial biogenesis in trophoblast cells, which was rescued by TFAM overexpression in our in vitro model. This molecular mechanism was validated in an L-NAME-induced PE rat model, human PE placentas, and primary trophoblasts. Collectively, our findings define the role of NOTCH3 deficiency in the pathogenesis of PE. Through characterization of NOTCH3-HEY1-FBP2/TFAM axis, we provided new mechanistic insight into NOTCH3-regulated mitochondrial biogenesis and its relevance to human diseases like placenta disorders.

articles.title: What is the association between mode of delivery at birth and childhood adiposity? Findings from the Southampton Women's Survey.
articles.authors: Crozier S, Galani S, Barton SJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a major public health concern. Caesarean section (CS) delivery has been linked to increased childhood adiposity; however, the literature is inconsistent.
AIMS: To examine the associations between mode of delivery at birth and adiposity in childhood and whether they differ by type of CS (planned versus emergency).
METHODS: The Southampton Women's Survey recruited 12,583 non-pregnant women between 1998 and 2002 in Southampton, UK. From 3153 women who had liveborn singleton infants followed up after birth, mode of delivery was recorded and adiposity measured at age 4, 6-7 and 8-9 years. Outcome measures were child body mass index (BMI) and fat mass and body fat percentage measured by Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry. Associations were investigated using mixed-effects linear regression models after multiple imputation by chained equations, adjusting for maternal (adiposity, age, education, pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, smoking during pregnancy) and child-related confounders (birthweight, sex, gestational age), ascertained using a Directed Acyclic Graph.
RESULTS: 16% of the women had an emergency CS, and 8% a planned CS. Adjusted analyses showed that CS (versus vaginal delivery) was associated with increased offspring adiposity, with the magnitude of association increasing with the age of the child. For example, compared to children born vaginally, those born via CS had an average fat mass percentage 0.09 standard deviations (95% CI 0.00, 0.18, p = 0.04) higher and showed a 0.03 standard deviation (95% CI 0.01, 0.06; p = 0.009) greater increase in body fat percentage per year. Emergency CS was associated with increased adiposity compared to assisted vaginal delivery, particularly for BMI and fat mass outcomes.
CONCLUSION: CS-delivered babies had higher childhood BMI, fat mass and body fat percentage. Emergency CS accounted for most CS deliveries and was associated with increased adiposity. The findings support important effects of maternal and early life factors on long-term health outcomes.

articles.title: Differential Effects of Potassium Channel Modulators on Mouse Sperm Motility and Function.
articles.authors: Ibadin NO, Diaz FJ
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding sperm function is important to maximize fertility in assisted reproduction and for development of male contraceptives.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of potassium channel modulators on mouse sperm motility and function.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A broad non-specific potassium channel blocker (TEAC), a KCNJ/Kir2.x-specific inhibitor (PA-6), and a potassium ionophore (valinomycin) were used. A comprehensive CASA analysis was performed to evaluate sperm motility parameters. Membrane integrity (hypo-osmotic membrane swelling) and presence of acrosome were also evaluated. To assess the direct effect of potassium channel modulators on sperm membrane potential, non-capacitated sperm was loaded with the voltage-sensitive dye DiBAC4(3) and changes in fluorescence over time were analyzed. Immunocytochemistry and western blot using Kir 2.1, Kir 2.2, and Kir 2.4 antibodies were utilized to assess the localization and expression of Kir2.X channels in mouse sperm.
RESULTS: The results reveal a complex interplay between these modulators and various aspects of sperm function. Valinomycin emerged as the most potent inhibitor, significantly reducing both progressive (9.67 ± 2.71, p = 0.0066) and total motility (23.95 ± 3.60, p = 0.0303) compared to control (26.20 ± 3.18 and 39.48 ± 3.97 respectively). While TEAC and PA-6 did not significantly affect these parameters (p = 0.3484 and p = 0.3389 respectively), all three modulators decreased sperm curvilinear velocity (TEAC, 38.71 ± 5.61 µm/s p = 0.0277; PA-6, 33.85 ± 4.00 µm/s, p = 0.0067; valinomycin, 22.28 ± 1.14 µm/s, compared to control (62.60 ± 8.11, p = 0.0002). PA-6 and valinomycin reduced sperm hyperactivation (PA-6, 0.97 ± 0.95, p = 0.0488 and valinomycin 0.48 ± 0.48, p = 0.0336, control 8.27 ± 3.90), with valinomycin also compromising sperm membrane integrity (11.68 ± 5.14, compared to control 37.70 ± 7.95, p = 0.0254). However, TEAC increased acrosome reaction by 43.5% compared to controls cells. PA-6 produced a rapid and sustained decrease in DiBAC4(3) fluorescence relative to control, consistent with membrane hyperpolarization in non-capacitated sperm, whereas TEAC had minimal effect on basal membrane potential. Immunocytochemistry further revealed that the inward rectifier potassium channels Kir2.1, Kir2.2, and Kir2.4 are expressed in mouse sperm with distinct, compartmentalized localization: Kir2.1 in the post-acrosomal head region, Kir2.2 along the…

articles.title: Lupus Nephritis in Pregnancy: A Case-Based Approach to Diagnosis and Management.
articles.authors: Ankawi G, Lightstone L, Koubar SH
articles.abstract: Pregnancy presents both a unique opportunity to diagnose previously unrecognized lupus nephritis (LN) and a critical period that influences long-term renal and maternal outcomes in women with established disease. For many young women, pregnancy represents their first significant interaction with the healthcare system. Abnormal findings such as persistent hematuria or proteinuria should not be dismissed as physiologic changes of pregnancy; rather, they should prompt appropriate evaluation for underlying kidney disease. In selected cases, kidney biopsy remains an important diagnostic tool during pregnancy when the results are expected to alter management. In women with established LN, disease activity at conception is the strongest modifiable predictor of maternal and fetal outcomes. Consequently, pregnancy should ideally be planned during sustained disease quiescence, underscoring the importance of preconception counseling, avoidance of unplanned pregnancies, and optimization of pregnancy-compatible immunosuppressive therapy. Pregnancy in women with LN poses several unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, including risk stratification, medication adjustments, prevention of disease flares, and management of maternal and fetal complications. A major clinical challenge is differentiating an LN flare from preeclampsia, as both conditions share overlapping clinical and laboratory features but require fundamentally different management strategies. Advances in angiogenic biomarkers, fetal surveillance, and multidisciplinary care have improved the ability to distinguish these conditions and optimize outcomes. Using a real clinical case scenario, this review discusses current evidence on the diagnosis and management of LN before and during pregnancy, including preconception counseling, disease monitoring, therapeutic considerations, and maternal and fetal risk assessment, emphasizing the importance of individualized, multidisciplinary care.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of the Oral Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Antagonist DW4902 for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding in Uterine Fibroids: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase II Trial.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Song JY, Park JY, Choi YS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of DW4902, a novel oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist, in premenopausal women with uterine fibroids and heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB).
DESIGN: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II trial.
SETTING: Twelve tertiary hospitals in Korea.
POPULATION: Premenopausal women with uterine fibroids and heavy menstrual bleeding, defined as a screening pictorial blood assessment chart score (PBAC) ≥ 120.
METHODS: Seventy-one women with uterine fibroids, HMB (screening PBAC ≥ 120) and other predefined criteria were randomized to placebo or DW4902 160, 240 or 320 mg once daily.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the proportion achieving PBAC < 10 during Weeks 6-12. Secondary endpoints included amenorrhea, haemoglobin change, fibroid and uterine volumes, pain scores, bone mineral density and safety.
RESULTS: During Weeks 6-12, PBAC < 10 was achieved by 73.33%-100.00% of participants receiving DW4902 160, 240 and 320 mg (p < 0.0001). Amenorrhea rates were likewise significantly higher in the DW4902 groups (≥ 73.33%), with bleeding suppression evident from Weeks 2 to 6. Haemoglobin levels increased significantly in the 160 and 240 mg groups. Fibroid and uterine volumes and fibroid-related pain were significantly reduced across all DW4902 dose groups. Hormone levels recovered after treatment discontinuation, and lumbar spine bone mineral density showed modest, reversible changes. Adverse events were mostly mild and comparable between groups, with no serious drug-related events.
CONCLUSIONS: DW4902 demonstrated a robust efficacy in reducing menstrual bleeding and improving fibroid-related outcomes with an acceptable short-term safety and bone density profile.

articles.title: Association of adverse perinatal outcomes of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy with maternal serum bile acid profiles.
articles.authors: Gou L, Wu X, Yin X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, yet current monitoring lacks predictive accuracy. This study aimed to explore alterations in serum bile acid profiles and their relationship with adverse perinatal outcomes in ICP.
METHODS: This study enrolled 149 pregnant women, including 77 normal pregnant women and 72 cases with ICP, subdivided into ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes and those without according to the perinatal outcomes. Serum concentrations of 15 bile acids were quantified using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and compared among the three groups.
RESULTS: ICP patients exhibited significantly lower gestational age at delivery, Apgar scores, and birth weight, alongside higher rates of cesarean delivery, low birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and preterm birth (all p < 0.05). Twelve bile acids were significantly elevated in ICP (all p < 0.01); notably, taurolithocholic acid elevation was exclusive to the ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes. Glycocholic acid (GCA), glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA), taurocholic acid (TCA), taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA), tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA), and total bile acid levels positively correlated with adverse perinatal outcomes (all p < 0.05). The combined indicator of these six indicators demonstrated superior predictive efficacy for adverse perinatal outcomes with an area under the curve of 0.836, sensitivity of 73.0%, and specificity of 82.9%.
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct serum bile acid metabolic signatures characterize ICP patients with adverse perinatal outcomes. Elevated levels of total bile acids and conjugated bile acids, including GCA, GCDCA, TCA, TCDCA, and TUDCA, were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes and might serve as candidate biomarkers for risk prediction. The multi-bile acid combined indicator demonstrated superior exploratory predictive performance over individual markers, offering a potential tool for identifying high-risk ICP patients, which requires prospective external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Management of Infants Born to Mothers with Q Fever During Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Moore E, Silcock R, Magalhães RS et al.
articles.abstract: We conducted a systematic review of published literature from 1953-2021 for cases of infants born to mothers who had Q fever during pregnancy. We describe clinical management characteristics and neonatal outcomes for 11 case reports. No live-born infant had confirmed C. burnetii infection. Placental infection was identified in 4 cases; all infants tested negative. Uncommon adverse obstetric outcomes included preterm birth and low birthweight. There were no cases of transmission through breastmilk. Infection-control precautions ranged from standard to airborne. Evidence indicated that vertical transmission to the fetus or live-born infant is rare. Maternal illness and fetal loss appear related to placental infection. Separation of mother and infant or avoidance of breastfeeding are not supported. Management should prioritize placental handling precautions and structured infant follow-up. No published clinical consensus guidelines exist for management of infants born to mothers with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) during pregnancy. Global collaboration and evidence gathering can inform evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Routine Prenatal Ultrasound at 36 Weeks: Impact on Obstetric Clinical Outcomes.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Minopoli M, Ceffa S, Schwartz A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of introducing a routine prenatal ultrasound scan at 36 weeks' gestation, integrated with a predefined clinical management pathway, on obstetric outcomes.
DESIGN: Single-centre retrospective study.
SETTING: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London, UK.
POPULATION: 37 001 singleton term pregnancies delivered between April 2016 and October 2024.
METHODS: From January 2020, universal 36-week ultrasound replaced targeted scanning within a predefined national management pathway; its impact was assessed using interrupted time-series analysis (ITSA).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were gestational age at birth in SGA and LGA neonates, and prenatal detection rate of breech presentation. Secondary outcomes included rates of neonatal intensive care unit admission, severe perineal trauma, shoulder dystocia and stillbirth.
RESULTS: SGA infants delivered at 37-38 weeks' gestation increased from 18.7% to 38.1% post intervention (p = 0.04) with a concomitant overall reduction in NICU admissions (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.66-0.82). The prenatal detection rate of breech presentation increased significantly from 78% to almost 90% (p = 0.002). The intervention was also associated with a significant reduction in third- and fourth-degree perineal tears (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.65-0.84).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine 36-week scan embedded within a structured clinical management pathway was associated with significant changes in obstetric metrics and improved pregnancy outcome. Overall, these findings provide real-world evidence on how a universal third-trimester ultrasound may selectively influence obstetric management and inform the ongoing debate on routine prenatal screening strategies.

articles.title: Phenotypic Severity Determines Overall Pregnancy Outcome and Survival in Fetuses With Turner Syndrome: Insights From a Large Multicenter Cohort.
articles.authors: Bedei I, Bruder J, Windhorst AC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate survival in fetuses with prenatally diagnosed Turner syndrome (TS) according to karyotype and phenotypic severity, and to estimate minimal survival (MS) proportions across cytogenetic subgroups.
METHODS: Retrospective multicentre cohort study including fetuses with prenatal TS diagnosed between 2000 and 2024. Karyotypes were classified as 45,X; mosaic; or structural X-chromosome anomalies. Phenotypic severity was defined by major structural abnormalities on prenatal imaging. Survival analyses and Cox proportional hazard models were applied. MS was calculated as the proportion of Live births (LB) relative to elective terminations (ET) and Spontaneous intrauterine deaths (SID) within each karyotype group.
RESULTS: Among 726 pregnancies, 451 (62.1%) were ET, 275 (37.9%) continued; of these, 98 (35.6%) resulted in LB and 177 (64.4%) in SID. Severe phenotypes were present in 92.4% of terminations, 81.0% of SIDs and 33.0% of LB. Mosaic and structural karyotypes showed a lower risk of intrauterine death than 45,X (HR 0.28 and 0.32), while severe phenotype strongly predicted mortality (HR 4.82). Most SIDs occurred before 30 weeks' gestation (median 21 weeks). MS was 9.6% for 45,X, 50.0% for mosaic and 36.8% for structural variants.
CONCLUSION: Survival in prenatally diagnosed TS is higher than historically reported. Phenotypic severity is the principal determinant of outcome.

articles.title: Qualitative multistakeholder enquiry into provider-client interactions during contraceptive counselling in Lagos and Kano states, Nigeria.
articles.authors: OlaOlorun FM, Morhason-Bello IO, Abubakar HD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality contraceptive counselling is essential for empowering women to make informed reproductive health decisions, yet there is limited understanding of how counselling practices align with established quality standards in diverse settings.
OBJECTIVE: This qualitative study explored the alignment between a standard definition of quality contraceptive counselling and actual practices in Lagos and Kano states, Nigeria, capturing multistakeholder perspectives.
METHODS: The study was qualitative and descriptive in design with data collected through in-depth interviews. Participants were recruited from four primary healthcare facilities and the communities they serve in Lagos and Kano states, Nigeria. 99 participants were purposively selected comprising female clients (n=49), male clients/partners (n=33), family planning providers and community health workers (n=6), community opinion leaders and non-governmental organisation representatives (n=5) and policymakers (n=6). Data were analysed using thematic analysis with deductive coding structured by the elements in Holt et al’s quality in contraceptive counselling framework.
RESULTS: An implementation gap was uncovered. While alignment with the definition of quality contraceptive counselling was initially affirmed, deeper inquiry revealed deficiencies. Needs assessments by providers were often superficial, and counselling was sometimes conducted in groups, limiting personalisation, though use of local languages was a strength. Decision-making support was hampered by workload of providers and resource constraints. Respect was generally shown, but visual privacy was often inadequate. Contextual differences were key: providers in Kano emphasised spousal involvement, while those in Lagos occasionally accommodated covert use.
CONCLUSIONS: Counselling in these settings often falls short of person-centred ideals due to systemic barriers like workload, resource shortages and sociocultural norms. To improve quality and client agency, we recommend standardising counselling protocols, retraining providers, allocating resources better and tailoring approaches to local contexts.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06081842.

articles.title: Scientific basis and methodological framework of a double-blinded prospective randomized clinical trial comparing euploidy rates among embryos created from sibling oocytes exposed to sperm after ultrashort abstinence compared to standard abstinence.
articles.authors: Hallisey S, Ni D, Paganetti E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male factor infertility contributes to a significant portion of infertility in couples. It is important to identify strategies to improve sperm's contribution to embryo development and quality. Currently, the recommended abstinence period for providing a sperm sample for use in IVF is extrapolated from semen analysis guidelines. Evidence suggests that a shorter period of abstinence may improve sperm DNA fragmentation, embryological, clinical and genetic outcomes. The primary aim of this study is to compare euploidy rates between embryos created from sibling oocytes exposed to sperm after an ultrashort period of abstinence (1 h) compared to standard abstinence (2-5 days).
METHODS: This is a double-blinded, prospective, randomized sibling oocyte trial in patients undergoing IVF with intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) or standard insemination and preimplantation genetic testing (PGT). On retrieval day, each patient's oocytes will be divided into two groups and randomized to exposure to sperm produced after an ultrashort period of abstinence (1 h) or a standard period of abstinence (2-5 days). All embryos will be biopsied for PGT to assess euploidy rates. If a euploid embryo is available, a frozen embryo transfer (FET) will occur in a subsequent cycle. Ancillary studies will evaluate the impact of an ultrashort period of abstinence on sperm DNA fragmentation and methylation.
CONCLUSION: This study will investigate whether providing a sperm sample after a shorter period of abstinence improves embryo euploidy for those undergoing IVF with PGT. In doing so, this study may inform future recommendations for abstinence prior to retrieval day for IVF.

articles.title: Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.
articles.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
articles.authors: Morgan RD, Burghel GJ, Shaw JM et al.
articles.abstract: Low-coverage whole-genome sequencing offers a scalable approach to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing in ovarian cancer. This multi-centre study describes the real-world implementation of one such assay, SeqOne SomaHRD, across four European laboratories between 9 January 2023 and 1 October 2025. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive if they had a Genomic Instability score (GIS) of ≥0.50 (GIS-high) and/or a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. GIS was generated from two bioinformatically derived measures of genomic instability: Large-scale Genomic Alterations (LGA) and Loss of Parental Copy (LPC). A GIS was generated for 2,608/2,625 (99.4%) tumours: GIS-high in 765 (29.3%), GIS-low in 1,684 (64.6%), and GIS-inconclusive in 159 (6.1%). BRCA1/2 genotype was available for 1,226/2,625 (46.7%) tumours, of which 142 (11.6%) had a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. Of the 1,130 tumours with both a reportable GIS and known BRCA1/2 genotype, 413 (36.5%) had HRD-positive status, including 135 with a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant and 278 (24.6%) with BRCA1/2 wild-type and GIS-high. Clinical turnaround time was ≤21 days for 2,573/2,625 (98.0%) tumours. Decentralised, low-coverage whole-genome sequencing generated a GIS for ovarian cancer within a consistently practical turnaround time and with a low rate of inconclusive results, identifying 278/1,130 (24.6%) evaluable tumours as HRD-positive based on genomic instability alone, without a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant.

articles.title: Targeted Long-Read Sequencing Enables Extended-Family-Independent PGT-M for HBB-Haemoglobinopathies.
articles.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
articles.authors: Romanou AF, Tšuiko O, Tomazou M et al.
articles.abstract: Targeted long-read sequencing (T-LRS) can integrate direct variant detection and haplotype phasing within a single molecular diagnostic assay for preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). An Oxford Nanopore-based T-LRS workflow was developed and validated for extended-family-independent PGT-M in HBB-haemoglobinopathies using 49 samples from ten family trios and two clinical PGT-M cycles. Extended-family-independent denotes preclinical establishment of parental haplotypes using genomic DNA from both prospective parents without requiring segregation data from additional relatives. Long-range PCR amplification of the HBB locus enables co-detection and phasing of pathogenic variants with flanking single-nucleotide variants, followed by inheritance assessment in offspring genomic DNA, whole-genome-amplified few-cell samples, and trophectoderm biopsies. Across successfully analysed samples, T-LRS achieved >200× coverage with Q20+ reads, allowing accurate detection of single-nucleotide variants, indels, and a large deletion. An average of 34.2 ± 19.0 single-nucleotide variants per family were available for haplotype reconstruction. Parental allele assignment and embryo genotypes showed complete concordance with expected inheritance patterns and established diagnostic methods. Overlapping amplicons provided internal quality control and mitigated allelic dropout risk. This standardized, locus-targeted workflow demonstrated analytical performance equivalent to that of conventional PGT-M assays within this cohort while reducing preclinical assay-development time and avoiding the need for additional relatives. These findings establish a proof-of-concept framework for scalable, cost-effective molecular diagnostics for HBB-haemoglobinopathies, with potential extension to other monogenic disorders.

articles.title: Natural-abundance carbon isotope profiling of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplement incorporation in extremely preterm infants: a sub-study of the Mega Donna Mega randomized clinical trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Chen CT, Sjöbom U, Andersson MX et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extremely preterm infants are deprived of most third-trimester long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid accretion. In the Mega Donna Mega trial, enteral arachidonic acid (ARA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) supplementation reduced severe retinopathy of prematurity despite modest early changes in circulating levels.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated whether natural-abundance carbon isotope ratio (δ13C) profiling detects early entry of supplemented ARA and DHA into circulating phospholipids in extremely preterm infants.
METHODS: This sub-study of the randomized Mega Donna Mega trial included 25 infants born before 25+2 weeks' gestation who received standard-of-care nutrition (SOC, n=12) or enteral ARA+DHA supplementation (intervention, n=13; 100 and 50 mg/kg/day, respectively) from ≤3 days after birth until 40 weeks' postmenstrual age. Serum phospholipid fatty acid composition and δ13C values were determined at Day 0-3, 10-16, 34-47, and 75-87. Group differences were assessed with mixed models of treatment group by sampling window.
RESULTS: Between-group differences in ARA and DHA weight percent (wt%) emerged late in the intervention (Day 75-87, mean [SD]: ARA 10.1 [2.0] versus 6.9 [1.4]; DHA 3.3 [1.0] versus 2.3 [0.7]). ARA and DHA δ13C were similar between groups at Day 0-3 and higher in supplemented infants from Day 10-16 (difference [95% CI]: ARA 1.9 [0.9, 2.8] mUr; DHA 2.0 [0.3, 3.6] mUr). The group-by-window interaction was significant for ARA δ13C (p=0.007) but not for DHA δ13C (p=0.11; p=0.005 after excluding one infant with necrotizing enterocolitis and low compliance).
CONCLUSIONS: Natural-abundance δ13C profiling showed that supplemented ARA and DHA were bioavailable and entered circulating phospholipids within two weeks of birth, before clear separation in fatty acid composition. Concentration-based biomarkers may underestimate early exposure to supplemented fatty acids in extremely preterm infants.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03201588, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03201588.

articles.title: ChatGPT versus Google Search-linked responses to surgical and fertility-related endometriosis questions: a cross-sectional content analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Ozkaya B, Ozkaya EB, Cote S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare guideline concordance, safety, actionability, and readability of ChatGPT and Google Search-linked responses to patient-facing surgical and fertility-related endometriosis questions.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional comparative digital content analysis of 40 prespecified questions across diagnosis/imaging, minimally invasive surgery, deep organ-involving disease, and fertility/ovarian reserve. For each question, one ChatGPT response and one Google Search-linked response archived on May 31, 2026 were scored independently by two physicians with platform and source identifiers concealed; readability was assessed using Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Flesch Reading Ease (FRES), and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG).
RESULTS: Eighty responses were analyzed. ChatGPT responses were longer than Google Search-linked responses (52.6 ± 3.9 vs 38.6 ± 4.0 words). ChatGPT had a higher overall clinical quality score (4.91 ± 0.11 vs 4.53 ± 0.23; paired mean difference, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.45), driven by completeness (0.94; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.10) and actionability (0.60; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.73). Safety scores were similarly high, and no response was judged harmful or misleading. Mean grade-level estimates for both platforms exceeded the sixth-grade reference benchmark.
CONCLUSION: In this controlled set of surgical and fertility-related endometriosis questions, ChatGPT responses received higher completeness and actionability ratings than Google Search-linked answers, with similarly high safety ratings. Both platforms had mean grade-level estimates above the sixth-grade reference benchmark, supporting clinician-reviewed educational use and further assessment of patient comprehension.

articles.title: Metabolomic profiling reveals a BMI-independent metabolic signature in Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.authors: Maraşlı U, Aksun S, Kablan SE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a common heterogeneous endocrine disorder characterized by metabolic alterations extending beyond obesity and androgen excess. This study aimed to define body mass index (BMI)-independent plasma metabolomic signature of PMOS and to evaluate associations with hyperandrogenism.
METHODS: Forty women with PMOS (mean age:22.9 ± 2.7 years; mean BMI:23.4 ± 4.6 kg/m2) and 40 age- and BMI-matched healthy women underwent clinical, biochemical, and hormonal assessment. Plasma metabolomic profiling was performed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Data were analyzed by principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), false discovery rate (FDR)-adjusted univariate analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and pathway enrichment analysis.
RESULTS: PCA and PLS-DA demonstrated clear separation between the PMOS and healthy control groups, with PLS-DA showing high discriminatory performance (accuracy = 0.95, R2 = 0.92, Q2 = 0.78; permutation test p = 0.002). After FDR correction, 31 metabolites differed significantly between groups. Threitol, a four‑carbon sugar alcohol was the strongest discriminatory metabolite (fold change = 5.86, FDR = 3.59 × 10-14) with an AUC of 0.995 (95% CI: 0.980-1.000), 95% sensitivity, and 100% specificity at the optimal cutoff. Cross-validated analysis using a linear support vector machine confirmed its discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.993, 95% CI: 0.976-1.000). Pathway analysis identified significant alterations in BCAA metabolism, alanine-aspartate-glutamate metabolism, and the citrate cycle. Threitol was inversely correlated with total testosterone, free androgen index, and AMH (all p < 0.001), whereas palmitoylcarnitine was positively correlated with total testosterone (r = 0.35, p = 0.001) and enoxolone was negatively correlated with both total testosterone (r = -0.34, p = 0.002) and AMH (r = -0.35, p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Metabolomic profiling identifies a BMI-independent metabolic signature in PMOS characterized by alterations in BCAAs and energy metabolism. Targeted associations between specific metabolites and androgen levels support the utility of refined metabolic phenotyping in PMOS.

articles.title: AI-assisted liquid biopsy for early breast cancer detection: a laboratory translation framework for future multimodal integration.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.authors: Alhazmi BA, Jaiswal V, Rekha A et al.
articles.abstract: Early breast cancer detection is imaging-dependent in clinical laboratory medicine, and there are important limitations for interval cancers and women with dense breasts. Liquid biopsy is being developed as an adjunct to imaging and tissue diagnosis. There are two classes of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) features and a separate class of extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated biomarkers, such as microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and proteins, to consider in the proposed framework. These literature reviews primarily focus on combinations of individual modalities, cfDNA-only combinations, cfDNA-protein panels, and multicancer models. There is a lack of prospective clinical validation of a machine learning model that integrates all three modalities for the early detection of breast cancer. We categorized performance evidence based on the purpose of the test for average-risk screening, dense breast triage, symptomatic assessment, high-risk surveillance, recurrence monitoring for breast cancer, and metastatic disease detection, and differentiated between direct breast cancer evidence and indirect methodological analogies. Translation involves modality-specific specimen processing, modality-specific analytical and clinical validation, locked/version-controlled pipelines, patient-, site-, and time-level data partitioning, leakage control, pre-specified thresholds and abstention rules, calibration assessment, external validation, subgroup analyses, reportable quality-control metrics, and defined revalidation triggers.

articles.title: The cholesterol-efflux capacity of follicular fluid HDL predicts normal fertilization in modified natural cycle-IVF.
articles.authors: Jia C, Wu W, Groen H et al.
articles.abstract: High-density lipoproteins (HDL) are the primary lipoprotein subclass in follicular fluid (FF), and their role in reproduction is gaining attention. This study aimed to determine whether the cholesterol efflux capacity of HDL particles in FF has clinical relevance for reproductive outcomes in modified natural cycle in-vitro fertilization (MNC-IVF). A total of 297 FF samples from MNC-IVF procedures (n=185 patients) at a single academic center were available for analysis. The cholesterol efflux capacity of HDL was determined using 3H-cholesterol-labeled human THP-1-derived macrophage foam cells. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy was used to characterize HDL particles in FF, including sizes, particle numbers, HDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein A-I levels. The association of HDL-related parameters with IVF outcomes, including normal fertilization, embryo fragmentation, development of top-quality embryos or biochemical and clinical pregnancy, was assessed using generalized estimating equations. A better follicular fluid HDL cholesterol efflux capacity was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of normal in vitro fertilization of the oocyte (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.40). Smaller HDL particles dominated in FF, supporting entry from the general circulation via the size-selective blood-follicle barrier. Furthermore, HDL cholesterol levels, HDL particle numbers or apolipoprotein A-I in FF showed no association with reproductive outcomes. These results illustrate a potential evolutionary role of HDL beyond its traditional association with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The cholesterol efflux capacity of follicular fluid HDL might serve as a biomarker for oocyte quality and in vitro fertilization potential, emphasizing its significance in reproductive processes.

articles.title: Retinopathy of prematurity: causes, treatment and prevention.
articles.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
articles.authors: Smith LEH, Komatsu H, Pivodic A et al.
articles.abstract: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is initiated at preterm birth. Vascular growth in the immature retina, conditioned to low intrauterine oxygen levels, is disrupted by rapid increases in oxygen which suppress oxygen-regulated growth factors. Maternally sourced essential lipids (ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids) and insulin-like growth factor-1 are also lost. Later, maturing (but avascular) retina becomes hypoxic and nutrient starved, driving a growth factor surge often causing destructive neovascularization. Current treatments address late-stage neovascular ROP by suppressing elevated vascular endothelial growth factor levels. Recent clinical studies address the initiating events, lack of specific maternally sourced lipids and growth factors, hyperoxia-induced metabolic changes, which induce suppression of normal retinal vascularization and retinal neural maturation. Early enteral supplementation with ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids reduces risk of neovascularization. Timed topical corticosteroids during early ROP which alter metabolism to promote normal vessel growth, show great promise in preventing severe disease. Risk algorithms with near 100% sensitivity and high specificity can reduce the number of screening examinations. AI-augmented photography and ultrawide field optical coherence tomography may further refine prediction, diagnosis and treatment. This review synthesizes recent clinical paradigm shifts toward early disease prevention, highlighting how novel metabolic, pharmacological, and digital health strategies can prevent ROP-related vision loss.

articles.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Follicular Fluid and in Vitro Fertilisation Outcomes: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Xiong X, Si M, Liu M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between follicular-fluid polymer concentrations and in vitro fertilisation (IVF) outcomes.
DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.
SETTING: An academic fertility centre in Beijing, China.
POPULATION: A total of 203 women, of whom 158 were undergoing their first embryo transfer, after excluding seven women who underwent preimplantation genetic testing.
METHODS: Polymer concentrations in follicular fluid were measured using pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were used to assess the associations between polymer concentrations and IVF outcomes.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Live birth was the primary outcome; clinical pregnancy and embryological outcomes were secondary outcomes.
RESULTS: Live birth occurred in 62 women (30.54% per included cycle; 39.24% per embryo transfer). For each standard-deviation increase in ln(polyvinyl chloride concentration + 1), adjusted coefficients were -1.328 (95% confidence interval [CI] -2.218 to -0.439) for the number of oocytes retrieved, -0.900 (95% CI -1.541 to -0.258) for the number of two-pronuclear zygotes and -0.599 (95% CI -1.057 to -0.140) for the number of good-quality embryos. The corresponding adjusted odds ratios were 0.547 (95% CI 0.360-0.829) for clinical pregnancy and 0.598 (95% CI 0.403-0.888) for live birth. Neither polystyrene nor polyamide 66 was statistically associated with these outcomes after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher follicular-fluid polyvinyl chloride concentrations were associated with poorer reproductive outcomes. These observational findings still require confirmation in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Injectable Hyaluronic Acid for Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Menabrito M, Calaf J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a chronic condition resulting from oestrogen deficiency and characterised by persistent genital, sexual, and urinary symptoms that can substantially impair quality of life. While local oestrogen therapy is highly effective, a significant proportion of women are unable or unwilling to use hormonal treatments, highlighting the need for effective non-hormonal options.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review examines local, non-hormonal approaches to GSM, with a particular emphasis on injectable hyaluronic acid-based therapies.
MAIN FINDINGS: Hyaluronic acid is integral to tissue hydration, viscoelasticity, and the maintenance of extracellular matrix integrity, processes that are compromised in GSM. Topical formulations are commonly used to provide surface hydration and symptom relief, while injectable approaches deliver hyaluronic acid to deeper tissue layers; the potential implications for the magnitude and duration of clinical benefit require further evaluation. Among injectable formulations, hybrid cooperative complex hyaluronic acid (HCC-HA) has been evaluated in small prospective studies and one randomised trial in women with sexual dysfunction rather than strictly defined GSM. Available studies report potential improvements in some symptoms, including vaginal dryness and dyspareunia. However, improvements were not demonstrated across all assessed outcomes, including certain sexual-function and quality-of-life measures. No serious adverse events were reported in the available studies, although larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to characterise the safety profile more fully.
CONCLUSIONS: Injectable hyaluronic acid-based therapies are emerging non-hormonal interventions for vulvovaginal symptoms associated with GSM. Current evidence does not yet establish their role as routine or guideline-recommended treatments. This evidentiary position should be considered separately from the intended purpose and regulatory status of individual devices. Larger independent trials, longer-term safety data, and health-economic evaluations are needed to define their comparative clinical role.

articles.title: Age and sex related differences on genotype stratified CYP450 mediated metabolism rate in healthy populations; a systematic review.
articles.journal: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology
articles.authors: Schaars KK, Bedi S, PSY-PGx Consortium et al.
articles.abstract: Variability in drug response is common, with up to 70% of patients experiencing insufficient efficacy or adverse drug reactions. While genetic polymorphisms in cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes explain part of this variability, factors such as sex and age may also be important. This systematic review summarizes evidence on sex- and age-related differences five CYP isoforms (CYP1A2, CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and CYP2D6). A search in MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Embase identified 23 studies combining CYP genotyping and phenotyping, of which 15 contributed to the sex analysis and 6 to the age analysis. Databases were searched up to 9 February 2026. Findings were heterogeneous, reflecting differences in study design, probe substrates, and genotyping panels. Some studies suggested higher CYP1A2 activity in males, while smoking was more consistently associated with higher activity. Oral contraceptive use was consistently associated with reduced enzyme activity in females. Limited midazolam-based evidence suggested modestly higher CYP3A activity in females, while one study reported discordant findings with endogenous markers. One study suggested a decrease in CYP3A activity with age. Limited evidence from two studies suggested lower CYP2C9 activity in females. For CYP2C19, results were mixed, but oral contraceptive use reduced activity and age-related decline was reported. Limited adult evidence suggested lower CYP2D6 activity in females within genotype groups. In infants, CYP2D6 activity was detectable early and remained relatively stable throughout the first year of life. Overall, sex- and age-related differences in CYP activity appear enzyme- and context-specific, but the heterogeneous evidence does not support sex- or age-based dose adjustment.

articles.title: Quinestrol induces cardiac impairments associated with MAPK and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway: A comprehensive biochemical, radiological, and histopathological investigation.
articles.authors: Ashfaq H, Jamil S, Otifi HM et al.
articles.abstract: Quinestrol (QNL) is a potent, long-acting synthetic estrogen which is historically used in contraceptive applications and currently employed primarily as a fertility-control agent for rodent population management. However, QNL intoxication caused severe organ damage including cardiotoxicity. The current study was conducted to explore cardiotoxic impacts of QNL at different dose concentrations. Thirty-two Sprague-Dawley rats were divided into four groups including control, QNL (0.1 mg/kg), QNL (1 mg/kg), and QNL (10 mg/kg) treated group. QNL intoxication significantly upregulated the expression of MAPK1, MAPK3, MAPK8, MAPK9, MAPK14, FOS, and JUN along with suppression of PIK3CA, AKT1, MTOR, RPS6KB1, and EIF4EBP1. The endogenous antioxidant enzymes (CAT, SOD, GPx, GST, GSR, GSH and HO-1) were significantly suppressed while the levels of ROS & MDA were elevated after QNL intoxication. Progressive ventricular remodeling and increase in ventricular dimension, wall thickness, end diastolic volume, end systolic volume and decrease in heart rate were observed after QNL exposure. There was significant increase in serum levels of CK-MB, CPK, LDH, cardiac troponin-I, BNP, NT-proBNP and CRP values, supporting myocardial injury following the administration of QNL. Moreover, QNL strongly regulated NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, COX-2, Bax, caspase-3, and caspase-9, while downregulating Bcl-2. The results were confirmed from the histopathological examination, which showed dosage dependent myocardial degeneration, inflammatory cell infiltration, oedema and vascular congestion, disorganization of myofibrillar structure and focal myocardial necrosis. Taken together, adverse effects of QNL exposure included dose-dependent myocardial injury, changes in oxidative status, elevation of inflammatory and apoptosis-associated markers, and echocardiographic abnormalities. The results suggest possible molecular alteration in cardiac damage in response to QNL treatment that warrant further cardiovascular safety studies.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance thermometry-based estimation of equivalent radiation dose and tumour control probability in combined radiotherapy and hyperthermia: a proof-of-concept and uncertainty study.
articles.authors: Carrapiço-Seabra C, Mingo Barba S, Godart J et al.
articles.abstract: To estimate the equivalent radiation dose in 2 Gy fractions (EQD2Gy) and tumour control probability (TCP) from probe based and magnetic resonance (MR) temperature measurements. In addition, we evaluate how uncertainties in MR thermometry affect these metrics in combined radiotherapy and hyperthermia for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC).Approach: Temperature data were collected from three patients with LACC treated with radiotherapy and MR guided deep hyperthermia (MRgHT). Intraluminal vaginal probes provided temperature measurements at surrogate locations, while MR thermometry enabled voxel-wise temperature mapping within the target volume. These data were used to estimate EQD2Gy and TCP for combined radiotherapy and hyperthermia treatments. To assess the robustness of MR-based estimates, systematic and random temperature errors were introduced into MR thermometry data using Gaussian error models to simulate artefacts. The resulting impact on temperature distributions, EQD2Gy and TCP was evaluated using standard deviation analysis and dose volume histograms.Main results: Probe-based temperatures ranged from 39.1-39.7 °C, resulting in EQD2Gy and TCP enhancements of 2.4-4.3 Gy and 20-57 %, respectively. MR-based temperatures were higher (39.4-40.3 °C), yielding EQD2Gy (3.4-7.1 Gy) and TCP (22-68 %). Systematic temperature errors produced changes of up to 2 Gy in EQD2Gy and 5 % in TCP. In contrast, random errors - more representative of typical MR thermometry artefacts - led to minimal deviations, with changes of approximately 0.2 Gy in EQD2Gy. Within clinically relevant temperature ranges, overall uncertainties remained limited to 0.7 Gy for EQD2Gy and 1 % for TCP.Significance: MR thermometry enables voxel-based estimation of biological treatment enhancement in combined radiotherapy and hyperthermia. Despite inherent temperature uncertainties, MR-based EQD2Gy and TCP estimates remain robust within clinical accuracy limits, supporting their use for treatment evaluation and future hyperthermia-informed treatment planning.

articles.title: Virtual reality to reduce anxiety during endometriosis-focused transvaginal sonography.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Berkowitz E, Mostafa J, Altshuler H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether an immersive three-dimensional virtual reality (VR) environment reduces patient anxiety during endometriosis-focused transvaginal sonography (eTVS). Secondary outcomes included pain intensity, physiologic parameters, and patient acceptability.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial, conducted at a tertiary referral center between December 2023 and August 2024, allocated women undergoing eTVS to VR distraction (VR-eTVS) or standard examination (Control). No a priori sample-size or power calculation was performed. Before and after the examination, participants completed the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory - State Anxiety Scale (STAI-S) and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain. Heart rate (HR) and mean arterial pressure (MAP) were also recorded. Women allocated for VR-eTVS reported their satisfaction and willingness to use the system again.
RESULTS: Of 155 women randomized (80 VR-eTVS; 75 control), four discontinued VR intervention. Baseline anxiety levels were comparable between groups. In the VR group, anxiety decreased significantly after examination [median STAI-S 45 (33-53) vs. 33 (26-44); P < 0.0001], accompanied by a reduction in HR [85 (78-97) vs. 79 (74-89); P = 0.003], while pain remained stable. In the control group, pain increased significantly [3 (0-6) vs. 5 (2-7); P = 0.01], with no significant change in anxiety. Post-procedural anxiety was significantly lower in the VR group compared with controls (P = 0.0001). In an intention-to-treat analysis of all 80 allocated VR participants, 86.3 % reported satisfaction with VR use, and 83.8 % indicated a willingness to use it again.
CONCLUSION: Immersive VR during eTVS was associated with reduced anxiety and stable pain scores. These findings warrant further evaluation in an adequately powered randomized trial.

articles.title: IVF outcome in patients with unexplained infertility after at least three failed IUI cycles: A propensity score-overlap weighted analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Luo R, Zhang C, Zhao Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of unexplained infertility (UI) following ≥3 failed intrauterine inseminations (IUIs) on reproductive outcomes in patients undergoing their first IVF cycle.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients aged <40 years who underwent their initial IVF cycle between July 1st, 2017, and June 30th, 2024. Among them, UI patients with ≥3 failed IUI attempts were assigned to the UI group, and patients with previous salpingectomy, tubal obstruction, or male infertility were assigned to the control group. The primary outcome was the cumulative live birth rate (cLBR). The secondary outcomes encompassed all measures related to the initial oocyte retrieval cycles and the subsequent fresh embryo transfer cycle. After propensity score-based overlap weighting, multivariate regression models were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORs) or β coefficients.
RESULTS: In this overlap-weighted cohort, UI patients had similar cLBRs to controls (adjusted OR 0.93, 95%CI [0.71, 1.23], P = 0.625). However, exploratory analyses suggested fewer available blastocysts (adjusted β -0.36, 95%CI [-0.70, -0.02], P = 0.038) and supernumerary embryos (adjusted β -0.46, 95%CI [-0.85, -0.08], P = 0.018) in UI patients during their first IVF cycle without adjustment for multiple comparisons. No significant differences were observed in other outcomes. Most effect estimates remained directionally consistent in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, UI patients following repeated IUI failures demonstrated neither markedly superior nor inferior cLBRs compared to the control population. Given the retrospective design and limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Are we doing enough for antenatal pelvic floor health? A cross-sectional survey of postpartum women's experiences of symptom enquiry, education and preventive care.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Lor KY, Rantell A, Araklitis G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) is common during and after pregnancy, yet symptoms are frequently normalised and opportunities for prevention may be missed. This study evaluated PFD risk factors, antenatal symptom screening, and access to pelvic health information and support.
STUDY DESIGN: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among postpartum women at a tertiary maternity hospital in South London, United Kingdom. Questionnaire responses were analysed alongside electronic health records. Free-text responses were evaluated using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Of 139 women approached, 124 completed the questionnaire (response rate 89.2%). The median age was 33 years. At least one recognised PFD risk factor was present in 115 women (92.7%), and 84 (67.7%) had two or more. The most prevalent risk factors were age >30 (62.9%), body mass index >25 kg/m2 (48.4%), multiparity (27.4%) and constipation (12.9%). Forty-eight women (38.7%) reported no antenatal screening for PFD symptoms. Reported screening rates were 58.1% for urinary symptoms, 35.5% for bowel symptoms, 20.2% for sexual symptoms and 16.9% for prolapse symptoms. Pelvic floor health was discussed with 68.5%; however, 41.9% were not advised to perform pelvic floor muscle exercises (PFME) and only 19.4% received practical instruction. Of eight women who reported PFD symptoms to a healthcare professional during pregnancy, four (50.0%) were referred for specialist pelvic health support.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite a high prevalence of recognised PFD risk factors, 38.7% of women reported no antenatal PFD symptom enquiry, and only 19.4% received practical PFME instruction. These findings highlight opportunities to improve the consistency of antenatal pelvic floor care through routine symptom enquiry, preventative education and targeted specialist support, in accordance with national recommendations.

articles.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
articles.authors: Wang Q, Zhang H, Zhao W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gitelman syndrome (GS), an autosomal recessive tubulopathy caused by SLC12A3 mutations, presents with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypocalciuria and hypomagnesemia. Pregnancy can exacerbate these imbalances, increasing maternal-fetal risks, yet standardized management remains lacking. This review summarizes complications, management strategies, and outcomes to guide evidence-based care.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CNKI were searched from inception to December 31, 2025, using 'Gitelman Syndrome' AND ('pregnancy' OR 'gestation'). Two reviewers independently performed literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. Core data were analyzed descriptively, categorical variables as frequencies (%), continuous as mean ± SD or median (range).
RESULTS: Fifty-six studies (96 pregnancies, 81 women) from 19 countries were included. Among pregnancies with available outcome data, reported maternal complications included gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets (HELLP) syndrome (3.1%); fetal/neonatal complications included preterm birth (16.7%), growth restriction (5.2%), and death (4.2%). Preconception diagnosis showed lower GDM (6.3% vs 18.4%) and fetal/neonatal death (0% vs 8.2%); these comparisons were descriptive and exploratory only. Oral potassium and magnesium were the main treatments. Potassium-sparing diuretics were used in 16 pregnancies (18 exposures); no malformations were reported, but safety is unestablished. Vaginal delivery occurred in 51.2% and Cesarean in 48.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: Preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit GS-complicated pregnancies, but evidence is limited by case-report data, publication bias, and heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed to clarify risk factors and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Mobile Health for Postpartum Contraception Knowledge in India (mMitra): Realist Evaluation Using Moderation Analysis and Structural Equation Models.
articles.authors: Chandrasekar A, Slaymaker E, Ford J et al.
articles.abstract:
