BACKGROUND: Indian National Family Health Survey data from 2021 suggest that 9.4% of women of reproductive age had an unmet need for spacing or limiting future pregnancies. Randomized controlled trials evaluating mobile health interventions (programs delivered via mobile phones) provide evidence of their potential benefit in addressing the determinants of misconceptions and lack of knowledge regarding postpartum family planning (PPFP) methods. The mMitra program has been implemented since 2014 and uses automated voice-messaging to deliver pregnancy and postpartum care information to socioeconomically vulnerable women in the Mumbai metropolitan area. However, the mMitra program has not been adequately evaluated to understand its impact on PPFP knowledge and outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to assess whether, how, why, for whom, and in what contexts the mMitra program affects PPFP awareness by analyzing cohort follow-up survey data, call duration, and attendance to measure the impact of listenership and by refining context-mechanism-outcome configurations (CMOCs) by testing for effect modification in logistic regression and structural equation models (SEMs).
METHODS: This study presents the quantitative findings from the realist evaluation of the mMitra program. Moderator analysis (through testing for effect modification in a logistic regression model) and SEMs were used to test CMOCs from an accompanying realist review.
RESULTS: After adjusting for religion as a potential confounder and including phone access as an effect modifier in the logistic regression model, mMitra call duration, a proxy measure for program engagement, had a modest effect on knowledge of one or more highly effective contraceptive methods (odds ratio 1.012, 95% CI 1.002-1.021; P=.02). In addition, 77% of women measured at baseline did not complete the endline survey at 6 months, potentially due to cultural expectations surrounding women returning to natal homes during their final months of pregnancy. SEMs show some evidence of an association between shared phone ownership and mMitra program engagement, potentially via the mechanism of women's ability to negotiate phone access.
CONCLUSIONS: This study adds to the growing body of evidence on the usefulness of SEM for testing CMOCs in realist evaluations. Issues with data collection and management, and the absence of survey data from locations outside Mumbai, limit the generalizability of the conclusions from this study.

articles.title: Human Papillomavirus Testing Compared With Cytology for Cervical Cancer Screening Among Women Living With HIV in the Dominican Republic.
articles.authors: Madeleine MM, Lantigua F, Benítez Abreu A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Women living with HIV (WWH) face elevated cervical cancer risk, yet evidence supporting primary human papillomavirus (HPV) testing in low-resource settings remains limited. We compared HPV testing with cytology for detection of cervical precancer among WWH in the Dominican Republic to inform national screening strategies.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis from US-Latin American-Caribbean HIV/HPV-Cancer Prevention Clinical Trials Network Trial 302 (Estudio Oportunidad, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05556772), 575 WWH contributed provider- and self-collected samples for cytology and HPV hierarchical testing. Women with positive results on cytology, provider-collected HPV testing, or self-collected HPV testing were referred for colposcopy and biopsy. Screening test characteristics were evaluated using centrally adjudicated histologic end points.
RESULTS: Women with positive results on any screening test had higher HIV viral loads, lower CD4 counts, and were younger than women with screen-negative results. Sensitivity to detect cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3+) by cytology (66.7% [95% CI, 49.2 to 80.5]) was lower than sensitivity of provider-collected results with either 13 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes (93.9 [95% CI, 78.7 to 98.5]) or 8 hrHPV genotypes (84.8% [95% CI, 68.3 to 98.6]). Self-collected samples had the highest sensitivity (97.0%, 95% CI, 81.3 to 99.6). Cytology missed 33.3% of CIN3+, hrHPV testing of provider-collected samples missed 6.1%-15.2% of CIN3+, and hrHPV testing of self-collected samples missed 3.0% of CIN3+.
CONCLUSION: Among WWH in the Dominican Republic, HPV testing, whether provider- or self-collected, outperformed cytology for detection of CIN3+. Both 13- and 8-genotype hrHPV panels demonstrated high sensitivity but low specificity, resulting in high referral rates to colposcopy. These findings support transitioning to primary HPV-based screening for WWH in the Dominican Republic to increase accuracy in detecting precancer and reduce the cervical cancer burden among WWH.

articles.title: The effect of mobile text messaging counseling on knowledge and self-efficacy in gestational diabetes: a randomized trial.
articles.journal: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
articles.authors: Yamaç SU, Vicdan N, Aydemir M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the effect of mobile text messaging counseling on diabetes knowledge and self-efficacy in gestational diabetes.
METHOD: This randomized controlled trial included 95 pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) at a university hospital in Türkiye. Participants received either structured Short Message Service (SMS)-based counseling plus routine care or routine care alone. The Gestational Diabetes Self-Efficacy Scale and Diabetes Knowledge Scale were administered at baseline and after 12 weeks.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable except for age. At 12 weeks, the intervention group had significantly higher diabetes knowledge and self-efficacy scores than the control group (p < 0.05). Post-intervention diabetes knowledge was moderately associated with self-efficacy (r = 0.53, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: SMS-based counseling was associated with greater diabetes knowledge and self-efficacy among women with GDM and may support self-management during pregnancy.

articles.title: Reconciling the medical relevance of mitochondrial transplantation in vivo.
articles.authors: Abay E, Sanchez-Gurmaches J, Molkentin JD
articles.abstract: Mitochondria transplantation is a proposed therapeutic approach to improve the function of diseased or injured tissue. It has garnered attention and sparked debate.

articles.title: Intrapartum oral azithromycin versus placebo alone or in combination with other antimicrobials on maternal infection in South East Asia.
articles.authors: Patel AB, Kurhe K, Bhargav S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In low-resource facilities that routinely use intrapartum prophylactic antimicrobials, the use of multiple antimicrobials could be rationalised by a single oral dose of oral azithromycin.
METHODS: The Azithromycin Prevention in Labor Use Study (A-PLUS), a randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial performed across eight sites in seven countries amongst women who planned to deliver vaginally. They were randomly assigned to receive study drug, a single intrapartum 2 gm oral dose of azithromycin or an identical appearing placebo. Data from four South-East Asia sites (Indian sites Nagpur and Belagavi, Pakistan, and Bangladesh) was analyzed to evaluate whether the use of non-study antimicrobials (alone or in-combination) given after randomization through one-day postpartum for any indication (prophylactic or treatment) modified the effect of study drugs on maternal outcomes (maternal infections, antibiotic usage 2-42days postpartum on ambulatory basis or re-hospitalization). The non-study antimicrobials given after randomization through 1-day postpartum was defined by four exposure sub-groups within azithromycin and placebo arm as, Use of: i) No non-study antibiotic; ii) Cephalosporin only; iii) Other non-study non-cephalosporin antibiotics; and iv) Cephalosporin and other non-study non-cephalosporin antibiotics. An intent to treat (ITT) analysis was adopted. Adjusted relative risks and 95% confidence intervals comparing azithromycin with placebo were estimated using Poisson regression models with robust variance estimators that included study site, maternal non-study antimicrobial use, and a treatment-by-non-study antimicrobial use interaction term.
RESULTS: All maternal non-study antibiotic subgroups had balanced randomization between azithromycin and placebo. The risk of any maternal infections was reduced when only azithromycin was received versus placebo (RR = 0.75; 95% CI-0.57-0.98) and when group iv antimicrobials were used with azithromycin compared to only group iv antimicrobials (RR = 0.79; 95% CI-0.66-0.95). The use of antibiotics from day2-42 was similar in both arms (azithromycin or placebo) with or without use of other antimicrobials.
CONCLUSIONS: This secondary analysis found no evidence that non-study antimicrobials use modified the effect of azithromycin on maternal outcomes. This study underscores the importance of considering an easily administrable intrapartum prophylaxis of oral monotherapy in low resource, high risk for…

articles.title: Multidisciplinary care models for managing pregnancies complicated with chronic diseases: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Amarasinghe GS, Weerasuriya SR, Malatzky C et al.
articles.abstract: Multidisciplinary care is a key recommendation for the management of complicated pregnancies in contemporary obstetrics, but how to implement it in the real world remains unclear and poorly supported by research evidence. This systematic review describes the characteristics and outcomes of multidisciplinary care models for managing pregnancies complicated with chronic diseases. PubMed/Medline, Embase, and CINAHL databases were searched for relevant studies published between January 2013 and January 2026. Studies were included if they described a multidisciplinary care model in which multiple clinical disciplines interacted during pregnancy. Reporting quality was assessed with the TIDieR checklist. The risk of bias and the certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tools and the GRADE tool. Of 8515 screened articles, 51 were included. Characteristics and outcomes were synthesized narratively. Models varied widely in team composition, communication patterns, and decision-making processes. Specific characteristics, including model design, performance monitoring, and funding, were described inconsistently. Available evidence on effectiveness was limited. There was very low-certainty evidence that multidisciplinary care reduced maternal mortality in women with chronic disease. Reduced maternal and fetal morbidity was also reported. Clinicians and policymakers can use this collective description to select strategies for effective multidisciplinary care models appropriate for the socio-economic, health system, and disease-related context of their specific setting. Studies with robust methodology would provide stronger evidence supporting multidisciplinary care during pregnancy. Standardized reporting of multidisciplinary care provision is also important for deriving sound conclusions about the effectiveness of the models and their adaptability across different health systems.

articles.title: The vitamin D-vitamin D receptor axis in uterine leiomyomas: A scoping review of clinical, molecular, and genetic evidence.
articles.authors: Katamba G, Kajabwangu R, Kanyesigye H et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine leiomyomas are the most common benign tumours of the female reproductive tract and a major cause of gynaecological morbidity worldwide. Observational and experimental studies have linked vitamin D and the vitamin D receptor (VDR) separately to uterine leiomyoma biology, including effects on cell proliferation and Wnt/β-catenin signalling in vitro; however, the breadth of this evidence has not been comprehensively mapped across clinical, molecular, and genetic domains. We conducted a scoping review following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from January 2016 to December 2025. Forty-two studies were included: 31 clinical, seven molecular, and four genetic. Most clinical studies reported lower circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations among women with uterine leiomyomas compared with controls, with several demonstrating inverse associations with fibroid size, volume, or number; however, fewer than half adjusted for BMI and only one study adjusted for ethnicity, limiting causal inference. Seven molecular studies examined the vitamin D-VDR axis in leiomyoma tissue and cells: three demonstrated reduced VDR expression, two demonstrated upregulated CYP24A1 expression, and two demonstrated calcitriol-mediated suppression of Wnt/β-catenin signalling (and, in one study, mTOR signalling). Four genetic studies showed inconsistent associations between VDR and vitamin D metabolism gene polymorphisms and leiomyoma susceptibility across populations. The evidence maps parallel associations of lower circulating vitamin D, lower VDR expression and higher CYP24A1 expression in leiomyoma tissue with the disease; no included study tested whether VDR mediates or modifies the relationship between vitamin D and leiomyoma. Findings remain heterogeneous and largely observational. Well-designed prospective cohort studies incorporating LC-MS/MS vitamin D measurement, concurrent tissue sampling, and full confounder adjustment are needed to clarify the clinical and mechanistic significance of this pathway.

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with puerperal sepsis at LUTH.
articles.authors: Baines SM, Kurehwatira KR, Siakabanze C et al.
articles.abstract: Puerperal sepsis remains a leading cause of maternal mortality in low-resource settings, contributing to 19% of Zambia's estimated 252 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. Despite its significant burden, localized data on risk factors remain sparse. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and determinants of puerperal sepsis at Livingstone University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), a tertiary referral centre in Southern Zambia. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using medical records of 460 postpartum women admitted to LUTH between January 2023 and December 2024. Data on demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were extracted using a standardized form in REDCap. Puerperal sepsis was defined as a genital tract infection occurring within six weeks postpartum (WHO criteria). Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression models were employed to analyse associations. The prevalence of puerperal sepsis was 5.4% (25/460). In adjusted analyses, elevated white blood cell count (AOR: 1.30 per unit increase; 95% CI: 1.13-1.50; p < 0.001) and lower haemoglobin levels (AOR 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.95; p = 0.019) were independent predictors of puerperal sepsis. Postpartum haemorrhage, antenatal visit frequency, maternal hypotension and multiple births were not significantly associated with puerperal sepsis after adjustment. Compared to non-sepsis cases, sepsis cases were more likely to involve younger maternal age (median: 22 vs. 26 years; p = 0.048) and prolonged labour (median: 11 vs. 9 hours; p = 0.044). Elevated white blood cell count, and lower haemoglobin levels were significantly associated with puerperal sepsis. These findings highlight the potential value of routine haematological assessment in identifying mothers who may require closer clinical monitoring. Strengthening routine monitoring and timely intervention may help reduce the burden of puerperal sepsis and improve maternal outcomes. However, given the limited number of outcome events, the findings should be interpreted with caution, and further studies with larger sample sizes are recommended.

articles.title: Psychosocial Considerations in the Aesthetic Care of the Perimenopausal and Menopausal Patient.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Razmi AN, Dayan S, Rieder EA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is associated with clinically significant changes in skin quality, hair, and body composition that frequently influence the pursuit of aesthetic interventions. Despite the growing number of perimenopausal and menopausal women seeking aesthetic care guidance specific to this population remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This review examines the impact of menopause on aesthetic concerns and discusses practical considerations for cosmetic dermatologists and plastic surgeons, including patient motivation, hormone therapy, communication strategies, and factors influencing treatment satisfaction.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative review was performed by searching PubMed through July 31, 2026, to identify all English language literature on menopause with keywords, aesthetic, body image, cosmetic dermatology, and self-esteem.
RESULTS: Psychosocial factors emerged as important considerations during patient evaluation for perimenopausal and menopausal women. The available literature supports integrating aesthetic treatments with broader menopause management, including hormone therapy, psychological screening, and expectation setting.
CONCLUSION: Perimenopausal and menopausal women represent a distinct aesthetic patient population with unique physiologic and psychosocial needs. Beyond procedural treatment, optimal care may include assessment of menopausal symptoms and mental health. Additional prospective studies are needed to better define treatment outcomes and evidence-based recommendations for aesthetic management.

articles.title: Multimodal Biomarkers in Pancreatic Cancer: From Early Detection to Precision Therapy.
articles.authors: Elghonaimy EA, Aguilera TA
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly lethal, with a 5-year relative survival of ∼13%. For decades, CA19-9 has been the principal clinical biomarker, but its limitations-including nonsecretion in Lewis-negative individuals, false-positive elevations with cholestasis, and inadequate sensitivity for early detection-have driven a rapidly expanding biomarker landscape. Blood-based multianalyte assays integrating circulating proteins, glycoproteins, methylated cell-free DNA, and tumor-derived signals, together with imaging-based deep learning, are improving early detection beyond CA19-9 alone. Molecular subtyping and postoperative circulating tumor DNA further refine prognosis, while germline and somatic alterations-including BRCA1/2/PALB2, MSI-H/dMMR, NRG1 fusions, KRAS G12C, NTRK, FGFR2, and BRAF V600E-are increasingly enabling biomarker-directed therapy. The next frontier is prospective validation and clinical integration of multimodal biomarkers to enable earlier diagnosis, more precise risk stratification, and equitable delivery of precision therapy.

articles.title: Anemia and Iron Status in Pregnant and Postpartum Women With Acute Heart Failure.
articles.authors: Nair M, Choudhury SS, Sundar A et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), iron-deficient anemia is highly prevalent and may compound the cardiovascular stress of pregnancy, yet its contribution to maternal acute heart failure (AHF) is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association of maternal anemia and iron status with AHF in pregnancy and post partum in India.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, unmatched, prospective case-control study recruited participants from 10 hospitals across 4 Indian states from February 2019 to November 2024. Incident cases were pregnant or postpartum women with clinically diagnosed AHF. Controls were women without history or symptoms of heart disease within 48 hours post partum. Data were analyzed from March 2025 to April 2026.
EXPOSURES: Maternal anemia and iron status. Blood samples collected at recruitment were analyzed for hemoglobin, ferritin, transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor, and hepcidin.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The outcome of interest was AHF, defined using clinical criteria. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of iron status and anemia with AHF, adjusting for potential confounders, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Subgroup analyses were performed in women with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. The discriminatory capacity of a model including anemia present before AFH onset vs a model with established risk factors only was examined using receiver operating characteristic curves.
RESULTS: Among 532 women with clinically diagnosed AHF (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-29] years) and 1091 controls (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-28] years), moderate and severe anemia were associated with 1.5-fold (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.05) and 5-fold (aOR, 5.06; 95% CI, 3.02-8.48) increased odds of AHF, respectively, compared with women without anemia. Higher soluble transferrin receptor levels (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.31-1.57) and the lowest hepcidin quintile (aOR, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.69-4.14), both indicative of iron deficiency, were independently associated with AHF. These associations persisted after adjusting for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and after excluding women with preexisting cardiac conditions, and they were consistent in subgroups with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. Adding anemia to established risk factors improved model discrimination for identifying AHF risk, increasing…

articles.title: Associations between cesarean delivery and adverse maternal and newborn outcomes by Robson Group: An analysis of the PRISMA study cohort in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Baumann SG, Yazdani NS, A J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Rising cesarean section (CS) rates in low- and middle-income countries may mask a triple burden of unmet need, overuse, and unsafe provision. Using the Robson ten-group classification, a global standard for monitoring institutional deliveries, we examined CS incidence and associations with adverse outcomes.
METHODS: Data were drawn from the Pregnancy Risk, Infant Surveillance, and Measurement Alliance Maternal and Newborn Health Study, an open cohort study in Kenya, Zambia, India, and Pakistan (2022-2025). We generated descriptive statistics for Robson groups and within-group relative risks of adverse events for CS versus vaginal delivery using multivariable adjusted log Poisson models.
RESULTS: Among 10 996 women, 29% delivered by CS. Group 5 (prior CS) and group 10 (preterm) were the largest contributors, accounting for 28% and 17% of all CS deliveries, respectively. Between-site differences in CS incidence were most pronounced for groups 2 and 4 (induced labor/pre-labor CS), ranging from 20% to 60% for nullipara and from 7% to 44% for multipara. Compared with vaginal delivery, CS was associated with an increased risk of maternal near miss, prolonged hospitalization, hemorrhage, and newborn intensive care unit admission. Stratified by Robson group, adverse outcome risk was concentrated among lower-obstetric-risk groups.
CONCLUSION: Repeat CS, preterm deliveries, labor induction, and pre-labor CS were drivers of CS. Although differences in risk magnitude associated with CS across Robson groups revealed important patterns for quality improvement, these estimates should not be interpreted as causal effects. Equipping facilities to manage labor induction, trials of labor after cesarean, and preterm deliveries is critical to improving quality of care.

articles.title: In Utero Exposure to Acetazolamide and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Reinaud C, Hoeltzenbein M, Touitou V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Data on pregnancy outcomes following acetazolamide exposure remain limited. The main safety issues relate to suspected teratogenic effects, supported by similarities between malformations reported in humans and animals. Other concerns include intrauterine growth restriction, amniotic fluid anomalies, and neonatal electrolyte imbalances. This study aimed to describe pregnancy outcomes and neonatal characteristics following acetazolamide exposure during pregnancy and to assess the association between first-trimester exposure and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using data from the French national Teratology Information Service (Centre de Référence sur les Agents Tératogènes, CRAT). We included all prospective pregnancies exposed to acetazolamide with a known outcome and an estimated delivery date before 1 January, 2024. The study proceeded in two stages. First, we described pregnancy and neonatal outcomes among all acetazolamide-exposed pregnancies, overall and according to timing of exposure (descriptive analysis). Second, we assessed the association between first-trimester acetazolamide exposure and adverse pregnancy outcomes, using a composite outcome including spontaneous miscarriage, medical termination of pregnancy, stillbirth, and major congenital malformation. We conducted this comparative analysis using a matched unexposed control group (1:4 ratio) randomly selected from the same database after exclusion of known teratogenic exposures and genetic disorders. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate crude conditional odds ratios.
RESULTS: Between 1988 and 2024, 135 prospective pregnancies were referred to the CRAT: 114 (84.4%) resulted in live births, 8 (5.9%) in miscarriages, 9 (6.7%) in elective terminations, 3 (2.2%) in medical abortions, and 1 (0.7%) in stillbirth. Among 87 first-trimester exposures with documented malformation status, three major congenital malformations unrelated to genetic disorders were identified (3.4%, 95% confidence interval 0.72-9.75). In the comparative analysis, first-trimester acetazolamide exposure was not associated with an adverse pregnancy outcome (crude conditional odds ratio = 1.03, 95% CI 0.51-2.09). Major congenital malformation rates did not differ between exposed (2.6%, 2/78) and unexposed pregnancies (2.8%, 9/327) [crude conditional odds ratio = 1.03, 95% confidence interval 0.21-4.99).
CONCLUSIONS: This study…

articles.title: Quality-of-life trajectories after laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis across public and private healthcare pathways: A prospective longitudinal study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Servidoni ACP, Andres MP, Brunoro MM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to prospectively evaluate quality-of-life (QoL) trajectories in women with endometriosis before and after laparoscopic excision, comparing outcomes across healthcare pathway (public vs. private) and endometriosis phenotype (superficial vs. ovarian and/or deep endometriosis).
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal observational study included 117 reproductive-age women with histologically confirmed endometriosis who underwent laparoscopic surgery at a tertiary referral institution in São Paulo, Brazil, between 2023 and 2025. Participants were classified according to healthcare pathway (private, n = 41; public, n = 76) and endometriosis phenotype (superficial, n = 42; ovarian and/or deep endometriosis, n = 75). QoL was assessed preoperatively and at 3 and 6 months postoperatively using the validated Brazilian Portuguese versions of the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) and 30-Item Endometriosis Health Profile (EHP-30) questionnaires. Longitudinal trajectories were evaluated using adjusted linear mixed-effects models, including group × linear and quadratic time interactions.
RESULTS: At baseline, public-sector patients reported greater pain severity and lower scores in several SF-36 domains, whereas American Association of Gynecologic Laparoscopists stage distribution did not differ significantly between healthcare pathways. Longitudinally, QoL improved across most SF-36 and EHP-30 domains in both healthcare groups. Significant healthcare pathway × linear time interactions were identified for SF-36 Physical Functioning, Pain, General Health, Social Functioning, Role - emotional, and Vitality (all P < 0.05), indicating that postoperative trajectories differed between healthcare pathways in selected generic QoL domains. In contrast, healthcare pathway × time interactions were not significant for most EHP-30 domains. Infertility-related QoL concerns did not show a significant longitudinal change during follow-up. No significant differences in SF-36 or EHP-30 longitudinal trajectories were identified between superficial and ovarian and/or deep endometriosis phenotypes.
CONCLUSION: QoL improved across most domains during the 6 months after laparoscopic endometriosis surgery in both public and private healthcare pathways and across endometriosis phenotypes. Differences in longitudinal trajectories between healthcare pathways were identified in selected SF-36 domains, whereas disease-specific EHP-30 trajectories were broadly…

articles.title: Background and Attitude of the Palestinian Community Toward Gender Selection Reproductive Technology: Scientific, Religious, and Sociocultural Perspectives.
articles.authors: Eid AM, Jetan M, Jodallah A et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to assess the Palestinian community's attitudes, ethical scores, and religious perceptions regarding the use of modern reproductive technology for gender selection, and to identify associated demographic factors. A cross-sectional survey was conducted on 416 participants in the Palestinian community, encompassing diverse age groups, educational levels, and family sizes. Data were collected on personal willingness to use gender selection technology, gender preference, ethical views, religious beliefs, and factors influencing decision-making. Statistical analysis, including Chi-square tests and median score comparisons, was performed to determine associations. A large majority of participants (86%) reported never using gender selection technology, and 79.3% expressed unwillingness to use it in the future. The primary barrier to acceptance was religious concern, with 97.1% stating they would reject the technology if not religiously approved. Most participants expressed no gender preference for their first child or overall family composition. Higher ethical concern scores were significantly associated with infertile participants, those with no children, and those who were illiterate (P < 0.05). Religious scores were significantly lower among post-graduate participants and those with two children. Demographic factors, including gender and income, were not significantly associated with willingness to use the technology. Attitudes toward gender selection in the Palestinian community are predominantly cautious and strongly mediated by religious beliefs, which serve as the main determinant in the decision-making process. Ethical concerns are highest among reproductively vulnerable groups (infertile or childless). These findings underscore the critical role of religious guidance and ethical counseling in shaping reproductive choices in conservative communities.

articles.title: Pregnancy as an important factor in female autoimmunity.
articles.authors: Pelczar P, Przywara D, Kowalczyk E et al.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune diseases (ADs) affect 5-10% of the population, with 80-85% of diagnosed patients being women. This pronounced sexual dimorphism is influenced by genetic factors (X chromosome), fluctuations in sex hormones, and unique immunological changes occurring during pregnancy and the postpartum period. These factors contribute to women's distinct susceptibility to autoimmune disorders and may influence their clinical course. This narrative review critically evaluates the immunological, hormonal, and pregnancy-related factors contributing to female autoimmunity with particular emphasis on the bidirectional interactions between pregnancy-induced immunomodulation and maternal autoimmunity. By contrasting four distinct diseases systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), multiple sclerosis (MS), and type 1 diabetes (T1D), representing different immune paradigms (type 1 T helper (Th1) vs. type 2 T helper (Th2), systemic vs. organ-specific), we aim to analyze how mechanisms like placental tolerance and fetal microchimerism specifically shape disease trajectories and obstetric outcomes, contextualized within the evolutionary pregnancy compensation hypothesis. A literature review (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) was conducted to synthesize clinical and molecular evidence. The mechanisms of placental immune tolerance, the phenomenon of fetal microchimerism, and the evolutionary pregnancy compensation hypothesis were analyzed. Selected autoimmune diseases were used to illustrate disease-specific manifestations of these mechanisms. The literature highlights the complex interplay between genetic, hormonal and immunological factors in female autoimmunity. Estrogens, progesterone, androgens and prolactin exert distinct immunomodulatory effects influencing immune cell activity, cytokine production and immune tolerance. Fetal microchimerism (FMc) may have long-term immunological consequences, potentially contributing to either immune regulation or autoimmune pathology. These mechanisms may help explain the variable effects of pregnancy on autoimmune disease activity and obstetric outcomes, as illustrated by SLE, RA, MS, and T1D. The pregnancy compensation hypothesis offers an additional evolutionary perspective. However, it remains speculative and requires further investigation. Pregnancy induces complex, disease-specific immunomodulatory changes. Instead of one-size-fits-all regimens, caring for pregnant women with autoimmune disease requires a…

articles.title: Advancing placenta accreta spectrum diagnosis: is 3-T MRI or combined MRI with ultrasound the answer?
articles.authors: Tan S, Richmond D, Mil M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compares the diagnostic performance of US and 3-T MRIin diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) disorder using final histopathological and surgical findings and explores the benefit of using a combined MRI and US approach to diagnose PAS.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed electronic medical records of all patients undergoing 3-T MRIplacenta at our institution between January 2020 and November 2023. The gold standard for PAS outcome was histopathology, and where unavailable, we referred to the operative notes. Patients without surgical or histopathologic data, and non-diagnostic MRI studies were excluded. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), confidence intervals, and p-values were generated for MRI, US, and combined MRI + US to detect PAS with subgroup analysis for placenta accreta/increta and percreta.
RESULTS: Eighty-eight patients met the inclusion criteria. The sensitivity and specificity of MRI for all PAS was 100.0% and 80.0% (p < 0.001), compared to US 89.5% and 62.0% (p < 0.001), and combined MRI + US 100.0% and 56.0% (p < 0.001), respectively. For diagnosing placenta percreta, MRI had a sensitivity and specificity of 83.3% and 94.3% (p < 0.001), compared to US 55.6% and 94.3% (p < 0.001) and combined MRI + US 83.3% and 92.9% (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Both US and 3-T MRIdemonstrated strong diagnostic performances for detecting PAS, with 3-T MRIdemonstrating stronger performance in this selective cohort, and not further improved by including US data. The continued use of US, MRI and clinical data for evaluating PAS disorder treatment options is recommended.
KEY POINTS: Question No dedicated study has evaluated the diagnostic performance of 3-T MRIor the combined use of MRI with US in PAS. Findings 3-T MRIdemonstrates high sensitivity and specificity for diagnosing PAS. The combined MRI and US assessment does not further improve diagnostic performance for PAS. Critical relevance statement 3-T MRImay be particularly useful as an adjunct in selected high-risk patients, equivocal ultrasound cases, or cases requiring assessment of myoinvasive disease and multidisciplinary surgical planning.

articles.title: The FOXM1-ZNF165-RICTOR transcriptional axis promotes ovarian cancer phenotypes through RICTOR-AKT signaling.
articles.authors: Han X, Qiu J, Jin F et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is characterized by transcriptional dysregulation and frequent activation of phosphoinositide 3-kinase-protein kinase B-mechanistic target of rapamycin (PI3K-AKT-mTOR) signaling, but transcriptional regulation of RICTOR-AKT signaling remains incompletely defined. We integrated public bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets with promoter analyses and experimentally tested FOXM1-ZNF165 and ZNF165-RICTOR regulation using genetic perturbation, chromatin immunoprecipitation-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, promoter-reporter assays, Western blotting, functional assays, and an A2780 xenograft model. Bidirectional RICTOR epistasis experiments were used to assess functional mediation. Zinc finger protein 165 (ZNF165) was overexpressed across independent ovarian cancer cohorts and was associated with overall survival. ZNF165 was the sole common upregulated ZNF-family candidate in two discovery datasets. Forkhead box protein M1 (FOXM1) bound the ZNF165 promoter and increased its transcription. ZNF165 depletion reduced proliferation, invasion, and xenograft growth. ZNF165 also bound the RICTOR promoter, increased RICTOR expression, and enhanced AKT Ser473 phosphorylation. RICTOR re-expression partially rescued the signaling and clonogenic effects of ZNF165 depletion, whereas RICTOR knockdown reversed the effects of ZNF165 overexpression. Torin1 reduced ZNF165-associated clonogenic and invasive phenotypes but was interpreted as an mTOR-pathway inhibitor rather than an mTORC2-specific probe. The data support a FOXM1-ZNF165-RICTOR transcriptional framework that promotes ovarian cancer phenotypes in part through RICTOR-AKT signaling. Further validation in HGSOC-relevant models, xenograft tissue, and independent clinical cohorts is required before prognostic or therapeutic application.

articles.title: Urinary incontinence and the impact on the quality of life of transwomen, travestis and non-binary people: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Dos Reis Galhardo D, Rosa BL, Carneiro EF et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This cross-sectional study investigated the frequency of urinary incontinence (UI), its associated symptoms, and the impact on quality of life (QoL) in a sample of the trans and non-binary population.
METHODS: The study included 140 participants, divided into three groups: trans/transvestite/transfeminine women, trans/transmasculine men, and non-binary people, who answered the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF) and King's Health Questionnaire (Br-KHQ).
RESULTS: The overall proportion of UI was 39.3%. Although the proportion was higher among trans women, transvestites, and transfeminine individuals (41.8%), non-binary people had the highest intragroup proportion (65%), reporting more frequent weekly losses, but in smaller amounts. Despite a better overall health perception, UI negatively impacted the personal relationships and emotions of non-binary participants. Specific symptoms, such as urgency, stress UI, and nocturia, were associated with adverse impacts on daily activities, relationships, emotions, and sleep/energy.
CONCLUSIONS: It is concluded that UI is a frequent condition that significantly affects the QoL of trans and non-binary people, highlighting the need for clinical approaches sensitive to the specificities of each gender identity.

articles.title: Effects of GynCo-Care nurse-led telecoaching and app-based self-management intervention on outcomes in women with gynaecological cancer: a quasi-experimental study.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.authors: Afiyanti Y, Rachmawati IN, Juliastuti D et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the effects of the GynCo-Care nurse-led telecoaching and app-based self-management intervention on nutritional status, sexual function, distress, and quality of life (QoL) among women with gynaecological cancer undergoing chemotherapy.
METHODS: A quasi-experimental, non-randomised, two-group pretest-posttest study with repeated measurements was conducted at a cancer centre hospital in Jakarta, Indonesia. Sixty-eight women with primary gynaecological cancer receiving chemotherapy were recruited. Outcomes were assessed at baseline (T0), week 4 (T1), and week 8 (T2). Adjusted generalised estimating equations (GEE) were used to estimate intervention effects.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed a greater reduction in nutritional risk at T1 (β, - 2.00; 95% CI, - 3.70, - 0.30) and T2 (β, - 5.53; 95% CI, - 7.14, - 3.92), and reduction in distress at T2 (β, - 1.04; 95% CI, - 1.80, - 0.28). Sexual function improved over time in both groups, whereas QoL rose at T1 and returned to baseline at T2 in both groups; no significant group × time effects were observed for sexual function, overall QoL, or any QoL domain. These findings were robust to multiple imputation.
CONCLUSION: The GynCo-Care intervention was associated with promising reductions in nutritional risk and distress than self-directed education among women with gynaecological cancer undergoing chemotherapy, whereas no between-group differences were observed for sexual function or QoL over 8 weeks. Given the quasi-experimental design, the baseline imbalance in nutritional risk, and the short follow-up, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and warrant confirmation in adequately powered randomised controlled trials with longer follow-up.

articles.title: Dynamic monitoring of cell-free DNA levels in glioblastoma patients: a longitudinal study on treatment response.
articles.authors: Roda D, Oliveira F, Caramelo F et al.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GB) is the most aggressive form of malignant glioma, characterized by a low survival rate and minimal improvements in patient outcomes over the past three decades. This study investigates the feasibility of detecting circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and analyses its dynamic fluctuations in a cohort of 59 patients undergoing chemoradiation treatment according to the standardized "Stupp protocol". In our cohort, longitudinal cfDNA levels remained broadly stable at the population level over the follow-up period; however, substantial inter-individual variability in individual trajectories was observed, highlighting the complexity of cfDNA dynamics in GB. At the individual level, longitudinal monitoring revealed that cfDNA levels generally declined following surgery and chemoradiotherapy, yet increased prior to or coinciding with radiological progression, supporting its potential utility as a biomarker for tumour burden estimation and treatment response monitoring. We further developed a cfDNA index model correlating preoperative cfDNA levels with gross tumour volume and clinical target volume, demonstrating a statistically significant association with radiological progression. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to propose a mathematically derived cfDNA index in GB. This simple, low-cost, and minimally invasive approach may offer a valuable tool for early risk stratification at diagnosis, complement longitudinal clinical assessment, and support individualized treatment planning and surveillance. Overall, these findings reinforce the potential of cfDNA quantification as an accessible biomarker to advance precision medicine in GB.

articles.title: Implementation of quality indicators for ovarian cancer in gynecological cancer centers certified by the German Cancer Society (DKG).
articles.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
articles.authors: Schulmeyer CE, Klages B, Utzig M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Since 2008, the German Cancer Society (DKG) has certified gynecological cancer centers to ensure high-quality care with guideline-based quality indicators (QI) as a core component. This article summarizes the German development and update of ovarian cancer (OC) QI based on the current S3-guideline (2026) and presents their performance.
METHODS: This was a retrospective, descriptive, observational analysis of aggregated annual-report data for treatment years 2019-2024; no inferential statistics were performed. QI were derived from strong S3-guideline recommendations through a structured multi-step process. Experts identified potential QI according to standardized criteria (including feasibility and impact on care). QI required ≥ 75% agreement. Since 2017, each tumor entity has been limited to five key QI in the certification dataset.
RESULTS: Eight guideline-derived QI are currently defined for OC, five QI are included in the certification program. In 2024, 184 certified centers treated 4.951 primary OC cases. At center level, the predefined target values were met for surgical staging (93.5% of centers; target ≥ 40%), offering genetic testing (97.8%; target ≥ 70%), complete macroscopic resection (99.5%; target ≥ 30%), and surgery by a gynecologic oncologist (98.9%; target ≥ 80%). All centers (100%) met plausibility limits for first-line chemotherapy (75.1% of advanced-stage patients). At patient level, pooled adherence rates improved over time; the median rate of offering genetic testing rose from 61% (2019) to 84% (2024). Two QI were retired in 2021, and one QI is pending until further guideline updates.
CONCLUSION: Guideline-based QI translate essential recommendations into measurable metrics, allowing objective assessment of quality. High and increasing adherence rates were observed in certified centers. These findings support the use of guideline-based QI for benchmarking and continuous quality improvement, although the observational design precludes causal attribution to certification.

articles.title: Revealing Neuroplasticity Following Sacral Neuromodulation Treatment with Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy.
articles.authors: Burkett LS, Ghatas MP, Patel RM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The objective of this study was to use functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to quantify prefrontal cortical activation in response to natural filling in female participants ≥ 6 months after sacral neuromodulation (SNM) treatment.
METHODS: Female participants with overactive bladder (OAB) and SNM implanted for ≥ 6 months underwent a natural filling protocol and recorded bladder sensation (0-100%) for this hypothesis-generating cross-sectional study design. Throughout filling, a 24-channel fNIRS device continuously measured oxyhemoglobin (O2Hb) in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) channels divided into brain regions: right, middle, and left. fNIRS signals were processed to remove motion artifacts and physiological noise. Data were interpolated to a reference time to account for variability in fill time. fNIRS patterns were evaluated during elevated sensation (time from first desire to void to 100% fullness) and were compared with normal controls and OAB patients without SNM.
RESULTS: Ten female participants completed the study with a median of 17 (6.8, 46) months from SNM implantation. Mean O2Hb increased during the elevated sensation period in all cortical regions, demonstrating activation. The SNM cohort was compared with healthy controls (n = 9) and an OAB cohort (without SNM; n = 11). The SNM O2Hb pattern was most similar to that in normal participants, though with a smaller increase in magnitude. Non-SNM-treated OAB O2Hb patterns were stable or decreasing.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings contribute to supporting the hypothesis that the PFC plays an inhibitory role in voiding function, which can be improved in women after SNM treatment.

articles.title: Complications Within 30 Days After Minimally Invasive Sacrocolpopexy by Robotic Versus Laparoscopic Approach: A National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) Database Study.
articles.authors: Smolinski M, Konci R, Bonhomme K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Robotic MISCP is increasingly used for improved ergonomics and visualization but comparative evidence to standard laparoscopy is limited. This study compares 30-day surgical complications after minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy (MISCP) performed laparoscopically versus robotically.
METHODS: Patients undergoing MISCP by laparoscopic and robotic approach (2022- 2024) were identified in the ACS National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. The primary outcome was a composite of surgical site infection, blood transfusion, return to the operating room, or readmission within 30 days or surgical length of stay > 7 days. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for age, race, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, diabetes, ASA class, concurrent incontinence procedure, concurrent adnexectomy, and concurrent hysterectomy.
RESULTS: Of the 9824 patients who met the inclusion criteria, 7296 (74.3%) underwent a robotic approach. Patients having a robotic MISCP were older, higher BMI, higher ASA class, and more often non-Hispanic white (all P < 0.001). The composite surgical complication outcome occurred in 4.5% of patients overall and occurred for fewer patients having robotic approach (4.3% vs 5.3%, P = 0.04). Surgical site infection was lower for the robotic approach (2.2% vs 3.0%, P = 0.01). There was no difference in conversion to abdominal or vaginal approaches, urinary tract injury and no difference in Clavien-Dindo 4 complications. On multivariable analysis, robotic MISCP was associated with lower odds of the composite outcome (aOR 0.72, P = 0.008) and surgical site infection (aOR 0.66, P = 0.008).
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic MISCP may be associated with slightly fewer 30-day complications than laparoscopic MISCP although overall complication rates are low.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding access to sexual and reproductive health and gender-based violence services in Brazil since the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: A multi-stakeholder qualitative analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Munezero A, Charles CM, Bahamondes L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Understanding how disruptions to essential sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender based violence (GBV) services because of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-COV-2;COVID-19) pandemic were experienced across different population groups is critical to health system responses. The objective of this study was to explore how the pandemic influenced knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to access to SRH and GBV services in Brazil.
METHOD: A qualitative study was conducted in five healthcare facilities in Brazil between November 2022 and May 2023. Purposive sampling included pregnant and non-pregnant women, partners, and healthcare professionals. Pregnant women were interviewed at two time points. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using inductive thematic content analysis guided by Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory.
RESULTS: A total of 99 participants contributed to 120 interviews. Political-institutional mistrust, conflicting public messaging, and health system reorganization affected access to SRH and GBV services. Although healthcare professionals reported continuity of essential services, women described reduced availability of gynecological care and contraceptive services. Socioeconomic barriers, transportation difficulties, and poor coordination further limited access, particularly for vulnerable groups. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified GBV by increasing household stressors such as unemployment and alcohol abuse while weakening safety nets. Victim blaming and financial dependence hinder reporting. Over time, pregnant women's perceptions shifted from fear of COVID-19-related fetal outcomes to concerns about vaccination and newborn care.
CONCLUSION: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on SRH and GBV service access in Brazil was not solely due to service disruption but resulted from dynamic interactions across political, institutional, interpersonal, and temporal levels.

articles.title: Efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan and bosentan in amelioration of estradiol induced endometrial changes via regulation of Wnt/β-catenin and IL6/JAK/STAT3 pathways.
articles.authors: Refaie MMM, Ibrahim MFG, Sherkawy HS et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial hyperplasia (EHP) commonly affects elderly females in the pre-menopausal period and can progress to carcinoma. Immune dysregulation has a crucial role in mediating such disorders. Thus, studying its pathogenesis and finding ameliorative medical treatment becomes mandatory. This motivated us to perform the current experiment of induced EHP in female rats using estradiol (EST) (2 mg/kg/day) intramuscular injection with or without using bosentan (BOS) (50 mg/kg/day) and/or Sacubitril/valsartan (SV) (60 mg/kg/day) for 3 weeks. We found typical histopathological features of EHP, elevation of total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), interleukin 6/Janus kinase/Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (IL6/JAK/STAT3), and Wnt/β-catenin pathways with increased uterine weights. However, there is a significant diminution in total antioxidant capacity (TAC) and caspase-3 immune expression. Interestingly, BOS and/or SV administration significantly ameliorated the histopathological and biochemical disturbances. This improvement may be attributed to the pharmacological ability of SV to block angiotensin receptors and neprilysin besides blocking endothelin receptors by BOS. Furthermore, SV/BOS could regulate apoptosis with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

articles.title: Histological subtype-specific gasdermin expression suggests distinct pyroptotic and inflammatory profiles in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Keskin A, Berkel C, Yeldir N et al.
articles.abstract: Gasdermin (GSDM) family members are key effector proteins that mediate pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death characterized by plasma membrane pore formation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Despite their established role in inflammation, the relationship between GSDM expression and systemic inflammatory responses across various histological subtypes of ovarian cancer remains poorly understood. In the present study, mRNA and protein expression levels of six GSDM family members were examined in ovarian cancer tissues representing various histological subtypes (serous, endometrioid, clear cell, and mucinous), and in benign/non-malignant (histologically normal) ovarian tissues obtained from healthy women without ovarian cancer. Besides, GSDM expression profiles were analyzed in peripheral blood samples obtained from ovarian cancer patients and control women. In addition, serum levels of certain inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-18) were measured in patients with ovarian tumors of different histological subtypes, and in control women. Our findings showed histological subtype-dependent differences in the expression of several gasdermin family members at both mRNA and protein levels, in ovarian tissue and serum samples. Notably, GSDMB and GSDMF protein levels were found to be significantly reduced in high grade serous tumors compared with benign (normal) ovarian tissues; and GSDMB protein levels were decreased in endometroid tumors compared to normal ovaries. Furthermore, we found that histological subtype-specific alterations in GSDM mRNA expression are more prominent in ovarian tissues than in peripheral blood mRNA samples. Analysis of serum cytokines demonstrated that patients with serous and mucinous ovarian cancer have higher levels of IL-1β and IL-18 in their serum, compared with those with other histological subtypes of ovarian cancer. These results likely indicate that inflammatory responses may vary among different ovarian cancer histological subtypes and point to the presence of histological subtype-specific inflammatory profiles in this highly heterogeneous malignant disease. Overall, our findings suggest that GSDM-mediated pyroptosis and associated inflammatory pathways differ across different histological subtypes of ovarian cancer and may possibly contribute to disease heterogeneity.

articles.title: The Menopausal Transition as a Critical Window for Cardiovascular Risk Modification and Intervention Opportunities.
articles.authors: Mehta JM, Manson JE
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the cardiometabolic changes that occur during the menopausal transition (MT), emphasizing how hormonal fluctuations may contribute to the development of adverse cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors. It identifies gaps in evidence regarding safe and effective treatments for cardiometabolic risk reduction during the MT.
RECENT FINDINGS: The MT is characterized by hormonal shifts driving adverse changes in body composition, lipid profiles, vascular function, and metabolic regulation. These alterations are associated with accelerated progression of cardiovascular risk factors and may contribute to the increase in CVD risk observed after menopause. Growing evidence suggests that the MT represents a distinct period of cardiometabolic vulnerability and provides an opportunity for early risk identification and prevention. Lifestyle and behavioral modifications, as well as control of blood pressure, lipids, and other established risk factors, are the foundations of risk-reducing management and treatment. Early cardiometabolic risk assessment and individualized, lifestyle -centered management are essential to optimize cardiovascular outcomes during the MT. Further research is needed to clarify therapeutic strategies for this critical window in women's cardiometabolic health.

articles.title: CGRP-CALCRL-VEGFR signaling promotes angiogenesis and cervical cancer progression.
articles.authors: Lu J, Li S, Han Q et al.
articles.abstract: Neuro-tumor crosstalk is increasingly recognized as a fundamental driver of cancer progression. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a neuropeptide classically associated with sensory neurons, has emerged as a key mediator of tumor growth, immune suppression, and cancer-associated symptoms across multiple malignancies. However, the role of CGRP signaling in cervical cancer remains poorly defined. We comprehensively analyzed CGRP expression and its clinical relevance in cervical cancer using TCGA transcriptomic datasets, gene correlation analyses, and survival models. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were leveraged to define the cellular distribution of the CGRP receptor calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CALCRL). In HUVECs, CALCRL was silenced by siRNA and evaluated using proliferation, tube-formation, gene-expression, rescue, and signaling assays, including exogenous α-CGRP stimulation and VEGFR1/VEGFR2 overexpression. In vivo, CGRP-receptor inhibition was evaluated in SiHa, CaSki, and HeLa xenograft models using Fremanezumab or olcegepant. Elevated CGRP expression was associated with adverse prognosis in TCGA-CESC, and independent clinical validation showed that high CALCB expression was associated with poorer survival (log-rank P = 0.0036). Single-cell transcriptomic analyses consistently revealed that CALCRL expression was highly enriched in endothelial cells. CALCRL silencing impaired endothelial proliferation and angiogenic capacity, whereas exogenous α-CGRP enhanced these phenotypes in control cells but not in CALCRL-silenced cells. VEGFR1 or VEGFR2 overexpression partially rescued the proliferation defect caused by CALCRL depletion. Pharmacological inhibition of CGRP-receptor signaling consistently suppressed tumor growth across SiHa, CaSki, and HeLa xenograft models. These findings provide preclinical evidence that CGRP-CALCRL signaling promotes cervical cancer progression through endothelial angiogenic activity and VEGFR-associated signaling, supporting further investigation of this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Predominance of Ureaplasma Parvum in Intrauterine Infection-Related Stillbirths in a series of 10 cases.
articles.authors: Huo L, Lei W, Liao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate whether stillbirths with funisitis are associated with intrauterine infection and specific microorganisms (especially Ureaplasma parvum).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 10 stillbirths with funisitis was conducted on fetal organ tissues; multiplex suspension microarray was applied to screen 12 common microorganisms in the female genital tract, with pathogen confirmation via quantitative PCR and pathogen serotype confi rmation via sequencing.
RESULTS: Our study revealed that UP represented the most commonly identified microorganism in organ specimens from stillbirths complicated by funisitis. Serovars 3 and 6 were most common. A positive UP finding in the stillbirth corresponded to a positive detection of UP in the maternal cervical swab.
CONCLUSION: There was a plausible association between UP infection and stillbirth with funisitis. The application of molecular pathology offers significant benefits for providing clues for elucidating the potential etiology and preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes. Due to the small sample size and lack of a control group, this study cannot establish a causal relationship between UP infection and stillbirth.

articles.title: Two Persons, One Womb: Testing the Social Construction of Reproduction in Conjoined Twins.
articles.authors: Villalba A
articles.abstract: Standard models of reproductive autonomy presuppose a singular and bounded subject. This paper challenges that assumption by analysing the limit case of dicephalus parapagus conjoined twins where two distinct persons share a single reproductive system. I argue that this physiological configuration creates an ontological indeterminacy that biological essentialism cannot resolve. Drawing on a previous constructivist framework of reproduction, I demonstrate that when gestation is a shared biological event but personhood is distinct, the designation of "mother" cannot be discovered in the tissue but must be acknowledged through intention. The analysis proceeds to examine the severe ethical conflict arising when one twin wishes to reproduce while the other does not. I contend that prioritizing the reproductive desire of one sister over the refusal of the other constitutes a violation of bodily integrity analogous to involuntary gestational surrogacy. Consequently, I argue that in shared bodies, the non-reproducing person must hold an absolute power of veto. This aligns with established bioethical precedents, such as those discussed by Robertson, where the right to avoid involuntary biological parenthood is often held to supersede a former partner's desire to gestate shared embryos. Finally, this paper posits that the principles derived from this extreme case offer a necessary heuristic for broader bioethical issues. The example of conjoined twins validates the distributed maternity of Reciprocal IVF in lesbian couples while simultaneously reinforcing the protections against coercive surrogacy. By deconstructing the most extreme form of shared biology, this paper offers an exploration of a case of fragmented maternity and its implications.

articles.title: Interleukin-6 and the maternal-placental immune axis in preeclampsia: from implantation to postpartum cardiovascular disease.
articles.authors: Baroutis D, Papapanagiotou A, Giannakaki AG et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and is increasingly understood as a disorder of maternal-fetal immune maladaptation, in which interleukin-6 (IL-6) occupies a central position. IL-6 is usually examined at a single disease stage, which obscures its role as a continuous mediator.
CONTENT: This narrative review traces IL-6 across the preeclampsia continuum: signalling biology; the decidual immune niche; the regulatory T-cell/T-helper-17 and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 axes; defective placentation; antiangiogenic endothelial injury; the clinical phenotype; postpartum inflammation; and remote cardiovascular disease. Evidence is labelled by provenance, the roles of IL-6 as biomarker, mediator and therapeutic target are distinguished, and aspirin, heparin and IL-6-directed therapies are appraised.
SUMMARY: IL-6 links immune-tolerance failure to angiogenic imbalance and endothelial dysfunction, and altered inflammatory profiles persist years after delivery. Causal evidence, however, rests largely on animal and in vitro work; human data are associative and confounded by shared cardiometabolic risk; and the first large trial of IL-6 ligand inhibition lowered inflammation without reducing cardiovascular events.
OUTLOOK: Longitudinal, signalling-specific measurement, explicit separation of marker from mediator and target, and safety-led evaluation in pregnancy are required before this axis can inform prevention or postpartum cardiovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: Genomic Correlates of Chemoradiation Response in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: Implications for Precision Oncology.
articles.authors: Jayalie VF, Rusda M, Gondhowiardjo SA et al.
articles.abstract: Locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) accounts for a major healthcare burden in low- and middle-income countries, where five-year overall survival remains below 75% despite concurrent chemoradiation therapy (CCRT) as the curative standard. Treatment response is highly variable, yet clinical management is largely uniform. This review synthesizes current evidence on the genomic correlates of CCRT in LACC, spanning alterations in PIK3CA, PTEN, TP53, KRAS, ARID1A, and APOBEC-driven mutational signatures. These pathways offer biologically coherent explanations for radioresistance, but the strength and maturity of supporting evidence vary considerably, and evidence for most markers remains prognostic rather than treatment-predictive. No single genomic marker yet supports routine clinical use, and genome-only models omit complementary contributions from the tumor microenvironment, hypoxia, cancer stem cell biology, and clinicopathological or imaging-derived parameters. We further discuss the translational gap between genomic discovery and clinical implementation, with particular attention to population representation and resource constraints in high-burden settings. Prospective, population-inclusive genomic trials are urgently needed to translate these findings into equitable precision radiotherapy for patients with LACC worldwide.

articles.title: Small area estimation of hysterectomy prevalence and cervical cancer screening in the U.S. states and counties.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.authors: Liu B, Stout NK, Lee R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening (CCS) is essential for early detection, yet reliable granular estimates at state and county levels remain limited, especially considering that hysterectomy, the second most common surgery among U.S. women, affects screening eligibility.
METHODS: Data from the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) and Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) for 2012-2016 and 2021-2023 were used to develop state- and county-level small area models estimating hysterectomy and CCS prevalence (with and without correcting hysterectomy). Model diagnostics and internal and external validation were conducted, including analyses of associations between CCS prevalence and cervical cancer incidence and mortality.
RESULTS: Model-based estimates of hysterectomy and CCS prevalence (both hysterectomy-corrected and uncorrected) were produced for all U.S. states and 3,142 counties for 2012-2016 and 2021-2023. Substantial geographic variation across counties was observed. Moderate negative correlations between CCS prevalence and cervical cancer incidence and mortality were identified, e.g., state-level weighted Pearson correlation coefficients were -0.3565 (p<0.0001) for 2012-2016 and -0.2638 (p<0.0001) for 2021-2023.
CONCLUSIONS: These modeled estimates improved precision and adjusted for differences between BRFSS and NHIS. Hysterectomy-corrected CCS estimates partially addressed misclassification of the screening-eligible population. By leveraging the large BRFSS sample and the higher response rates and household coverage of NHIS, this approach provides small area estimates to support cancer surveillance, targeted interventions, and public health decision-making.
IMPACT: These estimates serve as a resource for health departments and policymakers to identify underserved communities, prioritize resources, and monitor progress toward reducing disparities in cervical cancer prevention.

articles.title: Non-hormonal management of menopause symptoms-the statement of the European Society of Gynecology.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Castelo-Branco C, Kiesel L, Yoldemir T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal symptoms, particularly vasomotor symptoms (VMS), sleep disturbances, mood disorders, and genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), affect a substantial proportion of women and may significantly impair the quality of life. Although menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) remains the most effective treatment, many women have contraindications to hormonal treatment or prefer non-hormonal options.
OBJECTIVE: To review and provide evidence-based recommendations on current non-hormonal interventions for the management of menopausal symptoms.
METHODS: The European Society of Gynecology convened an expert panel that performed a comprehensive literature review using MEDLINE and EMBASE. Clinical guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyzes, randomized controlled trials, and relevant primary studies evaluating non-hormonal interventions for menopausal symptoms were identified, critically appraised, and synthesized through a structured consensus process.
RESULTS: Lifestyle modification, including healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight control, sleep hygiene, and behavioral interventions, forms the foundation of menopausal care. Among pharmacological therapies, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, clonidine, oxybutynin, and pregabalin demonstrate varying degrees of efficacy for VMS. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, particularly fezolinetant and elinzanetant, represent the most effective evidence-based non-hormonal pharmacologic therapies currently available. Cognitive behavioral therapy and clinical hypnosis effectively reduce VMS-related distress and improve sleep and quality of life. Evidence for complementary approaches such as mindfulness, yoga, acupuncture, acupressure, reflexology, phytoestrogens, S-equol, DT56a, purified pollen extracts, and black cohosh ranges from moderate to limited. For GSM, lubricants, moisturizers, hyaluronic acid preparations, and pelvic floor muscle training provide symptomatic benefit, whereas current evidence does not support routine use of vaginal laser therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-hormonal therapies provide effective and individualized treatment options for menopausal symptoms, particularly for women who are unable or unwilling to use MHT. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected pharmacologic agents, psychological interventions, and targeted GSM therapies represent the strongest evidence-based approaches currently available. The choice of…

articles.title: Topical Minoxidil for Female Pattern Hair Loss: Clinical Outcomes in Postmenopausal Women.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Waide RJ, Liu HP, Patel Shah A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female pattern hair loss (FPHL) affects up to 50% of women and becomes increasingly prevalent after menopause. Declining estrogen levels, altered hormonal balance, and follicular miniaturization contribute to disease progression, which can substantially impair quality of life (QoL).
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to review the pathophysiology and psychosocial impact of FPHL, discuss patient counseling and treatment expectations, and evaluate the benefits of topical minoxidil in postmenopausal women.
METHODS: Published evidence on FPHL pathophysiology, psychosocial outcomes, treatment barriers, and minoxidil efficacy and tolerability was searched for online using Google and via PubMed. Publications were reviewed for relevance based on the objectives as listed above before being selected for inclusion in our narrative. Findings from a post hoc subgroup analysis of postmenopausal women in a phase III clinical trial of once-daily 5% minoxidil topical foam (MTF) were also assessed.
RESULTS: FPHL is influenced by genetic susceptibility, aging, and menopausal hormonal changes. Hair loss is associated with reduced self-esteem, social withdrawal, anxiety, and impaired QoL. Delayed treatment initiation is common. In a phase III study, 5% MTF significantly increased hair count versus vehicle at 24 weeks. Post hoc analyses demonstrated significant hair regrowth in postmenopausal women with both early and advanced hair loss.
CONCLUSION: Once-daily 5% MTF is effective in postmenopausal women regardless of disease severity. Early recognition, patient education, individualized treatment selection, and psychosocial support are essential for optimal outcomes.

articles.title: Dry eye disease in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: the role of meibomian gland dysfunction and underlying mechanisms.
articles.authors: Bomze Z, Babik K, Nowinska A et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder that may be associated not only with reproductive and metabolic disturbances but also with ocular surface abnormalities, particularly dry eye disease (DED). Current evidence indicates that women with PCOS may exhibit structural and functional alterations of the meibomian glands, including gland loss, ductal abnormalities, and impaired lipid secretion, potentially contributing to tear film instability. Reduced tear break-up time (TBUT) is consistently reported, whereas Schirmer test results are often preserved, suggesting a predominantly evaporative dry eye phenotype. Hormonal imbalance, particularly hyperandrogenism, may play a complex and incompletely understood role in ocular surface homeostasis and could contribute to gland dysfunction. Furthermore, insulin resistance may impair meibomian gland metabolism, promote oxidative stress, and accelerate glandular atrophy. Chronic low-grade systemic inflammation has also been implicated and may further exacerbate ocular surface damage. The interaction of hormonal, metabolic, and inflammatory factors may increase the risk of DED in women with PCOS; however, the available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further well-designed studies are required to clarify underlying mechanisms and support the development of targeted multidisciplinary management strategies.

articles.title: Sexual, Pharmaceutical, and Lifestyle Variables in a Cohort of Pregnant Western Australian Women, and Their Association With Detection of Vaginal Microorganisms and Preterm Birth.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Payne MS, Doherty DA, Furfaro LL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The vaginal microbiome is shaped by factors such as sexual behaviour, smoking, and feminine hygiene practices. Although these associations are well documented in non-pregnant women, less is known in pregnancy, particularly in Australia, despite links between the vaginal microbiome and complications like preterm birth (PTB).
AIM: To document sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle variables in pregnant Australian women and examine their associations with vaginal microorganisms and, secondarily, PTB risk.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Mid-pregnancy (12-23 weeks' gestation) vaginal swabs from 936 women in the Predict1000 study were analysed for key microorganisms using qPCR. Participants completed a recruitment survey on medication use, urinary/vaginal infections, smoking, alcohol use, sexual practices, and vaginal douching. Associations between these factors, PTB (spontaneous and indicated), and specific microorganisms were assessed using Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney tests.
RESULTS: Thirteen percent of women reported smoking during pregnancy. Over half reported vaginal intercourse 1-2 times per week, although one quarter reported none. Thirty-two percent engaged in other sexual activities, most commonly oral sex (25%), followed by use of sex toys (11%). Vaginal douching was uncommon (3%). Sexual behaviour and douching were not associated with PTB risk. Smoking was associated with increased rates of non-optimal microbes, an association that persisted after correction for multiple comparisons. Associations between reduced frequency of vaginal intercourse (< 2 times/week) and lower prevalence of non-optimal vaginal microbes, and between douching and higher detection of Gardnerella vaginalis and Ureaplasma parvum, were also observed but did not remain significant after correction.
CONCLUSION: Sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle factors influenced the vaginal microbiota in pregnancy, but none were associated with PTB risk.

articles.title: Inositol for infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Vercoe MA, Rodenburg C, Mackenzie-Proctor R et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: This is an update of a previously published review. Women with infertility may use adjunctive therapies to improve reproductive outcomes. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are dietary supplements widely available and commonly used by women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS; renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in May 2026). The use of inositol for women with PCOS and infertility is based on proposed effects on insulin sensitivity and ovarian function. In clinical practice, myo-inositol is frequently prescribed for women with PCOS undergoing ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination or before in vitro fertilisation (IVF). However, the quality and certainty of the evidence supporting this practice remains unclear.
