This review aimed to assess the benefits and harms of inositol (including myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol) in women with PCOS experiencing infertility.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the benefits and harms of inositol oral supplementation for reproductive outcomes among women with polycystic ovary syndrome experiencing infertility.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL (which includes trial registries), the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group Specialised Register, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, AMED, and Epistemonikos to 10 November 2025. We also checked reference lists and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that compared any type, dose, or combination of oral inositol versus placebo, no treatment, or another active intervention in women with PCOS and infertility. Trials that compared different types of inositol were also eligible.
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were live birth and any adverse event (including miscarriage, multiple pregnancy, and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS)), as reported by trial investigators. Our important outcomes were clinical pregnancy and gestational diabetes.
RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two review authors independently selected eligible studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. We pooled studies using a fixed-effect model, and calculated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We assessed the overall certainty of evidence by applying GRADE. The primary analyses of all review outcomes were restricted to studies at low risk of selection bias. We also conducted sensitivity analyses including all…

articles.title: Patterns of Care in Patients With Cervical Cancer in Western Australia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Mannolini K, Nathan E, Leung Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is an important public health concern with underserved populations having higher incidence and mortality.
AIMS: To examine associations between patient and tumour characteristics, receipt of appropriate treatment and survival.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of cervical cancer patients managed by the Western Australian Gynaecological Cancer Service from 1 January 2009 to 31 December 2018. Appropriate treatment was defined by international guidelines. Univariable and multivariable analyses assessed associations between demographic and tumour factors and receipt of appropriate treatment. Survival outcomes were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: Of 526 patients included, 95.4% received treatment, of which 94.4% received appropriate treatment. Non-English-speaking patients had reduced odds of completing treatment (OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.80, p = 0.018), and patients of lower socioeconomic status had reduced odds of timely treatment (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.93, p = 0.025). Patients aged over 60 years had lower odds of receiving any, complete and timely treatment. Those diagnosed between 2014 and 2018, versus 2009-2013 had increased odds of completing treatment (OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.45-6.45, p = 0.003). Higher disease stage was associated with lower odds of receiving and completing treatment. Overall- and disease-free survival were poorer among patients aged over 60, those with advanced-stage disease, those diagnosed in 2009-2013, and those who received incomplete treatment or no treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Most patients received appropriate treatment. Non-English-speaking patients, older patients, and those of low socioeconomic status were less likely to receive appropriate care. Older age, advanced disease stage, diagnosis in 2009-2013, and incomplete treatment were associated with poorer survival.

articles.title: Misdiagnosed as a Urinary Tract Infection: A Rare Presentation of Advanced Vulval Carcinoma with Urinary Symptoms and Introital Obliteration in an Octogenarian.
articles.authors: Sarwade A, Sharma SV, Kolate D
articles.abstract: Vulval carcinoma is an uncommon but clinically significant gynecological malignancy that disproportionately affects elderly postmenopausal women. Diagnosis is frequently delayed because of atypical presenting complaints, social stigma surrounding genital examination, and the tendency to attribute symptoms to more benign urological conditions. We describe an 82-year-old multiparous woman (para 8, living 8) with a 30-year history of menopause who was initially managed elsewhere for a presumed urinary tract infection before being referred to our department. She presented with a 3-month history of progressive burning micturition and perineal pain. Examination revealed a fungating right labial mass with seropurulent discharge, complete obliteration of the introitus, and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Per-rectal examination confirmed posterior vaginal wall fixity. Punch biopsy of the lesion demonstrated well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Staging workup classified the disease as FIGO Stage IIIC. The patient was referred for multimodal oncological management. This case illustrates that urinary symptoms in elderly women warrant thorough genital examination to exclude vulval malignancy. A high index of clinical suspicion, early biopsy, and prompt oncological referral are essential to improving outcomes in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Patient Perceptions of Clinician Attire in the Outpatient Urogynecology Clinic.
articles.authors: Chong W, Gencerliler N, DiDominica M
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Clinician attire is a visible, nonverbal component of the clinical encounter that influences patient perception. Understanding its effect in sensitive subspecialties like urogynecology provides actionable insights for clinical communication.
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated how clinician attire influences patient perceptions of professionalism, friendliness, aptitude, and empathy within an outpatient urogynecology setting.
STUDY DESIGN: In this single-center, cross-sectional survey, adult female patients rated 4 standardized, artificial intelligence-generated photographs of a gender-neutral model wearing (1) formal attire, (2) formal attire with a white coat, (3) scrubs, and (4) scrubs with a white coat. Participants used a 5-point Likert scale to assess each image across the 4 domains. Data were analyzed using 1-way repeated-measures analysis of variance and mixed-effects linear regression models to assess the independent and interactive effects of scrubs and white-coat use.
RESULTS: A total of 222 participants completed the survey. Clinician attire significantly influenced all 4 perception domains (P<0.001). Formal attire without a white coat was consistently rated the lowest. Formal attire with a white coat received the highest ratings for professionalism and aptitude, whereas scrubs scored highest for friendliness and empathy. Mixed-effects models demonstrated that white coats independently correlated with higher ratings across all domains. Conversely, although scrubs were associated with higher perceived friendliness, empathy, and aptitude, they resulted in slightly lower professionalism ratings compared with formal attire. A negative interaction term indicated that the white coat's positive effect was attenuated when paired with scrubs.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinician attire significantly shapes patient perceptions in urogynecology. Although white coats bolster perceived professionalism and aptitude, scrubs enhance friendliness and empathy. Attire is a modifiable factor that clinicians can strategically align with the goals of specific encounters.

articles.title: Pedagogical assessment of an online nursing course on advanced practice in promoting childhood continence.
articles.authors: Rodrigues NDS, Coelho MMF, Martins G
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: to assess the pedagogical structure and content validity evidence of an online course on Advanced Practice Nursing in promoting infant continence.
METHODS: a methodological study for content assessment with the participation of 14 experts using the Educational Content Validity Instrument in Health. Data were analyzed using R 4.2.2 software, applying the Friedman and Kruskal-Wallis tests and calculating the Content Validity Coefficient and the Content Validity Index.
RESULTS: the course demonstrated high pedagogical validity and overall consistency across the instrument's domains, with an average score of 96.2% and expert assessments above the 80% cut-off point, demonstrating the robustness and practical applicability of the educational material.
CONCLUSIONS: the course demonstrated validity and relevance, establishing itself as an effective educational strategy for training nursing students in promoting infant continence.

articles.title: Male infertility disclosure on Reddit: a study of emotional expression, information exchange, and peer support.
articles.authors: Khatun M, Patel N, Loid M et al.
articles.abstract: Infertility imposes significant psychological and social burdens on both women and men. However, research on infertility communication has predominantly focused on women, leaving discussions of male infertility (MI) relatively underexplored. This study investigates MI-related communication within the r/maleinfertility subreddit on Reddit. Using natural language processing, we analysed 10,769 posts and 80,381 comments published between 2013 and 2025, examining sentiment, emotion, topic structure, hyperlink networks, and discussions surrounding diagnostic testing, treatment decisions, and donor sperm. Topic modelling revealed distinct communication functions. Posts primarily focused on clinical sense-making, including interpretation of semen analysis results, hormonal testing, and assisted reproduction decisions, whereas comments emphasised emotional support, experiential guidance, and alternative reproductive pathways. Emotional expression varied across topics, with heightened fear and sadness in discussions involving genetic testing, surgical sperm retrieval, and donor sperm. Hyperlink analysis revealed frequent references to peer-reviewed medical literature, suggesting active evidence-seeking behaviour. These findings highlight the role of online peer communities in providing emotional support and facilitating information exchange about MI. Such communities may complement clinical care by helping individuals interpret diagnoses, manage emotional distress, and navigate treatment and donor-related decisions.

articles.title: Environmentally Relevant F-53B Exposure Triggers Ovarian Cancer Progression via C5aR1-Mediated Noncanonical Signaling: An Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) Underlying Hybrid EMT and Stemness.
articles.authors: Dong S, Wang Y, Fang S et al.
articles.abstract: Significant gaps remain in the health risk assessment methodologies for the PFOS (perfluorooctanesulfonic acid) alternative 6:2 Cl-PFESA (6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate, F-53B), which has been widely recognized as the alternative to PFOS in China. To address this research gap, our study integrated multidimensional techniques to mechanistically construct an Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for F-53B-induced ovarian cancer progression. Our findings demonstrated that exposure to environmentally relevant concentrations of F-53B significantly enhanced the migratory and invasive capabilities of ovarian cancer cells. Within the AOP framework of F-53B-induced hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and enhanced tumor stemness, the upregulation of C5aR1─triggered by ERα acting as a noncanonical receptor of F-53B─constitutes the molecular initiating event (MIE). Following this MIE, the recruitment of β-arrestin1 and Src was induced, leading to the assembly of a C5aR1/β-arrestin1/Src signaling complex. This complex facilitated the binding of β-arrestin1 to β-catenin and drove the nuclear translocation of β-catenin, ultimately activating hybrid EMT and stemness of tumor cells. Administration of the C5aR1 inhibitor PMX205 effectively abrogated subsequent key events (KEs) caused by F-53B exposure. Through in vitro and in vivo validation, our study established an AOP framework that provides a novel perspective for evaluating the potential risk of PFAS substitutes in promoting cancer progression.

articles.title: Prevalence and Predictors of Intrauterine Device Failure Among Women in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Nanyiri J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although highly effective in unintended pregnancy prevention, intrauterine device uptake remains perennially low in sub-Saharan Africa, partly due to the perceived risk of device failure, whose prevalence and predictors remain poorly understood in the sub-regional context.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence and predictors of intrauterine device failure (IUDF) in women in sub-Saharan Africa.
METHODS: A scoping review approach was used, with comprehensive searches conducted in ten databases: ProQuest, EBSCO, PubMed, ScienceDirect, MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The search was guided by article saturation to minimize duplication. The Population (P), concept (C), and context (C) approaches were used to set the eligibility criteria, and data were analyzed using descriptive frequency counting and content analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 51 studies identified through the search strategy, only six full-text articles met the eligibility criteria. Only five of these studies quantified the prevalence of Intrauterine Device (IUD) failure, which ranged from 0.2% to 7.4%, with the highest reported in Ethiopia. Only three studies reported predictors of IUD failure, including nationality, increasing parity, mispositioning during insertion, small uterine cavity, and IUD fitting by less experienced healthcare workers.
CONCLUSION: Over the past 10 years, very few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have credibly estimated the prevalence of IUD failure or identified predictors of IUD failure. Only six studies made such an attempt; however, none were designed with methodological rigor to allow credible quantification of the prevalence of IUD failure. Although all six studies included IUD failure as an outcome, none explicitly examined the predictors of IUD failure. Nonetheless, the few available studies indicate that IUD failure is a reality, with significant variation across regions ranging from 0.2% to 7.4%. Both intrapersonal and service provision characteristics predict IUD failure, with the service provision factors taking precedence.

articles.title: Effects of a preconception lifestyle intervention on cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes: secondary findings from the BEFORE THE BEGINNING randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Sujan MAJ, Skarstad HMS, Rosvold G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity rates are rising globally, and many females of reproductive age are physically inactive, which may adversely affect future maternal and neonatal health. In this secondary analysis, we investigated the effect of a combined preconception lifestyle intervention on cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes after 7 weeks.
METHODS: This article reports analyses of secondary outcomes from the BEFORE THE BEGINNING randomised controlled trial, in which we randomised females who were planning pregnancy, at risk of gestational diabetes mellitus and did not have diagnosed diabetes 1:1 to intervention or control. The intervention consisted of time-restricted eating (TRE) and exercise training and spanned from preconception throughout pregnancy. TRE involved restricting energy intake to ≤10 hour/day on ≥5 days per week. Exercise volume was based on a heart-rate-based metric (Personal Activity Intelligence, PAI), with the goal of ≥100 weekly PAI-points. The main outcomes of interest in this secondary analysis were cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes after 7 weeks of intervention in the preconception period.
RESULTS: Among 167 randomised participants, we included 166 in the intention-to-treat analysis. After 7 weeks of preconception intervention, there was no significant between-group difference in relative peak oxygen uptake (0.8 mL·kg-1·min-1; 95% CI -0.2 to 1.9, p=0.10) or glucose area under the curve (0.0 mmol·hour/L; 95% CI -0.1 to 0.2, p=0.76).
CONCLUSION: 7 weeks of preconception TRE combined with exercise training did not result in statistically significant improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness or glycaemic outcomes in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04585581.

articles.title: Literature-Derived Network and Semantic Mapping of Pain Catastrophizing and Traditional East Asian Medicine Pattern Constructs.
articles.authors: Kim TY, Kim JH, Kim JH
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pain catastrophizing comprises rumination, magnification, and helplessness. Different medical traditions may describe neighboring cognitive, affective, somatic, and functional domains using different vocabularies. We characterized literature-derived conceptual proximity between pain-catastrophizing subdomains and traditional East Asian medicine pattern constructs without treating proximity as diagnostic or clinical correspondence.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, PubMed Central, and OASIS were accessed on June 5, 2026. The final analysis was restricted to 2259 PubMed Central-retrieved full-text records; 2214 met corpus criteria. Three pain-catastrophizing subdomains and 14 traditional East Asian medicine pattern constructs formed 42 candidate pairs, of which 24 were graph connected and 18 unconnected. The primary mapping score combined semantic similarity, a graph-derived weighted common-neighbor component, and binary graph proximity. Peer-review-requested validation quantified pattern- versus subdomain-level score variation, used 10,000 constrained permutations, and evaluated a node-strength-normalized common-neighbor sensitivity.
RESULTS: Pattern construct accounted for 99.91% of total primary-score variation, compared with 0.04% for pain-catastrophizing subdomain. Across the 24 connected pairs, 129 shortest two-edge paths involved six intermediate nodes rather than a single bridge. In the constrained null analysis, the maximum observed score was not unusually extreme (empirical p=0.0831), whereas the mean of the five highest scores (p=0.0024) and the concentration of variance by pattern construct (p<0.001) exceeded null expectations. Node-strength normalization changed the highest-ranked pattern construct from phlegm-related to dampness; adjusted and primary ranks remained correlated (Spearman rho=0.9509), but top-five overlap was 2 of 5.
CONCLUSION: The analysis identified a pattern-dominant, literature-conditioned structure rather than strongly pair-specific mappings. Results were sensitive to graph-strength normalization. They characterize conceptual proximity in published texts and graph structure; they do not establish diagnostic equivalence, clinical validity, causality, treatment efficacy, or treatment guidance.

articles.title: Research priorities for sexual and reproductive health, equity, and access in a post-Roe context.
articles.authors: DeCosta D, Desai S, Malcolm N et al.
articles.abstract: Since the 2022 U.S. Supreme Court ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, state-level laws governing health care provision and access have increased. While the current legal landscape has devastating consequences for abortion, evidence suggests ripple effects on sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care and equity broadly. A coordinated, robust body of research is needed to understand, anticipate, and respond to the far-reaching consequences of this ruling. This commentary brings together perspectives from the SRH and health services fields to present six research priorities that researchers, funders, policymakers, and advocates can leverage to advance SRH care access and equity.

articles.title: Sleep duration and anti-müllerian hormone levels in female firefighters.
articles.authors: Baker JA, Valenti M, Farland LV et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) levels and sleep duration in female firefighters.
STUDY DESIGN: We used baseline data collected at time of enrollment into the Women Firefighter Study, part of the Fire Fighter Cancer Cohort Study (FFCCS), including demographic information, reproductive history, and self-reported average off-duty sleep, along with serum AMH concentration.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: We used linear regression models to estimate the association between off-duty sleep duration (categorized by <7 hours and ≥ 7 hours on average) and log transformed AMH. We adjusted for age (continuous and squared), body mass index (BMI), and oral contraception use. The formula (exp (  β ^   )-1)*100 was used to calculate the percent difference in AMH values.
RESULTS: Among 566 participants, those that reported <7 hours of sleep while off-duty had statistically significantly lower AMH levels compared to those who reported ≥ 7 hours of off-duty sleep (-18.0 %, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -32.7, -0.2).
CONCLUSION: Less than 7 hours of off-duty sleep was associated with lower AMH levels. Increasing off-duty sleep is a potential modifiable risk factor to benefit reproductive health in female firefighters.

articles.title: Research progress of artificial intelligence applications in obstetrics.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Liu Y, Zhao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across obstetrics, with applications spanning electronic medical record analysis, prenatal ultrasound, fetal monitoring, prediction of pregnancy complications, labor management, postpartum care, and telemedicine. The evidence reviewed in this article indicates that AI can improve automated information extraction, image and signal interpretation, and risk discrimination across multiple obstetric tasks, with particularly consistent advances in fetal ultrasound analysis, cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation, and early prediction of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. However, model performance is heterogeneous and is often reported using discrimination or classification metrics rather than patient-centered clinical outcomes. In CTG research, models differ substantially in whether they classify interpretation categories, detect fetal hypoxia or acidemia, or predict neonatal outcomes, making direct comparison difficult. Similarly, high predictive accuracy for pregnancy complications does not establish that AI implementation itself improves maternal or neonatal outcomes, and the clinical benefit of treatment should not be attributed to the predictive model without intervention studies. Across obstetric applications, limited external validation, dataset shift, class imbalance, calibration, interpretability, workflow integration, and data governance remain major barriers to clinical translation. This review therefore emphasizes the distinction between technical model performance and demonstrated clinical utility, and highlights the evidence required to move AI applications from retrospective development toward prospective, clinically integrated obstetric care.

articles.title: Interplay of Insulin Resistance, Hyperandrogenism, and Obesity in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Insights.
articles.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
articles.authors: Bao F, Sun L, Guo W
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex disorder of ovarian dysfunction primarily driven by a self-perpetuating pathophysiological cycle. This network centrally involves the interplay of insulin resistance (IR), hyperandrogenism, and obesity. IR stimulates ovarian and adrenal androgen production and can promote increased food intake. The resulting hyperandrogenemia, in turn, exacerbates insulin resistance and contributes to obesity. Furthermore, obesity worsens both IR and hormonal dysregulation through the release of inflammatory cytokines and adipokines, thereby reinforcing the entire cycle. This narrative review aims to critically examine the core pathological interplay between IR, hyperandrogenism, and obesity in PCOS. Building on this foundation, the review systematically explores the rationale and emerging evidence for novel therapeutic strategies that target these key components, moving beyond the established framework of current treatments. Lifestyle interventions, including dietary modification and physical activity, remain the cornerstone of PCOS management, particularly for overweight and obese patients. Current PCOS management primarily relies on oral contraceptives for symptomatic control of hyperandrogenism. Insulin-sensitizing agents form the other pillar of therapy. While metformin is widely used, newer classes of antidiabetic drug-including Dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors, sodium-glucose co-transporter protein 2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists-have demonstrated potential benefits that extend beyond glycemic control, offering improvements in weight, insulin sensitivity, and androgen levels. The discussion also extends to future perspectives, evaluating investigational approaches such as stem cell therapy and aldo-keto reductase 3 inhibitors, which, though not yet part of clinical practice, may represent future targeted treatment avenues. The management of PCOS is evolving from a symptomatic approach towards a more pathophysiologically-targeted and personalized strategy. A deep understanding of the IR-hyperandrogenism-obesity cycle is crucial for developing and implementing these novel therapies, which hold promise for improving long-term reproductive, metabolic, and cardiovascular outcomes for patients with PCOS. Future research should focus on validating these emerging treatments through robust clinical trials and defining their place within individualized treatment algorithms.

articles.title: Semicurative Radiation Therapy for Cervical Cancer in a Nonagenarian: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.journal: Case reports in obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Kusada T, Kinjo M, Oshiro D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The number of nonagenarians has been increasing globally. However, they are less likely to get specialist consultations. This may be due to the lack of an appropriate treatment method for them and uncertainty about the intensity and range of treatments they need and can tolerate. Radiation therapy (RT) is often administered to older patients, including nonagenarians, and its efficacy and safety have been reported in many studies.
CASE PRESENTATION: We present a literature review and the case of a nonagenarian with cervical cancer who was treated with "semicurative" RT and achieved good treatment outcomes, although the observation period was only 12 months. We defined semicurative RT as RT that is less aggressive than curative RT but more aggressive than palliative RT or no treatment, aiming to control cancer. A 92-year-old woman was diagnosed with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics Stage IIB cervical squamous cell carcinoma. The patient and her family agreed that she would undergo semicurative RT. After completion of 45 Gy small-pelvis irradiation by external beam RT, tumor shrinkage was observed on magnetic resonance imaging, and her general condition was preserved. Therefore, irradiation at 18 Gy in three fractions was planned for the high-risk clinical target volume comprising the uterine cervix and tumor by brachytherapy. However, the patient experienced fatigue after the second fraction and requested to finish treatment without the last fraction. After treatment, the cervical tumor disappeared without severe late complications related to RT, despite vaginal adhesion, and the patient was able to perform activities of daily living.
CONCLUSION: Semicurative RT may be considered for nonagenarian patients with cervical cancer when their general condition is good and they want high treatment efficacy without severe complications. However, further studies on semicurative RT for this patient population are warranted.

articles.title: Glycoursodeoxycholic Acid and Insulin Resistance in Women With Normoandrogenic Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization.
articles.authors: Lv L, Yin X, Zhu T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To characterize paired serum and follicular fluid (FF) bile acids in normoandrogenic polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (NA-PMOS) and investigate associations of glycoursodeoxycholic acid (GUDCA) with endocrine-metabolic indices and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 20 women with NA-PMOS and 20 age-comparable controls without PMOS undergoing IVF. Fifteen bile acids were measured in serum and FF. Analyses assessed group differences, metabolic and IVF associations, and discrimination between diagnostic groups.
RESULTS: Compared with controls without PMOS, women with NA-PMOS had higher fasting insulin, triglycerides, and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and a lower high-quality embryo rate. GUDCA was lower in NA-PMOS in FF (137.01 vs. 332.60 nmol/L; p = 0.0004768; q = 0.007152) and serum (31.59 vs. 71.85 nmol/L; p = 0.03022; q = 0.2704). Apparent areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.849 for FF, 0.713 for serum, and 0.871 for their combination. Serum GUDCA correlated inversely with TyG (ρ = -0.582, p = 0.0028); the association persisted after adjustment for age, BMI, and diagnostic group (β = -0.348, p = 0.0415). Within NA-PMOS, serum GUDCA correlated inversely with fasting insulin and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). In the pooled cohort, FF GUDCA correlated inversely with baseline anti-Müllerian hormone, total testosterone, and oocyte counts. GUDCA in neither matrix was significantly associated with high-quality embryo rate.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower GUDCA in serum and FF characterizes this exploratory IVF-based NA-PMOS sample, with stronger between-group evidence in FF. Serum GUDCA was associated with metabolic indices, while FF GUDCA was associated with ovarian characteristics and response. No significant association with high-quality embryo rate was observed. These findings warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Prevalence of anaemia, associated factors and utilisation of anaemia control interventions among women of reproductive age in rural Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Johny V F, Mangalath SC, Maliakel SF et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anaemia remains a major public health concern among women of reproductive age, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite national initiatives in India, including Anaemia Mukt Bharat, the burden of anaemia and utilisation of control interventions vary across settings. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anaemia and examine its associated factors in a rural area of Kerala.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 160 women aged 18-49 years in a rural area of Thrissur district, Kerala, between September 2023 and March 2024. A multistage sampling technique was used. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and haemoglobin was measured using a portable haemoglobinometer. Anaemia was defined according to WHO criteria. Associations were assessed using χ2 tests and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: The prevalence of anaemia was 71.9%, with most cases being moderate (60.0%) and no severe anaemia observed. Younger women (18-24 years) had a higher prevalence. Women aged 25-34 years had lower odds of anaemia compared with those aged 18-24 years (adjusted OR (AOR) 0.08; 95% CI 0.01 to 0.67). Recent anthelminthic intake (AOR 0.30; 95% CI 0.13 to 0.72) and receipt of government iron supplementation (AOR 0.31; 95% CI 0.10 to 0.96) were associated with lower odds. Among recipients, obtaining iron supplementation from primary health centres was associated with lower odds than field-level distribution (AOR 0.14; 95% CI 0.04 to 0.57). Only 40.6% reported using any contraceptive method.
CONCLUSIONS: A high prevalence of anaemia was observed among women of reproductive age in this rural Kerala setting, with younger age, recent anthelminthic intake and government iron supplementation being significantly associated with anaemia status. These findings highlight the need for further research to better understand the utilisation of anaemia control interventions and their relationship with anaemia in similar settings.

articles.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a digital tool for monitoring family planning service quality in Women's routine visits: A mixed method formative pilot study.
articles.authors: Ubuane OI, Baruwa S, Akomolafe TO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The evolving landscape of family planning (FP) services in Nigeria includes digital tools for monitoring and assessing the quality of care (QoC), along with the broader healthcare system's focus on primary health care (PHC). This transformation is not unique to Nigeria; many countries recognize the crucial and interconnected roles that PHC and QoC play in ensuring access to essential health services, promoting community well-being, and improving health outcomes. This study aims to provide insights into the perceptions and experiences of women utilizing a digital tool to assess the QoC they receive in Nigeria, discuss the challenges faced by users, and their suggestions for improvement.
METHODS: The Digital FP QoC monitoring survey was self-administered by FP clients of Patent and Proprietary Medicine Vendors (PPMVs). Clients were encouraged to take a monitoring survey using QR code scanning. Two focus group discussions with five to ten women from each state were conducted after four weeks of data collection. The transcripts were uploaded and analyzed using the NVivo version R software.
RESULTS: The women's perceptions of the digital tool were overwhelmingly positive. Most women expressed that the survey questions were clear and easy to understand. Almost all women reported challenges with device compatibility and a lack of Internet data/network, highlighting the potential barriers faced by women in different regions, especially those in rural areas.
CONCLUSION: This study underscores the significance of healthcare provider support, user-friendly design, and the need for a balanced approach that considers the preferences and challenges faced by women from different demographic groups and regions.

articles.title: ASTRO study: acupuncture sets of trial reported core outcomes for women's health across the lifespan.
articles.authors: Levett KM, Buay VC, Citkovitz C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical trials of acupuncture are difficult to meaningfully aggregate due to small sample sizes and reductionist, heterogeneous outcome measures. To improve the quality of evidence, standardised reporting of minimum data that reflects whole-person health, essential to East Asian Medicine (EAM), is needed. The Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) initiative offers a methodology for developing core outcome sets (COS) through collaborative group consensus, including consumers. This study presents the 'Acupuncture Sets of Trial Reported Outcomes' (ASTRO) for women's health. Using domains of pain, sleep, mood/cognition and safety, the ASTRO framework captures EAM complexity as well as standardising reporting outcomes.
PURPOSE: To develop a COS for acupuncture trials in women's health, reflecting whole-person health outcomes across the lifespan.
METHODS: We used a COMET-informed three-stage consensus process involving practitioners, researchers, patients and policymakers to develop a COS for reporting minimum data for acupuncture trials in women's health. This process involved a systematic review, roundtable discussion, two-round Delphi survey and a consensus meeting. We examined the conditions of menstrual health, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, fertility, pregnancy and menopause to develop an outcome set for safety, feasibility and EAM specific outcomes.
RESULTS: From 320 studies, 579 outcomes were identified for the survey items and 319 respondents participated in two Delphi survey rounds. The attrition rate was 52% between surveys and respondents were mainly from English-speaking countries. A final COS of 12 outcomes was agreed on:Safety (n=2): serious adverse events and minor adverse events.EAM (n=8): primary and secondary patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), patient experience/satisfaction, EAM diagnostic indices (eg, tongue and pulse), demographics and changes in pain, sleep and mood/cognition.Feasibility (n=2): acceptability and cost.
CONCLUSIONS: The ASTRO Women's Health COS enables consistent, whole-person outcome reporting to improve the quality and comparability of acupuncture research.

articles.title: Large language model-assisted machine learning for postpartum urinary incontinence prediction: Model development and validation study.
articles.authors: Xie F, Wang X, Liu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Accurate prediction of postpartum urinary incontinence (UI) remains challenging, as existing models often fail to fully utilize information in unstructured electronic medical records (EMRs). This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model integrating structured and unstructured clinical data to improve postpartum UI risk assessment.
METHODS: Two prospective cohorts were recruited for model development and validation. A large language model (LLM) was used to extract clinical information from unstructured EMRs and integrate it with structured data. Seven machine learning algorithms were trained and internally validated using stratified five-fold cross-validation, with the optimal model selected based on the area under the curve (AUC). The final model was externally validated and compared with a baseline logistic regression model developed using structured data only. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was used to interpret feature importance.
RESULTS: A total of 1605 pregnant women were included, and 20.7% experienced postpartum UI. LLM achieved up to 98.9% overall accuracy in extracting information from unstructured EMRs. Among the seven models, the multilayer perceptron (MLP) achieved the best performance, with internal validation and external validation AUC of 0.813 and 0.782, respectively, outperforming the baseline model. SHAP identified severity of UI during pregnancy, duration of second stage of labor, and number of vaginal deliveries as the most influential predictive factors in the model. A web-based calculator was developed to support future clinical implementation.
CONCLUSIONS: By incorporating a LLM into the development process, we established a robust prediction model for postpartum UI. This innovative approach may facilitate early risk identification.

articles.title: Delayed Secondary Postpartum Hemorrhage 15 Days After Repeat Cesarean Delivery Complicated by Endometritis, Hysterotomy Dehiscence, and Definitive Hysterectomy.
articles.authors: Jaimes AVP, Sparagana S, Carrillo L et al.
articles.abstract: Delayed postpartum hemorrhage after cesarean delivery should prompt consideration of uterine incision dehiscence, particularly when accompanied by fever, persistent bleeding despite conservative therapy, or imaging suggestive of hematometra. Early multidisciplinary evaluation and timely definitive surgical management may be lifesaving and prevent progression to hemorrhagic shock, sepsis, and maternal morbidity.

articles.title: SVIP knockdown alters UPS protein expression in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells.
articles.authors: Kipel Ş, Çayli S, Aktaş Gİ et al.
articles.abstract: Testicular tumours are the most common malignant tumors in men between the ages of 15-34. Approximately 95% of testicular tumors arise from germ cells. Small VCP-interacting protein (SVIP) is a protein that regulates its function and autophagy by binding to p97/VCP, which is involved in protein degradation associated with the endoplasmic reticulum. Recent studies on SVIP have shown that SVIP is an androgen-sensitive protein. The development of secondary sex characteristics is influenced by androgens, which are significant steroid hormone. Androgens also initiate and maintain spermatogenesis in the male reproductive system. Mutations of androgen receptors are often seen in patients with disorders of male reproductive development and can cause male infertility. Studies are showing that the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) in the male reproductive system affects fertility. Therefore, investigating the expressions of USP26 and UXT, which are components of the UPS, is important for testicular biology. The expressions of SVIP, AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT were analysed by immunofluorescence, western blot and q RT-PCR method to determine the expressions of SVIP and the UPS proteins that it interacts in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells (CRL-2073) and to see the effects of suppressed SVIP expression on other proteins after SVIP siRNA transfection. At SVIP siRNA applied CRL-2073 cells, SVIP, AR, USP26 and Ubiquitin expressions decreased, while UXT expression increased, according to immunofluorescence and western blot results. According to the qRT-PCR results, SVIP gene expression decreased and AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT gene expressions increased in the group given SVIP siRNA. As a result, this study demonstrated the expression of SVIP and its interacting UPS proteins in CRL-2073 cells for the first time, making an unique and significant contribution to the literature.

articles.title: Disputes over frozen embryos in China: an empirical legal-ethical analysis of judicial practice.
articles.journal: Journal of law and the biosciences
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Lin Y
articles.abstract: This Article analyses 94 frozen-embryo dispute case records from China, identified through China Judgments Online and spanning docket years 2013-25. It distinguishes claims for continued performance of assisted reproductive technology (ART) medical service contracts from claims for embryo return or disposition. Four factual scenarios concern continued ART after a spouse's death or disappearance, posthumous family or kinship claims, post-divorce disputes, and return disputes during marriage; three records lack sufficient information for scenario assignment. Plaintiffs obtained full or partial embryo-related civil relief in 87 cases (92.55 per cent), including rights recognition that does not necessarily permit clinical embryo transfer. Courts used public-order and related ethical reasoning in divergent ways, while some decisions expanded protection for widowed women continuing an existing reproductive project. Persistent difficulties include embryos' uncertain legal status, gaps in rules for exceptional circumstances, conflicting normative frameworks, and safeguards against unlawful surrogacy. The Article proposes treating frozen embryos as a special category of 'ethical objects' and refining scenario-specific disposition rules, institutional obligations, and ethical oversight to protect reproductive interests while addressing downstream risks.

articles.title: Proteomics-based immune activation signatures are associated with kidney allograft rejection.
articles.authors: Schröter I, Loi L, Rudek M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biopsy-based diagnostics for the detection of kidney allograft rejection are invasive and imperfect, highlighting the need for non-invasive biomarkers. However, the potential of plasma proteomics for assessing alloimmune injury remains unclear.
METHODS: Therefore, proteomic profiling was performed in 88 kidney transplant recipients undergoing indication biopsy using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Differential protein expression analyses compared biopsy-proven rejection with no rejection. A composite proteomic score derived from the three most discriminatory proteins was evaluated in relation to histopathology, donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA), and graft outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 92 analyzed proteins, TNFRSF9 showed the strongest association with rejection, followed by CXCL9 and IL-12B. The composite proteomic score discriminated rejection from no rejection (AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), while integration with dd-cfDNA improved discrimination (AUC 0.88, 95% CI 0.78-0.99). Signals from the predefined inflammation-related protein panel increased progressively from no rejection to borderline changes and overt rejection (P < 0.001). The score correlated with histopathological indices of activity, antibody-mediated rejection/microvascular inflammation, T-cell-mediated rejection/tubulointerstitial inflammation, and chronicity. Patients with borderline changes displayed heterogeneous proteomic signatures, with most overlapping the no-rejection group and a smaller subset exhibiting rejection-like signatures. The score correlated moderately with dd-cfDNA (ρ=0.32, P = 0.009) and remained independently associated with death-censored graft failure (HR 2.67, 95% CI 1.31-5.42).
CONCLUSION: Together, these exploratory findings suggest that plasma proteomic signatures may reflect aspects of alloimmune injury across the rejection spectrum and are associated with chronic histological damage and graft failure. These findings support further investigation of plasma proteomics as a complementary approach for non-invasive assessment of kidney allograft injury while potentially also offering insights into mechanisms driving progressive allograft dysfunction.

articles.title: IVF medical tourism in Malaysia-an overview of current market dynamics and ethical challenges for intended parents/patients.
articles.journal: Journal of law and the biosciences
articles.authors: Chin AHB, Roslan R, Mohamad CABC et al.
articles.abstract: In vitro fertilization (IVF) medical tourism is expanding as more patients travel to jurisdictions offering treatments restricted or unavailable at home. Malaysia is a favored Asian destination because of its permissive clinical assisted reproduction environment, particularly in the case of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), elective egg freezing (EEF), and egg donation. Using credence goods theory, this article argues that the risk is information asymmetry. Fertility clinics possess information that intended parents/patients cannot readily assess, even after treatment, and may therefore misrepresent services. This asymmetry is intensified where decisions are emotionally-pressured, age-sensitive, costly, and irreversible. The article examines PGT-A, EEF, and egg donation as illustrations of this risk. It treats underhand practices not as established facts, but as possible vulnerabilities created by regulatory gaps. The analysis also examines the failures of the 2009 and 2016 ART (Assisted Reproductive Technique) services bills, arguing that durable legislation requires consensus among medical, religious, commercial, governmental, and patient stakeholders. Malaysia should replace non-enforceable guidelines with a coherent ART regulatory framework incorporating mandatory disclosure, advertising restrictions, independent counseling, cooling-off periods, licensing, audit, and enforceable sanctions. Such reforms would reduce misrepresentation, safeguard foreign patients, and strengthen Malaysia's standing as an IVF medical-tourism destination.

articles.title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
articles.authors: Brooks HL, Sylvester MA, Michea L
articles.abstract: Hypertension is an inflammatory disease with the immune system playing a key role in mediating hypertensive outcomes and end-organ damage. The risk of hypertension is greater in men than in women before women enter menopause. After menopause, a woman's risk for developing hypertension increases and accelerates beyond that of age-matched men. Moreover, after menopause, the rate of hypertension control in women is lower than in men. Indeed, cardiovascular drug efficacy in women is different from that in men, with recent studies highlighting serious side effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and β-blockers in postmenopausal women. Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

articles.title: Weight-loss effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-age women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Wu HY, Zhang M, Yao F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In reproductive-aged women with polycystic ovary syndrome, overweight or obesity exacerbates metabolic and reproductive risks; lifestyle interventions and metformin have limited weight-loss effects, and more effective pharmacological weight-loss strategies are urgently needed. The aim of this article is to evaluate the weight-loss and body-shape outcomes of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, and to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence.
METHODS: Multiple databases and trial registry platforms were searched (2015.1-2025.12), and parallel RCTs in reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists with non-GLP-1 regimens were included. The primary outcome was body weight change, secondary outcomes were BMI and waist circumference, and the exploratory outcome was visceral adiposity. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed, with effect sizes as mean difference or Hedges-corrected standardized mean difference, and RoB 2 and GRADE were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Five RCTs (N.=319) were included. Compared with controls, GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduced body weight (MD -2.80 kg, 95% CI: -3.94~-1.66), BMI (MD -1.02 kg/m2, 95% CI: -1.41~-0.62), and waist circumference (MD -3.53 cm, 95% CI: -4.63~-2.42), and sensitivity analyses showed consistent directions. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potentially larger effect with monotherapy (-3.43 vs. -2.04 kg, P=0.021); this finding is based on a limited number of comparisons and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. However, because the pooled estimate combines monotherapy and combination-regimen trials with different comparators (placebo, metformin, or calorie-restricted diet), this result should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Pooled analysis of visceral adiposity (k=3) showed a reduction (SMD -0.73, 95% CI: -1.35~-0.11), but precision was insufficient. RoB 2 indicated risk of bias in some studies; GRADE suggested low certainty for weight and body-shape outcomes and low certainty for visceral adiposity.
CONCLUSIONS: In reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, GLP-1 receptor agonists may offer weight-loss benefits and improvements in central obesity compared with conventional regimens; however, these findings are derived from a small, clinically heterogeneous pool of trials with…

articles.title: What's Hot and What's New in Xenotransplantation From the Young Investigator Committee of the IXA-Clinical Science.
articles.authors: Eisenson D, de Mazancourt ES, Ladowski J et al.
articles.abstract: The 2025 International Xenotransplantation Association (IXA) Congress in Geneva, convened in parallel with World Health Organization meetings on xenotransplantation guidance, marked a transition in clinical xenotransplantation from demonstrating that pig organs can function in humans to defining how graft injury is detected, interpreted, and managed in real time. We synthesize the major clinical themes that emerged from the meeting across kidney, heart, liver, and lung xenotransplantation. In kidney xenotransplantation, the NYU and Massachusetts General Hospital living-recipient experiences now delineate two complementary injury patterns-antibody- and complement-driven with a membranoproliferative, IgA-positive, innate-rich phenotype, and T cell-mediated with persistent innate immune activation-both converging on macrophage and NK-cell biology that conventional immunosuppression does not address. The first registration-supporting Phase 1/2/3 trial of a 10-gene-edited xenokidney (EXPAND) has begun, framed by IXA position-paper recommendations and supported by recent FDA approvals. In cardiac xenotransplantation, real-time complement-function monitoring, global longitudinal strain, and donor-derived cell-free DNA emerge as an actionable surveillance toolkit, while other allotransplant biomarkers translate poorly. In liver xenotransplantation, extracorporeal cross-circulation and the first preliminary data describing auxiliary pig-to-human liver transplant (171-day survival) position porcine livers as bridge-support platforms rather than definitive replacements. Lung xenotransplantation remains confined to ex vivo perfusion and short-term preclinical models. Cross-cutting priorities include donor-pig design and individual graft phenotyping that accounts for transgene expression heterogeneity, prospectively validated multimodal monitoring, management of nephrotic-range proteinuria and associated urinary loss of biologic immunosuppressants, and dedicated registry, ethical, and patient-engagement infrastructure to support trustworthy clinical expansion.

articles.title: "I Need a Doctor Online": Online Health Consultation and Perceived Patient-Centered Communication in the Association Between Health-Related Social Media Use and Cancer Screening Intention Among Brazilian Women.
articles.authors: Qiu SS, Zhang L, Xie Q et al.
articles.abstract: Breast and cervical cancer are leading causes of cancer-related deaths among Brazilian women, and regular screenings are vital for reducing mortality and are cost-effective for cancer prevention. In digital health communication environments, understanding how health-related social media use, online health consultation, and perceived patient-centered communication are associated with women's cancer screening intention has important implications for health communication theory and practice. Using cross-sectional national survey data from Brazil (N = 530 women), this study examined whether health-related social media use is associated with women's cancer screening intention and tested a moderated serial mediation model in which online health consultation and perceived patient-centered communication were examined as intervening variables, with online health information overload as a moderator. Results showed that health-related social media use was not directly associated with women's cancer screening intention (β = .021, b = .014, p > .05). However, the hypothesized serial indirect association through online health consultation and perceived patient-centered communication was statistically significant (β = .013, b = .008, bootstrap 95% CI = [.002, .017]). Online health information overload moderated the association between health-related social media use and online health consultation (b = .186, p < .001). Guided by Channel Complementarity Theory and the health communication pathway model, the findings suggest that health-related social media use may be associated with women's cancer screening intention through complementary online consultation and perceived patient-centered communication.

articles.title: Inhaled Glucocorticoids During Pregnancy: A Population-Level Drug Utilization Study in Denmark From 2001 to 2023.
articles.authors: Al-Sagit NNJ, Damkier P, Gram EB
articles.abstract: We investigated trends of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) use among pregnant women in Denmark from 2001 to 2023 using aggregated data from the Danish Health Data Authority, where recorded prescription redemptions in the National Prescription Register are linked to pregnancies recorded in the Danish Medical Birth Registry. Use of combination preparations (ICS and beta2-agonists) increased substantially (from 1.3 to 21 per 1000 pregnant women), corresponding to a 16-fold increase, while use of single-agent preparations (ICS) decreased gradually (from 17 to 11 per 1000 pregnant women). Combination preparations became more prevalent than single-agent preparations in 2020 among pregnant women, reflecting changes in treatment guidelines and recommendations in 2019. ICS use was higher before than during pregnancy in 2001 (22 vs. 18 per 1000 women) but lower before than during pregnancy in 2023 (30 vs. 32 per 1000 women), with the pattern reversing in 2015. Use during pregnancy was highest among the oldest women (≥ 40 years), with some variation over time, while it fluctuated substantially among the youngest women (≤ 19 years) and increased more steadily among women aged 20-39 years. Overall, our results highlight changes in ICS use among pregnant women that are well aligned with national and international asthma guidelines.

articles.title: Donor-derived cell-free DNA levels predict 3-year outcomes in kidney transplant recipients with stable function.
articles.authors: Cheng D, Cuello Garcia H, Li X et al.
articles.abstract: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is a promising noninvasive biomarker for detecting acute rejection in kidney transplant recipients, but its prognostic value in patients with stable graft function remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between dd-cfDNA levels and long-term clinical outcomes. We retrospectively analyzed 267 kidney transplant recipients with stable renal function between January 2020 and July 2023, stratified by plasma dd-cfDNA levels into three groups: A (<1%, n = 205), B (1-<2%, n = 34), and C (≥2%, n = 28). Each patient contributed a single index dd-cfDNA measurement obtained during routine outpatient follow-up, which defined baseline; the interval from transplantation to the index measurement did not differ among groups (p = 0.124). Clinical outcomes included changes in serum creatinine, incidence of adverse events, graft loss, patient mortality, and biopsy findings over three years. Creatinine levels remained stable in Group A but increased significantly in Groups B and C from baseline to year 3 (1.38 to 1.96 mg/dL, p < 0.0001; and 1.36 to 1.84 mg/dL, p = 0.0019, respectively). Adverse events were significantly more frequent in Groups B (41.2%) and C (42.9%) compared with Group A (9.8%, p < 0.001). Graft loss rates were 0.98%, 11.76%, and 7.14% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (p = 0.002), and mortality showed a significant increasing trend across groups (p = 0.023). Elevated dd-cfDNA levels are associated with adverse long-term outcomes in kidney transplant recipients with stable graft function, suggesting that dd-cfDNA may serve as a valuable tool for early risk stratification and long-term monitoring in transplant care.

articles.title: Immune protection against anogenital HPV in Rwandan women with and without HIV following the introduction of quadrivalent HPV vaccination.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
articles.authors: Castle PE, Rutwaza MG, Tuyishime O et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines have demonstrated population effectiveness in preventing cervical cancer. Evidence for protection of women with HIV (WWH) is lacking. In 2011, Rwanda introduced quadrivalent HPV vaccination nationally, primarily targeting girls in grade 6, providing an opportunity to evaluate its long-term effectiveness in WWH compared to women without HIV (WWoH).
METHODS: Data from 3,058 of 3,148 (97.1%) Rwandan women with complete results from four sub-cohorts recruited and enrolled were analyzed: 769 WWoH born before 1996, 755 WWoH born 1996 or more recently, 773 WWH born before 1996, and 761 WWH born 1996 or more recently. We tested vaginal and anal specimens for high-risk HPV genotypes. We used self-report of HPV vaccination and measured anti-HPV16 antibodies levels by HPV16 VLP ELISA as HPV vaccination proxies to examine the protective effects, using logistic regression, of HPV vaccination on vaginal and/or anal (combined, "anogenital") HPV16 and/or HPV18 (HPV16/18).
RESULTS: Self-reported HPV vaccination (vs. not) (adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=2.71, 95%CI=2.29-3.21) was most strongly positively, and WWH (vs. WWoH) (aOR=0.68, 95%CI=0.60-0.78) was most strongly negatively, associated with higher anti-HPV16 antibody levels. Anogenital HPV16/18 prevalence decreased from 11.0% to 2.5% in those with the lowest to highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels, respectively (ptrend<0.001). The highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels was associated with lower anogenital HPV16/18 (aOR=0.23, 95%CI=0.13-0.38); similar associations were observed for the highest quartile in WWH (aOR=0.23; 95%CI=0.12-0.46) as in WWoH (aOR=0.24, 95%CI=0.10-0.58).
CONCLUSION: WWH who were likely vaccinated against HPV vaccination had lower prevalence of anogenital HPV16/18.

articles.title: A Machine Learning Model for Predicting 28-Day Mortality in Critically Ill Ischemic Stroke Patients With Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on MIMIC-IV and eICU Databases.
articles.authors: Liu H, Fan C, Zou J
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) commonly complicates ischemic stroke (IS) in critically ill patients and is associated with increased mortality. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable model for predicting 28-day mortality in this population.
METHODS: We used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database for model development and internal validation and the eICU database for external validation. Critically ill IS patients with SIRS during the first ICU day were included. The model predicted mortality occurring between the 24-hour landmark and day 28 after ICU admission. MIMIC-IV patients were randomly divided into training and testing sets at a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression selected predictors for six algorithms. The model with the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the testing set was externally validated and compared with the Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score (OASIS) alone. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: The study included 2,438 patients: 1,620 from MIMIC-IV and 818 from eICU. Nine predictors were selected: age, white blood cell count, red blood cell distribution width, blood urea nitrogen, anion gap, Charlson Comorbidity Index, SIRS score, OASIS, and mechanical ventilation. Among the six models evaluated in the testing set, logistic regression (LR) achieved the highest AUC (0.846) and was therefore selected for external validation. In the external validation cohort, the LR model achieved a higher AUC than OASIS alone (0.794 vs. 0.758), and showed reasonable calibration and potential clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: We developed and externally validated an interpretable ML-based model for predicting 28-day mortality in critically ill IS patients with SIRS. The LR model showed good discrimination and reasonable calibration in external validation. Prospective multicenter validation and clinical-impact assessment are required before implementation.

articles.title: Predictive ability of hyperspectral signatures from single immobilized spermatozoa as a novel approach to non-invasive sperm selection during ICSI.
articles.authors: Gil Juliá M, Pacheco-Rendón RM, de Los Santos JM et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Can hyperspectral imaging of single immobilized spermatozoa prior to ICSI be used to characterize individual spermatozoa quality and develop predictive models for fertilization, blastulation, and blastocyst usability?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Hyperspectral imaging characterization of individual immobilized spermatozoa was successfully implemented prior to ICSI and enabled the development of predictive models for key reproductive outcomes.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Sperm selection during ICSI is mainly based on morphology and motility, which provide limited information about functional competence. Most techniques capable of assessing molecular sperm quality are destructive and cannot be applied to the injected spermatozoon. Hyperspectral imaging (HS) is a non-invasive technique capable of generating molecular spectral fingerprints of individual cells.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: This prospective two-phase study was conducted between March 2020 and August 2024 and included 93 couples undergoing ICSI cycles at a single IVF centre.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Single immobilized spermatozoa were imaged prior to ICSI using a hyperspectral camera coupled to a micromanipulation microscope. Phase I evaluated the feasibility and short-term technical repeatability of hyperspectral acquisition, as well as preliminary classification consistency across repeated acquisitions. Phase II included a safety evaluation using a sibling donor-oocyte design and the development of predictive models using hyperspectral spectra and clinical data. Machine learning models based on XGBoost decision trees were trained to predict fertilization, blastulation, and usable blastocyst formation.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Hyperspectral imaging was successfully implemented prior to ICSI. Phase I supported high short-term technical repeatability under stable acquisition conditions, with a global intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.999. Exploratory spectral classification across repeated technical acquisitions achieved a sensitivity of 93.84% and a specificity of 96.76%. In the safety evaluation, fertilization, blastulation, and usable blastocyst rates were comparable between HS-ICSI and standard ICSI groups. Predictive models based on hyperspectral spectra and clinical data were developed, with chained models integrating both data types showing the most favourable balance between predictive precision and uncertainty among the evaluated model…

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Technology-Based Educational Interventions for Improving Cancer Screening Among Migrant Women: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: Krzyż EZ, Lin CJ, Hulu SRK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migrant women have lower participation in breast and cervical cancer screening than non-migrant populations, contributing to delayed diagnoses and health inequities. Technology-based educational interventions may improve screening uptake; however, their comparative effectiveness remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the effectiveness of technology-based educational interventions for improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women using a network meta-analysis.
METHODS: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted across 6 electronic databases and clinical trial registries from inception to December 24, 2025. Eligible studies included migrant women receiving technology-based educational interventions to improve cancer screening uptake. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed in R using the netmeta package. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (16 datasets) were included. Multicomponent interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care (odds ratio 5.50, 95% confidence interval 2.56-11.82) and ranked as the most effective strategy (P score = 0.92). Text messaging, voice messaging, and video-based interventions demonstrated positive but nonsignificant effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Multicomponent technology-based educational interventions were more effective than single-modality approaches in improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women.
IMPLICATIONS FOR ONCOLOGY NURSING PRACTICE: Oncology nurses may play a central role in delivering multicomponent, culturally tailored interventions that combine digital education with personalized support, patient navigation, and community engagement. By integrating human connection with technology-assisted care, nurses may help address the complex cultural, informational, and access-related barriers that contribute to inequities in preventive cancer services.

articles.title: Hypogonadism in men with prolactinoma.
articles.authors: Broul M, Hujová A, Radovnická L et al.
articles.abstract: Hypogonadism is one of the most consequential manifestations of prolactinoma in men, yet its course is often reduced to a single testosterone result. Prolactin excess can reversibly suppress hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal signalling, whereas large tumours may damage gonadotroph function and other pituitary axes. These mechanisms create a dynamic phenotype that includes androgen-deficiency symptoms, impaired spermatogenesis, anaemia, adverse body composition, skeletal fragility and sexual dysfunction. Dopamine agonists are the usual first causal treatment, and transsphenoidal surgery is appropriate in selected patients; neither biochemical control nor tumour shrinkage proves gonadal or sexual recovery. Contemporary cohorts indicate that testosterone recovery occurs mainly during the first year but may continue through 24 months, and is more likely with smaller tumours, higher baseline or six-month testosterone, earlier prolactin normalisation and preserved pituitary function. Men with persistent symptomatic hypogonadism require a fertility-sensitive decision: continued observation when recovery remains plausible, consideration of testosterone replacement when fertility is not sought, or specialist gonadotrophin treatment when fertility is desired; clomiphene is an off-label option supported only by small uncontrolled studies. Sexual desire and erectile function should be measured separately because both may remain impaired despite eugonadism and require additional cardiometabolic, medication and psychosexual assessment. This Review integrates endocrine, reproductive and sexual outcomes into a time-resolved framework. The central principle is that prolactin control, endogenous gonadal recovery, fertility and sexual recovery are related but non-equivalent treatment goals.

articles.title: Polygenic scores improve persistent smoking prediction over single variants and phenotypic factors.
articles.authors: Jones SK, Benton ML, Tindle HA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Smoking is a leading cause of preventable death and illness. Genetically-informed precision interventions are feasible, but whether genetic risk for persistent smoking can be captured by high-risk single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) or requires comprehensive assessment using whole-genome polygenic risk scores (PRS) is unknown. This study compared discriminatory performance of a baseline model for long-term persistent smoking based on phenotypic predictors with models that (1) integrate phenotypic predictors with three well-characterized SNPs and (2) incorporate phenotypic predictors and PRS for smoking cessation.
DESIGN: Data were from the Nurse's Health Study (NHS) and NHS II, two all-female, prospective cohorts that collected data every 2 years. Two independent data sources were used from baseline (1976 for NHS and 1989 for NHS II) and up to 2014 for NHS and 2015 for NHS II.
SETTING: Population-based, longitudinal cohort studies of nurses from 17 states in the United States.
PARTICIPANTS: Female, baseline ever-smokers of European ancestry with whole-genome genetic data (NHS: n = 10 017; NHS II: n = 2793).
MEASUREMENTS: Baseline models included phenotypic and other predictors influencing smoking behavior: age, year of follow-up, smoking intensity, menopausal status, hormone replacement therapy use, early initiation of smoking and body mass index (kg/m2). Additional genetic predictors for persistent smoking were estimated by (1) three well-characterized risk SNPs for smoking (CHRNA5 rs16969968, CYP2A6 rs56113850, DRD2/ANKK1 rs1800497) and (2) PRS. The primary outcome of the study was improvement in predictive performance as measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC) between baseline models for long-term persistent smoking and models adding genetic risk with (1) risk SNPs and (2) PRS.
RESULTS: Within NHS, the baseline model showed moderate predictive performance for persistent smoking with an AUC of 0.674. Adding SNPs showed similar performance (AUC = 0.675), whereas adding PRS statistically significantly improved discriminatory performance, raising the AUC to 0.730, a 5.7% [95% confidence interval (CI) = 5.4%-5.9%] improvement in prediction (AUC) over baseline models. Results were replicated in NHS II, where baseline and SNP models performed moderately with AUCs of 0.671 and 0.677, and adding PRS increased the AUC to 0.735, representing a 6.4% (95% CI = 5.9%-6.8%) improvement in prediction over…

articles.title: Changes in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice following a competency-based educational intervention in pelvic organ prolapse and urinary incontinence care: a quasi-experimental single-group pretest-posttest study.
articles.authors: Elrefay BW, El-Nemer AMR, Fadel EA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the assessment of pelvic organ prolapse (POP), approximately half of women may present with varying degrees of pelvic organ descent, although many do not exhibit clinical symptoms. Therefore, nurses have an important role in timely assessment, prevention of complications, and provision of appropriate supportive care. This study aimed to evaluate changes in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice following a competency-based educational intervention for the care of women with POP and urinary incontinence (UI).
METHODS: The study followed a quasi-experimental, single-group pretest-posttest design and included 60 nurses working in the outpatient department of the Urology and Nephrology Center, Mansoura University, Egypt. Data were collected using three researcher-developed instruments: the Demographic Structured Interview Schedule, the Nurses' Knowledge Structured Interview, and the Nurses' Observational Practice Checklist. Nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice were assessed before the intervention and reassessed immediately after completion of the educational intervention.
RESULTS: Statistically significant immediate post-intervention improvements were observed in nurses' knowledge and clinical practice. The mean overall knowledge score increased from 17.05 ± 1.92 at baseline to 19.18 ± 1.97 immediately after the intervention (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < .001). Perineal care practice scores increased from 26.80 ± 6.93 to 49.33 ± 3.93, pessary insertion practice scores increased from 25.33 ± 6.81 to 50.73 ± 3.85, and pelvic floor muscle exercise instruction scores increased from 9.80 ± 3.25 to 20.42 ± 1.94 (all p < .001).
CONCLUSION: Participation in the competency-based educational intervention was associated with significant immediate improvements in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice related to POP and UI care. These findings represent short-term post-training changes, and further controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these improvements are sustained over time.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06639217, registered on 10 October 2024. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: The German ELSA Study: experiences of counselling and care in situations of unwanted pregnancy: a qualitative typology of women who terminate an unwanted pregnancy.
articles.authors: Wyrobisch-Krüger A, Hahn D, Herzig L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The contribution reports the findings from a set of interviews investigating the social and health resources and concerns of women who had terminated an unwanted pregnancy. The goal was to investigate their actions and experiences in connection with decision-making and termination. The research was conducted at Fulda University, Germany, and was part of the research project investigating the situations and experiences of women who had experienced an unwanted pregnancy, and the associated counselling and other services.
METHODS: Twenty-five semi-structured interviews conducted between February and August 2022 and analysed using the Documentary Method to generate a typology. The interviewed women were aged between 17 and 41.
RESULTS: Decisions about abortion are made in light of problems and resources, and are influenced by current and future (anticipated) life plans. Abortion is understood as an opportunity to realise or safeguard life planning (in relation to career, family, health and socioeconomic status). Four types were identified: "preserve" (protecting the achieved), "stabilise" (guarding agency), "orientate" (keeping options open), and "realise" (pursuing specific life goals). Notably, the identified types correspond broadly to specific age groups and phases (for example starting a family, birth of children, career development, or need for stability in challenging circumstances). The phase of life the woman was in at the time of the unwanted pregnancy was highly influential.
CONCLUSION: It is too rarely acknowledged that the decision to terminate a pregnancy may also represent a positive choice. For the interviewed women, a termination offered the possibility to retain agency in difficult situations, to strengthen their autonomy, to preserve development opportunities, and to protect existing achievements. The decision to terminate a pregnancy should therefore be understood as a resource-orientated aspect of biographical development.

articles.title: Beyond age and ovarian reserve: a prospective study exploring inflammatory and cycle-specific biomarkers to enhance IVF outcome prediction.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Omes C, Montobbio G, De Amici M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Conventional predictors such as age and AFC fail to fully explain the substantial inter-individual variability in in vitro fertilization outcomes. This prospective exploratory study investigated whether integrating systemic and local inflammatory biomarkers-specifically calprotectin measured in plasma and follicular fluid-with conventional clinical parameters improves the prediction of cumulative clinical pregnancy.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients undergoing in vitro fertilization and analyzed 75 completed cycles in which all retrieved oocytes and resulting embryos were used. Calprotectin concentrations were quantified in plasma and follicular fluid collected at oocyte retrieval.
