We evaluated associations with cumulative clinical pregnancy using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Predictive models obtained were internally validated using a bootstrapping procedure to estimate optimism-corrected discrimination.
RESULTS: Age and antral follicle count confirmed their established predictive roles, whereas calprotectin concentrations alone showed no significant association with cumulative pregnancy. In multivariable models, follicular fluid calprotectin showed a negative trend with pregnancy probability, whereas plasma calprotectin showed the opposite trend. Combining age, antral follicle count, and inflammatory parameters yielded strong discriminative performance; after bootstrap correction, the optimism-corrected area under the curve reached 0.862 for the peri-retrieval model and 0.841 for the post-fertilization model. Heatmap visualizations highlighted distinct risk patterns across age strata and inflammatory profiles.
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating local and systemic inflammatory biomarkers with conventional clinical predictors provides complementary insights into in vitro fertilization success, suggesting that local microenvironmental stress and systemic immune activation exert divergent effects on reproductive potential. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts.  TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06872294. Registered 20 March 2025.

articles.title: High AUC and selection stability do not establish single-gene biomarker value in tumor-versus-normal transcriptomics: a null-controlled multi-cohort analysis in endometrial carcinoma.
articles.authors: Luo L, Zhu Z, Xiao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic biomarker studies of endometrial carcinoma (EC) often report near-perfect discrimination, yet few candidates reproduce. Because tumor-versus-normal contrasts shift much of the transcriptome, a high area under the curve (AUC) can arise from many genes. We benchmarked discrimination and machine-learning selection stability against random gene sets. Vote counting across three Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts (162 EC, 50 controls) identified 182 recurrent genes. In The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) endometrial cohort, where 67.2% of genes were differentially expressed, the most stably selected gene, NUMA1, did not outperform random single genes (AUC 0.829; P = 0.235), nor did the recurrent signature (P = 0.193). Stability-selected multivariable gene sets reached AUCs of 0.995-0.999 in TCGA. After these TCGA results, we examined HAND2-AS1, OSR2, PEG3 and RUNX1T1 post hoc as an illustrative panel; TCGA therefore informed its selection, and GSE146889 was external but not blinded. These genes formed a three-cohort intersection only under a non-prespecified GSE106191 analysis; the prespecified analysis detected no differential expression. The panel exceeded random four-gene scores in TCGA (AUC 0.988; P = 0.006), but not recurrent-consensus subsets (P = 0.61), and showed no detectable advantage in GSE146889 (AUC 0.945; P = 0.064). Post hoc sensitivity analyses across six recorded analytic paths yielded the same qualitative pattern. The score correlated with stromal (rho = - 0.426) but not immune content (rho = - 0.014), and the genes were detected mainly in fibroblasts. In tumor-versus-normal data with marked compositional differences, neither high AUC nor stable selection establishes a gene's uniqueness or tumor-cell relevance; confirmation requires new, prespecified cohorts.

articles.title: Anatomy of periprostatic nerves and nerve-sparing strategy for radical prostatectomy.
articles.authors: Ma Q, Liu Y, Han Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical prostatectomy is an important curative treatment for localized prostate cancer, but postoperative urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction substantially impair quality of life. Understanding individual variation in periprostatic nerves, fascia, and supporting structures is essential for balancing oncological control with functional preservation. This narrative review examines periprostatic nerve and fascial anatomy, nerve-sparing grading systems, established surgical techniques, and emerging adjuncts for individualized surgical planning.
METHODS: PubMed was searched through July 2026 using 'prostate', 'pelvic autonomic nerve', 'neurovascular bundle', 'nerve sparing', 'radical prostatectomy', 'continence', 'erectile function', and 'NeuroSAFE'. Relevant guidelines and standard anatomical texts were also reviewed, alongside anatomical and clinical studies directly addressing periprostatic nerve anatomy, nerve-sparing techniques, or functional and oncological outcomes.
RESULTS: Anatomical and histological studies show substantial variation in periprostatic nerve distribution. Nerve fibres are not confined to conventional posterolateral neurovascular bundles. Some extend into the anterolateral prostate and course through multilayered, heterogeneous fascial structures. Anatomy-based grading systems provide practical intraoperative frameworks but cannot accurately quantify nerve preservation in individual patients. Bilateral or more extensive nerve sparing is associated with better recovery of urinary continence and erectile function. However, these associations are influenced by baseline function, tumour risk, surgeon experience, and inconsistent outcome definitions. Contemporary approaches increasingly preserve a broader complex of nerves, fascia, and supporting structures. Refined techniques may improve early functional recovery, although comparative long-term evidence remains limited. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging, NeuroSAFE, and intraoperative nerve-identification technologies may further support individualized planning and real-time adjustment of dissection planes.
CONCLUSIONS: A detailed understanding of individualized periprostatic nerve and fascial anatomy underpins effective nerve-sparing surgery. Integrating anatomy-based grading, patient-specific planning, and advanced adjunctive technologies may improve the balance between oncological control and functional preservation.

articles.title: Risk factors for congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract.
articles.authors: Chen CC, Lai PC, Shieh CC
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) are a leading cause of pediatric renal failure. This study evaluated risk factors and assessed their robustness.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus searches yielded 33 studies (24 case-control, 9 cohort). Frequentist and Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses estimated associations between CAKUT and maternal/neonatal risks.
RESULTS: Frequentist analysis identified increased risk for pre-pregnancy BMI 25.0-29.9 (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.06-1.45), ≥30 (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.51), and ≥25 kg/m² (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.11-1.37). Maternal age <20 years was protective (OR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51-0.73). Other predictors included family history of CAKUT/kidney disease, maternal diabetes subtypes (type 1, type 2, pre-gestational, and gestational diabetes), preterm birth (OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.25-2.03), small-for-gestational-age (SGA), and large-for-gestational-age (LGA). Bayesian analysis validated most factors. Although 95% CrIs crossed unity for BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m², BMI ≥ 30 kg/m², T2DM, SGA, LGA, alcohol consumption, RASi use, and hypertension, their posterior distributions were predominantly above 1. High BMI, family history, and diabetes remained robust in high-quality subsets.
CONCLUSIONS: Confirming established risks and identifying novel associations, these findings identify maternal metabolic factors as consistent correlates of CAKUT and support their evaluation as potentially modifiable targets.
IMPACT: Current meta-analyses lack synthesis on novel CAKUT determinants (maternal exposures, comorbidities, gestational weight gain, extreme fetal weight) and Bayesian approaches, which are essential to robustly address heterogeneity in sparse data. Our frequentist analysis confirmed established risks and identified novel associations: family history, SGA, LGA, and type 1 and 2 diabetes. Bayesian meta-analysis supported the main findings and showed posterior probabilities that OR > 1 of ≥90% for BMI subgroups, T2DM, RASi use, and hypertension. Maternal metabolic factors are consistently associated with CAKUT and represent potentially modifiable targets that warrant evaluation in future prospective and interventional studies.

articles.title: Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer.
articles.authors: Lübberstedt J, Braitsch K, Lammert J et al.
articles.abstract: Routine laboratory panels drawn during cancer treatment constitute longitudinal physiological recordings of organ function, yet their temporal structure is discarded by single-timepoint prognostic tools. A transformer trained on 2,777,595 laboratory measurements from 3905 patients with multiple myeloma or ovarian cancer predicted which of 162 treatment-associated complications would be newly recorded within two years, spanning eight clinical categories, achieving 1.5- to 6.1-fold enrichment above prevalence. Across individual endpoints it exceeded non-sequential baselines, including engineered-trajectory models, by +0.024 to +0.070 in mean AUROC. Predictions generalised across both cancers, divergence concentrating in disease-specific complications, and biomarker masking recovered signatures consistent with established pathophysiology. External validation on MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass showed transferability, strongest for renal and metabolic endpoints, attenuated for infection endpoints. On CoMMpass it added prognostic value to ISS staging. Routine oncological laboratory data carry complication-specific physiological signal months before a complication is recorded, and require no testing beyond standard oncological care.

articles.title: The Complex Relationship Between Volume and Outcome of AMS 800 Implants in the SATURN Database.
articles.authors: Van der Aa F, Thiruchelvam N, Heesakkers J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SATURN is a prospective, multicenter registry that collects data from 28 European centers. Contrary to expectations, previous analyses of the SATURN registry showed higher revision rates in higher-volume centers.
OBJECTIVE: We further evaluated the relationship between center volume and 1-yr safety outcomes after AMS 800 implantation using real-world SATURN data.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: We reviewed 1046 SATURN implantations and included 684 patients who received an AMS 800 artificial urinary sphincter from 25 European centers. Centers were categorized by annual AMS 800 implant numbers as low (<10), intermediate (10-25), or high (>25).
OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS AND STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: The 1-yr complication, revision, and explant rates were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests and Pearson chi-square tests, with multivariable Cox regression adjusted for relevant patient- and procedure-related covariates and accounting for center-level clustering.
RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Crude analyses differed by center volume for complications, revisions other than explantation, and all revisions, including explantation, but not for explants. Complication rates were 16.7%, 25.8%, and 17.8% in low-, intermediate-, and high-volume centers, respectively, demonstrating a nonmonotonic pattern with the intermediate-volume group as the main outlier. Rates of revision other than explantation were 5.1%, 12.3%, and 11.2%, respectively, whereas rates of all revisions including explantation were 9.6%, 18.9%, and 16.9%, respectively, and were thus higher in both intermediate- and high-volume centers than in low-volume centers. After adjustment, there was no statistically significant global association between center volume and any of the four 1-yr outcomes; the observed crude differences were not retained after adjustment. This observational registry analysis is subject to confounding and cannot establish causality.
CONCLUSIONS: Although crude analyses showed differences in complication and revision rates across volume groups, the complication pattern was nonmonotonic, with the intermediate-volume group representing the main outlier, whereas revision-related outcomes were higher in both intermediate- and high-volume centers than in low-volume centers. After multivariable adjustment and accounting for center-level clustering, no evidence of an independent center-volume effect was observed for any of the four 1-yr outcomes.

articles.title: Utility of Examining 100 Metaphase Cells in the Evaluation of Low-Level Aneuploidy Mosaicism.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.authors: Iwata-Otsubo A, Cai P, Knudson-Horneber L et al.
articles.abstract: Karyotype analysis is the gold standard of care for evaluating patients suspected of having mosaicism involving sex chromosomes or autosomes. Accurately determining the level of mosaicism is important, as it can vary widely and may be linked to disease severity. However, current guidelines do not clearly specify how many cells should be examined in order to exclude low-level mosaicism. In our retrospective study of cytogenetic results from 113 specimens, each with a minimum of 100 cells examined, we assessed whether the extensive analysis provided additional clinical value. Common indications for cytogenetic testing in these cases include Turner syndrome, premature ovarian failure, Klinefelter syndrome, infertility, and multiple miscarriages. In 83% (94/113) of cases, additional cells were examined because initial analysis suggested low-level mosaicism; however, further analysis did not confirm the initial findings in 66 of these 94 cases, indicating they were likely artifacts. Notably, none of the seven repeated analyses of 100 or 200 cells corroborated previous reports of low-level or clinically suspected mosaicism. Examination of additional cells confirmed the presence of a second cell line at low level in 25% (28/113) of cases, most often associated with X chromosome aneuploidies in adult females, likely age-related and without clear clinical significance. These results suggest that case-by-case consideration is still important, but no clinically significant findings resulted from analyzing more than 40 cells, indicating that extensive additional cell analysis is generally unnecessary for ruling out low-level mosaicism in clinical cytogenetic practice.

articles.title: Uterine Sarcomas: Updates and Challenges.
articles.journal: Surgical oncology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Avila M, Hoffman MS
articles.abstract: Uterine sarcomas represent a rare subset of sarcomas, making up 1% of all solid organ sarcomas and 3% of all uterine cancers. They arise as mesenchymal tumors from muscle and connective tissues. The most common subtypes include uterine leiomyosarcoma at 63%, low-grade and high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma at 21%, and the remainder include the less common subtypes like undifferentiated uterine sarcoma, adenosarcoma, perivascular epithelioid cell tumor, SMARCA4-deficient uterine sarcoma, uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor, NTRK-rearranged sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor. Through a surgical lens, this review will explore the most current diagnostic criteria and management strategies available.

articles.title: Systemic Lupus and Other Autoimmune Disorders During Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America
articles.authors: Patton KA, Siddique F, Lal AK
articles.abstract: Rheumatologic conditions occur in reproductive aged women, requiring a multidisciplinary approach to care. Patients require coordinated care with obstetrics, maternal fetal medicine, and rheumatology. Many drugs used for the care of rheumatologic conditions are safe in pregnancy, but detailed review should occur, ideally preconception, so the patient can be on the safest regimen while maintaining disease control. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies particularly pose unique risks of neonatal lupus syndrome, including cardiac manifestations. Medical management is unique to each disease and includes ultrasounds and antenatal testing to optimize both maternal and fetal well-being and minimize perinatal risks.

articles.title: Thrombocytopenia in Pregnancy: Diagnosis and Management.
articles.authors: Gupta A, Pishko AM
articles.abstract: Thrombocytopenia occurs in up to 10% of pregnancies and is most prevalent in later trimesters. In an uncomplicated pregnancy with platelet counts greater than 80 x 109/L, gestational thrombocytopenia is the most likely etiology. More severe thrombocytopenia, particularly those presenting in first or early second trimester, should prompt consideration of alternative causes including immune thrombocytopenia. When thrombocytopenia is accompanied by hemolytic anemia, patients should be evaluated for thrombotic microangiopathy. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia and hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet syndrome, are most common etiologies in late second and third trimesters.

articles.title: Menopause and Sexual Health in Older Adults.
articles.authors: Alvarez-Galiana VM, Martinez RC, Montero J
articles.abstract: While sexual health is a critical component of well-being in aging populations, it remains clinically underrecognized. Menopause is a systemic endocrine transition characterized by estrogen deficiency, driving a cascade of vasomotor, musculoskeletal, and genitourinary sequelae in older women. Hormonal shifts, specifically declining estrogen and testosterone, contribute to vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and decreased libido. These physiologic changes are further complicated by comorbidities, polypharmacy, and functional limitations. Similarly, gradual testosterone decline in men may impair libido and erectile function. This review provides a clinically focused framework for the evaluation and management of sexual dysfunction in geriatric practice.

articles.title: Hypogonadism in Older Men.
articles.authors: Chen AM, Garg R, Swerdloff RS
articles.abstract: Hypogonadism in older men refers to the late-onset clinical syndrome of impaired androgen production and/or spermatogenesis. Aging in men is associated with a gradual decline in serum testosterone concentrations. Some older hypogonadal men may benefit from testosterone therapy while others may not. The decision of whether to prescribe testosterone for an older hypogonadal man should be based on the severity of hypogonadism, an assessment of the potential benefits and risks of treatment, and the patient's willingness to accept the risks of treatment and monitoring. The choice of testosterone formulation depends on the patient's preferences, pharmacokinetics, treatment burden, and cost.

articles.title: Common Outpatient Procedures: Outpatient Gynecologic Procedures.
articles.journal: The Medical clinics of North America
articles.authors: Zarling N, Warsh S, Cleeves M
articles.abstract: Outpatient gynecologic procedures are core competencies for generalist clinicians and support access to comprehensive preventive and reproductive care. This review summarizes key outpatient gynecologic procedures, including cervical cancer screening, insertion and removal of intrauterine devices and contraceptive implants, and endometrial biopsies. Evidence-based approaches to pain management for intrauterine procedures are reviewed, including intracervical and paracervical blocks. Procedural pitfalls and strategies to reduce complications are discussed. Competence in these procedures enables timely, patient-centered preventative and reproductive care while minimizing need for specialist referral.

articles.title: 'Honestly, I can't even remember the last time someone taught me how to stitch': a qualitative training needs assessment for caesarean delivery providers in Tanzania.
articles.authors: Kikula A, Kaur K, Mkonyi MA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As access to caesarean delivery (CD) has expanded in Tanzania, surgical complications also increasingly contribute to maternal morbidity and mortality, which may in part be explained by limited structured training. This study aimed to identify training needs of CD providers in Tanzania to inform the development of a tailored surgical curriculum.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study using a thematic analysis framework. CD providers, including medical officers (MOs), assistant medical officers (AMOs) and an obstetrics and gynaecology (Ob/Gyn) specialist, at four public health facilities in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, were recruited. Semi-structured interviews were conducted between November and December 2024. Interviews were transcribed, translated from Swahili to English and analysed thematically by two investigators. Themes, subthemes and representative quotations were reported.
RESULTS: 13 CD providers were interviewed, including 7 female (54%) and 6 male (46%) participants. Median age was 50 years (IQR 18 years), and median length of practice was 6 years (IQR 15 years). Eight (62%) were MOs, four (31%) were AMOs and one (8%) was an Ob/Gyn specialist. Prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa was 0.99, reflecting high inter-rater reliability. Participants cited infrastructure and workforce limitations as key training and practice barriers. They emphasised a need for education around foundational and specialised surgical techniques to manage common intraoperative complications, such as postpartum haemorrhage, bladder and bowel injury and uterine extensions, in addition to other challenging clinical scenarios, such as obstructive labour, malpresentation, multiple gestations and intraperitoneal adhesions. Participants expressed interest in a short, intensive educational programme incorporating simulation, virtual learning, observership and mentorship.
CONCLUSIONS: Enhanced training in basic and specialised CD surgical techniques is needed to improve quality of CD services in Tanzania. Our findings will inform the development of a context-specific CD curriculum leveraging accessible technology and a train-the-trainer model for broader skills dissemination across the country.

articles.title: Phenotype Before Genotype? The Order of Cell-Free DNA and the First-Trimester Scan in 11,270 Pregnancies.
articles.authors: Mureşan MC, Mureşan MB, Dumitraşcu-Biriş D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine when cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was drawn relative to the first-trimester scan, whether the phenotype redirected genetic testing, whether a positive result's meaning varied with condition and phenotype, and what order changes when the same components are used.
METHODS: Observed: 11,270 singleton pregnancies scanned at 11-13+6 weeks (2009-2026); chart review of those with nuchal translucency (NT) 3.5 mm or more and cfDNA (n = 19); positive predictive value (PPV) across 1739 pregnancies with a cfDNA result. Modelled: five hypothetical pathways applied to 11,111 pregnancies. Abnormalities were known only where tested, so modelled counts are eligibility for referral and not detection rates.
RESULTS: Observed: cfDNA became available in November 2015 and was used in 7.6% of the 2016-2026 cohort; 40.2% of samples preceded the scan. Of those 19 pregnancies, 16 were sampled before any phenotyping and none later; all five low-risk results were superseded. PPV fell from 95% (trisomy 21) to 17% (sex chromosome aneuploidies). Modelled: both pathways had identical eligibility by design, differing by 261 additional modelled cfDNA tests that could not alter referral.
CONCLUSION: Order changed neither modelled eligibility nor assay capability, but determined whether screening information preceded the phenotype that establishes whether it is needed.

articles.title: Impact of electrical stimulation added to biofeedback and pelvic floor exercises after prostatectomy: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Galliou G
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The effectiveness of electrical stimulation in the rehabilitation of urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy remains debated. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of adding it to a treatment combining active pelvic floor exercises and biofeedback.
METHODS: A retrospective, single-center, observational study included 110 patients with urinary leakage after radical prostatectomy: 58 without electrical stimulation and 52 with electrical stimulation. The primary outcome was the change in the 24-h Pad-test between the initial assessment and the assessment performed after ten sessions. The secondary outcomes were the changes in the USP « stress urinary incontinence » subscore and the IPSS. An exploratory analysis of responders, defined by a reduction of at least 50 % in the Pad-test, was also performed.
RESULTS: The median relative reduction in the Pad-test was 78.4 % without electrical stimulation and 75.6 % with electrical stimulation, with no difference between groups (p=0.212). After adjustment for age, baseline Pad-test and type of surgery, electrical stimulation was not associated with the final Pad-test (B=0.075; p=0.724). Changes in the USP subscore and IPSS did not differ between groups. A reduction of at least 50 % in the Pad-test was observed in 86.2 % of patients without electrical stimulation and 67.3 % with electrical stimulation (p = 0.018). This responder analysis was exploratory.
CONCLUSION: In this observational setting, adding electrical stimulation to pelvic floor rehabilitation did not demonstrate an additional benefit after ten sessions. These findings should be considered exploratory.

articles.title: Effects of pneumoperitoneum pressure on perioperative atelectasis assessed using lung ultrasonography in patients undergoing robotic-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery: A prospective, randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Lin R, Hu X, Ni X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery commonly requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which promote perioperative atelectasis and may increase complication risk. We aimed to investigate the effect of low pneumoperitoneum pressure (LPP) on atelectasis following robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, surgeon- and assessor-blind, randomised controlled trial in women undergoing elective robot-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery. Participants were randomly allocated to the LPP (12 mmHg) or standard pneumoperitoneum pressure (SPP: 15 mmHg) group. Primary outcomes were modified lung ultrasound (mLUS) scores assessed after surgery and 30 min post-extubation. Secondary outcomes included incidence of atelectasis, percentage of desaturation in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU), lengths of PACU and hospital stay, surgeon satisfaction with the operative visual field, numeric rating scale pain score and modified clinical pulmonary infection score on postoperative day 1, and postoperative pulmonary complications 7 days postoperatively.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were enrolled (30 per group). The mLUSs were significantly lower in the LPP group versus the SPP group postoperatively (P < 0.001) and 30 min post-extubation (P < 0.001), particularly in the posterolateral lung region (P < 0.001). Compared with the SPP group, the LPP group experienced a 1.59-fold reduction in the risk of postoperative atelectasis 30 min post-extubation in the PACU (P = 0.004). Other secondary outcomes showed no significant intergroup differences.
CONCLUSIONS: A low pneumoperitoneum pressure during robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery reduced perioperative modified lung ultrasound scores and the incidence of early postoperative atelectasis. However, this imaging difference was not accompanied by significant improvements in oxygenation. Further studies powered for clinical pulmonary outcomes are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, https://www.chictr.org.cn/; ChiCTR 2400085515.

articles.title: Concomitant Right-Sided Bowel Resection at the Time of Left Colorectal Surgery for Deep Endometriosis: Is It Associated With Increased Major Morbidity? Evidence From 1,058 Patients.
articles.authors: Carrillo P, Crestani A, Denost Q et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Right-sided bowel localizations of deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) may be under-recognized preoperatively and are sometimes addressed concomitantly during planned left-sided colorectal surgery. We aimed to assess whether concomitant right-sided bowel procedures are associated with increased early major postoperative morbidity.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study based on a prospectively maintained institutional database.
SETTING: High-volume tertiary referral endometriosis center (IFEMEndo, Clinique Tivoli-Ducos, Bordeaux, France).
PARTICIPANTS: Consecutive women undergoing left-sided colorectal surgery for DIE between January 2021 and July 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Left-sided colorectal surgery alone (left-only group, n = 898) versus left-sided colorectal surgery with concomitant right-sided bowel procedures (left+right group, n = 160).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 1,058 women were included. Early major postoperative morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥IIIb within 30 days) occurred in 22/160 (13.8%) patients in the left+right group versus 66/898 (7.3%) in the left-only group (p = 0.007), with earlier onset in the combined group (mean postoperative day 9 ± 12 vs. 15 ± 23; p = 0.034). Early pelvic septic complications were also more frequent after left+right surgery (16.3% vs. 8.6%; p = 0.003). In models adjusted for age, BMI, smoking, and prior abdominal surgery, ileocecal resection (ICR) was associated with major morbidity (adjusted OR [aOR] 2.25, 95% CI 1.13-4.21; p = 0.01) and early pelvic septic complications (aOR 2.60, 95% CI 1.29-4.91; p = 0.005). Adjusted absolute risk of septic complications increased from 8.7% (95% CI 6.6-10.9%) without right-sided procedures to 16.3% (8.2-25.9%) with ICR and 22.0% (0.0-44.4%) with two or more right-sided procedures (n = 13). The association between ICR and major morbidity varied significantly according to the extent of left-sided surgery (interaction p = 0.022), with a pronounced association when ICR was added to conservative procedures and an attenuated, non-significant association when added to segmental resection.
CONCLUSION: In women undergoing left-sided colorectal surgery for DIE, concomitant right-sided bowel procedures were associated with higher crude early major morbidity and pelvic septic complications. The association between ICR and major morbidity differed according to the left-sided surgical context, being pronounced with conservative procedures and attenuated with…

articles.title: Brain and other central nervous system cancers cause comparatively few deaths but among the most years of life lost per death in Europe: a comparison of 21 cancer sites.
articles.authors: McLean AL, Senft C, McLean CW
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer burden in Europe is usually compared using deaths, incidence and survival, which do not show when in life deaths occur. Brain and other central nervous system (CNS) cancers cause relatively few deaths, but at younger ages than most cancers. We compared their position among cancer sites when burden is measured as years of life lost (YLL) rather than deaths.
METHODS: Eurostat deaths by age for 2023 in 31 European countries were analysed for all 21 site-specific cancer categories of the European cause-of-death shortlist. YLL were calculated from national life tables and valued with published country values of a statistical life year (VSLY). Sensitivity analyses varied discounting, life tables and valuation assumptions.
RESULTS: Brain and other CNS cancers caused 34,103 deaths (rank 10 of 21) and 688,800 YLL (rank 7). YLL per death was 20.2 years, the highest of the 21 sites, followed by cervical cancer (19.9); no other site exceeded 17.1. Deaths before age 65 accounted for 40.7% of deaths but 64.6% of YLL. These two cancers had the highest YLL per death in every sensitivity analysis. The VSLY-valued burden was EUR 85.4 billion (EUR 58.3 billion with discounted life years); monetary ranks matched YLL ranks for 17 of the 21 sites.
CONCLUSION: Ranked by deaths, brain and other CNS cancers fall in the lower half of cancer sites; ranked by YLL per death, they rank first or second, with cervical cancer. Monetary valuation expresses this burden in euros but does not change the ranking.
POLICY SUMMARY: European cancer monitoring reports mainly deaths and age-standardised mortality rates, and the premature-mortality indicator of the EU Country Cancer Profiles omits brain and other CNS cancers. Including them, and reporting YLL per death by cancer site, would show which cancers cause death at younger ages; both use existing Eurostat data.

articles.title: Association Between Serum Estradiol Change From hCG Trigger to Oocyte Retrieval and Clinical Pregnancy in Fresh GnRH Antagonist ICSI Cycles: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Özer DA, Kabukçu C
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess whether proportional serum estradiol change from trigger to retrieval is associated with clinical pregnancy in fresh gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonist intracytoplasmic sperm injection cycles.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 849 cycles from 727 patients. Estradiol change was expressed as the percentage change from trigger to retrieval day. Cycles were classified as Group A (decline ≥ 45%; n = 272), Group B (decline > 30% to < 45%; n = 279), or Group C (decline ≤ 30% or increase; n = 298). The primary outcome was clinical pregnancy with fetal cardiac activity. Analyses used multivariable logistic regression, with generalized estimating equations for repeated cycles within patients.
RESULTS: Of the 849 cycles, 391 (46.1%) had a positive pregnancy test and 340 (40.0%) resulted in clinical pregnancy. Cycles with clinical pregnancy showed a smaller estradiol decline than those without (median -34.7% vs. -39.6%; p < 0.001), whereas absolute estradiol difference did not differ significantly (p = 0.878). Clinical pregnancy rates differed across groups (30.5%, 45.5%, and 43.6%; p < 0.001) despite comparable fertilization rates, top-quality embryo availability, and numbers of embryos transferred. After multivariable adjustment, proportional estradiol change remained associated with clinical pregnancy (adjusted odds ratio 1.090 per 10-percentage-point increase, 95% confidence interval 1.005-1.183; p = 0.038); generalized estimating equations yielded similar results. Spontaneous abortion rates were similar among groups.
CONCLUSIONS: A more pronounced periovulatory estradiol decline remained modestly associated with lower odds of clinical pregnancy despite similar top-quality embryo availability. Proportional estradiol change may be a complementary marker of the periovulatory hormonal transition.

articles.title: Aging Skin as a Contributor to Sexual Dysfunction.
articles.authors: Fleshner L, Advani S, Klufas T et al.
articles.abstract: Sexual health remains an important aspect of quality of life into older adulthood. Sexual concerns are common yet often inadequately addressed in dermatology. Age-related cutaneous and mucosal changes may contribute to discomfort, dyspareunia, avoidance of intimacy, and a diminished self-image. These manifestations differ by gender identification and may be compounded by fluctuating hormone levels, medical comorbidities, and societal expectations surrounding aging and perceived desirability. Dermatologists are well positioned to identify and address these concerns. In this review, we examine the physiologic and psychosocial effects of aging skin and mucosa and how this might impact on sexual health, available therapeutic strategies, and special considerations for populations with distinct medical or psychosocial needs.

articles.title: Ovarian Carcinoma Immunoreactive Antigen domain-containing protein 2 (OCIAD2) maintains bone marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells during steady state hematopoiesis.
articles.authors: Sinha A, Praveen W, Sinha S et al.
articles.abstract: The OCIA (Ovarian Carcinoma Immunoreactive Antigen) domain-containing protein Asrij/OCIAD1 maintains mouse hematopoietic stem cell quiescence and prevents myeloproliferative disease. However, the role of its family member, OCIAD2, in mouse hematopoiesis is unidentified. We report that in the mouse bone marrow (BM), OCIAD2 expression is enriched in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), as compared to mature blood cells. We generated the first ociad2 knockout (KO) mice and show that they are viable and fertile. KO BM had a significant reduction in HSPC frequency, yet the abundance of lineage-committed progenitors or terminal blood cells was unaffected, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms downstream of HSPCs may be in play. A majority of the KO HSPCs were in the G0 stage of the cell cycle, indicating enhanced phenotypic quiescence, which may contribute to a reduced HSPC pool. Interestingly, the persisting OCIAD2-independent HSPCs responded to acute irradiation and chronic transplantation stress, yielding hematopoietic output comparable to controls. Further, transcriptome analysis of KO HSPCs at steady-state, revealed dysregulation of cell proliferation genes, including cMyc. In vitro pharmacological stabilization of cMyc rescued the proliferative potential and abundance of KO HSPCs. This suggests that reduced cMyc in KO HSPCs may contribute to their decreased proliferative activity and enhanced G0 state. Thus, OCIAD2 acts as a novel regulator of HSPCs during steady state hematopoiesis. Altogether, our study introduces a new mouse model that underscores the resilience of hematopoiesis through multiple pathways, with OCIAD2 knockout mice offering valuable insights into the regulation of blood stem cell quiescence and hematopoietic homeostasis.

articles.title: The "data vacuum" in menopausal mental health: A global analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Jiang J, Yang X, Zhu P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data are fundamental to scientific progress. However, disparities in data sharing and management have created a "data vacuum" in some regions. In China, this gap is particularly evident in women's health research, including menopausal mental health, where systematic comparisons of international and domestic data resources remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare international and Chinese data sources on menopausal mental health and to identify structural gaps in menopause-specific variables, mental health measurement, longitudinal design, and the integration of biological and social factors.
STUDY DESIGN: This study was a structured comparative review of data sources rather than a systematic review or meta-analysis. We included 37 data sources: 16 international cohorts and 21 Chinese data sources. Data were extracted across four predefined dimensions: (1) survey years and sample sizes; (2) menopause-related variables; (3) mental health variables; and (4) questionnaire and non-questionnaire variables. A descriptive comparative analysis was conducted to identify patterns, gaps, and contextual variations.
RESULTS: Only about half of the Chinese data sources included a menopausal status variable, and about 30 % used standardized mental health instruments. Compared with international cohorts, Chinese data sources showed less consistent coverage of menopause-specific variables, more fragmented mental health assessment, and more limited integration of longitudinal and biosocial data. These findings indicate that the "data vacuum" reflects a lack of harmonized, population-representative, longitudinal, and linkable data resources rather than an absence of published studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Chinese menopausal mental health research is constrained by structural gaps in data infrastructure. Addressing these gaps will require standardized core variable frameworks, expanded prospective cohorts, enhanced interdisciplinary collaboration, and integration of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence to improve data quality and research capacity.

articles.title: Quality of life, perceived stress, and coping strategies in Italian women with endometriosis: A cross-sectional online survey.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Conte L, Lupo R, Triglia C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic gynaecological condition that may affect physical health, psychological well-being, fertility, intimate relationships, and social and occupational functioning. This study examined quality of life, perceived stress, and coping strategies in Italian women with self-reported physician-diagnosed endometriosis.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 446 Italian women reporting physician-diagnosed endometriosis. Participants completed the Endometriosis Impact Questionnaire (EIQ), the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and the COPE-NVI-25. Analyses included one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlations, and multivariable linear regression with heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors; false-discovery-rate adjustment was applied to exploratory comparisons.
RESULTS: Mean age was 32.5 ± 8.1 years, and mean reported age at diagnosis was 26.8 ± 6.3 years. EIQ scores were highest in the physical and psychological domains, particularly among women diagnosed within the previous year. Perceived stress increased consistently with the frequency of all disease-related difficulties examined. PSS-10 scores correlated positively with all EIQ domains, most strongly for the psychological (r = 0.551; 95 % CI 0.483 to 0.613), social (r = 0.511; 95 % CI 0.439 to 0.577), and physical (r = 0.451; 95 % CI 0.374 to 0.522) domains, negatively with positive attitude (r = -0.412; 95 % CI -0.486 to -0.332) and problem-focused coping (r = -0.291; 95 % CI -0.374 to -0.204), and positively with avoidance strategies (r = 0.335; 95 % CI 0.250 to 0.415; all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, higher PSS-10 scores were independently associated with greater EIQ total score, lower positive attitude, higher avoidance strategies, and poor/fair self-rated health.
CONCLUSIONS: Endometriosis was associated with a broad multidimensional burden extending beyond pain. The findings support a multidisciplinary model of care that includes psychological assessment, fertility counselling, and support for relational and occupational consequences.

articles.title: Polypharmacy and the ageing brain: Anticholinergic burden in the ageing population and the impact of gynaecological medications.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Shetty P, Sujeewa Fernando BA, Fernando BA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population ageing is accelerating worldwide, with increasing multimorbidity and polypharmacy. Medicines with anticholinergic properties are widely prescribed in older adults for conditions, including depression, urinary incontinence, Parkinson's disease, allergies, and respiratory disorders. While short-term anticholinergic effects such as dry mouth and constipation are well recognised, increasing evidence suggests that cumulative anticholinergic exposure may contribute to adverse cognitive outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This review discusses the concept of anticholinergic burden, outlines commonly used tools to quantify exposure, and examines the evidence linking cumulative anticholinergic exposure with cognitive decline and other adverse health outcomes. It also explores strategies to identify and mitigate anticholinergic burden in clinical practice.
METHODS: Relevant literature on anticholinergic medications, burden scales, and associated clinical outcomes was reviewed. Attention was given to studies assessing cognitive and functional outcomes and to validated tools, including the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale, Anticholinergic Risk Scale (ARS), and Anticholinergic Drug Scale (ADS).
RESULTS: Observational studies have reported associations between higher cumulative anticholinergic burden and adverse outcomes including cognitive impairment, delirium, falls, and functional decline. However, findings regarding long-term cognitive decline and dementia remain inconsistent and vary according to drug class and the burden scale used. Anticholinergic burden tools can support identification of cumulative medication exposure, but their scores should not be interpreted as precise measures of individual cognitive risk.
CONCLUSION: Although the evidence linking cumulative anticholinergic exposure with long-term cognitive decline and dementia remains inconsistent and predominantly observational, higher anticholinergic burden has been associated with adverse outcomes including delirium, drowsiness, and an increased risk of falls, particularly in older adults. Routine assessment, careful medication review, and appropriate deprescribing may reduce avoidable harm. Integrating burden assessment into prescribing systems and clinical decision-support tools may further promote safer pharmacotherapy in an ageing society.

articles.title: LIM kinase inhibitors attenuate prostate enlargement and bladder outlet obstruction-associated detrusor pressure in rat models relevant to mixed lower urinary tract symptoms.
articles.journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics
articles.authors: Cen P, Qiu X, Chen M et al.
articles.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and overactive bladder (OAB) frequently coexist in men, producing mixed lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) that are inadequately managed by current combination pharmacotherapies. LIM kinase (LIMK) regulates actin cytoskeletal remodeling and smooth muscle tone. Here, we evaluated the in vivo effects of 2 LIMK inhibitors, SR7826 and LIMKi3, on prostate and bladder function in rat models of BPH and bladder outlet obstruction (BOO). In BPH rats, the prostate index was reduced by 0.080 ± 0.018 (SR7826, P < .01) and 0.058 ± 0.018 (LIMKi3, P < .05). Epithelial thickness was reduced by 17.71 ± 2.25 μm and 18.27 ± 1.72 μm, respectively (both P < .001). In the prostate, desmin decreased with both inhibitors (P < .05), α-smooth muscle actin decreased with LIMKi3 (P < .001), and vimentin increased with LIMKi3 (P < .01). LIMKi3, but not SR7826, reduced bladder index by 0.009 ± 0.002 (P < .05). Bladder wall structure and cholinergic-induced contractility were preserved. In BOO rats, maximum detrusor pressure was reduced by 32.2 ± 5.4 cm H2O (SR7826) and 32.8 ± 4.3 cm H2O (LIMKi3) (both P < .001). In conclusion, LIMK inhibition suppressed prostatic hyperplasia and altered prostatic contraction-associated protein expression in BPH rats, and reduced BOO-associated maximum detrusor pressure without impairing baseline cholinergic contractility. LIMK1/2 inhibition may represent a novel, pathophysiology-driven therapeutic strategy for the prostatic and bladder components of mixed LUTS. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Current pharmacotherapy for mixed lower urinary tract symptoms relies on combining α1-adrenoceptor antagonists (α1-blockers) and antimuscarinics-drugs with distinct targets and compounding adverse effects. This study demonstrates that LIM kinase inhibitors reduce prostatic hyperplasia and bladder outlet obstruction-associated maximum detrusor pressure in rat models while preserving baseline cholinergic bladder contractility, identifying LIM kinase as a candidate cross-organ target relevant to both voiding and storage dysfunction.

articles.title: Developmental Programming by Androgen Excess in Rats: A Cross-Talk Between Metabolic State and Ovarian Function.
articles.authors: Silva AF, Diaz VV, Higa R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse conditions during critical developmental windows can lead to health problems in adulthood, a process known as developmental programming. Prenatal androgen excess induces long-term reproductive and metabolic disturbances that lead to features similar to those of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). We investigated whether prenatal androgen excess alters metabolic status and ovarian function in adulthood.
METHODS: Pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats received daily subcutaneous injections of testosterone (1 mg) or vehicle during gestational days 16-19. Female offspring were evaluated at 90 d of age (young adulthood), during estrus. Glucose tolerance, serum lipids, ovarian weight, histology, and ovarian gene and protein expression were assessed.
RESULTS: Prenatally hyperandrogenized (PH) females exhibited an increased anogenital distance, a reduced ovarian weight and gonadosomatic index, impaired glucose tolerance, and elevated serum cholesterol and triglyceride levels. Ovarian PPARδ and PPARγ protein levels were increased, while Esr1 and Prβ mRNA levels were elevated. Star mRNA levels decreased, while 3β-HSD and 17β-HSD protein levels were increased, indicating altered cholesterol trafficking and steroidogenic regulation. Histological analysis revealed cystic and aberrant Graafian follicles, an increase in preantral follicles, a reduction in primordial, antral, and Graafian follicles, and fewer corpora lutea. These are consistent with disrupted follicular progression and ovulatory dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal androgen exposure induces long-lasting alterations in glucose and lipid metabolism and ovarian function in young adult female rats. These changes involve ovarian metabolic sensing, cholesterol transport, steroidogenesis, and follicular dynamics, providing insight into the mechanisms linking developmental programming by androgen excess to reproductive dysfunction and PCOS-like phenotypes.

articles.title: Women's experiences of seeking, undergoing and recovering from secondary sphincter repair following obstetric anal sphincter injury - A qualitative study.
articles.journal: Sexual & reproductive healthcare : official journal of the Swedish Association of Midwives
articles.authors: Johansson A, Ingemansson A, Sjödahl J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore women's experiences of seeking, undergoing and recovering from secondary sphincter repair following obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI).
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 women following secondary repair of OASI. Data were analyzed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: The main theme "Hope for healing" reflects women's experiences of secondary sphincter repair. Three categories emerged:" Navigating a fragmented path to care", "Entrusting healing to others" and "Living between recovery and persistent rupture", compromising six subcategories. Prior to surgery, women described having had negative healthcare encounters, resulting in broken trust and fragmented hope for healing. Approaching secondary sphincter repair was by no means easy but characterised by obstacles to overcome and great need for self-advocacy. When referred to and assessed by specialists, trust and hope were gradually restored. Following the surgery, some experienced great physical outcomes, such as restoration of continence. Others did not notice substantial improvements short-term but tried to remain hopeful for potential long-term effects. Regardless of physical outcomes, women emphasized the healing effects of being heard, treated with respect and given a chance. However, the women expressed a need for further follow-up and rehabilitation post-surgery to improve and/or sustain function and manage symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Following OASI, women struggle to be heard and face challenges in obtaining a referral for specialist evaluation, rendering them even more vulnerable in an already sensitive situation. Knowledge and attitudes regarding OASI within healthcare need to be addressed, along with clearer pathways to specialist care and better access to rehabilitation.

articles.title: Structural MRI Morphometry Across the Alzheimer's Disease Spectrum: Classification and Generalization.
articles.authors: Benyahia A, Araar IE, Bahi Azzououm A et al.
articles.abstract: Structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides quantitative measures of brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), but reliable classification also depends on the evaluation protocol and performance across cohorts. This study assessed a morphometry-based approach for distinguishing cognitively normal (CN) participants, those with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and those with AD. The primary cohort included 815 participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), with one screening MRI per participant and predefined training, validation, and test sets. MRI records were linked to FreeSurfer measurements using exact participant and image identifiers. A multinomial L2-regularized logistic regression classifier used 42 predefined structural features and five-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition site. In the held-out three-class test (n = 121), balanced accuracy was 0.6119 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.5291-0.6873) and the macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) was 0.7525. Recall was 0.8529 for CN, 0.2931 for MCI, and 0.6897 for AD. Additional development analyses examined demographic and clinical variables separately from the primary MRI-only result. For the binary transfer experiment, a separate ADNI-trained CN-versus-AD model using 32 shared morphometric features achieved balanced accuracy of 0.8458 and ROC-AUC of 0.9016 in site-grouped out-of-fold evaluation. The fixed model was then tested without target-cohort tuning on 181 older participants from the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS-1), grouped by Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR = 0 versus CDR > 0). External balanced accuracy was 0.6492 (95% CI: 0.5799-0.7158) and ROC-AUC was 0.7502. Because ADNI diagnoses and OASIS-1 CDR groups are not identical clinical endpoints, the external experiment was interpreted separately from the primary three-class analysis. The results demonstrate the value of reporting class-specific performance and independent-cohort evaluation when assessing structural MRI morphometry.

articles.title: Pregnancy Surveillance in the Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance Network: Findings from a Multisite Open Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.authors: Assefa N, Abdullahi YY, Muir JA et al.
articles.abstract: Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance (CHAMPS) investigates causes of stillbirth and deaths in children <5 years of age in high-mortality settings. Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance established pregnancy surveillance to prospectively monitor pregnancies and their outcomes and better understand maternal care in these settings. Pregnant women were enrolled during home visits or antenatal care from catchment populations in eight countries (Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and South Africa). At enrollment, data on maternal sociodemographic characteristics, obstetric history, and medical conditions were collected. Data on maternal and infant healthcare and outcomes were collected at delivery and 42 days postpartum. A total of 84,413 pregnant women were enrolled from June 2021 to July 2025; the median gestational age at enrollment was 21.3 weeks. Most (64,820/84,413; 76.8%) participants were <30 years of age (range: 12-55 years), and 70.6% of participants had previous pregnancies. Across sites, the median number of antenatal care contacts was three; 21.6% (15,302/70,940) of women experienced unsupervised or unassisted home deliveries, and 12.0% of newborns were low birthweight. Overall, a high stillbirth rate (22.9/1,000 births; range 4.3-26.5/1,000 among sites), neonatal mortality rate (17.6/1,000 live births; range 4.6-25.2/1,000 among sites), and risk of perinatal death (36.7/1,000 births; range 16.9-43.9/1,000 among sites) were found, with heterogeneity in all mortalities by site (P <0.001). The maternal mortality ratio was 177.5 per 100,000 live births. In the CHAMPS Pregnancy Surveillance catchment areas, women presented late for antenatal care, had too few antenatal contacts (<8), and experienced a high burden of adverse pregnancy outcomes. The findings highlight the need for better pregnancy care in similar areas with high child mortality.

articles.title: Miscarriages and Perinatal Deaths in Sierra Leone: Data From A Nationwide Household Survey.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.authors: Mathéron HM, Westendorp J, van Duinen AJ et al.
articles.abstract: Demographic data on adverse pregnancy outcomes in Sierra Leone are scarce. This study examined the prevalence of miscarriages and perinatal deaths from a community perspective by use of a population-based, cross-sectional household survey on surgical conditions conducted in Sierra Leone in 2019-2020. A weighted random cluster design was used to select the enumerator areas with a probability proportional to the population size. Seventy-five clusters were selected, with 25 households per cluster and two random participants per household. Women between 12 and 50 years of age were interviewed about family planning methods and their obstetrical history. A total of 3,745 participants were included; 914 were women of reproductive age. Family planning methods were used by 216/914 women (28.5%). In total, 2,160 lifetime pregnancies were recalled, of which 104/2,160 (4.8%) resulted in early pregnancy loss. Eighty-three (83/104; 79.8%) were reported as spontaneous abortion, 18/104 (17.3%) were intentional abortions. There were 55/2, 160 stillbirths reported (2.5%). The stillbirth rate was 18.4 per 1,000 births (95% CI: 11.2-31.0). The perinatal mortality rate, defined as stillbirth after a gestational age of 28 weeks or neonatal death within the first 7 days after birth per 1,000 births calculated over a 5-year period, was 38.4 per 1,000 births (95% CI: 26.7-55.0). This population-based survey demonstrates a high perinatal mortality rate and low use of family planning methods in Sierra Leone. Miscarriages were likely to be underreported. Improved access to affordable contraception and appropriate medical evaluation of pregnancy loss may help reduce the burden of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: The Rising Tide of Cardiovascular Risk in Younger Women.
articles.authors: Stuenkel CA
articles.abstract: Menopause management is in the midst of a paradigm shift as enthusiasm, fueled by the lay press and online influencers, increases amongst women, yielding an escalating interest in hormone therapy (HT) that has not been experienced since the turn of the last century. Updates to regulatory labeling of menopausal HT products include the removal of boxed warnings and language that recommended using the lowest dose for the shortest time while focusing on risks and benefits to those seeking menopause symptom relief-women younger than 60 or within 10 years of menopause. This renewed desire for menopausal HT must be tempered with the understanding that risks for cardiovascular disease (CVD) are also rising in premenopausal women as are hospitalizations for acute coronary syndromes. Factors that contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk include adverse pregnancy outcomes, which are occurring with increasing frequency. The metabolic changes that accompany the menopause transition further complicate a woman's cardiovascular risk profile. Many women today will arrive at menopause with more advanced CVD risk than what was encountered in the past. If women are considering HT for menopausal symptom relief or bone preservation, careful consideration is required to identify and treat modifiable CVD risks-dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, hypertension, and, increasingly, obesity-to targets established by guidelines before initiating HT. Risk assessment with validated risk calculators can help stratify CVD risk, a factor that determines lipid lowering therapy, and the advisability and choice of menopausal HT. The rising tide of cardiovascular risk does not have to make waves at menopause.

articles.title: A Randomized Trial of Fractionated CO2 Laser With Topical Clobetasol Compared With Fractionated CO2 Laser With Placebo for Treatment of Vulvar Lichen Sclerosus.
articles.authors: Dieter AA, Ferrante K, Gillingham A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare skin-related outcomes in women with vulvar lichen sclerosus treated with fractionated carbon dioxide laser with concomitant clobetasol propionate 0.05% with women treated with fractionated carbon dioxide laser plus placebo ointment.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial was conducted at nine U.S. sites from March 2022 to April 2025. English- or Spanish-speaking adult women with lichen sclerosus electing vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment were eligible. Women were excluded if they had prior vaginal mesh prolapse repair, previous radiation therapy, prior laser, immunomodulators or systemic therapy for lichen sclerosus, active genital infection, suspicious vulvar lesion or malignancy, active treatment for malignancy, or poor wound healing or if they were currently pregnant, lactating, or planning pregnancy. All participants underwent three vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatments 4-6 weeks apart and were randomized 1:1 to concomitant clobetasol propionate 0.05% or petrolatum-based ointment (placebo) 0.25-0.5 g nightly for 4 weeks starting at first laser treatment and then twice weekly until end of study. The primary outcome was proportion of women with improvement of 16 or more points on the Skindex-29, a validated questionnaire measuring a patient's skin-related symptoms and functioning, assessed at 4-5 weeks after completion of fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment. Additional outcomes included Skindex-29 domain scores, patient impression of improvement (PGI-I [Patient Global Impression of Improvement] score), treatment satisfaction, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Two hundred one participants were randomized, and 180 (89 clobetasol vs 91 placebo) had complete data. Most women indicated symptom onset 1 year or more before lichen sclerosus diagnosis, and approximately 90% had previously used topical corticosteroids. Nearly a third of all participants achieved the primary outcome (30.3% clobetasol vs 27.5% placebo, P=.67). Participants in the clobetasol arm demonstrated a greater improvement in Skindex-29 symptom score (mean change -19.0±18.5 clobetasol vs -10.1±19.8 placebo, P<.01) and total score (mean change -13.0±15.9 clobetasol vs -8.1±15.5 placebo, P=.04). More participants were "satisfied" or "very satisfied" with treatment after clobetasol (85.4% clobetasol vs 69.2% placebo, P=.01). Fifteen adverse events occurred in 12 participants (6 per cohort).
CONCLUSION:…

articles.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Boyd T, Kane S
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) presents unique clinical considerations related to fertility, medical therapy, and delivery planning. The strongest predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes is active disease, making maintenance of remission a central management priority. Prepregnancy counseling for patients with IBD should address reproductive goals, nutritional status, and the potential effect of prior pelvic surgery on fertility. Most established IBD therapies, including aminosalicylates, thiopurines, and biologic agents, can be continued to maintain remission, whereas methotrexate is contraindicated, and Janus kinase inhibitors and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators are generally avoided. Delivery planning should be individualized, with cesarean delivery generally favored for active perianal Crohn disease or rectovaginal fistula and shared decision making emphasized for patients with an ileal pouch-anal anastomosis. Optimal outcomes depend on coordinated multidisciplinary care that prioritizes disease control, treatment continuation, and individualized reproductive and delivery planning.

articles.title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Black-White Racial Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity.
articles.authors: Smith-Webb RS, Parker SE, Werler MM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the proportion of the Black-White racial disparity in severe maternal morbidity (SMM) that could be eliminated by preventing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,242,574 Black and White birthing people 12-55 years of age with deliveries in Massachusetts from 1998 to 2021 using PELL (Pregnancy to Early Life Longitudinal data system). Maternal race was used as a proxy for exposure to racism. The primary outcome was SMM excluding blood transfusion-only events (SMM-20); we also considered SMM including blood transfusion-only events (SMM-21) and cardiac complications. We conducted causal mediation analyses with HDP as the mediator and used G-estimation to estimate the Black-White racial disparity in SMM that would remain if HDP were prevented. We calculated the proportion of the disparity that could be eliminated by preventing HDP and severe HDP separately.
RESULTS: Compared with White birthing people, Black birthing people experienced 63.8 excess SMM-20 events per 10,000 in-hospital deliveries (95% CI, 58.1-69.6). If HDP were prevented, the disparity would be reduced to 38.6 excess SMM-20 events (95% CI, 32.9-44.2), suggesting that 39.6% of the absolute Black-White racial disparity in SMM-20 could be eliminated. The estimated proportions eliminated were 33.1% for SMM-21 and 57.6% for cardiac complications. The proportion of the Black-White racial disparity eliminated by preventing severe HDP alone was 27.9% for SMM-20, 20.7% for SMM-21, and 31.3% for cardiac complications.
CONCLUSION: Preventing HDP could substantially reduce Black-White racial disparities in SMM.

articles.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
articles.authors: Üstünel S, Ali N
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twenty cyclotides were modeled and screened against the predicted active site of CYP19A1. Based on an integrated evaluation of HADDOCK and ClusPro docking, binding orientation, and interaction characteristics, cycloviolacin O4 was prioritized as the lead candidate. The predicted CYP19A1-cycloviolacin O4 complex exhibited a HADDOCK score of -82.8 ± 9.8, a cluster RMSD of 0.2 ± 0.1 Å, and a ClusPro energy score of -872.1. Docking against the reference inhibitor exemestane and the reference peptide SNA-60-367-10 provided additional computational benchmarking. Subsequent 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations, normal mode analysis, and MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA calculations supported the predicted structural stability and dynamic compatibility of the complex, yielding binding free energies of -66.58 ± 3.46 kcal/mol (MM-GBSA) and -4.56 ± 4.29 kcal/mol (MM-PBSA). Computational safety assessment predicted cycloviolacin O4 to be non-antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic, while immune simulation suggested a balanced immune response. Collectively, these findings identify cycloviolacin O4 as a computationally predicted CYP19A1-binding cyclotide scaffold. However, these observations are derived exclusively from computational analyses and require biochemical, cellular, and in vivo validation before any conclusions regarding biological activity or therapeutic potential can be drawn.

articles.title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Perez SM, Boley AM, Reiley HB et al.
articles.abstract: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman's lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing "estrogen protection hypothesis," which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield inconsistent results. Our results establish that perimenopause is a mechanistically distinct neurobiological window characterized by a unique failure of hippocampal-dopamine circuit regulation. By identifying this specific period of circuit instability, this work provides a framework for stage-specific psychiatric interventions and reframes reproductive aging as a series of distinct transitions in brain function.

articles.title: Timing of Antenatal Care, Stillbirth, and Infant Mortality in Migrant Mothers in Australia.
articles.authors: Hossain S, Oei JL, Munasinghe S et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Timely antenatal care (ANC) reduces pregnancy risks, yet the association between delayed ANC and stillbirth or infant mortality among migrant mothers in Australia has not previously been investigated.
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether delayed ANC is associated with higher stillbirth and infant mortality among Australia-born compared with migrant mothers.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study assessed births to non-Indigenous mothers in New South Wales from January 1, 2002, to December 31, 2020, followed up to infant age of 1 year. Mothers were categorized as Australia-born, migrant from English-speaking country (ESM), or migrant from non-English-speaking country (non-ESM). Data were analyzed between August 2025 and June 2026.
EXPOSURES: Timing of first ANC, defined as 12 weeks or earlier, 13 to 19 weeks, 20 weeks or later, or no ANC.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcome was stillbirth (at ≥20 weeks) and infant mortality (at prehospital discharge, posthospital discharge, or 1 year). Adjusted relative risks (ARRs) were estimated using Poisson regression models, stratified by migration group.
RESULTS: This study included 1 720 033 births (median [IQR] maternal age, 31.2 [27.4-34.8] years; 884 235 male infants [51.4%]), including 1 132 193 (65.8%) to Australia-born, 116 026 (6.7%) to ESM, and 471 814 (27.4%) to non-ESM mothers. Late ANC (>12 weeks) was more common in non-ESM mothers (190 338 [40.3%]) than Australia-born (334 790 [29.6%]) or ESM (41 029 [35.4%]) mothers. In cross-group comparisons, non-ESM mother status was associated with higher risk of adverse outcomes regardless of ANC timing. Compared with Australia-born mothers with early ANC (≤12 weeks), a higher risk of stillbirth (ARR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.18-1.33) and 1-year (ARR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.22-1.44), predischarge (ARR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.25-1.54), and postdischarge (ARR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.03-1.37) infant mortality was observed in non-ESM mothers accessing ANC by 12 weeks. Similar risk patterns were observed in non-ESM mothers with late ANC. In within-group comparisons, among Australia-born mothers, each category of delayed ANC was associated with higher risk. No ANC was associated with the highest risks across all maternal groups for stillbirth and 1-year infant mortality. For non-ESM mothers, late ANC (≥20 weeks) was associated with a lower risk of predischarge mortality (ARR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.61-0.92) but a higher risk of postdischarge mortality (ARR, 1.30;…

articles.title: Robot-assisted hysterectomy for large uteri: perioperative outcomes with the da Vinci Xi and SP systems.
articles.authors: Masuda S, Kanno K, Kitamura R et al.
articles.abstract: We compared perioperative outcomes of robot-assisted hysterectomy (RAH) for large uteri using the da Vinci Xi and SP systems. This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients who underwent RAH for benign indications with a uterine weight of ≥ 500 g between January 2023 and April 2026 at a single Japanese center. Among 200 patients, 162 underwent Xi and 38 underwent SP procedures. Operative time (OT) did not differ significantly between the groups (104 [85-126] vs. 113 [98-133] min, p = 0.083), whereas docking time was shorter with SP (3 [2-4] vs. 2 [1-3] min, p < 0.001). Estimated blood loss (EBL) was lower with SP (25 [5-100] vs. 5 [5-34] mL, p = 0.043). After adjustment for uterine weight, body mass index, previous abdominal surgery, and severe endometriosis, SP use was independently associated with longer OT (unstandardized regression coefficient, 15.1 min; 95% confidence interval, 5.2-25.0, p = 0.003), whereas the robotic platform was not independently associated with EBL. Uterine weight and severe endometriosis were independently associated with longer OT, whereas uterine weight was associated with greater EBL. Postoperative complications and conversion to laparotomy did not differ considerably between groups. The SP system may offer an alternative to Xi for RAH in patients with large uteri.

articles.title: Functional recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a patient-centred perspective.
articles.authors: Mastroianni R, Ragusa A, Iannuzzi A et al.
articles.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) and urinary incontinence (UI) are among the most distressing sequelae after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), substantially affecting quality of life. Exploring patients' perceptions of functional recovery and willingness to undergo corrective surgery may improve rehabilitation and shared decision-making. This cross-sectional survey included patients previously treated with RARP, identified from a single-center IRB-approved prostate cancer database. Baseline demographic, clinical, and pathological data were collected. Erectile function was assessed using the IIEF-5. Patients completed the Sexual Recovery and Urinary Continence Recovery questionnaires after receiving standardized information on penile prosthesis (PP) and artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and ANOVA analyses were performed. Between April and September 2025, 214 patients completed the questionnaires. Mean age was 65 years, and 67% underwent nerve-sparing surgery. At a mean follow-up of 21 months (range 2-77 months), 89% reported postoperative ED, with a mean IIEF-5 score of 7; 93% had mild-to-severe ED. The mean importance of erectile function recovery was 8/10. Overall, 15% of patients with ED expressed interest in PP implantation. Younger men were more likely to consider PP surgery (p < 0.001). Although older men expressing willingness reported higher interest scores (9/10), differences across age groups were not statistically significant (p = 0.33). Overall urinary continence was rated 7/10, 39% reported UI, and 19% of patients with UI expressed willingness to undergo AUS implantation, with no significant age-related differences. Recovery of erectile and urinary function remains a major priority after RARP. Patients' willingness to consider definitive surgical rehabilitation highlights the importance of individualized counselling and shared decision-making.

articles.title: Comparing 7 mm versus 8 mm as the Optimal Threshold for Fresh Embryo Transfer Cancellation in Thin Endometrium: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Han Q, Teng Y, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract: This study looked at women with a thin uterine lining during in vitro fertilization to find out when it is better to freeze all embryos and transfer later instead of doing a fresh embryo transfer. We evaluated nearly 80,000 treatment cycles and analyzed 4,401 cycles in which women had a thin uterine lining. We found that for women with a lining thinner than 7 mm, freezing the embryos for a later transfer significantly increased the chances of a live birth. For women with a lining between 7 mm and 8 mm, a fresh transfer resulted in a higher chance of pregnancy. By favoring a 7 mm cutoff over an 8 mm cutoff, doctors can avoid unnecessary treatment delays and emotional stress for many patients while ensuring the best possible chance of a successful and healthy pregnancy.

articles.title: Early ICG Fluorescence During Layer-by-Layer Presacral Dissection in Robot-Assisted Sacrocolpopexy.
articles.authors: Tanaka Y, Takahashi A, Yoneoka Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Safe presacral access to the anterior longitudinal ligament during robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy requires an understanding of the layered anatomy around the hypogastric nerve and presacral vessels. Intravenous indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence has been reported to visualize pelvic vessels and provide anatomical cues along the hypogastric nerve pathway. This video demonstrates its early use during layer-by-layer presacral dissection.
METHODS: A 79-year-old woman with Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification stage III uterine prolapse underwent robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy. ICG (0.25 mg/kg) was administered intravenously immediately before commencing presacral dissection at the sacral promontory. White-light and near-infrared fluorescence views were alternated during layer-by-layer presacral dissection.
RESULTS: Major pelvic vessels became fluorescent within approximately 1 min after ICG administration. Layer-by-layer dissection delineated the prehypogastric nerve fascia and the anatomically presumed course of the hypogastric nerve.
