articles.title: Association of single intrauterine fetal demise with severe brain injury and death in liveborn cotwins delivered before 32 weeks: large single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Cui X, Li Y, Yin S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the independent association in twin pregnancy between single intrauterine fetal demise (sIUFD) and major short-term adverse outcomes, particularly severe brain injury (SBI) or death, in extremely and very preterm liveborn cotwins (delivered < 32 weeks), to examine whether this association extends beyond chorionicity and to identify critical gestational windows of vulnerability and potential mediating pathways.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included twin pregnancies, with or without sIUFD, delivered < 32 weeks at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China, between January 2014 and December 2024, with neonates admitted immediately after birth to the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sIUFD and the primary outcome, a composite of SBI or death of the liveborn cotwin prior to hospital discharge. Subgroup analyses stratified by chorionicity and gestational age at sIUFD were performed to identify risk patterns and critical gestational windows of vulnerability. Mediation analyses were conducted to explore whether the association between sIUFD and SBI or death was mediated by early-onset sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth or the 5-min Apgar score, and sensitivity analyses incorporating propensity-score matching to balance baseline confounders were performed to assess the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: In total, 1069 twin pregnancies delivered < 32 weeks were included (113 with and 956 without sIUFD). sIUFD was independently associated with significantly increased odds of SBI or death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 2.85 (95% CI, 1.61-4.97)). This association was consistent across monochorionic and dichorionic subgroups. The highest point estimate was observed when sIUFD occurred at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks' gestation (aOR, 3.72 (95% CI, 1.64-8.06)). Mediation analysis identified a 5-min Apgar score < 7, suggestive of perinatal asphyxia, as the primary mediator of SBI or death (proportion mediated: 24.30%), while disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth and early-onset sepsis acted as significant secondary mediators (proportions mediated: 6.60% and 4.30%, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: sIUFD is independently associated with an increased risk of SBI or death in liveborn cotwins delivered < 32 weeks, regardless of chorionicity, particularly when demise occurs…

articles.title: Efficacy of dietary supplements in improving sperm parameters in men with infertility: a network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Shen XY, Lu LJ, Che BW et al.
articles.abstract: This network meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy of various dietary supplements on sperm parameters in men with infertility, thereby providing evidence-based guidance for future clinical practice. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on dietary supplements for treating male infertility published from database inception up to January 16, 2026. The risk of bias in the included studies was assessed utilizing the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. This network meta-analysis included 56 studies. For improving semen volume, the top five supplements were lycopene, Nigella sativa oil (NSO), zinc, ubiquinol, and myoinositol. For improving sperm concentration, the top five supplements were omega-3, zinc, myoinositol, lycopene, and curcumin nanomicelle. For improving sperm progressive motility, the top five supplements were zinc, alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), myoinositol, vitamin E, and L-acetyl-carnitine (LAC). For improving the normal sperm morphology rate, the top five supplements were N-acetylcysteine (NAC), zinc, omega-3, NSO, and curcumin nanomicelle. For improving total sperm motility, the top five supplements were omega-3, curcumin nanomicelle, LAC, zinc, and ALA. For improving total sperm count, the top five supplements were ALA, curcumin nanomicelle, zinc, L-carnitine (LC), and LAC. Appropriate dietary supplements demonstrate significant efficacy in improving semen parameters in male patients with infertility. However, their efficacy varies across semen parameters. Zinc and omega-3 ranked relatively high across all six semen parameters. In clinical practice, the individual characteristics of different patients should be considered when selecting therapeutic agents and formulating personalized dietary supplement regimens.

articles.title: Updated clinical recommendations for cardiovascular risk assessment to facilitate hormone therapy prescribing: incorporating PREVENT risk calculator and the 2026 multisociety lipid guidelines.
articles.authors: Shufelt CL, Stuenkel CA, Lau ES et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women and is a key consideration when evaluating candidates for menopausal hormone therapy (HT). Over the past two decades, recommendations regarding HT use have evolved substantially and now include the understanding that cardiovascular risk varies according to age, time since menopause onset, and baseline cardiovascular health. Consequently, cardiovascular risk assessment has become an integral component of menopause management. The recent introduction of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) calculator and incorporation of PREVENT into the 2026 American College of Cardioloty/Amercian Heart Association multisociety dyslipidemia guideline represent an important shift in CVD prevention. PREVENT includes contemporary cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk factors and estimates both 10-year and 30-year cardiovascular risk for adults ages 30-79 years without known CVD. Concurrently, updated lipid management recommendations emphasize individualized risk assessment and consideration of risk-enhancing factors, and in some cases, coronary artery calcium scoring, along with more explicit lipid-lowering targets. This perspective provides a practical framework for integrating PREVENT-derived risk categories into menopause care. We outline cardiovascular risk stratification strategies for women considering HT, discuss the role of coronary artery calcium scoring and female-specific risk enhancers, and align contemporary lipid management recommendations with decisions regarding initiation of HT, including route of administration. By integrating cardiovascular risk assessment and menopause management, clinicians can optimize cardiovascular risk reduction and individualize treatment decisions for symptomatic midlife women.

articles.title: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause and prevalent cardiometabolic and skeletal outcomes in US women: a cross-sectional NHANES analysis.
articles.authors: Tang C, Zheng Y, Zhan L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate associations between bilateral oophorectomy performed after natural menopause and prevalent cardiometabolic and skeletal outcomes in US women.
METHODS: We pooled 10 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (1999-2018). The analytic cohort included 321 women with chronology-confirmed bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause and 5,363 referent women with natural menopause, no hysterectomy, and no confirmed bilateral oophorectomy. Survey-weighted quasi-Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios (PRs), adjusted for age, body mass index, education, smoking, alcohol use, and physical activity measured at the NHANES assessment. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control was applied across seven prespecified outcomes.
RESULTS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher cardiovascular disease prevalence (PR: 1.58; 95% CI: 1.13-2.21; P=0.008; q=0.039). Associations did not meet the false discovery rate threshold for diabetes (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.94-1.71), hypertension (PR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.93-1.22), osteoporosis (PR: 1.20; 95% CI: 0.90-1.60), or wrist fracture (PR: 1.54; 95% CI: 0.94-2.54). Hip and spine fractures were not estimable because of sparse exposed events. Adjustment for age at natural menopause attenuated the cardiovascular estimate (PR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.02-2.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher self-reported cardiovascular disease prevalence. Because outcome timing relative to surgery was unavailable and residual confounding remains, this cross-sectional association should not be interpreted as causal or as a basis for clinical recommendations.

articles.title: The effect of aerobic and core stabilization exercises on primary dysmenorrhea in high school girls: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
articles.authors: Cakmak Reyhan A, Yildirim A
articles.abstract: BackgroundPrimary dysmenorrhea is common in adolescents and is associated with menstrual pain, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life. Evidence regarding structured combined exercise programs implemented in school settings remains limited. This study examined the effects of a 12-week combined aerobic and core stabilization exercise program on pain, symptom severity, functional impairment, and quality of life in high school students with primary dysmenorrhea.MethodsA randomized controlled, assessor-blinded trial was conducted in which thirty high school girls were allocated to either an exercise group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). The intervention group completed a 12-week aerobic and core stabilization program, whereas the control group maintained usual activities. The primary outcome was menstrual pain intensity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included the Premenstrual Syndrome Scale (PMSS), Menstrual Symptom Questionnaire (MSQ), Functional and Emotional Measure of Dysmenorrhea (FEMD), Dysmenorrhea Impact Scale (DIS), and Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36).ResultsThe exercise group demonstrated reductions in pain intensity, menstrual symptom severity, and functional impairment (p < 0.001). Quality-of-life scores improved across all domains (p < 0.001). No meaningful changes were observed in the control group (p > 0.05). Between-group analyses favored the exercise intervention across all outcomes (p < 0.001).ConclusionA combined aerobic and core-stabilization exercise program may be a feasible and effective adjunctive strategy for managing primary dysmenorrhea in adolescents. However, the restrictive BMI eligibility range (19.0-24.9 kg/m2) limits the generalizability of these findings to adolescents outside this range.

articles.title: Phenotypic age acceleration mediates the association between plant-based diet and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome among postmenopausal women: a population-based cross-sectional analysis.
articles.authors: Li N, Zhou G
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome framework highlights the links among metabolic disorders, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular complications. Research examining how plant-based dietary indices influence the progression of CKM and the potential role of biological aging remains limited.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from 2,988 postmenopausal women participating in NHANES 2005-2018. Weighted logistic regression models estimated the associations between plant-based dietary indices and advanced CKM. Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the mediating role of phenotypic age acceleration.
RESULTS: Among the study population, 658 participants (22.0%) were identified with advanced CKM. A one-unit increase in the plant-based diet index (PDI) and the healthful PDI was associated with a lower odds of advanced CKM (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.96-1.00 and OR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.94-0.99, respectively). In contrast, each one-unit increase in the unhealthful PDI was associated with 4% higher odds of advanced CKM (adjusted OR: 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.07). These associations were consistent across population subgroups. Furthermore, phenotypic age acceleration partially mediated the association between PDI and advanced CKM, accounting for 16.0% (95% CI: 8.2%-25.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher adherence to healthy plant-based dietary patterns is associated with a lower likelihood of advanced CKM among postmenopausal women. The association between PDI with advanced CKM may be partly mediated through reduced phenotypic age acceleration.

articles.title: Breast cancer in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: clinicopathological findings and survival outcomes from a large registry-based cohort in Southern Iran.
articles.authors: Ghaedi A, Johari MG, Mallahi A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinicopathological characteristics, treatment patterns, and survival outcomes between premenopausal and postmenopausal women with breast cancer in Iran.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 6,930 women aged ≥18 years diagnosed with breast cancer between 2014 and 2022 from the Shiraz Breast Cancer Registry. Patients were stratified by menopausal status. Clinicopathological features, tumor receptor status, and treatment modalities were compared. Five-year overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Premenopausal women more frequently presented with aggressive tumor features, including larger tumor size, multifocality, necrosis, and adverse pathologic characteristics (all P<0.01). Postmenopausal patients had a higher prevalence of estrogen receptor-positive tumors (P=0.003) and more commonly received hormone therapy (P<0.001). Five-year OS was comparable between groups (96.1% vs. 96.0%, P=0.981), whereas DFS was higher in postmenopausal women (90.1% vs. 87.2%, P=0.030). In multivariable analysis, postmenopausal status (HR 0.49, 95% CI: 0.27-0.90) and hormone therapy (HR 0.43, 95% CI: 0.29-0.64) were independently associated with improved OS, whereas high tumor grade, concurrent lymphovascular and perineural invasion, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy were associated with poorer OS and DFS.
CONCLUSIONS: Menopausal status was associated with distinct tumor biology, clinicopathological features, and treatment patterns in breast cancer, with premenopausal patients showing more aggressive disease. Although menopausal status showed some association with survival outcomes, its effect appeared largely driven by age and underlying tumor characteristics, suggesting limited independent prognostic value.

articles.title: The relationships among gender perceptions, internalized misogyny, and body shame in postmenopausal women: a structural equation modeling study.
articles.authors: Gök B, Pelit Aksu S, Yaman Sözbir Ş
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations among gender perception, internalized misogyny, and body shame in postmenopausal women using structural equation modeling.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 210 postmenopausal women recruited between March and May 2026. Data were collected using the Gender Perception Scale, the Internalized Misogyny Scale, and the Body Shame subscale of the Objectified Body Consciousness Scale. Higher Gender Perception Scale scores indicate more egalitarian gender perceptions, whereas higher Internalized Misogyny Scale and Body Shame subscale scores indicate greater internalized misogyny and body shame, respectively. Structural equation modeling was used to simultaneously examine the hypothesized associations among these variables, with age, educational level, family type, and postmenopausal height reduction included as covariates.
RESULTS: Gender perception was negatively correlated with internalized misogyny (r=-0.478, P<0.001) and body shame (r=-0.286, P<0.001), whereas internalized misogyny was positively correlated with body shame (r=0.320, P<0.001). In the structural model, more egalitarian gender perception was associated with lower internalized misogyny (standardized β=-0.48, P<0.001) and lower body shame (standardized β=-0.17, P<0.05), whereas greater internalized misogyny was associated with greater body shame (standardized β=0.25, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: More egalitarian gender perception was associated with lower internalized misogyny and body shame, whereas greater internalized misogyny was associated with greater body shame. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal relationships. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify these relationships.

articles.title: Body composition and mortality across the reproductive cycle: findings from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
articles.authors: Liang I, Flynn S, Watson K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: There are greater changes in body composition during the menopause transition than at other stages in a woman's reproductive cycle. We studied fat mass (FM) and fat-free mass (FFM) in participants at different reproductive stages at the beginning of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) and evaluated their association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and total mortality.
METHODS: In 3,439 women from MESA, equations to determine FM and FFM were derived from bioelectrical impedance analysis performed at exam 5 and applied to exam 1. Women were divided into three groups: reproductive phase (before final menstrual period [FMP]), menopause phase (FMP to 2 years subsequently), and late menopause phase (>2 years after FMP). Adjusted Cox multivariate models evaluated the association between FM, FFM, anthropometric measures, and MACE/total mortality.
RESULTS: In the full cohort, higher FM was significantly associated with increased MACE (HR per kg, 95% CI: 1.03 [1.01-1.05]) and mortality (1.03 [1.01-1.05]), while higher FFM was associated with lower mortality (0.96 [0.93-1.00]). In the menopause phase, FM and FFM showed clinically significant associations with total mortality (FM 1.18 [1.02-1.38]; FFM 0.71 [0.50-1.00]). These associations were not observed in women aged 48-52 years old.
CONCLUSION: Higher FM is associated with a higher risk of MACE/total mortality, whereas higher FFM is associated with a lower risk of total mortality. Associations noted in women in the menopause phase but not among similarly aged women suggest ovarian aging may influence these relationships.

articles.title: Association of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acid intake and their ratio with severe dysmenorrhea among female adolescents: A case-control study.
articles.authors: Gracela E, Farapti F, Mat Daud Z' et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDysmenorrhea is a reproductive health disorder related to menstruation that is prevalent among adolescents and may lead to reduced productivity and quality of life. Severe dysmenorrhea is thought to be influenced by inflammatory mechanisms mediated by an imbalance in the dietary intake ratio of omega-3 to omega-6 fatty acids.AimTo examine the association between omega-3 intake, omega-6 intake, and the omega-3:omega-6 fatty acid intake ratio and severe dysmenorrhea compared with no dysmenorrhea among female adolescence.MethodsThis study used an analytical observational case-control design. The research was conducted from January to February 2025 at SMA Negeri 9 Surabaya, Indonesia, involving 90 female adolescents. The severity of menstrual pain was assessed using the Verbal Multidimensional Scoring System (VMSS). Dietary intake of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids was measured using a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (SQ-FFQ). Statistical analysis was performed using the Chi-squared test with a 95% confidence interval (CI).SummaryThe results of the study indicated a significant association between omega-3 fatty acid intake [P = 0.036, OR (95% CI) = 3.083 (1.170-8.129)] and the omega-3 to omega-6 intake ratio [P = 0.005, OR (95% CI) = 3.864 (1.573-9.492)] with severe dysmenorrhea. However, no significant association was found between omega-6 fatty acid intake and severe dysmenorrhea [P = 0.168, OR (95% CI) = 2.588 (0.818-8.188)]. Female adolescents are encouraged to pay attention to their dietary intake, particularly the consumption of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, which may be associated with the presence of severe dysmenorrhea.

articles.title: Dry eye disease in the menopausal transition: toward recognition as a hormonal manifestation.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Skurski ZP, Mikkilineni A, Simon JA
articles.abstract: Dry eye symptoms affect an estimated 64-80% of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women, placing dry eye disease (DED) among the most prevalent yet least recognized manifestations of the menopausal endocrine transition. The pathophysiology centers on androgen deficiency and altered estrogen signaling, with sex hormone receptors expressed throughout the ocular surface, and the 2025 Tear Film and Ocular Surface Society Dry Eye Workshop III recognizes sex, gender and hormones as one of seven major domains influencing DED. Objective ocular surface signs are significantly worse in postmenopausal compared with premenopausal women even when subjective symptoms are similar, mirroring the symptom-sign dissociation well recognized in genitourinary syndrome of menopause. This hormonally mediated dry eye is described in recent literature as menopausal dry eye. This opinion advocates for routine screening using the validated Ocular Surface Disease Index-6 questionnaire, counseling patients on the ocular implications of hormone therapy and timely referral to eye care providers for persistent or moderate-to-severe symptoms. Recognizing dry eye as a menopausal disease can improve how ocular symptoms are attributed, discussed and treated in midlife women.

articles.title: The management of endometriosis in adolescents and young adults: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Blyth U, Maslej L, Bennett G et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: What evidence-based strategies are used in the treatment of endometriosis-associated symptoms in adolescents and young adults?
SUMMARY ANSWER: The use of hormonal therapies and surgery was associated with improvements in pain symptoms in most studies; however, the certainty of evidence was very low, meaning that the true impact of these treatments remains uncertain.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Endometriosis is a chronic condition estimated to affect 1 in 10 women, with symptoms commonly present during adolescence. Current management strategies for endometriosis include analgesia, hormonal suppression, and surgery, as well as non-pharmacological measures.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This is a systematic review of the literature. Six databases (CINAHL, Cochrane Central Database of Controlled Trials, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsychInfo, and Web of Science Core Collection) were searched from inception to May 2026. Search terms were related to endometriosis combined with terms regarding management and the adolescent age group.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Eligible studies included participants aged under 24 years with endometriosis and reported on outcomes in the management of endometriosis-associated symptoms. Only studies with full texts or data available in English were included. Screening and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two authors. Key outcomes included pain, quality of life, recurrence, and side effects. Data were reported narratively. Risk of bias was assessed according to study design (ROB2, NOS, and JBI tools) and quality of evidence with the GRADE system.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The search identified 14 376 records, of which 333 full texts were assessed for eligibility, and 23 studies, with a combined total of 1561 participants, were included. There were two randomised controlled trials, one single-arm open-label interventional study, eleven cohort studies, and nine case series. Five studies investigated hormonal treatments, one other study assessed other pharmacological treatments, sixteen studies assessed surgical management with or without hormonal treatment, and one study investigated non-pharmacological treatments. Most studies reported improvements in pain symptoms; however, there was heterogeneity in study design, length of follow-up, and outcome measures.
LIMITATIONS REASONS FOR CAUTION: There is limited evidence in this age group. Most studies had a moderate risk of bias, and the…

articles.title: Longitudinal Dynamics of Circulating NET-Associated Biomarkers and Their Association with Progressive Perihematomal Edema After Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.authors: Wei N, Yang J, Yue J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), perihematomal edema (PHE) is a major driver of secondary brain injury, yet the temporal dynamics of circulating neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated biomarkers and their clinical relevance to PHE progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize their longitudinal dynamics and associations with PHE progression and clinical outcomes after sICH.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 200 patients with sICH (70 surgical and 130 non-surgical) and 50 healthy controls were enrolled, with serial peripheral blood samples collected at four predefined time points. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA), and neutrophil elastase-DNA (NE-DNA) complexes were quantified. NET-associated neutrophil phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, with scanning electron microscopy for complementary ultrastructural assessment. PHE volume was quantified using 3D Slicer, and 90-day functional outcomes were assessed. In the non-surgical cohort, five regression algorithms were compared for exploratory estimation of peak PHE volume from baseline features using all 36 baseline variables within nested cross-validation. SHAP was used to interpret the best-performing model.
RESULTS: Circulating NET-associated biomarkers were markedly elevated in patients with sICH (all P < 0.001), with descriptive plots suggesting different temporal patterns in the surgical and non-surgical subgroups. SEM revealed NET-like extracellular ultrastructures in peripheral neutrophils. In the non-surgical cohort, PHEV was highest at T3 (3-5 days after onset) among the four scheduled assessments; baseline MPO-DNA was strongly correlated with peak PHE volume (ρ = 0.76, P < 0.001) and remained independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Within the non-surgical cohort, exploratory machine-learning analysis identified CitH3, MPO-DNA, and hematoma volume as the top-ranked contributors to peak PHEV estimation. Higher baseline MPO-DNA was also independently associated with unfavorable 90-day functional outcome in this cohort.
CONCLUSION: Circulating NET-associated biomarkers showed temporal changes after sICH. In the non-surgical cohort, higher baseline MPO-DNA was associated with greater peak PHEV and unfavorable 90-day functional outcome. These findings point to a biological link that larger multicenter studies now need to…

articles.title: Clinical efficacy of mirabegron in the treatment of female patients with Parkinson's disease and overactive bladder.
articles.authors: Li L, Yu H, Zhang C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare short-term clinical outcomes and adverse events associated with mirabegron and tolterodine treatment in female patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and overactive bladder (OAB).
METHODOLOGY: This retrospective cohort analysis included 90 female patients with PD and OAB treated in Huzhou Third Municipal Hospital from January 2021 to October 2024. The final study cohort comprised 45 patients receiving mirabegron and 45 patients receiving tolterodine, selected in a 1:1 ratio with consideration of available baseline clinical characteristics. The primary efficacy outcome was the change in Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS) from baseline to 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in urinary diary variables and the occurrence of adverse events, while changes in the Nonmotor Symptoms Scale (NMSS) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) were considered exploratory outcomes.
RESULTS: A significant group × time interaction was observed for urgency episodes/24 hours (IRR=0.684, 95% CI 0.515-0.908, P=0.009), indicating a greater reduction over time in the mirabegron group. No significant interactions were observed for nocturia episodes/night (IRR=0.938, 95% CI 0.794-1.108, P=0.450) or micturitions /24 hours(IRR=0.962, 95% CI 0.906-1.021, P=0.202). Significant group × time interactions were also observed for OABSS (estimate=-0.422, 95% CI -0.813 to -0.031, P=0.034) and PSQI (estimate=-1.956, 95% CI -3.098 to -0.813, P=0.001), whereas the interaction for NMSS was not significant (estimate=0.244, 95% CI -0.754 to 1.243, P=0.631). There was no significant difference in the incidence of individual adverse events between the two groups after treatment (P>0.05). However, the proportion of patients experiencing at least one adverse event was significantly lower in the mirabegron group than in the tolterodine group (20.0% vs. 44.4%, P=0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort of female patients with PD and OAB, mirabegron treatment was associated with greater short-term improvements in selected OAB-related outcomes and sleep quality, as well as a lower proportion of patients experiencing adverse events, compared with tolterodine over 12 weeks. These findings require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

articles.title: Histopathological Subtype and Cancer Stem Cell Marker Expression in Advanced Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Two-Year Progression-Free Survival Study.
articles.authors: Budiana ING, Saspriyana KY
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late detection and significant recurrence rates make epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) one of the deadliest gynecologic cancers. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) have been associated with chemoresistance and relapse. However, their prognostic significance remains uncertain. This study examined CSC marker expression in advanced EOC with 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) and the predictive significance of type I/type II classification in histological subtypes.
METHODS: We performed an ambispective cohort study of 114 women with advanced EOC who had undergone optimal cytoreductive surgery and standard platinum-based chemotherapy. Expression of CD24, CD44, CD117, CD133, and aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) was studied by immunohistochemistry. PFS was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier methods and correlations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. The predictive value was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Independent predictors of PFS were identified by multivariate Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: Most patients had stage III disease (60.5%) and were 40-59 years old (65.8%) significantly associated with poor survival (P < 0.001). Type II cancers had significantly worse 2-year PFS compared to type I tumors (21.3% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.008). None of the single CSC markers were significantly associated with PFS in univariate analysis (all P > 0.05) and had poor discrimination in ROC analysis. The combined assessment of CSC markers and histological classification further improved the prognostic stratification and was significantly associated with PFS (P < 0.05). In multivariate analysis, age, tumor stage, and histology type were independent predictors of PFS.
CONCLUSION: Expression of CSC markers alone is not an independent predictor of 2-year PFS in advanced EOC. Its prognostic relevance is modulated by tumor histology as type I/type II provides a stronger and more consistent prognostic stratification.

articles.title: Relationship Between Estrogen-Induced BRCA2 and Development of Gastric Cancer.
articles.authors: Hayashi T, Konishi I
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) is the fourth most common malignancy, affecting one in 11 men (9.1%) and one in 23 women (4.38%). Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and smoking are the primary risk factors for GC. Individuals who have multiple other family members with GC are also at higher risk owing to lifestyle and genetic factors. H. pylori-eradicating medications can reduce the risk of disease. The incidence of GC increases after 50 years of age, particularly among men; however, the reason for the differing incidence rates between the sexes remains unclear.
METHODS: To clarify the reasons for sex differences in GC incidence rates from a molecular pathological perspective, we utilized cancer genome profiling (CGP) and information on BRCA2 expression levels obtained by immunohistochemistry and the number of GC cases in the family.
RESULTS: We investigated the incidence of GC in families with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and found it to be 4.2-fold higher than that in non-HBOC families. In families with versus without HBOC, men accounted for 74.57% and 53.67% of all GC cases, respectively, indicating that men are more likely to develop GC in the former group. Furthermore, estrogen stimulation induced breast cancer type 2 (BRCA2) expression in genetically modified mice as well as in cultured cells, and low-grade atypical cells were observed in the gastric mucosal tissues of female mice that underwent ovarian resection. Additional research experiment revealed that stimulation by the female hormone estrogen induces the expression of BRCA2, which suppresses the development of GC. Clinical studies have also shown that patients with GC who have high BRCA2 expression exhibit longer survival rates than those in whom BRCA2 expression is low.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the data suggest that the higher mortality rate of GC in men than in women may be due to a protective effect of BRCA2.

articles.title: N6-methyladenosine reader IGF2BP3 promotes endometrial cancer progression via modification of circ-EPB41L2 expression.
articles.authors: Lai L, Feng X, Zheng Y et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer is one of the primary contributors to cancer-related mortality on a global scale. Insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) is a reader protein of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modifications and serves a key role in the carcinogenesis of numerous solid tumors. The present study explored the role and underlying mechanism of IGF2BP3 in endometrial cancer. Bioinformatics methods were applied to examine m6A reader protein expression levels and their effect on survival. Reverse transcription-quantitative PCR and western blotting were used to determine IGF2BP3 expression in cancer and paracancerous tissues. After knockdown of IGF2BP3 expression, cell proliferation and migration were examined. Significantly expressed genes were identified through Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes and Gene Ontology analysis. Additionally, the cross-linking immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput sequencing (CLIP-seq) database and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP) techniques were employed to ascertain the targets of IGF2BP3. The present study revealed that the expression levels of IGF2BP1, IGF2BP3, RNA binding motif protein 15 and YTH N6-methyladenosine RNA binding protein C2 differed between normal and endometrial cancer tissue, based on The Cancer Genome Atlas analysis. Through examination of endometrial cancer tissues and Kaplan-Meier analysis, IGF2BP3 was determined to be a target for further research. Following knockdown of IGF2BP3 expression in HEC-1A cells using short hairpin RNA transfection, proliferation and migration were decreased compared with those in the control group. A transcriptome-wide RNA-sequencing assay indicated that circular RNA (circ) was abnormally expressed in endometrial carcinoma and was regulated by IGF2BP3. CLIP-seq database analysis and MeRIP suggested that circ-erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 like-2 (EPB41L2) was the target of IGF2BP3. IGF2BP3 was involved in the progression of endometrial cancer and served an oncogenic role by targeting circ-EPB41L2 in an m6A-dependent manner.

articles.title: Age-related differences in postoperative pain after single-port access adnexal laparoscopy: a three-arm analgesic strategy comparison.
articles.authors: Paik ES, Yu M, Kang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated age-related differences in postoperative pain and analgesic requirements after single-port access (SPA) laparoscopy for adnexal disease under three analgesic regimens.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 470 patients stratified into: <40 years (n = 257), 40-55 years (n = 138), and >55 years (n = 75). Patients received continuous wound infiltration (CWI) alone, intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV PCA) alone, or combined CWI + IV PCA. NRS pain scores at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h were the primary outcomes. Multivariable regression adjusted for analgesic regimen, surgery type, and body mass index, with additional adjustment for endometriosis in sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Unadjusted NRS scores did not differ among age groups. Rescue nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug use was higher in patients aged <40 years at 0-6, 6-12, and 24-48 h. After adjustment, patients aged <40 years had significantly higher NRS scores at 24 h (β = 0.276, p = 0.046). Combined CWI and IV PCA was associated with the lowest postoperative pain scores across age groups; however, a formal age × treatment interaction was not statistically significant. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Younger age (<40 years) was independently associated with modestly higher postoperative pain at 24 h after SPA adnexal laparoscopy, although this difference was below the minimal clinically important difference. These findings may inform individualized analgesic planning, pending confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Gestational PFOS Exposure Impairs Placental System A (SNAT2)-Mediated Amino Acid Transport and Labyrinth Vascularization in Rats and Differentiated BeWo Monolayers.
articles.authors: Yadav P, Hofmann A, Mishra JS et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study investigated mechanisms underlying perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS)-associated fetal growth restriction. Specifically, we asked whether PFOS directly impairs transcellular transfer of substrates representing three major nutrient classes-glucose, long-chain fatty acid, and system A-mediated neutral amino acid transport-across the placental epithelial barrier, and examined the transporters involved.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Syncytialized human BeWo b30 monolayers cultured on collagen-coated Transwell inserts were exposed to PFOS (10 and 50 μM) for 24 h. Transcellular transport of [3H]-2-deoxy-D-glucose, [1-14C]-linoleic acid, and the system A-specific substrate L-[14C]MeAIB was quantified. Transporter expression was assessed by digital PCR and Western blot. Timed-pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats received PFOS (10 or 50 mg/L, corresponding to 1.2 and 6.1 mg/kg/day) in drinking water from gestational day (GD) 4 to 20 (n = 5 dams/group). Maternal intake and body weight, fetal and placental weights, and labyrinth zone SNAT and CD31 expression were quantified.
RESULTS: In BeWo monolayers, PFOS did not alter transcellular transport of 2-deoxy-D-glucose or linoleic acid but reduced MeAIB transport by 24% (10 μM) and 28% (50 μM). SNAT2 mRNA and protein were dose-dependently downregulated; SNAT1 mRNA was reduced only at 50 μM, with no change in SNAT1 protein, and SNAT4 was expressed at very low levels in this model. In pregnant rats, PFOS reduced fetal weight at both exposures (9% and 15% at 10 and 50 mg/L) and reduced placental and labyrinth zone weights, without altering maternal water intake, feed intake, gestational weight gain, or litter size. Quantitative immunohistochemistry showed dose-dependent reductions in labyrinth zone SNAT2 (60% and 79% at 10 and 50 mg/L) and SNAT1 immunostaining, with no change in SNAT4, together with reduced CD31-positive area (19% and 33%).
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational PFOS exposure impairs placental system A-mediated neutral amino acid transport, as measured with the system A-specific substrate MeAIB, without detectable effects on 2-deoxy-D-glucose or linoleic acid transfer under identical conditions, and is accompanied by downregulation of the stress-responsive syncytiotrophoblast transporter SNAT2. In vivo, this epithelial transport defect coincides with reduced labyrinth zone vascularization. Together, these epithelial and vascular changes describe a plausible route by which a persistent environmental contaminant…

articles.title: Therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cells for the restoration of dysfunctional rat testes.
articles.authors: Mishra R, Kumari A, Negi A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chemotherapy, especially with alkylating agents, can impair spermatogonial stem cells in young males, leading to infertility. This study evaluates the therapeutic efficacy of bone-marrow-derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells (BM-MSCs) in restoring testicular function of the dysfunctional testes in a chemo-ablated infertile rat model.
METHOD: Wistar male rats were randomly divided into three groups: the first control group without any treatment; the second group was infertile chemo-ablated, generated through the intraperitoneal injections of 15 mg/kg of Busulfan, twice with a two-week interval; and the third group was chemo-ablated and subsequently treated with intra-testicular injections of enriched MSCs. The BM-MSCs were cultured and sorted using magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS), and purity was confirmed by Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS) analysis of positive and negative cell-surface markers. Purified MSCs were injected into the testes of the infertile rats. Results were evaluated after 2-10 weeks of treatment. After 2 weeks of MSC treatment, mating trials for these males were conducted every 2 weeks, and their testes, as well as serum samples; were collected for therapeutic assessment of MSCs.
RESULTS: Histological assessments of the excised testes revealed a gradual, significant improvement within 10 weeks of treatment. Additionally, the expression levels of stem cell and sperm maturation markers were elevated in the testes of treated animals, indicating recovery of spermatogenesis. Hormonal analyses demonstrated normalisation of FSH and Testosterone levels after treatment. Mating studies also demonstrated that the MSC-treated group delivered 7-8 pups per litter, whereas chemo-ablated animals remained totally infertile.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall findings support MSC transplantation as a promising approach to restore testicular function and fertility, inspiring continued exploration in regenerative medicine.

articles.title: Extracellular miR-517a in Embryo Culture Medium Is Associated With Implantation Failure After Frozen-Thawed Embryo Transfer.
articles.authors: Nagata K, Kajimura I, Nagata A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether placenta-associated microRNAs in embryo culture medium can serve as non-invasive biomarkers of embryo implantation potential.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 122 patients who underwent frozen-thawed embryo transfer in 2022. Embryos were evaluated using the Gardner classification, and those scoring ≥ 3BB were defined as morphologically good-quality. Placenta-associated microRNAs [chromosome 19 microRNA cluster (C19MC): miR-517a, miR-518b, miR-517c; chromosome 14 microRNA cluster (C14MC): miR-323-3p, miR-411, miR-433] in embryo culture medium were quantified by RT-qPCR and correlated with implantation outcomes.
RESULTS: Forty-nine patients (40.2%) achieved pregnancy and 73 (59.8%) did not. C19MC levels were significantly higher in the non-pregnant group, with miR-517a showing the strongest association with implantation failure (p < 0.0001, AUC = 0.7246). Among morphologically good-quality embryos, the pregnancy rate increased from 53.8% to 64.7% when embryo selection incorporated miR-517a assessment. Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that extracellular miR-517a remained independently associated with implantation outcome after adjustment for maternal age, trophectoderm grade, and fertilization method.
CONCLUSIONS: Extracellular miR-517a may provide clinically useful, non-invasive information regarding embryo implantation potential and may complement conventional morphology-based embryo assessment.

articles.title: Multiomic liquid biopsy: emerging applications in disease quantification, biomarker detection, molecular phenotyping, and cancer signal of origin prediction.
articles.authors: Gheeya JS, Welch L, Porter J et al.
articles.abstract: The field of cancer-related liquid biopsy, largely defined as plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis by next-generation sequencing (NGS), is rapidly evolving from genomics-only approaches to multiomic assays that add components such as DNA fragmentomics and epigenomics, with or without proteomics, to a genomic backbone. Here we describe how integration of epigenomic profiling, particularly tumor-specific methylation signatures, may extend ctDNA testing beyond detection of genomic alterations toward broader molecular phenotyping, with applications in alternative approaches to tumor fraction quantification, enhanced detection of actionable genomic biomarkers and mechanisms of resistance, histologic and lineage characterization, and cancer signal of origin prediction. This evolution has facilitated the clinical application of liquid biopsy across the cancer care continuum, from screening/early detection to determining minimal residual disease (MRD) in early-stage cancers to selecting treatment and determining mechanisms of acquired resistance in advanced-stage cancers. These new multiomic assays may also support prospective biomarker-driven clinical trials incorporating complementary measures of tumor burden, genomic alterations, and molecular phenotype. Collectively, these advances suggest that multiomic liquid biopsy platforms may represent a major advance in precision oncology, enabling dynamic and comprehensive characterization of tumor biology.

articles.title: Early detection and interception in hepato-pancreatic-biliary cancers: endoscopic imaging, liquid biopsy, and emerging molecular biomarkers.
articles.authors: Aseafan M, Alqayidi A, Dayis S et al.
articles.abstract: Early detection of hepato-pancreatic-biliary cancers requires different strategies because the populations at risk, precursor lesions, and accessible specimens vary by organ. This review examines established endoscopic imaging and tissue-acquisition pathways together with circulating and lesion-derived biomarkers. Inherited or familial pancreatic risk defines the main pancreatic surveillance population; endoscopic ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging are complementary, and prospective cohorts show a stage shift but also interval cancers and low-yield surgery. In pancreatic cysts, imaging features and selective tissue or cyst-fluid analysis can refine management, but no fluid marker independently identifies high-grade dysplasia with sufficient certainty. For biliary cancer, surveillance in primary sclerosing cholangitis depends on noninvasive imaging, whereas endoscopic ductal sampling, cholangioscopy-guided biopsy, and selective endoscopic ultrasonography address suspicious strictures; bile methylation and sequencing may increase diagnostic yield when an invasive procedure is already indicated. Endoscopy has a selective role in gallbladder lesions and a direct interception role in histologically confirmed ampullary adenomas. Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance remains based on ultrasonography with alpha-fetoprotein; cell-free DNA methylation and multi-analyte blood tests are promising but have not replaced guideline-based surveillance. Across organs, case-control accuracy does not establish surveillance utility. Liquid biopsy complements rather than generally replaces histopathological diagnosis. Established adjuncts must be distinguished from investigational assays, including those with prospective diagnostic validation but no demonstrated surveillance utility. Integration requires specimen-specific analytical validation, independent testing in the intended-use population, and evidence of incremental clinical value over standard imaging and endoscopy. Interventional studies must show that this approach reduces late-stage diagnosis without excessive false-positive procedures.

articles.title: Perceptions and Barriers to the Use of Modern Contraceptive Methods and HIV Prevention Among Youth Aged 16-20 in Rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Kazindu TM, Mwene-Batu P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study explored young people's perceptions of modern contraceptive methods and HIV prevention, alongside the socioeconomic and cultural barriers they encounter three years post-implementation of Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) in rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Evaluating this curriculum exposes critical implementation gaps.
METHODS: A qualitative cross-sectional study using semi-structured, face-to-face in-depth individual interviews was conducted in January 2025 among 64 students aged 16-20 across four secondary schools (two public, two faith-based) in South Kivu. A purposive stratified sampling strategy enabled intra-sample comparative analysis across genders and institutional models. Transcribed data underwent inductive thematic open coding with double independent coding to ensure inter-rater reliability.
RESULTS: Our findings expose a significant public health paradox. On one hand, an absolute semantic disconnect exists where 100% of interviewed youth were unfamiliar with the term "contraception", coexisting with a low rate of consistent condom use (17.7%) among sexually active participants, despite comprehensive theoretical mastery of HIV transmission pathways. On the other hand, constrained by community taboos and the fear of parental or religious sanctions, these adolescents underutilize formal youth-friendly healthcare channels. Instead, they engage in alternative risk behaviors, specifically the post-coital utilization of high-dose quinine and aspirin (reported by 40.9% of sexually active girls) as makeshift emergency contraceptives, inducing clinical side effects. Conservative religious leaders and parents with low formal education levels constituted the primary socio-cultural barriers, whereas schoolteachers were supportive.
CONCLUSION: Rural youth remain vulnerable to unintended pregnancies and HIV due to community-enforced silence and institutional linguistic barriers. Effective interventions must transcend classroom education to engage religious and parental gatekeepers, de-stigmatize family planning services, and adapt formal medical terminologies to local daily vernacular languages to align theoretical knowledge with behavioral change.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of uterosacral ligaments reveals progressive cellular remodeling in pelvic organ prolapse.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Liu L, Hao Y, Deng X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common disorder of pelvic support tissues, but its cellular basis in the uterosacral ligament (USL) remains poorly defined. Most existing single-cell studies, have failed to characterize stage-specific cellular changes across different POP severities, lacking a stage-resolved perspective across disease severity stages.
METHODS: We profiled USL samples from 10 women with POP (4 moderate, 6 severe) and 4 controls by single-cell RNA sequencing, and analyzed 167,609 high-quality cells using clustering, trajectory inference, differential expression, cell-cell communication, and transcription factor analyses to systematically decode progressive USL cellular alterations.
RESULTS: Ten major cell populations were identified. Fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells (SMCs), and endothelial cells formed the structural core of the USL, while macrophages, neutrophils, mast cells, and T cells showed progressive inflammatory activation with increasing disease severity. Fibroblasts were highly heterogeneous and shifted from progenitor-like and perivascular states toward inflammatory, matrix-remodeling, and myofibroblast-like phenotypes. SMCs moved from a contractile program to stress-responsive and ECM-remodeling states, and endothelial cells underwent functional reprogramming rather than major compositional change. Cell-cell communication between stromal cells declined, whereas fibroblast-immune interactions increased. Collagen-related signaling decreased, while immune-associated ligand-receptor programs became more prominent as disease advanced.
CONCLUSION: Distinct from previous cross-sectional single-cell studies on POP, this work provides a unique stage-resolved transcriptomic landscape covering moderate-to-severe POP stages. POP is marked by coordinated stromal remodeling, immune activation, and disrupted intercellular signaling in the USL. This single-cell transcriptomic atlas provides a refined framework for interpreting stage-specific molecular alterations across graded POP severities and may facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for pelvic floor dysfunction.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of prediction models for maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes in HELLP syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
articles.authors: Lu Y, Huang X, Lin X et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: HELLP syndrome is uncommon but can cause serious maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). We investigated whether routinely available clinical and laboratory variables could support outcome-specific risk prediction.
METHODS: We included all women with HELLP syndrome treated at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to June 2023. Five outcomes were modeled: placental abruption (PAB), posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and a severe maternal composite outcome. The primary analysis used repeated nested cross-validation in the full cohort. Missing-data filtering and imputation, predictor screening, model-family selection, hyperparameter tuning, and threshold estimation were performed within each outer training fold so that the held-out fold evaluated the entire modeling process. Candidate families were ridge logistic regression, elastic-net logistic regression, and random forest. A paired sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was conducted to assess the effect of replacing mean/mode imputation.
RESULTS: Among 272 women, PAB occurred in 33 (12.13%), PRES in 23 (8.46%), PPH in 19 (6.99%), DIC in 9 (3.31%), and the severe composite outcome in 25 (9.19%). The corresponding AUCs were 0.715, 0.677, 0.833, 0.907, and 0.742. Ridge logistic regression was selected in 62%, 74%, 56%, and 62% of the outer folds for PAB, PRES, PPH, and the severe composite outcome, respectively. For DIC, the single-predictor logistic regression fallback was selected in 85% of the outer folds. In the paired analysis, MICE changed AUC by -0.002 to 0.009 and AUPRC by -0.005 to 0.002. PAB, PRES, and PPH did not meet the prespecified analysis criteria. DIC and the composite outcome met these criteria, although both estimates were limited by sparse events and the lack of external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Although performance was not uniformly strong and external validation is still needed, routinely available data showed potential for early risk stratification. In particular, the severe composite outcome provided a clinically meaningful way to combine individually rare but serious complications and may help identify women who warrant closer surveillance.

articles.title: The estrogen-ECM-integrin- cytoskeleton axis in pelvic organ prolapse: a mechanobiological framework linking matrix remodeling to repair failure.
articles.authors: Yang X, Chen L, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common disorder of pelvic support, but its estimated prevalence depends strongly on ascertainment. A 2024 meta-analysis reported a pooled prevalence of 30.9%, increasing to 41.8% in examination-based studies. Altered collagen turnover and estrogen-responsive tissue remodeling are important features of POP, yet they do not fully explain how extracellular-matrix (ECM) abnormalities may become persistent defects in cellular force transmission and repair. This narrative Review develops an evidence-graded estrogen-ECM-integrin-cytoskeleton axis, organized around ECM mechanics and fibroblast mechanosensing. We distinguish ERα-, ERβ- and GPER-mediated signaling; indirect hormonal effects on the matrix presented to integrins; and the more limited evidence for direct hormonal control of integrin signaling in human POP. We examine LOX/LOXL-dependent matrix maturation while separating expression, catalytic activity and mature cross-link measurements. The integrin-talin-vinculin molecular clutch provides a candidate connection between abnormal matrix resistance, FAK/Src-RhoA/ROCK signaling, cytoskeletal function and YAP/TAZ-dependent transcription. However, POP-associated mechanics vary with tissue compartment, measurement scale and disease state. Reduced counter-resistance and clutch slippage therefore represent a testable scenario, not a universal disease sequence. We identify experiments that could distinguish matrix-mediated effects from intrinsic fibroblast dysfunction and connect these questions to biomaterial design, controlled loading and local pathway modulation. Clinical estrogen therapy and experimental mechanopharmacology must remain distinct: improved local tissue quality does not establish prevention of prolapse recurrence, and no YAP/TAZ-targeted drug is approved for POP.

articles.title: Hormonal contraceptive users exhibit increased approach responses to higher reward in an online approach-avoidance task.
articles.authors: Knihs de Camargo C, Vegelius J, Björkstrand J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hormonal contraceptives (HOC) are used worldwide; however, there are controversies regarding their effects on mental health with studies reporting HOC to be associated with mood symptoms, especially depression and anxiety. Costly avoidance, i.e., avoiding a potentially rewarding situation to minimize anticipated emotional distress, is thought to be a key component of affective disorders. This study aims to explore the relationship between the use of hormonal contraceptives, symptoms of depression and anxiety, and costly avoidance.
METHODS: Self-reported users of HOC (n = 139) and non-users (n = 209) completed the Inventory of Depression and Anxiety Symptoms (IDAS-II) and partook in an online approach-avoidance conflict task assessing costly avoidance. Statistical analyses included generalized mixed effects models, t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.
RESULTS: HOC users showed increased odds of approach behavior in the highest reward level. No direct associations were found between approach behavior and depression and anxiety symptoms. Upon further post-hoc analysis, HOC use did not moderate any association between approach behavior and affective symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: In line with previous literature, HOC users showed less avoidant behavior than non-users. Results should be interpreted with caution, as the observational nature of the study opens up to self-selection bias. However, this represents an important first observation that warrants further longitudinal and/or placebo-controlled studies.

articles.title: Cell-free DNA in human ovarian follicular fluid as a potential biomarker of embryo quality in IVF cycles: a pilot study.
articles.authors: Jo EH, Kim TH, Eum JH et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is growing interest in evaluating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in follicular fluid (FF) as a molecular feature of the follicular microenvironment and examining its association with subsequent embryo development. This exploratory pilot study aimed to investigate the association between FF cfDNA integrity, measured by the Arthrobacter luteus (ALU) 247/115 ratio, and morphology-based embryo quality in IVF cycles.
METHODS: This observational study analyzed 106 follicular fluid samples from patients undergoing IVF with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) at a single fertility center. FF samples were collected during ovum pick-up, and cfDNA concentrations were quantified using ALU-quantitative PCR. To evaluate the ALU247/115 ratio in relation to age, participants were categorized into three age groups.
RESULTS: The ALU247/115 ratio showed a significant but weak positive correlation with embryo quality score across all patients (n = 106, r = 0.23, p = 0.016). Subgroup analysis revealed stronger correlations in women under 35 years (n = 31, r = 0.38, p = 0.035) and those aged 35-39 years (n =40, r = 0.32, p = 0.044). No significant correlation was observed in women aged 40 or older (n = 35, r = 0.21, p = 0.225).
CONCLUSIONS: In women under 40, increased cfDNA fragmentation in FF was associated with lower morphology-based embryo quality. However, the observed correlations were modest, and the absence of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth outcomes limits clinical interpretation. These exploratory findings do not establish FF cfDNA as a clinically validated predictive biomarker or demonstrate that it improves embryo selection. Larger prospective studies incorporating embryo ploidy and clinically relevant reproductive outcomes are warranted.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes and associated maternal and infection-related factors in a rural malaria-endemic setting in Western Kenya.
articles.authors: Kituyi SN, Odongo AO, Wachuka R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal health during pregnancy is critical for favorable birth outcomes and long-term wellbeing of both mothers and infants. Women in rural, malaria-endemic regions face unique biological and socioeconomic challenges that may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). This study investigated the proportions and determinants of APOs among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Webuye sub-County Hospital in Western Kenya, a rural malaria-endemic setting.
METHODS: A secondary data analysis was conducted utilizing previously collected data of 302 women enrolled at different gestational ages and followed through delivery in a prospective cohort study. Maternal demographic, clinical, and infection-related factors were assessed, and associations with APOs were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Maternal age and gestational age at enrollment were significantly associated with malaria history (P-value <0.001). Maternal anemia (9.9%), abortion (6.3%), preterm birth (4.4%), miscarriage (1.7%), low birth weight (3.4%), stillbirth (7.6 per 1,000 births), neonatal death (3.8 per 1,000 live births) occurred at varying frequencies, indicating a range of adverse outcomes in the study cohort. Younger mothers (<20 years) and older mothers (>35 years) had a higher proportion of anemia (P-value = 0.026) than those aged 21-35 years, and reported malaria history was significantly associated with maternal anemia at enrolment (p-value = 0.02). An additional analysis using microscopy-confirmed malaria status showed a similar difference in hemoglobin levels between microscopy-positive and microscopy-negative participants (p-value < .001). Abnormal urinalysis findings suggestive of urinary tract infection were significantly associated with low birth weight (p-value = 0.031). No significant associations were found between APOs and infant sex, parity, gravidity, or maternal ABO blood type.
DISCUSSION: These findings describe the proportions of the occurrence of adverse outcomes in this rural population and identify maternal age, malaria exposure and abnormal urinalysis results as factors associated with selected outcomes. Strengthening malaria prevention, urinary infection screening, and encouraging early antenatal care attendance are critical to improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. Targeted interventions for adolescent and older mothers, along with enhanced point-of-care diagnostics, may reduce…

articles.title: Pregnancy Risk Information Systems for Psychotropic Medications: A Practical Review for Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.authors: Kim JH, Kim SH
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to summarize pregnancy risk information systems for psychotropic medications and recent evidence on reproductive safety, with the goal of improving clinicians' awareness of drug-specific risk information relevant to individualized clinical decision- making in women with psychiatric disorders of reproductive age.
METHODS: We narratively reviewed official reproductive safety information resources from Australia, Europe, Korea, the United Kingdom, and the United States, together with recent umbrella-review evidence on psychotropic medication safety during pregnancy. Information on selected agents was organized by drug class.
RESULTS: National systems differed in structure and clinical utility. Australia and Korea retain category-based elements, whereas sources from Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States provide more descriptive, context-based information. Antipsychotics were mainly associated with neonatal extrapyramidal or withdrawal symptoms and metabolic risk signals for selected agents. Mood stabilizers and anticonvulsants were more strongly associated with congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders. Benzodiazepines and hypnotics were mainly associated with neonatal sedation, respiratory depression, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and withdrawal symptoms after late-pregnancy or labor exposure. Antidepressants were associated with neonatal adaptation symptoms, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, and postpartum hemorrhage. Recent umbrella-review evidence showed that most reported associations remained at suggestive or weak levels of evidence.
CONCLUSION: Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy should be guided by individualized risk-benefit assessment, integrating drug-specific safety signals, evidence quality, exposure timing, lactation and fertility considerations, and the risks of untreated psychiatric illness.

articles.title: The strategic integration of emergency obstetric and neonatal care with contraceptive services.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Koch M, Kasliwal A, Ahsan A et al.
articles.abstract: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (CEmONC) indicators have strengthened health systems' capacity to manage acute obstetric emergencies and remain central to global maternal health monitoring. However, current EmONC frameworks omit contraception, despite its established role in preventing unintended pregnancy, supporting healthy interpregnancy intervals, and reducing recurrent exposure to obstetric risk. This gap reflects an artificial divide between emergency response and preventive care. This commentary argues that contraception should be recognized as an essential, integrated component of EmONC rather than a separate postpartum service. We outline the clinical rationale for embedding contraceptive counseling and provision within each EmONC signal function, noting that the nature of an obstetric emergency-hemorrhage, infection, hypertensive disease-often directly informs contraceptive eligibility and method selection. We further describe why the postpartum period after an obstetric emergency represents a critical, frequently missed opportunity for contraceptive counseling, particularly in low-resource and humanitarian settings where subsequent access to care is uncertain. We propose practical strategies for integration at the facility, health system, and global levels, including standardized counseling prompts, aligned supply chains, updated training curricula, and incorporation of contraceptive indicators into EmONC guidance and monitoring tools. Embedding contraception within EmONC would strengthen continuity across the maternal health continuum and better align global frameworks with the clinical realities of obstetric risk.

articles.title: Examining Implementation Barriers Among Community Champions Towards Improving Maternal and Child Health Outcomes Under the Uturo Model in Mbeya Region, Tanzania.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Mpambije CJ, Manyerere DJ, Myeya HE
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3.1 targets reducing the maternal mortality ratio to 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030. Developing countries have intensified diverse strategies to realise the target. Community mobilisation to improve maternal and child health (MCH) is part of these strategies. In Tanzania, diverse community-based initiatives have been introduced, including the Uturo model, introduced in Mbeya region in 2000 and implemented by community champions. While the model has recorded impressive MCH outcomes, the barriers community champions face during implementation remain underexplored. This study therefore aims to highlight the barriers community champions encounter when implementing the Uturo model in Tanzania.
METHODS: This study used a qualitative case study design to explore the barriers community champions encountered while implementing the Uturo model. The study used purposive sampling to select 81 participants. Primary data were collected through individual interviews and focus group discussions with leaders, community health workers, local leaders, healthcare workers, and the council health management team. A document review complemented these tools, and the data were subjected to thematic analysis.
FINDINGS: The findings revealed that community champions played a significant role in improving MCH under the Uturo model since its inception in 2000. However, champions face several barriers that threaten the model's effective performance, including a lack of incentives, impassable roads, insufficient training, and limited professionalism. The potential of community champions to deliver quality MCH services is further limited by political interference and entrenched cultural practices, coupled with shortages of healthcare workers.
CONCLUSION: The success of the Uturo model hinges on motivated and dedicated community champions as frontline facilitators of MCH service delivery. However, structural, community, and health system hurdles undermine their potential to improve MCH services. Moreover, these barriers affect their performance and threaten the model's sustainability and scalability. To advance progress towards SDG 3.1 by 2030, Tanzania should formally recognise and support community champions through appropriate financial and non-financial incentives, such as stipends or allowances, transport facilitation, and regular training, while maintaining the community participation that underpins the Uturo model.

articles.title: A Gap on Judgment of Fertility and the Need for Contraception Between Physicians and Patients With Rheumatic Diseases: A Multicenter Questionnaire Survey.
articles.authors: Moriyama M, Murakawa Y, Nagafuchi H et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Effective contraception is essential for women of reproductive age with rheumatic disease (RD), specifically those receiving teratogenic drugs, and physicians should recognize that these women may wish to conceive or control their fertility. This study aimed to evaluate the status of preconception care and contraception use, awareness, and counseling among women with RD in Japan.
METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire survey included Japanese women with RD (age: 18-45 years) and their attending physicians, conducted between September 2023 and May 2024 at 14 medical institutions. Patient and physician responses were linked and analyzed.
RESULTS: In total, 157 patients completed the survey. Of these, 35% of patients wished to conceive in the future and 38% were aware of their current need for contraception. The results revealed a gap between physicians' and patients' judgment of fertility and the need for contraception. Most patients used less effective contraceptive methods (condoms: 67.1%; withdrawal: 20.5%). Although patients were aware of the need for contraception, only 12% had received specific contraception instructions from their healthcare providers, whereas 39% had never received contraception counseling. Most of the patients decided on contraceptive methods themselves or together with their partners. One patient who tested positive for antiphospholipid antibodies used contraindicated estrogen-containing contraceptives.
CONCLUSION: Significant deficiencies exist in contraception counseling and awareness among women with RD. Proactive and system-building approaches are urgently required to improve preconception care and reproductive safety in this population.

articles.title: Genetic Counseling When One Partner Carries a CF-Causing Variant and the Other Has the Intronic IVS8-5T Variant.
articles.authors: Massie J, Archibald AD, Smith M et al.
articles.abstract: Complex genetic counseling situations can arise when whole-gene sequencing is used as part of reproductive genetic carrier screening or newborn screening for cystic fibrosis (CF). One of the most common scenarios is when one reproductive partner carries a CF-causing variant such as c.1521-1523del (or p.F508del) and the other partner carries the c.1210-12T[5] (or IVS8-5T) variant. Questions arise as to what information to provide about the likely outcome if the fetus or newborn has both variants in trans, as well as implications for future pregnancies and other family members. In this paper, we consider an approach to genetic counseling based on knowledge of CFTR biology and available clinical data.

articles.title: Investigating the association between blood lipid profiles and insulin resistance and β-cell function indices in pregnant women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Feng J, Xu X, Tian Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the associations between first-trimester lipid markers and second-trimester insulin resistance (IR) and pancreatic β-cell function (BCF) indices in pregnant women. An exploratory aim was to explore the apparent discrimination of lipid markers for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity.
METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis used prospectively collected cohort data from 1202 pregnant women in Beijing, China. Lipids were measured at 4-8 weeks of gestation, and a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test was performed at 24-28 weeks. The Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR) and the Matsuda index were analyzed as continuous measures of IR and insulin sensitivity. BCF was assessed using surrogate indices: the Homeostatic Model Assessment of β-cell function (HOMA-β) and the 60-min insulinogenic index (IGI60). Linear-regression models adjusted for age and early-pregnancy body mass index examined the associations between each lipid marker and continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index as the primary analyses and with HOMA-β and IGI60 as the secondary analyses. Binary logistic-regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses of cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity were exploratory.
RESULTS: After adjustment for age and early-pregnancy body mass index, all seven lipid markers were significantly associated with continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index (all nominal P < 0.05). No statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate β-cell-function indices HOMA-β or IGI60. In the exploratory analyses, the lipid markers were associated with the cohort-defined low-Matsuda category. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol had the highest observed area under the curve in the total population (0.723; 95% confidence interval 0.689-0.756). The exploratory cutoff selected by maximizing Youden's index was 0.65, with a sensitivity of 74.1% and a specificity of 62.5%.
CONCLUSION: First-trimester lipid markers were associated with second-trimester IR and insulin-sensitivity indices, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate BCF indices used in this study. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed moderate apparent discrimination for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity and should be considered a hypothesis-generating candidate marker requiring external validation.

articles.title: Clustering of Maternal and Perinatal Complications Following Fresh and Frozen Embryo Transfer in First-Time Mothers: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Landsverk E, Opdahl S, Bergh C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess how often women who give birth following frozen-thawed embryo transfer (frozen-ET), fresh embryo transfer (fresh-ET) and natural conception (NC) have pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications, develop a single complication, or experience multiple complications.
DESIGN: A population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Denmark (2008-2014), Norway (2008-2015) and Sweden (2008-2015).
POPULATION: Restricted to singleton pregnancies among first-time mothers, this study included 6634 deliveries after frozen-ET, 25 660 after fresh-ET and 523 277 after NC.
METHODS: The following complications were studied: stillbirth, neonatal death (0-27 days after delivery), preterm birth (gestational age < 37 weeks), small for gestational age or large for gestational age (birthweight < -22% or > +22% from the expected birthweight according to sex and gestational age), low birthweight (< 2500 g), macrosomia (≥ 4500 g), Apgar score < 5 at 5 min, major birth defects, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, placenta previa and placental abruption.
RESULTS: In first-time mothers, three of every four singleton pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET were without maternal and perinatal complications, compared to four of every five pregnancies after NC. In pregnancies with neonatal survival ≥ 28 days (99.3% after frozen-ET, 99.3% after fresh-ET, and 99.5% after NC), two or more complications affected one in 11 pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET, compared to one in 16 after NC.
