CONCLUSION: In this study, we observed that most first-time mothers experienced pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications following ART, and when complications occurred, they were typically without additional complications. Although single and multiple complications were more common following ART than after NC, the absolute differences were small. These findings may help set realistic expectations when counselling people who consider ART treatment, or those already in treatment.

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Muscle Reactivity Measured Using M-Mode Ultrasonography in Males With Post-Prostatectomy Incontinence.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
articles.authors: Ide Y, Shimizu N, Hyohdoh Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize changes in M-mode measures of bladder base movement during supervised pelvic floor rehabilitation and their associations with urinary incontinence severity.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 69 males with urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy who received supervised pelvic floor muscle training with ultrasound biofeedback. Within-participant changes, correlations, and regression analyses were performed. Firth logistic regression for continence included age, baseline pad weight, time from surgery to training, and baseline elevation time.
RESULTS: Median pad weight decreased from 247 (interquartile range, 64-684) to 40 (0-195) g/day, and elevation time shortened from 0.31 (0.24-0.45) to 0.20 (0.18-0.23) s (both p < 0.001; r = 0.83). Elevation speed increased (p < 0.001; r = 0.68), whereas elevation length did not change (p = 0.972; r = 0.00). Continence was achieved by 26 participants (37.7%). Pad weight correlated with elevation time at baseline (Spearman's ρ = 0.348; p = 0.003) and final assessment (Spearman's ρ = 0.417; p < 0.001). No statistically significant association was detected between baseline elevation time and continence in the main Firth model (adjusted odds ratio per 0.1-s increase, 0.954; 95% confidence interval, 0.633-1.349; p = 0.797).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower pad weight, shorter elevation time, and greater elevation speed co-occurred during supervised rehabilitation. Elevation time was associated with incontinence severity cross-sectionally. No statistically significant association was detected between baseline elevation time and continence in the main Firth model. Prospective validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Pre-eclampsia screening and prevention: Implementing FIGO guidelines in a Thai population.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Sophark I, Suksai M, Geater A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world implementation, screening performance, aspirin uptake, and safety of a FIGO (the International Federation of Gynecology & Obstetrics)-based first-trimester pre-eclampsia screening and prevention program.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women initiating antenatal care before 14 weeks of gestation at a tertiary referral center in southern Thailand from 2021 to 2024. Screening incorporated maternal factors, mean arterial pressure, and uterine artery pulsatility index. Women with a calculated risk of 1:100 or greater were classified as being at high risk and offered aspirin 162 mg nightly. Outcomes included screening coverage, detection rates, aspirin uptake, pregnancy outcomes, and bleeding complications.
RESULTS: Among 1713 pregnancies, 71 developed pre-eclampsia (4.1%), including 49 with severe features. Overall, 1106 women were screened (64.6%), but coverage reached 93.6% by the end of implementation. The screen-positive rate was 11.3%. Detection rates were 61.7% for overall pre-eclampsia, 69.6% for delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, 87.5% for delivery before 34 weeks of gestation, and 100% for delivery before 32 weeks of gestation, with false-positive rates of approximately 9%-11%. Aspirin uptake among screen-positive women was 99.2%. Pre-eclampsia was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery, preterm birth, lower birth weight, and neonatal intensive care unit admission. No eclampsia, placental abruption, maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal death, stillbirth, or neonatal death occurred. After adjustment for potential confounders, aspirin was not associated with the risk of an estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and the risk of an estimated blood loss of 1000 mL or more did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: FIGO-based first-trimester screening was feasible in routine care, with increasing coverage as implementation matured, near-universal aspirin uptake, and clinically useful detection of preterm pre-eclampsia. Aspirin use was not significantly associated with severe bleeding.

articles.title: HPV prevalence and risk factors in a population-based cervical cancer screening program in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
articles.authors: Turabova NR, Akhmedova LM, Akhmedova SK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-based evidence on high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) and cervical screening outcomes in Uzbekistan is limited. We assessed hrHPV prevalence, district variation, associated factors, and cytological findings in Tashkent.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 52,995 women aged 18-70 years attending routine cervical screening across Tashkent city during 2024-2025. HR-HPV testing was performed using real-time PCR; reflex liquid-based cytology was performed for all HPV-positive women. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent determinants of HPV positivity (n = 52,995) and cytological abnormality (n = 2,255 HPV-positive women with adequate cytology).
RESULTS: Overall HR-HPV positivity was 4.43% (95% CI: 4.26-4.61%), with significant heterogeneity across districts (p < 0.01); Bektemir district recorded the highest prevalence. Independent predictors of HPV positivity included older age (aOR 2.41, 95% CI 1.24-4.83, for 56-70 years), irregular menstruation (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.23-1.57), and early sexual debut, while barrier contraception (aOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.81) and grand multiparity (aOR 0.80, 95% CI 0.65-0.98) were protective. Among HPV-positive women, any cytological abnormality was detected in 24.6% and high-grade lesions in 17.3%. Keratosis was the strongest predictor of cytological abnormality (aOR 4.09-5.16, both p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: This large population-based study establishes a comprehensive HPV epidemiological baseline for Tashkent and demonstrates the clinical yield of HPV-primary screening with reflexive cytology triage. District-level heterogeneity and identified risk profiles provide evidence for geographically targeted program optimization in support of Uzbekistan's progress toward WHO 90-70-90 cervical cancer elimination targets.

articles.title: Age Redistribution and Demographic Contributors to Pelvic Organ Prolapse Disability Across Asia, 1990-2023: An Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Zhang W, Yang X, Zhu W
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine how the age distribution of pelvic organ prolapse-related disability changed across Asia and quantify the demographic contributors to changes in absolute disability burden.
METHODS: We analyzed Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for genital prolapse in five Asian regions and 34 countries and territories for 1990-2023. We assessed all-age years lived with disability and age-standardized rates. Age-specific rates and shares were examined among women aged 20 years or older using 5-year age groups and a final group aged 95 years or older. We decomposed adult burden changes into population growth, population aging, and age-specific rate change.
RESULTS: Counts increased in all five regions despite declining age-standardized rates. The age group with the largest disability share shifted from 65-69 to 70-74 years in High-income Asia Pacific and from 45-49 to 50-54 years in South Asia, but remained at 55-59 years in East Asia. Shares increased in all age groups aged 70 years or older in East Asia and High-income Asia Pacific. Population growth was the larger demographic contributor in South Asia, contributing 103.63% of the 1990 adult burden. Population aging contributed more than population growth in East Asia and High-income Asia Pacific, equivalent to 86.09% and 64.04% of their 1990 adult burdens.
CONCLUSIONS: Age redistribution differed across Asia. The age distribution of disability shifted toward older women in East Asia and High-income Asia Pacific, while middle adulthood remained prominent in South Asia. These patterns can inform pelvic floor care planning.

articles.title: Association Between Timing of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Diagnosis and Perinatal Outcomes: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Hasegawa T, Nakamura E, Sato S et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the association between the timing of gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosis and perinatal outcomes, including large-for-gestational-age birth, neonatal hypoglycemia, and postpartum dysglycemia.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included women with gestational diabetes mellitus who delivered at Saitama Medical Center between April 2020 and March 2023. Women were classified according to the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus before or at or after 24 gestational weeks. The primary outcome was large-for-gestational-age birth. Associations were evaluated in the overall cohort and after propensity score matching using infertility treatment, family history of diabetes, nulliparity, and pre-pregnancy body mass index.
RESULTS: Among 228 women, 97 were classified into the early diagnosis group and 131 into the late diagnosis group. The incidence of large-for-gestational-age birth was significantly lower in the early diagnosis group than in the late diagnosis group (13.4% [13/97] vs. 29.0% [38/131], p = 0.008). In the propensity score-matched cohort (92 pairs), this association remained significant (10.9% [10/92] vs. 28.3% [26/92], p = 0.005). Neonatal hypoglycemia and postpartum dysglycemia did not differ significantly between the groups after matching (p = 0.730 and p = 0.711, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed at or after 24 gestational weeks was associated with a higher incidence of large-for-gestational-age birth, whereas neonatal hypoglycemia and postpartum dysglycemia did not differ according to the timing of diagnosis.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection in Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province, China, 2021-2025.
articles.authors: Chen X, Cui D, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province of China, and to provide localized epidemiological data for the prevention and treatment of cervical cancer and related diseases.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on HPV genotyping data from 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital from 2021 to 2025. Overall infection rate, genotype distribution, age-specific positivity, and longitudinal trends were evaluated.
RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 18.57% (9,336/50,279), increasing from 15.30% in 2021 to a peak of 21.18% in 2023 but adjusting to 19.84% by 2025. Single infections were the predominant infection pattern (75.83%, 7,080/9,336). Age-specific prevalence exhibited a bimodal distribution, with the first peak in the ≤ 25 years group (23.56%, 810/3,438) and a second peak in the ≥ 56 years group (1,017/3,904, 26.05%). The five most prevalent genotypes were HPV52 (1,822/50,279, 3.62%), HPV16 (3.01%, 1514/50,279), HPV58 (2.46%, 1,239/50,279), HPV53 (1.97%, 989/50,279), and HPV39 (1.72%, 864/50,279), while HPV81 (1.70%, 856/50,279) were the most prevalent LR HPV genotypes. Annual analysis revealed HPV53 prevalence increasing significantly from 1.51% in 2021 to 2.72% in 2025 (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This study provides the largest-scale data on the recent epidemiological characteristics of HPV infection in Lianyungang, China, which will guide the development of local cervical cancer prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: Prevalance and factors associated with cervical cancer screening uptake among HIV positive women in the rural communities of Alebtong district in Uganda.
articles.authors: Atepo S, Iramiot JS, Wanume B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) is the leading gynaecologic malignancy in Uganda and affects about 6959 women and 4607 die annually. Despite the launch of the global call to elimination of CC in 2020, only 10% of women in Uganda are screened and studies in Uganda among women of reproductive age group(WRAG) living with Human Immune virus (HIV) [(WRAG-LHIV)] have reported rates of 30.3% to 39.4%. Subsequently 85% patients with CC present with advanced disease leading to poor outcomes. Furthermore, women living with (HIV) have a six-fold higher risk of developing CC compared to their HIV negative counterparts. Alebtong district in Northern Uganda is reported to have a higher HIV prevalence than the national average and CCS uptake among women of reproductive age group living with HIV (WRAG-LHIV) is unknown. Therefore this study aimed to determine the prevalence of CCS uptake and its determinants among WRAG-LHIV in Alebtong district.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at 7 purposively selected high volume antiretroviral therapy (ART) offering health facilities and their attached 34 community drug distribution points (CDDPs). 381 WRAG-LHIV were recruited by systematic sampling. Researcher administered pretested closed-ended questionnaires were used to collect quantitative data. The data was entered into Microsoft Excel and subsequently imported into Stata version 14 for statistical analysis. Statistical significance was set at a p-value < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 381 women with a mean age of 32.9 years (SD ± 7) participated in the study. The majority, 80.8% (308/381) had had at most primary education, 81.4% were either married/cohabiting and 53.3% (203/381) resided within 5 km of a health facility. Importantly, 53.5%( 204/381) had had early sexual debut and 81.6%( 311/381) were multiparous. The prevalence of cervical cancer screening (CCS) uptake was 49.6% (189/381). The statistically significant factors associated with CCS uptake were encouragement by friends and family members, spouse support, good knowledge about cervical cancer screening, and preference of male healthcare providers, literacy and distance of ≤ 5km.
CONCLUSION: CCS uptake among WRAG-LHIV was suboptimal and below the 70% target set for CC elimination. There is need for more emphasis on male involvement in terms of spouses and clinical team, peer advocacy integration of CCS into chronic care clinics and adopting modalities that would encourage community participation and males in…

articles.title: Transperineal strain elastography for evaluating periurethral biomechanics in women with stress urinary incontinence: a diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.authors: Shahbazkhani AH, Shakki Katouli F, Torabi S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) commonly reflects loss of urethral support and altered periurethral biomechanics. Strain elastography (SE) can quantify tissue deformation; however, its clinical diagnostic value for SUI is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate periurethral strain elastography in women with and without SUI and to compare its diagnostic performance with established kinematic ultrasound parameters.
METHODS: In a prospective case-control study, 43 premenopausal women (23 SUI, 20 controls) underwent standardized transperineal B-mode ultrasound and strain elastography. Four periurethral ROIs-posterior-mid (A1), anterior-mid (A2; prespecified primary outcome), posterior-upper (A3), and anterior-upper (A4)-were sampled at rest and during Valsalva. Kinematic measures (bladder-neck descent [BND], retrovesical angle [RVA]) were recorded. Analyses used parametric or nonparametric tests as appropriate, Cohen's d effect sizes, bootstrap 95% CIs (2,000 replicates), ROC curves, and exploratory logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and BMI. At rest, strain ratios (SRs) did not differ. During Valsalva maneuver, however, controls demonstrated significantly higher strain ratios than SUI cases in all four regions, including posterior-mid (A1; p = 0.006), anterior-mid (A2; p = 0.003), posterior-upper (A3; p = 0.037), and anterior-upper (A4; p = 0.004), demonstrating consistently higher relative periurethral strain-ratio values in controls during Valsalva. Despite statistically significant mean differences, SR variables showed poor raw discriminatory performance on ROC analysis (AUC range 0.248-0.336), reflecting an unexpected direction of discrimination (controls having higher, "stiffer," SR values than cases). In contrast, kinematic parameters demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy: RVA during Valsalva yielded an AUC of 0.953 (95% CI, 0.878-1.000), and BND yielded an AUC of 0.896 (95% CI, 0.785-0.993). In this sample, multivariable regression did not demonstrate a statistically significant incremental diagnostic benefit from SE beyond kinematic measures; however, the modest sample size and lack of internal validation limit the certainty of this finding.
CONCLUSIONS: Transperineal SE detected group-level differences in relative periurethral deformation during Valsalva, but strain-ratio measures showed poor standalone diagnostic performance. In this sample, SE did not demonstrate improved discrimination beyond conventional…

articles.title: The hidden burden of insomnia in late pregnancy: prevalence and risk factors among Egyptian women.
articles.authors: Essa A, Ebeid I, Noureldeen IM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep condition that has a harmful impact on one's quality of life and presents considerable health hazards, especially for pregnant women in their third trimester. It can lead to stress, postpartum depression and negative fetal outcomes. The prevalence and contributing variables of insomnia among pregnant women in Egypt have not been adequately studied. This study evaluated the prevalence of insomnia among third trimester pregnant women in Egypt and analyzed the associated risk factors.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This is a cross-sectional study of pregnant women in the third trimester at Menoufia University Hospital. The study included 390 participants. The study employed a pre-structured questionnaire that includes questions about sociodemographic and lifestyle attributes, accompanied by the ISI questionnaire used to diagnose and assess insomnia severity.
RESULTS: A total of 390 pregnant women in the third trimester completed the questionnaire. The prevalence of insomnia was 75.4% (n = 294), with 33.1% categorized as sub-threshold, 26.2% as moderate, and 16.2% as severe. Multivariate logistic regression identified maternal age 25-35 years (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 2.50-8.36) and age > 35 years (AOR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.01-9.70) as significant risk factors. Conversely, university education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11-0.61), overweight BMI (AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.16-0.62), and rural residence (AOR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.30-0.95) were significant protective factors. Linear regression further confirmed that higher insomnia severity scores were predicted by increased maternal age, while overweight BMI (B = -3.10), rural residence (B = -1.98), and nulliparity (B = -3.69) were significant negative predictors of severity (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Insomnia is highly prevalent among pregnant women, particularly in the third trimester. Advanced maternal age and urban residence were associated with a higher risk and severity of insomnia, while higher education and nulliparity appear protective. Further research is needed to develop strategies to improve maternal well-being and reduce adverse outcomes for mothers and infants.

articles.title: Assessing prevalence, risk factors, and the association between trichomonas vaginalis and urine glucose and albumin in pregnant women at Bamenda III, Cameroon.
articles.authors: Abongwa LE, Nakuh NM, Berinyu NS et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Trichomoniasis in pregnancy is associated with poor reproductive outcomes, including pelvic inflammatory disease, preterm delivery, and low birth weight. Urine albumin and sugar in pregnancy are major complications that might arise during pregnancy and are a cause for concern. This study aims to assess the prevalence and risk factors of Trichomonas vaginalis among pregnant women and their impact on urine glucose and albumin.
METHODOLOGY: The study was a cross-sectional study involving pregnant women at first antenatal visits from March to May 2024. A total of 200 pregnant women were recruited for the study. Vaginal swab samples were collected for the identification of Trichomonas vaginalis. Risk factors were identified using a closed-ended questionnaire, and the presence of albumin and glucose was identified using dipstick test strips.
RESULT: A total of 200 participants were recruited; the age ranges from 18 to 35 years, with a mean of 26.4± (4.5) years. The overall prevalence of T. vaginalis was 6.5% (13). The prevalence of urine albumin was insignificantly (p = 0.37) low 0 (0.0%) among those who were positive for T. vaginalis. Urine glucose was significantly higher (p = 0.001) in women who had trichomoniasis 10 (71.4%). Our data showed that women who had more than one sex partner [20.0%, Adjusted Odds Ratio (AOR) 0.158 (0.031-0.796); p = 0.025] and women with a previous history of STI [10.2%, AOR 5.261(1.282-21.585); p = 0.021] were at higher risk of acquiring T. vaginalis infection.
CONCLUSION: The high frequency of trichomoniasis requires that this test be made a routine test for pregnant women. The results report for the first time that glucose was high in pregnant women who were positive for trichomoniasis, thereby showing a need for further research considering the effects of gestational diabetes.

articles.title: Melon fruit microbiomes resemble aerial-tissue communities in a Turpan oasis field.
articles.authors: Zhou D, Sun X, Ni G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fruit-associated communities encounter belowground and aerial habitats, yet their position within the whole-plant microbiome remains unclear in field-grown melon. We profiled bacterial 16S rRNA gene and fungal internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS1) amplicons from rhizosphere soil and surface-disinfected roots, stems, leaves and fruits. Four cultivars were sampled at fruit set and maturity in a randomised-block Turpan oasis field.
RESULTS: Compartment was the strongest correlate of bacterial and fungal community structure. After nine melon-derived fungal operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were removed, the primary fungal analysis retained 805 OTUs across 152 samples. Compartment explained 28.6-46.8% of bacterial variation and 31.5-34.2% of fungal variation across Bray-Curtis and Aitchison distances; stage and compartment-by-stage terms were also supported. Primary whole-plot tests detected modest cultivar-associated variation under both distances, although the fungal Bray-Curtis result did not persist in the complete 120-sample sensitivity analysis, with a Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P value (q) of 0.167. Significant dispersion tests qualified several community-level effects. Fruit communities were closer to stems and leaves than to rhizosphere soil or roots. All four kingdom-by-distance fruit microbiome continuity scores exceeded their restricted null expectations, with one-sided P = q = 1/10,001. The dual-method screen identified 197 bacterial and 44 fungal stage-associated OTU-compartment associations. Seventeen bacterial OTUs met the abundance-occupancy criteria, whereas no fungal OTU met both thresholds. Whole-community composition was not significantly associated with the first principal component of fruit chemistry (PC1).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-season field survey, melon fruit communities more closely resembled those of aerial tissues than those of belowground compartments. This pattern was consistent across kingdoms and distance measures, but it does not identify a source or route of microbial movement. The recurrent bacterial candidates and the absence of fungal OTUs meeting both recurrence thresholds provide focused targets for culture-based, localisation and strain-tracking experiments.

articles.title: Exploring unmet needs and family planning among women with a history of preeclampsia: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Ceasar RC, Charles L, Guglielmo J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy associated with significant morbidity and mortality in both the mother and baby. Moreover, women with a history of PE are at markedly increased risk of recurrence. Thus, these women and their families face difficult family planning decisions, often with few resources to aid them in making their decision.
PURPOSE: We aimed to identify the unmet needs of women with a history of PE, with a focus on decision-making surrounding family planning.
METHODS: We conducted four virtual focus groups with 25 women between February 21, 2024 and March 20, 2024. We recruited potential participants from the "End Preeclampsia" website and newsletter in January 2024. To be eligible, potential participants needed to be at least 18 years old at the time of participation, have a history of PE, and report ever considering another pregnancy. Using rapid qualitative analysis methods, we analyzed the contexts and perspectives that contributed to women's lived experiences, particularly surrounding their family planning decision-making.
RESULTS: Four key themes emerged among women we interviewed. Participants reported 1) A lack of knowledge and awareness of PE prior to their diagnosis in past pregnancies; 2). Limited access to quality healthcare, consequently causing a delay in diagnosis and treatment; 3) A lack of emotional, informational, and provider support through their PE journey; and 4) having anxiety about future pregnancies due to the risk of PE recurrence. Altogether these themes heavily impacted participants' decisions on future family planning, resulting in delayed subsequent pregnancy or foregoing pregnancy altogether.
CONCLUSIONS: Women with a history of PE have substantial unmet needs, including a need for more prenatal education from clinicians, increased emotional support from family, friends and support groups, and a lack of available PE information and counseling to assist them in future family planning decisions.

articles.title: Cumulative risk factor burden and stillbirth: insights from real-world data.
articles.authors: Eskeland MS, Räisänen S, Owe KM et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop a stillbirth risk index based on cumulative burden of pre-pregnancy and early-pregnancy risk factors, to assist clinicians in planning antenatal care.
METHODS: This population-based cohort study used data from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway and Statistics Norway from 1999 to 2022. All individuals with singleton pregnancies in Norway who gave birth from gestational age ≥ 22 weeks were included, resulting in a study population of 1 350 936 births. Fifteen pre-pregnancy and early-pregnancy characteristics associated with ≥ 25% higher stillbirth rate compared to the total study population and with odds ratios ≥ 1.5 were included in the risk index. These were: Maternal age ≥35 years, maternal country of birth in South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa or unknown, education (none or compulsory or unknown), not being married/cohabitating, chronic hypertension, type 1 or 2 diabetes, parity ≥4, previous stillbirth, previous second trimester loss, daily smoking in first trimester, and lack of folic acid use during pregnancy.
RESULTS: There were 4941 (0.37%) stillbirths registered. Stillbirth rates increased with cumulative risk factor burden from 2.08 per 1000 births in individuals with none of the chosen risk factors to 13.61 in individuals with risk score ≥ 5. Odds ratios increased parallel from 1.58 (95% confidence interval 1.46-1.71) in individuals with risk score 1 to 6.62 (95% CI 5.62-7.78) in individuals with risk score ≥ 5. These patterns were consistent across two subperiods (1999-2010 and 2011-2022).
CONCLUSION: Cumulative burden of pre-pregnancy and early‑pregnancy risk factors can stratify individuals into meaningful risk groups, supporting tailored antenatal care.

articles.title: Multiple Chemical Class-Based Potent VEGFR2 Inhibitors as Anticancer Therapeutics: Structure-Activity Relationship and Chemicobiological Interactions Studies.
articles.authors: Bhagat RP, Samanta A, Maji A et al.
articles.abstract: Angiogenesis regulation is associated with disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, atherosclerosis, and cancer. Tumor development and metastasis are directly affected by tumor angiogenesis. In addition to tumor cells, host cells produce pro- and anti-angiogenic molecules that regulate tumor angiogenesis. VEGFs and their receptor, VEGFR2 (KDR), strongly influence angiogenesis. When activated, KDR undergoes autophosphorylation, which ultimately promotes endothelial cell proliferation, tumor angiogenesis, tumor growth, and metastasis. Overexpression of VEGFR2 has been observed in various cancer types, including hepatocellular carcinoma, renal carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, breast cancer, and cervical cancer. Researchers have developed several VEGFR2 inhibitors over the past few decades. This review examines the structure-activity relationships (SARs) of several recently developed chemical classes, including chalcones, quinazolines, pyridines, pyrimidines, thiadiazoles, indazoles, triazoles, quinoxalines, and pyrazoles, as VEGFR2 inhibitors, with an emphasis on anticancer activity. We also analyze the chemico-biological interaction profiles of several small-molecule VEGFR2 inhibitors. This review article provides an overview of the latest advances in medicinal chemistry approaches to VEGFR2 inhibitors.

articles.title: Association between polycystic ovary syndrome and asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Sini K, Bloom CI, Lee B
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is common in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and several plausible shared mechanisms may link the conditions, including metabolic dysfunction, systemic inflammation and hormonal pathways. We conducted a systematic review to synthesise the evidence, quantify any association, assess lung function data and identify gaps for future studies.
METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science Core Collection in April 2026. We included observational studies reporting asthma prevalence or lung function in women with PCOS. Crude and adjusted effect estimates were pooled separately using random-effects model meta-analyses. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2 statistics. Quality assessment was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools.
RESULTS: 13 studies (including over 28 million women, 11 cross-sectional and 2 longitudinal) were included. Of these, eight were assessed as moderate or high risk of bias. Meta-analyses showed that PCOS was associated with a higher odds of asthma in both crude (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.44 to 1.76, I²=72.0%, τ²=0.009) and adjusted analyses (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.40 to 1.77, I²=90.6%, τ²=0.007). The associations were not substantially different by PCOS or asthma ascertainment method. Only two lung function studies showed conflicting results.
CONCLUSIONS: PCOS appeared to be associated with asthma but this was driven by findings from cross-sectional studies which are at risk of reverse causation. Lung function evidence remains inconclusive. Future studies should prioritise standardised methods and longitudinal designs to establish temporality.

articles.title: Study of 34 prospective pregnancies in women receiving IL-1 inhibitors for autoinflammatory diseases and comparison to unexposed pregnancies (GR2 study).
articles.authors: M D, L S, V S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitors are widely used in autoinflammatory diseases (AID) such as Still’s disease and monogenic inflammasomopathies, including cryopyrinopathies (CAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever. As these conditions frequently affect women of reproductive age and data are limited, concerns remain regarding anti-IL-1 therapy safety during pregnancy. We aimed to evaluate maternal and neonatal outcomes in women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception and pregnancy.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included pregnant women from the Groupe de recherche sur la Grossesse et les Maladies Rares (GR2) prospective cohort, spanning 76 French centres before September 2024. Women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception or pregnancy were selected. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes were compared with a 1:1 matched control group of unexposed women with similar conditions and with the nationwide 2021 French National Perinatal Survey.
RESULTS: Thirty-four pregnancies (three twin pregnancies) in 31 women were exposed to anakinra (n=30) and/or canakinumab (n=5) for Still’s disease (n=15), familial Mediterranean fever (n=15), CAPS (n=3), undifferentiated systemic AID (n=2), tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome and recurrent pericarditis (n=1 each). Reported outcomes included infections (n=6), intrahepatic cholestasis (n=3), gestational diabetes (n=2), gestational hypertension (n=1) and intrauterine growth restriction (n=1). Median gestational age was 39 weeks with five preterm births between 32 and 37. One baby was diagnosed with laryngomalacia but did not require surgery. Paediatric follow-up (33 babies to 6 months, 30 thereafter for a median of 14.5 months (13–24)) confirmed normal infant development. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes did not differ between treated with anti-IL-1 and untreated with anti-IL-1 patients with AID.
CONCLUSION: Anti-IL-1 therapy, particularly anakinra, appears safe during pregnancy in women with systemic AID.

articles.title: Trauma in Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
articles.authors: Friend L, Saab M
articles.abstract: Trauma is the leading cause of death in reproductive-aged individuals, complicating 6% to 8% of pregnancies and accounting for approximately 20% of maternal deaths. This article reviews a maternal-first resuscitation approach, emphasizing that fetal survival hinges on maternal stabilization. It details pregnancy-specific alterations affecting the primary survey including difficult airway, respiratory compensation, aortocaval compression, and delayed recognition of hemorrhagic shock. It also provides guidance on blood product resuscitation, RhD considerations, TXA, and resuscitative hysterotomy. Diagnostic evaluation covers imaging recommendations and laboratory nuances. Finally, it addresses mechanism-specific injuries, intimate partner violence, fetal monitoring, patient counseling, and criteria for discharge.

articles.title: FDG PET/CT in Gynecologic Malignancies.
articles.journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
articles.ta: Magn Reson Imaging Clin N Am
articles.authors: Aslaner K, Ozkan ZG, Akin EA
articles.abstract: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT has become an essential complementary modality in the management of gynecologic malignancies, combining metabolic and anatomic information beyond the morphologic limitations of CT and MRI. This review examines its clinical roles and diagnostic limitations across cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vulvar, and vaginal cancers, focusing on nodal staging, recurrence detection, treatment response assessment, and prognostication. Its distinct strengths-nodal staging in cervical cancer and recurrence detection in endometrial and ovarian cancers-are highlighted alongside key interpretive pitfalls. Emerging approaches, including PET/MRI, volumetric parameters, FAPI and other novel radiopharmaceuticals, and radiomics, are discussed as future directions in gynecologic oncology.

articles.title: Risk factors for antepartum venous thromboembolism in pregnant people with sickle cell disease.
articles.authors: Gerber GF, Choupa S, Luo A et al.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a thrombophilia exacerbated by pregnancy. However, there is not strong evidence for thromboprophylaxis, perhaps because most data addressing pregnancy-related thrombosis in SCD is limited by derivation from administrative datasets. We studied venous thromboembolism (VTE) in a retrospective cohort of pregnant people with SCD who delivered singleton pregnancies at two academic centres between 1990 and 2021. Among 289 pregnancies to 197 SCD subjects, 6% had VTE. We compared characteristics of the first study pregnancy in which a VTE occurred (cases) to the first study pregnancy in subjects without pregnancy-related VTE (controls). Preconception complications associated with VTE were history of VTE (cases: 33% [n = 5/15] vs. controls: 4% [n = 7/182], p < 0.001), acute chest syndrome (ACS) (80% [n = 12/15] vs. 37% [n = 68/182], p = 0.001) and acute care for vaso-occlusive crisis (VOC) in the year before pregnancy (80% [n = 12/15] vs. 43% [n = 70/182], p = 0.006). Prenatal complications associated with VTE were ACS (47% [n = 7/15] vs. 10% [n = 19/182], p < 0.001) and VOC (93% [n = 14/15] vs. 65% [n = 119/182], p = 0.026). Fetal outcomes associated with VTE included gestational age at delivery (median [IQR] 37.0 [34.0-38.1] weeks vs. 38.3 [36.9-39.3], p = 0.004). Studies are needed to establish interventions that attenuate VTE risk and define prophylactic anti-coagulation parameters for this high-risk population.

articles.title: Jaeumganghwa-tang, a Korean National Health Insurance herbal extract, ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome related ovarian dysfunction with reduced apoptotic stress and improved FSH-responsive steroidogenesis.
articles.authors: Kwon S, Choi Y, So S et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) still remains understudied in the face of 8-13% prevalence in reproductive women. This study investigated the effects of Jaeumganghwa-tang (JGT), a Korean National Health Insurance herbal extract, on PCOS-related ovarian dysfunction and associated changes in apoptosis and FSH-responsive steroidogenesis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology identified overlapping targets between JGT and PCOS, followed by comprehensive functional enrichment analysis. Letrozole-induced PCOS rats received oral JGT (0.3, 0.6, 1.2 g/kg) for 4 weeks. Ovarian morphology, estrous cyclicity, apoptosis, ovarian hormone-responsive and steroidogenic markers, and circulating LH, FSH, and testosterone were assessed. CdCl2-exposed KGN cells were used for analyzing mitochondrial integrity with JC-10 and ATP, and FSH-induced cAMP signaling.
RESULTS: Network analysis identified 16 overlapping genes, including BCL2, BAX, and CYP19A1, with enrichment in apoptosis- and ovarian steroidogenesis-related pathways. JGT attenuated estrous-cycle disruption, cystic follicular accumulation, and endometrial thinning. Letrozole increased serum LH and testosterone; JGT reduced LH at 0.6 and 1.2 g/kg and testosterone at 1.2 g/kg, whereas FSH was not altered by letrozole. JGT also modulated ovarian AMH/AMHR2 and hormone-receptor expression and partially recovered steroidogenic markers. In KGN cells, JGT improved mitochondrial function, reduced apoptotic stress, enhanced FSH-induced cAMP signaling, and restored StAR, CYP19A1, and HSD3B expression together with estradiol and progesterone production.
CONCLUSION: JGT attenuated PCOS-related ovarian abnormalities and selected endocrine disturbances during letrozole exposure, accompanied by reduced apoptotic stress and improved FSH-responsive steroidogenic function. These associations warrant further causal validation.

articles.title: An oasis in the desert: Leveraging community pharmacy to advance maternal health.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.authors: DiPietro Mager N, Ojeda MS, Barnard M et al.
articles.abstract: Over a third of all U.S. counties are maternity care deserts, and rural areas are disproportionately affected. Rural women living in maternity care deserts find difficulty accessing health care, have a higher prevalence of conditions associated with poorer health and birth outcomes, and often face challenges related to social determinants of health. Community pharmacists are deeply under-utilized yet well-trained resources who can collaborate with healthcare workers and public health professionals to provide needed reproductive health services for those living in maternity care deserts. Building coalitions that recognize pharmacists as core collaborators in maternal and child health and dismantling structural barriers standing in the way will allow community pharmacists to fully realize their potential and provide essential care.

articles.title: Robotic-Assisted Uterus Transplantation: A Cadaveric Feasibility Model.
articles.authors: Eltemamy M, Kuznicki M, Isaacson D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To study the feasibility of robotic-assisted uterine allograft implantation in a human cadaveric model, addressing the technically demanding vascular anastomoses required for living-donor uterus transplantation. Over the past two decades, uterus transplantation (UTx) has progressed from preclinical studies through early clinical trials and into clinical practice (1-3). It remains the only therapeutic option for individuals with absolute uterine-factor infertility to carry their own pregnancy (4, 5). During early clinical trials, both living donor graft procurement and recipient implantation were performed exclusively via open laparotomy (1, 6, 7). Since that time, minimally invasive surgical approaches have been serially adapted to minimize donor surgical morbidity and take advantage of the superior 3D visualization and wristed instrumentation of the robotic platform (2, 5). Although robotic-assisted techniques have become well adapted and standardized for living donor hysterectomy at high-volume centers (4, 5), recipient implantation has received less development and remains predominantly performed through an open approach (2). Building upon the established success of robotic approaches in solid organ transplantation, such as robotic kidney transplantation, we aim to adapt these microsurgical techniques to recipient uterus transplantation.
DESIGN: Narrated, stepwise video of robotic implantation of a uterine graft in a cadaveric model using the da Vinci platform. This study was performed using a human cadaveric donor. Use of the donated body for research and educational purposes was authorized through the institution's body donation program in accordance with institutional policies and applicable regulations.
SUBJECTS: A uterine graft procured through an organ procurement organization from a 50-year-old brain-dead donor, implanted in a 67-year-old female cadaver in an academic cadaver laboratory.
EXPOSURE: Robotic-assisted uterus transplantation. The graft was benched to replicate a living-donor procurement, using only the anterior division of the internal iliac artery and taking the ovarian and inferior uterine veins without a venous patch, yielding six small-caliber vessels. After perfusion with histidine-tryptophan-ketoglutarate solution, each vessel was spatulated cranially and marked for orientation. Through a Pfannenstiel incision, four robotic arms were docked, and the recipient external iliac artery and vein were dissected bilaterally.…

articles.title: Associations of gestational diabetes mellitus with PFAS distribution and partitioning across the maternal-placental-fetal continuum.
articles.authors: Liu D, Zhao L, Wu J et al.
articles.abstract: Previous studies have indicated that maternal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) is associated with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), although the causality of this association remains uncertain. Given the metabolic disturbances, altered serum protein binding, and placental dysfunction associated with GDM, we hypothesized that PFAS concentrations and their concentration ratios across the maternal-placental-fetal continuum might differ by GDM status. In this study, we simultaneously quantified PFAS concentrations in four matched biological matrices, including maternal serum, placenta, cord serum, and umbilical cord tissue, from 156 mother-infant pairs; 30 mothers were diagnosed with GDM. We evaluated the distribution and partitioning patterns of PFAS across the four matrices and assessed the potential modifying role of GDM. PFAS concentrations showed matrix-specific distribution patterns, with higher concentrations in maternal serum than cord serum and higher in placental than umbilical cord tissue. Perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS) concentrations in umbilical cord tissue were higher in the GDM group, whereas no significant differences were observed for other PFAS or total PFAS across matrices. Compared with controls, the GDM group exhibited higher cord serum/placenta-to-maternal serum ratios for perfluorobutane sulfonic acid (PFBS) and higher umbilical cord-to-cord serum ratios for PFHxS and perfluorooctanoic acid. GDM showed nominal positive associations with the placenta-to-maternal serum ratio of PFBS and the umbilical cord tissue-to-cord serum ratios of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), and PFHxS, although none remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Interaction analyses further indicated that GDM modified the associations between maternal serum and placental PFAS concentrations for perfluoroheptane sulfonate (PFHpS), PFOA, and 6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonic acid (6:2 Cl-PFESA).

articles.title: State contraceptive coverage and interstate disparities in postabortion contraception receipt among patients traveling for care.
articles.authors: Hansen K, Boniface ER, Liberty A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether Oregon's Reproductive Health Access Fund (RHAF), which provides contraceptive coverage for individuals with incomes ≤250% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) regardless of state of residence, is associated with a reduction in disparities in receipt of postabortion contraception between Oregon residents and those traveling for care from Idaho.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data for individuals obtaining procedural abortion in Oregon (May 2021-May 2025). We compared contraceptive method received (none, moderately effective, or LARC) between Oregon (n=5,861) and Idaho residents (n=641). We used logistic regression with an interaction term (FPL*state) to estimate the interstate difference in the adjusted predicted probability of receiving LARC or moderately effective method.
RESULTS: Idaho residents were more likely to receive no contraception following abortion (43.5% Idaho vs 34.7% Oregon) and less likely to receive LARC (19.8% vs 24.8%, overall p<0.001) compared to Oregon residents. Oregon's RHAF was associated with reduced disparities in the interaction model. Among RHAF-ineligible patients (>250% FPL), the predicted probability of receiving LARC or moderately effective contraception was 22.4 percentage points (95% CI 13.5%-31.2%) higher for Oregon residents: 36.8% vs. 14.5% for Idaho residents. Among RHAF-eligible patients (≤250% FPL), the interstate difference was just 2.4 percentage points (95% CI -2.0%-6.8%): 49.9% Oregon vs 47.5% Idaho.
CONCLUSIONS: Oregon's income-based contraceptive coverage program was associated with a meaningful reduction in interstate disparities in receipt of postabortion contraception for patients traveling for procedural abortion care.
IMPLICATIONS: Income-based contraceptive coverage programs that extend to out-of-state patients may reduce geographic disparities in postabortion contraception receipt. As more people travel for needed abortion care, receiving states should expand access to postabortion contraception regardless of residency.

articles.title: Cutaneous Manifestations of the Menopausal Transition - Part 2: Hormonal Frameworks and Management of Skin and Hair Concerns.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
articles.authors: Li Y, Dave R, Kim U et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause represents a significant cutaneous biologic event, characterized by skin and hair changes in perimenopause that often precede more broadly recognized vasomotor symptoms for which women seek care. These skin and hair sequelae result from both estrogen decline and relative androgen excess and include skin barrier dysfunction, thinning and laxity, pigmentary dysregulation, hair loss and/or hirsutism, new or worsening acne, and vulvovaginal changes. Dermatologists are integral to the diagnosis and management of these menopause-associated skin and hair conditions and an important part of the patient's menopause care team. This installment translates the biology of Part 1 into practical, evidence-based clinical management. We review current data on menopausal hormone therapy and its dermatologic implications, including recent regulatory changes and evolving evidence on topical and systemic estrogen. We summarize management strategies for barrier dysfunction, dermal aging, hair and pigmentary disorders, perimenopausal acne, rosacea, and genitourinary syndrome and vulvar dermatoses. Throughout, we highlight therapies supported by high-quality evidence, flag areas where evidence remains limited, and offer counseling points for an increasingly complex therapeutic landscape. We aim to equip dermatologists to evaluate menopausal skin disease, apply hormonal and nonhormonal therapies, recognize conditions warranting interdisciplinary referral, and counsel patients on benefits, limitations, and uncertainties.

articles.title: Efficacy of enhanced recovery after surgery in pelvic floor reconstruction with transvaginal mesh: a propensity score-matched study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Zeng Q, Long X, Chen M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols on early postoperative recovery, complications, and anatomical and functional outcomes in female patients undergoing transvaginal mesh (TVM) surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing TVM for pelvic organ prolapse who received either conventional management (control group) or an ERAS protocol (ERAS group). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, and anatomical and functional outcomes at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively were compared between groups.
RESULTS: After matching, 69 patients were included in each group with balanced baseline characteristics (P > 0.05). The ERAS group showed significant improvements in the visual analogue scale at 24 h postoperatively, the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, time to first ambulation, postoperative length of stay, and hospitalization costs compared to the control group (P < 0.05). Regarding postoperative complications, the overall rate was significantly lower in the ERAS group (11.59 % vs. 24.64 %, P < 0.05). Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantitation (POP-Q) measurements and pelvic floor questionnaire scores postoperatively compared to preoperative values (P < 0.001). However, no significant differences were found between groups in POP-Q measurements or pelvic floor questionnaire scores at any postoperative time point (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: ERAS protocol for TVM surgery enhances early postoperative recovery and reduces complication rates without compromising the anatomical or functional efficacy of the procedure, indicating that ERAS represents a safe and effective perioperative strategy for this procedure.

articles.title: Bone biomarker concentrations at baseline and 24 h after resistance and interval running exercise in eumenorrheic females and oral contraceptive users.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Guisado-Cuadrado I, Romero-Parra N, Cupeiro R et al.
articles.abstract: Bone metabolism is influenced by both mechanical loading and the hormonal environment, yet their combined effects on the acute response to exercise remain unclear in premenopausal females. Therefore, this study aimed to examine baseline and 24 h post-exercise concentrations of bone biomarkers following resistance and interval-running exercise, considering menstrual and oral contraceptive (OC) cycle phases. Eight eumenorrheic and 8 OC users performed interval running (8×3 min at 85% maximal aerobic speed), whereas 9 eumenorrheic and 10 OC users completed eccentric-based resistance exercise (10×10 squats at 60% 1RM), according to their trained modality. Trials were conducted in randomized order during the early- and late-follicular phases (EFP, LFP) in eumenorrheic females and withdrawal and active pill phases (WP, APP) in OC users. Blood was sampled at baseline and 24 h post-exercise. Dickkopf-1 (DKK-1) and sclerostin showed Exercise×Time interactions, with lower concentrations 24 h after interval running. Osteocalcin showed Exercise×Phase and Exercise×Time interactions, with lower 24 h concentrations in the endurance- than resistance-trained group and lower concentrations in endurance-trained OC users during APP versus WP. Fibroblast Growth Factor-23 was lower at 24 h, while osteoprotegerin (OPG) was higher in APP than WP. Overall, interval running induced concurrent reductions in DKK-1, sclerostin, and total osteocalcin, indicating a short-term alteration in bone metabolic regulation. The reductions in DKK-1 and sclerostin are compatible with a transient decrease in Wnt pathway inhibition. Osteocalcin and OPG varied across OC phases, highlighting the relevance of considering hormonal status.

articles.title: Transphobia in public restrooms and its association with lower urinary tract disorders: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
articles.authors: Arnandes BCDS, Mariano BF, Delvaz LB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the health behaviors of transgender individuals in Brazil and their association with lower urinary tract dysfunction.
METHOD: An exploratory-descriptive, cross-sectional study using a convergent mixed-methods approach, conducted with transgender individuals in Brazil. Data collection took place between October 2024 and March 2025 via an online questionnaire that included sociodemographic data, the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms, and the Toileting Behavior - Women's Elimination Behaviors, as well as open-ended questions about experiences in public restrooms. The sample was obtained through convenience and snowball sampling. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics (p < 0.05), and qualitative data were analyzed according to Bardin.
RESULTS: A total of 131 participants took part, predominantly transmen, young, single, white, and with a college education. Harmful habits were identified, such as delaying, forcing, and anticipating urination, in addition to reports of embarrassment, insecurity, and transphobia. The most common urinary dysfunctions were overactive bladder, urinary retention, and incontinence.
CONCLUSION: There was evidence of a high prevalence of inappropriate practices, associated with negative experiences and a higher incidence of urinary dysfunctions.

articles.title: Symptoms of glucocorticoid-induced adrenal insufficiency - a systematic evaluation of clinician- and patient-reported symptoms and their significance for patients' decisions to take hydrocortisone stress doses.
articles.authors: Bjergstrøm MLL, Boesen VB, Tei RMH et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Glucocorticoid-induced adrenal insufficiency (GIAI) is a common, distinct form of adrenal insufficiency, yet its symptom profile remains poorly characterized. We systematically evaluated clinician- and patient-reported symptoms and the significance patients ascribe to them as indicators of a need for hydrocortisone stress doses.
DESIGN: Mixed-methods sequential survey and interview study.
METHODS: Endocrinologists from Danish tertiary adrenal centres evaluated the 80 symptoms in the Patient-Reported Outcomes version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (PRO-CTCAE), rated their relevance to GIAI, and suggested additional symptoms. Symptoms with mean relevance score ≥1 ('a little relevant') underwent final expert review before being explored in semi-structured patient interviews. Adult patients with GIAI for >6 months were recruited from endocrine outpatient clinics. Patients described symptom experiences, marked symptoms they recognized on the expert-generated list, and rated their significance for deciding to administer hydrocortisone stress doses. New symptoms were incorporated into subsequent interview rounds, continuing until symptom saturation.
RESULTS: Eleven endocrinologists identified 17 relevant symptoms; three were excluded during final expert review, leaving 14 symptoms for patient evaluation. Thirty patients (median [IQR] GIAI duration 5.0 [3.2-9.6] years) participated and identified 14 additional symptoms. The most frequently reported symptoms were fatigue, feeling unwell, lethargy, difficulty concentrating, and nausea (all ≥60%). Symptoms with the highest significance ratings were vomiting, nausea, dizziness, hot flashes, fatigue, and feeling unwell (all >3, 'moderately important').
CONCLUSIONS: We identified 28 GIAI-relevant symptoms and characterized their frequency and patient-reported importance in guiding real-world dosing decisions, providing a patient-centred basis for symptom monitoring in GIAI.

articles.title: Regional Cutaneous Vasodilatory Responses to Local Heating in Post-Menopausal Females with and without Hormone Replacement Therapy.
articles.authors: Li-Maloney C, McGarr GW, Johnson SJI et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We investigated whether post-menopausal females receiving hormone replacement therapy (HRT) exhibit greater nitric oxide (NO)-dependent cutaneous microvascular responses than those not receiving HRT, assessed via pharmacological NO synthase (NOS) inhibition during local heating. We also examined regional differences in microvascular response between and within groups.
METHODS: Twenty-one post-menopausal females (10 receiving HRT, 11 not receiving HRT) underwent assessment of cutaneous vascular conductance (CVC), expressed as a percentage of maximum vasodilation (%CVCmax), at the chest, abdomen, forearm, and calf using laser-Doppler flowmetry. Local skin temperature was raised from 33°C to 42°C for ∼30 min, followed by ∼40 min perfusion with 20 mm  NG-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME; NOS inhibitor) using intradermal microdialysis. The NO contribution to vasodilation was defined as the difference in %CVCmax between the 42°C and L-NAME plateau.
RESULTS: There were no significant differences in the NO contribution to vasodilation between groups or between sites within groups (all p > 0.107). During baseline, females not receiving HRT demonstrated 7.6 [0.8, 14.4]% higher %CVCmax at the forearm compared with abdomen (p = 0.021). During the 42°C heating plateau, this group also showed abdominal %CVCmax values that were 11.8 [0.04, 23.5]% lower than the calf (p = 0.041) and 12.7 [1.1, 24.4]% lower than the forearm (p = 0.025). Females receiving HRT demonstrated 12.0 [2.4, 21.5]% greater abdominal %CVCmax than those not receiving HRT (p = 0.014).
CONCLUSION: Altogether, our findings indicate that HRT is not associated with NO-dependent cutaneous vasodilation during local heating in post-menopausal females but is associated with regional heterogeneity in cutaneous vasodilatory responses.

articles.title: Cohort profile: Assessment of factors impacting on foetal and infant immunity, growth, and neurodevelopment in HIV and antiretroviral drug exposed uninfected children: The Siyakhula Study.
articles.authors: du Toit L, Molokoane F, Mulol H et al.
articles.abstract: This cohort profile paper describes the Siyakhula cohort, a prospective longitudinal study of mother-child dyads during the ante- and postpartum period. The cohort was established to investigate how in-utero and early postnatal environments altered by maternal HIV status influence infants' growth trajectories, cognitive development, immune development and function, irrespective of the infant's HIV status. Pregnant women aged ≥18 years with singleton pregnancies at <22 weeks' gestation (as per best obstetric estimate, including ultrasound), regardless of HIV status, were recruited from January 2018 to January 2021 and followed throughout pregnancy. After delivery, women were approached for continued enrolment in the postpartum arm, which followed the dyads for 24 months. A total of 315 pregnant women (152 living with HIV and 163 without HIV) were recruited. Routine (pregnancy-related clinical data, HIV status, anthropometry) and research-specific (socio-demographic information, body composition analysis, diet, vaginal swabs, bloods) were collected antepartum. Cord blood and placental samples were collected intrapartum, while breast milk, stool samples, and blood were collected postpartum. Infants had anthropometric measurements performed at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, as well as 6, 12 and 24 months. Neurodevelopmental assessments were conducted during later follow-up visits. Extensive clinical, immunological, metabolomic, nutritional, and developmental data, together with a large biorepository of maternal and infant biospecimens, have been established. This paper provides an overview of the cohort design, participant characteristics, available data and biospecimens, completed analyses, and future research opportunities. Future plans include developing immunometabolic signatures associated with optimal and suboptimal growth and neurodevelopment of infants in the first two years of life.

articles.title: Prevalence of intimate partner violence against women in East Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Markos Z, Aligaz EM, Zegeye ST et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a pervasive public health and human rights issue worldwide, with sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) bearing a disproportionately high burden. However, synthesized evidence specifically from the East African region is limited.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Forty-one cross-sectional studies reporting IPV among women in East Africa were identified from seven electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online [AJOL], CINAHL, and Google Scholar). Databases were searched from August 1 to September 30, 2025.Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklist for prevalence studies. A random-effects inverse-variance model was used to estimate pooled prevalence with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Subgroup analyses were performed by country, population, study setting, recall period, IPV type, publication year, sample size, and data collection tool. Publication bias was assessed via funnel plots, Egger's test, and the trim-and-fill method. Sensitivity analysis was conducted using leave-one-out procedures.
RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 41 studies. The overall pooled prevalence of IPV was 42.8% (95% CI: 38.3-47.9%), indicating high heterogeneity (I2 = 99.6%). Subgroup analyses revealed significant variation: the highest prevalence was among contraceptive users (72.6%, based on a single study) and ever-married/partnered women (55.1%), while the lowest was among refugees (31.0%) and in large-scale studies (32.9%). Country-level estimates were highest in Uganda (52.0%), followed by Tanzania (49.9%) and Ethiopia (44.5%), and lowest in Rwanda (20.9%). Studies using WHO standard tools reported higher prevalence (49.1%) than those using DHS modules (36.3%) No significant publication bias was detected (Egger's test *p* = 0.284).Subgroup analyses revealed statistically significant between-group differences (p < 0.05) for country, study setting, and population subgroups, but not for measurement tool (p = 0.068).
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis confirms a high prevalence of IPV among women in East Africa, with substantial variation across subpopulations, countries, and methodological factors. Findings highlight the need for targeted, context-specific interventions and the importance of standardized measurement tools in surveillance and research.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Core-Sheath Fiber Patch Based on Cellulose Nanocrystal-Reinforced and Curcumin-Loaded Polylactic Acid for Enhanced Pelvic Tissue Repair.
articles.authors: Wu C, Qi F, Zhang S et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects millions of women due to tissue defect, marked by disrupted collagen homeostasis and abnormal immune reaction. Therefore, there is a demand for developing a multifunctional patch resolving these current straits. Herein, we fabricated a multifunctional core-sheath fibrous patch via coaxial electrospinning, comprising cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) sheath and curcumin-loaded PLA core. Post-electrospinning heat treatment enhanced PLA crystallinity improved mechanical properties and enabled sustained curcumin release. The patch exhibited stable degradation, good biocompatibility, and potent anti-inflammatory activity. In vivo, the CNC-PLA/Cur-h patch achieved native-tissue-comparable biomechanical strength within 4 weeks, with enhanced neovascularization, elevated collagen I/III ratio, and well-organized extracellular matrix. RNA sequencing confirmed upregulated angiogenesis and ECM-related genes, as well as downregulated inflammatory markers. This multifunctional platform integrates mechanical robustness, controlled biodegradability, and proregenerative capacity, presenting a promising strategy for POP repair.

articles.title: One week as a marker of pessary success: findings from a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Brown C, Malyon A, Hartley P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is no standard timeframe to define a successful pessary fitting. Current literature use a variety of timepoints between 30 minutes to 36-months. This study aims to examine the number of women who continue vaginal pessary at set time intervals after the initial pessary fitting and help identify a timeframe of pessary cessation.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a large tertiary UK teaching hospital. Women of 18 years old and above who had a pessary fitted for prolapse symptoms were included. Data were collected at 1 week, then 3, 6, 12, 24 and 36 months to capture early and long term pessary continuation. Electrical medical records were reviewed to determine if a woman was continuing with pessary use after initial fitting. A time-to-event analysis was conducted to assess the probability of pessary discontinuation at the predefined time points.
RESULTS: A total of 98 of 159 women (62%) discontinued pessary use over the predefined time points. The most frequent time point for a women to stop pessary use was during the first week (59 out of 98 women stopped (60%). This was followed by 29 women stopping at 3 month (29.5%), 6 women stopped at 6 months (6.1%) and 3 women stopped at 12 months (3.1%). The remaining 68 (42.8%) women continued using the pessary and were asymptomatic. The most common reason for discontinuation was failure to retain the pessary followed by pain or discomfort.
CONCLUSIONS: Most women who discontinue pessary use do so within the first week after fitting, suggesting that one week may be an appropriate time point for assessing early pessary success.

articles.title: Efficacy of Cryotherapy Compared With Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure Among Women With and Without HIV in Kenya.
articles.journal: Journal of lower genital tract disease
articles.authors: Orang'o O, Mehta N, Mwangi A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among Kenyan women aged 15-44. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) in women with HIV (WHIV) is more likely to progress in severity compared with women without HIV. This study assesses the results of cryotherapy or LEEP for CIN among WHIV compared with women without HIV in Western Kenya.
METHODS: Eighty-six WHIV (39 cryotherapy, 47 LEEP) and 89 women without HIV (46 cryotherapy, 43 LEEP) who had follow-up within 24 months were included in this analysis. Women ineligible for cryotherapy underwent colposcopy/biopsy, and those with confirmed CIN 2/3 underwent LEEP. Women were followed every 6 months with VIA, Pap smear or colposcopy/biopsy. χ2 and Fisher exact tests were used to compare the proportions.
RESULTS: There was a significant difference in overall treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (15.12% vs 5.62% p=.039). There was a significant difference in treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV who underwent cryotherapy (18% vs 2.1%, p=.021). Among patients who underwent LEEP, no difference was observed in the treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (12.8% vs 9.3%, p=.742).
CONCLUSIONS: In our experience, LEEP is a more effective treatment than cryotherapy for WHIV compared with women without HIV for CIN in Western Kenya.

articles.title: Quality-of-life outcomes of MR-guided ultrahypofractionated SBRT versus CBCT-guided moderately hypofractionated IMRT for localized prostate cancer: an EPIC-based real-world comparative study.
articles.authors: Shirafuji T, Yamada Y, Saito M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance-guided stereotactic body radiation therapy (MR-linac SBRT) is increasingly used for localized prostate cancer; however, its impact on patient-reported quality of life compared with cone beam computed tomography-guided conventional intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) remains unclear. We compared quality-of-life outcomes between MR-linac SBRT and IMRT using the Expanded Prostate Cancer Index Composite (EPIC-50).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 82 patients with localized prostate cancer treated with MR-linac SBRT (n = 51) or IMRT (n = 31) between 2022 and 2025. Clinically meaningful declines in EPIC-50 domain scores were assessed at 1-3 and 9-12 months. Predictors of urinary quality-of-life deterioration were evaluated using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: The proportions of patients with clinically meaningful declines in urinary, bowel, sexual, and hormonal domains did not differ significantly between the treatment groups at either 1-3 or 9-12 months. Symptom-directed pharmacotherapy was initiated more frequently after IMRT, including medications for lower urinary tract symptoms (P = .028), gastrointestinal symptoms (P = .0044), and vasomotor symptoms (P = .0014). Among patients receiving MR-linac SBRT, a higher baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) was associated with urinary quality-of-life deterioration. An IPSS cutoff of ≥9 was significantly associated with urinary deterioration (odds ratio, 27.0, 95% CI 4.11-541.49; P = .0002).
CONCLUSIONS: MR-linac SBRT showed no significant differences in patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes compared with IMRT and was associated with less frequent use of symptom-directed pharmacotherapy. Baseline IPSS may help identify patients at increased risk of urinary quality-of-life deterioration after MR-linac SBRT.

articles.title: Predictive Value of Maternal Peripheral Blood PAF and sFlt-1 Levels for Preterm Birth Secondary to PPROM.
articles.authors: Li X, Li J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a leading cause of preterm birth, which seriously endangers maternal and neonatal health. Platelet-activating factor (PAF) and soluble FMS-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) play important roles in pregnancy, but their predictive value for preterm birth following PPROM remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of maternal peripheral blood PAF and sFlt-1 levels for spontaneous preterm delivery (SPTD) secondary to PPROM.
METHODS: A total of 85 singleton pregnant women with a gestational age of 23 + 0 to 30 + 6 weeks who were diagnosed with PPROM were enrolled. Based on the occurrence of SPTD within 14 days after sampling, the participants were divided into an imminent SPTD group (iSPTD, n = 45) and a non-imminent SPTD group (non-iSPTD, n = 40). Serum levels of PAF and sFlt-1 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariate logistic regression was used to analyze their independent association with SPTD within 14 days post-sampling, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were employed to evaluate their predictive value.
RESULTS: Maternal peripheral blood levels of both PAF and sFlt-1 were significantly higher in the iSPTD group than in the non-iSPTD group (all p < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that PAF (odds ratio [OR] = 1.272, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.094 - 1.480) and sFlt-1 (OR = 1.179, 95% CI: 1.058 - 1.315) were independent risk factors for SPTD within 14 days after sampling. ROC curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) for predicting SPTD within 14 days was 0.762 for PAF and 0.738 for sFlt-1. The combined nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.829, demonstrating good predictive performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated maternal peripheral blood levels of PAF and sFlt-1 are independent risk factors for SPTD within 14 days after sampling in patients with PPROM. Both biomarkers exhibit predictive value for SPTD, and their combination in a nomogram model can further improve predictive performance, showing potential for clinical application.

articles.title: Serum Vitamin D Combined with Obstetric Parameters to Construct a Nomogram Model for Predicting the Risk of PFD Disorders.
articles.authors: Li JC, Song JN, Liu CH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) significantly impacts women's quality of life and mental health. Although existing studies suggest various obstetric factors may contribute to PFD, there is a lack of early prediction tools based on readily available indicators. This study aimed to develop a nomogram model incorporating serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)VitD] levels and routine obstetric parameters to predict the risk of PFD.
METHODS: A total of 300 women who delivered and completed a 6-week postpartum follow-up were enrolled. Data on age, body mass index (BMI), duration of the second stage of labor, neonatal birth weight, and serum 25(OH) VitD levels within 24 hours postpartum were collected. Participants were divided into PFD and non-PFD groups based on follow-up outcomes. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors for PFD, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression revealed that age, BMI, duration of the second stage of labor, birth weight, and 25(OH)VitD levels were independent predictors of PFD (p < 0.05). The nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.830 with calibration curves demonstrating good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA indicated substantial clinical net benefit across a wide probability threshold range.
CONCLUSIONS: The developed nomogram model effectively predicts postpartum PFD risk using easily obtainable pre- and post-delivery indicators. This model may facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals, guiding personalized rehabilitation strategies and improving early intervention and prevention of PFD.

articles.title: Nationwide Assessment of Trends, Characteristics, and Outcomes of Pregnancy for Cancer Survivors.
articles.authors: Matsuo K, Komura N, Yamaguchi A et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cancer survivors are individuals with a diagnosis of malignant neoplasm, either living with (ie, current cancer survivors) or free of (ie, past cancer survivors) cancer. As the prevalence of cancer survivors of reproductive age increases worldwide, assessment of pregnancy characteristics and outcomes among past cancer survivors is important.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the temporal trends, clinical and obstetric characteristics, and maternal morbidity at delivery among current and past cancer survivors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide cross-sectional study used National Inpatient Sample data for hospital deliveries from 2016 to 2023. Analyses were conducted from April to May 2026.
EXPOSURE: A prior or current diagnosis of cancer at hospital delivery, with individuals classified as being a past cancer survivor, a current cancer survivor, or an individual without a cancer diagnosis.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: The primary outcome was severe maternal morbidity at delivery, assessed with multivariable generalized linear models with a Poisson distribution.
RESULTS: Among 28 360 443 hospital deliveries, there were 106 740 (0.4%) hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors, 21 975 (<0.1%) for current cancer survivors, and 28 231 728 (99.5%) without a cancer diagnosis. The median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 33 (29-36), 32 (27-36), and 29 (25-33) years among past cancer survivors, current cancer survivors, and individuals without a cancer diagnosis, respectively. During the 8-year study period, hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors increased from 30.1 to 45.6 per 10 000 hospital deliveries (average annual percentage change [AAPC] = 6.3% [95% CI, 5.1%-7.9%]), whereas hospital deliveries for current cancer survivors were unchanged (7.0 to 7.4 per 10 000 hospital deliveries; AAPC = 0.2% [95% CI, -2.8% to 3.7%]). Most hospital deliveries (57.6%) for past cancer survivors were full-term, whereas only 39.6% were full-term for current cancer survivors.
