Compared with the no cancer group, the severe maternal morbidity rate was higher for the past cancer survivor group (11.9 vs 6.8 per 1000 hospital deliveries; adjusted incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.45 [95% CI, 1.37-1.53]) and for the current cancer survivor group (48.2 vs 6.8 per 1000 hospital deliveries; adjusted IRR, 3.80 [95% CI, 3.58-4.04]), including the inpatient maternal mortality rate during the hospital delivery admission (273.0 vs 7.0 per 100 000 hospital deliveries;…

articles.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.authors: Zenjaya KT, Christopher C, Timothy RA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening condition and often diagnosed late, with many patients presenting in advanced heart failure. This study aimed to examine the demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and maternal and neonatal outcomes METHODS AND RESULTS: This meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 4,341 records up to May 2025, were identified and 122 eligible studies reporting PPCM clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes were included. Heterogeneity was explored through meta-regression analyses assessing demographic, clinical, and study-level variables. An aggregate of 66,908 PPCM patients were reported across the included studies, with a pooled mean age of 30.1 years. Black or African women accounted for a disproportionately large proportion of the reported population compared with other racial groups. Approximately 62% of women presented with advanced heart failure (NYHA class III/IV). Pre-existing diabetes mellitus (OR 5.09) and hypertensive disorders, including pre-existing hypertension (OR 10.07), gestational hypertension (OR 7.75), and pre-eclampsia (OR 9.27), were associated with higher odds of PPCM. The pooled mean LVEF at diagnosis was 29.98%, which subsequently improved to 46.47% at 6 months and 49.12% at 12 months. Despite over half of PPCM patients achieving LVEF recovery (55%), maternal mortality remained high at 6% and neonatal mortality at 4%. Pharmacological treatments for PPCM varied widely, with high heterogeneity suggesting substantial differences in prescribing practices across studies.
CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

articles.title: Metabolic-reproductive axis in normogonadotropic anovulation: a comparative study of polycystic ovary syndrome and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian dysfunction.
articles.authors: Brodowicz J, Solnica B, Gawron I
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare hormonal and metabolic profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian dysfunction (HPOD), with particular emphasis on kisspeptin and ghrelin concentrations and on PCOS subsets characterized by hyperandrogenemia (HA), insulin resistance (IR), and obesity.
METHODS: The prospective study involved women aged 18-45 with menstrual irregularities. Participants underwent gynecological evaluations, including pelvic ultrasound, and biochemical serum analyses to assess hormonal and metabolic parameters.
RESULTS: Kisspeptin (p = 0.003) and ghrelin (p = 0.006) concentrations were significantly higher in PCOS than in HPOD. Distinct hormonal and metabolic profiles characterized PCOS, HPOD, and PCOS phenotypes. In PCOS, kisspeptin concentrations were higher in women with IR (p < 0.001) and HA (p = 0.003), whereas ghrelin concentrations did not differ by IR (p = 0.611) or HA (p = 0.153). Neither kisspeptin (p = 0.428) nor ghrelin (p = 0.240) differed by BMI category. Kisspeptin concentrations were positively correlated with ghrelin, thyroid-stimulating hormone, IR indices, C-reactive protein, and interleukin-6, and negatively with sex hormone-binding globulin and free thyroxine (all p < 0.05). Ghrelin concentrations positively correlated with dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate and negatively with free thyroxine (all p < 0.05). There were fewer significant correlations in HPOD. In multiple regression, ln(IL-6) was an independent positive predictor of ln(kisspeptin) (β = 0.296, p = 0.027) and fT4 a negative predictor (β=-0.059, p = 0.027), while for ln(ghrelin) only 17-OH-progesterone remained a positive independent predictor (β = 0.042, p = 0.019), with metabolic markers losing significance.
CONCLUSIONS: The lack of classical PCOS markers as independent predictors suggests that kisspeptin and ghrelin are regulated by primary inflammatory, thyroidal, and steroidogenic axes, with kisspeptin appearing inflammation-sensitive and ghrelin steroidogenesis-related, supporting a multi-axial model of PCOS.
STUDY REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov(NCT06793098), on January 20, 2025.

articles.title: Modeling the Effects of Hormonal Oral Contraceptive Dosing on Contraceptive Efficacy.
articles.authors: Kim R, Zhao L, Oremland LS et al.
articles.abstract: Examining the impact of oral contraceptive (OC) dosing is important to understand how hormonal contraceptives influence ovulation, the menstrual cycle, and critically, the contraceptive state. In this paper, we develop a mechanistic mathematical model that captures hormone dynamics observed in available data. The model enables us to assess the robustness and effectiveness of various contraceptive dosing regimens, and to evaluate how the dosing strength and the schedule of hormonal OCs affect contraception. Our model incorporates the pharmacokinetics of two exogenous hormones, progestin and ethinyl estradiol (EE). We characterize the impact of dosing schedules (using daily doses with no placebo pills, 24 days of active hormone pills followed by 4 placebo days, or 21 days of active hormone pills followed by 7 placebo days) and dosing strengths on hormonal cycling dynamics. Our results show that with an increasing dose of progestin, the cycle length increases, while increasing the dose of EE removes the periodic behavior completely. We found that the no-placebo dosing schedule shows the most consistent dynamics, while regimens with placebo days had more irregular dynamics. Our model also demonstrates that two theoretical scenarios of individuals with physiologically normal menstrual cycles and the same cycle length may experience different contraceptive efficacy for the same OC dose strength and schedule. Future studies using our model may inform evidence-based dosing protocols and guide clinical decision-making, particularly in the case of missed doses.

articles.title: Markers of Cardiovascular Risk Associated With Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Crooks T, Kondapalli L
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: We sought to provide a brief review of available scores and factors to consider when assessing cardiovascular risk of pregnancy. We also discuss maternal cardiovascular risk stratification of survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer and congenital heart disease and identify gaps in knowledge.
RECENT FINDINGS: The modified WHO 2.0 I-IV in conjunction with the CARPREG II provides the most robust risk score to date but still has shortcomings. No score specifically addresses cardiovascular risk of pregnancy in survivors of cancer. While several tools for assessing risk exist, consideration of patient-specific factors also play an important role. Moderate and high-risk patients may be best cared for by multidisciplinary teams.

articles.title: Factors associated with long-acting reversible contraceptive choice following voluntary termination of pregnancy.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Xu S, Damião SMP, Milhinhos CRF et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify sociodemographic, reproductive and healthcare-related factors independently associated with long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) choice following voluntary termination of pregnancy (VTP).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted at a VTP Unit in a Portuguese tertiary-care hospital between January 2025 and January 2026. Variables included age, ethnicity, educational level, occupational status, access to a family physician, attendance at a family planning consultation during the previous year, contraceptive method used before the index pregnancy, parity and previous VTP. The primary outcome was LARC choice following VTP.
RESULTS: Of 1,025 women assessed, 860 were included [median age 27 years (23-32)]; Among these, 482 (56.0%) selected a LARC: 233 (48.3%) chose a 52 mg LNG-IUD, 226 (46.9%) an ENG implant and 23 (4.8%) a Cu-IUD. In the multivariable analysis, younger age, higher parity, and occupational status were independently associated with LARC choice (p < 0.05). Each five-year increase in age was associated with a 24% reduction in the odds of LARC selection (aOR 0.76, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Younger age, higher parity and occupational status were independently associated with LARC choice. These findings may contribute to understanding post-VTP contraceptive patterns and identify areas for further research on contraceptive choice.

articles.title: Risk factors for gestational diabetes in pregnancies resulting from in vitro fertilisation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Rakhmanova S, Saipova M, Fazliddinova F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical, metabolic, body-composition and circulating miR-29 correlates of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in singleton pregnancies conceived after in vitro fertilisation (IVF).
METHODS: This observational cohort study included 210 singleton pregnancies (110 conceived after IVF and 100 conceived spontaneously) managed at a single tertiary centre between January 2022 and December 2024. GDM was defined as the diagnosis recorded in the clinical record and was based on the local 75-g oral glucose tolerance test protocol at 24-28 weeks. Body composition was measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis at 8-12 weeks and whole-blood miR-29a and miR-29b expression at 11-13 weeks by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR, normalised to miR-93-5p. Associations were examined using the chi-square test, Student t test, Pearson correlation, logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: GDM occurred in 43 women (20.5%) and was more frequent after IVF than after spontaneous conception (27.3% versus 13.0%; p=0.010). In multivariable analysis, pre-pregnancy obesity (adjusted OR 10.74; 95% CI 3.99-28.94), triglycerides at or above 2.0 mmol/L (6.57; 2.57-16.77), low miR-29a (5.99; 2.41-14.92) and IVF conception (4.19; 1.55-11.36) were independently associated with GDM; the association with polycystic ovary syndrome was borderline (2.69; 0.99-7.30). Women with GDM had higher body fat percentage and visceral fat area (both p<0.001), but body fat percentage was not independent of the other covariates (3.00; 0.90-10.05; p=0.075). miR-29a discriminated GDM with an area under the curve of 0.81 (0.74-0.87).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, GDM in IVF pregnancies was associated with pre-pregnancy obesity, dyslipidaemia and lower circulating miR-29a expression. Estimates were sensitive to the diagnostic threshold applied and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Intracrinology and tissue-selective effects of tibolone: mechanisms and implications.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: de Melo NR, Schmidt do Prado-Lima PA, Melo Pompei L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tibolone is a synthetic steroid widely used for the treatment of menopausal symptoms and prevention of osteoporosis. Unlike conventional menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), tibolone is converted into metabolites with estrogenic, progestogenic and androgenic activity, and their relative availability may differ among tissues. Intracrinology, whereby circulating steroid precursors are locally converted into active hormones or inactive metabolites within target tissues, provides a potential framework for understanding these differential effects. This study aimed to critically examine the intracrinological basis of tibolone pharmacology and assess the extent to which tissue-specific metabolism may contribute to its differential clinical effects across estrogen-sensitive tissues.
METHOD: A critical narrative review of experimental studies, randomized clinical trials and systematic reviews was conducted to evaluate tibolone metabolism and the distribution and activity of its metabolites in major target tissues, including breast, uterus, vagina, brain and bone.
RESULTS: Tibolone acts predominantly as a prodrug and is converted into three active metabolites: the estrogenic compounds 3α-hydroxytibolone and 3β-hydroxytibolone, and the Δ4-isomer, which has progestogenic and androgenic properties. Experimental evidence indicates that tissue-specific differences in enzyme expression, sulfation, desulfation and possibly membrane transport may influence the local balance and availability of these metabolites. In breast and uterine tissues, preclinical studies suggest a predominance of sulfated metabolites, a pattern compatible with comparatively limited availability of unconjugated estrogenic metabolites. In bone and vaginal tissue, clinical benefits are compatible with sufficient local or systemic estrogenic activity. Evidence relating intracrinology to effects in the central nervous system remains limited and largely indirect. Across tissues, clinical outcomes are influenced by population characteristics, underlying pathology, dose and concomitant treatment, and do not directly establish the proposed metabolic mechanisms.
CONCLUSION: Intracrinology provides a biologically plausible framework for understanding the tissue-selective effects of tibolone. However, clinical findings are largely compatible with, rather than confirmatory of, this mechanism, and the balance of benefits and risks appears to vary according to tissue, clinical context and individual…

articles.title: Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Dominguez EG, Junak M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection.
METHODS: We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection.
RESULTS: mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P < 0.0001). Integrating microbial abundance with end motif features improved differentiation between clinically significant pathogens and corresponding noise from the same microbes in noninfection samples. For Staphylococcus infections, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the combination model was higher than than that for microbial abundance alone (0.892 vs 0.431, respectively; P = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

articles.title: Urine as a liquid allograft biopsy: emerging technologies for noninvasive monitoring in kidney transplantation.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.authors: El Fekih R, Akalin E
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Long-term kidney allograft survival remains limited by immune and nonimmune injury, while conventional surveillance tools are constrained by delayed detection, limited specificity, or invasiveness. Urine provides an accessible window into the allograft, containing inflammatory mediators, cells, extracellular vesicles, nucleic acids, proteins, peptides, and metabolites reflecting intra-graft processes.
RECENT FINDINGS: Over the past two decades, urinary biomarkers have evolved from single-analyte discovery to molecular signatures matched to kidney biopsy findings. Urinary CXCL9/CXCL10, urinary-cell mRNA, extracellular-vesicle transcriptomics, donor-derived cell-free DNA, proteomics, and metabolomics provide complementary measures of allograft injury and have demonstrated encouraging diagnostic performance. Although some remain limited by variable specificity, analytical standardization, reproducibility, or insufficient prospective validation, others have undergone multicenter validation, assay standardization, and progression toward clinical implementation.
SUMMARY: Urinary biomarkers are unlikely to replace biopsy with a single universal test. Their greatest potential lies in context-specific applications, including risk stratification, surveillance, biopsy triage, differential diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment-response monitoring. High negative predictive value across several platforms may support reducing unnecessary biopsies. Clinical translation will depend on standardized, transferable assays, external validation in representative populations, clearly defined contexts of use, and evidence that biomarker-guided strategies improve patient and allograft outcomes.

articles.title: Birth and long-term health outcomes of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate treatment for heterotopic pregnancy: A retrospective study and focused literature review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Chen Q, Wan S, Li Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report birth outcomes and long-term intellectual and physical development follow-up data of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate (MTX) injection for heterotopic pregnancy (HP), and to summarize relevant published cases.
METHODS: We included 29 patients with HP involving uncommon ectopic implantation sites who underwent transvaginal ultrasound-guided local MTX injection to treat the ectopic gestation (2006-2023). We evaluated birth outcomes and the intellectual and physical development in offspring aged 4-17 years, and conducted a focused review of published cases from 1990 to 2025 via PubMed.
RESULTS: Pregnancy outcomes were available for 27 of 29 patients. Twenty-four women delivered 26 live-born offspring, including 23 without and three with congenital anomalies (congenital heart disease, hypospadias, and multiple craniofacial and limb abnormalities, respectively). Matched comparative analyses included 11 preschool-aged, eight school-aged, and seven adolescent offspring. Across the cognitive, anthropometric, blood pressure, and laboratory outcomes assessed, three between-group differences showed nominal P-values of below 0.05, involving preschool uric acid, school-age systolic blood pressure, and adolescent blood urea nitrogen. Among these, the systolic blood pressure difference was accompanied by high-normal blood pressure or hypertension in some offspring in the MTX group. None of the three differences remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. After the exclusion of overlapping observations, the focused literature review identified 14 independent live-born offspring from previously reported cases, of whom two had congenital anomalies.
CONCLUSION: Most live-born offspring following local MTX treatment for HP had no congenital anomalies, and no long-term offspring outcome comparison remained statistically significant after FDR correction. However, congenital anomalies were reported in both our cohort and the published literature, and the small sample size and limited evidence preclude firm conclusions regarding long-term safety.

articles.title: High-throughput simultaneous determination of 51 herbicide residues in drinking water by online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.authors: Zhong Z, Wang K, Lin Q et al.
articles.abstract: An online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (online SPE-UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed for the simultaneous determination of 51 herbicides, including triazines, sulfonylureas, amides, and phenylureas, in drinking water. Water samples were filtered through a 0.22 µm hydrophilic polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) membrane, adjusted to pH 6, enriched on an Oasis hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB) online solid-phase extraction (SPE) column with 0.1% formic acid in water as the loading solution, and separated on an ACQUITY UPLC HSS T3 column using 0.1% formic acid in water-acetonitrile. Detection was performed in positive electrospray ionization (ESI+) and multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode. The method showed good linearity for all analytes, with correlation coefficients greater than 0.995. The limits of detection and quantification were 0.146-0.833 ng L-1 and 0.487-2.778 ng L-1, respectively. Mean recoveries at 5, 10, and 50 ng L-1 ranged from 68.0% to 118.9%, with intra-day and inter-day RSDs of 0.2-9.5% and 1.0-19.9%, respectively. Matrix effects were weak for forty-seven compounds, moderate for three, and strong for one. The method was successfully applied to 84 real samples from 28 water treatment plants in southeastern China. Overall detection rates decreased from raw water to finished water and tap water, with triazines and amides as the predominant detected classes. This analytical method provides reliable technical support for drinking water quality surveillance and health risk assessment.

articles.title: TMEFF2 is associated with trophoblast dysfunction in missed abortion.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Liu J, Zhang P, Li J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Missed abortion (MA) is a common complication of early pregnancy, and its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Abnormal trophoblast proliferation and migration are associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including MA. This study aimed to compare TMEFF2 expression in chorionic villous tissue between women with MA and those with normal early pregnancy and to evaluate the association between TMEFF2 and proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration in HTR-8/SVneo cells.
METHODS: The study included 21 women with MA and 21 women with normal early pregnancy. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was performed to evaluate the histomorphological features of chorionic villi. TMEFF2 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry and Western blotting. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, TMEFF2 was overexpressed or knocked down, and changes in TMEFF2 expression were assessed by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction and Western blotting. Cell Counting Kit-8, wound-healing, and Transwell migration assays were used to assess proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration.
RESULTS: TMEFF2 expression was significantly higher in the chorionic villous tissue from women with MA than in tissue from controls. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, TMEFF2 overexpression was associated with reduced proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration, whereas TMEFF2 knockdown showed the opposite pattern.
CONCLUSION: TMEFF2 is upregulated in chorionic villous tissue from women with MA and is associated with reduced proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration in HTR-8/SVneo cells in vitro. These findings provide preliminary evidence of an association between TMEFF2 and MA.

articles.title: Utility of Artificial Intelligence in Diagnosing Image-Based Vaginal Pathology.
articles.authors: Shekar A, Shalom DF, Reddy M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used by patients for health-related concerns before formal medical evaluation. However, data evaluating the diagnostic performance of these AI models for vaginal pathology are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of publicly available AI models for image-based identification of vaginal pathology and compare their performance with expert physician review.
STUDY DESIGN: This diagnostic‑accuracy study assessed 25 deidentified clinical images representing various vaginal conditions. Four publicly accessible AI models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Grok) and 2 board-certified urogynecology and reconstructive pelvic surgery physicians independently provided top 3 and top 1 diagnoses, malignancy identification, diagnostic confidence (0-100%), and triage recommendations using a standardized prompt.
RESULTS: Experts achieved top 3 diagnostic accuracy of 84% and top 1 accuracy of 66%. AI systems demonstrated variable performance, with mean top 3 accuracy of 51.8% and a mean top 1 accuracy of 32.5%. ChatGPT and Gemini achieved the highest AI performance (68% and 68% top 3 accuracy; 44% and 52% top 1 accuracy, respectively). In malignant cases (n=3), the correct diagnosis was included in the top 3 in 83.5% of evaluations across both groups, with AI slightly more likely to rank malignancy first. AI systems recommended urgent evaluation more frequently than experts (77% vs 22%).
CONCLUSIONS: Publicly available AI models demonstrate moderate accuracy in identifying vaginal pathology from images but perform below expert clinicians. While some models approach expert performance in detecting malignancy, they tend to over-recommend urgent care, highlighting a limited but evolving role for patient-facing AI in image-based triage.

articles.title: Data Sharing in Autism Research: Case Studies From the United States and the United Kingdom and Recommendations for Practice.
articles.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
articles.authors: Grant A, Ellis R, Axbey H et al.
articles.abstract: Data sharing has become common in Autism research. In the context of a history of eugenics, additional risks are present, including re-identification, misinterpretation and deficit-framing of Autism. We, a group of community members and researchers, aimed to (a) describe our 'opt-in' data-sharing approach in two Community-Based Participatory Research studies based in the United States (AASPIRE Outcomes Project) and the United Kingdom (Autism from Menstruation to Menopause; AM2M), (b) report on how many people opted to data share and (c) co-develop recommendations for ethical data sharing in Autism research. In the AASPIRE Outcomes Project, 680 of 870 (78.2%) participants opted to share quantitative survey data, with no differences by demographic, disability, or health characteristics. In AM2M, 36 of 100 (36.0%) participants opted to share longitudinal qualitative data, with significant variation when controlling for family-wise error rate by menopause status (p = .007). We provide recommendations for ethical data sharing in Autism research, directed at governments, policy makers, research funders, data repositories, ethics boards and researchers. We favour approaches that centre autonomy and dignity, including, 'opt-in' data-sharing consent models and Autistic community participation. We hope that these recommendations will balance data-sharing benefits with strong protections for Autistic research participants.Lay AbstractData sharing is when people's information from a study are anonymised (names taken out) and shared in an online library. Other researchers can use this data to answer new research questions at reduced cost.Some funders say researchers must share data. However, some Autistic people worry this could be bad for Autistic people. One solution is letting research participants decide if they want to share their answers. This is called 'opt-in' data sharing.We are a neurodiverse group of Autism researchers and community members. We had three goals:1. Share how we handled data sharing in studies in the United States and the United Kingdom;2. Say how many people agreed to data share3. Make recommendations for ethical data sharing in Autism research.We had concerns about data sharing, including not keeping participants' identities private and researchers doing studies that were dehumanising or used deficit views of Autism. For this reason, the U.S. study decided not to share interview data, and both studies used separate data-sharing information…

articles.title: Oral-gut-vaginal microbiota crosstalk with host immunity and metabolism in pregnancy disorders.
articles.authors: Ge Y, Weng H, Chen G et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy represents a critical stage in which both maternal and fetal health are of paramount importance. This review systematically examines the temporal dynamics of maternal microbial communities across multiple anatomical niches-including the vaginal, intestinal, and oral ecosystems-during pregnancy, and explores their profound connections with gestational health. We highlight the specific associations between site-specific microbial dysbiosis and adverse outcomes such as preterm birth, gestational diabetes, and preeclampsia. In addition, we delineate the mechanisms by which the immune microenvironment at the maternal-fetal interface maintains dynamic equilibrium under microbial regulation, and underscores the role of microbial metabolites as transgenerational signaling molecules critical for fetal development. Furthermore, we dissect the pathological disruption of the "microbiota-immune-metabolism" network in pregnancy-related disorders and evaluate the potential of targeted strategies-including probiotic supplementation and nutritional interventions-to restore microbial homeostasis and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. Finally, we emphasize the contribution of breast milk microbiota and immune components to offspring immune programming and outline future translational research directions, aiming to provide a scientific foundation for microbiota-based monitoring and early intervention in pregnancy health.

articles.title: Interventions to prevent suicide and suicidal thoughts or behaviours in the perinatal period: a global mixed-methods systematic review.
articles.authors: Fernandez Turienzo C, Erpolat YD, De Backer K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicide is a leading cause of maternal death during the perinatal period. While routine enquiry and identification is widely recommended, evidence on comprehensive interventions remains limited. This review evaluated global evidence on the effectiveness of interventions for perinatal suicide, associated thoughts and behaviours, and key implementation features.
METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods systematic review using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology. We searched eight databases and other sources from inception to December 3, 2025, for global evidence across all income settings without language restrictions. We included studies evaluating interventions, programmes or strategies reporting on our primary outcome: perinatal suicide or suicidal thoughts or behaviours (including ideation, self-harm, attempts) during pregnancy or one year after birth. Data were extracted and appraised for methodological quality. Meta-analysis was not possible due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity; data were synthesised using a convergent integrated approach. PROSPERO: CRD42025625903.
FINDINGS: We screened 27,045 records; 19 records representing nine studies were included: three randomised controlled trials, one secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial, one non-randomised controlled trial, one quasi-experimental study, one cross-sectional descriptive study, one economic modelling, and one qualitative study. Studies were conducted between 2011 and 2025 in North America, Europe and Asia and included 3613 participants from at risk or disadvantaged populations across eight studies, plus a simulated cohort of 1000. We found trials of indirect clinical interventions targeting parenting or attachment did not reduce suicidality, whereas task-shared behavioural activation psychotherapy targeting depressive drivers, was associated with an 80% reduction in odds of suicidal ideation at three months in a secondary trial analysis. System or community-level strategies in three trials and the modelling were associated with reduced suicide or suicidal ideation by integrating routine screening within multidisciplinary pathways that ensured immediate linkage to care. Informal or crisis support mechanisms facilitated immediate access and worked as protective buffers against self-harm in two feasibility and qualitative studies; faith practices helped counter barriers to formal care while helplines remained limited by them.
INTERPRETATION: Our results…

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes of Kielland's rotational forceps-assisted vaginal births in a tertiary care center.
articles.authors: Naseef P, Leps C, Almoi E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of second-stage Cesarean section (CS) have increased substantially, contributing to higher maternal morbidity and long-term risks in future pregnancies, including repeat CS and placenta accreta spectrum. Reducing unnecessary second-stage CS is therefore an important goal in modern obstetric care. Fetal malposition, particularly occiput transverse and posterior positions, is a key cause of labor dystocia and operative delivery. While several interventions exist, their success is variable. Kielland's rotational forceps can facilitate vaginal birth and potentially avoid CS, but their use has declined due to safety concerns and limited training, leaving a gap in contemporary evidence comparing outcomes with other delivery methods.
OBJECTIVE: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes between rotational and nonrotational forceps use in a tertiary care setting.
STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of all forceps-assisted births at a tertiary care hospital in Toronto, between January 2014 and December 2021. Maternal outcomes included postpartum hemorrhage defined as estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and significant obstetric anal sphincter injuries defined as 3B, 3C and fourth degree perineal lacerations. Neonatal outcomes included Apgar scores, cord blood gases, need for resuscitation, and neonatal head trauma.
RESULTS: Among 1606 forceps-assisted births, 26 (1.6%) required Kielland's rotational forceps. Episiotomy was universal in the rotational group (n=26/26, 100%) compared with 90.1% (n=1423/1580) in the nonrotational group. Significant OASIS occurred less frequently with rotational forceps (7.6%, n=2/26 vs 10.8%, n=172/1580), while rates of PPH were comparable (26.9%, n=7/26 vs 28.8%, n=456/1580). No major PPH (≥1000 mL) or shoulder dystocia occurred in the rotational group. Low 1-minute Apgar scores (<7) were more common in the rotational group (26.9%, n=7/26 vs 14%, n=227/1580), but all infants achieved scores ≥7 at 5 minutes. No cases of cephalohematoma, subgaleal hematoma, or intracranial hemorrhage occurred in the rotational group.
CONCLUSION: Kielland's rotational forceps are a safe alternative to second-stage CS when performed by experienced operators. Their use was not associated with excess major maternal morbidity or significant neonatal trauma, in comparison to nonrotational forceps. Our data support efforts to transfer these skills to trainees and larger studies are needed to confirm these single…

articles.title: Fluctuating Methylation-based ctDNA Detection in NSCLC Surveillance: Implications for Serial Monitoring and Specificity.
articles.authors: Cho JM, Clark G, Bogardus M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) addresses key limitations of traditional radiographic and tissue-based screening by providing a noninvasive alternative for the surveillance of NSCLC. In our study, we aim to evaluate trends in the performance of a commercially available methylation-based ctDNA test, characterize patient factors associated with fluctuating ctDNA positivity, and evaluate the clinical implications of serial monitoring.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who underwent lung resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy for NSCLC followed by posttreatment ctDNA testing from 2024 to 2025. The primary outcomes include patient- and tumor-related risk factors associated with ctDNA positivity. A subgroup analysis of the ctDNA-positive group evaluated clinical events and genomic profiling that may influence transient ctDNA positivity.
RESULTS: Of the 85 patients studied, 17 (20%) had at least one positive ctDNA test. Both ctDNA-positive and negative groups had similar patient and tumor-related features. Ten (59%) patients with a positive result subsequently tested negative, and 11 (65%) had a ctDNA tumor fraction near the limit of detection (LOD) without radiographic recurrence. No consistent associations were found with timing, adjuvant therapy, inflammatory markers, or tumor genomics. Three patients with ctDNA fractions above the limit of detection had confirmed recurrence; none in the ctDNA-negative group had disease recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the utility of serial ctDNA testing is promising for NSCLC surveillance, isolated low-level positivity may not warrant clinical action. We observe frequent low-level, transient ctDNA positivity without radiographic evidence of recurrence, suggesting limitations in assay specificity and need for trend-based interpretation instead of isolated testing.

articles.title: Personalizing postpartum cardiovascular prevention after preeclampsia: Is routine statin therapy justified in normotensive survivors? A critical narrative review.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Cardiovascular risk and prevention
articles.ta: Int J Cardiol Cardiovasc Risk Prev
articles.authors: Naja S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-related cardiovascular risk-enhancing factor associated with increased lifetime cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. However, long-term cardiovascular risk varies according to postpartum blood pressure, metabolic health, and development of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
CURRENT CLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS: Current guidelines recognize preeclampsia as a risk-enhancing factor to support cardiovascular risk assessment and shared decision-making regarding lipid-lowering therapy. However, preeclampsia alone is not an indication for routine statin therapy, and no postpartum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) target is recommended solely on the basis of previous preeclampsia.
EVIDENCE GAP: Existing evidence is derived mainly from observational studies involving heterogeneous populations. Few studies have evaluated women who remain normotensive with favorable metabolic profiles, and no completed randomized trial has demonstrated that postpartum statin therapy improves long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
MAIN ARGUMENT: Lifelong cardiovascular surveillance is warranted after preeclampsia, but routine statin therapy for all survivors is not supported. Lipid-lowering therapy should be individualized according to overall cardiovascular risk.
FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Future studies should identify high-risk phenotypes, validate postpartum risk prediction tools such as PREVENT, and determine whether selected women benefit from targeted statin therapy.

articles.title: Effect of group-based training interventions on mothers' knowledge about menstruation in the selected districts of Jimma zone: A controlled quasi-experimental study.
articles.authors: Olika AK, Debelew GT, Birhanu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Menstrual health plays an important role in adolescent development; however, many girls in resource-constrained settings enter menarche with inadequate knowledge due to restricted access to information and the influence of prevailing social and cultural norms. Strengthening mothers' knowledge may provide an indirect but effective approach for improving menstrual awareness among adolescent girls. In Ethiopia, little evidence exists regarding interventions specifically designed to improve maternal knowledge of menstruation. This study therefore assessed the impact of group-based training on mothers' knowledge, aiming to enhance understanding and dispel misconceptions. A quasi-experimental controlled study was conducted in Omo Nada and Shabe Sombo districts of Jimma Zone, Ethiopia, among 390 mothers of adolescent girls aged 10 to 19 years. One district received the intervention, while the other served as a comparison area. The intervention group participated in six structured sessions on menstrual health and hygiene, whereas the comparison group received routine health education. Data were collected using pre-tested questionnaires at baseline and endline and analyzed using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression models to account for clustering within villages and kebeles. Following the intervention, the proportion of mothers with adequate menstrual knowledge increased from 46.7% to 99.5% in the intervention group. After adjusting for potential confounders and clustering effects, mothers in the intervention area were more than seven times as likely to have adequate menstrual knowledge compared with those in the comparison area (AOR = 7.55, 95% CI: 4.69-12.16). The findings suggest that a group-based, mother-focused educational intervention was associated with substantial improvements in maternal knowledge of menstruation. Such interventions may contribute to improving menstrual health literacy among mothers and, ultimately, support better menstrual health outcomes for adolescent girls.

articles.title: Management of a Tubo-Ovarian Abscess: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study of Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Failure of First-Line Medical Therapy.
articles.authors: Satouf A
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical characteristics, antibiotic management, and outcomes of a consecutive cohort of women admitted with tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) and to determine the factors associated with failure of first-line medical therapy.
DESIGN AND SETTING: This is a retrospective cohort study, with the setting of the Gynaecology Department at the University Hospitals of Leicester, United Kingdom.
POPULATION: A total of 61 women who had a working diagnosis of TOA were identified during the study period; 14 (23%) were excluded when an alternative final diagnosis was made, and a further three women were excluded due to incomplete outcome documentation, so 44 women with a confirmed diagnosis of TOA remained for analysis.
METHODS: Demographic data, together with the microbiological, radiological, antibiotic, and procedural data, were systematically extracted from clinical records and coded. The outcomes were compared between women whose abscess resolved with antibiotics alone and those who required radiological or surgical drainage, using Fisher's exact test for categorical variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: These are the success of first-line antibiotic therapy, need for image-guided or surgical drainage, and length of hospital stay (LOS).
RESULTS: Median age was 41 years (IQR: 33.5-51), and median BMI was 28 kg/m² (IQR: 24-32.5). Among the 44 women with complete documented treatment outcomes, antibiotics alone were successful in 31 (70.5%), while 13 (29.5%) required further treatment with image-guided drainage or surgery. Procedures included image-guided drainage (n = 2), laparoscopic drainage or definitive laparoscopic surgery (n = 5), laparoscopic surgery converted to laparotomy (n = 3), and primary laparotomy (n = 3). A prior history of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) (62% vs 3%, p < 0.001), previous admission with TOA (46% vs 13%, p = 0.043), and an abscess diameter >6.5 cm (64% vs 25%, p = 0.033) were each significantly more common among women whose medical management failed. LOS was also significantly longer in women who failed medical therapy (median 6 vs 4 days, p = 0.030). Almost a quarter (23%) of women initially coded as TOA (14/61 excluded cases) ultimately had an alternative diagnosis established on imaging, most commonly hydrosalpinx or salpingitis.
CONCLUSIONS: First-line antibiotic therapy resolved TOA in approximately 7 of 10 women with a documented treatment outcome in this…

articles.title: Beyond Layer Count at Caesarean Delivery: A Focused Clinical Review and Trial-Design Framework for Endometrium-Sparing Uterine Closure.
articles.authors: Puttakul W, Kantathavorn N, Chotichavanrattanakun K et al.
articles.abstract: Debate about uterine closure at Caesarean delivery often centers on layer count, although scar healing also depends on tissue handling, suture technique and material, operative context, and maternal factors. Layers describe anatomical repair planes, not the number of individual stitches. This focused clinical review asks whether true anatomical three-layer endometrium-sparing closure improves clinically meaningful scar outcomes compared with an optimized two-layer endometrium-sparing repair. We classified evidence as direct, near-direct, closely related, or indirect, without pooling biologically non-equivalent techniques. No completed head-to-head trial was identified. The closest randomized evidence evaluates a standardized closure package and suggests improved 6-month scar morphology relative to traditional double-layer closure; it does not test the independent benefit of a third anatomical layer. Component-level findings support precise reporting of endometrial handling, myometrial apposition, locking, bite geometry, tension, and suture material. Maternal and obstetric risk factors must also be considered; nutritional effects on uterine niche formation remain insufficiently established. Current evidence neither identifies a universally superior layer count nor demonstrates prevention of Caesarean scar pregnancy or placenta accreta spectrum by a particular closure strategy. We propose a trial comparing two fully specified, optimized endometrium-sparing packages with equivalent surgeon training and fidelity monitoring, blinded standardized imaging, symptom and reproductive outcomes, and prospective assessment of safety, feasibility, and maternal, operator, and center factors. This framework separates plausible healing mechanisms from demonstrated clinical benefit and defines the comparison needed to determine whether an anatomical third layer adds value.

articles.title: Serum testosterone and uric acid: Key biomarkers for predicting response to drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol tablets (II) in adolescents polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Chen X, Teng Y, He Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) poses diagnostic and management challenges. Although combined oral contraceptives (COCs) can improve symptoms, treatment response varies.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy of drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol tablets (II) (DRSP/EE (II)) and explore predictors of therapeutic response.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective study.
METHODS: Adolescents with PCOS and healthy controls were retrospectively included. Among patients treated with DRSP/EE (II), clinical, biochemical, and sex-hormone indices were assessed at baseline and at 3 and 6 months, including total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), free androgen index (FAI), uric acid (UA), and lipid profile. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with treatment response, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess discriminative performance.
RESULTS: The PCOS group had higher androgen levels and lower SHBG than controls. TT and FAI decreased significantly after 3 and 6 months of DRSP/EE (II), while SHBG increased. Triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, and HDL-C increased. Responders had higher baseline TT (2.03±0.59 vs. 1.55±0.46 nmol/L; FDR P=0.009) and lower UA (314.43±61.33 vs. 372.16±77.16 μmol/L; FDR P=0.023) than non-responders. Multivariable logistic regression showed that TT (OR=6.893; P=0.004) and UA (OR=0.984; P=0.002) were independently associated with treatment response. ROC analyses showed AUCs of 0.716 for TT and 0.713 for UA, while the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.815, with 87.8% sensitivity and 75.0% specificity.
CONCLUSION: DRSP/EE (II) effectively improves hyperandrogenism in adolescent PCOS but may worsen lipid profiles. Baseline TT and UA are promising predictors of clinical response and may facilitate individualized management.

articles.title: National perioperative outcomes of sacrocolpopexy versus colporrhaphy with apical suspension for pelvic organ prolapse: A retrospective cohort study (2008-2021).
articles.authors: Sebai T, Toutounji K, Abdul Khalek J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects up to 40% of women and often requires surgical repair, which can result in unfavorable outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: We compared perioperative outcomes of anteroposterior colporrhaphy with apical suspension versus minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy (SCP), hypothesizing differences in outcomes between the two approaches.
DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database from 2008 to 2021, including 15,015 women aged 18-89 years.
METHODS: Patients who underwent colporrhaphy with apical suspension (n=6,906) were compared to those who underwent laparoscopic or robotic SCP (n=8,109). We recorded baseline demographics and comorbidities. Primary outcomes included overall complications, infections, urinary tract infections (UTIs), unplanned readmissions, and length of hospital stay. Multivariable logistic regression and 1:1 propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounding factors.
RESULTS: Patients undergoing SCP were younger and healthier at baseline. After adjustment, colporrhaphy was associated with significantly higher odds of any complication (adjusted OR 1.34), minor complications (OR 1.42), infections (OR 1.35), UTIs (OR 1.57), and prolonged hospital stay >2 days (OR 1.49). After propensity score matching, rates of complications remained higher in the colporrhaphy group: Overall complications (8.5% vs. 6.5%), infections (6.7% vs. 5.0%), and UTIs (5.6% vs. 3.6%) (all p<0.001). Severe complications, reoperation, and mortality rates were low and similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: Minimally invasive SCP may be associated with more favorable short-term perioperative outcomes than colporrhaphy with apical suspension, supporting its consideration in appropriately selected patients.

articles.title: Reproductive History, Biological Indicators, and Pain Vulnerability in Aging Women: A Multi-Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Zhang W, Wang Z, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain disproportionately affects women, yet the relationship between female reproductive history and long-term pain vulnerability remains insufficiently understood. Using three population-based cohorts from the UK, China, and the US, we evaluated associations between reproductive factors and pain-related phenotypes in aging women. Endogenous reproductive milestones showed nonlinear associations with pain risk. Specifically, both earlier and later ages at menarche and menopause, as well as shorter and longer reproductive lifespans, were linked to higher pain vulnerability. Childbirth-related characteristics, such as higher parity, earlier age at first birth, and longer interbirth intervals, were also associated with increased pain vulnerability. Reproductive surgeries and exogenous hormone use were consistently associated with pain phenotypes, with timing-dependent effects. In the UK Biobank, reproductive factors showed both shared and site-specific associations across seven chronic pain sites. These reproductive-pain associations were amplified among women with higher adiposity, greater socioeconomic deprivation, a history of depression or anxiety, and hypertension. Exploratory mediation analyses implicated inflammatory, hormonal, and metabolic indicators as potential biological correlates of several reproductive-chronic pain associations. Together, these findings highlight reproductive history as an important life-course factor associated with pain vulnerability and provide insights for future studies investigating mechanisms and risk stratification of chronic pain in women.

articles.title: Toward a Cross-Pathway Susceptibility Profile for Urinary Tract Infection After Pelvic Floor Reconstruction.
articles.authors: Pop-Lodromanean D, Grigore N, Hașegan A et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Urinary tract infection (UTI) is a frequent early complication after pelvic floor reconstruction. This study examined whether perioperative UTI is associated primarily with the surgical approach or with recurring patient-, disease-, and care-related factors.
METHODS: Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for 376 women treated with pelvic floor reconstructive surgery from 2020 through 2025. According to the principal reconstructive procedure, the cohort was divided into three surgical strata: mesh-based sacrospinous fixation accompanied by transobturator tape (TOT) or tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) insertion; combined anterior and posterior colporrhaphy with a midurethral sling; and anterior and posterior colporrhaphy performed without an associated sling procedure. The study endpoint was a symptomatic urinary tract infection confirmed by urine culture during the initial hospital admission. Associations between candidate predictors and infection were estimated separately within each surgical stratum. Stratum-level effect estimates were then integrated using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model to obtain pooled odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Cross-stratum variability was quantified through Cochran's Q test and the I2 statistic.
RESULTS: Of the 376 women included, 71 experienced a symptomatic, culture-confirmed infection during the perioperative period, producing an overall event rate of 18.9%. The proportion of affected patients varied numerically among the three reconstructive pathways, although no statistically significant difference was observed in the unadjusted comparison. When risk estimates were synthesized across surgical strata, higher odds of infection were observed in postmenopausal women, patients older than 63 years, those with grade III-IV pelvic organ prolapse, women with morbid obesity, patients requiring bladder catheterization for more than 3 days, and those undergoing hysterectomy during the same operation. The principal significant associations showed little or no between-stratum heterogeneity, suggesting a consistent direction of association across surgical approaches, although the limited number of subgroups (k = 3) and instances of non-estimable models restrict definitive conclusions regarding reproducibility; further validation in larger cohorts is warranted.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative urinary tract infection after pelvic floor reconstructive surgery appears to reflect a multifactorial susceptibility…

articles.title: Profiles of emotion regulation difficulties in the transition to menopause: a latent profile analysis.
articles.authors: Brandão T
articles.abstract: The menopausal transition is associated with heightened psychological vulnerability, yet individual differences in emotion regulation (ER) during this period remain poorly understood. This study applied latent profile analysis to identify distinct ER difficulty profiles in women during menopause transition and examined attachment anxiety and avoidance as predictors of profile membership. A sample of 455 women aged 40-60 years at different stages of the menopausal transition (late reproductive, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal) participated in this cross-sectional study. Four profiles were identified: High ER Difficulties (11.2%), Moderate ER Difficulties (48.1%), Emotional Clarity Deficit (11.4%), and Low ER Difficulties (29.2%). Profiles differed significantly on depression, anxiety, stress, menopause-specific somatic and psychological symptoms, and personal burnout (all p < .001, with large effects), with one key exception: the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile did not differ from the Low ER profile on any outcome despite presenting the highest lack of emotional clarity scores in the solution. Attachment anxiety and avoidance both predicted membership in the High and Moderate ER profiles, whereas only attachment avoidance uniquely predicted the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile. These findings provide initial person-centered evidence of ER heterogeneity in the menopausal transition. The Emotional Clarity Deficit profile, which was statistically associated with attachment avoidance, represents a configuration not captured by severity-based approaches; however, its clinical significance and stability remain to be established through replication in independent samples and longitudinal research.

articles.title: Hysteroscopy for Suspected Uterine Malignant Tumor: A Nationwide Survey of Practice Patterns and Oncologic Concerns Among Gynecologic Oncology Institutions in Japan.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Sakai K, Takashima A, Nagasaka K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Hysteroscopy for suspected endometrial cancer (EC) remains controversial because of concerns about transtubal tumor cell dissemination. However, its potential utility has been reported for diagnostic evaluation when a definitive diagnosis cannot be established by conventional endometrial sampling and as part of fertility-sparing treatment. In Japan, hysteroscopic surgery for EC and atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) is not yet covered by national health insurance. We investigated current practice and perceptions among gynecologic oncology institutions in Japan.
METHODS: A web-based questionnaire developed by the Japan Society for Hysteroscopy was distributed to members of the Japan Society of Gynecologic Oncology between May and June 2024. It addressed the use of diagnostic, inpatient operative, and office operative hysteroscopy for suspected EC, during fertility-sparing treatment, and for differentiating corpus from cervical origin, together with reasons for reluctance and views on insurance coverage. One response per institution was analyzed.
RESULTS: Responses from 205 institutions were analyzed. For suspected EC, 31.2% of institutions never performed diagnostic hysteroscopy, 49.8% performed it selectively but reluctantly, and 19.0% performed it actively or routinely; the figures for inpatient operative hysteroscopy were similar (37.1%, 43.9%, and 19.0%). The main reason for reluctance was concern about peritoneal dissemination (69.7%). Diagnostic hysteroscopy was used during fertility-sparing treatment by 33.2% of institutions and for differentiating corpus from cervical origin by 13.7%. Overall, 62.4% of institutions desired insurance coverage of hysteroscopic surgery for EC and AEH, rising to 91.5% among those actively using hysteroscopy.
CONCLUSIONS: Hysteroscopy for suspected EC is used cautiously and heterogeneously in Japan, reflecting concern about oncologic safety. Standardized safety protocols, Japanese outcome data, and an appropriate reimbursement framework are needed.

articles.title: Use of transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage in the Nordic countries: A survey of incidences and indications.
articles.authors: Hoffmann CH, Hansen LK, Lantto A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical guidelines for cervical cerclage vary in terms of indications and patient management. In this study, we investigated the incidence, indications, surgical techniques, timing of placement, and peri- and postoperative care for both transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage use in the Nordic countries.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study was a cross-sectional survey. An electronic questionnaire was developed and distributed via an electronic data capture system (REDCap) to an obstetrician from all birth units in Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden. The primary outcome was the reported incidence of transvaginal cerclage, both history- and ultrasound-indicated, and of transabdominal cerclage.
RESULTS: The estimated incidence per 100 000 births of history-indicated transvaginal cerclage was 231 in DK, 70 in FI, 140 in IS, 133 in NO, and 166 in SE. For ultrasound-indicated transvaginal cerclage, the estimated incidence per 100 000 births was 166 in DK, 21 in FI, 140 in IS, 17 in NO, and 59 in SE. For transabdominal cerclage, the estimated incidence was 63 in DK, 7 in FI, 28 in IS, 31 in NO, and 18 in SE.
CONCLUSIONS: There is substantial variation in the use of cervical cerclage between the Nordic countries. We advocate for a harmonized Nordic model of cerclage care to ensure equitable and consistent practice across countries, coupled with a Nordic research collaboration network that can drive knowledge generation and implementation across the region.

articles.title: Genetic variants in recurrent euploid pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Aminbeidokhti M, Halstead M, Rodriguez-Escriba M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) affects ~ 5% of couples. Known causes of RPL include aneuploidies and unbalanced chromosome rearrangements, however the genetic basis of losses with normal karyotype and chromosomal microarray analysis remains unclear. We hypothesized that deleterious variants in genes essential for early development, including genes previously associated only with neonatal lethal disorders, contribute to RPL.
METHODS: Genome sequencing was performed on 118 families with unexplained, euploid RPL; 95% lacked major fetal structural anomalies on ultrasound. A tiered variant prioritization pipeline integrated model organism, human population databases, essential developmental pathways, and fetal transcriptomic profiles. Rare variants (allele frequency ≤ 0.1%) were assessed and confirmed by orthogonal methods. Parental samples were analyzed for mosaicism.
RESULTS: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants were identified in 18 families (15.3%) across 17 genes. These include six families with DHCR7, PIEZO1, PIGV, PRF1, SLC12A3, and SMN1 biallelic variants; two cases with ALAS2 and IKBKG hemizygous variants; and four pregnancies with heterozygous alterations inherited from affected parents with MYH3 and TNNI3 variants, and from asymptomatic parents with SCN5A and FLT4 variants. Additionally, four families had presumed de novo heterozygous variants in the EFTUD2, HNRNPK, FGFR2, and KAT6A genes (associated with autosomal dominant conditions), while two exhibited parental germline mosaicism in the FGFR2 and PORCN genes. Variants of uncertain significance were detected in 12 families (10.2%) across the ABCB7, CLPB, CRB2, FBN1, FLT4, GJA1, LYST, MAGED2, PTPN14, RNF213, TLR8, and VPS35L genes. Of 28 genes with plausible variants, 13 genes were previously implicated in perinatal lethality, whereas 15 were novel candidates. Overall, variants in candidate genes were inherited in 80% of families. Four additional families (3.4%) had biallelic ultra-rare variants in genes, which are involved in fundamental developmental pathways but not yet linked to human disease, pointing to a possible role in prenatal lethality. Transcriptomic analyses supported novel gene involvement in hematopoiesis, cardiovascular development, inflammation, and fluid homeostasis processes.
CONCLUSIONS: Genome sequencing revealed plausible monogenic etiologies for unexplained euploid pregnancy loss, providing new insights into the biology of early human lethality, phenotypic…

articles.title: The future of maternal mortality measurement: implications of reduced DHS availability.
articles.authors: Ahmed SMA, Cresswell JA, Aujla M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) have historically filled key data gaps in global maternal mortality monitoring. Amid uncertainty regarding funding and their future availability, this study evaluates the potential impact of reduced DHS data availability on United Nations maternal mortality estimates.
METHODS: We conducted a modelling analysis using the UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group's BMat model to assess the contribution of DHS data to maternal mortality estimates. We compared three scenarios: [1] exclusion of all DHS data [2], exclusion of DHS conducted since 2015, and [3] a counterfactual with the "status quo" including all eligible data sources. Changes in 2023 maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and uncertainty intervals were evaluated globally, regionally, and nationally.
RESULTS: DHS contributed 21% of all country-year data and were the sole source of data in 23 countries. Excluding all DHS data led to a 15% reduction in the point estimate of the global MMR and a 70% increase in uncertainty. The post-2015 exclusion scenario resulted in a 10% global MMR reduction. These effects were most pronounced in countries and regions lacking alternative data sources (e.g., sub-Saharan Africa and Oceania regions). The exclusion narrowed uncertainty intervals in a few cases, mainly where DHS estimates were less consistent with other national data sources.
CONCLUSIONS: A sustained reduction in the availability of DHS data would substantially affect global maternal mortality estimation, particularly in data-scarce and high-burden settings. The findings highlight the urgent need to strengthen sustainable national data systems, including civil registration and vital statistics and health management information systems.

articles.title: Hugo RAS versus da Vinci Xi for robot-assisted simple hysterectomy in endometrial cancer: a concurrent-period comparison of operative efficiency, cost structure, and the cost of early adoption.
articles.authors: Sakamoto I, Nozaki T, Fukada N et al.
articles.abstract: Assessing a newly introduced robotic platform is complicated by calendar-time confounding and early institutional experience. We compared Hugo robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with da Vinci Xi for robot-assisted simple hysterectomy in endometrial cancer, restricting the primary analysis to their concurrent-use period. This single-centre retrospective cohort comprised 219 patients with clinical stage I disease operated between May 2018 and November 2025; procedures with lymphadenectomy or sentinel lymph node biopsy were excluded to standardise surgical content. The primary concurrent-period analysis included 67 procedures (da Vinci Xi 37, Hugo RAS 30), and cost data were analysable for 61. The adjusted mean difference in total operative time was 16.3 min (95% confidence interval [CI] 6.0-26.6), decreasing to 6.1 min (95% CI - 0.7 to 13.0) in an exploratory analysis excluding the first ten Hugo RAS procedures. Adjusted ratios for recorded consumable and operative costs were 0.808 and 0.923, respectively. These estimates compare early Hugo RAS use with established da Vinci Xi use; the exploratory exclusion cannot isolate learning from platform effects or predict steady-state performance. The findings apply to simple hysterectomy without nodal assessment and do not establish comparative safety, oncologic equivalence, or overall economic superiority.

articles.title: Understanding family planning progress in Malawi: a mixed-methods case study.
articles.authors: Alhassan N, Chifungo C, Memon ZA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over the last three decades, Malawi has achieved remarkable progress in family planning. Modern contraceptive prevalence rate increased from 7% in 1992 to 66% in 2024. From a country where family planning was banned in the 1960s, Malawi is now one of the best performing countries in contraceptive access and equity in sub-Saharan Africa.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the drivers of Malawi’s family planning progress from 1992 to 2024. We comprehensively examined policy, programme, financing, community, household, couple and individual-level drivers of Malawi’s accelerated progress in modern contraceptive use and equity.
METHODS: We relied on a mixed-methods case study approach that combined data from a narrative literature review, secondary analysis of Malawi Demographic and Health Surveys, policy and programme review and primary qualitative data. The narrative literature, policy and programme reviews examined the broader policy and socio-economic drivers that accelerated contraceptive use. The quantitative analysis decomposed the contribution of factors responsible for the modern contraceptive prevalence rate change between 2005 and 2016. The qualitative data provided contextual insights from key national stakeholders and community members on key factors influencing contraceptive use. The results from these data sources were integrated and synthesised to provide a comprehensive understanding of the drivers of contraceptive use and equity in Malawi.
RESULTS: The synthesis of results across the different data sources showed four essential drivers of Malawi’s progress in family planning. These were (1) creation of an enabling family planning policy environment through effective formulation and implementation of policies and programmes, (2) effective demand creation interventions that increased knowledge of family planning methods and addressed misinformation, (3) improved supply of contraceptive services via community outreach mechanisms and deployment of trained health workers at the local level and (4) socio-economic progress and increased women’s decision making.
CONCLUSION: The results highlight important lessons and family planning best practices that can be implemented in low-and middle-income countries experiencing slow progress in modern contraceptive use. Malawi’s training and deployment of a lower cadre of health workers to provide injectables can be used to bridge inequalities in contraceptive access in countries with limited health…

articles.title: Lao PDR's achievements in family planning: a mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: Chanthavilay P, Sengchaleun V, Pabouriboune P et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The use of modern contraceptives and family planning (FP) services has increased globally; however, progress varies across countries and regions. The current research aims to examine the key socioecological determinants driving the demand for and utilisation of modern contraceptive methods in the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), providing insights into the factors that facilitate contraceptive uptake.
METHODOLOGY: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach including: (1) a systematic literature review to synthesise existing evidence, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data to identify demographic and behavioural trends, (3) a desk review of relevant policies and programmes to evaluate the policy landscape and (4) community-based qualitative design to explore sociocultural and contextual factors supporting FP uptake.
RESULTS: Modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR) rose steadily from 38.6% in 2005 to 56.3% in 2017, associated with education, household wealth, contraceptive knowledge and age at first sex, alongside marked geographic and ethnic disparities that persisted throughout. Policy analysis identified three programmatic phases: foundation-building (1988–2005), scale-up aligned with the Millennium Development Goals (2005–2015) and an equity-focused phase emphasising adolescent health (2015–present). Qualitative findings revealed five interconnected themes driving FP progress in Lao PDR: political commitment, financing sustainability, health systems strengthening, community-driven demand generation and women’s reproductive agency. While strong policy commitment and expanded service delivery have improved access, donor dependency, geographic barriers for rural and ethnic minority populations and persistent gender-based decision-making constraints continue to limit equitable contraceptive use.
CONCLUSION: Lao PDR’s FP success reflects the simultaneous alignment of political will, financing structures, service delivery and shifting social norms. Sustaining and extending these gains will require a structured domestic financing transition, strengthened commodity supply and workforce systems, expansion of youth-friendly services into rural and ethnic minority areas and continued investment in gender-transformative community engagement to translate increased spousal communication into genuine shared decision-making.

articles.title: How Bolivia became a positive outlier in family planning: an in-depth mixed-methods case study.
articles.authors: Cardona C, Andersen L, Branisa B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bolivia made remarkable progress in increasing modern contraceptive use among all women of reproductive age, achieving an exponential annual growth rate exceeding 5% between 1989 and 2016—from 8% to 32.4%. Based on a systematic, criteria-based country selection process implemented by the Exemplars in Global Health coalition, Bolivia was identified as a case for in-depth analysis of progress in family planning. In this study, we aimed to identify the socioeconomic, demographic, political, programmatic and health system factors that have contributed to Bolivia’s success in family planning.
METHODS: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach, incorporating results from: (1) a systematic literature review, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data, (3) a desk review of policies and programmes and (4) qualitative analysis of primary data. This study summarises the findings from these four analyses.
RESULTS: Bolivia’s progress in family planning outcomes is the result of a multifaceted approach emphasising political commitment, community engagement, health system strengthening and innovative service delivery mechanisms. Key initiatives such as the Universal Maternal and Child Health Insurance and the Revolving Fund for Contraceptives were instrumental in improving the accessibility of family planning services. These efforts ensured a steady supply of contraceptives and reduced financial barriers for marginalised populations particularly in rural and underserved areas.
CONCLUSION: Bolivia’s success in family planning since 1989 has been driven by strong political commitment and policy reforms that created a supportive sexual and reproductive health policy landscape. This, combined with the contributions of non-governmental organisations, has improved access to family planning services. Despite these advancements, service gaps persist for adolescents and marginalised groups, highlighting the need for continued investment in education and healthcare. This study provides valuable insights for enhancing contraceptive use and meeting family planning needs in similar global contexts.

articles.title: Drivers of increased voluntary modern contraceptive use in Kenya: a mixed-methods analysis.
articles.authors: Ontiri S, Oenga D, Chabeda S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An analysis of 130 countries identified Kenya as one of six nations that significantly increased both its modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR) and family planning (FP) demand satisfied with modern methods between 1994 and 2020. This study aimed to identify the major socio-ecological determinants that contributed to increased use of modern contraceptives in Kenya and to provide an in-depth, contextualised understanding of the specific policies, strategies and programmes implemented by Kenya to achieve this remarkable success.
METHODS: This mixed-methods study combined quantitative analysis of nationally representative datasets, a systematic review of peer-reviewed and grey literature, policy, programme and financial analysis of government and donor initiatives, and qualitative research including key informant interviews and focus group discussions. Data were analysed thematically and triangulated across sources to identify drivers of FP progress, assess trends in mCPR and method mix, and contextualise findings.
RESULTS: Findings revealed that Kenya surpassed its 2020 modern contraceptive rate target of 58%, more than doubled the use of modern contraception (from 27% in 1993 to 61% in 2020), and significantly reduced the unmet need for modern FP (from 36% in 1993 to 14% in 2020). Five major themes emerged as the key drivers of Kenya’s performance: (1) strong political commitment, (2) supportive donor and domestic financing, (3) incremental expansions in service delivery and infrastructure, (4) community engagement programmes and (5) increased women’s empowerment.
CONCLUSION: Lessons learnt from Kenya’s progress on FP may inform policy and programme decisions in other low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: A synthesis of six countries' successes in increasing modern contraceptive uptake at scale: a mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: St-Onge Ahmad S, Memon ZA, Samuel K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Data on facilitators to increase family planning (FP) services uptake in low- and middle-income countries is limited. This paper synthesises cross-cutting findings from six country mixed-methods case studies identified within the FP Exemplars FP project. We aimed to derive broader insights from analyses of policies, quantitative trends and contextual factors from 1994 to 2020 in Bolivia, Lao People’s Democratic Republic (PDR), Kenya, Malawi, Senegal and Sierra Leone.
