METHODS: Drawing on the results, we compare drivers of change in modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR); use the Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition and risk factor analysis to measure relative contributions of knowledge of individual FP methods to mCPR growth; map key developments occurring during and 5 years preceding maximum mCPR growth intervals (MGIs) and examine the association between official development assistance (ODA) and mCPR using Spearman’s rank correlation.
RESULTS: Compound mCPR annual change rates were 1.12% for Bolivia, 3.20% for Lao PDR, 3.98% for Kenya, 5.32% for Senegal, 5.44% for Malawi and 10.76% for Sierra Leone. Top drivers of mCPR increase were mean modern methods known of FP (MMK) and education. In Lao PDR, MMK was associated with mCPR in 2005 and 2012. Knowledge of implants was the strongest mCPR growth driver in Kenya, Malawi, Senegal and Sierra Leone. The MGI in Bolivia was 1998–2003, Kenya 2010–2015, Malawi 2009–2014, Senegal 2012–2017, Sierra Leone 2008–2013 and Lao PDR 1995–2000. During these time periods, we found that creation of laws, policies and programmes and international commitments played a role in all case countries, while product introduction, supply chain management, service integration, mass media, community-level initiatives, donor/domestic financing and institutional/structural changes played a role in some and mixed evidence for the role of ODA in mCPR growth.
CONCLUSION: Donor funding is important but insufficient for mCPR growth; country-level commitments through legislation, structural changes and targeted programming are key to achieving FP progress.

articles.title: PREGNANCY OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY COHORT OF WOMEN WITH REPAIRED TETRALOGY OF FALLOT.
articles.authors: Franch MJA, Pijuan-Domenech A, Ródenas-Alesina E et al.
articles.abstract: Most women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) now reach reproductive age, but pregnancy outcomes in contemporary cohorts, particularly after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), remain uncertain. The aim of this study as to assess maternal cardiac, obstetric and neonatal outcomes in a contemporary cohort of women with rTOF. We retrospectively included all pregnancies in women with rTOF followed at a tertiary referral center for complex congenital heart disease (CHD) and high-risk pregnancy between 2013 and 2024. A total of 44 pregnancies in 32 women with rTOF were included, resulting in 45 live births. Severe PR was present in 43% of pregnancies, and 40% had undergone prior PVR. Maternal cardiac events occurred in 6.8%: 2 cases of supraventricular arrhythmias and 1 case of thrombosis on an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead. Among women with prior PVR, transvalvular gradients increased transiently during pregnancy and returned to baseline postpartum. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks, vaginal birth was preferred and cesarean section was performed in 18% of pregnancies. The most frequent adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes were low birth weight (22%) and preterm birth (11%), both associated with lower pre-pregnancy right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) possibly reflecting impaired uteroplacental perfusion related to right ventricular dysfunction. In conclusion, in this contemporary cohort, pregnancy in women with rTOF was associated with low risk of maternal cardiac events, mainly supraventricular arrhythmias. However, low birth weight and preterm birth remained frequent and were associated with lower pre-pregnancy RVEF, underscoring the importance of specialized cardio-obstetric follow-up.

articles.title: Cutaneous Manifestations of the Menopausal Transition - Part 1: Epidemiology, Biology, Diagnosis and Workup.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
articles.authors: Kim U, Gangal A, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause represents a physiologic transition characterized by the cessation of ovarian follicular estrogen synthesis and subsequent alterations in the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, with broad systemic and cutaneous consequences. This review (Part 1) provides a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and clinical evaluation of dermatologic manifestations associated with perimenopause and menopause. We summarize key hormonal changes, including declining estrogen and dynamic androgen shifts, and their downstream effects on skin structure and function through nuclear and membrane-associated estrogen receptor signaling pathways. The impact of estrogen deficiency across major cutaneous compartments-including the epidermis, dermis, hair follicle unit, sebaceous glands, vasculature, pigmentary system, and immune milieu-is examined, with emphasis on mechanisms underlying xerosis, impaired barrier function, dermal atrophy, alopecia, vasomotor instability, dyschromia, delayed wound healing, and vulvovaginal dermatoses. Dermatology-specific examination findings, limited utility of routine hormonal testing, and specific laboratory workup in patients with atypical or rapid-onset cutaneous hyperandrogenism are covered. This review equips clinicians with a mechanistic understanding of menopause-associated skin changes to support accurate diagnosis, appropriate workup, and informed management.

articles.title: Genetic Diagnoses and Postnatal Outcomes in a Prenatal Cohort of Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita.
articles.authors: Haizler-Cohen L, O'Brien D, Field E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe genetic diagnoses and characterize postnatal outcomes in a prenatal cohort of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) evaluated at a quaternary fetal center.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of pregnancies referred between 2014 and 2026 for contractures involving ≥ 2 body areas. We categorized cases into three groups using the Hall classification. Demographics, prenatal imaging, genetic results, autopsy findings, and postnatal outcomes were collected.
RESULTS: Ninety-four pregnancies were included: 15 with isolated arthrogryposis, 32 with arthrogryposis and systemic anomalies excluding the central nervous system (CNS), and 47 with arthrogryposis and CNS involvement or fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS). Genetic findings in our cohort included 18 aneuploidies, 3 copy number variants and 25 single gene disorders. Of pregnancies with non-diagnostic cytogenetic findings that underwent next-generation sequencing (NGS), 50% (24/48) had a molecular diagnosis. Neonates with FADS had notably poor outcomes, including high mortality (86%, 6/7) and failed intubation (50%, 3/6) rates. Of neonates with isolated arthrogryposis, 77% (10/13) survived but frequently required respiratory or feeding support, orthopedic surgery, ambulation assistance and had neurodevelopmental delays.
CONCLUSIONS: AMC is genetically heterogeneous with frequent underlying single gene disorders, supporting the use of NGS in prenatal diagnosis. Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain high, particularly with FADS.

articles.title: Symptom, not solution: Digital contraceptives, structural ambivalence, and the cracks in contraceptive care.
articles.authors: Klim C
articles.abstract: Digital contraceptive technologies are increasingly promoted as solutions to persistent problems in contraceptive care, including user dissatisfaction and limited pharmaceutical innovation. Drawing on qualitative workshops with contraceptive users in Australia, this article interrogates this solutionist framing by exploring how digital contraceptives are understood and evaluated in relation to everyday experiences of contraceptive care. Although participants recognised certain benefits, they frequently described these technologies as inadequate or disappointing solutions. Rather than treating their responses as matters of individual preference or technical failure, I show how dissatisfaction with digital contraceptives reflects broader structural critiques of contraceptive care. What appear as 'emergent frictions' in the form of cost, usability, security, and design are, in fact, symptomatic of 'embedded fractures', including gendered responsibility, fragmented educational infrastructures, the commodification of care, and political precarity. By reframing participants' ambivalence as a response to structural conditions rather than to discrete technologies, the article re-situates digital contraception within the broader landscape of contraceptive care and challenges solutionist approaches to future improvements.

articles.title: A Mixed-Method Feasibility Study of an Online Group Program for Pregnant Women With ADHD.
articles.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
articles.authors: Marcussen K, Kristensen RK, Jensen AT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnant women with ADHD may experience specific challenges related to executive functioning, emotional regulation, and preparation for motherhood. ADHD Mother's Online Resources (AMOR) is a 10-week online group program developed to provide ADHD-adapted psychoeducation, practical coping strategies, and peer support during pregnancy. This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of AMOR among pregnant women with ADHD in Denmark.
METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods feasibility study using pre- and post-intervention questionnaires and post-program individual and focus group interviews. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, adherence, satisfaction, perceived credibility, and negative effects. Secondary outcomes included self-reported ADHD symptoms, perceived stress, depressive and anxiety symptoms, emotion regulation difficulties, and ADHD-related quality of life. Qualitative interviews with 12 participants were analysed using the Framework Method, informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability.
RESULTS: Fifty-seven women self-referred within 3 months, and all three groups reached capacity within 24 h. Thirty-two women were enroled; 27 completed the program (program retention 84.4%) and 25 completed follow-up questionnaires (follow-up retention 92.6%), and mean session attendance was 80%. Satisfaction was high with a total mean Client Satisfaction Questionnaire score of 25.76; 88% would recommend the program and 88% intended to continue using the techniques. Reported negative effects were infrequent and mild. Qualitative findings indicated high acceptability, with participants describing the program as relevant, supportive, and meaningful. Perceived benefits included practical strategies, normalization, peer support, increased self-acceptance, improved partner communication, and greater confidence in communicating with healthcare professionals. Quantitative changes in symptom-based measures were small, with improvements observed particularly for anxiety symptoms and ADHD-related quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Findings suggest substantial unmet need for ADHD-adapted perinatal support. AMOR appeared feasible, acceptable, and well tolerated among pregnant women with ADHD. Future controlled studies should evaluate its effectiveness and impact on maternal psychosocial outcomes and postpartum well-being.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: S-20240074, 11/05/2024.

articles.title: Sex differences in gastrointestinal permeability during acute uncompensable heat stress: Role of menstrual phase hormones.
articles.authors: Leach S, Allsop EJ, Martin IA et al.
articles.abstract: Hyperthermia can increase gastrointestinal permeability, allowing microbes to leak from the intestinal lumen to the hepatic portal and systemic circulation. However, the extent to which sex and menstrual cycle hormones impact the risk of increased gastrointestinal permeability during heat stress is unclear. Twenty-four healthy young adults [12 male, 24 ± 3 years old; 12 female (5 oral contraceptive users), 23 ± 2 years old] participated in the study. Initially, participants completed a control trial (no heat or exercise) to determine baseline gastrointestinal permeability. Then, participants took part in a hyperthermia trial, in which deep body temperature was increased by +1.5°C from baseline via a water-perfused suit combined with semi-recumbent cycling at 40 W. Oestradiol was measured at baseline during the hyperthermia trial. In both trials, permeability was assessed by measuring the urinary excretion of orally ingested sucrose (10 g) and the lactulose/rhamnose ratio (L/R, 1 g each) to assess gastroduodenal and small intestinal permeability, respectively. Data are presented as the change in excretion from control to hyperthermia. Pooled analysis of all participants identified that hyperthermia increased small intestinal permeability [ΔL/R = 0.012 ± 0.029 (95% confidence interval 0.000 to 0.025), P = 0.050, d z   = 0.43]. Although there were no sex differences at the group level, we identified a strong positive correlation between ΔL/R and baseline oestradiol concentration within females (r = 0.709, P = 0.040). Gastroduodenal permeability did not increase with hyperthermia (P = 0.136), nor were there any differences between the sexes (P = 0.411). Future studies should confirm whether oestradiol plays an independent role in modulating heat-induced gastrointestinal permeability in humans.

articles.title: Underfunded, Overperforming: Endometrial cancer leads basic and translational science publications per NCI dollar.
articles.authors: Richardson MT, Gallivan A, Zello L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare relative research funding and basic and translational science publications for gynecologic cancers vs. other common cancers, normalized to incidence and mortality rates.
METHODS: SEER data were used to investigate incidence and deaths in the US from 2004 to 2024. Research funding was derived from National Cancer Institute (NCI) data. Google Scholar was utilized to identify oncology and medicine related journals with the highest H-indices. All abstracts on PubMed were reviewed and number of basic and translational science articles manually calculated.
RESULTS: In 2024, new diagnoses of breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers totaled 313,510, 299,010, 234,580, and 152,810, respectively. Endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers accounted for 67,880, 19,680, and 13,820, respectively.NCI funding in 2023 was approximately $542.0 million for breast, $258.6 million for prostate, $435.0 million for lung, and $238.6 million for colorectal cancers, compared to $20.0 million, $132.0 million, and $20.7 million for endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers, respectively.Across the highest impact journals from 2004 to 2024, 24,169 basic/translational science publications were found: 8859 (breast), 4161 (prostate), 3537 (lung), 4321 (colorectal), 412 (endometrial), 2231 (ovarian), and 648 (cervical). When adjusted for incidence, ovarian cancer had the highest number of publications, at 220.9 publications per 100,000 cases. When adjusted for funding, endometrial cancer had the highest number of publications, at 23.1 publications per $1 million average annual NCI funding.
CONCLUSION: Funding relative to disease burden varies considerably among gynecologic cancers. Endometrial cancer receives the lowest NCI funding of any cancer studied when adjusted by incidence and mortality. Despite this, endometrial cancer produced the most basic and translational science publications per dollar.

articles.title: Updates in osteoporosis medications: maximizing benefits and minimizing risks.
articles.authors: Okazaki KM, Wang JY, Yu EW
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis is a major public health concern affecting approximately 1 in 3 women and 1 in 5 men over the age of 50 globally. Hip fractures are a significant complication of osteoporosis and are associated with approximately 20%-24% mortality in the year after fracture. While medications can substantially reduce fracture risk, these therapies remain significantly underutilized. This treatment gap is partly driven by confusion among healthcare professionals and patients regarding potential treatment complications. This narrative review provides a practical overview of strategies to maximize benefits and minimize risks of pharmacologic osteoporosis therapies, including calcium/vitamin D, bisphosphonates, denosumab, parathyroid hormone (PTH) analogs, romosozumab, raloxifene, and menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). In addition to reviewing the latest data about therapeutic efficacy and safety, we provide a summary of best practices to mitigate potential side effects. Relevant updates include new data on the efficacy of bisphosphonates in lower risk patients, recommendations for using osteoanabolic agents as first-line for very high fracture risk patients, important considerations regarding multiple vertebral fractures when discontinuing denosumab, as well as cardiovascular safety data and the option of a shortened course for romosozumab. FDA updates are highlighted: removal of the osteosarcoma black-boxed warning for PTH analogs, nuances in the warnings regarding MHT, and addition of a black-boxed warning for severe hypocalcemia with denosumab in chronic kidney disease. The benefits of osteoporosis medications in preventing high-morbidity fragility fractures significantly outweigh the small risks of serious complications. It is essential for clinicians to understand the myths and realities of these treatments and to implement mitigation strategies to ensure patient safety. By effectively addressing these issues, healthcare professionals can play a vital role in closing the osteoporosis treatment gap.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Pudendal Nerve Block in Elderly Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery: Impact on Anesthetic Consumption and Postoperative Recovery-A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Yang C, Lu Z, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nerve block is often used for multimodal analgesia. Surgeries for pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in elderly patients are focused on the perineal area, where pudendal nerve block (PNB) can provide analgesia or anaesthesia. There are limited studies on PNB in POP surgery, mainly addressing postoperative pain relief. This prospective randomized controlled trial examined the impact of ultrasound-guided PNB on intraoperative medication and postoperative recovery in elderly POP surgery patients.
METHODS: Patients aged 60-70 undergoing total vaginal hysterectomy (with or without sacral fixation/colporrhaphy) under general anesthesia were randomized into two groups: PNB (pudendal nerve block) and NPNB (no pudendal nerve block). Anesthesia was induced with target-controlled infusions of remifentanil (3 ng/mL) and propofol (3 µg/mL). The study compared intraoperative anesthetic doses, hemodynamic changes, cardiovascular drug needs, wakefulness time, and post-op recovery quality between the groups.
RESULTS: 58 patients completed the study. The PNB group required significantly less remifentanil (386.6 ± 239.1 µg vs 563.1 ± 235.7 µg, p = 0.005) and propofol (645.5 ± 315.2 mg vs 804.2 ± 297.2 mg, p = 0.028) compared to the NPNB group. Intraoperative hemodynamics were more stable in the PNB group, with a reduced need for vasopressors. The PNB group also exhibited faster emergence, lower postoperative pain, and less oversedation,with a non-significant trend toward higher QoR-40 scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided PNB in elderly POP surgery patients reduced opioid and anesthetic doses, shortened awakening time, and produced clinically favourable improvements in postoperative recovery. Larger studies are needed to confirm these benefits for postoperative rehabilitation.

articles.title: Maternal cardiovascular and pregnancy outcomes among pregnant patients with mechanical and bioprosthetic valves.
articles.authors: Essa A, Kovell LC, Wilkie GL
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with mechanical heart valves in pregnancy are at a substantially higher risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Management of patients with mechanical heart valves poses a unique challenge, and strategies for anticoagulation in these patients remain controversial. The goal of this project was to determine rates of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes in patients with mechanical valves compared to those with bioprosthetic valves, and assess outcomes in patients with mechanical valves using low molecular weight heparin and warfarin.
METHODS: A retrospective query was performed using Epic Cosmos to evaluate pregnancies affected by mechanical and bioprosthetic heart valves between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Patient demographics and rates of adverse cardiac outcomes in the perinatal period, including heart failure, arrhythmia, and stroke, were assessed. The rate of anticoagulation with low molecular weight heparin and warfarin in patients with mechanical heart valves was evaluated, and cardiac and perinatal outcomes were determined and compared between groups. Rare outcomes were reported as <10 to protect patient privacy.
RESULTS: Baseline demographics between patients with mechanical and bioprosthetic heart valves were similar. Rates of heart failure (22.9%) and stroke (11.7%) were significantly higher in patients with mechanical compared to bioprosthetic heart valves, though the rates of maternal arrhythmia were similar between groups. Valve thrombosis was a rare outcome for patients with mechanical valves, with fewer than 10 events in the study sample. Perinatal outcomes including preterm and cesarean delivery were similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, mechanical heart valves are associated with high rates of heart failure and stroke in pregnancy. Rates of adverse events may be similar for patients using low molecular weight heparin compared to warfarin for anticoagulation in pregnancy.

articles.title: Generation of mixed ovarian cancer and fibroblast spheroids by bioprinting.
articles.authors: Atwal A, Richardson A
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional tumour-stroma models are urgently needed to improve the predictive power of preclinical drug screening in ovarian cancer, a disease with high mortality and limited therapeutic success. Here, we present a droplet-bioprinted ovarian cancer model incorporating OVCAR-4 cells expressing nano-luciferase and primary cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) embedded within a collagen (Telecol)-based hydrogel. Using the CELLINK BIO X system, we generated reproducible mini-spheroids with controlled architecture, enabling systematic evaluation of cancer and CAF cell density and chemotherapeutic response. Bioprinted spheroids showed good reproducibility across plates when bioink volume and printing conditions were stable. Increasing cancer cell density produced a non-linear rise in luminescence, and this could be at least partially corrected by normalisation to initial cell number. CAFs consistently and robustly enhanced cancer cell growth in a ratio-dependent manner, and confocal imaging revealed that CAFs frequently organised into encapsulating structures around cancer clusters, forming stromal niches associated with matrix contraction and increased cancer-CAF interface. However, CAFs did not protect cancer cells against carboplatin, as drug sensitivity remained comparable in monoculture and CAF co-cultures. This suggests that CAF-driven growth support and CAF-driven chemoresistance are mechanistically separable in this model. Together, this work establishes a mechanically tunable, spatially defined bioprinted ovarian cancer-CAF model that captures key stromal interactions which are not reproduced in studies using CAF conditioned media alone, while remaining compatible with automated, higher-throughput workflows.

articles.title: Fragment-end sequence architecture of cell-free DNA and its association with tumour DNA in non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.authors: Das D, Gupta P, Tambade R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentation patterns provide a promising source of molecular information for liquid biopsy applications. However, the sequence features underlying fragmentation and their relationship to tumour-derived DNA remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterized fragment-end sequence signatures of extracellular cfDNA across cell lines, extracellular compartments, stress conditions and plasma from patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: cfDNA derived from cell lines was characterized using Oxford Nanopore sequencing, followed by fragment-end analysis. Publicly available Nanopore cfDNA datasets from healthy individuals and NSCLC patients were analyzed to examine dinucleotide patterns and derive a motif ratio index. These signatures were further assessed for their association with estimated ctDNA abundance in an independent cohort of 50 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients.
RESULTS: Nanopore sequencing of A549, H460 and WI38 cell-line cfDNA revealed reproducible end-motif patterns, with enrichment of AT-, GT- and CT-containing termini. Analysis of plasma cfDNA from healthy individuals showed distinct end-motif profiles from cell-line-derived cfDNA, with separation maintained after reducing 4-mer motifs to 5'-terminal dinucleotide features. An exploratory motif ratio based on these patterns showed a modest increase in lung cancer patients compared with healthy individuals. In an independent Illumina cohort of 50 NSCLC patients with activating EGFR mutations, 5'-terminal dinucleotide frequencies were associated with estimated circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) abundance using cross-validated LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression (Spearman ρ = .73, p = 3.35 × 10‒9). The predefined motif ratio showed a strong correlation with estimated ctDNA concentration (Spearman ρ = .76, p = 1.89 × 10‒10).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that simple, interpretable cfDNA end-motif signatures capture sequence features associated with ctDNA abundance and warrant further validation for non-invasive cancer monitoring.

articles.title: Levator hiatus width as a complementary measurement tool in assessing pelvic floor dysfunction.
articles.authors: Gayathri AP, Subbaiah P, Neshatian L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Levator hiatus width (LHW) is a measurement along with H- and M-lines in MR defecography to evaluate pelvic floor dysfunction. Our study aimed to correlate the resting LHW with the resting and defecation-phase H-line and M-line, the presence of pelvic organ prolapse (POP), and to evaluate the reliability of measurement between readers.
METHODS: This Institutional Review Board (IRB) approved case-control study retrospectively reviewed MR defecography exams of 70 patients with symptomatic pelvic floor dysfunction and 19 age-matched controls. LHW, H-line, and M-line in resting (RPH, RPM) and dynamic defecation phases (DPH, DPM) were measured, and the anterior, middle, and posterior compartment pelvic floor descent was graded. Three readers analyzed each exam, and their interobserver variability was compared.
RESULTS: LHW was abnormal (>4.5 cm) in 29 patients (41.4%). Mean (± SD) LHW was 4.4 ± 1.1 cm in patients and 3.7±1.0 cm in controls. Abnormal LHW was significantly associated with RPH (P<0.001), RPM (P<0.001), and several compartment-specific prolapse findings on logistic regression, including bladder descent, vaginal descent, enterocele, and sigmoidocele. Intraclass correlation coefficients showed greater agreement between the two readers with dedicated training to read MR defecography.
CONCLUSION: Resting LHW was associated with several MRI markers of POP and may provide complementary information during MR defecography. Its added diagnostic value beyond H-line and M-line was not formally assessed in this exploratory analysis and requires validation. Dedicated training in reporting MR defecography can reduce interobserver variability in interpretations.

articles.title: Sample size calculations for developing clinical prediction models for binary outcomes: applied methodological study with real examples.
articles.authors: Yimer NB, Belsti Y, Teede H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare existing sample size calculations for developing prediction models in rare and common outcome scenarios, and to explore how the choice of method influences required sample sizes and their implications for clinical use.
DESIGN: Applied methodological study with real examples.
SETTING: Monash Health public maternity hospitals (two secondary and one tertiary), Australia, 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: 78 170 singleton pregnancies recorded from 2016 to 2024.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Required sample size, and model calibration, discrimination, prediction errors, and clinical use (net benefit).
RESULTS: Three sample size calculation methods were applied: method 1, target of minimising overfitting and estimating average risk precisely based on a closed form solution; method 2, target of minimising overfitting and overall prediction error based on a simulation based approach; and method 3, targeting individual level prediction stability. A simulation based general framework that encompassed and extended methods 1-3 was also applied. These approaches were illustrated with rare (pre-eclampsia) and common (gestational diabetes) outcomes to determine how sample sizes influenced the main outcome measures. Sample sizes required for developing a clinical prediction model varied by sample size method, choice of predicted outcome, development method, and performance targets. Compared with the gestational diabetes model, the pre-eclampsia model required consistently larger sample sizes (eg, method 1 required 3097 and 519 patients for pre-eclampsia and gestational diabetes, respectively). For both outcomes, method 2 required moderate minimum sample sizes (pre-eclampsia 3935 and gestational diabetes 954 patients), whereas method 3 needed larger sample sizes (pre-eclampsia 150 318 and gestational diabetes 52 269 patients to target prespecified uncertainty interval widths). The general simulation based approach showed that penalised logistic regression models had the most stable calibration, even at smaller sample sizes, whereas unpenalised regression models improved with increasing data. The random forest model gave consistent discrimination but showed persistent miscalibration (slope 1.7) across all sample sizes.
CONCLUSIONS: Required sample sizes varied across methods because different model performance targets were optimised: population level accuracy was achieved with modest samples, whereas individual level accuracy and prediction…

articles.title: A hypothesis framework linking the menopausal transition, sleep and brain waste clearance: Insights from experimental models.
articles.authors: Zamani A, Jenkins L, Rodger J et al.
articles.abstract: The menopausal transition is increasingly recognized as a neuroendocrine transition with implications for brain health, sleep, cognition and vulnerability to neurodegenerative disease. Fluctuating and declining ovarian hormones coincide with sleep disruption, vasomotor symptoms, cognitive complaints, neuroinflammation and altered blood-brain barrier integrity. Current preclinical models each capture selected components of the menopause transition and provide essential mechanistic insights into the effect of ovarian hormone loss on the brain. Across these models, endocrine change is associated with impairments in hippocampal and prefrontal-dependent cognition, altered sleep-wake regulation, vascular dysfunction, glial activation, disrupted synaptic and mitochondrial homeostasis and exacerbation of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease-like pathology. An emerging but understudied mechanism linking menopause, sleep and neurodegeneration is the glymphatic system, a sleep-dependent brain waste clearance pathway. This review synthesises current evidence to highlight how menopause-related sleep disruption, vascular dysfunction, neuroinflammation and potential alterations in brain-waste clearance may converge to shape cognitive ageing and neurodegenerative disease risk.

articles.title: 1H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women.
articles.authors: Mekle R, Fleck L, Bauer M et al.
articles.abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided suction with balloon tamponade for cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy: a combined treatment strategy.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Lucidi A, Liberati M, Di Tizio L et al.
articles.abstract: Cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy (CSEP) is a severe iatrogenic complication of cesarean delivery (CD). However, there is no consensus yet on how to treat CSEP. This report describes a minimally invasive approach combining ultrasound-guided suction evacuation of the ectopic sac followed by immediate balloon tamponade insertion at the site of the prior CD. Continuous visualisation of the uterine-bladder interface helps prevent accidental uterine or bladder injuries, while mechanical balloon may help in providing adequate haemostasis. In our experience, this method may be a reasonable and potentially effective minimally invasive approach to treating CSEP, though it requires confirmation in adequately powered randomised controlled trials.

articles.title: Robotic Myomectomy for High Fibroid Burden: A Multimodal Blood-Sparing Strategy for the Removal of 40 Leiomyomas.
articles.authors: Augusto KL, Bilhar APM, Karbage SAL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate robotic myomectomy for a high leiomyoma burden using a multimodal blood-sparing strategy.
SETTING: Tertiary referral center for advanced minimally invasive gynecologic surgery.
PARTICIPANTS: A 25-year-old nulligravid woman. MRI showed a 1152-cm³ uterus with multiple leiomyomas, including an 8.6-cm dominant lesion.

articles.title: Digital health interventions and maternal outcomes among pregnant women in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Avenorgbo SK, Acheampong K, Morgan AK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of maternal mortality and morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains high, driven by under-resourced health systems and challenges with accessibility and affordability. However, Digital Health Interventions (DHIs) are optimising maternal health, particularly antenatal care (ANC) outcomes in these settings.
OBJECTIVES: This paper presents a comprehensive synthesis of the effects of DHIs on maternal outcomes during pregnancy in LMICs.
METHODS: The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and searched six databases, Cochrane, Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, between 1st and 30th June 2023. Reference list screening, which involved manually checking the bibliographies of included full-text studies to identify additional relevant studies, complemented the electronic search. The review included empirical quantitative studies published in English between 2018 and 2023 that reported on DHIs in ANC in any LMIC. We critically appraised, extracted data from, and narratively synthesised all included studies.
RESULTS: The included papers comprised randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (n = 3), cross-sectional studies (n = 3), and mixed-methods studies (n = 2) from five LMICs. Most DHIs used smartphone technologies primarily for education, advice, and ANC reminders. DHIs improved maternal health behaviours, but evidence on clinical outcomes was inconclusive because data were limited.
CONCLUSION: The paper reports that DHIs improve maternal behaviours and could foster the attainment of maternal and neonatal goals in LMICs. Future research should establish the clinical outcomes associated with DHIs to inform inclusive policy responses, since equity, sustainability, and clinical outcomes remain uncertain.

articles.title: Allele-frequency optimization of SNP panels for non-invasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT): a theoretical analysis.
articles.authors: Trombetta B, Pistacchia L, Diverio S et al.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT) exploits cell-free fetal DNA circulating in maternal plasma to assess paternity before birth and is increasingly based on large panels of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). In SNP-based NIPAT, marker panels are traditionally designed by selecting polymorphisms with a minor allele frequency (MAF) near 0.5, in order to maximize expected heterozygosity. However, this criterion does not necessarily maximize the evidential value contributed to the Combined Paternity Index (CPI). Here we develop an analytical model that, starting from the informative mother-fetus genotype configurations observed in maternal plasma cell-free DNA, formally derives the expected contribution of a single biallelic SNP to the CPI as a function of allele frequency. We show that the expected proportion of informative loci, corresponding to one-half of the expected heterozygosity, is maximized at MAF = 0.5, but that this frequency corresponds to a local minimum of the expected evidential contribution, which instead peaks at MAF = 0.147. At this optimum, the reduced probability that a locus is informative is more than offset by the higher Paternity Index generated when the detectable paternal allele is rare. We further show that the expected Probability of Exclusion (PE) reaches its own maximum at MAF = 0.211. Overall, these results demonstrate that no single allele frequency simultaneously maximizes all three relevant forensic performance metrics (proportion of informative markers, PI, and PE), and that SNP selection for NIPAT should explicitly consider which of these quantities is to be optimized, rather than relying implicitly on the maximum-heterozygosity criterion alone.

articles.title: Zona pellucida-based immunocontraception for canine fertility control: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Awawdeh L, Alani N, Callcott ET et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the extent, characteristics and gaps in published evidence on zona pellucida (ZP)-related immunocontraceptive development relevant to female dogs, distinguishing canine reproductive observations from immunogenicity, surrogate-model and mechanistic evidence.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological guidance and reported using the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The eligibility period was expanded to include studies published from 1979 through December 2025, ensuring inclusion of early foundational research on canine zona pellucida (ZP)-based immunocontraception. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and databases accessed through EBSCO were searched. Supplementary searches of Google Scholar and citation searching were undertaken to identify additional relevant records. Eligible evidence was charted descriptively according to publication, animal model, intervention, study design, and reported outcomes. Consistent with the descriptive scoping review approach, no meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken.
RESULTS: The current map contains 19 primary reports, including seven with female-dog reproductive or ovarian observations and two additional canine immunogenicity reports. These are report counts, not independent-cohort counts. Canine pregnancy, pup-production, cycle, endocrine and ovarian outcomes were measured in varying combinations. Related endocrine and histopathology reports explicitly reused animals. Small groups, inconsistent outcome denominators, incompletely described assessment procedures and incomplete source availability limit interpretation. A structured post-treatment breeding assessment establishing reproductive recovery was not identified in the available canine texts.
CONCLUSIONS: The literature maps a heterogeneous development pathway from antigen characterisation to small canine reproductive experiments. The main gaps concern cohort independence, reproductive denominators, standardised ovarian assessment, post-treatment fertility recovery and longitudinal welfare outcomes. This map identifies questions for research; it does not estimate comparative effectiveness, grade safety, or recommend clinical use.

articles.title: HIF-1α-SLC2A1 signaling contributes to neutrophil extracellular trap-induced senescence-associated changes in retinal pigment epithelial cells.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Li J, Xue H et al.
articles.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in sterile inflammatory injury, but their contribution to dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is not well defined. We examined NET formation in patients with dry AMD and assessed its effects on retinal injury and retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells. Neutrophils isolated from patients with dry AMD exhibited greater PMA-induced NET formation than those from healthy controls, accompanied by higher serum levels of MPO-DNA complexes and cell-free DNA. In sodium iodate (NaIO₃)-treated mice, H3Cit signals accumulated predominantly in the outer retina adjacent to the RPE. Suppression of NET formation with GSK484, as well as neutrophil depletion with anti-Ly6G, reduced retinal damage, preserved RPE morphology, and improved retinal function. NET exposure also induced senescence-related changes in ARPE-19 cells, whereas DNase I markedly weakened these effects. Proteomic profiling pointed to Toll-like receptor and HIF-1 signaling as candidate pathways involved in NET-mediated injury. NET treatment increased TLR2 and MyD88 expression and promoted HIF-1α accumulation in the nucleus without an obvious change in total HIF-1α abundance. Further analysis identified SLC2A1 as a downstream target of HIF-1α. Reporter assays showed that HIF-1α enhanced SLC2A1 promoter activity through a hypoxia-response element, while HIF1A knockdown reduced NET-induced RPE senescence. Re-expression of SLC2A1 partially restored the senescent phenotype. These findings support a contribution of NETs to experimental retinal injury and implicate HIF-1α-SLC2A1 signaling in NET-induced senescence-associated changes in RPE cells.

articles.title: Data-driven cardiometabolic profiling in untreated women with Rotterdam-defined polycystic ovary syndrome: Unsupervised clustering and machine-learning profile assignment.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Kurt A, Yıldız AG, Ulusoy CO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic risk in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is heterogeneous and may not be fully captured by Rotterdam phenotypes. We aimed to identify data-driven cardiometabolic profiles at initial diagnosis and to evaluate supervised models for profile assignment.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, clinic-based study included 485 newly diagnosed, untreated women aged 18-45 years with Rotterdam-defined PCOS. Ten routinely available cardiometabolic variables were median-imputed, standardized, reduced by principal component analysis (PCA), and clustered using k-means. Profiles were characterized using variables withheld from clustering and evaluated in missing-data, anthropometry-excluded, age/body mass index-adjusted laboratory-only, and internal assignment-stability analyses. Patient-level cross-validated logistic-regression and random-forest models were used for profile assignment.
RESULTS: K-means identified a metabolically favorable profile in 342 patients (70.5%) and a metabolically unfavorable profile in 143 (29.5%). The unfavorable profile showed higher adiposity, central obesity, fasting glucose, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol, transaminases, white blood cell count, insulin resistance, post-load glucose responses, C-reactive protein (CRP), platelet count, lipid-derived indices, and androgen bioavailability, together with lower sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG). Rotterdam phenotype distribution did not differ between profiles (P = 0.650). The profile structure was broadly robust to k-nearest-neighbor-imputed and complete-case clustering (adjusted Rand index [ARI] = 0.783 and 0.909, respectively), whereas age/BMI-adjusted laboratory-only clustering showed lower agreement with the primary partition (ARI = 0.307). Training-fold refitting with held-out centroid assignment showed high internal assignment stability (ARI = 0.909). The independent clinical-endocrine model showed moderate discrimination (receiver operating characteristic area under the curve [ROC-AUC], 0.718), whereas secondary cluster-recovery models showed higher discrimination (ROC-AUC, 0.889-0.942; random forest, 0.935).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine baseline clinical and laboratory data identified a metabolically unfavorable PCOS profile that was not fully reflected by Rotterdam phenotype distribution in this clinic-based cohort. These exploratory findings require external validation and outcome-based evaluation before their…

articles.title: Association between vulvovaginal symptoms and intimate hygiene habits, sociodemographic and clinical data in Spanish women: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Domínguez-Romero MV, Alburquerque-Sendín F, Punzano-Martínez N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between self-reported vulvovaginal symptoms, intimate hygiene practices, and sociodemographic and clinical characteristics in adult Spanish women.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between February 2025 and January 2026 among 154 adult women (median age 27 years, interquartile range [IQR] 20). Self-reported vulvovaginal symptoms were assessed with the Spanish version of the Vulvovaginal Symptoms Questionnaire (VSQ), and intimate hygiene practices with a questionnaire adapted from a previously published instrument. Variables with p < 0.20 in non-parametric bivariate analyses were entered into a forward stepwise multiple linear regression model.
RESULTS: Overall, 57.8 % of women reported at least one physical vulvovaginal symptom, most frequently discharge (34.4 %), odor (22.7 %) and dryness (20.1 %); emotional, daily-life and sexual-life impact was reported by 66.2 %, 33.1 % and 38.3 %, respectively. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were not associated with VSQ scores, except for sexual activity. In the multivariable model (adjusted R2 = 0.334), higher VSQ scores were associated with external (β = 0.416) and intravaginal (β = 0.328) use of anti-itch creams, use of sanitary pads or pantyliners outside menstruation (β = 0.242) and sexual activity (β = 0.208) (all p ≤ 0.002). Washing the genital area after defecation was associated with lower VSQ scores (β = - 0.157, p = 0.021).
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported vulvovaginal symptoms were common and more closely associated with product use and behavioral factors than with sociodemographic or clinical characteristics. Given the cross-sectional design, the associations with anti-itch creams and pantyliners could reflect product use in response to pre-existing symptoms and should not be interpreted as causal.

articles.title: What Patients are Reading About Prenatal Cell-Free DNA: An Analysis of Leading Publicly Available AI-Chatbots.
articles.authors: Finkelstein MS, Rose SL, Jenkins L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the quality, consistency, and framing of information about prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening generated by publicly available chatbots, including variation across simulated user age profiles.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative content analysis of outputs from three publicly available chatbots. To reduce carryover effects and personalization, prompts were entered using a VPN, private browsing, and cleared browser cookies. Outputs were generated using distinct simulated user age profiles. Analysis examined informational completeness, framing of benefits and limitations, terminology, source transparency, and age-related differences in responses.
RESULTS: Chatbot outputs varied substantially across platforms and user profiles, with misinformation, omissions, and incomplete information identified. Common themes included inconsistent explanations of the purpose and scope of cfDNA screening, frequent omission of test limitations and downstream implications, and variable readability scores (at a 9th-14th grade level) and terminology that sometimes conflate screening with diagnostic testing. Citations to high-quality sources were limited or absent. Age-based profile variation was associated with differences in tone, complexity, and emphasis, suggesting implicit tailoring of information presentation.
CONCLUSION: Publicly available chatbots may provide inaccurate or inconsistent information about cfDNA screening. As these tools are increasingly used outside clinical settings, improving accuracy, transparency, discussion of limitations, and source citation is essential to support reliable patient-facing health information.

articles.title: Endometrial ultrasound features associated with methotrexate success in tubal ectopic pregnancy: a prospective case series.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Shirazinezhad S, Khademi F, Elhaie M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic pregnancy is an important cause of maternal morbidity in early pregnancy. Single-dose methotrexate is commonly used for haemodynamically stable women with unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, but treatment success varies. The association between pre-treatment endometrial ultrasonographic features and treatment outcome remains uncertain.
METHODS: This prospective case series included 177 women with confirmed tubal ectopic pregnancy who received a single intramuscular dose of methotrexate (50 mg/m2) at two tertiary hospitals in Isfahan, Iran, between January and December 2024. Transvaginal ultrasonography was used to measure endometrial thickness and classify the endometrial echo pattern as homogeneous or triple-layer. Treatment success was defined as a ≥ 15% decline in serum β-hCG from day 4 to day 7 after treatment, followed by weekly monitoring until the concentration became undetectable. Associations with treatment success were assessed using univariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Treatment success occurred in 94 of 177 women (53.1%). Responders had lower median baseline β-hCG concentrations (500 versus 1400 mIU/mL; P < 0.001), thinner endometrium (7 versus 9 mm; P = 0.009), and a higher proportion of homogeneous endometrial appearance (65.9 versus 49.4%; P = 0.026). In univariable logistic regression, baseline β-hCG (P = 0.003), ectopic pregnancy size (P = 0.013), and homogeneous endometrial appearance (P = 0.027) were significantly associated with treatment success; endometrial thickness showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.0498).
CONCLUSION: Baseline β-hCG, ectopic pregnancy size, and endometrial appearance were associated with single-dose methotrexate success in univariable analyses, while endometrial thickness showed a borderline association. Because no multivariable model was fitted, these findings should not be interpreted as independent predictors. Endometrial ultrasonographic features may provide supportive information alongside established clinical factors such as baseline β-hCG.

articles.title: Computed tomography derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in high-risk breast cancer using fully automated deep learning algorithms.
articles.authors: Tsou TC, Yang Z, Wang T et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer.
METHODS: We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins.
RESULTS: Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

articles.title: Interleukin-11 Contributes to TGF-β-induced Fibrotic Responses in Endometriosis.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Ono Y, Zhang D, Tanaka K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory gynecological disorder characterized by progressive fibrosis, yet the mechanisms driving fibrosis remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the role of interleukin-11 (IL-11) in endometriosis-associated fibrosis.
METHODS: With informed consent, ovarian endometriotic tissues, cyst fluids, and primary human endometriotic stromal cells (ESCs) were obtained from patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery. Publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to identify the cellular source of IL11 expression. IL-11 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry and ELISA, and its functional role in ESCs was investigated using quantitative PCR, IL-11 neutralization, and collagen gel contraction assays.
RESULTS: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified an IL11-high stromal cell population enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling genes. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated strong IL-11 expression predominantly localized within fibrotic areas of ovarian endometriotic lesions. In addition, IL-11 concentrations in ovarian endometrioma cyst fluid were significantly higher than those in non-endometriotic ovarian cyst fluid (median: 90.81 vs. 28.91 pg/mL, p < 0.001). In ESCs, TGF-β stimulation significantly increased IL11 mRNA expression (19.2-fold, p < 0.05) and IL-11 secretion (3.7-fold, p < 0.001). IL-11 stimulation also increased the mRNA expression of CTGF (1.4-fold, p = 0.02), PAI-1 (1.3-fold, p = 0.027), and IL-6 (1.4-fold, p = 0.020) in ESCs. Furthermore, IL-11 significantly enhanced collagen gel contraction (relative gel area: 1.00 vs. 0.81, p < 0.05), whereas IL-11 neutralization partially attenuated TGF-β-induced gel contraction (0.46 vs. 0.77, p = 0.063).
CONCLUSION: IL-11 acts as a downstream mediator of TGF-β signaling and promotes profibrotic remodeling in endometriotic stromal cells. These findings identify IL-11 as a potential therapeutic target for endometriosis-associated fibrosis.

articles.title: Rising Prevalence and Lateralization Differences of Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformations: A 12-Year Study in Urban China, 2013-2024.
articles.authors: Cheng X, Nie L, Meng C et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations (CPAMs) are rare developmental anomalies of the lung, with limited population-based data on their epidemiological characteristics and temporal trends, particularly in China.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the demographic and clinical characteristics of CPAM cases in urban China, analyze associated maternal and fetal risk factors, and evaluate temporal trends in overall prevalence and by lung laterality.
METHODS: A total of 135 CPAM cases and 3208 controls were included in a retrospective population-based study using data from a major maternal and child health registry in Beijing. Descriptive statistics, multivariable logistic regression, and Joinpoint regression were used to analyze trends and identify risk factors.
RESULTS: The overall prevalence of CPAMs increased significantly from 2013 to 2024 (APC = 6.69%, p < 0.05). Right-lung CPAM cases exhibited an increase (APC = 16.48%, p < 0.05), while left-lung cases remained stable (APC = -0.61%, p > 0.05). Multivariable analysis identified gravidity (aOR = 41.91, 95% CI: 25.65-71.09) and twin pregnancy (aOR = 4.66, 95% CI: 1.38-13.32) as significant risk factors. Maternal age, education, residence, and gestational age were also associated with CPAM occurrence.
CONCLUSION: This study provides epidemiological evidence on CPAMs in a Chinese urban population, highlighting a considerable increase in prevalence over the past decade, particularly in right-lung cases. Identified risk factors suggest a role of obstetric history and plurality in CPAM etiology. These findings underscore the need for enhanced prenatal surveillance and further investigation into the mechanisms underlying laterality-specific trends.

articles.title: Prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening of chromosome abnormalities: A technical standard of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and the College of American Pathologists (CAP).
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.authors: Hilton BA, Bhatt S, Cacheris P et al.
articles.abstract: The American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the College of American Pathologists work group developed this technical standard to address challenges associated with laboratory validation and implementation of prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening. Given that cfDNA screening is the most sensitive and specific screening test available for common fetal aneuploidies, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine recommend that prenatal cfDNA screening be offered to all pregnant persons as a first-tier screening option, regardless of their risk status. Fetal cfDNA in maternal circulation originates from placenta-derived trophoblasts, allowing for the identification of fetuses at increased risk for trisomies 13, 18, and 21 and aneuploidy of sex chromosomes, in addition to recurrent segmental aneuploidies associated with syndromes. Multiple cfDNA analysis techniques exist, and because of the complex nature of this screening, this technical standard aims to promote uniform laboratory practices. This document deals with the technical standards applicable to prenatal cfDNA screening of chromosome abnormalities in maternal plasma. This document serves as a resource to assist clinical laboratories with the validation methods, ongoing monitoring of test quality and performance, and the interpretation and reporting of these results.

articles.title: Global barriers among healthcare professionals in the adoption of imaging for endometriosis diagnosis: Impact on clinical practice.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Fragkoudi A, Sirohi D, Avery JC et al.
articles.abstract: This study aims to explore healthcare professionals' perceptions of barriers and clinical impact influencing the adoption of non-invasive imaging modalities for endometriosis diagnosis. A global cross-sectional survey was distributed through formal and informal FIGO committee networks. Content analysis was used to analyze the qualitative responses from the survey. Of the 360 respondents, 83.3% were gynecologists. In total, seven main topics were identified as barriers, including the lack of training and expertise (n = 173, 48.2%), cost and accessibility (n = 98, 27.3%), professional and institutional challenges (n = 28, 7.8%), diagnostic limitations (n = 15, 4.2%), equipment quality (n = 11, 3.1%), patient barriers (n = 9, 2.5%), and cultural and clinical resistance (n = 4, 1.1%). Respondents felt that adopting non-invasive imaging techniques for endometriosis diagnosis could lead to general impact on clinical practice (n = 118, 32.8%), changes in surgical and medical management (n = 84, 23.3%), shift in diagnostic approach (n = 77, 21.4%), challenges and considerations (n = 32, 9.7%), and improved patient-centered care (n = 25, 6.9%). This study highlights barriers and potential clinical impact of integrating non-invasive imaging into endometriosis diagnosis. Although clinicians recognize its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce reliance on surgery, widespread adoption is hindered by training gaps, resource limitations, and systemic variability.

articles.title: Association of second-trimester maternal serum AFP with umbilical venous blood flow and placental morphometry: a prospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Tavukcuoglu Z, Cicek S, Kapudere B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and umbilical venous Doppler measurements may reflect different aspects of fetoplacental function, but their relationship during the second trimester remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate associations between maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein multiples of the median (AFP MoM) and umbilical venous Doppler parameters, foetal weight percentile, and placental morphometry.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 104 singleton pregnancies examined at 16-22 weeks. Maternal blood sampling and ultrasound/Doppler assessment were performed on the same day. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlations and partial Spearman correlations adjusted for gestational age. Exploratory comparisons between pregnancies with AFP <2.0 MoM and AFP ≥2.0 MoM were also adjusted for gestational age. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate.
RESULTS: AFP MoM was available for 103 pregnancies and was not associated with foetal weight percentile or umbilical venous Doppler parameters. A weak inverse association with placental length was observed after gestational-age adjustment (partial r = -0.229; nominal p = 0.021), but it did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction (p = 0.193). In the exploratory analysis, the AFP ≥2.0 MoM group had a lower adjusted placental length (difference, -11.63 mm; 95% confidence interval, -21.10 to -2.17; nominal p = 0.017), but this difference was not significant after correction (p = 0.149).
CONCLUSION: Maternal serum AFP MoM was not associated with contemporaneous umbilical venous Doppler parameters or foetal weight percentile. Findings involving placental length were weak and should be considered exploratory.

articles.title: Fertility preservation and reproductive counseling in women with hereditary gynecological cancer predisposition: A scoping review of BRCA1/2 and Lynch syndrome care pathways.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Mondal R, Nandi M
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study maps the evidence on fertility preservation, reproductive counseling, contraception, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and care pathway integration for women with hereditary gynecological cancer predisposition, principally breast cancer genes 1 and 2 (BRCA1 and BRCA2) and Lynch syndrome, and derives a clinical decision-making framework.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The core search covered seven databases, Google Scholar and 11 gray literature sources from January 2000 to June 2025; a targeted supplementary search of MEDLINE and Embase for contraception and HRT was run to 7 October 2026 in response to peer review. Records from both searches were combined for selection. Two reviewers screened records and charted data, and findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Of 5113 records identified, 4273 were screened after de-duplication, 280 were assessed in full, and 99 sources were included. Evidence came mainly from high-income countries and concerned BRCA1/2 carriers; 12 sources focused on Lynch syndrome. Oocyte and embryo cryopreservation were feasible, but live-birth outcomes were rarely reported. Oral contraception was associated with lower ovarian cancer risk and, in BRCA1 carriers, a modest increase in breast cancer risk with longer use. HRT after premenopausal risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy was not associated with increased breast cancer risk in women without breast cancer yet remained underused. Counseling content and timing were inconsistent, and evidence for Lynch syndrome, low- and middle-income countries, and minority ethnic populations was sparse.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive counseling covering fertility preservation, preimplantation genetic testing, contraception, and HRT should begin at genetic diagnosis and precede irreversible surgery. The proposed 10-step framework requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Mode-specific fetal heart rate signal dropout as a marker of perinatal asphyxia: A multicenter observational study using causal machine learning methods.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Karmakar D, Mendis L, Keenan E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiotocography (CTG) is the standard method for intrapartum fetal monitoring. Modern systems acquire fetal heart rate (FHR) using external Doppler ultrasound (US) or internal fetal scalp electrocardiography (ECG). We evaluated whether mode-specific FHR signal dropout was associated with perinatal asphyxia and whether it should be retained as an informative, mode-aware feature for downstream predictive models.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study using routinely collected clinical and CTG data from Mercy Hospital for Women, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010-2021; Werribee Mercy Hospital, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010-2021; and the Czech CTU-UHB database from University Hospital Brno, for 2010-2012. A total of 46 662 labor episodes at ≥36 weeks' gestation with ≥15 min of interpretable CTG data in the final 60 min before birth were analyzed (32 242 in the model-development cohort, 548 in the Czech validation cohort, and 13 872 in the Australian community validation cohort). The exposure was mode-specific FHR dropout, classified as US low dropout, US high dropout (>30%), ECG low dropout, or ECG high dropout (>30%). The primary outcome was sustained perinatal asphyxia, defined using a Delphi-consensus composite of clinical, biochemical, and neurologic criteria.
RESULTS: In the model-development cohort, 860 cases of perinatal asphyxia occurred (2.67%, 95% CI 2.49%-2.85%). Compared with US low dropout, ECG high dropout was associated with higher risk of asphyxia (inverse probability weighting IPW-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.14, 95% CI 2.20-4.48; targeted maximum likelihood estimation-adjusted OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.21-3.58), corresponding to an absolute risk increase of 2.27% (one additional case per 44 births). Survival analysis supported elevated hazards (HR 4.76, 95% CI 2.98-7.62). External validation supported the direction of association, although estimates varied across cohorts.
CONCLUSION: In retrospective multicenter analyses, high FHR dropout during ECG monitoring was associated with increased perinatal asphyxia risk. These findings support evaluating mode-specific dropout as an informative signal-quality feature in future predictive models. Prospective validation of such models is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (Breus' mole): A nationwide retrospective study in Japan.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Nagao T, Ito Y, Suemitsu T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence, diagnostic features, and perinatal outcomes of massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (MST) in Japan.
METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective study (2018-2023) analyzed confirmed cases of MST, defined as a laminated hematoma with a maximum thickness ≥1 cm. Maternal characteristics, sonographic patterns, and perinatal complications were evaluated.
RESULTS: Of 346 741 deliveries across 87 tertiary perinatal centers, 69 pathologically confirmed MST cases were identified at 27 centers, yielding an incidence of 0.019% (69/346 741). Median maternal age was 33 years and body mass index (BMI) was 21.1. Chronic hypertension was present in 8.7% (6/69). Diagnoses occurred antenatally in 81.2% (56/69) and postpartum in 18.8% (13/69). Ultrasound findings included placentomegaly or a placental mass with variable echogenicity. During follow-up, echogenicity changed in 28% of cases and lesion size in 57%. Perinatal outcomes included induced abortion in 13.0% (9/69), miscarriage before 22 weeks in 5.8% (4/69), stillbirth in 7.2% (5/69), preterm birth in 52.2% (36/69), and term delivery in 21.7% (15/69). Among preterm births, one neonatal death and two infant deaths occurred. After excluding induced abortion and miscarriage before 22 weeks, small-for-gestational-age status was present in 53.6% (30/56) of infants, pre-eclampsia occurred in 16.1% (9/56), and preterm premature rupture of membranes occurred in 23.2% (13/56). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was required for 82.4% (42/51) of live births.
CONCLUSION: MST is a rare but high-risk placental disorder associated with miscarriage, stillbirth, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth, and pre-eclampsia. When MST is suspected antenatally, close maternal and fetal surveillance is warranted.

articles.title: Assessment of fetal head descent and risk of complicated forceps delivery: Role of the suprapubic descent angle.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Hashiramoto S, Takita H, Suzuki Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the suprapubic descent angle (SDA) with conventional measures for discriminating complicated forceps delivery and to explore whether discrepancies between SDA-derived station and conventional fetal station assessments identify higher-risk cases among women undergoing forceps delivery.
METHODS: This prospective cohort included consecutive women with term, singleton, cephalic fetuses in occiput anterior position undergoing forceps delivery at a single tertiary center in Japan during 2025. Before forceps application, SDA, transperineal ultrasound station, angle of progression, head direction, and digital station were assessed. Complicated forceps delivery comprised ≥3 traction attempts, failed forceps requiring cesarean delivery, obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI), blood loss >1500 g, or significant neonatal trauma. Receiver operating characteristic curves assessed discrimination. Internal validation used 2000 participant-level bootstrap samples, repeating regression fitting and Youden cutoff selection. Sensitivity analysis excluding OASI from the composite outcome was also conducted.
RESULTS: Among 118 women, 23 (19.5%) experienced the composite outcome. SDA showed the highest area under the curve (AUC) among individual measures (0.765; 95% confidence interval, 0.641-0.890). The discrepancy between digital station and SDA-derived station had an apparent AUC of 0.838 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.836. Apparent sensitivity and specificity at the data-derived cutoff were 69.6% and 91.6%; corresponding optimism-corrected estimates were 64.8% and 90.5%. Excluding OASI left 12 events; the apparent and optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.880 and 0.879.
CONCLUSIONS: The SDA and the discrepancy between digital station and SDA-derived station showed promising discrimination of complicated forceps delivery. External validation is required before clinical application or recommendation of a cutoff.

articles.title: Effect of the menstrual cycle on common cold susceptibility and severity: insights from the Pittsburgh cold study 3 dataset.
articles.authors: Hanstock HG, Harrison SE
articles.abstract: Changes in circulating immune parameters over the menstrual cycle have been previously described, but there is limited evidence linking these changes to alterations in common cold susceptibility. Using data from the Pittsburgh Cold Study 3 we investigated whether menstrual cycle phase affects susceptibility to and severity of experimental rhinovirus infection. This secondary analysis included 27 naturally menstruating (NM) women and 17 hormonal contraception (HC) users <40 years. Cycle day and phase were estimated from self-reported data, whereby the first five days of the cycle were labelled as the early follicular (EF) phase, the final 10 days as the luteal (L) phase and remaining days as the transition period (TP). Dominant phase during the 5-day post-inoculation quarantine was taken as the mode for EF (n = 9) and L phases (n = 5) only. Objective cold development did not differ between NM (44%) and HC (35%; p = 0.549), nor between phase on quarantine day 1 within NM (χ2 = 0.89, p = 0.64). However, rhinovirus severity was lower during in L versus EF, represented by peak viral nasal titre (p = 0.003, d = 1.71), total symptom scores (p = 0.01, d = 1.37) and total adjusted mucus weight (p = 0.03, d = 0.86). These observations were supported by linear mixed models for viral load and symptoms during quarantine, which showed blunted viral load and symptom trajectories in L vs. EF. These exploratory, hypothesis generating findings suggest that menstrual cycle phase may influence common cold severity in healthy premenopausal women.

articles.title: Development of a Self-Management Program for Pelvic Organ Prolapse Patients Based on the LEARNS Model: A Delphi Study.
articles.authors: Zhang L, He F, Qiao X et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop a practical, scientifically valid self-management care plan for patients with Pelvic Organ Prolapse (POP) based on the LEARNS model, thereby providing evidence-based guidance for clinical practice and improving patient outcomes.
METHODS: Following comprehensive preliminary work-including an extensive literature review-we initially drafted a self-management plan for POP patients grounded in the LEARNS framework. Subsequently, we conducted two rounds of written expert consultation using the Delphi method, followed by rigorous statistical analysis to validate the proposed indicators.
RESULTS: All 15 questionnaires distributed in each of the two Delphi rounds were returned, yielding a 100% response rate that demonstrated high expert engagement. In the first and second rounds, coefficients of variation ranged from 0.11 to 0.24 and 0 to 0.24, respectively, while expert authority coefficients reached 0.876 and 0.906. Kendall's coefficients of concordance for primary and secondary indicators ranged from 0.158 to 0.215 in the first round and 0.184 to 0.327 in the second round, with all P-values < 0.05 indicating significant consensus. Ultimately, the program comprised six primary indicators and sixty secondary indicators, structured systematically according to the LEARNS model.
CONCLUSION: The self-management program for POP patients, developed based on the LEARNS model, provides a structured framework through six key stages- "Listen, Establish, Adopt, Reinforce, Name, and Strengthen"-to help patients progressively master self-management measures and enhance their self-management capabilities during the hospital stay.

articles.title: Pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A beyond the first trimester: Predictive value for adverse pregnancy outcomes (Review).
articles.authors: Kavvalou M, Tzanaki I, Velegrakis A et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) is a placentally-derived metalloproteinase that serves a key role in trophoblast invasion and fetal growth through the regulation of insulin-like growth factor bioavailability. Since its introduction into first-trimester aneuploidy screening, low maternal serum PAPP-A concentrations have been consistently associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preeclampsia, preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, low birth weight and stillbirth. Although the clinical importance of reduced first-trimester PAPP-A concentrations is well established, the predictive value of PAPP-A measurements beyond the first trimester, particularly during the second trimester, remains less clearly defined. The present review summarizes the current research regarding the association between maternal serum PAPP-A concentrations throughout pregnancy and adverse obstetric outcomes, with a particular emphasis on second-trimester findings. Available evidence suggests that persistently low maternal serum PAPP-A concentrations from the first into the second trimester are associated with placental dysfunction-related complications. However, despite statistically significant associations, the predictive performance of PAPP-A as a standalone biomarker remains limited. Future prospective studies are required to determine whether incorporating second-trimester PAPP-A into multimarker prediction models can improve risk stratification, clinical decision-making and pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Plasma cell-free DNA-based next-generation sequencing for molecular profiling of diffuse gliomas.
articles.authors: Singh S, Singh J, Bhardwaj S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the utility of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) for molecular profiling of diffuse gliomas (DG) by assessing concordance with matched tumor tissue DNA, mutation profiles, variant allele frequencies, therapeutically actionable alterations, and survival associations.
