METHODS: A total of 30 DG cases were included, and 10 healthy controls were included. Paired plasma cfDNA and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor tissue DNA were analyzed using targeted NGS.
RESULTS: Plasma cfDNA concentrations were higher in patients with DG (n = 30) than in healthy controls (P = .0002), though this comparison was limited by the small, unmatched control cohort (n = 10). Targeted sequencing predominantly identified single nucleotide variants (81%). Gene-level concordance between plasma cfDNA and tumor tissue DNA was 90.0%, whereas ≥1 matched variant was identified in 76.7% of cases. Plasma cfDNA detectability and concordance varied across DG subtypes, and multiple therapeutically actionable alterations involving receptor tyrosine kinase, MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and mismatch repair pathways were identified. Higher plasma cfDNA concentrations were associated with shorter survival, whereas cases with matched plasma and tissue variants demonstrated longer survival; however, these associations were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Plasma cfDNA-based liquid biopsy may serve as a minimally invasive approach for molecular profiling of DG, demonstrating high gene-level concordance with tumor tissue DNA and detection of clinically relevant, potentially actionable genomic alterations. Although variant-level concordance and detectability varied across glioma subtypes, these findings support a complementary role for plasma cfDNA analysis in DG. Further prospective studies, including serial sampling and matched leukocyte controls, are needed to improve analytical sensitivity and define its clinical utility.

articles.title: Performance evaluation of a novel size-based microfluidic platform for rare cell detection in blood and malignant effusions.
articles.authors: Saini VM, Oner E, Cahill C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating tumour cells (CTCs) are promising minimally invasive biomarkers of tumour dissemination and disease biology, but low abundance and phenotypic heterogeneity make them challenging to isolate, particularly in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Physical cell-selection approaches based on size and deformability may facilitate recovery of heterogeneous tumour populations. This study evaluated the performance of the Bio-Rad™ Genesis Cell Isolation System, a microfluidic platform based on these properties, across different tumour phenotypes and liquid biopsy sample types.
METHODS: Recovery capabilities of the Genesis enrichment and enumeration workflows were evaluated using the EpCAM-high H1975 and EpCAM-low H1299 NSCLC cell lines, and a standardised spike-in protocol. Following optimisation, peripheral (Pe) and pulmonary vein (PV) blood from patients with resectable NSCLC, ascites from patients with advanced gynaecological cancers, and matched Pe blood and pleural fluid (PF) from patients with advanced NSCLC were assessed using the enumeration workflow. Tumour cells were identified by immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: High and consistent recovery was observed for both H1975 and H1299 cells, independent of EpCAM expression, with mean recovery of 68.81 ± 10.53% and 65.17 ± 9.53% using enrichment, and 70.05 ± 10.06% and 80.51 ± 5.72% using enumeration, respectively. CTCs were detected in 2/11 Pe blood and 3/4 PV samples from patients with resectable NSCLC. Ascites contained 69-1113 ascites epithelial cells (AECs)/mL, with 89.31-98.21% occurring within clusters. Pleural epithelial cells (PECs) were identified in 3/3 PF samples from advanced NSCLC patients (16.3-132 cells/mL), predominantly as clusters, but were absent from matched Pe blood. Notably, PECs were detected in PF despite negative cytology in one patient.
CONCLUSIONS: The Genesis demonstrated consistent, EpCAM-independent recovery, across NSCLC models and enabled tumour cell and cluster detection across diverse clinical liquid biopsy specimens. Its ability to analyse tumour-rich fluids, including a cytology-negative PF sample, supports further investigation as a versatile and complementary platform for rare cell detection and characterisation.

articles.title: PADI2 facilitates progression and cisplatin resistance of epithelial ovarian cancer via m6A methylation.
articles.authors: Yin X, Zhou J, Zhao S et al.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy resistance is a challenge in the management of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). The regulation of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification has emerged as a potential strategy to overcome this resistance. Peptidyl Arginine Deiminase 2 (PADI2) was found to be upregulated and highly methylated in EOC samples, correlating with a poor prognosis. Downregulation of PADI2 inhibited colony formation, cell proliferation, and cisplatin (cDDP) resistance in EOC cells. METTL3 was identified as the m6A writer of PADI2 mRNA, while YTHDF2 recognized and bound the m6A-methylated PADI2 mRNA, enhancing its translation. This activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway facilitated cDDP resistance in EOC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Knockdown of METTL3 or YTHDF2 decreased PADI2 mRNA expression and suppressed tumor growth and cDDP resistance. In conclusion, a mechanism was identified whereby m6A-modified PADI2 induces cDDP resistance and EOC progression, providing a potential target for the development of therapeutic strategies for EOC treatment.

articles.title: Household wealth, marriage, and male fertility in sub-Saharan Africa: a cross-sectional comparative study from three countries.
articles.authors: Michael TO
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male fertility remains underexplored in demographic and health research across sub-Saharan Africa, where analytical focus is disproportionately placed on women. Yet men's socioeconomic positions, particularly as reflected by household wealth, and marital union trajectories play critical roles in shaping fertility outcomes and population dynamics.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined how household wealth and marital union status intersect to influence fertility outcomes among men in Nigeria, South Africa, and Uganda.
DESIGN: A cross-sectional, comparative analysis was conducted using harmonized data from multiple rounds of the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series-Demographic and Health Surveys (IPUMS-DHS).
METHODS: The study analysed a pooled weighted sample of 20,587 men aged 15-59 years. Descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and general linear models (GLMs) were used to assess associations between fertility (number of children fathered), household wealth quintiles, marital union status, and their interaction effects.
RESULTS: Mean number of children fathered was highest in Uganda (2.60), followed by Nigeria (2.29), and lowest in South Africa (1.48). Men in multiple marital unions reported substantially higher fertility (mean = 6.10) compared with men in one union (3.44) and never-married men (0.16). Fertility declined across wealth gradients, from 2.57 among the poorest to 1.87 among the richest quintile and increased sharply with age and early union entry. Marital union status was a strong predictor of fertility (Partial η² = 0.082), and the interaction between union status and wealth was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Men in one union within the poorest quintile had 1.47 fewer children (B = -1.465, p < 0.001) compared with men in multiple unions.
CONCLUSION: Male fertility in sub-Saharan Africa is strongly shaped by the intersection of household wealth and marital union status. Without male-inclusive and socioeconomically responsive reproductive health policies, fertility inequalities and demographic pressures are likely to persist across the region.

articles.title: Pelvic organ prolapse: emerging concepts in molecular mechanisms and tissue repair.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: He Z, Tong H, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common and progressive pelvic floor disorder associated with pregnancy and vaginal delivery, ageing, obesity, menopause and other conditions that increase or prolong mechanical burden on pelvic supportive tissues. Previous studies have linked POP to extracellular matrix remodeling, oxidative stress, hormonal changes, genetic susceptibility and fibroblast dysfunction. However, these findings are still often presented as separate pathogenic theories or molecular observations, which makes it difficult to explain how mechanical challenge, cellular dysfunction and structural failure are biologically connected during disease progression. In this Review, we propose that POP can be more coherently understood along a mechanics-cell-matrix axis. Within this framework, chronic mechanical loading and impaired adaptive repair are regarded as the disease-setting in which prolapse develops. Mechanotransduction-related pathways are then considered the upstream bridge linking altered tissue mechanics to fibroblast state change. Oxidative stress, autophagy-related disturbance, apoptosis and senescence are further discussed as bridge-amplifier processes that deepen repair failure, whereas extracellular matrix imbalance is viewed as the structural endpoint of declining tissue support. Hormonal status, genetic susceptibility and immune remodeling further influence the course of POP. Fibrosis-associated fibroblast activation may coexist with collagen disorganization, matrix degradation and impaired elastic recoil. This review connects these tissue findings with the distinctive mechanical demands of pelvic support and considers their implications for repair (Tian et al., BJOG, 2024, 131, 1029-1041; Guler and Roovers, Biomolecules, 2022, 12, 94; Wu et al., Front. Med., 2024, 11, 1303044; Ruiz-Zapata et al., Sci. Rep., 2016, 6, 22971).

articles.title: Identification of novel ferroptosis-associated prognostic genes in cervical cancer using bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Chu H, Tang G et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is a common malignant tumor among women worldwide. However, the relationship between CC and ferroptosis remains to be elucidated. The present study screened differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in CC from The Cancer Genome Atlas database and identified DEGs associated with ferroptosis using the FerrDb database. A total of 2,563 DEGs were upregulated and 2,120 DEGs were downregulated which were more notably enriched in the early region 2 binding factor targets and G2M checkpoint. By crossing ferroptosis-driver, ferroptosis-marker and ferroptosis-suppressor genes and DEGs, 80 ferroptosis-associated prognostic genes were identified. In total, 24 potential targeted drugs targeting key genes were predicted, providing a possible basis to predict the prognosis and treatment of CC. The expression levels of stearoyl-CoA desaturase, transferrin receptor (TFRC) and carbonic anhydrase 9 were experimentally validated by PCR, which was consistent with the present bioinformatics analysis. Furthermore, knocking down TFRC inhibited cell proliferation and migration in CC cells in vitro. In conclusion, the present study identified key genes associated with ferroptosis in CC and further research is warranted to explore their underlying mechanisms and potentially become effective clinical prognostic biomarkers in the future.

articles.title: Differentiation of PD, MSA and PSP using clinical data from the prospective AIDP cohort.
articles.authors: Xie T, Vaillancourt DE, Barmpoutis A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiation of clinical features among Parkinson's disease (PD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy parkinsonism (MSAp) is challenging, with a paucity of comparative studies on comprehensive and overlapped clinical features across three of them.
OBJECTIVE: Comprehensive data from the Automated Imaging Differentiation for Parkinsonism (AIDP) study could offer valuable insights into their diagnostic differentiation among PD, PSP and MSAp.
METHODS: Demographics, comprehensive motor and non-motor features, daily living function and quality of life (QoL) data were prospectively collected from individuals with PD, probable PSP, and probable MSAp at their second AIDP study visit. Clinical diagnoses were confirmed independently by three movement disorder neurologists. Cross-sectional group comparisons were conducted using Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise tests. Median and logistic regression models were applied to assess differences, adjusting for age, sex, disease duration and levodopa equivalent dosage.
RESULTS: Among 168 individuals (90 PD, 56 probable PSP, 22 probable MSAp), overall motor, non-motor, daily living functions and QoL measures were found to be more impaired in MSAp and PSP than PD. Individuals with PSP experienced more oculomotor and cognitive impairment than PD and MSAp. Systolic and diastolic orthostatic blood pressure (BP) drop, orthostatic lightheadedness, and urinary incontinence were associated with MSAp. The presence of systolic orthostatic BP drop was also against the diagnosis of PSP. There were no differences in anxiety, depression, fatigue and constipation across three parkinsonism subtypes.
CONCLUSION: Distinct impairments across PD, PSP, and MSAp in this well-characterized, prospectively collected, comprehensive motor and non-motor dataset provide valuable information for clinical differentiation.

articles.title: Controlled Pt Doping of Silica-Supported Ni Nanoparticles through Surface Organometallic Chemistry on Metals: Applications as Catalysts for Selective Hydrogenation Reactions.
articles.authors: Zuluaga A, Smitkriti S, Vanoye L et al.
articles.abstract: Silica-supported Ni/Pt nanoparticles were synthesized through the selective Pt doping of silica-supported Ni nanoparticles using an original approach that can be considered as a Surface OrganoMetallic Chemistry on Metals (SOMC@M). The targeted bimetallic nanoparticles were obtained via the selective grafting of Pt-(COD)-Me2 onto the surface of the nickel nanoparticles. The resulting solids were fully characterized using several techniques, including infrared spectroscopy, HAADF-STEM, and HRTEM with EDX, confirming the successful incorporation and uniform distribution of Pt centers onto the Ni nanoparticles without side deposition of Pt onto the silica support. These experimental observations were also supported by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations. Further H2 treatments at 500 °C were applied to the Pt-grafted Ni NPs to enable the removal of surface Pt ligands and the diffusion of Pt atoms into the Ni nanoparticles. This SOMC@M methodology was able to secure the precise control over Pt loading and Pt distribution within the Ni NPs, key parameters for enhancing catalytic performance. The resulting materials were found to exhibit remarkable selectivity in both the hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene and the semihydrogenation of hex-3-yn-1-ol, demonstrating the potential of SOMC@M as a versatile approach for the design of tunable and efficient bimetallic catalysts.

articles.title: Short-term low-dose aspirin attenuates metabolic and endothelial dysfunction, as well as prothrombotic and inflammatory responses, orchestrated by combined oral contraceptive exposure in female rats.
articles.authors: Fabunmi OA, Fabunmi FC, Olaiya AO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherothrombosis is a chronic, multifactorial, and progressive disease responsible for a significant number of deaths globally. It involves interactions between endothelial dysfunction, coagulation activation, platelet activity, and fibrin turnover. Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) may influence these pathways, potentially altering thrombotic risk. The aim was to assess the impact of COC administration on metabolic status and the risk of atherothrombotic disorders in young female rats, beyond evaluating the therapeutic effects of short-term low-dose aspirin (LDA) treatment.
METHODS: Thirty (n = 30) five-week-old female Sprague Dawley rats were given low-dose COC (LCOC) or a high-dose COC (HCOC) for six weeks before treatment with LDA for another four weeks. These rats were compared with those given only LCOC or HCOC without LDA treatment. Whereas rats that received distilled water (as a vehicle) and LDA only served as controls. Body weight and metabolic status were measured weekly. Parameters related to glucose regulation, lipid profiles, inflammatory cytokines, haematological indices, coagulation, and endothelial dysfunction were evaluated at the end of the experiment.
RESULTS: Rats exposed to HCOC exhibited abnormal metabolic and lipid profiles, including impaired glucose tolerance, accompanied by significantly higher insulin (p < 0.001), triglycerides and very low-density lipoprotein levels (p = 0.004) when compared with control groups. The HCOC treatment was also associated with elevated platelet count (p = 0.02) and markers of inflammation and endothelial dysfunction, including IL-6 (p < 0.05), TNF-alpha (p < 0.05), MCP-1 (p < 0.001), TF (p < 0.001), D-dimer (p < 0.001), von Willebrand factor (p < 0.05), and low nitric oxide (p < 0.001) when compared with control groups. Notably, SBP and MAP (p = 0.02) were also significantly higher in these animals, suggesting an increased atherothrombotic risk in response to HCOC when compared to control groups. Interestingly, short-term LDA attenuate atherothrombotic risk by improving metabolic status, alleviating inflammation, and lowering the markers of coagulation and endothelial dysfunction in rats exposed to HCOC.
CONCLUSION: Short-term LDA reduces the risk of atherothrombotic disorders by attenuating biomarker level associated with metabolic dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, proinflammation, and hypercoagulation in female rats exposed to high-dose COC. However, additional experimental…

articles.title: "Hearing the Ovarian Cancer Whisper": A Pipeline Program Introducing Medical Students to Gynecologic Oncology, Focusing on the Diagnosis and Management of Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Slaybe A, Barengo NC, Runowicz CD
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pipeline programs help medical students explore and define future career pathways. The "Hearing the Ovarian Cancer Whisper" (HOW) Dr. Robert C. Knapp Award was created to expose medical students to gynecologic oncology, with emphasis on recognizing, treating, and improving outcomes for patients with ovarian cancer. This study describes and analyzes the characteristics of HOW participants and their eventual residency choices.
METHOD: We conducted a non-concurrent cohort study evaluation using the HOW database of medical students who received the Dr. Robert C. Knapp Medical Student Award and completed the four-week gynecologic oncology elective between 2011 and 2025. Baseline information included medical school, sex, and scholarship year. Follow-up information was obtained through phone, email, or text communication and included residency, fellowship, specialty, and practice location. Of 149 award recipients, 24 were excluded because of missing information, nonresponse, dropout, or pending follow-up, resulting in 125 participants in the primary analytic cohort.
RESULTS: Among the 125 participants included in the primary analysis, 53.6% entered an OBGYN residency and 46.4% another specialty. Three participants subsequently pursued gynecologic oncology fellowship training during the observation period. Most participants were female (84.0%). Florida International University Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine accounted for the largest proportion of participants (44.0%). The distribution of OBGYN residency entry varied by scholarship year, although the overall association did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.080).
CONCLUSION: These findings describe the longitudinal career trajectories of participants in a gynecologic oncology educational program but do not establish that program participation caused or independently influenced specialty choice.

articles.title: Study on copy number variant detection results of 472 fetuses with non-structural ultrasound abnormalities in non-advanced age pregnant women and the correlation with adverse obstetric history.
articles.authors: Lin L, Wu H, Zheng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate copy number variant (CNV) results in 472 fetuses with non-structural ultrasound abnormalities among pregnant women under 35 years, and analyze the association between adverse obstetric history and pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) CNVs and variants of uncertain significance (VUS).
METHODS: A total of 472 pregnant women aged <35 years with fetal non-structural ultrasound abnormalities were retrospectively enrolled. All participants were divided into groups with or without adverse obstetric history. We summarized the distribution of non-structural ultrasound abnormalities, calculated the overall and stratified detection rates of P/LP CNVs and VUS, and compared differences between groups.
RESULTS: The mean maternal age was 28.73 ± 3.59 years; 22.0% had a positive history. Abnormal ultrasound soft markers accounted for 82.6% of cases, followed by fetal growth restriction (12.3%) and abnormal amniotic fluid volume (4.0%). The overall detection rates were 5.7% for P/LP CNVs and 9.1% for VUS. The highest detection rate of P/LP CNVs was observed in fetuses with abnormal amniotic fluid volume (10.5%), while the highest detection rate of VUS was seen in abnormal ultrasound soft markers (9.2%). The combined detection rate of P/LP and VUS differed among different types of isolated abnormal ultrasound soft markers, with tricuspid regurgitation, persistent right umbilical vein and persistent left superior vena cava showing higher detection rates. No significant differences in overall P/LP CNV and VUS rates were found between women with and without adverse pregnancy history (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Non-advanced age pregnant women with fetal non-structural ultrasound abnormalities carry a non-negligible risk of P/LP CNVs and VUS. Different ultrasound soft markers present distinct CNV detection rates. Adverse obstetric history does not alter the P/LP CNVs and VUS detection rate.

articles.title: Appraisal of clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements on aspirin in pregnancy: a systematic review using the AGREE II instrument.
articles.authors: Hu Y, Chen D, Ni J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recommendations regarding the use of aspirin in obstetrics vary across clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements of differing quality. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the quality of these documents, with particular focus on the recommended daily dosage, timing of initiation, and cessation of aspirin in the obstetric setting. This study employed a systematic review and quality appraisal approach using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation (AGREE) II methodology.
METHODS: The study included the most recent versions of all international and national/regional clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements on aspirin use in pregnancy, published in English or Chinese. Data were retrieved from PubMed (11 April 2025), three Chinese academic databases (the Chinese Medical Association Database, Wanfang Data and China National Knowledge Infrastructure) and four guideline databases (11 April 2025). Two reviewers independently screened the searched items and extracted data. Four reviewers independently scored documents using AGREE II. Recommendations from all documents were tabulated and visualized using a color-coded grid.
RESULTS: A total of 32 documents were include, encompassing six obstetric conditions: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS), Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR), advanced maternal age, pregnancy loss, stillbirth and hypertension/pre-eclampsia. The included documents demonstrated strong performance in the domains of scope and purpose (median score: 89.67%, inter-quartile range [IQR] 61.11%-98.61%) and clarity of presentation (median 87.93%, IQR 50%-100%). The editorial independence domain also received relatively high score (median 73.59%, IQR 0%-100%). However, performance was lower in the domain of applicability (median 45.08%, IQR 0%-89.58%). Although aspirin 75-100 mg daily represents the most commonly recommended dosage, a broad range of dosing recommendations exists across most clinical scenarios. However, considerable controversy existed regarding the optimal timing of discontinuation, particularly in cases of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy/pre-eclampsia.
CONCLUSION: Guidelines and consensus statements, which were generally of relatively high quality, demonstrated that most documents support the use of aspirin for specific obstetric complications. Given these substantial variations in dosage ranges, treatment timing, and combination therapy recommendations, developing standardized,…

articles.title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Treatment with Botulinum Toxin A Compared to Drug Therapy in Patients with Urge Incontinence: A Clinical Trial Study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology of India
articles.authors: Ghanbari Z, Eftekhar T, Deldar M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urge incontinence is one of the disorders that affect many individuals. Treatment of patients is based on drug strategies; however, complete recovery has not been established. The use of botulinum toxin A is an important therapeutic approach that is used alongside other treatments today; however, few studies have been conducted.
METHODS: Sixty patients participated in this study. Patients are divided into three groups of 20 people. One group was treated with Botox (200 IU), the second with Botox (300 IU), and the third with antimuscarinic drugs. Patients were followed up for 6 months. At the end of 6 months of treatment, the results were evaluated by visiting the patient or calling them and asking the questions of the ICIQ-OAB questionnaire.
RESULTS: The percentage of changes in the number of urinations at night in the second group was higher compared to the other two groups; it was statistically significant (p = 0.018). Based on the results, it was shown that no complications were observed in the patients of the both groups. On the contrary, it was shown that in the second group, complications were observed in 4 patients (20%) (p = 0.03).
CONCLUSION: In general, it can be said that treatment with Botox (200 IU) can have a better effect on improving the frequency of urination compared to the other two types of treatment.

articles.title: Information rather than architecture: cross-learner attribution and clinician-model complementarity in CIN2+ risk prediction for women referred for colposcopy.
articles.authors: Wu Y, Wang A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep tabular models, including self-supervised and pretrained foundation models, are increasingly proposed for clinical risk prediction, but their value over conventional learners is rarely tested against matched controls, and their role relative to clinician judgement is seldom examined.
METHODS: In a retrospective single-centre cohort of 879 women referred for colposcopy (242 CIN2+, 27.5%), 15 routinely recorded variables, including a clinician image-based assessment documented before histopathology, were modelled with ten model families under one fixed protocol (single fold assignment and seed, no tuning). Discrimination was compared by paired DeLong tests and bootstrap. Two analyses were pre-specified: exact Shapley attribution of discrimination to five clinical groups of variables in every model family, and a complementarity analysis asking whether routine data identify CIN2+ among women judged negative by the clinician. Frozen models were evaluated in a 103-case two-centre external cohort.
RESULTS: Out-of-fold AUROC ranged from 0.726 to 0.761. No model outperformed logistic regression (AUROC 0.757; CatBoost -0.002, p = 0.860; TabPFN +0.004, p = 0.554), and three matched ablations of a self-supervised tabular Transformer were null (all p ≥ 0.096). Removing the clinician assessment lowered AUROC in all ten families (by 0.041 to 0.072; all p ≤ 0.008). Shapley attribution ranked five variable groups identically in every family (Kendall's W = 1.00; permutation p < 0.001): the clinician assessment (39% to 50% of discrimination above chance), then cytology, HPV testing, colposcopic findings and demographic history. The clinician assessment alone had sensitivity 0.504 and specificity 0.882; 49.6% of CIN2+ occurred in clinician-negative women. Re-reviewing the 20% of clinician-negative women with the highest model risk identified 34.2% (95% CI 25.7-42.7%) of the missed CIN2+, against 20% expected at random, raising pathway sensitivity to 0.674 at specificity 0.733. External AUROC of logistic regression was 0.710.
CONCLUSIONS: On routine structured data from a colposcopy-referral population, and under a common protocol, model architecture did not determine performance; predictor information did. Retrospectively, routine data complemented the clinician modestly in clinician-negative women, rather than replacing clinical judgement. Claims that complex architectures improve clinical tabular prediction should be tested against logistic regression with…

articles.title: Preparedness of undergraduate health students to provide women-specific epilepsy care: knowledge gaps and stigmatizing attitudes in Saudi Arabia.
articles.authors: Alzahrani F, Alharbi Y, Almuzaini Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with epilepsy have distinct reproductive, clinical, and psychosocial healthcare needs that require women-specific care. This study assessed the preparedness of undergraduate health students by examining their knowledge, attitudes, and stigmatizing beliefs.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 339 undergraduate health students at Taibah University, Saudi Arabia, using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Multiple linear regression examined the factors associated with total knowledge score, while the ≥60% knowledge benchmark was retained for descriptive and exploratory sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 7.37 ± 2.96 out of 16 (46.1%), and 23.6% met the ≥60% benchmark. Knowledge gaps were most evident in reproductive health, hormonal influences, fertility, antiseizure medication safety, and contraceptive counseling topics. Attitudes were generally supportive, although stigma persisted regarding marriage, parenting, and close relationships. Male gender and earlier academic year were associated with lower adjusted knowledge scores, whereas field of study, epilepsy history, formal education, and recent training were not significantly associated with knowledge.
CONCLUSION: Undergraduate health students demonstrated substantial knowledge gaps in women-specific epilepsy care, despite generally supportive attitudes. Reviewing curricular coverage and addressing identified gaps in reproductive health, medication safety, contraception, pregnancy-related care, and stigma may enhance preparedness for evidence-based, patient-centered care. The threshold-based logistic sensitivity analysis should be considered exploratory because of the low events-per-parameter ratio.

articles.title: From evidence to impact: purposeful use of implementation science theories, models, and frameworks in genomics and precision health.
articles.authors: Fariman S, Best S, Taylor N et al.
articles.abstract: A growing number of genomics precision health applications are supported by robust evidence, yet their integration into routine clinical and population health practice remains slow, uneven, and inequitable. This article demonstrates how implementation science (IS) theories, models, and frameworks (TMFs) can support the translation of evidence-based genomics applications by presenting three cases from pediatric precision oncology, reproductive genetic carrier screening, and population genomic screening for hereditary conditions. Across the three cases, IS TMFs were purposefully selected, adapted, combined, or supplemented to fit the implementation context, core complexities, and the conceptual work required, and were revisited as implementation evolved. We argue that this purposeful approach can provide an operational backbone for integrating precision health innovations into real-world systems of care and help transform individual implementation efforts into transferable knowledge.

articles.title: Age-specific HPV genotype distribution and associations with cervical lesions and vaginal microecological status in Northeast China: a retrospective study of 73,828 individuals.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: He Y, Pan Y, Sheng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is a major etiological factor in cervical carcinogenesis. HPV prevalence and genotype distribution show substantial geographic heterogeneity across China, highlighting the need for region-specific epidemiological data. This study characterized age-specific HPV infection and genotype patterns in Northeast China and further examined their associations with cervical pathology and vaginal microecological status.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed HPV genotyping data from 73,828 individuals tested between 2020 and 2024. Histopathological data were available for 8,755 women, and vaginal microecological assessments were available for 2,428 women. Age-related differences, HPV genotype distributions, infection patterns, and their associations with cervical pathology and vaginal microecological categories were evaluated using nonparametric and χ² tests.
RESULTS: Overall HPV positivity was 20.83% (15,376/73,828) and showed a bimodal age distribution, with the highest prevalence among participants aged < 25 years (34.44%) and a second peak at 60-65 years (25.90%). HPV16, HPV52, and HPV58 were the three most frequently detected genotypes. Single HR-HPV infection differed significantly across cervical histopathological categories and was most frequent in cervical cancer (57.81%, P < 0.001). HPV positivity also differed across vaginal microecological categories (P < 0.001), with the highest rate observed in the bacterial vaginosis group (32.66%); however, no individual HPV genotype remained significantly associated with microecological category after FDR correction.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide regional epidemiological evidence for HPV surveillance and cervical cancer prevention planning and support further prospective investigation of the relationship between vaginal microecological alterations and HPV infection.

articles.title: The Psychological and Relational Impact of Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser Syndrome: Perspectives of Patients, Mothers and Partners.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Li K, Wakefield CE, McGill BC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome (MRKHS) is a rare reproductive disorder with long-term psychosocial impacts. However, understanding of family and partner relationships that integrates the perspectives of patients, parents, and partners remains limited.
AIMS: To evaluate the psychosocial impact of MRKHS with a focus on psychological and relational functioning, from patient, parent, and partner perspectives in an Australian cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with MRKHS aged ≥ 18 years (n = 23), their parents (n = 8), and partners (n = 3) were recruited from a tertiary centre in Sydney, Australia. Three tailored questionnaires used validated self-report measures to assess physical and psychological health, family functioning, relationship satisfaction, fertility-related quality of life (QoL), sexual function, and personal identity. Comparison data were drawn from published validation studies.
RESULTS: Patients with MRKHS reported comparable self-perceived health and relationship satisfaction to reference groups, but higher anxiety (p = 0.002), more significant dyspareunia (p = 0.006), and poorer perceived family functioning (p < 0.001). They reported better overall fertility-related QoL than couples undergoing fertility treatment (p = 0.03) but had lower scores on the relationship subscale (p = 0.002). MRKHS had a central impact shaping self-identity (p = 0.002). Mothers and partners reported positive wellbeing and family or relationship functioning, although the findings are preliminary due to the limited sample size.
CONCLUSION: MRKHS affects multiple facets of patients' lives, particularly psychological well-being, pain-related sexual function, family dynamics, and personal identity. Optimal care should incorporate tailored psychological support and facilitate open communication between patients and their support network. Larger studies are warranted to examine the psychological impact of MRKHS on parents and partners.

articles.title: Is Ultrasound in Pregnancy an Opportunity for Prevention of Pelvic Floor Dysfunction: A Randomised Controlled Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Ma S, Hay-Smith J, Davie G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy and childbirth are major risk factors for urinary incontinence. Antenatal pelvic floor muscle exercises (PFME) may prevent urinary incontinence. Transabdominal ultrasound scan (TAUS) in pregnancy offers a teachable moment for voluntary pelvic floor muscle contraction (VPFMC).
AIMS: To assess trial methods and feasibility of TAUS in pregnancy to confirm correct VPFMC.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A parallel randomised controlled pilot trial (registered 22/4/2022, Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, ACTRN12622000608763, https://www.anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=383043). Between 30/5/2022 and 29/2/2024, 50 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies were randomised to routine fetal anatomy scan (FAS) or FAS with TAUS assessment of VPFMC. Participants completed questionnaires in pregnancy and postpartum. Sonographers recorded TAUS information. Study findings were analysed descriptively.
RESULTS: From 50 participants (27 control, 23 intervention), 44 (24 control, 20 intervention) and 40 (21 control, 19 intervention) completed the 36 weeks and 3 months postpartum questionnaires, respectively. VPFMC assessment added 3 min (interquartile range 2-5) to FAS. Twenty (91%) intervention participants demonstrated correct VPFMC; sonographers considered VPFMC identification 'easy' for 19/22 (86%). Sixteen of twenty participants (80%) agreed the intervention was worthwhile. Mean PFME self-efficacy increased from baseline in both groups. The proportion of women reporting practicing PFME at least a few times a week increased in both groups during pregnancy, but this was only maintained postpartum in the intervention group.
CONCLUSION: Using TAUS to confirm correct VPFMC at FAS is feasible and acceptable to women and sonographers, and may improve PFME engagement postpartum. A definitive trial is warranted.

articles.title: Operationalizing a Framework for Appraising Seriousness to Guide Decision-Making in Prenatal Care.
articles.authors: Kleiderman E, Laberge AM, Newson AJ et al.
articles.abstract: The seriousness of a genetic condition plays an important role in shaping expectant parents' understanding of results and options following prenatal testing. Yet it is well recognized that the decisions that follow such testing can be fraught. One key concern is that prenatal care professionals can emphasize biomedical or clinical interpretations of seriousness at the expense of more contextual elements as they relate to the circumstances and values of expectant parents. In this article, we draw on three exemplar clinical case studies to demonstrate how a framework for considering seriousness can be employed to expand the breadth and depth of conversations between prenatal care professionals and expectant parents, encourage shared meaning-making around seriousness, and support expectant parents to navigate prenatal decision-making in a way that aligns with their preferences, values, and circumstances. Our framework provides an underpinning structure to the conversations and conceptual spaces in which parental perceptions of seriousness are contextualized and animated. This, in turn, can lead to more effective counseling and improved decision-making based on relevant and contextualized information.

articles.title: Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Daily Clinical Practice, from Voice Dictation to Operating Room Organization: A Targeted Narrative Review with Hysteroscopy as a Clinical Exemplar.
articles.authors: Haimovich S, Fazel A
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering routine care through documentation tools, decision support, and hospital operations. The central question is whether these systems improve clinical work and patient care once embedded in routine workflows, not only whether they perform well on test data. This targeted narrative review follows AI from voice dictation and ambient documentation to operating room (OR) organization, using hysteroscopy as a clinical exemplar of the transition from technical performance to clinical utility. Evidence identified through targeted searches completed on 6 September 2026 was appraised with a framework that distinguishes image-level from patient-level results, internal from independent validation, and discrimination from clinical utility. Randomized trials and multisite observational data show modest, product-dependent benefits of clinician-reviewed ambient documentation; inaccuracies persist. Evidence for patient-message drafting derives from ratings of responses to public-forum questions and supports only bounded, supervised feasibility testing. In hysteroscopy, selected models discriminate well in narrowly defined tasks, but most studies are retrospective, image-level, or internally validated, and patient-level errors in high-risk categories are seldom reported. Reported gains in OR scheduling come largely from simulation. Safe implementation requires a defined clinical need, baseline measurement, subgroup-aware local validation, accountable review, and predefined criteria for expansion or withdrawal.

articles.title: Ovarian Preservation Before Puberty: Surgical Management of Adnexal Torsion in Prepubertal and Prepubertal-Predominant Paediatric Cohorts-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Bakhsh H
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adnexal torsion is a gynaecological emergency in which ovarian preservation or removal is decided intraoperatively. Prepubertal girls have the longest reproductive and endocrine horizon, yet they are commonly pooled with postmenarchal adolescents. This review estimated how often torsion episodes in prepubertal and prepubertal-predominant paediatric cohorts are managed by oophorectomy, together with imaging findings after ovarian-sparing surgery, recurrence and diagnosed malignancy. Methods: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261496245) searched Europe PMC (including MEDLINE), OpenAlex, preprint servers, ClinicalTrials.gov and citation networks to 2 September 2026, with an update search to 12 October 2026; Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL and CENTRAL were not searched. Eligible cohorts documented premenarchal status (direct evidence) or had a central age of 12.0 years or younger (indirect evidence). Proportions were pooled with a binomial-normal generalised linear mixed model; JBI appraisal and GRADE were applied. Results: Thirty studies were included. Across 14 cohorts (1011 episodes), 42.8% (95% CI 28.1-58.9) were managed by oophorectomy, with extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 94.0%; 95% prediction interval 6.0-89.9%); the estimate was 33.4% (8.5-69.8) in the 4 cohorts with documented premenarchal status and 24.8% (14.4-37.3) in the 7 cohorts meeting all appraisal items. Follicular activity or normal morphology was seen on follow-up imaging in 89.9% (81.9-95.9) of 234 imaged adnexa after ovarian-sparing surgery. Recurrence was 12.9% (6.6-21.0; 11 cohorts) and diagnosed malignancy 2.7% (1.0-4.6; 7 cohorts). Certainty was very low for ovarian loss and imaging findings and low for recurrence and malignancy. Conclusions: Reported oophorectomy rates in prepubertal-predominant cohorts vary widely and often exceed the low prevalence of diagnosed malignancy, but these data cannot establish how many removals were avoidable. The findings support alignment with existing ovarian-conservation guidance and better reporting of menarchal status, indications for removal and functional follow-up.

articles.title: Predictors of Blood Transfusion Following Cesarean Delivery in Resource-Constrained Settings: The Impact of Out-of-Hours Surgery.
articles.authors: Muresan C, Biriș M, Roșca R et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Perioperative red blood cell (RBC) transfusion after cesarean delivery reflects both obstetric hemorrhagic risk and the capacity of the care environment. We evaluated whether out-of-hours cesarean delivery was independently associated with transfusion in a Romanian tertiary maternity unit operating under constrained resources. Methods: We conducted a retrospective unmatched case-control study of cesarean deliveries performed from 2023 to 2025. All eligible transfused women were included as cases; two non-transfused controls per case were randomly selected within each calendar year. Eligibility required preoperative hemoglobin ≥ 10 g/dL and normal coagulation. The primary exposure was out-of-hours surgery, and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal, obstetric, placental, and hematological factors. Results: The source population contained 6773 cesarean deliveries, with 608 transfusions (9.0%). The analytical sample comprised 401 cases and 802 controls. Out-of-hours procedures occurred in 64.1% of cases and 52.5% of controls (crude OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.26-2.07). After adjustment, out-of-hours delivery remained associated with transfusion (aOR 2.03, 95% CI 1.45-2.84). Placenta previa, suspected placenta accreta spectrum, and lower preoperative hemoglobin were the strongest clinical predictors. When postoperative/pre-transfusion hemoglobin was added, the out-of-hours association attenuated to an aOR of 1.02 (95% CI 0.63-1.65); sensitivity analyses remained consistent with the primary model. Conclusions: Out-of-hours cesarean delivery was associated with approximately two-fold higher transfusion odds after adjustment for the measured clinical factors. Because cesarean indication, urgency, and labor characteristics were not available, this association may partly reflect the different case mix and acuity of out-of-hours surgery rather than the working period itself. Attenuation after adjustment for post-exposure hemoglobin is compatible with, but does not establish greater perioperative blood loss. In high-cesarean, resource-constrained settings, standardized hemorrhage-risk identification and equivalent preparedness across duty periods warrant prospective evaluation in studies that also record indication and urgency.

articles.title: The Effect of Vitamins During Pregnancy on Pregnancy and Assisted Reproduction Outcomes: An Umbrella Review.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Liu H, Qin L et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Vitamin deficiency is associated with multiple adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Objective: To summarize systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and to evaluate the impact of vitamin deficiency and vitamin supplementation during pregnancy on maternal and fetal outcomes, including outcomes of assisted reproductive technology (ART). Methods: Prior to conducting this umbrella review, we registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251026875). We searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library for all systematic reviews and meta-analyses concerning vitamin status assessment and supplementation during pregnancy up to April 2025, and extracted all relevant pregnancy outcomes associated with prenatal vitamins. Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment (AMSTAR 2) were completed by two independent reviewers. Data were quantitatively synthesized, and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were mainly reported. Results: A total of 33 eligible systematic reviews and meta-analyses covering 679 primary studies were included, which explored 29 maternal-fetal outcomes related to six vitamins from the perspectives of vitamin insufficiency/deficiency and supplementation. Vitamin B12, folate, vitamin C and D deficiencies were linked to higher risks of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), pre-eclampsia, low birth weight, recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA), preterm birth and other adverse outcomes. Low vitamin D also correlated with poorer assisted reproductive outcomes including reduced clinical pregnancy and live birth rates. Appropriate supplementation of folate, vitamin C and D may lower the risks of megaloblastic anemia, premature rupture of membranes, GDM and stillbirth, and improved neonatal growth. Vitamin A exerted no notable influence on pregnancy outcomes. Conclusions: Insufficiency or deficiency in vitamin B12, folic acid, vitamin C, and vitamin D is more likely to result in adverse pregnancy outcomes. Supplementation with folic acid, vitamin C and vitamin D during pregnancy can improve the incidence of maternal and fetal outcomes to some extent.

articles.title: Clinical and Functional Outcomes of Contemporary Salvage Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy for Failed Primary Therapy: A Single Institution Review.
articles.authors: Ye E, Bissette RG, Vassallo M et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Salvage radical prostatectomy (SRP) is a potentially curative option for recurrent localized prostate cancer after primary radiation or focal therapy, historically limited by technical complexity and poor functional outcomes. This study characterizes contemporary perioperative, oncologic, and functional outcomes of salvage robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (sRARP) at a single institution over two decades. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing SRP from 01/01/2004 to 06/30/2026, identified via institutional database queries and natural language processing keyword searches with chart confirmation; analysis was restricted to the robotic-assisted subset. Complications within 90 days were graded by the Clavien-Dindo classification. Biochemical recurrence-free survival (bRFS) required freedom from PSA persistence and recurrence (PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL, with biochemical recurrence documented in the medical record) and is reported as a proportion. Results: Of 4002 records identified, 30 patients met inclusion criteria; 24 (80%) underwent sRARP. Extraprostatic disease was present in 54% (13/24) and positive margins in 43% (10/23). Within 90 days, 43% (10/23) had a complication (13% grade ≥ III); 30% (7/23) had a later complication, and 4% (1/24) required later urinary diversion. At a median follow-up of 32.1 months, bRFS was 39% (9/23), and 33% (8/24) had PSA persistence. Incontinence rose from 18% (3/17) at diagnosis to 87% (20/23) post-SRP; at longer-term follow-up (27.3 months), 79% (11/14) used ≥1 pad/day. Erectile dysfunction was present in 82% (14/17) at 22.0 months. Additional cancer-directed therapy was given in 50% (12/24). Conclusions: In this small, descriptive series, sRARP was feasible, but only 39% of patients were free of biochemical recurrence and functional burden was substantial. sRARP may represent a treatment option for carefully selected patients with recurrent localized prostate cancer; however, individualized counseling and further multicenter evaluation are essential.

articles.title: Adjunctive Autonomic Regulation Practices in Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Ersoy Ö, Akçay M, Pekmez YT et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pelvic floor physiotherapy (PFPT) and biofeedback are established conservative treatments for pelvic floor dysfunctions, but clinical response is heterogeneous. We explored whether exposure to a structured multicomponent set of non-device home practices, described here as adjunctive autonomic regulation practices, was associated with patient-reported improvement when used alongside standard PFPT/biofeedback. The study was exploratory and was not designed to establish an autonomic mechanism or causal treatment effect. Methods: This retrospective, observational, nonconcurrent comparative cohort study included adults treated in the same tertiary pelvic floor rehabilitation unit during two distinct periods. The adjunct-exposed cohort (Group A; September 2022-March 2023) received PFPT/biofeedback plus a structured multicomponent home program; the historical comparator (Group B; January-June 2019) received PFPT/biofeedback without the adjunct. Both programs included diaphragmatic breathing; in the standard program, no fixed breathing rate or duration was prescribed, whereas the adjunct included slow-paced breathing at approximately 6 breaths/min for 5 min three times daily. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients classified as responders according to improvement in the MYMOP2 Profile Score from baseline to approximately 2 months. The historical dataset operationalized clinically meaningful response as >1.0-point improvement. Between-group analyses were unadjusted. Results: A total of 111 patients were analyzed (Group A, n = 35; Group B, n = 76). MYMOP2 response occurred in 31/35 patients (88.6%) in Group A and 42/76 patients (55.3%) in Group B (Pearson chi-square: chi2(1) = 11.81, p < 0.001). The unadjusted risk ratio (RR) was 1.60 (95% CI 1.27-2.03), and the unadjusted absolute difference was 33.3 percentage points (95% CI 17.9-48.7). Using recently proposed physiotherapy-specific RR reference thresholds at a baseline risk near 0.5, the numerical RR lies in the upper medium range and close to the proposed large-effect threshold; this describes magnitude only and does not imply a causal treatment effect. Conclusions: Patients exposed to the adjunctive multicomponent program had a higher unadjusted MYMOP2 responder rate than patients in a nonconcurrent historical standard-rehabilitation cohort. Because the cohorts were separated in time, baseline characterization was incomplete, follow-up availability may have introduced…

articles.title: A Cross-Sectional Study Investigating Urinary Levels of Nerve Growth Factor and Its Precursor in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.authors: Nociti V, Bientinesi R, Cicia A et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: As multiple sclerosis (MS) progresses, most patients develop lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) indicative of an overactive bladder (OAB), primarily due to neurogenic detrusor overactivity, which is the most common abnormality identified during urodynamic testing. Therefore, biomarkers for OAB would be valuable additions to diagnostic tools. This study aimed to compare urinary levels of nerve growth factor (NGF) and its precursor, pro-NGF, in MS patients with and without OAB. Methods: We enrolled patients with relapsing MS (RMS), some exhibiting LUTS suggestive of OAB, along with healthy controls (HCs). Urine samples were collected, and NGF and pro-NGF levels were measured using ELISA kits. Results: Neither an ELISA kit specific for NGF nor a kit recognizing both NGF and pro-NGF detected measurable levels of these proteins. However, an ELISA kit selective for pro-NGF detected similarly low concentrations of this protein in a few samples from each group. Conclusions: Our ELISA results, measuring urinary NGF and pro-NGF levels in MS patients and HCs, are consistent with other studies that failed to detect these proteins in the urine of patients with OAB of various etiologies or in HCs. It is possible that urinary levels of NGF and pro-NGF are so low that the detection limits of ELISA kits and other available immunoassays are insufficient for their reliable measurement.

articles.title: Advances in Intrauterine Contraception and Therapeutic Intrauterine Devices, 2016-2026: A Targeted Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Biriș M, Buciu VB, Cîtu IM et al.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine contraception has changed over the past decade through longer validated duration, lower-dose hormonal devices, redesigned copper devices, new indications, and better safety surveillance. This targeted scoping review (OSF registration 10.17605/OSF.IO/3GUQF) mapped English-language primary human studies published from 1 January 2016 to 5 September 2026 in journals indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE). A reproducible search targeted to the major device programs, randomized trials, and large surveillance cohorts identified 766 PubMed/MEDLINE records, with no additional unique records from Scopus or Web of Science; of the 624 unique records screened, 123 reports were assessed, and 114, from 66 distinct trials, cohorts, or data sources, were included and appraised with design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools. Two single-arm programs and a 7-year randomized trial supported the efficacy of 52 mg levonorgestrel intrauterine devices (LNG-IUDs) through 8 years. Lower-dose LNG-IUDs eased placement but were associated with higher ectopic pregnancy rates in four Scandinavian analyses and with less antidepressant use than the 52 mg device. Smaller or size-matched copper devices improved continuation and reduced expulsion in randomized comparisons, whereas a low-copper nitinol device had a higher 5-year pregnancy rate than expected with TCu380A. Perforation was uncommon but more frequent after postpartum insertion and during breastfeeding; immediate postpartum insertion carried the highest expulsion risk. One randomized trial and its secondary analyses supported the 52 mg LNG-IUD for emergency contraception. Therapeutic evidence was strongest for heavy menstrual bleeding and endometrial hyperplasia, whereas intrauterine ball and precious metal designs showed no consistent benefit. Progress refined rather than replaced the T-shaped IUD.

articles.title: Associations Between Masseter Muscles Tension, Postural Pattern, Pelvic Type and Postural Stability in Women with Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
articles.authors: Wójcik M, Góral K, Małysz J et al.
articles.abstract: Background: This study aimed to examine the associations of pelvic type and body posture pattern with masseter muscle measurements and postural stability parameters in women with POP, and to assess the relationship between masseter muscle measurements and postural stability under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Methods: This observational study included 61 women: 31 with advanced POP (grade 3-4 according to the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification system [POP-Q]) and 30 healthy controls. Masseter muscle measurements, postural stability parameters (center-of-pressure sway and surface area), body posture pattern, and pelvic type were assessed. Postural stability was measured with eyes open and closed. Two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Tukey's post-hoc test, and Pearson's correlation coefficient were used for statistical analysis. Results: Pelvic type was not significantly associated with any of the analyzed parameters. Body posture pattern was associated with significant differences in most postural stability parameters (p < 0.05) under both visual conditions, with the highest values observed in women with a posterior posture pattern. Conclusions: In women with advanced POP, body posture pattern was associated with differences in postural stability parameters, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed for pelvic type. No statistically significant correlations were detected between masseter muscle measurements and postural stability. These findings should be interpreted cautiously, given the observational study design, and do not establish causal relationships.

articles.title: Carrier Screening and Potential-Difference Response of a Piezomagnetic-Piezoelectric Semiconductor PN-Junction Sandwich Fiber Under a Local Magnetic Field.
articles.authors: Liu C, Zhou W, Ma Y et al.
articles.abstract: Carrier screening and observation geometry determine how a local magnetoelectric response contributes to a potential-difference readout. This study develops a finite-length one-dimensional analytical model for a weak PN-junction piezoelectric-semiconductor fiber between magnetostrictive layers subjected to a localized magnetic-field increment about a prescribed bias. Cross-sectional force balance, two-carrier drift-diffusion, blocking end conditions, and interface continuity yield a four-region solution that separates the junction reference from the magnetic increment. In the representative weak-junction case, the end-to-end difference is about 1% of the peak local magnetically induced potential, whereas observation pairs at the field-region edges and near the junction give differences about 200 and 50 times larger than the end-to-end value. For equal screening and a step field, the response of a fixed interior pair peaks when the field-region edges reach the observation points. Uniformly doped and symmetric weak-junction controls have identical magnetic increments under equal screening despite their different reference fields. Layer thickness modifies both magnetic conversion and carrier screening. The resulting continuum-model relations identify how excitation width, screening length, and observation position jointly govern internal magnetic-field readout.

articles.title: Obesity and Diabetes in Pregnancy and Maternal and Child Health: The Gerar Cohort Profile, Brazil.
articles.authors: Oliveira MP, Stork SS, Piovezan AP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-pregnancy obesity and GDM increase maternal-fetal oxidative stress, but their consequences for women's health and child development are still unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This paper describes the methodological design, recruitment strategy, data collection methods, and baseline characteristics of the Gerar Cohort, a prospective longitudinal study designed to investigate the relationship between pre-pregnancy obesity and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with oxidative stress biomarkers and their effects on maternal and child health outcomes through 12 months postpartum.
METHODS: Women were recruited early in their prenatal care in a city in Southern Brazil. Sociodemographic and clinical data, as well as blood samples, were collected each trimester. At childbirth, umbilical cord blood and placental tissue were collected. Children were followed up until 12 months of age, with blood collection at 4 and 12 months. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee.
RESULTS: A total of 189 women were recruited in the first trimester; 136 were followed up until the third trimester; 23 pregnancy losses were recorded. Pre-gestational obesity was observed in 24.3% (95% CI 18.4-31.1), and 27% (95% CI 20.8-33.9) of women were diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus. Fifty-nine umbilical cord blood samples and 61 placental fragments were collected. In the children's follow-up, 71 children were taken for ophthalmological examination at 1 month of age; 60 attended the pediatric consultation at 4 months; 56 children attended the neurological evaluation at 6 months and 50 at 12 months.
CONCLUSIONS: The Gerar Cohort successfully implemented its recruitment and biospecimen collection procedures within public healthcare services.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gynecology and Obstetrics: Medico-Legal, Ethical, and Governance Challenges-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Santangelo G, De Angelis G, Muzii L et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering gynecologic and obstetric imaging, risk prediction, decision support, robotic surgery, remote monitoring, and patient communication. An estimated 260,000 maternal deaths occurred worldwide in 2023, and in England obstetric claims account for 11% of clinical negligence claims but 55% of their value. AI errors, bias, or opacity in this specialty therefore carry major clinical and legal consequences. Objective: To synthesize the principal medico-legal and bioethical challenges associated with AI in gynecology and obstetrics and to propose a lifecycle governance framework for responsible clinical adoption. Methods: A narrative review with thematic synthesis was conducted. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for records published from January 2020 to August 2026, supplemented by citation chaining and official legal databases. Two reviewers screened 131 records against predefined eligibility criteria; 41 sources (36 publications and 5 legal instruments) were included and analyzed thematically. Selection is reported in a PRISMA-style flow diagram. Results: Six connected risk domains were derived from five prespecified themes, namely validation and generalizability; professional competence and automation bias; distributed liability and evidentiary opacity; informed consent and patient autonomy; privacy and cybersecurity of reproductive data; and discrimination, access, and reproductive justice. Generative AI adds risks of hallucination, non-reproducibility, persuasive framing, and undocumented use. Existing law does not eliminate clinician responsibility: accountability is shared across developers, institutions, and professionals, but clinical judgment and documented oversight remain central. In the European Union, Medical Device Regulation and GDPR obligations already apply, whereas AI Act requirements for AI-enabled medical devices apply from August 2028 and the revised Product Liability Directive covers products placed on the market after 9 December 2026; causation and professional fault remain governed by national law. Conclusions: Safe adoption requires more than technical accuracy. We translate the findings into seven actionable institutional requirements, namely accountable ownership, minimum local validation, role-specific training, auditable documentation, equity monitoring, post-deployment surveillance, and incident reporting. AI should augment-not displace-clinically accountable and…

articles.title: A Protocol for Evaluating the Effectiveness of an Integrated Group Postpartum and Well-Child Care Model on Maternal and Child Health Outcomes.
articles.authors: Gresh A, Kapito E, Mambulasa J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The building and then testing of high-quality maternal and infant health care service delivery models are urgently needed to address the persistent maternal and infant health disparities globally. A range of health system and social drivers contribute to maternal and infant morbidities and mortality, including limited access to care and preventive services and variation in care quality. These poor outcomes have led to calls for a broader redesign of maternal and infant health services and delivery systems. One promising model is group care, which has shown potential for maternal and child health care redesign, but has been studied mainly during the antenatal period. This paper describes the study protocol our team will use to evaluate the effectiveness of group postpartum and well-child care.
METHODS: We will conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial with mixed methods across 16 clinics in Zomba District, Malawi to test the model's impact on select maternal and infant health outcomes. We hypothesize that compared to usual care, women in the intervention group will have decreased postpartum depression symptoms, anemia, and hypertension and infants will have increased vaccination rates and more optimal secondary outcomes for the dyad, such as uptake of family planning, exclusive breastfeeding, childhood development (gross and fine motor skills, social-adaptive development, and nutrition). We will also qualitatively explore clinic- and patient-level implementation facilitators and barriers for group care and the health and social needs that arise in the 12 months after birth for both women and their infants in both arms.
DISCUSSION: This study will be the first to conduct an adequately powered trial of a group postpartum and well-child care model in a low-resource setting. Findings from the study will contribute important evidence on how postpartum and well-child care may be improved during the first year after birth.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov registration number: NCT07414901.

articles.title: Congenital Syphilis in South Africa: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Health System Drivers, Prevention, and the Path to Elimination.
articles.authors: Phiri S, Skepu A, Nxumalo Z et al.
articles.abstract: Congenital syphilis (CS), caused by vertical transmission of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum, remains a major but preventable cause of foetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality globally. Despite established antenatal screening programmes and the availability of effective treatment with benzathine penicillin G (BPG), South Africa continues to experience a substantial burden of maternal and congenital syphilis, with a 2023 national case rate approximately four times the World Health Organization (WHO) elimination target. This narrative review synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed publications, national surveillance reports, and policy documents identified through systematic searches conducted up to September 2026 [searched through August 2026] on congenital syphilis in South Africa. It addresses the microbiology and pathogenesis, epidemiology, clinical burden, diagnostic approaches, health system determinants, and strategies for elimination. Persistent transmission is associated with documented gaps in antenatal booking, repeat screening, treatment completion and partner management, and with recurrent benzathine penicillin shortages; HIV co-infection, poverty and other social and structural factors are likely contributors, but direct evidence for them is more limited. Congenital syphilis remains associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including miscarriage, stillbirth, prematurity, neonatal mortality, and long-term disability. The elimination of congenital syphilis in South Africa requires strengthening antenatal care coverage, universal and repeat syphilis screening, prompt and complete maternal treatment, partner services, enhanced surveillance systems, and closer integration with HIV programmes. Progress towards the country's 2028 elimination target will depend on a coordinated health systems approach aligned with WHO triple-elimination validation criteria.

articles.title: Correlation Between Clinicopathological Findings, Cervical Smear, and HPV Results: A Retrospective Study of Women Referred for Colposcopy.
articles.authors: Kökbudak N, Solmaz M, Kılınç F et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the association of cervical cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, and colposcopic findings with histopathological outcomes in women referred for colposcopy. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 756 women who underwent colposcopy with cervical biopsy at a tertiary center between January 2022 and June 2025 and had HPV genotyping and conventional cytology results. The primary endpoint was cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) on biopsy; the highest grade across biopsy and conization specimens and CIN3+ were secondary endpoints. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and diagnostic accuracy was reported according to STARD 2015. Results: CIN2+ was found in 85 women (11.2%). HPV-16 positivity (OR: 2.87; 95% CI: 1.72-4.77), epithelial cell abnormality on cytology (OR: 4.28; 95% CI: 2.05-8.92), and positive colposcopy (OR: 3.39; 95% CI: 2.00-5.73) were independently associated with higher odds of CIN2+. Adding colposcopy to a pre-colposcopy model increased the AUC from 0.730 to 0.770 (p = 0.034; optimism-corrected 0.753). Colposcopy had a sensitivity of 71.8% (95% CI: 61.4-80.2%) and an NPV of 94.6% (95% CI: 92.1-96.3%), but 24 of 85 CIN2+ cases (28.2%) had a negative colposcopic impression; results were similar for the highest-grade endpoint (92 CIN2+ cases). Conclusions: In this referral population, HPV-16, cytological abnormality, and colposcopic impression provided complementary information on the odds of CIN2+. Because more than one-quarter of CIN2+ cases were not colposcopically apparent, a negative colposcopy should not be considered sufficient to exclude high-grade disease, particularly in women with HPV-16 positivity or abnormal cytology. Prospective validation is required before these associations are used for triage.

articles.title: Legionella Pneumonia in the Molecular Diagnostics Era: From Intracellular Pathogenesis to Precision Management.
articles.authors: Liu L, Zhang B, Sang K et al.
articles.abstract: Legionella pneumophila is a major cause of severe community-acquired pneumonia and one of the most lethal respiratory pathogens. Nevertheless, it remains substantially underdiagnosed because conventional diagnostic assays are slow, insensitive, or limited to specific serogroups. In this narrative review, we integrate fragmented literature regarding Legionella pneumonia, covering its intracellular pathogenesis, clinical spectrum and patient management. Evidence was identified through a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC (23 September 2026) and prioritized by design, with primary clinical and mechanistic studies and systematic reviews taking precedence over narrative summaries and with society guidelines used to anchor management recommendations. We argue that this field is undergoing a diagnostic paradigm shift fueled by culture-independent molecular assays. We first review the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system and intracellular lifecycle that allow Legionella to replicate within macrophages while evading host innate immunity. We then summarize the full clinical spectrum, ranging from self-limited Pontiac fever to fatal Legionnaires' disease complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome, as well as epidemiological characteristics including waterborne transmission and outbreak risks. The core of this review examines how metagenomic next-generation sequencing, targeted NGS, plasma microbial cell-free DNA and syndromic multiplex PCR are reshaping diagnostic workflows, and compares the strengths and limitations of these novel tools with urinary antigen testing and bacterial culture. Pooled estimates place the sensitivity of urinary antigen testing at 0.79 overall and 0.86 for serogroup 1, and that of respiratory PCR at 97.4%, with specificities of 1.00 and 0.99, respectively. We further evaluate contemporary therapeutic evidence, including fluoroquinolone versus macrolide monotherapy, combination regimens, and adjunctive corticosteroid therapy. Throughout this review, we highlight that Legionella is a pathogen whose clinical presentation, diagnostic yield and prognosis are highly dependent on host immune status, exposure setting and appropriate diagnostic stewardship. We conclude by identifying critical knowledge gaps and outlining a framework for diagnosis-driven precision antimicrobial management of this underrecognized pathogen. That framework is an evidence-informed synthesis rather than a validated pathway: no prospective study has yet…

articles.title: DBS Direct Elution and Multiplex Digital PCR for SMN1 and SMN2 Copy-Number and CFTR Variant Detection: Development and Validation of a Molecular Screening Workflow.
articles.authors: Dikoglou-Tzanetatou E, Skopa I, Poulou M et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Scalable molecular workflows may facilitate carrier screening for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and cystic fibrosis (CF). This study aimed to develop and validate a dried blood spot (DBS)-based multiplex digital PCR (dPCR) workflow for SMN1 and SMN2 copy-number analysis and targeted detection of CFTR p.Phe508del. Methods: The workflow combined direct DNA elution with multiplex dPCR. Analytical validation used 50 previously characterized samples, with multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) and Sanger sequencing as reference methods. The workflow was subsequently applied to 1670 women from Crete and Ikaria, Greece, followed by targeted testing of 10 partners. Results: All 50 directly eluted samples amplified successfully. dPCR showed complete agreement with reference methods. Repeatability coefficients of variation were below 5%. Copy-number classification performance estimates are apparent, as thresholds were derived and evaluated in the same small validation cohort. Among 1670 women screened, 34 (2.04%) were identified as SMN1 carriers and 20 (1.20%) as CFTR p.Phe508del carriers. Partner testing identified two carrier couples. Conclusions: The DBS-based multiplex dPCR workflow demonstrated complete analytical concordance with reference methods in this preliminary validation and was implemented in a population screening cohort. Its targeted scope leaves residual carrier risk, requiring appropriate counseling. Larger independent validation and formal throughput and cost assessments are needed before routine implementation.

articles.title: Persistent High-Risk HPV Positivity Without Confirmed CIN2+: Diagnostic Uncertainty, Risk Stratification, and Management-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Gavril ST, Matasariu DR, Scripcariu IS et al.
articles.abstract: Primary high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing detects cervical precancer earlier than cytology and, by design, generates a large population of virus-positive women in whom high-grade disease is not confirmed. Where the infection persists, the clinician must judge whether a negative or non-diagnostic assessment reflects absence of disease or failure of detection. This review asks what that state represents, which tools reclassify absolute CIN3+ risk, and how surveillance and intervention should be balanced. This narrative review synthesises relevant evidence from published studies and international guidance on persistent hrHPV infection, diagnostic assessment, risk stratification and management, with reporting guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). Persistent hrHPV positivity without confirmed CIN2+ is a heterogeneous risk state, not a diagnosis, and covers three clinical situations that should not be conflated. Absolute CIN3+ risk is set principally by genotype and by the duration of type-specific persistence; genotype alone spans an approximately twenty-fold range of immediate risk in hrHPV-positive screening populations. Pooled colposcopic sensitivity for CIN2+ was approximately 75% in heterogeneous referral populations, while one selected retrospective series of cytology-negative hrHPV-positive women reported sensitivity near 50%. Selected referral cohorts have reported CIN2+/HSIL detection yields of approximately 8% to 14% among persistently hrHPV-positive women with normal cytology; these composite, selection-dependent estimates should not be read as the prevalence of occult CIN3+. Extended genotyping and p16/Ki-67 dual-stain cytology carry guideline-adopted management rules, although validation specifically after documented persistence remains limited. Controlled evidence for treating persistent hrHPV without confirmed CIN2+ is sparse and conflicting.
