Recent randomised trials of vaginal interventions report discordant short-term virological results, and none establishes durable clearance or a reduction in CIN3+ risk. Short-term loss of HPV detectability is not equivalent to prevention of precancer, and management should remain risk-based.

articles.title: Incidence, Prognosis, and Management of Occult Endometrial Carcinoma After Hysterectomy for Benign Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Chen YH, Ding DC
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Occult endometrial carcinoma, incidentally diagnosed after hysterectomy for presumed benign disease, raises concerns regarding its incidence, the prognostic effects of minimally invasive surgery and morcellation, and subsequent management. This systematic review synthesized the available evidence and performed meta-analysis where appropriate. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register were searched using a sensitivity-tested strategy. After de-duplication and screening, 76 studies met the eligibility criteria. Incidence was pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis of proportions with the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation. Subgroup analyses examined surgical contexts, including hysterectomy for benign disease, morcellation-specific cohorts, and pelvic organ prolapse surgery. Survival and management outcomes were synthesized narratively. Results: Among 68 studies with extractable denominators, the pooled incidence (proportion of hysterectomies with carcinoma on final pathology) of occult endometrial carcinoma following hysterectomy for benign disease was 0.33% (95% prediction interval, 0.04-0.87%). Incidence was lowest in selected morcellation cohorts (0.22%) and higher in unselected benign hysterectomy cohorts (0.33%) and prolapse populations (0.43%; test for subgroup differences, p = 0.03), with substantially higher rates among older patients. The pooled incidence of occult uterine malignancies, including sarcoma, was 0.54%. For endometrial carcinoma specifically, the limited observational evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between power morcellation or laparoscopic surgery and poorer survival, although confidence intervals were wide. However, morcellation was associated with increased mortality among patients with uterine sarcoma. Occult endometrial carcinomas were predominantly early-stage and low-grade, with 81.8% classified as International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics IA, and approximately 91% achieving 5-year overall survival. In a small series of selected high-risk patients, completion staging resulted in upstaging in 25% and informed adjuvant treatment decisions. Limited observational data did not demonstrate a statistically significant survival benefit of complementary lymphadenectomy, although estimates were imprecise. Conclusions: Occult endometrial carcinoma occurs in approximately 0.2-0.4% of hysterectomies performed for benign disease, with a…

articles.title: Maternal FNDC5 and ADIPOQ Genetic Variants as Potential Modulators of Susceptibility to Spontaneous Preterm Birth.
articles.authors: Kadivnik M, Zlatunić P, Drinić M et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) is a complex and heterogeneous pregnancy outcome in which maternal metabolic and endocrine pathways may contribute to susceptibility to preterm delivery. This study investigated whether two maternal genetic variants involved in metabolic signaling, ADIPOQ rs266729 and FNDC5 rs1746661, are associated with preterm birth (PTB) in a Croatian population. This case-control study included 401 women: 200 with PTB and 201 with term delivery. Maternal genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral blood, and both variants were genotyped using TaqMan-based real-time PCR. Genotype and allele distributions, inheritance models, allelic combinations, logistic regression, and gene-gene interaction were analyzed. Neither variant was significantly associated with overall PTB, and no significant gene-gene interaction was observed (p = 0.18). In early PTB, only a borderline, non-significant tendency toward a higher ADIPOQ rs266729 G allele frequency was found (39% vs. 27%; OR 1.74, 95% CI 0.99-3.04; p = 0.05), which was not supported by genotype, inheritance-model, or regression analyses. The G-T allelic combination was more frequent in early PTB (13.6% vs. 4.6%; p = 0.03) but not after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted p = 0.09). No significant association between the investigated variants and PTB was demonstrated. The borderline findings in early PTB are hypothesis-generating and require replication in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Angiotensin II-Induced Cardiac Fibrosis: Genomic and Molecular Drivers, Emerging Biomarkers and Therapeutic Perspectives.
articles.authors: Martínez-Rodríguez NL, Campos-González JA, López-Camarillo C et al.
articles.abstract: Chronically elevated angiotensin II (Ang II) drives adverse cardiac remodelling, converting a reparative response into progressive interstitial and perivascular fibrosis that stiffens the ventricle and precedes overt heart failure. Acting through the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, Ang II generates reactive oxygen species, recruits and polarises immune cells and activates resident fibroblasts, converging on transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-dependent and mechanotransductive programmes that drive myofibroblast differentiation and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. The magnitude of this response varies between patients: germline variation in renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) genes, loci for heart failure and imaging-defined fibrosis, epigenomic reprogramming of the fibroblast, non-coding RNA networks and metabolic rewiring of collagen-producing cells all modulate the transition from compensated hypertrophy to fibrotic failure. This review integrates these genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic layers with the signalling architecture of Ang II-induced fibrosis, and reviews the circulating biomarkers-collagen turnover peptides, matricellular and immune mediators, non-coding RNAs and cell-free DNA methylation signatures-that could detect fibrotic activity before remodelling becomes irreversible. We then consider why fibrosis regression under RAAS blockade appears heterogeneous, which emerging targets are mechanistically credible, and how genotype-biomarker-imaging phenotyping could enrich antifibrotic trials. Priorities for ancestrally diverse cohorts and standardised biomarker methodology are identified.

articles.title: Pregnancy as a Stress Test for β-Cell Autoimmunity: The Autoimmune Phenotype of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Yanachkova V, Shivarov V, Kostadinov N et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous metabolic disorder comprising pathophysiological phenotypes that differ in their underlying mechanisms, clinical presentation and long-term outcomes. While pregnancy-induced insulin resistance remains the predominant pathogenic mechanism, a subset of women develops hyperglycemia largely because of reduced pancreatic β-cell reserve accompanied by islet autoimmunity. This autoimmune phenotype links gestational diabetes with autoimmune diabetes, but its boundaries and clinical significance remain incompletely defined. We aimed to review current knowledge of the autoimmune phenotype of GDM, with focus on immune pathophysiological mechanisms, biomarkers, clinical characteristics and implications for precision medicine, and to distinguish findings demonstrated directly in GDM from mechanisms extrapolated from type 1 diabetes (T1D). This narrative review was based on a structured PubMed/MEDLINE search from database inception through the end of October 2026, supplemented by targeted searches, manual screening of reference lists, and relevant clinical guidelines and consensus documents. Evidence obtained directly in women with GDM was considered alongside selected mechanistic literature from T1D and adult autoimmune diabetes. In some women with GDM, islet autoantibodies are associated with impaired β-cell function and an increased risk of autoimmune diabetes after delivery. The cellular mechanisms underlying these associations remain insufficiently studied in GDM. Pregnancy may act as a physiological metabolic stress test that exposes previously compensated β-cell dysfunction associated with islet autoimmunity, although its influence on the underlying autoimmune process remains uncertain. Islet autoantibodies are enriched among women with GDM, but their frequency varies widely between populations and assays and is lower after delivery than during pregnancy. The number and persistence of antibodies, particularly when combined with reduced endogenous insulin secretion, carry considerably more prognostic weight than a single positive result. Cellular immune mechanisms are well characterized in T1D but remain largely unvalidated in GDM. Recognition of the autoimmune phenotype extends the concept of GDM beyond a purely glucose-based classification. It is best viewed as a spectrum ranging from isolated seropositivity to pregnancy-unmasked autoimmune diabetes rather than as a uniform…

articles.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis of Rat Urethral Tissue Following Simulated Childbirth Injury and Microenergy Acoustic Pulse Therapy.
articles.authors: Lin G, Zhao L, Xing E et al.
articles.abstract: Microenergy acoustic pulse (MAP) therapy has been associated with functional and structural improvement after childbirth-related urethral injury, but its multicellular effects remain incompletely defined. We explored treatment- and injury-associated differences in the urethral microenvironment using single-cell RNA sequencing. Eight female Sprague-Dawley rats were assigned to sham, vaginal balloon dilation plus ovariectomy (VBDO), VBDO plus beta-aminopropionitrile (BAPN), or VBDO plus BAPN and MAP (MAP) groups, with one 24-week-old and one 48-week-old rat per group. Urethral tissues were analyzed for cell composition, differential gene expression, Gene Ontology enrichment, stem/progenitor features, senescence-associated secretory phenotype activity, and CellChat-inferred intercellular communication. A balanced single-cell dataset comprising 23,128 cells was used for downstream comparative analyses and resolved 19 annotated cell-type/state categories. Across the injury- and age-associated experimental conditions, epithelial, vascular, stromal, immune, and muscle compartments showed distinct transcriptional patterns, whereas MAP-treated samples showed a distinct cellular distribution; a separate histological cohort showed higher urethral muscle content. MAP-treated samples also showed differences in CellChat-inferred signaling activity in selected extracellular-matrix, adhesion, vascular, developmental, and neural/neuromuscular pathways, including fibronectin 1 (FN1), collagen (COLLAGEN), angiopoietin (ANGPT), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), Wingless/Integrated (WNT), Notch (NOTCH), reelin (RELN), Slit guidance ligand (SLIT), neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM), and neurexin (NRXN). Exploratory enrichment analysis identified treatment-associated differences in translation, oxidative metabolism, stress adaptation, synaptic-organization processes, progenitor-associated transcriptional states, and senescence-related programs. The treatment-split marker manifold approximation and projection (UMAPs) are descriptive and do not provide evidence of increased muscle-cell number; the reported difference in muscle-associated staining content derives from a separate animal-level histological analysis. Overall, the findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require validation in independently replicated cohorts.

articles.title: Adenomyosis and Its Impact on Reproduction, Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Newborn.
articles.authors: Signorile PG
articles.abstract: This narrative review covers the diagnosis of adenomyosis; its impact on fertility, assisted reproduction, pregnancy, childbirth, and the newborn; and its uterus-sparing management. Diagnosis is delayed by about 11 years, and no classification is universally accepted. After in vitro fertilization, adenomyosis lowers clinical pregnancy and live birth rates and doubles miscarriage risk. Because oocyte number and morphology are preserved and miscarriage remains increased with donor oocytes and euploid embryos, the deficit appears mainly uterine; however, age and coexistent endometriosis contribute. In pregnancy, it is associated with preeclampsia, preterm birth, placental malposition and placenta accreta spectrum, cesarean delivery, and postpartum hemorrhage, and newborns are more often small for gestational age, of low birth weight, and extremely preterm. The evidence is observational and of low to very low certainty, and defective remodeling of the junctional zone spiral arteries remains a hypothetical unifying mechanism. In selected observational cohorts, pregnancy was reported in approximately half of infertile women after uterus-sparing surgery, which has not been compared with medical treatment or assisted reproduction in randomized trials and carries a risk of uterine rupture. Management rests on individualized counseling; proposed preventive measures, including low-dose aspirin and correction of vitamin D or folate deficiency, remain untested in adenomyosis.

articles.title: Serial Tumor-Agnostic Plasma Profiling with a Compact NGS Panel During First-Line Therapy for Newly Diagnosed Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.
articles.authors: Zakharova G, Zauzolkov O, Khristichenko A et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling may complement tissue hotspot testing and reveal molecular changes during treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). We prospectively studied 39 patients with newly diagnosed unresectable mCRC receiving first-line therapy. Cell-free DNA was collected before treatment and after two and four cycles and analyzed using a 10 kb, 10-gene hybrid-capture sequencing panel with molecular barcodes and error correction. Baseline oncogenic variants were detected in 32 of 35 evaluable patients (91.4%). Compared with routine tissue PCR for shared RAS/BRAF targets, plasma testing showed 84.2% sensitivity (16/19) and 100% specificity (19/19) in the intention-to-test cohort, compared with 88.2% sensitivity (15/17) and 100% specificity (17/17) among technically evaluable samples. Three activating KRAS variants (L19F, A59T, and A146T) lay outside the tissue assays' target regions; patients carrying these alterations received anti-EGFR therapy. Patients with metastases in two or more organs had more detectable oncogenic alterations than those with one metastatic site (median, three versus two; adjusted q = 0.00184; rank-biserial correlation = 0.687). Serial sampling revealed divergent trajectories of individual variants in nine patients. Early reductions in plasma variant allele frequencies tended to be greater among partial responders, although associations with radiological response were not significant after multiple testing correction. Compact tumor-agnostic plasma sequencing provides complementary molecular information, but its clinical utility requires further validation.

articles.title: Effect of the rs12249854 Polymorphism in the HECTD2 Gene and Selected Clinical Variables on the Response to Intradetrusor Injection of Botulinum Neurotoxin Type a in Female Patients with Overactive Bladder: A Single-Center Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Ciećwież SM, Lewandowska K, Boroń A et al.
articles.abstract: The HECTD2:rs12249854 polymorphism may be associated with a weaker response to an intradetrusor injection of botulinum neurotoxin type A (BoNT/A) in patients with overactive bladder (OAB). This prospective study analyzed the link between the HECTD2:rs12249854 polymorphism and the response to BoNT/A treatment in 156 OAB patients, based on changes in urodynamic parameters and ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-LUTS-QoL scores six months after the injection. BoNT/A treatment contributed to improvements in all parameters except the average flow rate. Wild-type homozygotes (TT, n = 137) differed from TA heterozygotes (n = 19) solely in terms of pretreatment ICIQ-OAB Part A and ICIQ-LUTS-QoL Part A scores, both of which were higher in the heterozygotes. Thus, the HECTD2:rs12249854 polymorphism does not appear to be associated with the response to BoNT/A treatment. Patients with neurogenic OAB (n = 60) had a higher pretreatment detrusor pressure at maximum flow than those with idiopathic OAB (n = 96), but this difference was no longer observed after BoNT/A treatment. Good responders to the BoNT/A injection (defined as at least 50% decrease in the ICIQ-LUTS-QoL Part A score, n = 50) had a higher body mass index and parity and a lower pretreatment maximum flow rate than poor responders (n = 106). Before formulating any definitive conclusions, the results of this exploratory study should be verified in an adequately powered multicenter cohort.

articles.title: Validation of Multi-Residue GC-MS/MS and LC-MS/MS Methods for the Analysis of Pesticide Residues in Botanicals.
articles.authors: Butovskaya E, Castrezzati G, Migliorato G et al.
articles.abstract: Botanical food supplements are increasingly consumed worldwide. As finished products, they may be contaminated with pesticide residues, which can potentially become concentrated relative to the raw botanical materials during processing steps. In this study, analytical methods were developed for the quantification of 252 pesticide residues in botanical food supplements using LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS, with both techniques employing a common sample preparation procedure. Sample extraction and clean-up were performed using a QuEChERS-based approach combined with dispersive solid-phase clean-up step using graphitized carbon black (GCB) and primary-secondary amine (PSA) sorbents followed by Oasis® WAX cartridge purification. Method validation was performed in accordance with the EU guidance document SANTE/11312/2021. The validated methods were subsequently applied to ten plant extract samples to assess their applicability to different botanical food supplement matrices. Multiple pesticide residues were detected in three samples, with concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 0.19 mg/kg. The application of the methods to real samples confirmed suitability for the analysis of diverse botanical matrices and underscored the need for robust analytical approaches to support the routine monitoring of pesticide residues in botanical food supplements and ensure consumer safety.

articles.title: Comparative Label-Free Proteomics of a High-Glucose Syncytialised Trophoblast Model Identifies Mitochondrial Fission Factor (MFF) as a Candidate Serum Biomarker Associated with Hyperglycaemic Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Sharma AK, Yalavarthi C, Savithri P et al.
articles.abstract: Placental protein markers of maternal hyperglycaemia in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) remain scarce. We aimed to find trophoblast proteins that change under high glucose and to test whether a lead candidate is also raised in maternal serum. In our established insulin-resistant model, we used label-free liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to compare BeWo cells syncytialised with forskolin/8-Br-cAMP in high-glucose (25 mM) medium, with or without vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), with undifferentiated control cells in normoglycaemic (5 mM) medium (n = 3 per group); glucose and differentiation therefore varied together. Of 3528 protein groups, 388 were differentially abundant (24 at Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05). Mitochondrial fission factor (MFF), the outer-membrane receptor for dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1), increased 4.5-fold (q = 0.040), whereas DRP1 was unchanged; mitochondrial calcium-uniporter components, pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 3 and glycogen synthase 1 also increased. VEGF did not alter this signature (MFF: 0.91-fold, p = 0.71). Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) confirmed higher MFF in high-glucose cell lysates (+48%) and, independently of in vitro differentiation, in gestational-day-7 serum of streptozotocin-treated hyperglycaemic pregnant rats (+41%; both p < 0.001; n = 3 per group), consistent with reported increases of MFF in GDM placentae. As serum was sampled after hyperglycaemia developed, these data show association, not prediction. MFF is a candidate serum biomarker of hyperglycaemic pregnancy; studies separating glucose from differentiation and validation in women are needed.

articles.title: LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Hepatic Metabolic Homeostasis: Cholesterol, Triglyceride, Glucose and Pathological Implications.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Liu T, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract: The liver coordinately maintains cholesterol, triglyceride, and glucose homeostasis by integrating the synthesis, storage, utilization, and inter-conversion of these metabolic programs, and their dysregulation contributes to metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are not translated into proteins, regulate gene expression through interactions with DNA, RNA, and proteins at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and epigenetic levels, and have emerged as central determinants of hepatic metabolic balance. This review systematically summarizes how lncRNAs govern cholesterol biosynthesis and efflux, triglyceride synthesis and lipolysis, glycogen turnover, gluconeogenesis, and glycolysis in hepatocytes. Unlike pathway-by-pathway descriptions, we highlight that these programs are coupled through shared signaling networks, including PI3K/AKT/mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), 5'-AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), SREBP, PPAR, and FoxO1, and that pleiotropic lncRNAs coordinate lipid and glucose outputs rather than controlling a single isolated process. We further examine how lncRNA dysregulation drives MASLD, HCC, T2DM, and GDM, and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Finally, we outline current limitations, including incomplete molecular characterization, low cross-species conservation, heterogeneous experimental validation, and unresolved delivery challenges, which must be addressed before lncRNA-based strategies reach clinical application.

articles.title: Prominent Hepatic Injury in 56-Week-Old Female Mice with Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Synthase (cGAS) Deficient.
articles.authors: Suksamai C, Bhunyakarnjanarat T, Dityen K et al.
articles.abstract: Current preclinical studies evaluating cGAS inhibition as a novel anti-inflammatory strategy rely predominantly on young murine models, leaving the impact of aging largely unexplored. At baseline, aged (56-week-old) female mice, in both WT and cGAS-/- mice, demonstrated more pronounced oxidative stress (malondialdehyde) and diminished antioxidant capacity (glutathione) relative to young (8-week-old) controls. Upon the induction of liver ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), the most severe hepatic damage was provoked exclusively in aged cGAS-/- mice. This exacerbated injury was confirmed by elevated liver enzymes, higher histological scores, widespread apoptosis (activated caspase-3), enhanced macrophage accumulation (F4/80+ cells), and increased serum cell-free DNA as a tissue damage marker. Additionally, aged cGAS-/- mice exhibited a significant surge in serum IL-6 and gut barrier dysfunction (FITC-dextran assay) at 6 h post-injury. Mechanistically, while cGAS-/- macrophages showed blunted inflammatory signaling upon lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation, co-incubation with D-galactose, which induces intracellular peroxide accumulation, restored their pro-inflammatory responses to WT levels. Concurrently, starvation protocols revealed that cGAS-/- hepatocytes were more vulnerable to mitochondrial oxidative stress (MitoSOX) than WT cells. Ultimately, aging critically modifies the cGAS-deficient phenotype, warranting the careful re-evaluation of cGAS therapeutic models in aged populations.

articles.title: Dry-Sand Layer Regulates Soil Moisture Stratification and Plant Community Assembly in the Desert-Oasis Ecotone.
articles.authors: Lu Y, Wang J, Ma J et al.
articles.abstract: The desert-oasis ecotone is ecologically fragile, yet the profile-scale role of the Dry-Sand Layer (DSL) in regulating soil moisture stratification and plant community assembly remains poorly understood. We systematically investigated six representative sites across the middle Heihe River Basin (with soil types transitioning from silt loam to aeolian sandy soils), combining multi-depth soil hydro-physical profiling (0-120 cm) with comprehensive vegetation sampling (across 90 nested quadrats recording 37 vascular plant species). A distinct DSL commonly formed at 60-80 cm depth across sandy sites, characterized by a bulk density of 1.39 g. cm-3 and a distinct moisture trough (typically < 2.0%), decoupling shallow root zones from subsoil moisture pools (1.10% to 5.09%). This edaphic boundary filtered out deep-rooted species, restricting vegetation to shallow-rooted xerophytic shrubs and grasses (e.g., Reaumuria soongarica (Pall.) Maxim., Aristida adscensionis L.) exhibiting high interspecific niche overlap (>0.86) and clustered spatial patterns (C > 1). Structural equation modeling indicated that subsoil moisture regulated by the DSL directly drives plant community diversity (path coefficient β = +0.54) and coverage (β = +0.61). Overall, the DSL serves as an essential eco-hydrological buffer balancing shallow soil moisture retention and subsoil conservation, indicating that ecological restoration in hyper-arid ecotones should prioritize DSL preservation and native shallow-rooted vegetation.

articles.title: Role of Serum HE4, Selected Clinical Features and Diagnostic Prediction Models in Differentiating Benign and Malignant Endometrial Lesions in Polish Women: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Krejczy K, Rzepka J, Wiśniewska O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The differentiation of endometrial cancer from non-malignant endometrial findings remains clinically important. We evaluated serum human epididymis protein 4 (HE4), clinical and ultrasound features, and two published diagnostic models, the Risk of Endometrial Malignancy (REM) score and Model A.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort, 110 women with abnormal uterine bleeding and/or ultrasound abnormalities underwent HE4 testing, transvaginal ultrasonography, and hysteroscopy with histopathological assessment. Original univariable analyses were supplemented by reanalysis of the individual study records, including ROC metrics, paired comparisons of AUCs, and an exploratory logistic model adjusting for age and endometrial thickness.
RESULTS: Endometrial cancer was diagnosed in 18 women; 92 had non-malignant findings. Median HE4 was higher in the cancer group (118.35 versus 52.3 pmol/L; p < 0.001, as originally reported). The AUC (95% bootstrap CI) was 0.834 (0.686-0.951) for HE4, 0.905 (0.794-0.981) for REM, and 0.840 (0.702-0.948) for Model A. AUC differences were not statistically significant (paired DeLong tests, all p > 0.10). In an exploratory adjusted analysis, each doubling of HE4 was associated with higher odds of malignancy (adjusted OR 5.41; 95% CI 1.81-16.21; p = 0.0025).
CONCLUSIONS: HE4 and both published models discriminated between malignant and non-malignant findings in this selected cohort. The findings are exploratory and require independent validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Pre-clinical medical students' perception of surgical professions and balance with personal life - a single-centre exploratory analysis.
articles.authors: Becker H, Gött H, Tellermann J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical professions deal with serious challenges to inspire students to pursue a surgical career and counteract demographic change. Students' interest in sub-specialization is influenced by socio-economic factors including work-life balance, flexible working hours and appreciation. However, robust data about the current perception of surgical professions in the early stage of medical education is lacking so far.
METHODS: We performed a voluntary online survey among students who participated in an elective neurosurgical course during their preclinical stage of medical studies. The investigator-developed survey addressed perception of unspecified surgical professions, including personal requirements, profession impact on health and lifestyle and the topic of gender disparities and family planning and was conducted before the students entered their elective course. We also assessed viewpoints on support programs facilitating compatibility of surgical training and family life.
RESULTS: A total of 109 students participated in the voluntary survey (66.1% female, 33.0% male, 0.9% not specified). Overall, 56.0% of respondents reported prior experience with surgical professions and 33.9% planned to pursue a surgical career. Most respondents (68.8%) rated surgical professions as more physically demanding than other specialties, and about half (49.5%) considered them more harmful to physicians' health. In contrast, only 26.6% rated the mental burden as higher in surgical than in other specialties. In the exploratory gender comparison, female participants more often agreed that male residents have better career chances in surgery, whereas male participants more often responded neutrally to this statement. Overall, 89.0% of participants expressed interest in unspecified support programs to improve the compatibility of professional and personal life, and 65.1% would be willing to accept a one-year extension of their surgical residency.
CONCLUSIONS: In summary, pre-clinical medical students of a preselected cohort tend to rate surgical disciplines as demanding, competitive and difficult to balance with private life. Most participants expressed interest in support programs for combining surgical training and family life which needs further evaluation in future studies.

articles.title: Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy.
articles.authors: Ganster F, Kallenberg F, Titova A et al.
articles.abstract: Histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previously, reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated H3K9ac were observed in placentas from women with preeclampsia. Building on these findings, this study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is associated with changes in placental histone modifications. Immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence were performed on placental sections from 60 patients stratified into four groups: women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed groups compared to unvaccinated controls, with the most pronounced reduction observed in women with prior infection during gestation. H3K9ac levels did not differ significantly between groups in any compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between SCT H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight, and a sensitivity analysis excluding cases with additional placental pathologies confirmed the robustness of the findings. As no gene expression profiling was performed, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 changes cannot be inferred. These descriptive findings warrant further investigation integrating epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches to clarify their functional relevance for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Future considerations in the surgical technique for vasectomy.
articles.authors: Mutter M, Garrett J, Williams J et al.
articles.abstract: There have been minimal changes in the vasectomy surgery technique in the last 50 years. Since the introduction of the "No Scalpel" technique in the 1970's, which itself is a minor change in how to open the scrotal skin, the traditional vasectomy has changed little with time. Nevertheless, there are now exciting new modalities being developed for the obstruction of the vas deferens that could change the technique for the better in the future. One of them is injection of a vasal-occlusive polymer (plug) that aims to be a less invasive and reversible form of male contraception. This product appears to be in the development pipeline of several companies worldwide. Another technique involves using a bipolar laparoscopic vessel sealing technology for a sealed vasectomy procedure that may be done transdermal in the future. In the everchanging area of reproductive health, there will be more male contraceptive techniques developed that improve accessibility, efficiency, and likely reversibility of male sterility.

articles.title: Genome sequencing in prenatal precision medicine of congenital malformations: Clinical experience from a single center.
articles.authors: Westenius E, Conner P, Sahlin E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As a part of implementing genome sequencing in prenatal precision medicine at the department of Clinical Genetics and Genomics, Karolinska University Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden, we evaluated the utility of genome sequencing for prenatally detected malformations, including diagnostic yield, turnaround time and impact on current and future pregnancies.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study comprised 218 fetuses with different malformations. One hundred and two prospectively collected samples were analyzed using clinical trio genome sequencing, and if non-diagnostic, they underwent research analysis. In addition, 116 samples were collected retrospectively and included all fetuses referred for clinical trio genome sequencing during the study period. As part of the clinical routine at the time of the study, quantitative fluorescent-polymerase chain reaction and chromosomal microarray had been performed before genome sequencing in 84.9% (185/218) of cases.
RESULTS: Clinical genome sequencing identified a molecular diagnosis in 22.5% (49/218) of the cases. Research analysis revealed two additional causative variants increasing the diagnostic yield to 23.4% (51/218). The phenotypes of the cases were divided into different groups with following diagnostic yields: 36.2% (21/58) in multisystem malformations, 30.8% (8/26) in skeletal malformations, 25.0% (14/56) in malformations in the central nervous system, 15.6% (5/32) in thoracic malformations, 11.5% (3/26) in abdominal malformations, and 0% (0/20) in other isolated anomalies. Additionally, four variants were considered potentially clinically relevant. A total of 39.2% (20/51) of the causative variants were related to a risk of recurrence. The turnaround time for clinical genome sequencing in ongoing pregnancies, when requested before gestational week 21 + 6 and prior to a parental decision on pregnancy continuation, was 12.5 ± 5 days (mean ± standard deviation, n = 40). Pregnancies with diagnostic results from genome sequencing were more likely to be terminated than those with normal results (p = 0.012, Fisher's exact test).
CONCLUSIONS: Genome sequencing has an important role in prenatal precision medicine, since it can detect the underlying cause of prenatally detected malformations in a reasonable time. As causative chromosome aberrations were excluded in most of the cases, an even higher diagnostic yield can be expected if genome sequencing is offered as a first-line test or after a normal rapid…

articles.title: Uterine management during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy: outcomes from a standardized surgical technique.
articles.authors: Duca LL, Armengaud C, Bader G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The optimal uterine management during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy remains debated. Although supracervical hysterectomy is generally preferred because of concerns regarding mesh exposure, total hysterectomy may be indicated in selected clinical situations. We compared perioperative and anatomical outcomes according to uterine management during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 178 patients undergoing primary laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy for stage ≥2 pelvic organ prolapse (POP-Q) between January 2010 and May 2025. Patients underwent uterine preservation (n=115), supracervical hysterectomy (n=31), or total hysterectomy (n=32). Primary outcomes were severe postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grades III-IV) and prolapse recurrence according to the composite Barber definition. Secondary outcomes included mesh exposure and postoperative anatomical results.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 18.5 months, severe complications were uncommon with no statistically significant differences between groups (0.9%, 3.2%, and 3.1%; P=0.30). Mesh exposure (2.6%, 0%, and 6.2%; P=0.40) and prolapse recurrence (12%, 19%, and 6.3%; P=0.30) did not differ according to uterine management. Post operative point C differed across groups (P<0.01), as did point Ba (P=0.03). Point Bp did not differ significantly (P=0.20;).
CONCLUSIONS: Severe postoperative complications and prolapse recurrence were uncommon in this cohort, with no statistically significant differences between uterine management groups. Given the small number of events and the limited size of the hysterectomy groups, these findings do not establish comparable safety or effectiveness. The clinical relevance of the observed differences in postoperative POP-Q measurements remains uncertain.

articles.title: Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT) alleviates inflammation-driven perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 cascade.
articles.authors: Du J, Cheng Y, Liu B et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction is closely correlated with chronic ovarian inflammation and decreased ovarian reserve, with the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory pathway serving as the core pathogenic regulator. Targeted inhibition of this inflammatory signaling cascade and subsequent ovarian cell apoptosis is a key therapeutic approach for improving perimenopausal ovarian lesions. Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT), a classic TCM formula, clears internal heat and nourishes yin and blood, and is traditionally used for perimenopausal night sweats due to yin deficiency with internal heat. Consistent with the pathology of perimenopausal ovarian inflammatory injury, these traditional properties provide an ethnopharmacological basis for alleviating chronic ovarian inflammation and protecting granulosa cells, supporting its potential in treating perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT) and its heat-clearing herb group (QRJD) on ovarian dysfunction in a natural perimenopause (PM) rat model.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: UHPLC-MS/MS characterized the chemical and blood-absorbed components of DGLHT and QRJD. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations identified core targets and bioactive constituents. Naturally aged rats (12-14 months old) were randomized into Control, PM, DGLH-L/M/H, QRJD, and celecoxib (CEL) groups. Parameters assessed included body weight, ovarian index, estrous cyclicity, serum sex hormones, follicular atresia, granulosa cell apoptosis, inflammatory factors in serum and ovarian tissue, and the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway activity. Validation was performed in TLR4-overexpressing KGN cells treated with DGLHT-containing serum.
RESULTS: Baicalein and Wogonin were identified as key blood-absorbed components targeting TLR4, Caspase-3, IL-1β, and TNF-α. Both DGLHT and QRJD restored estrous cycles, improved ovarian coefficients, expanded the pool of healthy follicles, and reduced follicular atresia rates. Additionally, both formulations reduced granulosa cell apoptosis, corrected hormonal imbalances (increased E2 and P4, decreased FSH and LH), and downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-18, TNF-α) and key proteins (TLR4, NF-κB p65, NLRP3, Caspase-3). Their anti-inflammatory efficacy was comparable to that of CEL, with medium- and high-dose DGLHT demonstrating superior endocrine protection. In vitro,…

articles.title: Distinct Plasma and Fecal Lipidomic Responses to Stearic, Palmitic and Oleic Acids-Enriched Diets in Postmenopausal Women.
articles.authors: Zhang W, Matuszek G, Dolnikowski GG et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary saturated fat intake is associated with an unfavorable plasma lipidomic profile and increased CVD risk. Stearic acid (18:0), a saturated fatty acid (SFA) has been shown to lower plasma LDL-cholesterol concentrations compared to other shorter-chain SFAs, but its broader lipidomic effects remain unclear. We aimed to address this by analyzing fasting and non-fasting plasma and fecal lipidomes using samples from a randomized crossover study in postmenopausal women (N=20, 64±7 years, BMI 26.4±3.4kg/m2) who consumed isocaloric diets enriched in 16:0, 18:0, and 18:1 for 5 weeks each, with 2-week washouts. Lipidomic profiles (cholesteryl esters [CE], diglycerides and triglycerides [DG, TG], phosphatidylcholines [PC], ceramides (Cer), sphingomyelins [SM], and free fatty acids [FFA]) were measured by QTOF mass spectrometry. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis, and spearman correlation analyses assessed diet separation (Variable Importance of Projection score >1.0) and associations between lipidomic and circulating lipid profiles, respectively. The 16:0 diet resulted in higher fasting plasma concentrations of lipid species across multiple classes relative to the 18:0 and 18:1 diet. The nonfasting lipidome showed higher long-chain glycerolipids, PC species, and CE 16:1 concentrations after the 18:0 compared to the 16:0 diet, and higher FFAs and several sphingolipid species in the fecal lipidome relative to the 18:1 diet. Several SM, DG, TG, and PC species were positively associated with LDL cholesterol and TG concentrations (r= 0.68 to 0.75, FDR<0.1) in fasting plasma following the 18:0 diet. These findings demonstrate that individual SFAs exert differential effects across metabolic compartments, influencing circulating lipid concentrations.

articles.title: Association of over-the-counter contraceptive pill use and knowledge of side effects in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.authors: Rodriguez MI, Burns H, Modlin EW et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Misconceptions about oral contraceptive side effects are common among users and may contribute to dissatisfaction and discontinuation independent of actual side effect experience.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether users of oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) hold accurate expectations about common side effects, including both labeled effects and commonly held misconceptions, and whether these expectations differ by how the pill is obtained, by prescription or over the counter (OTC).
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of baseline survey data that included information on contraceptive counseling (e.g., source, timing, and content) in a prospective cohort study of OCP users. Our primary outcome was the difference in knowledge of expected side effects between individuals obtaining their pills by prescription versus OTC. We assessed four side effects in two categories: effects listed in FDA-approved labeling for both progestin-only (POP) and combined (COC) pills (irregular bleeding/spotting; lighter or absent periods) and commonly held beliefs not supported by placebo-controlled evidence (weight change; decreased libido).
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 741 participants including 299 (40.4%) acquiring OTC POPs and 442 (59.6%) by prescription. The cohort was predominantly White (70.7%), aged 18-24 (36.6%), employed (65.0%), and commercially insured (62.6%). The OTC group had increased odds of anticipating irregular bleeding or spotting compared to the prescription group (aOR 1.42; 95% CI 1.03, 1.96) but were less likely to anticipate lighter or absent periods (aOR 0.67; 95% CI 0.49, 0.92). The OTC group was less likely to expect decreased libido (aOR 0.47; 95% CI 0.31, 0.70). There was no significant difference in expectations of weight change between groups (aOR 0.78; 95% CI 0.56, 1.08).
CONCLUSION: Individuals acquiring their OCP OTC had similar or more accurate side-effect expectations than those obtaining their OCP by prescription, including less endorsement of decreased libido, a commonly held but unsupported belief. Neither group differed in its expectation of weight change.

articles.title: Hofbauer Cells and Placental Villous Inflammation in Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Spatial and Functional Analyses.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Weng J, Copple K, Bernier E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth is a major cause of neonatal morbidity/mortality strongly associated with pathological placental inflammation, but cellular mechanisms leading to this inflammation are poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE(S): Our objectives were to ascertain which immune cells are in the placental villi, understand cell-specific profiles through technologies maintaining cell localization within the tissue, and determine the role of Hofbauer cells in the dysregulated placental inflammation during preterm versus term birth with a focus on spontaneous preterm birth.
STUDY DESIGN: We first evaluated what cells (immune) are in the placental villi and which could be contributing to placental inflammation. We included 228 patients with preterm or term deliveries, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, and obtained placentas for histological analysis and performed imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on a subset of tissue (n=24). Fresh placentas were also obtained to determine the inflammatory mediator profile and cell-specific protein production by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and flow cytometry (n=8-11).
RESULTS: Imaging mass cytometry revealed that placental macrophages (Hofbauer cells) were the main immune cell in the placental villi. Furthermore, we observed that preterm placentas, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, had significantly increased CD163+ and CD68+ cells compared to term. Placental villi macrophages in spontaneous preterm versus spontaneous term analyses revealed a predominance of inflammatory genes and pathways with an involvement from trophoblast cells supporting inflammation, whereas stromal cells were primarily involved in extracellular matrix remodeling. Spontaneous vs non-spontaneous comparisons supported that even though both preterm birth groups are inflammatory, key inflammatory pathways such as TNF⍺ are enriched in spontaneous PTB, while in the term comparisons the pathways were either not related to inflammation or vastly different, with IL-2 being the top signaling pathway. In an ex vivo model of inflammation using placental explants, we found increases in pro-inflammatory mediators that coincided with our bioinformatic analyses. Primary cell experiments, using isolated cytotrophoblasts and Hofbauer cells, further supported that Hofbauer cells were a key contributor to pro-inflammatory mediator production.
CONCLUSIONS: This work showcases the cell-specific profile of placental macrophages and the inflammatory…

articles.title: Postoperative Hormonal Regimens and Two-Year Ovarian Endometrioma Recurrence Following Laparoscopic Cystectomy: A Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Lu W, Miao H, Liu M et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare 24-month imaging-defined ovarian endometrioma recurrence hazards across four postoperative hormonal regimens after laparoscopic cystectomy.
DESIGN: Single-center weighted retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Guangdong Women and Children Hospital.
PATIENTS: Women aged 18-45 years who underwent laparoscopic cystectomy for ovarian endometrioma from August 2015 to August 2023 with documented 6-month prescription coverage for one regimen.
INTERVENTIONS: Combined oral contraceptives (COC), gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists (GnRH-a), dienogest, or dydrogesterone initiated within 1 month without switching or sequential therapy.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Imaging-defined recurrence was a new endometrioma-compatible cyst >2 cm on at least two follow-up ultrasound examinations or confirmed by repeat surgery or pathology. Among 1121 women, 160 (14.3%) experienced recurrence within 24 months. Compared with COC, GnRH-a (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.405; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.253-0.649) and dienogest (adjusted HR, 0.417; 95% CI, 0.251-0.690) were associated with lower recurrence hazards. The dydrogesterone estimate had a wider 95% CI (adjusted HR, 0.504; 95% CI, 0.265-0.958). Higher baseline cancer antigen 125 (CA-125; adjusted HR per 1 U/mL, 1.002; 95% CI, 1.001-1.004) and deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE; adjusted HR, 2.358; 95% CI, 1.593-3.490) were associated with greater recurrence hazards.
CONCLUSION: Among women with documented 6-month prescription coverage, GnRH-a and dienogest were associated with lower 24-month hazards of imaging-defined ovarian endometrioma recurrence than COC. The dydrogesterone estimate was below 1 but less consistent across sensitivity analyses. These associations should not be extrapolated to overall endometriosis control or long-term pain outcomes.

articles.title: Video-Based Coaching in Essentials in Minimally Invasive Gynecologic Surgery (EMIGS): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Nolan W, Parikh S, Barbaresso R et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To determine the effect of video-based coaching on skill acquisition for Essentials in Minimally Invasive Gynecologic Surgery (EMIGS).
DESIGN: Single-site randomized controlled trial.
SETTING: Academic institution.
PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Obstetrics and Gynecology residents (PGY1-PGY4) and medical students (MS3-MS4).
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to a control cohort without video-based coaching or an intervention cohort with video-based coaching, where participants' surgical video was critiqued and the participant was given individualized strategies to improve performance. All participants underwent a baseline evaluation performing EMIGS tasks, followed by repeat testing after one month.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: After randomization, there were no significant demographic differences between cohorts with respect to level of training, prior laparoscopic experience, or days between completion of initial and final tasks. Baseline laparoscopic performance did not differ between cohorts. After the intervention, participants in the coaching cohort improved their time to complete the running suture task (Task 5) by a median of 250 seconds, compared with a 60-second improvement in the control cohort (p = 0.011). Medical students experienced a large effect, with a 361-second improvement in Task 5 performance compared with 80 seconds in controls (p = 0.032). Residents with coaching improved by 196 seconds compared with 60 seconds in resident controls (p = 0.083).
CONCLUSION: Video-based coaching improved EMIGS Task 5 acquisition. EMIGS curricula within residency programs may benefit from incorporating video-based coaching to improve task acquisition.

articles.title: Clinical readiness of first-trimester gestational diabetes prediction: From risk score to care pathway.
articles.authors: Mihoci EC, Socolov D, Socolov RV et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess whether first-trimester gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) prediction can improve clinical decisions, rather than merely predict a later abnormal glucose test.
METHODS: We critically reviewed targeted PubMed searches, independent validations, prospective implementation studies, randomized trials and guidelines. Searches were non-systematic and selection limitations are reported.
RESULTS: Routine clinical and glycemic predictors are feasible, but transportability, calibration, and strategy-level benefit are not established consistently. RESPECT 2 demonstrated implementation feasibility; a trial of nutrition support in 519 model-selected women did not significantly reduce GDM. TOBOGM investigated treatment after early biochemical diagnosis, not care guided by a risk score. Direct trials of the complete prediction-guided strategy remain limited.
CONCLUSION: First-trimester scores should not replace recommended diagnostic testing. Clinical adoption requires local validation, a prespecified beneficial action, evaluation of costs and harms, and comparative trials measuring maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Adnexal Torsion: A Case Report of Organ Loss and Clinical Overview of a Time-Sensitive Gynecologic Emergency.
articles.authors: Leonard CD, Anderson S
articles.abstract: Adnexal torsion is a time-sensitive gynecologic emergency requiring rapid surgical intervention to prevent organ loss. This manuscript presents an evidence-based overview of the condition and contextualizes a case of delayed diagnosis in a 20-year-old cisgender woman. The patient presented with acute abdominal pain and a large ovarian cyst with normal Doppler flow. Despite specialist consultation, torsion was not recognized until hospital day 5. Absent blood flow on repeated Doppler prompted emergency laparoscopy, which revealed complete right adnexal necrosis requiring salpingo-oophorectomy. A literature synthesis revealed that normal imaging often provides false reassurance and that timely surgical exploration guided by clinical suspicion achieves high organ salvage rates. The case demonstrates that clinical suspicion must guide surgical decision-making because imaging cannot reliably exclude torsion. Improved awareness of the variable presentations of torsion and lower thresholds for diagnostic laparoscopy are essential to prevent organ loss and preserve full reproductive function. Accepted October 13, 2026. Published online XXX.

articles.title: Bridging Evidence and Practice: Recent Advances in Hypothyroidism Management during Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.authors: Osman M, Sheikh Z, Ripa FA et al.
articles.abstract: Deficiency of thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine and triiodothyronine, results in the clinical condition known as hypothyroidism, a prevalent endocrine disorder globally, particularly in women of childbearing age. Dynamic changes occur in thyroid function during pregnancy to provide adequate levels of thyroid hormones to the mother and the fetus. Hashimoto thyroiditis remains the most widespread reason for gestational hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and in mildly iodine deficient populations. Iodine plays a vital role in the synthesis and regulation of thyroid hormones; therefore, during pregnancy, iodine consumption must be increased by 50% to produce the required amount of maternal thyroid hormones and meet the increased demand of the developing fetus. Evidence-based studies have shown that even minor alteration in maternal thyroid function can cause pregnancy-related complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes (e.g. miscarriage, perinatal death, pre-eclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, low birth weight and postpartum hemorrhage). Therefore, the timely assessment and appropriate management of gestational hypothyroidism is crucial to ensure optimal maternal and fetal outcomes. Levothyroxine remains the standard treatment for hypothyroidism, significantly reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with hypothyroidism. The present review provides an update on the diagnosis and management of hypothyroidism in pregnant women, highlighting the different types, causes, signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism, and the obstetric outcomes of each type of hypothyroidism along with the treatment strategy. Current key recommendations based on clinical evidence by health practitioners are also provided to assist in planning and choosing the individualized treatment regimen for patients with hypothyroidism before and during pregnancy.

articles.title: The promise and limitations of cell-free DNA fragmentomics for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance.
articles.authors: Parikh ND, Singal AG
articles.abstract: A phase 2 cell-free DNA fragmentomics signature biomarker validation study in two populations from Guatemala and Romania showed promising performance for early-stage HCC detection when combined with serum alpha-fetoprotein and demographic factors.1 In this Viewpoint, we critically appraise the study and contextualize the findings in the current early detection HCC biomarker landscape.

articles.title: Reproductive burden in women with central hypersomnolence disorders: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Houziaux H, Gauriau C, Labonne A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Women with narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia face specific challenges in their reproductive lives, due to, (1) the potential teratogenic effect of several commonly prescribed therapies, (2) the reduced efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives with some agents, and (3) treatment discontinuation during pregnancy, which often impairs daily functioning. This study aims at evaluating those challenges.
METHODS: An 11-item survey was distributed to 91 women diagnosed with narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia in one reference center. The first section covered diagnosis, treatments, and contraception. A second section addressed pregnancy history and outcomes. Finally, the patients were asked to assess the impact of their disorder on domains related to reproductive health and womanhood.
RESULTS: Responses from 91 women diagnosed with narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2 or idiopathic hypersomnia were analyzed. 84,6% of patients received an enzyme-inducing treatment as first-line therapy, although most (68.1%) were already using oral hormonal contraception at treatment initiation. Consequently, 42 (45.1%) changed their contraceptive method. 22 (24.2%) reported a pregnancy after diagnosis and provided pregnancy-related outcomes. Communication with primary care professionals was rated as difficult, with many respondents reporting challenges obtaining clear guidance. On a scale from 0 to 10, the negative effect of the disease on women-specific aspects of their life was 5.56/10.
CONCLUSION: Narcolepsy and idiopathic hypersomnia are rare diseases that are usually under-recognized among non-specialists. Women report unmet needs regarding their condition and its treatment. Structured therapeutic education programs should be implemented to support decision-making around medications, contraception, pregnancy planning, and perinatal care.

articles.title: HPV16 A4 sublineage and its characteristic E6/E7/E2/LCR polymorphisms is associated with LSIL persistence in eastern Chinese women.
articles.authors: Sun Y, Zhang L, Wang L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) sublineages exhibit differential oncogenic risks, but their effects on the prognosis of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) remain unclear. This study investigated the association between HPV16 sublineages and their characteristic single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and the outcomes of LSIL among eastern Chinese women.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: A total of 110 patients of LSIL with HPV16-positive colposcopy biopsy were enrolled and they have been followed up every six months for 2 years. Variant types were determined by bidirectional sequencing of HPV16 DNA E2, E6, E7, LCR and L1 from cervical exfoliated cells.
RESULTS: Among 110 HPV16-positive patients with LSIL, phylogenetic analysis identified four sublineages, including A1 (5.5%), A2 (10.0%), A3 (14.5%), and A4 (70.0%). A characteristic set of 15 SNPs across the E6, E7, E2, and locus control region (LCR) regions was identified in 77.9% (60/77) of A4 isolates. Compared with the combination of A1, A2, and A3 sublineages, the A4 sublineage exhibited a higher persistence rate (28.57% vs. 12.12%) and a lower regression rate (61.04% vs. 84.85%) (p = 0.016). After adjusting for age, the A4 sublineage was significantly associated with LSIL persistence (OR = 4.04, 95% CI = 1.50-10.91, p = 0.006). In silico, A4 LCR gained an activator protein 1 (AP-1)-binding site spanning 7170-7178.
CONCLUSIONS: The HPV16 A4 sublineage, defined by a characteristic 15-SNP signature and a gained AP-1 binding site in the LCR, represents the predominant high-risk variant in Eastern Chinese women with LSIL. Its strong association with lesion persistence (OR = 4.04) supports its utility as a clinically accessible molecular marker for early triage of LSIL patients, potentially reducing unnecessary interventions and enabling personalized surveillance.

articles.title: "Turn that down a few notches": A qualitative analysis of uncertainty and psychosocial burden among non-BRCA previvors.
articles.authors: Chess I, Holtzman S, Leschly J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Risk reducing decisions impact previvors' identity, family experiences, and relationships. These decisions are especially challenging for non-BRCA previvors, who face vague guidelines and limited evidence. This qualitative study explored non-BRCA previvors' attitudes toward family planning, relationships, and the burden of previvor status.
METHODS: Previvors with non-BRCA mutations (Lynch-related, PALB2, RAD51C, BRIP1, CHEK2) were recruited from an urban gynecologic oncology clinic. We conducted semi-structured telephone interviews which were transcribed verbatim. Two investigators independently coded a subset of interviews, resolved discrepancies with a moderator blinded to study background, and then refined the codebook and applied across all transcripts to identify themes.
RESULTS: Twenty-one previvors completed interviews (median age 39). Three overarching themes emerged: impact of previvor status on mental health, on personal identity, and impact of medical experience on decision making. Those considering future fertility worried about assisted reproductive technology (ART) cost and time pressure from risk reduction timelines; those not pursuing fertility worried about early menopause and mutation transmission to children. Previvor status impacted romantic relationships differently, with some describing strains caused by altered family planning and cancer prevention timelines, while others feeling no impact. Previvors emphasized the physician-patient relationship and shared decision-making. Many expressed frustrations regarding access to reliable data amid unclear guidelines. The lower penetrance of the non-BRCA did not lessen the psychosocial burden of previvor status in our cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Family planning, relationships, and previvor burden are central concerns for previvors. Ambiguity surrounding non-BRCA variants emerged as an independent source of distress shaping daily lives. Physicians can better partner with previvors by acknowledging these challenges to align medical and personal goals.

articles.title: Rapid genotyping of FecB mutation in sheep using CRISPR-Cas12a orthology-assisted assay.
articles.authors: Li S, Shi S, Yang J et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate genotyping of the Fecundity Booroola (FecB) gene, a key determinant of ovine fecundity, is essential for effective breeding programs. However, current methods are largely constrained by their reliance on specialized equipment and high operational costs, which collectively limit their applicability for large-scale, on-site genetic screening. To address these challenges, we systematically evaluated five Cas12a orthologs and identified Gs12-19 as the optimal candidate. Based on this, we developed a novel detection platform integrating the CRISPR-Gs12-19 system with allele-specific amplification and fluorescence-based signal readout, which enables discrimination between homozygous wild-type sheep (AA) and FecB mutation carriers (AG or GG, collectively designated as RG). Coupled with a portable blue-light excitation device and a custom-designed Red Channel Quantification (RedQ) analytical program, the platform was field-tested on 153 randomly selected samples from a core crossbred sheep population. The method achieved 98% accuracy in mutation-carrier classification when benchmarked against Sanger sequencing. Collectively, this study offers a rapid, visually interpretable, and field-deployable platform for FecB mutation-carrier screening with high sensitivity and specificity, providing a practical solution to accelerate marker-assisted selection in sheep breeding.

articles.title: Management of presacral hemorrhage during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy using an autologous round ligament patch: a video case report.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Sepulveda CS, Ramirez IR, Rojas RG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Presacral hemorrhage during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy is an uncommon but potentially serious complication that can be difficult to control using standard techniques. Autologous tissue may serve as a readily available adjunct in challenging intraoperative bleeding scenarios.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 66-year-old woman with symptomatic stage III pelvic organ prolapse underwent laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy. During suture placement at the sacral promontory, brisk presacral bleeding occurred that was not adequately controlled with bipolar coagulation and compression. A small fragment of the round ligament was harvested laparoscopically and applied directly over the bleeding site. Bipolar energy was delivered through the tissue, resulting in cessation of bleeding. The procedure was completed without conversion, transfusion, or use of commercial hemostatic agents. Postoperative recovery was uncomplicated, and no recurrent bleeding or prolapse was observed at 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSION: The use of an autologous round ligament fragment as a tissue interface for bipolar coagulation may represent a feasible adjunct for controlling difficult presacral bleeding during minimally invasive pelvic surgery. This approach is immediately available and cost-neutral; however, its mechanism and generalizability remain uncertain. Further experience is needed to define its role relative to established hemostatic techniques.

articles.title: Health Professionals' Preferences for Genetic Prenatal Testing-An International Discrete Choice Experiment Survey.
articles.authors: Malmgren CI, Grauman Å, Johansson JV et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study explored healthcare professionals' preferences regarding prenatal genomic testing following the detection of a foetal anomaly and their attitudes towards uncertain results.
METHOD: HCPs involved in genetic prenatal diagnostics were asked to fill in a cross-sectional survey-based study using a discrete choice experiment to assess their preferences for prenatal genomic testing and attitudes towards uncertain results.
RESULTS: When ranking the different attributes, diagnostic yield was seen as the most important factor, followed by test safety, waiting time, and the professional responsible for communicating results. Regarding the DCE, respondents favoured tests with a higher probability of obtaining results and shorter turnaround times. The findings also revealed a consistent pattern of caution towards uncertainty, particularly among clinical geneticists compared to gynaecologists who preferred rapid return of test results. Clinical geneticists also assigned greater and almost equal importance to who was communicating the results, time to result, and the reporting of uncertain findings. In addition, respondents chose neither test option in approximately one third of choice tasks, suggesting that healthcare professionals were willing to forgo testing altogether when they perceived the balance between benefits and potential harms was unfavourable.
CONCLUSION: The cautious approach observed among healthcare professionals contrasts with findings from studies of prospective parents. Women generally preferred receiving as much information as possible from prenatal testing, including uncertain findings and secondary findings.

articles.title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016-2024: A population-based observational study.
articles.authors: Wang F, Yang H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016-2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR.
METHODS: We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2024) for subgroup analysis.
RESULTS: Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92). Urban MMR declined significantly (P < 0.0001), whereas rural MMR showed no significant temporal change (P = 0.313) and remained higher than urban levels (9.57 vs 7.58 per 100,000). Indirect obstetric causes accounted for 66.7% of maternal deaths, compared with 33.3% for direct causes, with no significant temporal trends in either category. Women aged 30-39 years accounted for 63.6% of maternal deaths, and 83.9% of deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals.
CONCLUSION: Taiyuan has maintained a low MMR through sustained investment in maternal healthcare; however, substantial urban-rural disparities remain. Indirect obstetric causes predominated among maternal deaths, suggesting a transition in the spectrum of maternal causes of death. Continued efforts to strengthen rural maternal health services and promote equitable, life-course-oriented maternal care are essential to further reduce preventable maternal deaths.

articles.title: Validity and reliability analysis of the Korean version of the Partners in Health Scale for middle-aged women.
articles.authors: Lee H, Kim J
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Middle-aged women experience persistent and multifaceted health-related changes during the menopausal transition that require ongoing self-management. However, validated instruments for assessing self-management in this population are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the validity and reliability of the Korean version of the Partners in Health Scale for middle-aged women (K-PIH-MW).
METHODS: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 312 community-dwelling Korean women aged 45-64 years. Content validity was assessed by six experts. Construct validity was examined through confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), including factor-level convergent and discriminant validity. Convergent construct validity was also evaluated using theoretically related external measures. Internal consistency reliability was assessed using Cronbach's α, Spearman-Brown coefficients, and McDonald's ω, as appropriate.
RESULTS: The K-PIH-MW demonstrated good content validity (scale-level content validity index = .96). CFA supported the original four-factor structure, with acceptable model fit (comparative fit index = .97, Tucker-Lewis index = .96, root mean square error of approximation = .08, standardized root mean square residual = .03). Factor-level convergent and discriminant validity among the four domains were supported. Convergent construct validity was supported by significant positive correlations with self-care agency (r = .63, p < .001), physical health-related quality of life (r = .31, p < .001), and mental health-related quality of life (r = .40, p < .001). The overall internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = .92), with satisfactory domain-level reliability based on Spearman-Brown coefficients and McDonald's ω.
CONCLUSION: These findings support the validity and internal consistency of the K-PIH-MW as a multidimensional measure of self-management among middle-aged women. The instrument may be useful for assessing self-management across multiple domains and identifying areas that may require additional support in clinical and community settings.

articles.title: Minimally invasive surgery improves surgical and analgesic outcomes in overweight or obese patients with borderline ovarian tumors: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Lee SM, Kim S
articles.abstract: This study aimed to compare surgical outcomes between minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and open surgery in overweight or obese patients with borderline ovarian tumor (BOT) and identify risk factors for additional analgesic use despite patient-controlled analgesia .We selected patients with a body mass index of 25 or more who underwent surgery for BOT at Korea University Anam Hospital from 2006 to 2023. Patients who underwent laparoscopic or robotic surgery were categorized into the MIS group, while those who underwent open surgery were categorized into the open surgery group. For statistical analysis, the Student t test, chi-square test, Fisher exact test, and logistic regression analysis were performed using SPSS. Of 128 patients, 90 were in the MIS group, and 38 were in the open group. Compared with the open surgery group, the MIS group had a shorter surgical time (P < .001), lower estimated blood loss (P < .001), a shorter hospital stay (P < .001), and a lower rate of additional analgesic use despite patient-controlled analgesia (P = .002). There was no significant difference in disease-free survival between the 2 groups. No deaths occurred during follow-up. MIS compared to open surgery was identified as a factor associated with significantly lower use of additional analgesics (adjusted odds ratio, 0.13; 95% confidence interval, 0.037-0.470; P = .002). In overweight or obese patients with BOT, MIS was associated with better surgical outcomes and a reduced need for additional analgesics during hospitalization compared with open surgery. These findings suggest that MIS may be a feasible surgical option for these patients.

articles.title: Construction of a nomogram for predicting pathological upgrading after LEEP in patients with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 based on colposcopic morphological features: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Chen L, Xie Y, Liu D et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grade 1/2 diagnosed by colposcopy-directed biopsy may underestimate the final lesion grade found on excision. In patients who proceed to Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP), postoperative pathology may show histopathological upgrading relative to the preoperative biopsy. Although HPV testing and ThinPrep Cytology Test (TCT) are standard screening tools, their differential value in this LEEP-selected CIN1/2 population remains unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with pathological upgrading after LEEP and to construct an internally validated nomogram based on colposcopic morphological features. We retrospectively analyzed 122 patients who underwent LEEP for clinical indications between 2020 and 2025 with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2. Pathological upgrading was defined as biopsy CIN1 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN2, or biopsy CIN2 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN3 (invasive carcinoma included). These 2 transitions were prespecified and are clinically distinct; event counts were, therefore, also reported by baseline biopsy grade. Multivariable logistic regression was used to develop a nomogram. Discrimination and calibration were assessed with ROC analysis and bootstrap internal validation; clinical utility was explored with decision curve analysis (DCA). Pathological upgrading occurred in 46/122 (37.7%) patients in this LEEP-selected cohort, including 4/15 (26.7%) with baseline CIN1 and 42/107 (39.3%) with baseline CIN2. In the multivariable model, Reid Colposcopic Index (OR = 1.41, P = .013) and number of involved quadrants (OR = 1.93, P = .018) were significantly associated with upgrading, whereas menopausal status (OR = 2.83, P = .059) and biopsy count (OR = 0.70, P = .068) did not reach conventional significance but were retained as candidate predictors. HPV genotype category and TCT were not significantly associated with upgrading. The nomogram showed apparent AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.719-0.883) on internal evaluation; calibration and DCA supported exploratory clinical utility within this surgical cohort. In women with biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 who already had indications for LEEP, colposcopic morphological features (Reid score and lesion extent) were more informative than HPV/TCT for predicting histopathological upgrading after excision. The nomogram may assist risk stratification within this selected surgical population. An ROC-derived probability threshold of 43% is presented only as an…

articles.title: How 37 Weeks Came to Define Preterm Birth and Why It Matters Today-Making of a Threshold.
articles.authors: Yu D, Norman M, Morin M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Preterm birth, defined as birth before 37 completed weeks of gestation, affects over 13 million births annually worldwide and remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. Despite the universal adoption of the 37-week threshold to define preterm birth, its historical origin and rationale remain unclear.
OBSERVATIONS: This review traces the evolution of the concepts of fetal maturity and gestational timing from ancient medicine to modern obstetrics. The idea of birth occurring too early can be traced to ancient Greek and Chinese medical writings, but the current 37-week threshold emerged in the mid-20th century, when definitions of prematurity shifted from birth weight-based criteria to gestational age. However, the basis for this threshold was not explicitly documented, and no clear evidence that its selection was based on a specific biological, clinical, or epidemiological justification was identified. Advances in obstetric dating and neonatal care have reshaped the clinical meaning of gestational age, with modern research and practice increasingly moving beyond a simple preterm-term dichotomy to the introduction of several subcategories of preterm birth. Growing evidence that infants born at 37 to 38 weeks face considerably higher short- and long-term health risks than those born later further challenges the assumption that 37 weeks represents a biologically sharp boundary.
