CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The 37-week threshold for preterm birth has long been used in epidemiological surveillance, research, and clinical classification, although no clear documentation supporting its selection has been identified, and it may be insufficient for a better understanding of short- and long-term health of the offspring. A more precise assessment of gestational age, together with high-resolution clinical and population data, may support a more refined classification of different preterm birth categories and further advance clinical care, research, and public health.

articles.title: Real-world evaluation of the NHS testing criteria for glucokinase hyperglycaemia in pregnancy.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.authors: Jones O, Brackenridge A, Houghton J et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Criteria for Glucokinase-Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young (GCK-MODY) genetic testing are now being integrated into the National Health Service (NHS) services using fasting glucose, body mass index (BMI) and ethnicity. We aimed to assess the national screening criteria for GCK-MODY in a multi-ethnic population.
METHODS: GCK-MODY testing was offered to women with gestational diabetes that met criteria in a multi-ethnic cohort. Data from the national testing centre was used to compare patient characteristics in those positive and negative for GCK-MODY.
RESULTS: Fewer cases of GCK-MODY were found when testing using NHS criteria (0.14%) than expected (0.9%). Individuals testing positive for GCK-MODY had a higher HbA1c than negative individuals (p < 0.001). There was no difference in 2-h glucose increment (p = 0.829).
CONCLUSIONS: Current criteria may not effectively identify a high-risk cohort of individuals to test, given the prevalence of GCK-MODY in those tested, leading to over-testing. HbA1c may prove a useful additional screening parameter. Further studies are needed to improve the criteria's utility across different ethnicities.

articles.title: Patient and partner experiences of prostate cancer survivorship in Ireland: findings from the co-designed PRO-ACT study (CTRIAL-IE 24-45).
articles.authors: Flynn CR, Sweeney M, Sullivan J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy among men in Ireland, yet patient and partner experiences regarding sexual wellbeing, treatment preparedness, and survivorship needs remain poorly characterised.
METHODS: The PRO-ACT study employed parallel, co-designed online surveys for patients with PCa and their partners across the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. Surveys were developed collaboratively with a patient previously treated for PCa and disseminated online between November 2024 and June 2025. Descriptive statistics summarised demographics, treatment preparedness, partner inclusion, sexual wellbeing, mental health, multidisciplinary consultation, and urinary/bowel toxicities.
RESULTS: A total of 598 patients and 538 partners participated. Preparedness for treatment-related sexual consequences was low: 66.3% of patients felt underprepared, and 53.1% of partners received no explanation. Sexual difficulties were widespread, with 85.4% of patients reporting erectile problems and 84.3% reporting decline in sexual wellbeing; 68.0% of partners also reported deterioration. Mental health impacts were substantial (patients: 58.7%, partners: 51.5%), yet psychological support was rarely offered. Urinary incontinence (63.7%), obstructive symptoms (40.4%), and bowel disturbances (40.1%) were common. Multidisciplinary involvement was inconsistent, with only 48.6% offered cross-specialty consultations.
CONCLUSIONS: This first all-island assessment demonstrates major gaps in information provision, partner inclusion, psychosexual support, and toxicity management. Findings highlight the need for structured, personalised, multidisciplinary survivorship pathways recognising sexual wellbeing and mental health as core components. Results provide actionable insights for Ireland's next National Cancer Strategy.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture at Front-Mu acupoint group attenuates stress urinary incontinence in rats by modulating oxidative stress and Nrf2 signaling.
articles.authors: Huang H, Chen B, Hu J et al.
articles.abstract: To investigate whether electroacupuncture (EA) at the Front-Mu acupoint group improves stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in rats through modulation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway. Sixty-five female SD rats were randomized into sham (n = 10) and SUI model (n = 55) groups. SUI was induced by vaginal dilation and bilateral ovariectomy. Successfully modeled rats were randomly divided into model, DMSO, EA, ATRA (Nrf2 inhibitor), and EA + ATRA groups (n = 10 each). EA was applied at Zhongji (CV3), Guanyuan (CV4), and bilateral Dahe (KI12) once daily for three days. Urodynamic parameters (MBC, ALPP), antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, GSH-Px), oxidative stress markers (8-OHdG, 4-HNE), apoptosis (TUNEL, Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-3), and Keap1/Nrf2 mRNA and protein expression were assessed. EA significantly increased MBC and ALPP, enhanced SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px activities, and decreased 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) and 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) levels (all P < 0.05). EA also reduced the apoptotic index, Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, and cleaved caspase-3 expression (all P < 0.05). Furthermore, EA upregulated Keap1 and Nrf2 mRNA and protein expression (all P < 0.05). These protective effects were partially abrogated by ATRA co-treatment. EA at the Front-Mu acupoint group alleviates SUI, associated with modulation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway, enhancing antioxidant defense and inhibiting apoptosis. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic support for further investigation of electroacupuncture in SUI treatment.

articles.title: Temporal trends in patients undergoing artificial urinary sphincter implantation: explantation outcomes and early failure patterns in a tertiary reconstructive referral center.
articles.authors: Roessler N, Vetterlein MW, Klemm J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Baseline characteristics and perioperative risk profiles in patients undergoing artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation have changed over time, potentially influencing clinical outcomes. This study assessed temporal trends in patient characteristics and explantation outcomes to inform preoperative counselling and risk stratification.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included male patients undergoing AUS implantation between 2009 and 2025, stratified into four implantation periods. Explantation-free survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Risk factors for explantation were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 491 patients were included (2009-2012: N = 177; 2013-2017: N = 159; 2018-2022: N = 107; 2023-2025: N = 48), with a median follow-up of 54 months (IQR 14-116). Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, with a relative increase in prior radiotherapy from 35% to 42% over time. Explantation rates were 36%, 27%, 22%, and 17%, respectively, predominantly due to erosion and infection. In multivariable analysis, prior radiotherapy (HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.30-2.70), prior BPH surgery (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.10-2.77), and prior bulbar urethroplasty (HR 2.10, 95% CI 1.12-3.93) were independent predictors of explantation. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant differences in explantation-free survival between periods (p = 0.8), although a numerical increase in early explantations within 24 months was observed (7.9% to 13%). In a supplementary analysis focusing on early explantation, prior radiotherapy (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.38-4.39) and prior urethral surgery (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.31-4.77) were independently associated with increased risk. Later implantation periods showed an increase in early explantation risk; however, this did not reach statistical significance. The study is limited by its retrospective single-center design.
CONCLUSION: The AUS remains a durable and effective treatment option for male incontinence, with stable outcomes across implantation periods. Careful preoperative counselling and structured follow-up remain essential, particularly in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Patient acceptance and implementation of automated breast ultrasound in intensified breast cancer surveillance.
articles.authors: Hatzipanagiotou ME, Hartwig K, Fernandez-Pacheco M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) is a standardized ultrasound technique that may reduce operator dependency compared with hand-held ultrasound. Evidence on patient acceptance and implementation in intensified breast cancer surveillance remains limited. This study evaluated patient acceptance and clinical implementation of ABUS within a certified center of the German Consortium for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center observational study, women enrolled in an intensified breast cancer surveillance program underwent ABUS examinations and completed standardized questionnaires. Patient-reported outcomes included examination-related discomfort, comparison with mammography, willingness to repeat the examination, and willingness to recommend ABUS. Workflow parameters and changes in acquisition time over repeated examinations were assessed prospectively.
RESULTS: 73 women contributed 162 ABUS examinations and corresponding questionnaires. Of these, 46/73 (63.0%) carried pathogenic variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, or TP53, and 27/73 (37.0%) had a previous breast cancer diagnosis. Median pain score was 0 (IQR 0-1) for both breasts. Among women with previous mammography and an available comparative rating, 56/57 (98.2%) rated ABUS as more comfortable. All 73 participants (100%) were willing to undergo future ABUS examinations and recommend the procedure. Mean acquisition and interpretation times were 31.9 ± 6.2 and 9.95 ± 4.0 min, respectively. Acquisition time decreased significantly with increasing examination number (β = - 1.72 min/examination; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: ABUS was associated with high reported patient acceptance and was feasible to integrate into intensified breast cancer surveillance, with improving acquisition efficiency over time.

articles.title: Beyond Obliteration: Anatomical Characterisation of Residual Vaginal Length Following Colpocleisis.
articles.authors: Pandey D, Kottayam D, Arja K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Colpocleisis is an established obliterative procedure for advanced pelvic organ prolapse in women who no longer desire vaginal intercourse. This video demonstrates the surgical anatomy and key operative steps of Le Fort, total colpocleisis, and colpocleisis with hysterectomy, and correlates these techniques with the postoperative vaginal anatomy and residual vaginal length.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted between September 2024 and August 2025 in women undergoing colpocleisis for stage III or IV POP. Vaginal length was measured preoperatively, immediately after surgery, and at 6 months. Perioperative outcomes, complications, recurrence, and patient satisfaction were recorded. The accompanying video demonstrates Le Fort colpocleisis, total colpocleisis, and colpocleisis with hysterectomy, highlighting key operative steps and their relationship to postoperative anatomy.
RESULTS: Twenty-one women underwent surgery. All achieved successful anatomical correction without recurrence during follow-up and reported high postoperative satisfaction. Mean vaginal length decreased from 8.70 ± 1.98 cm preoperatively to 3.76 ± 0.41 cm immediately after surgery and 3.90 ± 0.45 cm at 6 months. The mean reduction in vaginal length from baseline to 6 months was 4.80 ± 1.90 cm. Thus, successful colpocleisis resulted in substantial shortening of vaginal length, with persistence of a short measurable vaginal segment at 6 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Colpocleisis provides effective prolapse correction with substantial reduction in vaginal length while leaving a measurable residual vaginal segment. Objective characterisation of this postoperative anatomy may improve understanding of the anatomical outcome of colpocleisis.

articles.title: Inflammaging and Cellular Senescence in Postmenopausal Depression: Linking Estrogen Deficiency, Immune Dysregulation, and Brain Aging.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.authors: Zhang L, Yao Y, Cai X
articles.abstract: Postmenopausal depression is clinically heterogeneous and cannot be explained by estrogen deficiency alone. We propose a conceptual, testable neuroimmune-aging model in which endocrine decline may interact with inflammaging, cellular senescence, and brain vulnerability in a subset of women. The evidentiary base is uneven: direct studies of senescence in well-phenotyped postmenopausal depression are lacking; clinical endocrine data come mainly from perimenopausal depression; molecular-senescence findings come from late-life depression or general major depressive disorder; and most cellular and brain mechanisms are supported by aging or preclinical models. Reduced estrogen signaling may weaken immune homeostasis, whereas peripheral cytokines or senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors could influence vascular and neural interfaces, glia, neurotransmitter metabolism, stress signaling, mitochondrial function, and neuroplasticity. These pathways are candidate mediators, not established causal mechanisms. Clinically established care remains diagnosis-based antidepressant treatment, evidence-based management of vasomotor and sleep symptoms, and individualized menopausal hormone therapy for appropriate candidates. Anti-inflammatory, microbiome-based, and senescence-targeted strategies remain investigational; no senolytic or senomorphic is approved for depression or menopause-related mood symptoms. Prospective studies integrating menopausal staging, prespecified confounders, senescence biomarkers, neuroimaging, and mood outcomes are needed to test this model.

articles.title: Preimplantation genetic testing in Italy: a single-cycle retrospective analysis.
articles.authors: Conforti A, Faggionato C, Vigiliano V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) is a diagnostic procedure performed during assisted reproductive technology (ART) to detect chromosomal and monogenic abnormalities before embryo transfer. In Italy, the Italian ART Register (IARTR) monitors ART and PGT activity. Within a National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) project, entitled "Development of the Italian Preimplantation Genetic Testing (PGT) Network", we developed a monitoring system based on ART single-cycles in which PGT was performed.
METHODS: Data on ART-PGT cycles performed in 2024 were collected from 24 Italian ART centers. A relational database was developed including cycle-level and embryo-level variables. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics, Version 29 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).
RESULTS: Overall, 2181 ART-PGT cycles involving 1358 patients were analyzed. Genetic testing was performed in 1195 cycles during 2024, and next-generation sequencing was the most frequent technology (96.5%). PGT for aneuploidies (PGT-A) was the most frequent procedure (1065 cycles), followed by PGT for monogenic/single gene defects (PGT-M) (114 cycles) and PGT for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) (110 cycles). The main indication for PGT-A was advanced maternal age (59.4%), for PGT-M was beta-thalassemia (29.6%), for PGT-SR reciprocal chromosomal rearrangements (61.3%). A total of 3771 embryos were analyzed, of which 7% yielded no result. Most blastocysts were biopsied on day 5 or 6 and were classified as having good or optimal quality. Embryo transfer was performed in 761 cycles, most as single embryo transfer, resulting in a clinical pregnancy rate of 49.1%.
CONCLUSIONS: The single-cycle monitoring system for ART-PGT was feasible and effective in collecting detailed clinical and laboratory data. This approach represents an innovation in epidemiological surveillance and may be useful in quality assessment and standardization of ART-PGT practices in Italy.

articles.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
articles.authors: Vahab N, He E, Sarwar T et al.
articles.abstract: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM (Length-efficient sUbword-based Nucleic Acid Foundation Model), an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling of long RNA transcripts. We systematically evaluate tokenization strategies and vocabulary sizes to investigate the trade-offs between sequence compression, representation granularity, computational efficiency, and downstream performance. Across multiple RNA prediction tasks, including transcript classification, subcellular localization, and RNA-protein interaction prediction, LUNA-FM achieved competitive performance compared with existing RNA FMs while reducing effective input length and fine-tuning cost. We also found that frequency-based subword tokenization generally produced more stable and effective representations than likelihood-based approaches, although the optimal vocabulary size remained task dependent. Training-set motif discovery identified candidate motifs enriched relative to matched low-attribution and dinucleotide-shuffled controls of preeclampsia-associated lncRNAs. Overall, our findings highlight the task-dependent effects of subword tokenization and vocabulary size, extend RNA FM evaluation to longer transcript inputs, and establish LUNA-FM as a competitive model with favourable recorded fine-tuning times.

articles.title: Technical difficulty of levonorgestrel 52-mg intrauterine device placement and six-month clinical outcomes among women with and without isthmocele: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Laporte M, Marcelino AC, Juliato CRT et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare pain and difficulty during levonorgestrel 52-mg intrauterine device (LNG 52-mg IUD) insertion in women with and without isthmocele and, secondarily, to assess changes in uterine bleeding, and chronic pelvic pain six months after insertion.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our prospective study was conducted at the Universidade Estadual de Campinas, Brazil. Women aged 18-43 years with at least one caesarean delivery ≥6 months previously, with or without ultrasound-diagnosed isthmocele, were included. Insertion pain, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain were assessed using a 100-mm visual analogue scale (VAS). We included 260 women (103 with and 157 without isthmocele), providing 80% power at α = 0.05 to detect differences in insertion outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with insertion difficulty and severe pain.
RESULTS: Insertion success was similar in women with and without isthmocele (99.0% vs. 98.7%; p = 1.000), as were pain intensity (p = 0.80) and insertion difficulty (p = 0.19). Of 224 women reporting at least one symptom at baseline, 89 (39.7%) had isthmocele and 135 (60.3%) did not. At six months, both groups showed significant reductions in heavy menstrual bleeding, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain (all p < 0.001). Prolonged menstrual bleeding (≥8 days) decreased significantly among women with isthmocele; however, the group-by-time interaction was not significant (p = 0.21).
CONCLUSION: Isthmocele was not associated with greater insertion pain or difficulty. Six months after LNG 52-mg IUD insertion, both groups showed improvements in heavy menstrual bleeding, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain.
SHORT CONDENSATION: Isthmocele was not associated with greater insertion pain or difficulty of the LNG 52-mg IUD. Six months after IUD insertion, both groups showed improvements in heavy menstrual bleeding, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain.

articles.title: Plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA sequencing identifies clinically unsuspected cases of Toxoplasma gondii infection in immunocompromised patients: a single-centre experience.
articles.authors: Goren LR, Lehman AC, Drozdov D et al.
articles.abstract: Toxoplasmosis can be challenging to diagnose, particularly in immunocompromised patients with nonspecific clinical presentations. We present a retrospective, single-centre case series of eight Toxoplasma gondii infections identified by plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing in allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Nested within a larger cohort evaluating cfDNA utilization, this case series highlights a positive clinical impact of cfDNA testing in 5 out of 8 (62.5%) patients, including earlier diagnosis and changes in clinical management. These findings illustrate the potential utility of plasma cfDNA sequencing as a complement to conventional diagnostics across diverse clinical presentations of toxoplasmosis.

articles.title: Screening performance and optimal threshold of the American Diabetes Association Diabetes Risk Score in a large multistate Sudanese population: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Noor SK, Ali HSAHM, Eldouma MYM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Validated non-invasive risk stratification tools can support diabetes prevention in resource-constrained settings. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) Diabetes Risk Score is widely used but has not been rigorously evaluated in sub-Saharan African populations. This study assessed the screening utility and optimal score threshold of the ADA Diabetes Risk Score in the population in Sudan.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, population-based study was conducted in 2023 across eight Sudanese states, using multistage cluster random sampling from 32 community health centres. Sudanese adult ≥18 years completed the self-administered ADA Diabetes Risk Test questionnaire (7-item, maximum score 10). Among the 1855 eligible participants, 203 with a prior physician diagnosis of diabetes were retained as the reference group for diagnostic performance analysis. Associations were evaluated using χ² tests and multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic analysis with Youden index optimisation was used to derive the optimal score threshold. All inferential analyses were performed using R (V.4.4.3).
RESULTS: Among participants (64.3% female; 80.3% aged <40 years), 10.8% (n=200) were classified as high-risk by the standard ADA threshold (score ≥5). Using physician-diagnosed diabetes (n=203) as the reference, the Youden-optimal threshold of 3.5 achieved sensitivity 59.6% (95% CI 52.2% to 66.0%) and specificity 79.7% (95% CI 77.8% to 81.5%), with area under the curve 0.744 (95% CI 0.707 to 0.781, p<0.001). The overall number needed to screen was 9.3, ranging from 43.8 in adults aged <40 years to 1.1 in those aged >60 years. On multivariable logistic regression, hyperlipidaemia (OR: 5.33, 95% CI 3.43 to 8.17) and gestational diabetes (OR: 4.50, 95% CI 1.62 to 11.8) were the strongest independent predictors of high-risk ADA classification.
CONCLUSION: The ADA Diabetes Risk Score demonstrated moderate screening utility in this Sudanese population. A threshold of 3.5 may improve sensitivity for identifying at-risk individuals compared to the standard cut-off of ≥5. These findings are hypothesis-generating; external validation against biochemical endpoints is required before clinical adoption.

articles.title: MRPL47 as a mitochondrial biomarker for early detection and therapeutic response in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Pradeep M, Kadamberi IP, George J et al.
articles.abstract: The MRPL47 (mitochondrial ribosomal protein large subunit 47) gene in chromosome 3q26 encodes a protein that is part of the large subunit of the mitochondrial ribosome. We observed that MRPL47 is frequently amplified and overexpressed in ovarian cancer samples. Importantly, increased expression of MRPL47 mRNA is associated with high levels of MRPL47 protein in patients with ovarian cancer. High expression of MRPL47 is also associated with poor overall and recurrence-free survival of patients with ovarian cancer. Gene set enrichment analysis and target-specific knockdown assays revealed that the cMYC transcription factor regulates MRPL47 expression. Furthermore, MRPL47 was identified at very high levels in the plasma samples of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer compared to those of healthy volunteers. MRPL47 was also associated with cisplatin resistance, whereas its expression predicted sensitivity to cisplatin therapy. Notably, MRPL47 improved metabolic fitness in cancer cells by promoting mitochondrial translation, cellular respiration, and glycolysis. Taken together, our results demonstrate that MRPL47 can serve as a diagnostic biomarker for ovarian cancer and potentially for other cancers that exhibit 3q26 locus chromosomal amplification.

articles.title: Integrating hormonal analyses into the development of hormonal male contraception: geographic centre as a determinant of individual response.
articles.authors: Zitzmann M, Schlatt S, Nieschlag E et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Are the geographic recruitment centre and dynamic sex-steroid profiles, particularly for dihydrotestosterone, associated with inter-individual differences in libido and mood-related adverse events during hormonal male contraception?
SUMMARY ANSWER: In this multinational analysis of the WHO testosterone undecanoate/norethisterone (TU/NETE) enanthate trial, geographic cluster was associated with distinct androgenic profiles and clinical responses; lower dihydrotestosterone exposure emerged as a consistent predictor of decreased libido and mood-related adverse events.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Combined testosterone-progestin regimens can suppress spermatogenesis effectively, but the WHO TU/NETE trial was discontinued prematurely because of mood-related adverse events despite high contraceptive efficacy. The endocrine mechanisms underlying these adverse effects remain incompletely understood.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This secondary analysis used serial hormone and adverse-event data from the multinational WHO/CONRAD trial, which enrolled 320 men. However, 255 participants had serum samples available for centralized steroid analysis and constituted the present analytical cohort, as the samples from Jakarta, Indonesia (65 subjects) were not sent to the Central Laboratory.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Healthy male participants were recruited across European/Australian, South American, and Asian centres and grouped into geographic clusters. Serum testosterone, calculated free testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estradiol, and norethisterone were analysed centrally by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Longitudinal mixed-effects models and time-to-event analyses were used to evaluate associations between hormone trajectories, geographic cluster, age, libido changes, and mood disorders.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Marked cluster-dependent heterogeneity was observed. Participants from Chile showed higher total and free testosterone and persistently higher dihydrotestosterone concentrations over time, accompanied by a higher incidence of increased libido. Participants from India showed lower dihydrotestosterone exposure and higher norethisterone concentrations and no libido and mood changes. European/Australian participants showed comparatively lower dihydrotestosterone concentrations and the highest cumulative incidence of mood disorders. Declining dihydrotestosterone concentrations were associated with decreased libido…

articles.title: SGLT2 inhibitors for peripartum cardiomyopathy: A call for a dedicated trial.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.authors: Acharya B
articles.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) accounts for more than 60% of pregnancy-related cardiogenic shock in the United States, yet specific evidence-based therapies remain limited. Despite guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, left ventricular ejection fraction recovery is incomplete in up to 50% of patients, and mortality reaches 20% in high-risk populations. A recent propensity-matched cohort of 10,907 PPCM patients found that sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.25-0.92), heart failure exacerbation (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.76-0.90), and all-cause re-hospitalization (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.93), corroborated by two independent case reports showing rapid left ventricular ejection fraction recovery on empagliflozin-containing regimens. However, residual confounding, notably a significant baseline left ventricular ejection fraction imbalance despite matching (35.0% vs. 45.0%; P < 0.01) and unreported bromocriptine use, limits causal inference. The convergence of real-world evidence, case reports, and mechanistic plausibility supports early SGLT2i consideration in appropriately selected PPCM patients. A dedicated randomized controlled trial, stratified by disease severity, lactation status, and race, and designed with careful ethical consideration, is now scientifically justified and ethically imperative.

articles.title: Beyond geographic access: Rural disparities in gynecologic oncology across the care continuum.
articles.authors: Schultz B, Hutchcraft ML
articles.abstract: Rural patients in the United States face disproportionate gynecologic cancer mortality compared to urban patients, driven by overlapping geographic, socioeconomic, and structural barriers that vary across cancer types and the care continuum. This review synthesizes the literature on rural disparities in cervical, endometrial, and ovarian cancers from prevention through survivorship. Rurality is defined variably across the literature, most commonly using government classification systems such as Rural-Urban Continuum Codes or Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Rural women experience lower Human Papillomavirus vaccination rates and reduced uptake of guideline-concordant cervical cancer screening, higher rates of late-stage ovarian cancer diagnosis, and delayed endometrial cancer diagnosis. Even when rural patients access subspecialist care, treatment quality gaps persist, including higher rates of open surgical staging for endometrial cancer and reduced access to brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer. Survival disparities remain even among rural patients treated at tertiary centers with subspecialist involvement, underscoring that geographic access alone is insufficient. Insurance status, health literacy, financial hardship, and limited social support compound these barriers throughout the continuum. Interventions including telehealth, shared care models, community-based navigation, and Medicaid expansion show promise but remain incompletely evaluated in gynecologic oncology. Most existing literature documents disparities without evaluating interventions, and variability in how rurality is defined limits generalizability. Rural women deserve more than documentation of the disparities they face, and closing these gaps will require both coordinated action across clinical, institutional, and policy levels and a stronger evidence base for targeted interventions.

articles.title: Pelvic floor knowledge and unhealthy habits related in female athletes: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Bosch-Donate E, Vico-Moreno E, Romero-Franco N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe pelvic floor (PF)-related knowledge and unhealthy habits among female athletes, and to examine their associations with PF dysfunction (PFD) symptoms, sports characteristics, academic level and help seeking attitudes.
METHODS: A total of 538 female athletes (36.7 ± 11.3 years) completed an anonymous online questionnaire covering age, academic level, sports experience, unhealthy PF-related habits, PFD symptoms, professional healthcare-seeking attitude and knowledge about urinary incontinence (UI), anorectal incontinence (ARI), pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and female sexual dysfunction (FSD). Adequate knowledge was considered as ≥70% correct responses.
RESULTS: Female athletes demonstrated adequate knowledge regarding UI, ARI and POP, but insufficient knowledge about FSD (52.6%). Several PFD symptoms were associated with lower knowledge levels and a higher number of unhealthy habits compared with athletes without these symptoms (p<0.05). Younger athletes showed lower knowledge about ARI (p=0.033) and POP (p=0.003), while older athletes showed lower knowledge about FSD (p<0.001). Athletes who rejected professional healthcare showed lower knowledge across all PFD domains (p<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Female athletes reporting symptoms suggestive of PFD showed lower levels of knowledge and a higher number of unhealthy PF habits compared with those without symptoms. Although athletes generally demonstrated an appropriate level of knowledge regarding PFD, important gaps were observed in the FSD domain and in unhealthy toileting and sport-related habits, particularly among athletes without university studies. Differences in knowledge were also observed according to age and healthcare-seeking attitudes, highlighting areas that may be considered in future educational initiatives.

articles.title: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus (Hakim's syndrome): A cerebrovascular disorder. The contributions of Salomón Hakim (1922-2011).
articles.authors: Román GC, Jackson RE, Pardo-Turriago R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In 1957, Salomón Hakim MD (1922-2011), a Colombian neurosurgeon, discovered normal-pressure hydrocephalus (NPH), a cerebrovascular disorder that involves cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, cerebral arterial and venous blood flow, as well as the glymphatic circulation.
METHODS: We review the contributions of Hakim beginning with the initial 7 cases of NPH he studied and treated in Bogotá, Colombia, and the original articles published in 1965 in association with colleagues from neurology, neuropathology, and neurosurgery at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School in Boston, USA. We present Hakim's experimental studies on the pathophysiology of NPH that led him to successfully design CSF shunting valves for the surgical treatment of NPH.
RESULTS: The epidemiological measurement of NPH is affected by underdiagnosis despite the typical clinical features centered on ventriculomegaly and Hakim's triad of abnormal gait, urinary incontinence and cognitive decline. Earlier difficulties in visualizing the cerebral ventricles were solved by computerized tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain images, particularly after frequent falls in the elderly, allowing the quantification of the ventriculomegaly by measuring the Evans index, the callosal angle and the ALVI index. The recent introduction of Arterial Spin-Labeled Magnetic Resonance Imaging (ASL-MRI) to quantify cerebral blood flow (CBF) after the CSF tap test has simplified the diagnosis of NPH. Denying the existence of NPH was based on the lack of randomized, placebo-controlled trials but this has been answered by international trials demonstrating the benefit of CSF shunting.
INTERPRETATION: We confirm the existence of NPH-the clinical syndrome discovered by Salomón Hakim-a curable cerebrovascular disorder, grossly underdiagnosed, and we emphasize the overall poor prognosis of the untreated NPH patients in contrast with the usual return to normal life resulting from surgical treatment. Given the extensive and valuable contributions of Salomón Hakim to the discovery, pathogenesis, clinical and surgical treatment of this neurological condition, 70 years after his discovery we propose renaming idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus as Hakim's syndrome.

articles.title: A cross-sectional study of contraception and abortion utilization among female sex workers in the democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, and Nigeria: preferences, access, and barriers.
articles.authors: Moss RA, Danel I, Kamau G et al.
articles.abstract: Female sex workers (FSW) report high rates of unintended pregnancy and unmet need for contraception. Using convenience sampling, this cross-sectional study included 853 FSW recruited from eight cities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Kenya, and Nigeria, where proportionate mortality from unsafe abortion is high. The study examined contraceptive prevalence, preferences, access, and barriers, and abortion history, methods and complications. Non-condom modern contraceptive prevalence was higher among FSW in Kenya (73.2%) than in the DRC (40.8%) and Nigeria (26.9%). A greater proportion of FSW in Kenya reported no abortion in the past five years (82.8%) compared with the DRC (54.0%) and Nigeria (33.9%). Among those reporting abortion, the mean number was lower in Kenya (1.5) than in the DRC (1.7) and Nigeria (2.2). Cost was a common barrier to accessing contraceptives in the DRC and Nigeria (approximately one-third of respondents) but less common in Kenya (9%). Contraceptive preferences differed. The majority of FSW in Kenya preferred long-acting reversible contraception (LARC). Although the majority of FSW in the DRC and Nigeria preferred condoms, client dynamics in criminalized settings may limit consistent condom use making them ineffective. Improving access to free or affordable non-condom modern contraceptives, particularly LARC, is critical to reducing unintended pregnancies and preventing morbidity and mortality from unsafe abortion among FSW. Increased education and counseling on LARC methods may further support uptake.

articles.title: The developing fetal immune landscape and congenital viral infection.
articles.authors: Chima SC, Sun SJ, Duell T et al.
articles.abstract: Fetal development is a complex process that can lead to adverse health consequences when impaired, such as congenital anomalies, fetal growth restriction, preterm birth, and stillbirth. Although there is a well-developed literature on the timing of adaptive immune cell appearance in the fetus, comparatively little is known about the ontogeny and functional maturation of the innate immune system over gestation. This knowledge gap limits our understanding of how intrauterine infections influence fetal development and contribute to adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Thus, the goal of this review is to summarize existing knowledge of the ontogeny of the fetal adaptive and innate immune systems throughout gestation, and how they are impacted by infection. We examine the emergence of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, while highlighting changes in immune lineages across the fetal brain, liver, thymus, bone marrow, spleen, and placenta, which play critical roles in immune competency and tolerance. The role of innate immunity in immunocompetence and pathogen responses is highlighted when known. Finally, we address how vertically transmitted and teratogenic viral infections disrupt normal immune and tissue development. Collectively, these studies demonstrate the dynamic, tissue-specific immune landscape that evolves throughout gestation.

articles.title: Reproductive Implications of a Rare Paternal Dicentric Rearrangement 45,XY,dic(5;13)(p15;p12) in an IVF Cycle With Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Structural Rearrangements: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Do VN, Tran HP, Van Nguyen T et al.
articles.abstract: This case highlights the counseling challenges associated with a rare paternal dicentric rearrangement. PGT-SR identified only one transferable balanced/normal copy-number profile among four biopsied blastocysts, underscoring the need to discuss the possibility of few or no transferable embryos and the limitations of PGT-SR.

articles.title: Circulating tumor DNA in Hodgkin lymphoma: biological classification, molecular residual disease, and integration with PET response.
articles.authors: Bednarek M, Komossa M, Bidzińska J
articles.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and its tumor-derived fraction, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), enable non-invasive tumor genotyping, longitudinal disease monitoring, and molecular residual disease (MRD) assessment. Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is particularly suitable for ctDNA-based analysis because malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells usually constitute only a small fraction of the tumor mass, whereas plasma may contain a strong tumor-derived DNA signal. This narrative review summarizes the potential applications of cfDNA-based ctDNA analysis in hematologic malignancies, with a focused emphasis on cHL. We discuss pre-analytical and analytical requirements, including plasma processing, tumor-informed and tumor-naive sequencing, error suppression, droplet digital PCR, and control for clonal hematopoiesis. We then synthesize evidence for ctDNA as a dual-readout biomarker: a baseline tool for non-invasive biological classification and a dynamic measure of molecular response. Published studies identify cHL genomic subtypes, associations with the tumor microenvironment, and prognostic information complementary to PET and conventional risk factors. Age-specific evidence is uneven, and most studies demonstrate analytical feasibility or prognosis rather than benefit from a ctDNA-triggered intervention. ctDNA-MRD should complement FDG-PET/CT; it cannot localize disease or currently replace established staging and response criteria. Routine implementation will require harmonized sample handling, validated assays and reporting thresholds, external quality assessment, and prospective trials demonstrating that ctDNA-guided treatment improves disease control, toxicity, or quality of life.

articles.title: Autologous platelet-rich gel activated by calcium gluconate for postoperative endometrial repair in moderate-to-severe intrauterine adhesion: a retrospective preliminary evaluation of efficacy.
articles.authors: Li Y, Han Y, Cao J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the effect of calcium gluconate-activated autologous platelet-rich gel (APG) on endometrial repair in patients with moderate-to-severe intrauterine adhesion (IUA).
METHODS: In this study, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe IUA who were undergoing hysteroscopic transcervical resection of adhesion surgery were recruited and grouped based on whether they underwent APG treatment (APG group) or not (non-APG group; n = 30 each). Hysteroscopy examination and transvaginal ultrasonography were performed after surgery to evaluate adhesion recurrence and endometrial thickness. Simultaneously, patients self-recorded the menstrual volume using a menstrual diary.
RESULTS: There was no significant difference in baseline characteristics, preoperative uterine adhesion grade, endometrial thickness, or menstrual pattern between the APG and non-APG groups (p > 0.05). After treatment, compared with the non-APG group, the postoperative adhesion recurrence rate (13.3% vs. 36.7%) and adhesion grades (75% mild and 25% moderate vs. 72.7% mild and 27.3% moderate) were significantly decreased in the APG group (p = 0.039). The endometrium thickness in the APG group was greater than that in the non-APG group (6.29 ± 0.24 mm vs. 5.10 ± 0.16 mm, p = 0.000), and the endometrial thickness increment was substantially higher in the APG group than that in the non-APG group (2.82 ± 0.17 mm vs. 1.84 ± 0.12 mm, p = 0.000). Furthermore, more participants in the APG group experienced significant recovery in menstrual volume at 3 months after surgery (p = 0.031), and participants from the APG group maintained improved menstrual volume 6 months after surgery (p = 0.029). Multivariate analysis confirmed the beneficial effect of APG in promoting endometrial repair.
CONCLUSION: Calcium gluconate-activated autologous platelet-rich gel has the potential to reduce postoperative recurrence and improve menstrual properties in patients with moderate-to-severe IUA.

articles.title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation versus sham stimulation and dexamethasone versus amisulpride for preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic gynecologic surgery: protocol for a randomized 2 × 2 factorial trial.
articles.authors: Li Y, Zhang J, Xu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a common complication after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Although multimodal prophylaxis is recommended, clinical practice still relies largely on pharmacologic interventions. Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) at the P6 acupoint may have potential benefit for PONV prevention. However, its effectiveness when incorporated into pharmacologic prophylaxis, and whether its effect varies according to the antiemetic used, remain unclear. This trial aims to evaluate the effect of P6-TEAS on PONV prevention in patients receiving dexamethasone or amisulpride.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial will enroll 212 women undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive one of four treatment combinations: TEAS plus dexamethasone, TEAS plus amisulpride, sham stimulation plus dexamethasone, or sham stimulation plus amisulpride. TEAS or sham stimulation will be delivered at the P6 acupoint in two 1-h sessions, before surgery and at 24 h after surgery. The primary outcome will be the incidence of PONV within 48 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include PONV-related symptoms and severity, use of rescue antiemetics, opioid consumption, pain scores, recovery milestones, patient satisfaction, QoR-15 scores, and length of hospital stay. Safety outcomes will include adverse events related to TEAS or study drugs and perioperative hemodynamic events requiring treatment.
DISCUSSION: This trial will evaluate P6-TEAS versus sham stimulation as the primary comparison and provide exploratory estimates for the dexamethasone-versus-amisulpride comparison and the TEAS-by-drug interaction. The findings may inform integrated prevention strategies for PONV after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07631910, identifier NCT07631910.

articles.title: Association of viral load values with cervical lesion severity and exploratory genotype analysis in HPV-positive Indian women.
articles.authors: Singh N, Zakiya Z, Singhal S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hybrid Capture 2 (HC2) provides a semi-quantitative estimate of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) burden as relative light units/cutoff (RLU/CO), and HPV genotyping may add value to triage assessment. We evaluated the association of RLU/CO with cervical lesion severity and explored whether genotype information improves diagnostic performance in HPV-positive Indian women.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in two sequential phases. In the initial phase, 217 consecutive HPV-positive women underwent HC2 HPV DNA testing, colposcopy-guided biopsy, and histopathological assessment. In a subsequent phase, an additional group of 111 HPV-positive women underwent the same clinical and histopathological assessment and also provided specimens for HPV genotyping. The genotype-enriched group was analysed separately for genotype distribution, co-infection patterns, and exploratory genotype-integrated prediction models. Age, Histopathology, and viral load (HC2 RLU/CO) were analysed in the full cohort. The genotyped subset was additionally evaluated for HPV genotype distribution and genotype-integrated ROC models. Descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis testing with Holm-adjusted Dunn's post-hoc comparisons, and ROC analyses with 95% confidence intervals and paired DeLong comparisons were performed.
RESULTS: RLU/CO values differed across study-specific histopathological severity categories, with higher median values in LSIL, HSIL, and invasive cervical cancer than in normal histology and chronic cervicitis. In the cohort of 328 women, RLU/CO discriminated HSIL or invasive cervical cancer (severity score ≥3) with an AUC of 0.798 (95% CI, 0.726-0.868). A study-derived Youden-index cutoff of 12.08 RLU/CO yielded a sensitivity of 81.1% (95% CI, 69.5%-90.9%) and specificity of 73.1% (95% CI, 68.0%-78.0%). Among 111 genotyped participants, HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype, and multiple-genotype infections occurred in 64 participants (57.7%). In the genotyped subgroup, comparative ROC analysis for HSIL or invasive cervical cancer showed AUCs of 0.659 for RLU/CO alone, 0.608 for RLU/CO plus HPV16/18, and 0.461 for RLU/CO plus other high-risk HPV. Neither genotype-integrated model improved discrimination compared with RLU/CO alone; these exploratory estimates require validation in larger independent cohorts.
CONCLUSION: HC2 RLU/CO showed potential for identifying HSIL or invasive cervical cancer. The study-derived cutoff requires…

articles.title: The breast at perimenopause.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Rousset-Jablonski C, Gompel A
articles.abstract: Perimenopause, defined as the transition between regular menstrual cycles and confirmed menopause, is characterized by erratic hormonal secretions and metabolic disorders which can have potential consequences for breast health. During this period, benign breast diseases may worsen, adversely affecting quality of life and possibly increasing the risk of breast cancer. These aspects have implications for the clinical management of these women. Breast cancer has different characteristics and risk factors for women in premenopause, perimenopause and postmenopause. This narrative review analyzed available data on these risk factors during perimenopause, including the impact of hormonal contraception and menopause hormone therapy. Incidence and mortality, and subtypes of breast cancer differ in women according to the stage of menopause, ethnicity, the level of income of countries and public health resources. These inequalities in risk levels, breast cancer types and prognosis may affect screening and preventive strategies - an issue clinicians should be aware of. Among breast cancer survivors, the menopausal transition raises the question of a shift from tamoxifen, usually used in perimenopausal women, to aromatase inhibitors, indicated after menopause; the treatment may complicate the diagnosis of menopause. Women in the perimenopause may experience differences in the frequency and severity of endocrine therapy side effects.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease: Integrating Epidemiology, Clinical Guidelines, Molar Measurement, and Emerging Therapies.
articles.authors: Thomas PE, Vedel-Krogh S, Kronenberg F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD = myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, peripheral artery disease) and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma concentrations of Lp(a) are >90% genetically determined. Multiple drugs in development reduce lipoprotein(a) by 80% to 98%. While the recently announced topline results, the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial of pelacarsen did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint despite lowering Lp(a), and 3 other cardiovascular outcomes trials remain ongoing. Lipoprotein(a) testing is currently increasing rapidly in many countries.
CONTENT: Most guidelines on dyslipidemia and prevention of cardiovascular disease worldwide now advise that Lp(a) should be measured once in all adults, ideally jointly with the first lipid profile ordered. If previous lipid profiles were taken, then Lp(a) should be included in the next lipid profile. Lipoprotein(a) should ideally be measured in nmol/L, and repeat measurements are relevant if drugs are given to lower Lp(a) concentrations, initially at suspected acute coronary syndrome or stroke and again after 1 month, and sometimes in women after menopause. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial assessment of a patient's overall cardiovascular risk. Clinical chemistry laboratories that measure lipid profiles should therefore also offer Lp(a) testing. This is easily done as Lp(a) assays can be run on most major clinical chemistry platforms. High Lp(a) is >105 nmol/L (>50 mg/dL).
SUMMARY: As use of Lp(a) testing is increasing rapidly worldwide, more clinical chemistry laboratories will likely offer this test locally. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial lipid assessment of a patient's cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Transperineal Ultrasound Assessment of Fetal Head Descent and Successful Manual Rotation in Women Undergoing Labor With Neuraxial Analgesia.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Suzuki Y, Takita H, Matsuoka R et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Manual rotation is commonly used to correct fetal head malrotation during labor. This study assessed the effectiveness of manual rotation under neuraxial analgesia and evaluated whether transperineal ultrasound (TUS)-derived parameters were associated with procedural success and could provide additional information when considering manual rotation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 59 women with fetal rotational abnormalities during labor under neuraxial analgesia at a tertiary care center. Rotational abnormalities were defined as occiput posterior or occiput transverse positions with a midline angle (MLA) ≥ 45°, assessed 1 h after full cervical dilation. Manual rotation success was defined as correction to an MLA < 45°. Delivery, maternal, neonatal, and TUS-derived parameters were compared between successful and unsuccessful cases.
RESULTS: Manual rotation was successful in 44 of 59 cases (74.5%). The vaginal delivery rate was significantly higher in the successful group than in the unsuccessful group (90.9% vs. 46.7%, p < 0.001). No significant differences were noted in maternal or neonatal outcomes. Among TUS parameters, only the TUS-station was significantly associated with procedural success. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified a cutoff of 14.3 mm, above which the likelihood of successful rotation was 95.8%. In exploratory logistic regression models, TUS-station remained associated with successful manual rotation after adjustment for clinically relevant covariates.
CONCLUSIONS: Manual rotation performed under neuraxial analgesia was associated with a high-procedural success rate. A TUS-station ≥ 14.3 mm was associated with a high likelihood of successful manual rotation and may provide complementary information when considering the procedure, although further validation is required.

articles.title: Second-Trimester Assessment of Lower Uterine Segment Microvascular Flow and Residual Myometrial Thickness for Predicting Pregnancies at Low Risk for Developing Uterine Scar Dehiscence After Cesarean Delivery: A Prospective Preliminary Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Muto M, Horinouchi T, Kawakami K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To determine whether second-trimester assessment of lower uterine segment microvascular blood flow using superb microvascular imaging complements residual myometrial thickness for predicting pregnancies at low risk of developing uterine scar dehiscence, a precursor lesion of uterine rupture after previous cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This prospective study included 77 women with singleton pregnancies and at least one previous cesarean delivery. Transvaginal ultrasonography was performed at 19-21 and 25-27 weeks of gestation to measure residual myometrial thickness and assess lower uterine segment microvascular blood flow using superb microvascular imaging. Uterine scar dehiscence was diagnosed by macroscopic findings at cesarean delivery. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Seventeen women developed uterine scar dehiscence. Residual myometrial thickness was thinner and microvascular blood flow was detected less frequently in women with than without uterine scar dehiscence at both gestational periods. At 25-27 weeks of gestation, combining microvascular blood flow assessment with residual myometrial thickness improved discrimination over residual myometrial thickness alone (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.77 vs. 0.65; p = 0.02), improving exclusion of uterine scar dehiscence. After adjustment for residual myometrial thickness, microvascular blood flow remained independently associated with the absence of uterine scar dehiscence (odds ratio, 11.1; 95% confidence interval, 2.74-61.0; p = 0.0005).
CONCLUSIONS: Superb microvascular imaging provides information complementary to residual myometrial thickness. Combined second-trimester assessment, particularly at 25-27 weeks of gestation, may improve prediction of pregnancies at low risk for developing uterine scar dehiscence.

articles.title: Placental angiogenic biomarkers for triage of suspected preeclampsia and prediction of maternal and neonatal morbidity in a high-risk population.
articles.authors: Lodewijks EJ, Hendrix MLE, Suiters MJM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Placental angiogenic biomarkers, including soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and placental growth factor (PlGF), are used to predict preeclampsia (PE) and related adverse outcomes . This study aimed to assess differences in sFlt-1/PlGF ratios among high-risk women according to PE, maternal and neonatal morbidity, and to evaluate the predictive performance of thresholds > 38 and > 85, including time to delivery.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 289 high-risk singleton pregnant women (2015-2019) were included. sFlt-1/PlGF ratios were measured after 24 weeks of gestation and compared across outcome groups.
RESULTS: sFlt-1/PlGF ratios were significantly lower in the reference group compared to the confirmed and the suspected PE group. Ratios > 38 were associated with PE (OR 12.2 (95% CI 4.9-30.7; p < 0.001)), maternal morbidity (OR 22.5 (95% CI 8.9-56.7; p < 0.001)), neonatal morbidity (OR 4.0 (95% CI 2.0-8.0; p < 0.001)) and delivery within one, two, and three weeks (OR 20.0, 9.2, and 14.6; all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio supports individualized management in high-risk pregnancies.

articles.title: Variation of the uterine flexion angle before and after voiding in nulliparous women with anteverted uterus: FLEXIMIX study.
articles.authors: Chiron B, Aujoulat P, Gergaud L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resistance during intrauterine device insertion (IUD) may be influenced by the uterine flexion angle. While bladder filling has been used to facilitate catheter insertion for hysteroscopy and embryo transfer, the only study assessing this strategy for IUD insertion found no benefit. However, the physiological effect of bladder filling on uterine alignment has not been rigorously evaluated. This effect may be particularly relevant in nulliparous women with anteverted uteri. The study aimed to evaluate the variation in uterine flexion angle between full and empty bladder conditions in nulliparous women, and to determine the prevalence of uterine anteversion in a European population.
METHODS: Prospective single-center study included 250 nulliparous women aged 18 years or older. Participant underwent two transabdominal ultrasounds: with a full bladder / after voiding. Uterine version and flexion were assessed by measuring the angles formed by the uterine body, cervix, and vaginal axis.
RESULTS: Among the 215 participants with uterine anteversion (87.0%), paired flexion angle measurements were available for 212 (84.8% of the total cohort). Among these 212 women, the mean change in flexion angle was 48.0° (SD 36.7°, p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.31). In 60.8% of cases, bladder filling changed an acute flexion angle to an obtuse one. The point of uterine flexion was located approximately 20-21 mm from the external cervical os, just beyond the internal os, suggesting a mechanical effect of bladder distension on uterine alignment.
CONCLUSIONS: Bladder filling significantly modifies uterine flexion in nulliparous women with anteversion. This physiological effect provides a plausible anatomical mechanism that may facilitate IUD insertion. Further interventional studies are needed to determine its clinical applicability.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, trial registration number: NCT06669845, registration date: 2024-10-31.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes, surgeon-rated fatigue, and scar satisfaction after dual-port versus single-port laparoscopic myomectomy: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Li Y, Su Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic myomectomy is commonly used for women with symptomatic uterine fibroids who wish to preserve the uterus. Single-port laparoscopy reduces the number of abdominal incisions but may increase instrument crowding and ergonomic difficulty during myometrial dissection and suturing. Dual-port laparoscopy may provide a practical balance between reduced-port access and operative maneuverability. This study compared perioperative outcomes, surgeon-rated fatigue, and patient-reported scar satisfaction between dual-port and single-port laparoscopic myomectomy.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women who underwent elective laparoscopic myomectomy for solitary uterine fibroids at a tertiary center between January 2024 and November 2025. Propensity scores were estimated using age, body mass index, fibroid diameter, fibroid location, pelvic adhesion grade, medical comorbidity, and number of previous pelvic surgeries. One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed with a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score. Primary multivariable models in the matched cohort additionally adjusted for operating surgeon and year of surgery and used matched-pair clustered robust variance estimation. Alternative-model sensitivity analyses and regression diagnostics were also performed.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 190 women were included, with 95 patients in each group. Estimated blood loss was lower in the dual-port group (mean ± standard deviation, 45.53 ± 38.12 vs. 76.32 ± 69.94 mL; median [interquartile range], 30.0 [20.0-50.0] vs. 50.0 [30.0-100.0] mL). In the fully adjusted matched-cohort model, dual-port surgery remained associated with lower blood loss (β = -23.07 mL, 95% CI - 39.14 to - 7.01; P = 0.005), whereas the operative-time association was attenuated (β = -0.13 h, 95% CI - 0.27 to 0.00; P = 0.053). Surgeon-rated fatigue was available for 110 of 190 patients (57.9%) and scar satisfaction for 78 of 190 patients (41.1%); both were analyzed as exploratory complete-case outcomes. Postoperative recovery outcomes showed no consistent between-group pattern, and only one postoperative complication occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In this propensity score-matched cohort, dual-port laparoscopic myomectomy was associated with lower estimated blood loss after adjustment for operating surgeon and year of surgery. The operative-time finding was suggestive but not independently confirmed…

articles.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus and risk of long-term cardiometabolic disease.
articles.authors: Shen Y, Perng W, Dabelea D et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), or hyperglycaemia first diagnosed during pregnancy, is associated with adverse outcomes for the mother and offspring. In this narrative review, we first summarize the epidemiological evidence regarding long-term maternal and offspring cardiometabolic consequences of GDM, including the role of heterogeneity in the aetiology of GDM in shaping the long-term effects of GDM exposure. Next, we discuss established mechanistic processes, such as β-cell stress, vascular dysfunction and developmental programming, that link GDM to long-term maternal and offspring outcomes and, accordingly, hold potential to be therapeutic targets. We also discuss emerging evidence for connections between other processes, such as placental signalling, and cardiometabolic risk after GDM. Finally, we discuss the role of potential avenues for cardiometabolic risk mitigation following GDM exposure, including lactation and breastfeeding, postpartum monitoring and lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Risk prediction for neonatal resuscitation and intensive care admission after cesarean under general anesthesia.
articles.authors: Liu C, Zhao L, Yin M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates delivered by cesarean under general anesthesia (GA) may require resuscitation or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. This study aimed to develop and validate clinical prediction models for these outcomes.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included singleton cesarean deliveries under GA at four tertiary centers from January 2009 to August 2023. Patients were randomly split into development and validation cohorts (7:3). Candidate clinical and anesthesia-related variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and risk stratification.
RESULTS: Among 1523 neonates, 1067 were assigned to the development cohort and 456 to the validation cohort. Neonatal resuscitation occurred in 212 neonates (13.9%), and NICU admission occurred in 482 (31.6%). The resuscitation model yielded development/validation AUCs of 0.834/0.682, versus 0.810/0.773 for NICU admission. Earlier gestational age was a major predictor of both outcomes, with anesthetic regimen, dexamethasone exposure, and gestational diabetes also contributing to risk estimation.
CONCLUSION: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related variables may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and NICU admission risk after cesarean under GA. These models may support neonatal team preparedness and delivery-room resource planning.
IMPACT: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related data may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission risk after cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. This multicenter study focuses on neonates already exposed to general anesthesia rather than comparing anesthetic techniques. The models incorporate maternal, obstetric, fetal, and anesthesia-related variables, including the induction-to-delivery interval, for individualized pre-delivery risk estimation. The NICU admission model showed more consistent validation performance than the neonatal resuscitation model. These tools may support neonatal team notification, delivery-room readiness, and multidisciplinary planning in high-acuity cesarean deliveries.
